intro.heading: Al Barsha South against the community next door, and why it changes nothing
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Barsha South is, for most families here, a search made in a specific moment: a Diploma Programme student has come home with a predicted grade that does not match the university offer, and a parent wants someone in the room by the weekend. The first instinct is geographic. Is there a better pool of tutors in Al Barsha 1, where the American School of Dubai sits? Does Dubai Marina have more IB specialists because it has more IB families? Should the search widen to Motor City, or to the Jumeirah Village communities on the other side of Al Khail Road?

Those questions have answers, and this page gives them in a table rather than in adjectives. But the conclusion is the same whichever community you compare against, and it is worth stating before the detail: a twenty-minute drive radius is a terrible way to choose a Chemistry HL teacher. Al Barsha South is bounded by Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road to the south and Al Khail Road to the north-east, with no Metro station inside it. The nearest Red Line stops, Mall of the Emirates and Equiti, sit on Sheikh Zayed Road and are a drive away in their own right. Anyone travelling to a villa here between four and six in the afternoon is sitting in the same traffic your own school run sits in.

What that travel does to a lesson is measurable. A sixty-minute session booked for 4pm realistically starts at 4:15pm and finishes early because the tutor has a second family in JVC at six. The parent pays a travel premium for the privilege. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate survey puts in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching online. The gap is not a quality gap. It is a car.

IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, and will not pretend otherwise on a page that ranks for the phrase. In-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For families in Al Barsha South, every lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing for past papers and a written note after each session. The thing a family here gains by accepting that is the only thing worth comparing communities over: the tutor is chosen from the whole pool rather than from the handful of people willing to drive to Al Barsha South 2 at five in the evening.

The rest of this page is built as a comparison, because that is how the decision is actually made. It sets Al Barsha South against Al Barsha 1, Jumeirah Village Circle and Motor City on schools, commute and realistic session timing. It puts the published AED rates for each delivery model side by side with their sources. It explains who regulates your child's school and what a private tutor is legally required to hold. And it is explicit about what a tutor may and may not touch inside an IB Internal Assessment, because the Dubai search results for this phrase include at least one operation selling finished coursework.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-barsha-south.programmesIntro: Families in Al Barsha South send children to IB continuum schools, British schools running IGCSE before a Diploma split, and one or two that offer both routes at sixteen. These are the IB programmes a tutor here is asked for, and what each one actually demands of a student in this part of Dubai.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, assessed internally and reported against learner-profile attributes rather than percentages. There is no external examination. Support at this stage is usually literacy and number fluency, plus helping a child articulate their thinking in an exhibition presentation, which is the first piece of extended independent work the programme asks for.
programmes.countryNote: Bloom World Academy and Nord Anglia International School Dubai both run a primary phase near Al Barsha South, and a family moving in from a British primary often finds the inquiry structure unfamiliar rather than harder. KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the PYP in every Dubai private school, which is frequently the first subject a new arrival here asks for help with.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 1-8 and converted to a 1-7 grade by school-set boundaries. MYP has no public mark scheme to practise against, which is exactly why students arrive at a tutor confused about why a piece of work scored 5 rather than 7. The work is criterion decoding: reading the descriptor and matching it to evidence.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma step is the single most requested piece of work from Al Barsha South families, because several schools in the Al Barsha corridor run MYP to Year 11 and then ask students to choose HL subjects with no IGCSE grade to reason from. A tutor here spends the first two sessions establishing what a child can actually do, not what their MYP grade says.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Graded out of 45. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly 20 to 25 per cent of the final grade, which means a quarter of the result is decided months before the examination hall.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students sit the May session, which UAE schools treat as the live one. Diploma students in Al Barsha South typically have internal IA deadlines set by their own coordinator well ahead of the IB's upload window, so the practical calendar a tutor works to here is the school's, not the IB's. We do not publish IB session dates: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so confirm every date with your child's IB coordinator.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining two or more DP courses with a career-related study and a personal and professional skills core. Fewer Dubai schools offer it than offer the full Diploma, and it suits a student who wants IB subject rigour in two or three areas without carrying six subjects plus the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: CP students in Dubai usually need help with the DP courses inside the programme rather than the career-related study, so support here is ordinary Diploma subject teaching at HL or SL. Families in Al Barsha South considering the route should ask their school directly which DP courses it will run alongside the CP core, because that varies school by school in this emirate.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-barsha-south.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Al Barsha South families ask for most often, and what makes each one hard rather than what makes it popular. The description names the component where marks concentrate, because that is where a limited number of sessions should go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries the whole course. At HL the Paper 3 extended investigation is the component students have least practice at, because it asks them to follow an unfamiliar mathematical argument rather than answer discrete questions. Proof by induction and complex numbers are where HL marks concentrate; at SL, calculus notation and the graphical calculator cost more marks than the theory does.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-heavy work. Students who chose AI because it sounded lighter find the HL statistics content, including chi-squared and regression interpretation, considerably less forgiving than expected. The graphical calculator is assumed throughout, and marks go missing when a student can get an answer from the device but cannot justify the method in writing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The mechanics and fields topics are conceptually linked, and a student who memorised equations separately falls apart in Paper 2 extended response. HL-only content on induction and quantum physics arrives late in the second year. Paper 1 multiple choice rewards fast recognition of a situation, which is a practised skill rather than a known fact.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most requests. The internal assessment is the component most often rescued late, usually because a student chose an investigation with no measurable variable. Paper 2 extended response needs structured reasoning against the command term, and students who can do the chemistry still lose marks writing an unordered answer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content makes this course feel heavier than it is. The real difficulty is data-based questions, where a student must read an unfamiliar graph and comment on reliability rather than recall a fact. HL extension on plant biology and neurobiology is poorly consolidated in most schools because it lands in the final term.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is worth more than prose quality. Students lose marks drawing an unlabelled axis or omitting the shift arrow, then write three paragraphs that cannot recover the point. The internal assessment requires three commentaries on real news articles, and choosing an article with no clear economic concept is the most common early error.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided textual analysis on an unseen non-literary text is the component that separates grades. Students trained to write about novels struggle with an advertisement or a political speech. The Individual Oral requires a global issue linked to two works, and a poorly chosen global issue limits the mark before the student speaks.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study application rather than theory recall. The HL extension and the Paper 1 pre-released case study reward students who have read the material closely enough to quote it. The internal assessment is a research project on a real organisation, and access to usable primary data is the practical constraint most Dubai students hit.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 and 2 test theory, abstract data structures and the option topic, not coding ability. The internally assessed solution needs a genuine client and documented testing, which is where most of the mark sits. HL students must handle recursion and object-oriented design in pseudocode, which few have seen before the course.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Support here is ordinary language teaching for the school's own scheme of work, and we work to that scheme rather than substituting material, which schools are not permitted to vary without Ministry permission.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects plus a prescribed-title essay. TOK marks are decided by how precisely a student handles a knowledge question, not by how much they know. Students in Dubai often write a general essay on truth when the title asked about a specific area of knowledge, and lose the top band on relevance alone.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a chosen subject, with a supervisor at school. Support is process coaching: narrowing a research question, planning a method, reading a draft and giving written feedback. The student writes every word of it, and a tutor who offers anything else is creating a malpractice case against the child.

sections.heading: What searching for an IB home tutor in Al Barsha South actually gets you
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Barsha South, in the open market, costs between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour and brings one person's subject range to your door. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350; independent home tutors advertising directly quote 200 to 500. That price includes travel, and travel is why the rate sits above the AED 150 to 300 a qualified subject tutor charges to teach the same hour online.

The second thing the search gets you is a short list. The number of people who can teach Diploma Chemistry HL to a high standard, hold the required work permit and are willing to be in Al Barsha South 2 at 4:30pm on a Tuesday is small. Families discover this at the point of booking, usually after being offered a tutor whose actual specialism is Year 9 science. The constraint is geometric rather than anything to do with teaching quality: a tutor who drives can only serve the families inside their own radius.

IB Gram answers the search differently. Lessons for Al Barsha South families are taught one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and the tutor is selected from the full pool rather than from the people who live nearby. We do not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service, and the comparison tables further down this page are the argument for why accepting that is a good trade rather than a compromise.

The rest of the page takes the comparison seriously instead of asserting it. There is a table setting this community against Al Barsha 1, JVC and Motor City. There is a table of published AED rates with their sources. There is a table on the delivery models measured against each other on cost, travel, tutor pool and scheduling. If the conclusion were close, the tables would show it.

sections.heading: Al Barsha South against Al Barsha 1, JVC and Motor City
paragraphs: The comparison a parent here makes is almost always with one of three neighbours: Al Barsha 1 to the north, Jumeirah Village across Al Khail Road, or Motor City over the E311. Each has a credible claim to a better tutor supply, and the table below sets out what each actually offers an IB family in terms of schools inside the community, drive time at school-run hour, and the earliest a lesson can realistically begin if someone has to travel.

Read the fourth column first. The earliest realistic session start is the number that decides whether tutoring fits into a school week, and it degrades fast once travel enters the picture. A family in Al Barsha South 3 whose child finishes at 3:15pm can begin an online lesson at 3:45pm. The same family waiting for a tutor who has come from Al Barsha 1 is looking at 4:30pm at best, and a tutor crossing from JVC in the opposite direction at the same hour is unreliable by fifteen minutes in either direction.

The fifth column is the one that undercuts the premise of the whole search. The tutor pool reachable within twenty minutes differs between these communities by a meaningful amount, but the pool reachable over video is identical from all four, and it is a hundred times larger. The comparison matters a great deal if you are hiring someone to drive. It stops mattering entirely if you are not.

One practical note on the second column. School provision in a community is not the same as tutoring supply in that community. Al Barsha 1 has more IB schools inside it than Al Barsha South, which raises local demand as much as it raises local supply, and the schools in both clusters draw students from across New Dubai rather than from their own streets.

sections.heading: What the Dubai tutoring market charges, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest option rather than the most expensive one, because that is the order a parent's budget works in. A university-student tutor teaching online advertises from AED 45 to 65 on EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 on Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor teaching online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and premium named or examiner-track tutors reaching AED 650 at BartyED.

Now add the car. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's 2026 survey and at 200 to 500 by independent home tutors. Set that against AED 150 to 300 for the same qualification teaching online, and the in-home premium is roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour. Over a two-session week across a Diploma year, that is a four-figure difference in AED for the travel alone.

The honest question is what the premium buys. It buys physical presence, which matters for some children, and it buys a tutor who can sit beside a nervous fourteen-year-old. It does not buy a better teacher, and in Al Barsha South it actively narrows the choice of teacher, because only the people inside the drive radius are available at all. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Every figure above belongs to the company that published it, not to IB Gram. We do not publish a price list on these pages. The route is a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many sessions the problem actually needs, which for a single IA rescue is often four and for a two-year HL subject is a weekly slot. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for one hour a week are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

sections.heading: Online against in-home in this community, on the four things that change
paragraphs: Comparisons between online and in-home tutoring usually get argued on feel. Measured instead on the four variables that differ, the picture is clearer: cost per hour, time lost to travel, size of the available tutor pool, and how easily a session can be moved. Three of those four favour online delivery regardless of where in Dubai you live, and the fourth is the only genuine argument for in-home.

Travel time is the variable Al Barsha South makes worse than most. The community has no Metro station, sits between two motorways and empties onto Umm Suqeim Street and Hessa Street, both of which back up between four and six in the afternoon. A tutor who has committed to 4pm here and 6pm in JVC is managing a schedule, not a child's learning, and the family who holds the later slot absorbs the slippage.

Rescheduling is where the difference compounds across a Diploma year. A family travelling in the Eid or National Day weeks, a child sitting mocks, a Ramadan timetable that moves everything after Iftar: each of these is a thirty-second change to an online booking and a negotiation with a driver's route for an in-home one. Across two years of DP, the number of lessons that simply happen rather than being rearranged is the quiet reason online packages finish their syllabus.

The honest column in the table below is the last one. A child who genuinely cannot hold attention on a screen, or a Year 4 pupil who needs someone physically turning the page, is better served in person, and we would rather say so than sell the wrong thing. For Diploma-level work, where sessions are built around past papers on a shared screen and written feedback on the student's own document, the screen is not a limitation at all.

sections.heading: The 4pm problem: why an Al Barsha South session really starts at 4:45pm
paragraphs: This community's geometry is specific and it matters to a tutoring schedule. Al Barsha South 1, 2 and 3 are bounded by Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, with Umm Suqeim Street and Hessa Street carrying most of the local movement. There is no Metro station inside the community. The nearest Red Line stops are on Sheikh Zayed Road, which means a tutor without a car is not a realistic in-home proposition here at all.

School end times in the Al Barsha cluster stack up between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, and the bus runs from the Al Barsha and Al Barsha South schools finish dropping between 3:15pm and 4:15pm depending on route. A child who is home at 3:20pm has eaten and is ready at four. A child on a longer route is not ready until 4:30pm. Either way, the window between the school bus and the evening collapse of attention is roughly four hours long, and it is the whole scheduling problem.

An online lesson occupies that window precisely. It starts when the child is ready rather than when a car arrives, and it gives back the twenty to forty minutes a travelling tutor needs. Families here commonly settle on 4pm or 4:30pm for younger students and 6:30pm to 8pm for Diploma students who need a gap between school and more school. During Ramadan, slots shift after Iftar, which is a scheduling change rather than a different service.

The practical consequence is that a weekly slot in Al Barsha South survives the term. The sessions that get cancelled across a Diploma year are the ones that depended on a drive through Hessa Street at five. Over two years, consistency is what finishes a syllabus; a slightly better tutor seen two-thirds of the time is worse than a good tutor seen every week.

sections.heading: Why the answer is the same from Al Barsha South, Marina or Motor City
paragraphs: Take the comparison to its end. If a family moved from Al Barsha South 2 to Dubai Marina tomorrow, their IB tutoring decision would be identical. The local tutor pool would be deeper and more expensive, the drive times would be different, and the choice between paying a travel premium for a nearby generalist or paying a specialist rate for the right subject teacher would be exactly the same choice. The geography changes the inputs. It does not change the conclusion.

This is why the eight communities listed higher up this page carry notes about schools and commutes rather than claims about tutor quality. There is no reason to believe that the best Economics HL teacher available to a Dubai family happens to live within twenty minutes of any particular villa. Searching by area is a proxy for searching by availability, and once availability stops being constrained by a car, the proxy has no information left in it.

What does carry information is the match itself. Which component is the student losing marks on. Whether the school runs Maths AA or AI, and at which level. When the school's internal IA deadline falls, as distinct from the IB's upload window. Whether the child needs a teacher who rebuilds confidence or one who drills past papers hard. None of those questions have a postcode in them, and all of them change the outcome more than a drive time does.

So the recommendation for an Al Barsha South family is the same one we would give a family in The Springs or Arjan: choose the subject specialist, take the free trial lesson, and keep the slot in the hour that genuinely works around your school bus. The community you live in determines when the lesson should start. It should not determine who teaches it.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and who is allowed to tutor in the UAE
paragraphs: Your child's school in Al Barsha South is regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes each report on its own site. If you want to know how a school is performing, read the report there rather than a tutoring company's summary of it.

The regulator differs by emirate, which matters for families who move. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK's responsibility, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education.

On the tutor side, private tuition in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website or e-services. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

One rule catches parents by surprise. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. If someone offers you your child's own classroom teacher privately, that is a problem for the teacher and for your child. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval and does not claim any.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what an IB tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: This matters more in the Dubai search results for IB tutoring than it should. At least one operation ranking for these queries sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. A family paying for it is buying a risk to their child's entire Diploma.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the subject content an IA rests on. A tutor may help a student narrow a research question, discuss whether a method will produce usable data, explain an assessment criterion in plain words, and read a draft the student wrote and give written feedback on it. That is ordinary supervision, the same thing the school's own supervisor does, and it is what makes the difference between a mid-band IA and a strong one.

A tutor may not write any part of the work, dictate sentences for a student to type, produce the analysis, or edit a draft to the point where the words are no longer the student's. The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay, the TOK essay and exhibition, and the MYP Personal Project. We also do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright problem.

Every IB Gram tutor working with an Al Barsha South student is briefed on this before the first session, and it is written into the session notes. If you ask us to do the work, we will decline and explain why, which is occasionally an uncomfortable conversation and always the right one. The published assessment criteria for every component are on ibo.org, and a student who understands what criterion C is asking for will write a better IA than one who was handed a finished document.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Barsha South, and what happens if the specialist is booked
paragraphs: The process is four steps and the first one is free. You tell us the school, the subject, the level and the component that is going wrong. We propose a specialist and a slot that fits around your school bus. You take a trial lesson at no cost, with no card required and no package agreed. If the match is right you keep the slot; if it is not, you tell us what was wrong and we propose a different tutor.

What we will not do is pretend that every subject at every level is instantly available. Diploma Higher Level teaching in narrow subjects, Computer Science HL and Further Mathematics among them, has a genuine waiting time, and the honest answer in that case is a date rather than a yes. Where a UAE-based specialist is not free, the match may be a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the identical syllabus on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before you book rather than after.

Session timing is set at the start and left alone. Families in Al Barsha South mostly take 4pm to 5:30pm for MYP students and 6:30pm to 8:30pm for Diploma students, Sunday to Thursday, which keeps the slot clear of the Hessa Street and Umm Suqeim Street crawl. Slots move after Iftar during Ramadan and we hold the same tutor through the change. Travel between terms does not interrupt anything, because the lesson follows the family rather than the address.

Lead forms on this page collect a parent's name, contact details, the child's school, year group and subject, used only to propose a tutor and arrange the trial lesson. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs how that is handled, the privacy policy is linked from every page, and you can ask for the record to be deleted at any point.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: A message naming the school, the year group, the subject, the level and what specifically is going wrong. 'Chemistry HL, Paper 2 extended response, IA due in five weeks' gets a better match than 'needs help with science'. The component is what determines which specialist is right.

process.title: We propose a specialist and a slot

The proposal names the tutor, their subject and component experience, and a slot that works around the Al Barsha South school-bus drop rather than around the tutor's convenience. If the specialism has a waiting time, we give you the date instead of a vague yes.

process.title: Free trial lesson, nothing agreed
process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video at no cost, with no card required and no package committed. The point is for your child to decide whether this person can teach them, which is not a question a parent can answer from a profile page.

process.title: Set the slot and leave it alone
process.description: Once the match works, the weekly time is fixed and protected. Each session ends with a written note of what was covered and what to practise. Changing the time later is a message, and moving slots after Iftar during Ramadan is routine rather than a disruption.

process.title: Review against the school's own calendar
process.description: Every few weeks we check the plan against your child's school deadlines, not a generic syllabus order. Internal IA dates, mock windows and coursework hand-ins come from the school's coordinator, and the tutoring plan follows them.

whyPoints.description: Every claim this page makes about communities, rates and delivery models sits in a table with its source named. Three of six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars. A parent in Al Barsha South should be able to check the numbers before making a decision.

whyPoints.title: Matched by component, not by proximity

Choosing from the full pool rather than a twenty-minute radius is the single biggest difference between online and in-home delivery, and it is not a small one.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly, up front
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, and we say that on the page that ranks for the phrase rather than at the bottom of a booking form. Home visits are a service we offer only in India.

whyPoints.title: Clear academic-honesty boundary
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains criteria and gives written feedback on the student's own work. Nobody at IB Gram writes an IA, an Extended Essay or a TOK essay, and we decline when asked. At least one page competing for this search sells finished coursework, and the risk of that falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around an Al Barsha South school week
whyPoints.description: Slots are set around the school-bus drop and the evening traffic on Hessa Street and Umm Suqeim Street, not around a generic timetable. The lessons that actually happen across a two-year Diploma are the ones that never depended on a drive at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor in Al Barsha South who comes to the villa?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We do not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For Al Barsha South families, every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The independent market does offer in-home visits, quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey and 200 to 500 by direct home tutors, and that rate includes travel. The trade is straightforward: paying for a drive narrows your choice to whoever is willing to be in Al Barsha South 2 at half past four, rather than opening it to the full specialist pool.

faqs.question: Is the tutor pool in Al Barsha 1 or Dubai Marina better than in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: For in-home tutoring, yes, measurably. Al Barsha 1 and Dubai Marina have deeper local supply because they have more IB families and more schools inside them. For online tutoring the question has no content: the pool reachable over video is the same from Al Barsha South 3 as it is from JBR, and it is far larger than any drive radius. If you are hiring someone to travel, compare communities carefully. If you are not, compare specialists instead and pick the slot that fits your school bus.

faqs.question: Which schools in and around Al Barsha South do your IB students attend?
faqs.answer: Students we support in this part of Dubai attend Safa Community School, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Bloom World Academy and GEMS Founders School Al Barsha inside or bordering Al Barsha South, and Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, American School of Dubai, Kings' School Al Barsha and Repton Al Barsha in the cluster just north. Across Al Khail Road we work with students at Arcadia Global School, Sunmarke School and JSS International School. These schools are named as context for the area. IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them, and we would not claim one.

faqs.question: What time can an IB lesson start for a child in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: Schools in the Al Barsha cluster finish between roughly 2:45pm and 3:30pm, and buses drop between 3:15pm and 4:15pm depending on the route. An online lesson can begin as soon as your child has eaten, which for most families here means 4pm. Diploma students more often take 6:30pm to 8:30pm so there is a gap between school and more school. Sunday to Thursday slots run to 9pm Gulf Standard Time, and during Ramadan the whole schedule shifts after Iftar with the same tutor kept in place.

faqs.question: How much does online IB tutoring cost compared with a home tutor in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Taking published figures rather than estimates: a qualified subject tutor teaching online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one is AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey and 200 to 500 from independent home tutors. The in-home premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour is travel. Those are market rates from the companies that published them, not IB Gram prices; we start with a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many sessions the problem needs.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask any individual tutor directly whether they hold one. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write my child's IB Internal Assessment if the deadline is close?
faqs.answer: No, and you should walk away from anyone who agrees to. Under IB rules the work must be the student's own, and the malpractice consequence falls on your child rather than on the person who sold it. What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial: teach the underlying content, question whether a method will produce usable data, explain each assessment criterion in plain words, and give written feedback on a draft your child has written. With five weeks left that is usually enough to move an IA up a band, and it leaves the Diploma intact.

faqs.question: Why does Al Barsha South have no Metro station, and does it affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: The community sits between Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, away from the Red Line, which runs along Sheikh Zayed Road. The nearest stops, Mall of the Emirates and Equiti, are a drive away. It matters for in-home tutoring because a tutor without a car is simply not a realistic option here, which narrows local supply further than the map suggests. For online lessons it is irrelevant, beyond explaining why the evening traffic on Hessa Street and Umm Suqeim Street is the real constraint on session timing.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP to the IB Diploma. Where does tutoring help most?
faqs.answer: At the point of subject choice and in the first term. Several schools in the Al Barsha corridor run MYP to Year 11, so students pick Higher Level subjects with no IGCSE grade to reason from and often choose badly. A tutor's first job is establishing what the child can actually do rather than what the MYP grade reports. After that the work is specific: mark-scheme literacy, command terms, and the habit of answering the question asked. MYP has no public mark scheme, so this is usually the first time a student has seen one.

faqs.question: Do you teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Dubai families this is not optional. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in every private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes are prohibited. We teach to the school's own scheme of work rather than substituting material, because schools are not permitted to use different or additional content without prior Ministry permission. For a family newly arrived in Al Barsha South, this is often the subject where the gap is largest and least expected.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Al Barsha South Diploma families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One weekly slot per problem subject is the normal start, 60 or 90 minutes, with the same tutor each week. Families carrying two difficult subjects often take consecutive evenings so the week has a rhythm, and we keep both tutors working to one shared deadline calendar to avoid both setting work for the same weekend. A single bounded problem, an IA write-up or a Paper 3 technique gap, is usually four to eight sessions with a stated finishing point rather than an open commitment.

faqs.question: What happens if the Higher Level specialist we need is not available?
faqs.answer: We give you a date instead of a yes. Narrow Higher Level subjects, Computer Science HL and Further Mathematics among them, have genuine waiting times, and pretending otherwise wastes your week. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match may be a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the identical syllabus on Gulf Standard Time, and we tell you that before the trial lesson rather than after you have booked. None of the competitor pages researched for this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely as effective for a Diploma student as someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For Diploma-level work, yes, and the reason is mechanical. Sessions are built around past papers on a shared screen with the mark scheme visible, annotation of the student's own document, and written feedback afterwards. All of that works better on a screen than on a kitchen table. The group it suits less well is young children and students who genuinely cannot hold attention on video, and we would rather say so than sell the wrong thing. For a sixteen-year-old working on Paper 2 technique, the screen is not a limitation.

faqs.question: How do I read a KHDA inspection report for a school in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: Read it on KHDA's own site rather than in a summary. KHDA inspects every Dubai private school annually and publishes the report, graded across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. The useful part for a tutoring decision is not the overall band but the subject-level judgements and the section on students' attainment and progress in that subject. A school rated highly overall can still have a weak department, and that department is usually the reason a parent in this community starts searching for a tutor in the first place.

faqs.question: Do you have an office in Dubai we can visit?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and a tutoring page that implies one is misrepresenting itself. Everything runs over live video and message, with a UAE-timed schedule and a named tutor you keep. Two of the competitor pages researched for this market route UAE parents to Indian phone numbers, and one shows a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page. We would rather be plain: no premises, no visits, one-to-one online teaching timed to Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: What do you collect on the enquiry form, and can we have it deleted?
faqs.answer: A parent's name and contact details, the child's school, year group, subject and level, and a short description of the problem. It is used to propose a tutor and arrange the free trial lesson, and for nothing else. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs how it is handled, and the privacy policy is linked from every page. You can ask for the record to be deleted at any point and we will confirm when it is done. We do not ask for grades or a photograph of your child.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.tutorsIntro: These are the kinds of tutors Al Furjan families are matched with for Diploma and Middle Years work: subject specialists who teach one programme rather than every subject on a list, and who have marked or taught the exact components your child sits.

intro.heading: What an Al Furjan parent is really asking for
paragraphs: Al Furjan is a villa and townhouse community sitting between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Yalayis Road, with Discovery Gardens on one side and Dubai Investments Park on the other. Almost nobody who lives here walks to school. Children are collected by bus between 06:30 and 07:15 and returned between 15:20 and 16:10 depending on the route, the school and whether an after-school club ran. That single fact shapes every tutoring decision a family here makes, and it is the reason a search for an IB home tutor in Al Furjan is usually a search for a workable slot rather than a search for a subject expert.

The second fact is the tutor pool. Al Furjan is residential, not academic. The Diploma specialists in Dubai cluster around the schools that run the programme, and those schools sit in Al Barsha, Al Khail, Dubai Investments Park, Nad Al Sheba and Jumeirah. A Chemistry Higher Level teacher who will drive to Al Furjan for a 17:00 lesson is a small group of people, and most of them are already committed to the families nearest them. Hiring the tutor who happens to be free and nearby is how a student ends up with a generalist maths tutor for a Physics Higher Level problem.

IB Gram does not solve that by sending someone to your door. Home visits are a service we run in India only. Across the UAE every lesson is one-to-one over live video, and we say so in the first paragraph of every page because the alternative is wasting a parent's time. What that buys an Al Furjan family is the end of the geography problem: your child gets the Mathematics Analysis and Approaches specialist or the Visual Arts examiner, not the person with the shortest commute.

The rest of this page is written around the school run, because that is the constraint we hear most often from this community. It sets out what time a session can honestly start for the main school routes serving Al Furjan, what the Dubai market charges for in-home and online tuition so you can judge any quote you receive, how the KHDA mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education requirement sits alongside the Diploma, and where the line falls between legitimate Internal Assessment support and work a tutor must never touch.

If you are reading this in the middle of a bad term, the useful next step is small: one free trial lesson, with the specific paper or criterion your child is struggling with on the screen. You will know inside forty minutes whether the match is right, and so will we. Nothing is paid for the trial, and a family that decides against it has lost an hour rather than a month of fees. That is deliberate, because the single most expensive mistake in this market is paying for three months before anyone checks whether the tutor knows the component.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.programmesIntro: Al Furjan children are spread across all three IB programmes because the community feeds schools in three different directions. The notes below describe what each programme asks of a student here, and where the school run interferes.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units rather than subject timetables, so a child can look settled while a specific skill quietly slips. Reading fluency, number bonds, written structure and the ability to explain a method out loud are the four things that show up later as Middle Years problems. Assessment is continuous and teacher-designed, which means there is no exam result to react to. Parents usually notice through homework taking twice as long as it should.
programmes.countryNote: Al Furjan primary children are mostly on buses to Jebel Ali, Dubai Investments Park and Jumeirah Park, with arrivals from 15:20. PYP sessions work best at 16:00 or 16:30, kept to forty minutes, and twice a week rather than once for ninety minutes. Dubai private schools also run mandatory Arabic and Social Studies from primary, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils under KHDA rules, and that is often the subject a PYP parent here asks about first.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against criteria A to D in every subject group, each on an eight-point scale, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. A student can know the content and still sit at a 4 because they never answer the command the criterion asks for. Criterion D in the sciences, the reflection strands in Individuals and Societies, and the process journal in Design are the usual places marks disappear. Nothing about this is obvious from a report card.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years students in Al Furjan are the group most affected by the bus timetable, because Years 9 to 11 often have after-school commitments that push arrival past 16:00. A 17:00 or 17:30 online slot is the realistic pattern. This is also the stage where the MYP to Diploma decision arrives, and where a student heading for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level needs algebraic fluency built in MYP 4 and 5, not in the first term of Diploma 1.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly 20 to 30 per cent of the grade, set and marked inside the school against published criteria. The Diploma does not fail students on content; it fails them on volume management. Four internal deadlines landing in the same fortnight is the normal cause of a dropped grade, and it is entirely predictable from the start of the year.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Al Furjan travel furthest, because the Dubai schools offering the full Diploma are concentrated away from the Jebel Ali corridor. An 18:00 or 19:00 session is standard for this group, and many families run a double slot at the weekend during the mock window. UAE schools sit the May session, and the honest planning horizon is the twelve weeks before it, not the four. Universities in the UAE and abroad also differ on whether they accept Mathematics Applications and Interpretation for engineering, which is a Diploma 1 decision.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and a language development component. It suits a student who wants Diploma-level academic work in two or three subjects alongside a vocational pathway. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools, so most families meet it as an alternative when the full Diploma is not the right fit.
programmes.countryNote: Few schools near Al Furjan run the Career-related Programme, so a family here considering it is usually looking at a move or at the Diploma with a reduced subject load. Where CP students do need support, it is almost always in the two Diploma courses and in the reflective project, which is marked on criteria that reward evidence of process over polished prose. Those sessions run online on the same timetable as Diploma sessions.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.subjectsIntro: Requests from the Al Furjan and Jebel Ali corridor concentrate in the sciences and maths, partly because those are the Higher Level choices that decide engineering and medicine applications. These are the subjects most asked for, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic manipulation, calculus and proof. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a two-question extended investigation worth 20 per cent of the grade, which rewards students who can sustain an argument across twenty minutes rather than recognise a question type. Marks are lost in the Toolkit-style modelling questions and in failing to show method when the calculator gives the answer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-led methods. The graphic display calculator is central rather than incidental, and Higher Level statistics goes well beyond what most students expect. The common error is treating it as the easier route; it is a different subject, and some engineering courses will not accept it, which makes the Diploma 1 choice consequential.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Organised into themes from space, time and motion through to nuclear and quantum physics. Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and the data-based section; Paper 2 carries the extended response. Uncertainty propagation and gradient interpretation cost more marks than any single topic, and both are teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Built around structure and reactivity rather than a topic list, with continuous reference to the data booklet. Students lose marks on energetics sign conventions, on explaining rather than describing trends, and on organic mechanisms drawn without curly arrows or lone pairs. The Scientific Investigation is where a weak hypothesis becomes an unrecoverable grade.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Reorganised around unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and continuity. The subject punishes imprecise language: a student who writes that something increases, rather than naming the mechanism and the direction, scores nothing. Statistical treatment of data and the use of standard deviation and error bars are reliably under-taught.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed through diagram-led extended response and three Internal Assessment commentaries on published news articles. Students lose marks by drawing a correct diagram and then not referring to it in the analysis, and by choosing articles with no clear economic concept to anchor the commentary.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as Ansoff, SWOT, break-even and investment appraisal, applied to real organisations. The examined papers are case-study based, so command-term discipline decides the grade: evaluate, examine and discuss each require a different shape of answer. The Higher Level research project needs a real organisation and primary data, which takes longer to arrange than students expect.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works, plus the Individual Oral linking a global issue to one literary and one non-literary text. The Higher Level Essay adds 1,200 to 1,500 words of independent criticism. Weak candidates summarise; strong candidates argue from the text's construction.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic to all pupils under KHDA rules, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. For Diploma candidates the assessed components are reading, writing, listening and an individual oral built from a visual stimulus. Vocabulary breadth and the ability to speak for eight minutes without prompting are the two trainable gaps.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word exhibition commentary on three objects and a 1,600-word essay from six prescribed titles. Together they contribute to the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. Students fail Theory of Knowledge by writing opinion essays; the mark scheme rewards the quality of the knowledge argument and the use of real examples.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay in a chosen subject, supervised in school. The research question is where the grade is decided, usually months before the writing. Essays that fail are almost always answering a question too broad to answer in 4,000 words, and that diagnosis takes one honest conversation.

subjects.name: Design Technology and Computer Science
subjects.description: Both carry substantial internal work: a design cycle project in Design Technology and a solution with documentation in Computer Science. Internal work is marked on process evidence, so the student who builds something impressive without recording iterations scores below the student who documents a modest solution properly.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.regionsTitle: Al Furjan and the communities around it
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.regionsIntro: Al Furjan sits in the Jebel Ali and Dubai South corridor. These are the neighbouring communities whose children share the same school routes and the same evening traffic, and whose families book the same session times.

regions.name: Al Furjan
regions.note: Villas and townhouses across the Quortaj, Masakin, Dar and Murooj districts, with two metro stations on the Route 2020 line. School buses serve the community on long loops, which is why arrival times vary by twenty minutes between neighbours.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens
regions.note: High-density apartment living in themed districts immediately north of Al Furjan. Study space is the constraint rather than travel time, and an online session with headphones in a shared room is a practical setup many families here already run.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park
regions.note: Home to several of the IB and British-curriculum schools that Al Furjan children attend, which means a short bus run in and a long one back when the Green Community and DIP gates queue at pickup.

regions.name: Jebel Ali
regions.note: The industrial and residential district south of Al Furjan, with established schools serving long-settled families. Parents working in Jebel Ali Free Zone often finish later, which pushes supervised study and tutoring into the 19:00 slot.

regions.name: Dubai South
regions.note: The newer residential districts around the Expo site and Al Maktoum airport. School options are still thin on the ground, so children commute north, and the bus run is the longest in this cluster.

regions.name: Emaar South
regions.note: Villa communities near the golf course, with a young family profile and primary-heavy demand. Sessions here skew to PYP and early MYP, in the 16:00 to 17:00 band, and often for two siblings in sequence.

regions.name: Green Community
regions.note: Low-rise villas and apartments inside Dubai Investments Park, close enough to several schools for a short run. Families here have the earliest practical session start in the whole cluster.

regions.name: Dubai Production City
regions.note: Apartments and townhouses north-east of Al Furjan, served by the same corridor of schools along Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. Diploma students here commonly travel to Al Barsha and Al Khail for school.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Al Furjan and Jumeirah Park
schoolClusters.note: The nearest cluster, reachable on a short bus run or a parent drop. Most are British-curriculum schools running IGCSE at 16, with some continuing into the Diploma. Children in the Masakin and Quortaj districts are usually on these routes.

schoolClusters.city: Schools in Dubai Investments Park and Jebel Ali
schoolClusters.note: The southern cluster, carrying both IB continuum schools and large British and Indian-curriculum schools. This is where most of the Diploma and Middle Years students in Al Furjan actually sit their lessons during the day.

schoolClusters.city: Schools along the Al Barsha and Al Khail corridor
schoolClusters.note: The longer commute, taken by families who want a specific Diploma offer. A bus from Al Furjan to this corridor runs forty to sixty minutes in the afternoon, which is why these students book the latest sessions.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.modesIntro: Three session patterns cover almost every Al Furjan family. The difference between them is not price but how the week is shaped around the bus timetable and the internal deadline calendar.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, same slot every week
modes.description: One sixty-minute session a week in a fixed slot the family keeps for the term, with the same tutor each time. This is the pattern that works for a student who is coping but underperforming, and it is the only pattern that builds a usable record of what has been covered. The fixed slot matters more in Al Furjan than in most communities because the alternative is renegotiating around bus times every week.

modes.title: Twice weekly through an assessment block
modes.description: Two shorter sessions in a week, used when several internal deadlines land together or a mock series is three weeks out. Two forty-five minute sessions beat one ninety-minute session for retention, and they let a tutor set work on Monday and check it on Thursday rather than two weeks later. Families in Al Furjan usually run this pattern from January through the mock window and again in the four weeks before the May session.

The tutor reads the criteria with the student, questions the research question or hypothesis, and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. The tutor does not write, rewrite or supply content. That boundary is stated at the first session and recorded, because the consequence of crossing it falls on the student, not on us.

modes.description: Two children in the same household taught in sequence rather than together, because a Year 8 Middle Years student and a Diploma 2 student need different tutors and different content. Running them back to back keeps the evening to one block and means one device and one quiet room serve both. Many Al Furjan households with villa layouts find this easier than two separate evenings.

sections.heading: What time a tutoring session can actually start in Al Furjan
paragraphs: The earliest realistic weekday start for a serious Diploma session in Al Furjan is 16:30, and for most families it is 17:00. That is not a scheduling preference; it is arithmetic. School buses serving the Al Furjan villas run long loops that pick up and drop off across four districts, so the bus that reaches Masakin at 15:25 reaches Murooj at 15:50. Add a snack and a change of clothes and the first usable minute is thirty minutes after arrival.

The picture changes by school. A child at a Dubai Investments Park school on a short run can be home by 15:20 and ready at 15:50. A Diploma student travelling to the Al Barsha or Al Khail corridor will not be through the door before 16:30, and if there is a Creativity, Activity, Service commitment or a sports fixture it is 17:30. The second group is the larger one for Diploma, because the Jebel Ali corridor has fewer full Diploma schools than the areas further north.

This is where online delivery stops being a compromise and becomes the reason the arithmetic works. A session at 19:15 is impossible for an in-home tutor crossing Dubai in evening traffic and entirely ordinary over video. It also means a cancelled session can be rescheduled to the next evening rather than the next week, because nobody is driving anywhere. Families here use that flexibility more than any other feature.

One practical note on the setup. Fix the slot at the start of term and treat it like a timetabled lesson. The families who negotiate the time weekly are the families who lose two sessions a month to traffic, fixtures and fatigue, and two sessions a month is a quarter of the term.

sections.heading: What home tutoring in Al Furjan costs, and what the travel actually buys
paragraphs: Start with the number families here quote most: a visiting one-to-one tutor in Dubai costs roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour, with the travel built into the rate. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages are common at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. These are market figures from published sources, not an IB Gram price list.

Online rates sit lower and the gap is almost entirely travel. EdFlik publishes online rates from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end, with university-student tutors. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the examiner end of the market.

The question worth asking is what the AED 150 travel premium buys in Al Furjan specifically. It buys presence in the room, which matters for a Year 5 child who will not sit still on a video call. It does not buy subject depth, and in this community it often costs it, because the tutor who will drive to Al Furjan for 17:00 is drawn from whoever is within a twenty-minute radius. For a Physics Higher Level student that trade is the wrong way round.

Where families here waste money is predictable: paying a premium rate for homework supervision, booking ninety-minute sessions for a child who concentrates for fifty, and starting in April for a May session. The cheapest effective intervention in this market is an honest diagnostic in the autumn term followed by one weekly session, and it costs a fraction of a six-week rescue.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home visit, measured on this community
paragraphs: A fair comparison has to be specific to where you live, because the variable that changes is travel. From Al Furjan, a tutor coming from Al Barsha in evening traffic is twenty-five to forty-five minutes each way. That return trip is either priced into the lesson or priced into the tutor's willingness to take a 19:00 booking, and usually both. A family comparing an AED 250 online specialist against an AED 350 visiting generalist is not comparing like for like.

The second variable is the pool. Online, the constraint is the tutor's calendar. In-home in Al Furjan, the constraint is the map, and the map is small. For Mathematics at Middle Years level the map is usually large enough. For Chemistry Higher Level, Economics Higher Level or Arabic B at Diploma level it frequently is not, which is how a family ends up with a tutor teaching one level below the one their child sits.

Against that, in-home has two genuine advantages and it is worth naming them. A young child is easier to hold in a room than on a screen, and a visiting tutor sees the desk, the folder and the state of the notes. Online recovers the second by asking the student to share their actual work on screen and by writing a session note the parent reads, but the first is real, and for PYP children under eight a parent sitting in for the first ten minutes is the practical workaround.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one online across Al Furjan and the whole UAE. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visiting is an India-only service. That is a limit, stated plainly, and the table below is the case for why it is the right limit in this particular community.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the IB Diploma in the May session, which means the Diploma 2 year has one shape and every family in Al Furjan is living inside it whether or not they have mapped it. Counting backwards is more useful than counting forwards, because the deadlines that decide grades are internal and they arrive before the exams. The Extended Essay and the subject Internal Assessments are finished and uploaded well before any paper is sat.

The pattern across Dubai schools runs roughly like this. Extended Essay final drafts land in the first term of Diploma 2. Internal Assessments for the sciences, mathematics and the humanities cluster between November and February. The Theory of Knowledge essay is due in the same window. Mocks sit in January or February. Then the May session itself. A student who is still writing an Internal Assessment in March has lost the revision weeks that the May papers need.

We do not publish specific IB exam or results dates on these pages, and the reason is honest rather than cautious: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so we cannot verify a date well enough to put it in front of a parent who will act on it. Your child's Diploma coordinator holds the real internal calendar, and it is the document worth asking for in September. Cambridge and Pearson dates are a different matter and are published below for IGCSE families.

What this means for booking is simple. The useful tutoring year starts in September, not in March. A weekly session from the autumn term costs less in total than a crisis block in the spring and produces a better result, because the Internal Assessment marks are already banked by the time the papers arrive.

sections.heading: KHDA, and what the mandatory UAE subjects mean alongside the IB
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the reports. For a parent in Al Furjan, the inspection report is the most useful free document available about any school on the school-run map, and it names subject-level strengths rather than giving a single verdict.

KHDA also sets a requirement that surprises families new to Dubai: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. These run alongside the IB, not instead of part of it. KHDA's guidance requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

The language rules are specific. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes.

One limit matters for tutoring. For the mandatory UAE subjects, KHDA states that the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support for these subjects therefore works from the school's own material and the Ministry's prescribed content. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, and does not claim to be; a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you are about to hire legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question almost nobody in the Al Furjan WhatsApp groups asks, and it is the one with a clear answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The government's own service page for it is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing.

The terms are worth knowing before you hand over a monthly fee. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time and applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. There is no fee to pass on, so a tutor charging you for permit costs is charging you for nothing.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so we do not quote an amount; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source. The practical step for a parent is to ask the tutor directly whether they hold a private tuition work permit, and to treat an evasive answer as an answer.

There is a related rule for Abu Dhabi families and it is worth knowing even in Dubai. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. So the appealing idea of hiring your child's own class teacher privately is the one arrangement the rules specifically exclude.

sections.heading: Where the line falls on Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
paragraphs: The UAE tutoring market contains businesses that sell completed Internal Assessments. One of them advertises them at a fixed price. If your child submits work they did not produce, the consequence falls on them: the IB treats it as malpractice and the Diploma is at risk, not the vendor's revenue. So the boundary is worth stating in plain terms rather than leaving to inference.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. A tutor can read the assessment criteria with the student and explain what each strand actually rewards. A tutor can interrogate a research question until it is answerable, teach the statistical or mathematical technique the investigation needs, model how a published study structures its analysis, and give written feedback on the student's own draft naming what is missing against the criteria. That is teaching, and it is where most of the available marks are.

What a tutor may not do is write, rewrite, draft, outline for the student to fill in, or supply content that then appears in the submission. IB Gram tutors state that boundary at the first session of any Internal Assessment block and give feedback in writing so the school can see the nature of the support. A school that asks what help a student received should get an answer that holds up.

There is a related rule on materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We cite and link the official sources and work from what the school has issued. Reproducing those documents is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure for the student.
bullets: A tutor may teach technique, question a research question and give written feedback
A tutor may not write, draft or supply any part of a submitted piece

sections.heading: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, and what Al Furjan families need on file
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that converts an international school certificate into a UAE-recognised one, and it matters for any student applying to a UAE university or needing the certificate attested locally. Families in Al Furjan tend to meet it late, usually in the last term of school, and the subject choices that satisfy it were made two years earlier. Knowing the British-track rule in Year 9 is worth more than knowing it in Year 13.

For British-curriculum students the published requirement is specific. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for that count.

That last point corrects an error already in this market. One ranking competitor page tells UAE parents that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced rule is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic education from the count. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the IB there is no equivalency points figure on this page, because none has been read on a Ministry source. We will not publish one. Nor does IB Gram perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation; it is a Ministry process and the Ministry's own channel is the place to verify requirements before you act. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, and any page suggesting otherwise is selling urgency.

sections.heading: What happens when no specialist is free for your slot
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in this market implies infinite availability. The truthful position is that a narrow subject at Higher Level in a fixed evening slot is sometimes not available in the week you ask, and a family in Al Furjan deserves to hear that before paying rather than after. Mathematics and the three sciences at Middle Years and Diploma Standard Level are the easiest to cover. Arabic B, Design Technology, Music and the smaller Higher Level options take longer.

When the specialist for your subject and slot is not free, you get one of three honest answers. Either we offer a different time with the right tutor, or a short wait with a date attached, or we tell you we cannot cover it and you should look elsewhere. We do not substitute a tutor one level below the one your child sits and hope the difference is not noticed, because in Higher Level subjects it is noticed in about two sessions.

Match time for the common subjects is usually a few days rather than a few weeks, and the trial lesson is the test. If the match is wrong, say so after the trial and we will try one more tutor or stop; there is no obligation and no payment taken for the trial. The families who get the best results from this are the ones who treat the trial as an interview rather than a formality.

The one thing that genuinely reduces availability pressure is booking earlier in the year. In January and February, when every Diploma 2 family in Dubai is looking for the same Higher Level specialists at the same evening times, the calendar is the binding constraint. In September it rarely is.

whyPoints.description: The limit on in-home tutoring in Al Furjan is the map. Online, the limit is a calendar, which is a much larger space. For a Chemistry Higher Level or Economics Higher Level student that difference is the difference between a tutor who knows the Internal Assessment criteria and one who knows the topic.
