faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who visits my villa in Al Furjan?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Every lesson we run for UAE families is one-to-one over live video; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. The Dubai market does have visiting tutors, typically at AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, so the option exists if presence in the room is what you need. For Middle Years and Diploma work from an Al Furjan address, online usually gives you a better-matched tutor at a lower rate, because the tutor is chosen from everyone available in UAE evening hours rather than everyone within a twenty-minute drive.

faqs.question: What time do Al Furjan families usually book their tutoring sessions?
faqs.answer: The common band is 17:00 to 19:30 on weekdays. Buses serving the Al Furjan villas arrive between 15:20 and 16:10 depending on the district and the school, and Diploma students travelling to the Al Barsha or Al Khail corridor are often home closer to 17:00. Add thirty minutes to settle and a 17:30 or 18:00 start is realistic for most. Primary children on short Dubai Investments Park runs can start at 15:50. Weekend mornings are the least contested slots in this community and worth asking about if weekday evenings are full.

faqs.question: Which schools do children living in Al Furjan actually attend?
faqs.answer: Three clusters cover most of them. The nearest includes Safa Community School, The Arbor School, Dubai British School Jumeirah Park, Sunmarke School and Arcadia Global School. The southern cluster in Dubai Investments Park and Jebel Ali includes Greenfield International School, Nibras International School, The Winchester School, Delhi Private School Dubai and Jebel Ali School. Families wanting a specific Diploma offer travel north to the Al Barsha and Al Khail corridor. Those schools are named as context for the school run only; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Is online tuition really as effective as a tutor sitting in the room for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For Diploma work, yes, and often better, because what decides the grade is the quality of the subject match rather than physical proximity. A Higher Level session is mostly working through a paper, a mark scheme and an Internal Assessment criterion, all of which share to a screen cleanly. The honest exception is children under eight, who are genuinely easier to hold in a room than on a call. For those families a parent sitting in for the first ten minutes is the practical fix, and short forty-minute sessions work better than long ones.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for IB tutoring from an Al Furjan address?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates, as read in October 2026, run from AED 33 to 150 per hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB specialist. The examiner end of the market reaches AED 650. Monthly packages seen in Dubai include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures from the providers who published them, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: What should an Al Furjan parent ask a tutor about their UAE work permit?
faqs.answer: Ask one direct question: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published. Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor who adds a permit charge to your fee is billing you for an item that has no price.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with the Internal Assessment without crossing an academic honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction is clear. A tutor can read the criteria with your child, question a research question until it is answerable, teach the statistical or practical technique the investigation needs, and give written feedback on your child's own draft against each criterion. A tutor cannot write, rewrite, outline for filling in, or supply content that ends up in the submission. IB Gram tutors state that boundary at the first session of any Internal Assessment block and give feedback in writing, so if the school asks what help was received there is a straight answer.

faqs.question: My child goes to a school in Dubai Investments Park. Does the short bus run help?
faqs.answer: It helps more than most parents realise. Children on Dubai Investments Park and Green Community routes are often home by 15:20 to 15:40, which makes a 15:50 start workable. That matters for primary and early Middle Years students, who concentrate better before dinner than after it, and it means the whole evening is clear afterwards. The trade is at pickup, when the DIP and Green Community school gates queue, so arrival drifts later on fixture days. Book the slot that holds on a bad day rather than a good one.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to take Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the IB in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and states that combined classes are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Tutoring support for these subjects works from the school's own material, since additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma student in this part of Dubai usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session per subject is the normal starting point, and for most students it is enough if it starts in the autumn term. Two sessions a week are worth adding in two situations: when several Internal Assessment deadlines land in the same fortnight, and in the weeks before mocks. Two shorter sessions beat one long one, because the tutor can set work on Monday and check it on Thursday. Families who start in the spring usually need more hours in total than families who started in September, for a worse result.

faqs.question: Does KHDA approve or licence individual private tutors in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, which means school licensing and the annual inspection reports you can read online. Individual tutors are permitted through MoHRE instead. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a separate licence issued to training institutes that operate premises in Dubai, and it is not something a one-to-one tutor holds. IB Gram holds no KHDA approval, accreditation, licence or partnership and does not claim one. Treat any page claiming a KHDA endorsement for individual tutors as describing something that does not exist in that form.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no tutor free for my child's Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You get a straight answer rather than a substitute. Mathematics and the three sciences at Middle Years and Standard Level are usually covered within a few days. Arabic B, Design Technology, Music and the smaller Higher Level options take longer, and in January and February, when every Diploma 2 family in Dubai wants the same evening slots, they can take longer still. If we cannot cover your subject and time we will tell you to look elsewhere. We do not put a tutor one level below your child's on the call and hope nobody notices.

faqs.question: My child is in Middle Years and the report says 4s everywhere. What is actually wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually the criteria rather than the content. The MYP marks criteria A to D in each subject group on an eight-point scale, and a student who understands the material can still sit at a 4 by never doing what the criterion asks. Criterion D in the sciences, the reflection strands in Individuals and Societies and the process journal in Design are the common losses. A diagnostic session that reads one marked task against the criterion usually finds it in forty minutes, which is why we ask for an actual marked piece of work rather than a report card.

faqs.question: Do we need tutoring to get Ministry of Education equivalency for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a Ministry process and tutoring is not a requirement for it. What matters is the subject and grade profile. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at E. For the IB there is no points figure we will publish, because none has been read on a Ministry source. Verify current requirements through the Ministry's own channel before acting.

faqs.question: Can both of my children have sessions on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and running them back to back is what most Al Furjan households do. They are taught separately by different tutors, because a Year 8 Middle Years student and a Diploma 2 student need different subject specialists and different content; a shared session would shortchange both. Consecutive slots mean one quiet room and one device serve the evening, and each child gets their own written session note afterwards. The common pairing we see from this community is a Middle Years sibling at 17:30 and a Diploma sibling at 18:30.

faqs.question: It is already late in the Diploma year. Is there any point starting now?
faqs.answer: There is, but the plan has to change. With eight weeks or less before the May session, the useful work is past papers by component with marked feedback, not fresh content teaching. A good tutor will pick the two or three topics that appear most often in the papers your child loses marks on and drill those, rather than attempting a full syllabus review that cannot be finished. What a late start cannot recover is Internal Assessment marks, which are already submitted. That is the argument for an autumn start next time.

intro.heading: The real question behind an IB home tutor search in Al Garhoud
paragraphs: Al Garhoud is a small, settled neighbourhood wedged between Dubai International Airport, the Creek and Al Garhoud Bridge. It has villas on quiet streets, a golf club, a handful of hotels and a school population that is largely out of the area by 7:30am. When a parent here types an IB home tutor in Al Garhoud into Google, the search looks geographic, and it is not. Nobody wants a tutor because they live nearby. They want one who has taught their child's exact course, and nearby is simply the only filter Google offers.

That matters more in the IB Diploma than in almost any other curriculum, because the Diploma is not one qualification. It is six subjects chosen from six groups, three normally at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. A student doing Chemistry HL, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL and History HL needs three different specialists, and two of those three are genuinely scarce in any single Dubai neighbourhood. A tutor who taught GCSE science for a decade is not a Chemistry HL tutor, and will not know what the HL-only material demands.

So the honest version of the answer runs like this. Within a short drive of Al Garhoud you will find competent generalists, a reasonable number of Mathematics and Physics tutors, fewer Chemistry HL specialists, very few for History HL, Economics HL or a Group 2 language at the right level, and almost nobody who has supervised an Extended Essay to completion. That is not a complaint about Garhoud; it is arithmetic. The IB accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment while the UK curriculum accounts for 37 per cent, so IB-specialist supply is thin everywhere and thinner in a neighbourhood of this size.

IB Gram's answer is to drop the geographic filter entirely. All UAE tuition is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video with screen sharing and a shared whiteboard. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits exist only in our India service. We state it this plainly because the phrase parents search is a home-tutor phrase and nobody should discover the format after paying. In exchange, a Garhoud student is matched against every available specialist for their exact subject and level rather than the subset who will drive over Al Garhoud Bridge at 5pm.

The rest of this page is built to be used rather than read. There is a coverage table that says which IB subjects have real specialist depth and which do not. There is a list of questions to ask a prospective tutor, with the weak and strong answers written out, so a parent can run the test themselves. There is a permit table so you can check the person teaching your child is working legally. There are the Dubai market rates in dirhams with every figure attributed. And there is a plain statement of what a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment, because some of the results in this search sell finished coursework.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-garhoud.programmesIntro: Al Garhoud families touch the IB at three different points, and the tutoring question is different at each. A PYP child needs skills, an MYP child needs criterion literacy, and a Diploma student needs a subject specialist with a mark scheme open.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-based, with no examinations and no subject marks. Reporting is against conceptual understanding and learner profile attributes. Children leave the PYP articulate and used to presenting work, and sometimes under-practised in written fluency and number facts, which is where almost all PYP tutoring requests actually sit.
programmes.countryNote: Garhoud's primary-age children are spread across schools in Oud Metha, Festival City and Al Qusais rather than concentrated in one. PYP requests from this area are mostly about reading age and times tables, and the sensible format is short, frequent, cheerful online sessions rather than a long weekly block.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of 8 for a total of 32, converted to a 1-7 grade. The Personal Project falls in MYP 5. A parent reading an MYP report without the criteria in front of them cannot act on it, which is why the first job here is usually translation rather than teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Several families in this part of old Dubai move into an IB school from an Indian or British middle school, arriving in MYP 3 or 4. The gap is rarely content. It is the shift from marks out of 100 to four criterion descriptors, and from answering questions to designing investigations.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and CAS. Most assessment is external and sat in one session, with internal assessment coursework in every subject. HL papers carry additional content and an extra paper in the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the specialist question bites in Al Garhoud. Deira International School and Universal American School across the water in Festival City run Diploma courses, and students from them typically need two or three different subject specialists at once, plus somebody competent to supervise an Extended Essay process.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-garhoud.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma subjects Al Garhoud families ask about most, with a note on what each one actually assesses and where the marks go missing. Availability differs sharply between them, and the coverage table further down is honest about which.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic, proof-heavy and the usual prerequisite for engineering and economics degrees. HL adds substantial content and a third paper that permits a calculator and rewards sustained multi-step reasoning. Marks are lost on unjustified steps and on the exploration, where students pick a topic too broad to show personal engagement.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics-led, with heavier technology use. It suits students heading for business, design, medicine-adjacent and social science routes, but some universities specify Analysis and Approaches for quantitative degrees. The route decision should be made against named university entry requirements, not against which course looks easier.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The HL course adds depth across organic chemistry, energetics and equilibrium, and HL students sit an extra paper. The common failure is confident recall with weak application: students can define enthalpy and cannot interpret an unfamiliar data set. The internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to generate real quantitative data.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity dominate early, with fields and quantum physics later. Students who arrived from IGCSE often lose marks because they treat an explanation question as a definition question. Written answers must connect a cause to an effect using the correct quantity; practising that phrasing is more productive than re-reading the topic.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy with precise command-term expectations. The difference between outline, explain and evaluate decides several marks per paper. Data-based questions reward careful reading of axes and units, and the internal assessment needs a measurable variable rather than an interesting idea.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries much of the mark: correctly labelled axes, shifted curves, identified areas. HL adds quantitative content and policy depth. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on recent news articles, and students lose marks by summarising the article instead of applying a named diagram and theory to it.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source evaluation, essay structure and knowledge of prescribed topics. HL adds a regional depth study. The internal assessment is a historical investigation with a strict word limit and a required evaluation of sources. This is one of the hardest subjects to find a local specialist for in any single Dubai neighbourhood.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools and frameworks applied to real organisations, with HL adding further content and a pre-seen case study element. Marks go missing when students describe a framework rather than using it to reach a judgement. The internal assessment requires genuine research, which means planning access to information early.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis across literary and non-literary texts, with an individual oral and a written assessment. HL adds a further essay component. The bottleneck is almost always analysis of technique rather than reading comprehension, and it responds quickly to a repeatable paragraph structure built on one device and its effect.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
subjects.description: The TOK exhibition and essay, a 4,000-word Extended Essay in a chosen subject, and CAS. These are supervised in school and are where timelines slip. A tutor may coach planning, question research design and teach referencing, but may not write or draft any part of the submission.

sections.heading: What a search for a tutor near Al Garhoud actually returns
paragraphs: Type the phrase and you get three kinds of result. Agencies that serve all of Dubai and have no particular presence in Garhoud, marketplaces listing independent tutors by distance, and content pages written to rank rather than to inform. Almost none of them tell you the one thing that decides the outcome: whether anybody on their books has taught your child's subject at your child's level and read its current mark scheme.

The distance filter is actively misleading for the IB. A tutor three kilometres away who teaches British curriculum GCSE maths is a worse match for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL than a specialist who is not in Dubai at all, because the HL course includes content and a paper the GCSE teacher has never seen. The same applies in reverse: an excellent Diploma Chemistry tutor is the wrong person for a Year 7 reading problem. Matching on subject and level is the only filter that predicts anything.

The second thing the search hides is the gap between an agency saying yes and a specialist being free. Any agency will take an enquiry for History HL. Fewer can produce someone who has supervised a historical investigation. Asking when the tutor will start, and who specifically, usually separates the two inside one phone call. If the answer is that a tutor will be assigned later, ask for the subject and level they have actually taught before you pay anything.

sections.heading: Ten minutes that tell you whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Parents are asked to judge subject expertise they do not have, which is an unfair test, so here is a fair one. Four questions, each with a weak and a strong answer written out. Any competent IB specialist will answer all four without hesitation. A generalist will be vague on at least three. You do not need to understand the subject to hear the difference.

The questions work because they probe structure rather than content. Anybody can claim to know Chemistry. Only somebody who has taught the Diploma course can tell you how many papers an HL student sits, what the internal assessment is worth, which command terms appear in which paper, and what separates a 5 from a 6 in practice. Ask them during the trial lesson rather than on the phone, and ask the student afterwards whether the tutor used the mark scheme or just explained the topic.

One more test is worth running before you commit. Ask the tutor to mark one page of your child's most recent written work in front of you, out loud, saying what each annotation is worth. A specialist does this comfortably and names the mark scheme language. A generalist corrects spelling and says it looks fine. That single exercise has saved more Garhoud families a wasted term than any review page.

If a tutor declines to be asked these questions, that is itself the answer. A specialist is usually pleased to be asked, because it is the first time anybody has treated their expertise as a thing with content. Run the questions during the free trial rather than over the phone, where anybody can sound convincing, and write the answers down so you can compare two tutors honestly a week apart.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not informal work, and most parents do not know this. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Anybody who tells you a permit costs money, or that permits are optional, is wrong on a point of fact you can verify on u.ae in a minute.

Eligibility is broad rather than narrow. The published categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service listing is issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. A tutor who has not heard of it has not looked.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount you see quoted online is unverified and should be ignored. Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it requires a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute. IB Gram is not KHDA licensed, holds no such permit, and does not operate premises in the UAE, which is why you will not see that claim anywhere on this site.

Abu Dhabi adds a rule reported in the local press and worth knowing even in Dubai: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from providing paid tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. If a tutor offers to teach your child privately while teaching them at school, that is a question to take to the school, not a convenience.

sections.heading: What you are buying when you pay a travel premium
paragraphs: A parent can check almost all of this for themselves, which is the point of publishing it. Search any two Dubai tutoring providers and compare their advertised monthly packages: online blocks appear around AED 799 for eight sessions, while in-home monthly packages of four two-hour sessions appear at roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799. Same number of contact hours, double the money. The difference is not the teaching. It is a car crossing Al Garhoud Bridge twice.

Hourly figures tell the same story and are easy to verify against the sources. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both online, both generally generalist. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors as high as AED 500. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the named or examiner-level end. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

Those are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices, and they are listed here so a Garhoud parent can tell a fair quote from an inflated one. Our own model is a free trial lesson first, one per subject before any payment, then a written quote against a plan — because Mathematics SL for one term and Chemistry HL through a final year are not the same commitment and should not carry the same number.

The useful conclusion is not that in-home tutoring is bad value. It is that the travel premium buys proximity, and proximity is the one variable that does not affect how well a Diploma subject is taught. Spend the same money on a better-matched specialist and the hour does more.

sections.heading: Why proximity stopped being the useful constraint
paragraphs: Ten years ago a tutor had to be local because the lesson needed a table. That constraint is gone, and what replaced it is better suited to the IB than the old arrangement ever was. A shared screen shows the marked paper, the mark scheme and the student's working at the same time. Annotations are saved, so the next session starts from the last one rather than from memory. A past paper can be opened mid-sentence. None of that happens around a kitchen table with a single printed sheet.

The operational gains matter as much as the pedagogical ones in this part of Dubai. A session does not depend on airport-road traffic. An illness moves a slot by a day instead of losing it. A family travelling over a long weekend can keep the session. A student who finishes an examination at 11am can take a lesson at noon. For Diploma students in a final year, where missing two weeks of a cumulative subject is genuinely costly, that reliability is worth more than a tutor's postcode.

The trade is real and should be stated. A young child may focus less well on a screen. A household with no quiet corner finds it harder. A student who needs physical apparatus handled for them cannot have that online. For those cases in-home tutoring is the better choice, and a Garhoud family can find it in the market at the rates published above. IB Gram simply does not sell it here, because home visits are part of our India service and not a UAE one.
For a Diploma student choosing between a specialist on a screen and a generalist at the table, though, there is not much of an argument. The subject is the constraint. Everything else is logistics.

sections.heading: The Diploma subjects where a generalist genuinely cannot help
paragraphs: Some IB subjects can be taught adequately by a strong graduate who reads the syllabus carefully. Others cannot, and it is worth being specific about which, because this is exactly where a local-only search fails a Garhoud family.

Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the clearest case. The HL course includes material and an extra paper that no British A-Level or IGCSE teacher will have taught, and the internal assessment demands a topic with enough mathematical substance to show genuine personal engagement without exceeding what the student can actually handle. A tutor who has not read HL exploration criteria will approve a topic that cannot score well, and the student discovers this months later.

History HL is the second. It requires knowledge of prescribed subjects and world history topics, source evaluation under timed conditions, and a historical investigation with a strict word limit and a required source evaluation section. A generalist can improve essay writing in general and cannot teach the specific structures the papers reward. Economics HL is similar in a different way: the diagrams are the marks, and a tutor who draws them imprecisely teaches a student to lose marks neatly.

Group 2 languages are the quiet problem. Students are placed in a phase or a course level rather than a year group, and a tutor who teaches the language fluently but does not know the assessment at that level will drill vocabulary the student does not need. Ask any prospective language tutor which course and level they have taught, and what the oral component requires, before anything else. The same caution applies to Extended Essay supervision, which is a process skill rather than a subject one and is the single most commonly over-promised service in this market.
bullets: Mathematics AA HL: extra paper, extra content, exploration criteria a generalist has not read
History HL: prescribed topics, timed source work, a word-limited investigation
Economics HL: diagram precision is the mark scheme
Group 2 languages: level and oral format matter more than fluency

sections.heading: Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the line a tutor cannot cross
paragraphs: In this search result you will find at least one operation selling completed Internal Assessments. A family should know what that is before they consider it: under IB rules it is malpractice, the investigation falls on the student, and the possible outcome is the loss of the Diploma. The website that took the payment faces nothing. That asymmetry is the whole reason to be clear about where legitimate help stops.

What a tutor may do is substantial. They may teach the subject content the assessment rests on. They may help a student narrow a research question until it is answerable. They may explain the assessment criteria, read them with the student, and mark a completed draft against them. They may teach referencing and show how to acknowledge a source. They may question a method, point out that a data set will not support a conclusion, and insist on a timeline. They may teach the student how to write a reflection that identifies a decision and its consequence.

What a tutor may not do is write, draft, edit to completion or produce any part of the submission, supply data the student did not collect, or dictate sentences for transcription. The practical test is whether the student can explain, unprompted, why every sentence and every decision is in the work. If they cannot, it should not be there. Any tutor who offers more than this is offering your child a risk disguised as a service.

Stated positively: the help worth paying for is the help that transfers. A student taught to evaluate their own data against a criterion can do it in the next assessment, in the Extended Essay, and at university. A student handed a finished piece has bought one grade and learned nothing, and has an inconsistency sitting on their record.

sections.heading: KHDA, MoE equivalency, and what Garhoud parents should plan for early
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Across the other emirates the map is different: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there; Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the regulator does more than inspect.

The number worth knowing is scale. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, American at 14 per cent and the IB at 7 per cent. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, and seven new private schools were confirmed for that intake, three of them IB, adding 16,846 places.

The thing Garhoud families most often leave too late is equivalency. For students on a British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires passes in five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently ranking states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong; the published rule is five. On the American track, English proficiency can be shown with a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the IB there is no points threshold published in the source above, so no figure appears here. Confirm the IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before planning around it. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring service performs or can promise, and tutoring is not required for it.

process.description: The review point is the next marked paper or assessment, not a fixed number of weeks. If the grade moved, we keep going or change the target. If it did not, we change the tutor or the approach and tell you which we think is the problem.

whyPoints.description: The permit table exists so you can verify the person teaching your child is working legally. The private tuition permit is free and runs two years, so there is no reason for a legitimate tutor to be unable to show one.

whyPoints.description: We teach, question, mark and coach process. We do not write or draft internal assessments, Extended Essays or TOK work, and the section above states exactly where the line sits. In a search result containing sellers of finished coursework, that is worth reading first.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB specialist near Al Garhoud who knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics and the sciences at Standard Level, usually yes somewhere in east Dubai. For Mathematics AA HL, History HL, Economics HL or a Group 2 language at the right level, often not within a sensible drive of Al Garhoud, because the IB accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private enrolment and specialist supply follows enrolment. That is why we match online on subject and level instead of on distance. If nobody suitable is free we say so and give a realistic date rather than substituting a tutor who has taught a different qualification.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send someone to our villa in Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson runs online, one-to-one, over live video with screen sharing and a shared whiteboard. Home visits are part of our India service and are not offered anywhere in the UAE. We say this in the first paragraph because the phrase most parents search is a home-tutor phrase, and the format should never be a surprise after payment. In-home tutoring does exist in the Dubai market at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, so a family who needs that format can find it; we simply are not the provider of it.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a tutor really knows the IB course?
faqs.answer: Ask four things. How many papers does my child sit in this subject at this level. What is the internal assessment worth and what must it contain. Which command terms cost marks most often. What separates a 5 from a 6 in practice. A specialist answers all four precisely; a generalist is vague on at least three. Then ask them to mark one page of your child's work aloud, saying what each annotation is worth. Mark-scheme language means they have marked before. Spelling corrections and reassurance mean they have not.

faqs.question: Should I ask an Al Garhoud tutor to show me a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing with a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, you should disregard any specific amount quoted online.

faqs.question: Can my child's own schoolteacher tutor them privately for extra money?
faqs.answer: Be careful. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction on serving students affiliated with the tutor's school. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify the current policy. Beyond the rules, there is an obvious conflict in paying the person who sets and marks your child's assessments. If the teaching is not working at school, the first conversation belongs with the school.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay an IB tutor in old Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market figures read in October 2026: budget online generalists advertise from around AED 33 to 65 an hour, qualified subject tutors online AED 150 to 300, IB specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home visits AED 180 to 500 including travel, and premium named tutors up to AED 650. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 for budget weekly sessions, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Those are market rates, not ours; we quote after a free trial against a written plan.

faqs.question: Why is a travel premium of AED 100 an hour not worth paying?
faqs.answer: Because it buys proximity, and proximity does not affect how well Chemistry HL is taught. Compare two advertised Dubai packages and the arithmetic is visible: online blocks appear at roughly AED 799 a month for eight sessions, in-home monthly packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. The same contact hours cost about double. If a family genuinely needs a tutor in the room, that premium is reasonable. If the reason is habit, the same money spent on a better-matched specialist buys considerably more teaching.

faqs.question: My child does Maths AA HL and Chemistry HL. Do we need two tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly. Those are two separate syllabuses with separate papers, separate internal assessments and separate failure modes, and very few people teach both at Higher Level credibly. Two specialists on two evenings is the normal arrangement, with one written plan covering both so the total workload stays visible. This is exactly the request a distance-based search handles badly, because the chance of finding both specialisms within a short drive of Al Garhoud at the same time is low.

faqs.question: What is the Extended Essay and how much can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: It is an independent piece of research of up to 4,000 words in a subject the student chooses, supervised in school and assessed externally. A tutor may help narrow the research question, teach research method and referencing, read the assessment criteria with the student, question whether the evidence supports the argument, and hold the student to a timeline. A tutor may not write, draft or edit the essay to completion, and may not supply material the student then presents as their own. Most Extended Essays fail on timeline rather than on ability, so the coaching that matters is scheduling.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Higher Level and Standard Level in practice?
faqs.answer: They are different syllabuses rather than the same course at two speeds. HL carries additional content, more teaching hours, and in several subjects an extra examination paper. Internal assessment requirements can also differ in scope. The practical consequence for tutoring is that an SL specialist is not automatically an HL one, and a tutor who has only taught SL will not know what the HL-only topics demand. Ask specifically which level a prospective tutor has taught, and do not accept the subject name alone as the answer.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor start if our deadline is in three weeks?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics or a science at Standard Level, usually within a few days. For Mathematics AA HL or a Group 4 subject at Higher Level, up to a week. For History, Psychology or a language at the right level, two weeks or more is realistic, which may be after your deadline. We will say that rather than start a match we cannot complete. If the deadline cannot move, a short diagnostic block with an available generalist can sometimes stabilise examination technique while the specialist search continues.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Garhoud students mostly attend?
faqs.answer: Al Mawakeb School Al Garhoud sits inside the area, and a large share of older students cross the Creek to Dubai Festival City for Deira International School or Universal American School, both of which carry IB Diploma provision. Others travel to Oud Metha for schools such as The Indian High School Dubai, St Mary's Catholic High School or Dubai Gem Private School, or east to Al Qusais for The Millennium School Dubai and Westminster School Dubai. These names are local context only; we have no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: What time do lessons realistically start for a Garhoud family?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school rather than the home. A child at Al Mawakeb School Al Garhoud is home quickly and can start at 4pm. A child crossing to Dubai Festival City arrives closer to 3:45pm or 4:15pm on a normal day, which makes 5pm the safer slot. Families commuting from Al Qusais or Oud Metha through the airport road at peak usually settle on 5:30pm or 6pm. Because sessions are online, the slot can be set to the real arrival time and changed permanently if the route changes.

faqs.question: What does UAE Ministry of Education equivalency require for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: On the British track the published requirement is passes in five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. One currently ranking competitor page states six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. For the IB there is no points figure in that source, so confirm it on moe.gov.ae before planning around it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment without risking malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the underlying content, help narrow a research question, explain and mark against the assessment criteria, teach referencing, challenge a method that will not produce usable data, and enforce a timeline. A tutor may not write, draft or edit the work to completion, supply data the student did not collect, or dictate sentences. The working test is whether the student can explain any sentence or decision in the submission without prompting. At least one site in this search sells finished internal assessments; that is malpractice and the consequence lands on the student.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor is not the right fit?
faqs.answer: Say so early rather than waiting for a report. Fit problems usually show in the first two or three sessions and are often about pace or manner rather than expertise. We will change the tutor and say whether we think the mismatch was personality, level or subject, because the three need different replacements. The written plan exists partly for this reason: if the target criterion or paper technique has not moved by the review point, the plan itself is evidence about whether the approach or the person was the problem.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-garhoud.closingHeading: Ask for the name and the level before you pay anything
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-garhoud.closingBody: The single most useful thing a Garhoud parent can do is refuse to book a tutor who has not been named, with the subject and level they have actually taught stated out loud. Send us the subject, the level, the year and the next deadline, and you will get either a named specialist or an honest no with a date. The first lesson is free, one per subject, taken before any payment, and it is best spent running the four questions on this page with your child's most recent marked work on screen. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-habtoor-city.tutorsIntro: These are the Diploma Programme specialists most requested by families living on the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor: Maths AA and AI, the three sciences, Economics and English A. Each teaches one subject group properly rather than every subject vaguely.

intro.heading: Start with the syllabus, not the search radius
paragraphs: A search for an IB home tutor in Al Habtoor City is a search for proximity, but proximity is not the variable that decides a Diploma Programme grade. The variable is whether the person sitting with your child has taught the exact course on the exact syllabus, and can name the component weightings without looking them up. A Maths Analysis and Approaches Higher Level student sits three papers and an exploration; Paper 3 alone carries twenty per cent of the grade and has no equivalent at Standard Level. A tutor who has never set a Paper 3 question will teach the first two papers well and leave a fifth of the grade untouched.

Al Habtoor City sits on Sheikh Zayed Road between Business Bay and Al Safa, three residential towers above a hotel and theatre complex, with the Dubai Water Canal on one side and Safa Park across the road. It is a dense, vertical, professional neighbourhood. The children living in it attend schools scattered from Al Safa and Jumeirah through to Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, which means the house next door may hold a student on a completely different curriculum. Local tutor supply therefore tells you very little about local demand, and a tutor two minutes away is still the wrong tutor if they teach Mathematics Applications and your child is sitting Analysis.

IB Gram answers the question honestly. Tutoring for families here is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the past paper open on screen. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; door-to-door home tutoring is a service we run only in India. That is not a workaround. It is what lets a family in a Sheikh Zayed Road tower book a Chemistry Higher Level specialist who has marked the Reactivity topics for years, instead of the best available teacher within a twenty-minute drive at five o'clock on a weekday.

What follows is built the way a subject teacher would build it. The second section lays out the Diploma Programme assessment architecture component by component, with Standard and Higher Level weightings side by side. The third does the same for command terms, because the command term is the mark scheme: a question that says 'outline' and a question that says 'evaluate' want different paragraphs, and students lose marks on perfectly correct physics by answering the wrong verb. After that come the subject-level failure modes, what tutoring costs in this market in AED with each figure attributed, how past papers should actually be used, and where the academic-honesty line sits on an Internal Assessment.

Prices are quoted as the market, never as a promise. Published rates on the Dubai market run from roughly AED 45 an hour for a university-student tutor working online to AED 650 for a named premium specialist, and the spread tells you more about who is teaching than about the quality of the teaching. Those numbers are in the rate table below with the provider that published each one, so you can check them yourself rather than take our word for any of it.

The 2025 science courses: Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44%, Scientific Investigation at 20%

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-habtoor-city.programmesIntro: Students in the Al Habtoor City towers come through the three IB programmes in sequence, and the syllabus demands change sharply at each handover. What a tutor needs to know differs completely between a PYP enquiry unit, an MYP criterion and a DP paper.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Marked out of 45, with 24 the conditional pass. Each subject carries internally assessed work worth 20% to 30% and externally marked papers for the rest. The grade a student finishes with is mostly decided by how precisely they answer the command term in front of them, which is why syllabus-specific teaching matters more here than in any earlier programme.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students sit the May session, which is the one the emirate's schools build their calendars around. The November session functions as a resit and a route for students arriving mid-cycle. Teaching for Al Habtoor City families is scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, typically between 16:00 and 21:00 on weekdays, so a session fits after the Business Bay or Al Safa school run rather than competing with it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria worth eight marks apiece, so 32 marks convert through published boundaries into a 1-7 grade. There is no end-of-course paper unless a school opts into eAssessment. The Personal Project in MYP 5 is marked across three criteria out of 24. Tutoring here is criterion work: knowing what Criterion C in Sciences actually rewards is worth more than extra content coverage.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving the Jumeirah and Al Safa catchment run MYP to year 5 and then split students between the Diploma Programme and IGCSE, which makes MYP 4 the year the decision quietly gets made. Families in the Al Habtoor City towers often ask for MYP support precisely at that point, to keep both routes open.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent research piece with a supervisor; the TOK course produces a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title plus a 950-word exhibition commentary. Together the Extended Essay and TOK essay contribute up to three points on the 45-point scale. Both are student-owned work, so support is process coaching: question framing, source discipline, structure and feedback on drafts the student has written.
programmes.countryNote: Extended Essay supervision inside Dubai schools varies by department, and students in the Jumeirah cluster regularly arrive with a research question too broad to answer in 4,000 words. Narrowing it is the single highest-value hour of coaching available, and it has to happen early in the first DP year rather than in the term the essay is due.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-habtoor-city.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma Programme subjects families on the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor request most, with the part of each course where marks are genuinely won or lost rather than a general description of the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a graphic display calculator and punishes shaky algebra; Paper 2 allows one and punishes shaky calculator technique. At Higher Level, Paper 3 presents two extended investigative problems worth 20% of the grade. Proof by induction, complex numbers and the Maclaurin series are where Higher Level students most often stall.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Heavier on statistics, modelling and technology use than Analysis. Chi-squared tests, regression and confidence intervals recur. Students lose marks by reporting calculator output without interpreting it, and by failing to state hypotheses and conclusions in the terms the mark scheme asks for.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised into Structure 1-3 and Reactivity 1-3. Energetics calculations, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most dropped marks. Paper 1 is 36% of the grade and Paper 2 is 44%, with the Scientific Investigation making up the remaining 20% across both levels.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E, from space, time and motion through to nuclear and quantum physics. Uncertainty propagation, graph gradients with units and the long structured questions on Paper 2 are the recurring weak points. Higher Level content sits inside the same themes rather than in a separate add-on section.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Built on the unity-and-diversity and form-and-function themes at four levels of organisation. Students who revise by memorising definitions tend to fail the application questions, which ask them to read unfamiliar data and apply a named process to it rather than recall it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries, each 800 words, built on recent news articles and worth 30% at Standard Level. Diagram accuracy with fully labelled axes carries real marks, and Higher Level Paper 3 is a quantitative paper that rewards practice rather than reading.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen guided textual analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works, plus the Individual Oral on a global issue. Higher Level adds a 1,200-1,500 word essay. Students lose marks by summarising content instead of analysing how the writer's choices produce an effect.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as the Ansoff matrix and the business canvas are examinable, not decorative. Case-study papers reward candidates who apply a named tool to the specific firm in front of them. Quantitative elements, including break-even and investment appraisal at Higher Level, are frequently under-practised.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, with research methods threaded through all three. Marks turn on precise use of named studies as evidence for a specific claim, and at Higher Level on the extended response questions that demand a counter-argument.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, so support has to be matched to the correct stream rather than to the subject name.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-habtoor-city.regionsIntro: Al Habtoor City sits inside a stretch of Dubai where the school catchments overlap heavily. These are the neighbouring communities whose families book the same Diploma Programme specialists, with the detail that changes how a session is scheduled.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Immediately inland across the Dubai Water Canal, and the nearest Red Line metro station to the Al Habtoor City towers. Students here often finish the school day late because of the canal-side traffic, which pushes a first realistic session start towards 17:00.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: Directly across Sheikh Zayed Road, villa stock and the catchment for several long-established British-curriculum schools. A short physical hop that can still cost twenty minutes at the Safa interchange on a weekday afternoon.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: Low-rise and residential, feeding the same Jumeirah school cluster. Families here frequently run two children on different curricula, so sessions get stacked back to back in one evening rather than spread across the week.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: Coastal, older villa communities, closest to the Jumeirah school strip. Pick-up is early relative to Al Barsha schools, which makes a 16:00 start workable here when it is not elsewhere in the cluster.

regions.name: Jumeirah 3

sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in Al Habtoor City is really asking
paragraphs: The phrase means: find somebody competent, soon, who can teach my child the course they are sitting without the family having to drive anywhere. Two of those three requirements have nothing to do with geography. The third is a request to remove travel from the arrangement, and a live video lesson removes it more completely than a tutor who still has to reach Sheikh Zayed Road through a weekday evening.

What a parent is buying is subject depth. The Diploma Programme is six courses sat at two different levels with a different assessment structure in almost every subject group, which means a tutor who is genuinely strong in Chemistry Higher Level is usually not the same person who is strong in Maths Applications. Hiring on proximity forces a compromise on exactly the thing that decides the grade. Hiring on subject, which online delivery makes possible, does not.

The honest position is this. IB Gram matches students in Al Habtoor City with Diploma Programme subject specialists and teaches them one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. The comparison table in the pricing section below sets the two formats against each other on cost, travel and tutor pool so you can judge the trade rather than take it on trust.

The rest of this page is syllabus. If you already know which component is failing, skip to it. If you do not, the architecture section tells you how to find out: look at the weightings, look at the last two internal grades, and work out which component is holding the aggregate down. That single calculation usually identifies the problem faster than any diagnostic test.

sections.heading: The Diploma Programme assessment architecture, component by component
paragraphs: Every Diploma Programme subject splits its grade between externally marked papers and internally assessed work, and the split is published. A parent who knows the split can see immediately where the hours should go. A student sitting Chemistry at either level carries 20% of the final grade in a Scientific Investigation marked out of 24 against four criteria, which means a weak investigation costs more than a weak Paper 1 section.

The table below sets out the components for the subjects most requested along this corridor, with Standard and Higher Level weightings beside each other. Two things usually surprise families. The first is how much of the grade sits in work completed during the course rather than in the examination hall. The second is how different the Higher Level structure can be from Standard Level in the same subject: Maths Higher Level adds a whole extra paper, while English A Higher Level redistributes weight into an additional essay.

Read the table as a budget. If a student has fifteen weeks before the final internal deadline and the investigation is worth a fifth of the grade, then a quarter of the available tutoring hours belongs to that investigation rather than to content revision. Most families discover this too late, after the coursework has been submitted at a mark that caps the grade regardless of how the papers go.

One caution on dates. The Dubai schools in this cluster sit the May session, and the November session functions as a resit route. Specific IB examination and results dates are not published here because they must be confirmed against the official IB source or your child's Diploma Programme coordinator before anybody plans around them.

sections.heading: Command terms are the mark scheme, and most lost marks are command-term errors
paragraphs: A Diploma Programme question is an instruction. The verb at the front tells the examiner what the mark scheme will accept, and a student who writes a beautiful explanation in answer to a question that said 'state' has wasted the paragraph without earning the mark. This is the most fixable category of lost marks in the entire programme, and it is almost never taught explicitly in class because the class is busy covering content.

The pattern is consistent across subjects. 'Outline' wants a brief account with no development; 'explain' wants a reason or mechanism; 'discuss' wants a balanced review that presents more than one position; 'evaluate' wants a judgement supported by evidence and an acknowledged limitation. In the sciences, 'determine' signals that a calculation and a final answer with units are expected, while 'suggest' invites a plausible hypothesis the student is not required to have met before.

The table below lists the terms that recur most in Higher Level papers across the sciences, Maths and Economics, what the examiner is actually looking for, and the failure that costs students marks. The way to use it in a session is mechanical: take a past paper the student has already attempted, circle the command term in each question, then re-mark their answer against the verb rather than against the content. Students typically find two or three marks per paper this way within one session.

This is also where a non-specialist tutor is least useful. Knowing the physics is not the same as knowing that a six-mark 'discuss' question in Paper 2 needs a structure, or that 'compare and contrast' requires similarities and differences explicitly signposted rather than two separate descriptions left side by side for the examiner to reconcile.

sections.heading: Where students on this corridor actually lose marks, subject by subject
paragraphs: Marks are lost in predictable places, and the places differ by subject in ways a parent can check against a returned paper. In Maths Analysis and Approaches, the damage is concentrated in Paper 1, because it is sat without a graphic display calculator and exposes algebraic fluency that the calculator has been quietly covering for all year. A student who scores well on Paper 2 mocks and badly on Paper 1 mocks does not have a topic problem, they have an algebra problem, and the fix is drill rather than reteaching.

In the sciences, two failure modes dominate. The first is uncertainty and graph work: propagating an uncertainty, reading a gradient with correct units, deciding how many significant figures a final answer may legitimately carry. The second is the long structured question in Paper 2, where students know the content but produce answers that collapse under a six-mark command term. In Chemistry specifically, energetics and equilibrium calculations and the organic mechanisms account for a disproportionate share of dropped marks.

In Economics, diagrams are marked. Axes have to be labelled, curves have to be named, the new equilibrium has to be shown rather than described, and the commentary has to connect the diagram to the article it was built on. In English A, the single most common loss is summary masquerading as analysis: a student who retells the text accurately earns very little, while one who explains how a specific choice of structure or register produces an effect on a reader earns the band.

A first session is spent diagnosing which of these is happening rather than teaching anything. The evidence is already in the house: the last two returned papers, the teacher's comments, and the pattern of marks lost by question type. Reading those three together usually identifies the problem inside forty minutes and makes the remaining hours useful instead of general.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs around Sheikh Zayed Road, and who publishes each figure
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for Dubai publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. So here are the market bands in AED with the provider that published each one, read in October 2026. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list: our own quote follows a free trial lesson and depends on subject, level and how many sessions a term actually needs.

Start at the bottom rather than the top, because that is where most families start. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, both drawing largely on university-student tutors. That price buys supervision and homework help. It does not reliably buy somebody who can mark a Higher Level Paper 3 answer against the real mark scheme, and the gap shows up in exam terms rather than in term one.

The middle band is where most Diploma Programme teaching sits. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching AED 500. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour for a premium named tutor.

Monthly figures are often more useful than hourly ones for budgeting. Packages seen on the Dubai market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Set against KHDA's confirmation on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, a tutoring budget is now the part of the education bill a family still controls.

sections.heading: Past papers are a diagnostic instrument, and most students use them as revision
paragraphs: A past paper worked through with the mark scheme beside it tells you precisely which marks a student cannot currently earn. A past paper worked through for practice tells you how the student feels about the subject. The difference between the two is whether anybody reads the result properly, and this is the single biggest change a good tutor makes to how a student revises.

The method is unglamorous. Sit the paper under timed conditions. Mark it against the published scheme without generosity. Sort every lost mark into one of four causes: the content was not known, the content was known but the command term was misread, the method was right and the execution slipped, or time ran out. Those four causes need four completely different responses, and treating them all as 'needs more revision' is why months of work sometimes move a grade by nothing.

Time pressure deserves separate attention because it is the cause students least often name. If the final third of a Paper 2 is consistently thin while the first third is strong, the problem is pacing and the fix is a timing protocol rather than more content. For Higher Level Maths Paper 3, where two extended problems carry 20% of the grade, pacing is most of the skill: a student who spends forty minutes on the first problem has already lost the second.

A note on materials. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are copyright and are not reproduced or distributed by IB Gram. Sessions work from the official sources your child's school already provides, from the subject guides their teachers issue, and from questions written for the session, with the official syllabus pages linked rather than copied.
bullets: Sit it timed, mark it strictly, then classify every lost mark

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor may not cross on an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This matters more in this market than almost anything else on the page, because the search results for Dubai IB help include operators selling finished Internal Assessments outright. One such site advertises completed IAs for several thousand dirhams. Buying one is academic misconduct under IB rules and puts the student's whole diploma at risk, not just one subject grade.

The boundary is clear and it is worth stating in plain terms. A tutor may teach the criteria, explain what each one rewards, discuss a proposed research question, point out where a method will not generate usable data, show the student how to mark their own draft against the published descriptors, and give written feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor may not write any part of the exploration, the investigation, the essay or the commentary, may not supply text to be pasted in, and may not edit a draft into a finished state on the student's behalf.

In practice the most valuable honest help arrives before any writing happens. Most weak Scientific Investigations are weak because the research design could never produce enough data to analyse, and that is visible in ten minutes to somebody who has read the criteria. Most weak Extended Essays are weak because the question is too broad for 4,000 words. Fixing either of those is teaching, it is fully permitted, and it moves more marks than any amount of polishing at the end.

Supervision also sits with the school, not with us. Your child's Internal Assessment and Extended Essay are signed off by their teacher and coordinator, who confirm the work is the student's own. Anything a tutor does has to survive that conversation unchanged, and we work on the assumption that it will be checked.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and what they do to a DP timetable
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi has its own authority in ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram holds no permit, licence or accreditation from any of these bodies and claims none.

The part that directly affects a Diploma Programme timetable is the mandatory subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the two groups. Combined classes are prohibited.

Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that no mandatory subject lesson should run shorter than 25 minutes. Using different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry of Education permission is not allowed, which is why support in these streams has to follow the school's own material rather than an alternative syllabus. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education are required to hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects.

The practical consequence for a family in Al Habtoor City is that a Diploma Programme week already carries more timetabled hours than the six-subject model suggests, which is why a tutoring slot has to be placed carefully rather than squeezed in. It is also why two sessions a week is a heavier commitment in Dubai than the same two sessions would be elsewhere, and why most families here start with one and add the second only in an exam term.
