faqs.question: Can I actually get an IB home tutor in Al Habtoor City who comes to the tower?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and door-to-door home tutoring is a service we run only in India. In-home tutors do work on this corridor independently, and the Dubai market prices those visits at roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour according to Bestimate's rate table, with some independent tutors charging up to AED 500. What you give up by booking a visit is choice: your options narrow to whoever can reach Sheikh Zayed Road on a weekday evening, which rarely includes a specialist in the exact subject and level your child is sitting.

faqs.question: How do I know whether a tutor really knows my child's IB syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions before you book. First, what are the component weightings for this subject at this level? A specialist answers without hesitating. Second, how many marks is the internally assessed piece worth and what are its criteria called? For the sciences the answer is 24 marks across four criteria; for a Maths exploration it is 20 marks across five. Third, what is the difference between a question that says 'outline' and one that says 'evaluate'? A tutor who cannot separate those two will teach content well and lose marks on the paper anyway.

faqs.question: Which IB component should we spend the tutoring hours on first?
faqs.answer: Work it out from the weightings rather than from how the student feels. Take the last two internal grades per component, multiply each by its published weight, and find which component is pulling the aggregate down hardest. If a Scientific Investigation is worth 20% of a science grade and the draft is sitting mid-band, that single piece of coursework outweighs several topics of content revision. Most families discover this after submission, when the mark has already capped the grade, which is exactly the wrong time to find out.

faqs.question: My child scores well in Maths mocks on Paper 2 but badly on Paper 1. Why?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 is sat without a graphic display calculator and Paper 2 is not, so a gap between them is almost always algebraic fluency rather than a topic gap. The calculator has been quietly covering for shaky manipulation all year, and Paper 1 removes the cover. The fix is drill on algebraic technique under timed conditions, not reteaching the topics, and it moves faster than most parents expect because the underlying understanding is usually already there. A diagnostic first session looking at the two mock papers side by side will show this within about forty minutes.

faqs.question: What does IB tutoring cost per hour for a family on Sheikh Zayed Road?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget online end, where EdFlik and Tutopiya both operate, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level rates sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and BartyED advertises AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are market figures with sources, not our price list. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, based on subject, level and the number of sessions a term genuinely needs.

faqs.question: Is a cheap online tutor at AED 50 an hour worth trying first?
faqs.answer: It depends what you need. At that price you are generally buying a university-student tutor who can supervise homework, keep a routine and recap content, and for a student who is simply not sitting down to work that may be exactly the problem solved. What it does not reliably buy is somebody who can mark a Higher Level answer against the real scheme or restructure a failing Internal Assessment. The usual pattern is that the gap stays invisible through term one and appears in the first set of mock results, which is an expensive way to learn it.

faqs.question: How many marks is the DP Scientific Investigation worth and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: In the current Chemistry, Physics and Biology courses the Scientific Investigation is worth 20% of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level, and it is marked out of 24 across four equally weighted criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The report has a 3,000-word limit. The most common reason an investigation underperforms is a research design that could never generate enough usable data, which is a problem of planning rather than writing, and it is visible to anybody who has read the criteria before the student starts collecting.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with their IB Internal Assessment legally?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach the criteria, explain what each one rewards, challenge a research question, point out a method that will not produce analysable data, show the student how to mark a draft against the published descriptors, and give written feedback on work the student wrote. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply text to be inserted, or edit a draft into a finished state. Operators in this market do sell completed assessments; buying one is misconduct under IB rules and risks the whole diploma rather than one subject grade.

faqs.question: Do private tutors visiting Al Habtoor City need a permit, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold one; the official route is the MoHRE private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: Which exam session will my child in Al Habtoor City sit?
faqs.answer: Dubai schools build their Diploma Programme calendars around the May session, and the November session exists as a resit route and a path for students joining mid-cycle. Specific IB examination and results dates are deliberately not published on this page: the official IB source blocks automated checking, so any date here would be unverified, and an unverified date a family plans around is worse than no date. Confirm the window with your child's Diploma Programme coordinator or on the official IB assessment pages before booking travel or scheduling a revision block around it.

faqs.question: How does an online session work when the subject needs diagrams and working?
faqs.answer: Through a shared whiteboard, with the student writing and the tutor annotating in the same space, which is closer to sitting side by side at a table than most parents expect. A past paper is open on screen, the student works through a question in real time, and the tutor marks the attempt against the scheme as it appears. Sessions are recorded, so a derivation can be rewatched the night before a test. For the sciences, data, graphs and uncertainty calculations are worked on the same shared surface rather than described.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for a niche Higher Level subject at an Al Habtoor City address?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we give you an expected date rather than filling the slot. Thin cover shows up most in the smaller Higher Level subjects and in particular language combinations, and a tutor learning the syllabus alongside your child is worse than waiting two weeks for the right one. Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, a specialist elsewhere in our network teaches the session on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before you book rather than after. A disclosed gap costs us a booking; an undisclosed one costs a student a term.

faqs.question: Can Al Habtoor City sessions move to post-Iftar timings during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most households in this cluster that works better than the usual slot. School hours shorten, afternoons are used differently and concentration in the late afternoon drops, so a session that normally runs at 17:00 is often more productive after Iftar. We reset the timetable for the month and move it back afterwards. The same flexibility applies to mock weeks and internal deadline crunches, when families frequently pause weekly sessions entirely for a fortnight and resume once the school's own assessment calendar clears.

faqs.question: Does my child still need Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the IB?
faqs.answer: In a Dubai private school, yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required alongside the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's current requirements were to be in place from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in those subjects because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is counted in 40-minute units. Support in these streams has to follow the school's own material, since using different or additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough for a Higher Level subject in Al Habtoor City?
faqs.answer: For most students in a non-exam term, yes, provided the hour is used for diagnosis and correction rather than re-delivering the lesson. One properly marked past-paper section a week, with the lost marks classified and the specific weakness drilled, outperforms two hours of general review. In an exam term or when a major internally assessed piece is due, families here commonly add a second session for a defined block of weeks and then drop back. Starting with one and adding later is also the cheaper way to find out what is actually needed.

intro.heading: What "knows the IB" has to mean before you hire anyone
paragraphs: Every tutoring advertisement in Dubai says it covers the IB. The claim is almost never tested, and it is easy to test. Ask three questions. Which criteria is the Internal Assessment in this subject marked against, and how many marks does each carry? What is the word limit on the Theory of Knowledge essay, and what is the Theory of Knowledge exhibition commentary limit? How are the three core points awarded between the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge? A tutor who teaches the Diploma regularly answers all three without pausing. A strong general tutor who has read a syllabus summary does not.

This matters more in the IB than in a linear examined course, because a meaningful share of the grade in every subject is internally assessed against published criteria, and the core carries three points of its own. A tutor can be excellent at the physics and still be no use on the Internal Assessment, because the Internal Assessment is marked on personal engagement, exploration, analysis, evaluation and communication rather than on physics alone. That is the specific gap families in Al Jaddaf run into, and it shows up two months before a deadline.

On the home-tutoring question, the honest answer first. Home tuition in Dubai exists and is priced accordingly. Published in-home one-to-one rates run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions appear in the market. A noticeable share of that premium is the tutor's travel, and Al Jaddaf sits on a road network that funnels through Dubai Healthcare City, the Creek crossings and Al Khail Road.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Jaddaf or anywhere else in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time; sending tutors into homes is a service we run only in India. We state that before the price table rather than after it, because a family reading this deserves to know what they are choosing between. The argument for our model is not that it is cheaper. It is that an Al Jaddaf student needing a Chemistry Higher Level specialist with Internal Assessment experience gets one, rather than the best available tutor who can reach the building by five o'clock.

Al Jaddaf itself is a useful place to make this argument, because the neighbourhood is compact and its school options are not. Swiss International Scientific School Dubai sits inside the district. The rest of the IB provision Al Jaddaf families use is spread across Dubai Festival City, Sobha Hartland, Nad Al Sheba and further out, which means households minutes apart are following different timetables and different subject combinations. No local tutor pool maps onto that spread.

The sections below give the things a parent can actually check: what each of the six subject groups demands, the word and page limits across the core components, where IB marks are lost in ways nobody warns about, what the regulators do and do not certify, and where the academic honesty line sits on an Extended Essay. No IB exam or results dates appear here, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than none.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.programmesIntro: Al Jaddaf families reach us at three points in the IB continuum, and the work differs sharply between them. These are the programmes we cover.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus a core of the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Forty-two points come from the six subjects at a maximum of seven each, and up to three more from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination, for a maximum of 45.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the main May session. No IB session or results date appears on this page: the IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and an unverified exam date is something a family would plan a term around. Your school's IB coordinator holds the authoritative calendar, including the internal deadlines for Extended Essay and Internal Assessment drafts, which matter more to a tutoring plan than the external dates do.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and converted to a grade from one to seven using school boundaries. Most years carry no external examination, so the grade is built entirely from classroom tasks, and the Personal Project arrives in the final year.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the mandatory UAE subjects run alongside this. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, calculating instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. Al Jaddaf families should count those periods into the week before adding evening commitments.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led framework rather than a content syllabus, with transdisciplinary units and an exhibition in the final year. Tutoring at this stage is about underlying literacy and numeracy fluency rather than about the programme itself, and short targeted blocks usually beat ongoing weekly arrangements.
programmes.countryNote: The most useful request we get from Al Jaddaf primary families is bridging work for a child who has moved into an IB school from a different system mid-year, where the gap is usually in written fluency rather than in mathematics. A handful of sessions on writing stamina and reading comprehension does more than a term of general support.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: EE, TOK and CAS
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is an independent research essay with a 4,000-word limit. Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an essay on a prescribed title with a 1,600-word limit and an exhibition of three objects with a commentary limited to 950 words. Creativity, Activity, Service is not graded but must be completed for the Diploma to be awarded.
programmes.countryNote: The core is where Al Jaddaf families most often ask for help and where the honesty line is tightest. A tutor may discuss a research question, explain what a criterion rewards, and comment on the student's own draft. A tutor may not produce the essay, restructure it to a standard, or supply the argument. Providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments; that is an IB malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the candidate.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Al Jaddaf families ask for most. Each entry names what the subject actually assesses and the internally assessed component a tutor must know, because that is the component a general tutor cannot cover.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, calculus technique and proof, with induction, complex numbers and the Maclaurin series at Higher Level. Paper 1 is sat without technology. The internally assessed Exploration is worth twenty per cent and is marked on presentation, communication, engagement, reflection and use of mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, regression and hypothesis testing with a graphic display calculator permitted throughout. Marks shift from computation to justification: why this model, what the parameters mean, where it stops holding. The Exploration carries the same twenty per cent and the same five criteria.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, waves, electricity, magnetism, nuclear physics, and additional Higher Level content. The internally assessed investigation requires a student-designed experiment with uncertainty analysis, and the uncertainty treatment is where most marks are lost rather than in the physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, atomic structure, bonding, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, redox and organic chemistry. The investigation is assessed on exploration, analysis, evaluation and communication, and a well-executed experiment with a thin evaluation section scores below a modest one fully evaluated.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cell biology, molecular biology, genetics, ecology, evolution and human physiology, with plant biology and additional systems at Higher Level. Data-based questions on unfamiliar material are the discriminator, and they reward students who read axes and units before reading the question.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and introductory concepts. The internally assessed portfolio requires commentaries on published news articles applying a specific part of the syllabus, and the commonest failure is a commentary that summarises the article rather than analysing it with a diagram.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business organisation, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with the Higher Level extension and a research project. Application to a real organisation decides the marks; generic theory earns knowledge credit and then stops.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis of literary and non-literary texts, with Paper 1 guided analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay. Students lose marks by describing a text's content rather than analysing how its choices create effect.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by an essay on a prescribed title, limited to 1,600 words, and an exhibition of three objects with a commentary limited to 950 words. The essay rewards engagement with the prescribed title as written, and the commonest failure is answering an adjacent question the student found easier.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent research essay in a chosen subject with a 4,000-word limit, supervised in school and assessed on focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation, and engagement. Research question scope decides the outcome before any writing happens.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in Al Jaddaf: the honest version
paragraphs: Home tuition is a real market in Dubai with real prices, so here they are. Published in-home one-to-one rates run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's rate table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions circulate in the market. Against that, a qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. The gap is not a quality gap. A substantial part of it is the tutor's travel time.

For Al Jaddaf specifically, that travel is worth thinking about concretely. The district sits beside Dubai Healthcare City Phase 2 and the Creek, with access funnelling onto a small number of routes that also carry Festival City and Business Bay traffic in the late afternoon. A visiting tutor loses time getting in and time getting out, and both are priced into the hour whether the invoice itemises them or not. The second cost is invisible: the tutor has to be someone whose other families are also within reach, which narrows the pool before subject matching even begins.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Al Jaddaf or anywhere else in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. That is a limit, not a feature we are pretending away. What it buys an Al Jaddaf family is specificity: a Chemistry Higher Level specialist who has marked the investigation against its four criteria, rather than the best tutor who can reach the building before five o'clock.

sections.heading: The six subject groups, and the component a general tutor cannot cover
paragraphs: The Diploma is six subjects, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, drawn from six groups: studies in language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, and the arts. Forty-two of the forty-five points come from those six at a maximum of seven each. The remaining three come from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together. That structure is why a tutoring plan built subject by subject can still miss three points entirely.

Within each subject there is an internally assessed component, and that is the part a strong general tutor typically cannot teach. In mathematics it is the Exploration, worth twenty per cent. In the sciences it is a student-designed investigation assessed on exploration, analysis, evaluation and communication. In economics it is a portfolio of commentaries on published articles. In business management it is a research project. In language and literature it is the individual oral. Each is marked against published criteria that have very little to do with raw subject knowledge.

So the test for an Al Jaddaf family is narrow and easy to apply. Ask a prospective tutor to name the criteria for the internally assessed component in the subject you need, and roughly what each is worth. A tutor who teaches the subject regularly answers immediately. A tutor who does not will talk about the subject instead, which is the moment to keep looking. This single question filters more effectively than any qualification list.
The table sets out what each group assesses internally, because it is the part school information evenings cover least and the part a tutor is most often hired too late to help with.

sections.heading: Word and page limits across the IB, in one place
paragraphs: This is a table nobody in the UAE tutoring market publishes, and it is among the most practically useful things a Diploma parent can have. Limits matter because exceeding them has consequences, and because a student who knows the limit before starting plans differently from one who discovers it with a first draft already written. The Extended Essay is limited to 4,000 words. The Theory of Knowledge essay is limited to 1,600 words. The Theory of Knowledge exhibition commentary is limited to 950 words across three objects.

The practical point is about scope rather than counting. A research question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words is the single commonest Extended Essay failure, and it is visible at the question stage, months before the word count becomes a problem. A student who chose a question needing 9,000 words to do justice spends the final weeks cutting argument rather than improving it, and the criteria reward focus and method heavily. Two hours of question-narrowing work at the start is worth more than twenty hours of editing at the end.

The Theory of Knowledge essay has a different failure shape. The prescribed title is set by the IB and must be answered as written. Students repeatedly answer an adjacent question they find more interesting, and the essay reads well while scoring poorly, because engagement with the title as written is what the criteria ask for. One session spent taking a prescribed title apart clause by clause prevents that outcome entirely.

Where a subject's internally assessed component has its own length guidance, your school's subject teacher holds the current figure, and we work from what they give rather than from a remembered number. The IB revises guidance, and a tutor quoting last cycle's limits is a liability. Everything in the table below is a published limit for the core components; for subject-specific guidance, the teacher is the source.

sections.heading: Where IB marks are lost in ways nobody warns about
paragraphs: Ask an Al Jaddaf parent why a predicted grade slipped and the answer is usually about workload. Ask the criteria and the answer is often narrower and more fixable. Across subjects, the same four leaks recur: an internally assessed component started too late to be evaluated properly, command terms answered at the wrong level, data-based questions attempted without reading the axes, and reflection treated as a closing paragraph rather than as something present throughout.

The evaluation leak is the biggest. In the sciences, a student runs a competent experiment, presents clean data, and writes three lines of evaluation. The criteria award evaluation substantial weight, so a modest experiment thoroughly evaluated outscores an impressive one barely discussed. The same shape appears in the mathematics Exploration, where reflection carries its own criterion and is routinely added at the end instead of appearing at each decision point. Neither is a knowledge problem and neither takes long to fix once named.

Command terms are the second. The IB publishes them, and they are tiered: state, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, discuss. A student who describes when the question said evaluate has written something true and unmarkable. One session with the command term list and three past questions usually moves marks more than a month of content review, and it transfers across every subject the student takes.

The third is the predicted grade mechanism, which Al Jaddaf families often misunderstand. Predicted grades come from the school, based on the school's evidence, and university offers rest on them. That means the school's internal assessments matter in their own right, not merely as practice. A student treating a December internal paper as a mock has misread the stakes, and a tutoring plan that peaks only in the spring arrives after the predictions have been made.

sections.heading: Al Jaddaf's school pattern, and why no local pool matches it
paragraphs: Al Jaddaf is small and its school options are not contained within it. Swiss International Scientific School Dubai sits inside the district, running IB programmes alongside a bilingual model. Everything else Al Jaddaf families use is elsewhere: Dubai Festival City across the Creek, Sobha Hartland and Mohammed Bin Rashid City south along Al Khail Road, Nad Al Sheba beyond that. Families living in adjacent towers can therefore be following different timetables, different subject combinations and different internal deadline calendars.

That spread is the structural reason a local tutor pool does not match local demand. A pool bounded by a practical drive from Al Jaddaf might serve one school's subject mix well and another's poorly, and no tutor can specialise in six subjects across three schools' internal calendars. The Diploma makes this sharper than other curricula do, because the internally assessed components are subject-specific and the core components are supervised in school, so a tutor has to work alongside one school's deadlines rather than a national timetable.

There is a Dubai-level context worth having. KHDA reported 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with the International Baccalaureate at seven per cent of enrolment against thirty-seven per cent on UK curricula. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them IB, creating 16,846 places, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for that academic year. The IB share is growing from a small base, which is precisely why specialist supply lags locally.

For a family in Al Jaddaf the practical conclusion is unexciting and useful. Choose on subject, level and internal-assessment experience, treat geography as solved by live video, and get the school's own internal deadline calendar into the tutor's hands in the first week.

sections.heading: The academic honesty line, drawn where the IB draws it
paragraphs: The IB's academic honesty rules are stricter than most families expect and the consequences land on the student. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own. A tutor who writes, completes, substantially rewrites or supplies any part of an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay, Internal Assessment or Personal Project is creating a malpractice exposure for the candidate, and a finding can cost a Diploma. There are providers in this market advertising completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is not a shortcut; it is a risk transferred onto a sixteen-year-old.

The legitimate version of help is more useful than the illegitimate version anyway. A tutor can take a student's own draft and mark it against the published criteria. A tutor can explain what a criterion is asking for when the wording is opaque, which is frequently. A tutor can model an evaluation or a reflection on an unrelated investigation, then hand the student's own back untouched. A tutor can teach referencing properly, which prevents more honesty cases than any warning does, because most cases begin as citation failures rather than as deliberate cheating.

On materials, IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are copyright works. We reference and link the official sources; we do not reproduce them or supply them as downloads. In sessions we show a student how to find the current document on the organisation's own site, which also means they can check a claim a tutor has made, including ours.

Practically, we keep a short session note recording what was covered and whose work was in front of us. If a school ever raises a question about work a tutor was involved in, a parent can hand that note over. Transparency costs nothing in advance and is the only thing worth having afterwards.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and getting started from Al Jaddaf
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. A KHDA inspection rating is a judgement about a school. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises and staff that we do not hold. Any provider implying regulator endorsement is making a claim worth checking first.

Tutoring is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, no amount is quoted here.

To start, send the subject and level, which internally assessed component is in progress, the school's internal deadline for it, and two evening windows that genuinely work from Al Jaddaf after the school run. We match a subject specialist, run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep, and give you a plan afterwards. One trial per student, nothing charged beforehand, and no card details required to book it.

If no specialist is free we say so, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing whoever is available. Scarcity concentrates in Higher Level sciences and in the weeks when internal deadlines cluster. Finally, the limits: nobody can promise a grade and this page does not, and nothing here implies tutoring is required for Diploma award, for university admission or for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, which are processes with their own published rules to verify with the authority.

process.title: Test the IB claim in one question
process.description: Ask any prospective tutor to name the criteria for the internally assessed component in your child's subject and roughly what each is worth. A tutor who teaches it regularly answers at once. One who does not will talk about the subject instead, and that is the moment to keep looking.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Which subject, Higher or Standard Level, which internally assessed component is in progress, and the school's internal deadline for it. Those four facts decide the match. The school's internal calendar matters more to a tutoring plan than the external session date does.

process.title: Fix a slot the Al Jaddaf commute allows
process.description: Tell us the school and the genuine time the student is home. Al Jaddaf's short journeys often make 16:30 achievable, which is earlier than most Dubai districts manage. If the school is in Nad Al Sheba, expect 17:15 and consider a weekend morning instead.

process.title: Run one free trial lesson
process.description: Live and one-to-one in the slot you intend to keep, so you are testing the real arrangement rather than a demonstration. One per student, no payment taken beforehand, no card details required. The tutor writes a short note on what they found and what they would address first.

process.title: Put the internal deadlines in the plan first
process.description: Build the term around the school's internal deadlines for Internal Assessments, Extended Essay drafts and Theory of Knowledge submissions, then fit content work around them. A plan that peaks only before the external session arrives after predicted grades have been made.

process.title: Review at the next school assessment
process.description: The school's own internal assessment is the checkpoint, and it also feeds the predicted grade. If marks have not moved where the plan predicted, the plan changes or the tutor does, and replacement inside the same week is possible because the match was never bounded by a drive.

whyPoints.title: The internal assessment is part of the match, not an afterthought
whyPoints.description: We confirm a tutor has experience of the published criteria for the component your child is working on before the match is made. That is the part a strong general tutor typically cannot cover, and it is where families in Al Jaddaf most often discover the gap too late.

whyPoints.title: Honest about home visits
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Al Jaddaf or anywhere in the UAE, and we say it before the price comparison rather than after. Home tuition is a real option at AED 180 to AED 500 per hour in this market; we are not it, and we set out what each format gives you.

whyPoints.title: A pool that matches Al Jaddaf's school spread
whyPoints.description: Al Jaddaf families attend schools inside the district, across the Creek and south on Al Khail Road, with different subject mixes and different internal calendars. No pool bounded by a drive matches that spread. A national one does, and live video is what reaches it.

whyPoints.title: Limits and criteria, written down
whyPoints.description: The Extended Essay at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600, the exhibition commentary at 950. Subject-specific guidance comes from your child's teacher, because the IB revises it and a tutor quoting last cycle's figures is a liability rather than an expert.

whyPoints.title: No dates we could not verify
whyPoints.description: No IB session or results date appears on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and an unverified exam date is something a family would plan a whole term around. Your school's coordinator is the source.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line stated before work begins
whyPoints.description: Feedback on the student's own draft, criteria explained, evaluation modelled on unrelated material, referencing taught properly. Never writing, never restructuring to a standard, never supplying argument or data. We keep a session note of whose work was in front of us.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who visits our apartment in Al Jaddaf?
faqs.answer: From some Dubai agencies, yes. Published in-home one-to-one rates run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, with monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions appearing in the market. IB Gram is not among them. We deliver one-to-one tuition for UAE families online over live video on Gulf Standard Time and send no tutors to UAE addresses; home visiting is a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a tutor really knows the IB or just says so?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions before hiring. Which criteria is the internally assessed component in this subject marked against, and roughly what is each worth? What is the word limit on the Theory of Knowledge essay and on the exhibition commentary? How are the three core points awarded between the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge? Someone who teaches the Diploma regularly answers all three without pausing. A strong general tutor who has read a syllabus summary will redirect the conversation to the subject itself, which is your answer.

faqs.question: What is the word limit on the Extended Essay and does it really matter?
faqs.answer: Four thousand words, and it matters at the question stage rather than at the editing stage. The commonest Extended Essay failure is a research question too broad to answer in that space, chosen months before the limit becomes a practical problem. The criteria reward focus and method heavily, so a student cutting argument in the final weeks is losing marks that better question-framing would have protected. Two hours spent narrowing the question at the start is worth more than twenty hours of editing at the end.

faqs.question: How many points is the IB core worth, and how are they awarded?
faqs.answer: Up to three of the forty-five. Forty-two points come from the six subjects at a maximum of seven each, and the remaining three come from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge assessed together through a published matrix. Creativity, Activity, Service is not graded but must be completed for the Diploma to be awarded. The practical consequence is that two written components, with no examination to recover them, carry three points, and a plan built subject by subject can miss them entirely.

faqs.question: Which Theory of Knowledge mistake costs students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Answering an adjacent question rather than the prescribed title as written. The titles are set by the IB and the criteria reward engagement with the title itself, so an essay that reads well while addressing a neighbouring question scores poorly and the student cannot see why. The fix is a single session taking the title apart clause by clause before any writing begins. The essay limit is 1,600 words and the exhibition commentary is limited to 950 words across three objects.

faqs.question: Why does my child's science Internal Assessment score lower than the experiment deserved?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the evaluation section is thin. The criteria for a scientific investigation cover exploration, analysis, evaluation and communication, and evaluation carries substantial weight. A competent experiment with clean data and three lines of evaluation scores below a modest experiment whose limitations, anomalies and improvements are discussed properly. It is not a knowledge problem and it does not take long to fix once it has been named, which is why starting the component early matters more than working harder on the practical.

faqs.question: Are IB predicted grades from the school, and do they matter as much as people say?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. Predicted grades come from the school, based on the school's own evidence, and university offers rest on them. That means internal assessments carry real stakes in their own right rather than functioning as practice. An Al Jaddaf family whose tutoring plan peaks in the spring arrives after the predictions have been made. If university applications are in view, the internal assessment calendar is the one to plan around, and your school's coordinator holds it.

faqs.question: Which IB school is actually inside Al Jaddaf?
faqs.answer: Swiss International Scientific School Dubai sits inside the district, running IB programmes alongside a bilingual model. Beyond that, Al Jaddaf families use schools elsewhere: Universal American School Dubai and Deira International School across the Creek in Dubai Festival City, and North London Collegiate School Dubai, Hartland International School and GEMS Modern Academy south along Al Khail Road. KHDA reported the IB at seven per cent of Dubai private enrolment in 2024-25. Schools are named as market context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: What time can lessons start for a student living in Al Jaddaf?
faqs.answer: Earlier than in most Dubai districts, which is a genuine advantage. Al Jaddaf's journeys are short, so a student at a school inside the district or across the Creek in Festival City is often home in time for a 16:30 start. A student travelling to Sobha Hartland sits better at 17:00, and one commuting to Nad Al Sheba at 17:15 or later. Pick the slot for your worst normal weekday rather than your best, because the co-curricular fixture is what breaks a weekly arrangement.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have IB accreditation or KHDA approval?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. KHDA is Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; it regulates and inspects schools, and an inspection rating judges a school rather than any tutor. A KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises and staff. Treat any claim of regulator endorsement as a reason to check further.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a UAE permit, and what should I ask about it?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tutoring in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, with no fee and a stated two working days. Ask for the permit category. No fine schedule is published, so any quoted fine amount is unverified.

faqs.question: Why does this page not list the IB exam and results dates?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified from the IB itself, whose website blocks automated checking. An unverified exam date on a landing page is something a family might plan a term of revision around, and publishing it would be worse than leaving it out. UAE schools sit the main May session. For every date that matters, including internal Extended Essay and Internal Assessment deadlines, your school's IB coordinator holds the authoritative calendar, and those internal dates shape a tutoring plan more than the external ones do.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with the Extended Essay without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may help narrow a research question so it is answerable in 4,000 words, explain what a criterion rewards, ask questions that expose a weak argument, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not produce the essay, restructure it to a standard, or supply the argument. The school supervisor remains the supervisor. Providers in this market sell completed assessments outright, which is a malpractice trigger whose consequence lands on the candidate rather than the seller.

faqs.question: Can one tutor support several IB subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and we would not aim for it. The internally assessed components differ by subject and are marked against different criteria, so a tutor strong in two subjects may be strong in only one component. Where one specialist genuinely covers both at the right level, the scheduling saving for an Al Jaddaf family is real. Where they do not, two exact matches beat one approximate one, and the difference usually appears in whichever internally assessed component the tutor was weaker on.

faqs.question: What happens if no IB specialist is available in our Al Jaddaf time slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing whoever is free. Scarcity concentrates in Higher Level sciences and in the weeks when internal assessment deadlines cluster across schools, which is also when demand peaks. The alternatives are a different slot, a shorter commitment with a specialist whose availability is limited, or command-term and technique work while the subject slot is pending. Weekend mornings widen the choice more than any other scheduling change.

We will match a specialist whose internal assessment experience we have checked, run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep, and build the plan around your school's internal calendar. Lessons are one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khail-gate.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work to a dated two-year plan rather than an open weekly arrangement, anchored to the student's own school deadlines for internal assessment, the Extended Essay and mocks.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a calendar problem before it is a teaching problem
paragraphs: Most families buy Diploma tutoring in Year 13, after a mock. By then the subject levels are fixed, the Extended Essay question is set, two or three internal assessments are submitted or nearly so, and the only remaining variable is paper technique. That is a real variable and worth money, but it is the last and smallest of several, and it is the one bought at the highest price under the most pressure.

The decisions that actually determine a Diploma score happen earlier and quietly. Which six subjects, at which three Higher Levels. Which mathematics course. Whether the Extended Essay question is narrow enough to argue. Whether each internal assessment's design can reach the top of its criteria. Whether the student can carry the load they have chosen. Every one of those is a Year 12 question, and every one of them is cheaper to influence then than to compensate for later.

That makes the Diploma unusual among qualifications a Dubai family might buy support for. An IGCSE problem can often be fixed in a term. A Diploma problem noticed in Year 13 is frequently a Year 12 decision that cannot be reversed. A student in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level who should be in Applications Standard Level is carrying a structural disadvantage that no quantity of sessions in the final term undoes.

The calendar also explains why support spread evenly across two years wastes money. The load is not flat. Term one of Year 12 is decision-heavy and teaching-light. The middle of Year 12 is internal-assessment design and Extended Essay question setting. Year 13 winter is completion and mocks. Year 13 final term is papers. A plan that matches that shape uses perhaps a third of the hours an evenly spread plan would, for more effect.

The second thing this page does is answer the home-tutoring question properly rather than deflecting it. In-home tutoring in Dubai is a genuine market with published rates, real advantages for some students and a measurable cost in travel. A family in Al Khail Gate deserves the actual numbers and the actual trade, not an assertion that online is better. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India, and the comparison below is there so the choice is informed rather than assumed.

What follows is the two-year calendar laid out term by term, the in-home premium priced against it, what the Al Khail Gate commute does to a weekday evening, and where the academic-honesty boundary sits across a programme in which most of the assessed work is written at home. Read it once at the start of Year 12 and the rest of the programme becomes a scheduling exercise rather than a series of surprises, which is a better position for a household to be in than any amount of last-term intensity can buy.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khail-gate.programmesIntro: Al Khail Gate families reach the Diploma by several routes, and the entry route changes what the first year of support should do.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, graded 1 to 7 for a maximum of forty-two, plus up to three core points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay combined on a published matrix. CAS is a completion requirement. Each subject grade combines external papers with internal assessment at published shares.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma is offered by a minority of private schools, with International Baccalaureate students around seven per cent of private enrolment against thirty-seven per cent on UK curricula. Al Khail Gate families generally commute to IB schools in Al Barsha South, Nad Al Sheba or the Sobha Hartland area rather than finding one on the doorstep.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's feeder programme, assessed against four criteria out of eight each rather than on papers. Students arriving in the Diploma from MYP bring documented process habits and independent research skills, and almost no practice at writing a complete argument to a clock.
programmes.countryNote: The practical consequence for a Dubai family is that an MYP-entry student usually needs a timed-writing block in term one of Year 12, while an IGCSE-entry student needs the opposite: help with independent research and extended writing rather than with examination technique.

programmes.name: IGCSE as the Diploma entry route
programmes.description: The commonest feeder in Dubai, since UK curricula dominate enrolment. The tier matters: Cambridge Extended or Pearson Higher covers algebraic and scientific content the Diploma assumes, while Core or Foundation omits topics Higher Level courses treat as prior knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE in the June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with its November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

programmes.name: IB Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project, offered by a few UAE schools. Subject tutoring works identically for the Diploma courses taken within it; the core requirements and the final certificate differ.
programmes.countryNote: Worth asking about directly if a Dubai school presents it as an alternative, because for university entry and for Ministry of Education equivalency the Career-related Programme and the full Diploma are not interchangeable. The school's admissions office will state plainly which certificate a student ends with.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khail-gate.subjectsIntro: These subjects generate the most Al Khail Gate requests, described here by when in the two years the work has to happen rather than by syllabus content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The level and route decision belongs to term one of Year 12 and is specified by many STEM degrees. The exploration topic should be settled by mid-Year 12; left to Year 13 it becomes the piece of work that competes with mock revision.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology throughout. A rigorous course aimed at different destinations rather than an easier one, and the right choice for many students, provided the intended degree does not specify Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The scientific investigation needs a viable research question by mid-Year 12, because a design that cannot generate usable data caps the analysis criteria later. Organic mechanisms and energetics are the predictable paper weaknesses in Year 13.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency is the gatekeeper and shows in term one of Year 12, which makes it the cheapest moment to address. Graph interpretation and uncertainty handling carry weight across both the papers and the investigation.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content tempts students to treat it as a memory subject through Year 12 and discover in Year 13 that data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments carry the marks. Early practice at reading a graph and stating a limitation pays twice over.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal commentaries are built on published articles, so article selection in Year 12 determines how much syllabus the student can demonstrate. Diagram marks are explicit, and students who draw loosely lose them consistently.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessed across unseen analysis, a comparative essay and an oral on a global issue. The oral needs a global issue and extracts chosen well before Year 13, and students who leave the choice late end up defending a thin pairing.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, contributing core points with the Extended Essay. It runs across both years with its own deadlines and is the component students most often treat as paperwork until the points are counted.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Subject chosen and research question set in Year 12. Most of the recoverable marks are decided by that question: too broad and no argument is possible, too narrow and there is nothing to investigate. Supervision checkpoints are school deadlines, not IB ones.

sections.heading: The home-tutoring question, answered properly
paragraphs: In-home tutoring in Dubai is a real market and the published figures are specific. Bestimate's rate work puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with travel included in both. Comparable qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing around AED 270 and Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Monthly packages circulating in the market run roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against about AED 799 for eight online sessions.

What the in-home premium buys is worth stating without irony. A person in the room changes the behaviour of some students entirely. A parent can overhear. A younger student who will not settle at a screen settles at a table. For a household where the real problem is that no work happens unsupervised, those are not luxuries and the premium may be the best money spent.

What it also buys, in Al Khail Gate specifically, is a drive. The community sits beside the Al Khail Road interchange, which is among the busier corridors in the city in the late afternoon. A tutor travelling here between four and seven is paid for time in traffic, can usually offer one window per evening, and loses the session rather than moving it when a school bus runs late. Across a Diploma year, a lost session a fortnight at specialist rates is a significant sum spent on nothing.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Khail Gate or anywhere else in the Emirates. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time. A family that wants in-home delivery should buy it from somebody who sells it, with the published rates above as the benchmark, and this page is written so that choice is made with the numbers in hand.

sections.heading: Year 12, term by term: the decisions that set the ceiling
paragraphs: Term one of Year 12 is the most consequential and the least used. Subject and level choices are either confirmed or adjusted in these weeks, and after them the school timetable hardens. A student who has taken three demanding Higher Level subjects plus an Extended Essay in one of them, and who is already struggling in week six, has a window of perhaps a month in which a change is administratively simple. Raising it then is cheap; raising it in Year 13 is usually impossible.

The mathematics route is the sharpest of those decisions because several engineering, physics, mathematics and economics degrees specify Analysis and Approaches, sometimes at Higher Level. A student who chose Applications for comfort may find a course closed in Year 13 with no route back. Reading the actual entry requirements of a handful of plausible universities takes an evening and should happen in term one, not during the application.

The middle of Year 12 is design work. The Extended Essay subject and research question are set, and most of that essay's available marks are decided by the question: too broad and no argument can be sustained, too narrow and there is nothing to investigate. Internal assessment topics are chosen in several subjects, and in each the design determines whether the top criteria are reachable at all. A chemistry investigation whose method cannot produce usable data cannot be analysed well however good the write-up.

The final stretch of Year 12 is where internal assessment drafting should begin in earnest, in parallel with ordinary teaching. Students who leave all of it to Year 13 end up writing three or four substantial pieces of coursework in the same winter as mocks, which is the single most common reason a Diploma student's grades slip in the final year. Nothing about that is unavoidable; it is a scheduling failure with a known date.

sections.heading: Year 13 counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages, because the IB's own website blocks automated checking and no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. A date a family plans around has to be right, so confirm the window and the results dates with the school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, and treat any third-party calendar as a prompt to check rather than a source.

What can be planned without those dates is the sequence, because the sequence is set by the school. Internal assessment submission deadlines come first, generally spread across the autumn and winter of Year 13. Theory of Knowledge has its own exhibition and essay deadlines. The Extended Essay has a final submission date with supervision checkpoints before it. Mocks sit in the winter. Then the paper phase, then the session.

The useful discipline is to write those dates on one page in September of Year 13 and plan hours around them rather than around how a student feels in a given week. A student with two internal assessments due within a fortnight of the mock series has a problem that is visible in September and invisible in November, and moving one of those drafts forward by three weeks is a conversation the school will usually have if it happens early.

The paper phase itself is the part most families already understand, and it is the shortest. Full papers to time, losses categorised into content, technique, misreading and clock, and work directed at whichever category dominates. New content goes in only where a named gap exists. For Higher Level students the extended problem-solving papers need long uninterrupted blocks, which in this community usually means a weekend morning rather than another weekday evening after the Al Khail Road run.

sections.heading: Internal deadlines beat examination dates, and nobody tells parents that
paragraphs: Parents arrive at Diploma tutoring asking about examinations because examinations are the visible event. The deadlines that actually govern the two years belong to the school, are published in its own calendar, and are the ones a student can miss without anybody outside the building noticing until a grade arrives. An internal assessment submitted late, or submitted as a first draft because time ran out, caps a subject grade as firmly as a weak paper does.

There is a structural reason this is under-discussed. Schools publish these dates to students, often through a portal or a planner rather than directly to parents, and the dates are subject-specific rather than consolidated. A family would have to collect six subject calendars plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge schedules to see the whole picture, and almost nobody does. The students who cope best are the ones whose households did exactly that in September.

The practical request is simple and schools answer it willingly: ask the Diploma coordinator for a consolidated list of internal deadlines for the year. With that one document, the heavy fortnights are visible months ahead, and support can be placed where the collisions are rather than spread evenly across a year that is not evenly loaded.

This is also the strongest argument for starting support in Year 12 rather than Year 13. In Year 12 the deadlines are about design decisions that are cheap to influence and expensive to leave. In Year 13 they are about completion under pressure. The same number of hours does more in the first case, and the families who report that Diploma tutoring was worth it are overwhelmingly the ones who bought it early.

sections.heading: Academic honesty across two years of work written at home
paragraphs: The Diploma is unusual in how much of its assessed work is produced outside a supervised hall. Internal assessments in every subject, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition: all written at home, over months, with feedback permitted within defined limits. That makes the honesty boundary a practical daily question rather than an abstract principle, and it is the reason a family should establish where a tutor stands before any work begins.

The working rule is that the student produces the work and the tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on it. In practice a tutor can explain a published criterion, ask what evidence supports a claim, point out that a methodology is uncontrolled, show a worked example of a comparable problem, and mark a draft against the criteria. A tutor cannot write any part of it, cannot edit it to completion, cannot do the mathematics or the analysis for it, and cannot supply a model to be submitted.

This matters commercially as well as ethically because the Gulf market is not clean on this point. Operations advertising completed Internal Assessments for sale exist in these search results, at fixed prices. For an IB student, submitting bought work is a malpractice matter with consequences that follow the student rather than the seller, and a family is entitled to ask any provider directly what it will and will not produce. An evasive answer is itself an answer.

The adjacent boundary is copyright on board materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. A tutor should link them at their official source rather than distributing copies, and a provider advertising a downloadable library of board material is describing its standards more accurately than its marketing does.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE subjects and the summer between the two years
paragraphs: Three features of the UAE calendar shape a Diploma plan and are missing from any schedule imported from elsewhere. The first is that Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Those are real timetable hours on top of six Diploma subjects and the core.

KHDA also sets how they run: separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for the two groups strictly prohibited, Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, and instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. A Diploma week in Dubai is therefore fuller than the programme outline suggests, and plans that assume otherwise overcommit the student.

The second is Ramadan, which compresses the school day and moves the household evening. In this community that usually means sessions shift to after Iftar or to weekend mornings for the month. Because delivery is online, that is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation. What should be decided in advance is which work pauses: paper practice can continue in shorter form, while internal assessment drafting almost always stalls unless a checkpoint was deliberately placed before the month.

The third is the summer between Year 12 and Year 13, which is the single most valuable and most wasted stretch in the Diploma. It is the only period with genuinely free time and no competing deadlines, and it is the natural moment to finish internal assessment drafts. A student who arrives in Year 13 with two drafts substantially complete has a materially different year from one who arrives with none, and the difference was made in weeks when nothing else was happening.

sections.heading: What the Al Khail Gate commute does to a weekday session
paragraphs: Al Khail Gate has no IB Diploma school on its doorstep, so every Diploma student here commutes, and they commute in different directions. Some travel to the Motor City and Dubai Sports City cluster, which is close in distance and can be slow at the Al Khail Road interchange. Others travel towards Al Barsha South or Dubai Hills, and others south towards Nad Al Sheba. That variety means arrival times differ household by household rather than by community, which is unusual and worth asking about rather than assuming.

The practical range is wide. A student at a school in the Motor City cluster can be home soon after the bell and able to work by late afternoon. A student travelling towards Nad Al Sheba or Al Barsha South in term-time traffic may not be settled until well after five. Add an after-school activity or a CAS commitment and the realistic window closes further. Setting a session time from the timetable rather than from the actual arrival time is how a weekly slot quietly becomes a weekly rearrangement.

This is also why long sessions have to be weekend sessions. Higher Level extended problem-solving papers and full timed papers need an uninterrupted block that a weekday evening in this community cannot reliably provide. A Saturday or Sunday morning, sat properly to time, is worth more than two interrupted weekday hours, and it is the only way most Diploma students in the belt actually sit complete papers under conditions.

None of this argues for or against any format on its own. It argues for building the plan from the real arrival time and the real weekend availability, which is a two-minute conversation at the start and the difference between a plan that runs for a year and one that is renegotiated monthly.

sections.heading: What IB Gram claims, and what it does not
paragraphs: Stated plainly: IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no office, centre or branch in the UAE. The phrase approved is used loosely in this market, and several competitor pages make claims their own permit position does not support. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises; we do not hold one and do not imply it.

On the regulatory position for individual tutors, the facts are public and worth knowing. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted is unverified.

What we do claim is narrow and checkable. Tutors teach a named subject at a named level, mark work against published expectations in the session, and send a short note afterwards naming the component, the marks and the next target. There is a free trial lesson before any payment is taken, and it functions as a diagnosis: if the honest conclusion is that tutoring is not the bottleneck, that is what gets said.

We publish no statistics about our own outcomes, no star ratings and no student counts, because we cannot produce the underlying data and a figure without its sample, date and method is decoration. Every AED band on this page is a market rate published by a named provider or rate study, cited as such, and every regulatory statement is drawn from the authority's own published material.

process.description: One document listing every internal assessment deadline, the Extended Essay checkpoints and the Theory of Knowledge dates for the year. Diploma coordinators provide it willingly when asked directly, and it makes the heavy fortnights visible months in advance.

process.description: The trial works one real component live, marked against published expectations, and ends with the tutor naming whether the loss is content, command term, method or clock, and where in the calendar the hours should go. No payment is taken before it.

process.description: Levels and route checked against actual degree requirements, the Extended Essay question narrowed, each internal assessment design tested against its criteria. These are the cheapest hours in the programme and the ones most families skip entirely.

process.title: Place the rest at the collisions

whyPoints.title: Planned across two years, not bought after a mock
whyPoints.description: The decisions that set a Diploma score, levels, mathematics route, Extended Essay question, internal assessment design, are Year 12 decisions. Support bought in Year 13 can only work on what is left, which is the smallest and most expensive variable.

whyPoints.title: The in-home premium shown, not dismissed
whyPoints.description: Published Dubai figures put in-home at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included against AED 150 to 300 online, and monthly packages at roughly double for the same eight contact hours. We put the comparison on the page so the choice is informed.

whyPoints.title: Internal deadlines treated as the real calendar
whyPoints.description: Examinations are the visible event; school deadlines govern the two years and are the ones a student can miss unnoticed. We ask for the consolidated list first and plan hours around the collisions it reveals.
