faqs.question: Is it too late to start IB tutoring if my child is already in Year 13?
faqs.answer: Not too late to be useful, but you are buying the last and smallest variable. By Year 13 the subject levels are fixed, the Extended Essay question is set and most internal assessment design decisions have been made. What remains is paper technique, command-term discipline, timing and the completion of coursework already in flight, all of which respond to work. What cannot be recovered is a level choice or a research question that was wrong, which is why the same budget spent in Year 12 does considerably more.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to apartments in Al Khail Gate?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Khail Gate or anywhere else in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time. If in-home delivery is what your household needs, the published Dubai market band is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and that is the benchmark to hold a provider to.

faqs.question: What does in-home Diploma tutoring actually cost compared with online?
faqs.answer: Roughly double for the same contact hours on published figures. Monthly packages circulating in the market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is eight contact hours, against about AED 799 for eight one-hour online sessions, also eight. Hourly, Bestimate puts in-home at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 online and AED 200 to 450 for specialists. The gap is mostly the journey.

faqs.question: Which Year 12 decisions matter most for a Diploma score?
faqs.answer: Four. The six subjects and which three are at Higher Level, because the timetable hardens after term one. The mathematics route, because several engineering, physics, mathematics and economics degrees specify Analysis and Approaches. The Extended Essay research question, because most of that essay's marks are decided by whether the question can be argued at all. And each internal assessment design, because a method that cannot produce usable data caps the analysis criteria before any writing happens.

faqs.question: How do I find out my child's internal assessment deadlines?
faqs.answer: Ask the Diploma coordinator for a consolidated list for the year. Schools publish these dates, but subject by subject and usually to students rather than parents, so a family would otherwise have to assemble six subject calendars plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge schedules. With the list in one place, the fortnights where two deadlines collide or a submission sits beside a mock become visible months ahead, and a draft can be moved forward by agreement rather than missed.

faqs.question: Can you tell me the exact dates of my daughter's IB papers and results?
faqs.answer: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and we deliberately do not publish specific examination or results dates on these pages. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family plans around has to be correct. Confirm the window and the results date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge qualifications sat alongside, UAE centres sit the June and November series.

faqs.question: Should my son use the summer between Year 12 and Year 13 for tutoring?
faqs.answer: For internal assessment drafting, yes, and it is the most under-used stretch in the Diploma. It is the only period with free time and no competing deadlines, which makes it the natural moment to get two or three drafts substantially complete. A student arriving in Year 13 with drafts in hand has a materially easier winter than one arriving with none, because coursework then collides with mocks. Using the entire summer is counterproductive; the final few weeks are usually enough.

faqs.question: How many Diploma subjects is it worth paying for at once?
faqs.answer: One weekly, with short blocks elsewhere, for most families. Three Higher Level subjects plus Extended Essay coaching is three or four recurring commitments that very few households sustain for two years. The shape that works is a single weekly specialist session on the subject furthest from target, a Year 12 design block covering the decisions across all six subjects, and a final-term intensive on two subjects. Spread thinly across six, the same budget produces nothing measurable in any of them.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor do with an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the underlying subject, question whether the design can reach the top criteria, explain each published criterion, ask what evidence supports a claim, and give feedback on drafts the student has written. What a tutor must not do is write any part of it, do the mathematics or analysis for it, edit it to completion, or supply a model for submission. Operations selling completed Internal Assessments exist in this market at fixed prices, and the malpractice consequence lands on the student rather than the seller.

faqs.question: Why do Diploma grades often slip in the winter of Year 13?
faqs.answer: Because coursework and mocks arrive together. Students who leave internal assessment drafting to Year 13 end up writing three or four substantial pieces in the same weeks as mock examinations, and something gives. It is not an unavoidable feature of the programme; it is a scheduling outcome with a known cause and a known date. Drafting in the final term of Year 12 and over the summer removes most of it, which is why the deadline list collected in September is worth more than an extra session in February.

faqs.question: Do the UAE mandatory subjects affect a Diploma student's week?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year and instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Schools must also run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of those subjects, which creates fixed timetable blocks. A Dubai Diploma week is therefore fuller than six subjects plus the core implies, and tutoring plans should assume fewer free evenings.

faqs.question: What time can a session start for a student living in Al Khail Gate?
faqs.answer: It depends on the direction of the commute rather than the community, which is unusual. Students at schools in the Motor City and Dubai Sports City cluster can often work by late afternoon. Students travelling towards Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills or Nad Al Sheba in term-time traffic on the Al Khail corridor may not be settled until after five, and a CAS commitment pushes it later. Long sessions for full timed papers realistically have to be weekend mornings.

faqs.question: Can the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay points be worth chasing?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are frequently the cheapest points available. The two combine on a published matrix to award up to three additional points on top of the forty-two from six subjects, and both are written over months with supervision rather than sat under a clock. Three points changes many university offers. A student treating the core as paperwork while grinding at a subject grade is usually working harder for less, and the fix is to set the Theory of Knowledge essay title and the Extended Essay question early.

faqs.question: Does any tutoring provider hold KHDA approval for IB work?
faqs.answer: A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, requiring initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is the only thing the phrase could properly refer to. IB Gram holds no such permit and claims no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. If a provider uses the phrase, ask for the permit number.

faqs.question: What happens if the specialist we need is not available at our time?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a generalist. A particular Diploma subject at a particular level at a particular hour does occasionally come up empty, especially in the weeks before the session when demand peaks across the city. The options are a different time, a different tutor with a handover of the student's component plan, or a wait with a date attached. A mismatched tutor in a Diploma subject costs a term, and in Year 13 a term is not available.

intro.heading: The honest answer to the home-tutor question in Al Khawaneej
paragraphs: Parents in Al Khawaneej search for a home tutor for a practical reason. The community sits at the eastern edge of Dubai, secondary students travel out of it to school, and by the time a Diploma student is home the useful part of the evening is already shortening. Getting into a car again to drive somewhere for a lesson is not a realistic plan, so the obvious thought is to have somebody come here instead. That is a sensible thought and it deserves a proper answer rather than a sales pitch.

The answer has three parts. The first is what the in-home market actually costs around here, which is more than most families expect, because the price includes a drive out to the eastern suburbs and back. Published Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor teaching online, and monthly in-home packages circulate at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits against around AED 799 for eight online sessions.

The second part is what the drive does to the clock. A tutor travelling out to Al Khawaneej needs the session to start late enough that they can get here, which in practice means the lesson begins after the hour when your child is most able to use it, and finishes at an hour that competes with sleep. Families discover this in the second week, not the first, and it is the commonest reason an in-home arrangement quietly stops. A tutor who has already driven forty minutes is also disinclined to end a session early on a bad evening, which is the moment when ending early would have been the right call.

The third part is the service itself, stated plainly. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For UAE families the teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own work on screen. That removes the drive from both sides of the arrangement: the session can start when your child is ready rather than when a car arrives, and the tutor can be a Diploma subject specialist rather than whoever lives within range.

What follows is the detail an Al Khawaneej family actually needs: which schools this area feeds and what each run does to the clock, where the usable hours in the week really are, what the market charges and what it is charging for, who may legally tutor your child under UAE rules, and where the line sits on Diploma coursework. The intention is that you could use this page to make a decision even if you decided against us.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.programmesIntro: An Al Khawaneej family searching for IB support might mean any of three programmes, and the answer to the timing question differs for each. These are the three as they appear in the schools this area uses.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The workload is the heaviest a school student in this catchment will meet, and it arrives with internal deadlines that cluster. Most Al Khawaneej enquiries for IB support concern a Diploma student in the first or second year of this.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate programmes held seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new International Baccalaureate schools among seven new private schools, creating 16,846 new places in total. Supply is growing; it is not yet concentrated at the eastern edge of the city.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five years before the Diploma, assessed by summative tasks against four criteria rather than by terminal papers. The timing question is gentler here because the workload is lighter, but the habits that decide whether a Diploma year is survivable are formed in these years rather than in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Al Khawaneej family has children in both programmes, the sensible arrangement is usually to protect the Diploma student's best evening hour and give the Middle Years student a weekend morning, rather than splitting the same tired weekday window between two children.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary years taught through transdisciplinary units. Support at this stage is usually about numeracy, reading fluency or written explanation rather than about any subject in particular, and short frequent sessions work better than long ones.
programmes.countryNote: Primary provision is closer to home in this part of Dubai than secondary provision, including a Dubai Schools campus at Al Khawaneej, so a younger child's day typically ends earlier than an older sibling's. That difference is worth using when the family timetable is being built.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Al Khawaneej families most often ask about, with a note on what each one demands of an evening session specifically, since that is the constraint this page is about.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus, algebra and proof. Needs a student who can still concentrate, so it is the wrong subject for a slot immediately after a long bus route. Works best in a protected weekend morning hour where sustained problem work is possible.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-based work. More forgiving of a tired student than Analysis and Approaches because tasks can be broken into shorter pieces, which makes it a reasonable weekday evening subject.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Problem-solving with units and uncertainties throughout. Benefits from short frequent sessions rather than long ones, because the gains come from repeated practice at starting questions rather than from extended explanation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation-heavy in the early topics and reasoning-heavy in organic chemistry. The calculation work tolerates a tired slot; the organic reasoning does not, which is worth knowing when a weekly hour is being placed.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Large volume of precise recall plus command-term discipline. Suits a weekday evening because it can be worked in twenty-minute blocks, and it rewards frequent short retrieval practice more than any other Diploma science.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams, definitions and evaluation. The evaluation marks need a student who can hold two sides of an argument at once, so the harder parts belong in the better slot of the week rather than the convenient one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study application and a written internal assessment. Drafting work is best done when the student is fresh; terminology and tool practice can sit comfortably in a weekday session after a long day.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Close analysis, comparative work and oral assessment. Oral preparation is the part most often left too late, and it is also the part that suits a short, frequent slot better than a single long session.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Compulsory, and the element most often neglected until its deadline. Support is about structuring an argument and understanding what the assessment asks for; the essay and exhibition remain the student's own work.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A four-thousand-word independent piece of research with a supervisor at school. Coaching covers question scoping, research planning and feedback on the student's drafts, and never extends to writing or rewriting any of it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.regionsTitle: Where Al Khawaneej students travel, and what each run costs in time
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.regionsIntro: This is the school-run geography that decides an Al Khawaneej evening. The notes are about journeys and clock time rather than about what each place is like.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: The nearest substantial school cluster and the destination for a large share of Al Khawaneej secondary students. The shortest of the regular runs, and the one that leaves the most usable evening behind it.

regions.name: Al Mizhar
regions.note: Immediately adjacent, sharing the same road network and much of the same school cluster. Families in the two communities face near-identical timetables, which is why advice that works in one works in the other.

regions.name: Al Warqa
regions.note: A longer run towards the biggest cohorts in eastern Dubai. Buses serving these schools make multiple stops, so the journey home is frequently longer than the journey out and arrival time is less predictable.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: Among the longest regular runs from Al Khawaneej. A student on this route loses the largest share of the evening to travel, and is the clearest case for moving demanding work to a weekend morning.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej 2 and Al Aweer
regions.note: The outer edge, with large plots and the longest pick-up times inside the community itself before the bus even leaves. Any in-home arrangement out here carries the full travel premium described below.

sections.heading: What time the day actually ends for an Al Khawaneej student
paragraphs: This is the number everything else depends on, and most families have never written it down. There is the time the school day finishes, which is what the school publishes. There is the time the bus leaves, which is later. There is the time the bus reaches Al Khawaneej, which depends on how many stops come before yours. And there is the time the student is actually at a desk, fed and capable of thinking, which is later again and is the only one that matters for booking a lesson.

For a student travelling to the Mirdif cluster the gap between the first number and the last is modest. For a student on a route to Al Qusais or deep into Al Warqa it can be an hour and a half or more, and on days with a co-curricular commitment after school it is longer still. That is not a complaint about the schools; it is the geography of a city where the eastern villa communities grew faster than secondary provision followed. It does mean that an arrangement designed around the published end of the school day will fail.

The practical exercise takes a week. Write down, each weekday, the time your child was genuinely ready to work. Not the time they walked in. The time the bag was down, the food was eaten and the first page was open. Five numbers later you will have the real window, and it is almost always later and shorter than expected. Book the session inside that window and attendance stops being a battle; book it outside and no amount of good teaching will survive.

sections.heading: What an in-home tutor costs in this part of Dubai, and what the money buys
paragraphs: Take the cheapest published figure first and work up, because that is the order a family actually encounters the market in. Tutopiya advertises online tuition from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from around AED 45 to 65, both drawing heavily on university students, several of whom study out at Academic City. Move up and Unitors publishes from AED 150 an hour for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialist tuition at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with BartyED at AED 650 for premium named teaching.

Now the in-home column. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors are quoted between AED 200 and 500. Monthly packages in circulation run AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits, against around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Set those two package prices side by side and the market has answered the question for you: the same quantity of teaching is priced at roughly double when somebody has to drive. All of these are provider-published figures read in October 2026, quoted here as market information rather than as IB Gram prices.

What the premium buys is presence in the room and an hour of a tutor's driving, in that order. What it does not buy is a wider choice of teacher. A tutor willing to drive to Al Khawaneej on a Tuesday evening is a small subset of the Diploma teachers in Dubai, and for a scarce subject at Higher Level the subset may be empty. The alternative is not worse teaching for less money. It is the same money spent on a subject specialist who does not have to be in the car, with the session starting at the hour your child can use rather than the hour the traffic allows.

sections.heading: Designing the week when the evenings are short
paragraphs: Once the real window is measured, the week can be designed instead of hoped for. The principle is simple: put the work that needs a rested brain where a rested brain exists, and put the work that tolerates tiredness in the leftover time. Most families do the reverse, giving mathematics the weekday slot after a ninety-minute bus ride and leaving the weekend for nothing in particular.

Weekend mornings in the UAE are the single most underused resource in a Diploma household. Saturday at nine in the morning is a completely different student from Thursday at six in the evening, and it costs the family one hour of a two-day weekend. The trade that persuades most students is explicit: one weekend morning hour in exchange for one weekday evening with no academic work at all. The total hours are the same and the output is not.

Mid-week placement matters for a smaller reason that adds up. A session early in the school week gives a student days to act on what was fixed, and the tutor can ask about it at the next session. A session on the last evening of the school week lands feedback into a weekend and it is usually gone by Monday. Over a term that difference is worth a surprising amount. During Ramadan the whole structure moves later rather than pausing, which keeps the year continuous instead of leaving a four-week hole. None of this requires more hours than a family is already spending.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child in the UAE
paragraphs: This is worth knowing before you invite anybody into an arrangement, in-home or otherwise. Private tutoring in the UAE operates under a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

The practical consequences for an Al Khawaneej family are three. A tutor who tells you no permit is required is wrong: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the Ministry are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount you are quoted as a deterrent is unverified and should be treated as such. And because the permit costs nothing, a licensing fee added to your invoice deserves a direct question about what it covers.

There is a further point about school staff. Press reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff there may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify current wording with the relevant authority before relying on it. Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is an entirely different instrument from an individual's permit. IB Gram has no UAE premises and holds no KHDA permit, and does not describe itself as KHDA approved.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and where coaching stops
paragraphs: Diploma students carry three core elements alongside their six subjects, and two of them produce written work that is assessed. The Extended Essay is four thousand words of independent research with a school supervisor. Theory of Knowledge produces an essay and an exhibition. Each subject also produces an internal assessment. All of this has to be the student's own work, and the boundary between useful coaching and malpractice is worth stating in both directions.

A coach may help a student narrow a research question until it is answerable in the word count, plan a research timetable backwards from the school's internal deadlines, explain what the assessment criteria reward, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A coach may not write any part of it, rewrite the student's sentences into their own voice, supply the argument, or produce the data. Operators in this market sell completed Internal Assessments outright; a student who submits one risks their entire Diploma, and IB Gram will not produce assessed work at any price.

There is a scheduling point hidden in this. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are the elements most often left too late, because they have no weekly homework to force progress and their deadlines are months away. For a student with a short weekday window, the only realistic place for sustained essay work is a weekend morning, which is another argument for protecting that hour from the start of the Diploma rather than discovering the need for it in the final term.

sections.heading: Equivalency and attestation: the paperwork nobody mentions until Year 13
paragraphs: A Diploma student in Dubai who intends to study at a UAE university will meet the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, and it is better met in the first Diploma year than in the last term of the second. Equivalency is the Ministry's recognition of a foreign school certificate, and it has published requirements per curriculum track. It is a regulatory process the Ministry runs; no tutoring provider performs it, guarantees it or speeds it up, and anybody telling you otherwise is selling something.

The British track's requirements are published and specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor page states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which is wrong, and inheriting that error costs a family real planning time. The American track requires English proficiency evidenced by an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61 or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the International Baccalaureate specifically, no points threshold is published here, and none should be taken from a tutoring page. Verify the current IB requirement on the Ministry's own channels or with your school's university counsellor before planning around any figure. The practical advice for an Al Khawaneej family is the dull but effective kind: ask the school's counsellor in the first Diploma year what the current equivalency route looks like for your child's intended destination, and keep the documents you are told to keep. Tutoring is about the grades, not the paperwork.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we will tell you about availability
paragraphs: Begin by measuring the week, as described above, because it changes which conversations are worth having. Then send two things: the most recent marked piece of work in the subject that prompted the enquiry, with the teacher's comments left on, and the school's list of internal deadlines for the term. The first gives the diagnosis and the second gives the shape of the next two months.

Then a free trial lesson, one-to-one over live video, used as a diagnostic rather than a demonstration. Ask the tutor to work through the marked script and name where the marks went. An hour that ends with a specific answer and a plan is worth booking against. An hour spent on the tutor's own background is not, however impressive the background. If the match is wrong, say so in the first week; that is normal and costs nothing early.

Here is the limit, before you have to ask for it. Higher Level specialists in the scarcer Diploma subjects are thin on the ground, and in some weeks no UAE-based specialist holds an evening slot that fits an Al Khawaneej timetable. Where that happens you will be told and offered a specialist based elsewhere, teaching the same course over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time. What will not happen is a general tutor being presented as a subject specialist because the schedule was awkward. No competitor page reviewed for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to homes in Al Khawaneej?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For UAE families, teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own work on screen. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation. It removes a drive from both sides of the arrangement, which lets the session start when your child is actually ready, and it widens the choice of teacher from whoever will travel east to whoever teaches the subject at the right level.

faqs.question: How much does an in-home tutor cost in the eastern suburbs of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's Dubai rate table, with independent home tutors quoted between AED 200 and 500 an hour. Monthly in-home packages circulate at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Set against around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, the market is pricing the same quantity of teaching at roughly double when somebody has to drive. These are provider-published figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start for a student travelling home to Al Khawaneej?
faqs.answer: Later than the school day ends, and the gap is bigger than most families assume. There are four different times involved: the bell, the bus departure, the arrival in Al Khawaneej and the moment a student is fed and genuinely able to work. For a long run to Al Qusais or Al Warqa, the gap between the first and the last can exceed an hour and a half. Measure it across one week by writing down when the first page was actually open, then book inside that window.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Khawaneej secondary students usually attend?
faqs.answer: The community holds primary provision and a Dubai Schools campus, so secondary students generally travel out, most often west to the Mirdif and Al Mizhar cluster and sometimes further to the larger schools in Al Warqa, Al Qusais or Silicon Oasis. That single fact shapes the family timetable more than anything academic does. Students we support attend schools across both groups, and naming them implies no affiliation, endorsement or partnership with any of them.

faqs.question: Is a weekend morning session really better than a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: For work that needs sustained thought, usually yes, and by a wide margin. A rested student at nine on a Saturday morning is a different student from one who arrived home at five after ninety minutes on a bus. The trade that persuades most families is explicit: one weekend morning hour in exchange for one weekday evening with no academic work at all. The hours are the same and the output is not. Mathematics, Extended Essay drafting and analytical writing belong in that slot.

faqs.question: My child has co-curricular activities after school. How does tutoring fit?
faqs.answer: It does not, on those days, and planning as though it does is what breaks arrangements. On a day with a commitment after school, a student travelling back to Al Khawaneej has no usable academic window left, and a session booked there will be attended badly or cancelled late. Treat those days as scheduled no-tutoring days, put the weekly session on a clear evening early in the school week, and use a weekend morning for anything that needs real concentration.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring as effective for an IB Diploma student as somebody in the room?
faqs.answer: For one-to-one work on a specific subject, the evidence families report is that the format matters far less than two other things: whether the tutor actually specialises in the subject at that level, and whether the session is placed when the student can concentrate. Online teaching tends to win on both, because it removes the travel filter from the choice of tutor and the travel delay from the start time. A shared whiteboard and the student's own script on screen covers the working methods a Diploma subject needs.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working with Al Khawaneej families need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount quoted to you as unverified.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without writing it?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a line worth stating both ways. A coach may help narrow the research question until it is answerable in four thousand words, build a research timetable backwards from the school's internal deadlines, explain what the criteria reward, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A coach may not write any part of it, rewrite the student's sentences, supply the argument or produce the data. The essay is submitted as the student's own work, and operators selling finished coursework put that at risk.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Diploma student in Al Khawaneej start with?
faqs.answer: One, placed well, for most students. A second is worth adding for a specific reason: a subject that has collapsed, a cluster of internal deadlines, or a mock window. For a student with a ninety-minute usable weekday evening, a second weekly session frequently displaces work rather than adding to it. Two short sessions on separate days beat one long block for problem-based subjects, and a weekend morning plus one short weekday evening is the arrangement that holds up best over a term.

faqs.question: What happens to tutoring during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Sessions move rather than stop. School days shorten, the household rhythm shifts and the useful working window moves into the evening after Iftar, so the weekly slot moves there and the year stays continuous. Families who pause for the month consistently find the restart costs more than the break saved, because work that had been secured has to be rebuilt. Confirm your own school's published Ramadan timings, which vary between schools in this catchment and change the available window.

faqs.question: My child is in the first Diploma year and already behind. What should the first month do?
faqs.answer: Diagnose rather than cover. The first Diploma year goes wrong in predictable places: quantitative fluency for students arriving from a criterion-assessed programme, and independent written work for students arriving from a heavily scaffolded one. A marked script and one session usually separate the two. The first month should fix whichever it is, not attempt a sweep of the syllabus, because a student who cannot start a question unaided will not be helped by meeting more content they cannot start questions on.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is available for my child's Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You will be told, before you book. Specialists in the scarcer Higher Level subjects are thin on the ground, and in some weeks nobody UAE-based holds an evening slot that fits an Al Khawaneej timetable. Where that is the case, the alternative offered is a specialist based elsewhere teaching the same course over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time. What will not happen is a general tutor being presented as a subject specialist because the schedule was difficult to fill.

faqs.question: What should an Al Khawaneej family send before the first Diploma session?
faqs.answer: Three things. The most recent marked piece of work in the subject that prompted the enquiry, with the teacher's comments left on. The school's list of internal deadlines for the term, so the plan is built against real dates rather than an assumed uniform term. And the measured time your child is genuinely able to work on a weekday. The first two produce a diagnosis and a timeline; the third decides whether the slot you book is one that will still be running in week nine.

Write down for one week when your child was genuinely ready to work, and the right slot becomes obvious. Then compare honestly: the in-home market prices eight hours of teaching at roughly double the online figure, and the premium buys a drive rather than a better teacher. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and does not visit UAE homes. Send a marked script, take the free trial as a diagnostic, and judge it on whether it told you where the marks went.

intro.heading: Al Mamzar runs on a school-run clock, and tuition has to fit inside it
paragraphs: Al Mamzar is a narrow coastal strip at the top of Deira, pressed between Al Mamzar Beach Park, the Corniche and the creek that marks the Sharjah border at Al Khan. Almost nobody who lives here goes to school here. Children leave the district every morning on buses bound for Al Garhoud, Al Qusais, Oud Metha, Mirdif and Al Nahda, and they come back between ten past three and five past four depending on which bus route they are on and how the Al Ittihad Road interchange is behaving. That single fact shapes everything about tutoring in this neighbourhood.

A parent typing "IB home tutor in Al Mamzar" into Google is rarely asking for a stranger in the living room. They are asking for the hour between the bus and dinner to produce something. The classic in-home arrangement works against that hour rather than with it. A Diploma specialist who lives in Jumeirah or Al Barsha will spend forty to seventy minutes crossing the city at 4.30pm, and the Sharjah-bound evening flow through Al Mamzar and Al Nahda is among the slowest stretches in the emirate. The tutor arrives tired, the clock has already eaten the slot, and the family pays for the travel inside the hourly rate.

IB Gram works the other way round. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, and the tutor is chosen for the subject and the level rather than for the postcode. A student at a Deira school sitting Chemistry HL gets a Chemistry HL teacher. A student halfway through a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches internal assessment gets somebody who has read a pile of those explorations against the published criteria. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and pretending otherwise on a Dubai page would be dishonest.

The trade is worth naming plainly. You lose the physical presence of an adult at the table, which matters for some younger students and for a few families who want a visible supervisor. You gain a far wider pool of subject specialists, a session that starts on time because nobody is parking, and a rate that is not carrying a driver's hour. The tables further down this page put real AED figures against both options so the comparison is yours to make rather than ours to assert.

Dubai gives this decision a particular texture. The emirate held 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen curricula, with UK programmes at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, American at 14 and the IB at 7. That last figure is small, and it is the whole reason a neighbourhood-radius search for a Diploma tutor so often comes back empty. There are simply not many IB households per square kilometre in Deira, and the ones there are tend to cluster around three or four schools.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mamzar.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the three IB programmes a Deira family is likely to meet, plus the IGCSE year that sits between them in most British-curriculum schools near Al Mamzar. Each note below is written for this part of Dubai rather than for the UAE in general.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Progress is read through transdisciplinary units, the exhibition in the final year, and the teacher's own assessment against learner-profile attributes. Tutoring at this stage is about literacy fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining reasoning aloud, because every later IB course rewards a student who can say why rather than only what.
programmes.countryNote: Al Mamzar's PYP families mostly travel to Mirdif or Al Garhoud. A 4.15pm session works well for this age group because the bus arrives earlier for primary routes, and thirty to forty minutes is the honest ceiling for concentration after a full day plus a bus ride in the heat.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks are reported on four criteria per subject, each out of eight, and converted to a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. Students who drift here usually understand the content and lose marks on criterion wording: an investigation that never states a hypothesis, or a reflection that describes rather than evaluates. That is a fixable, teachable gap.
programmes.countryNote: Uptown International School in Mirdif runs the full MYP and draws from the northern Dubai belt, including Al Mamzar. Students arriving from a CBSE or British primary often meet criterion-based marking for the first time in Year 7, and the first two reports are where a Deira family usually decides tuition is needed.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The grade is built from externally marked papers and internally assessed coursework that is externally moderated. Two years is less time than it sounds, because the internal assessment deadlines in each subject cluster into a single autumn term in Year 13.
programmes.countryNote: Deira International School and Universal American School Dubai are the closest Diploma centres to Al Mamzar, both a short run down Al Garhoud. UAE schools sit the May session, so a Year 13 student here spends the second half of the autumn term on internal assessments and the spring on past papers.

programmes.name: IGCSE, the year before the Diploma
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools near Al Mamzar run Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE at 16 and then split students into A Level or the IB Diploma. The two boards tier differently, Cambridge through Core and Extended and Pearson through a single tier with stepped questions, and that difference changes what revision should look like.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Scholars Private School in Al Qusais and St Mary's Catholic High School in Oud Metha both take students from this part of Deira. A family planning a move into the Diploma at 16 is best served by using the IGCSE years to build algebraic fluency and written explanation, which is where Diploma entrants most often arrive short.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mamzar.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and MYP subjects Deira families book most often, with a note on where marks actually go missing. The description is deliberately specific: a tutor who cannot name the failure mode cannot fix it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation carry the HL paper. Marks leak in Paper 1, where no calculator is allowed and students who have learned the graphing display instead of the algebra stall on exact values. The exploration rewards a genuine mathematical question, not a survey dressed up with regression.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and financial mathematics dominate. The common loss is interpretation: a correct chi-squared statistic with no sentence saying what it means about the data. HL adds matrices, graph theory and a heavier modelling load that catches students who chose AI expecting an easier ride.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward students who draw the free-body diagram before reaching for an equation. Paper 2 extended response is where marks go, because a numerical answer without units, significant figures or a stated assumption is marked down even when the physics is right.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are the three reliable stumbling blocks. HL organic demands curly arrows drawn from the correct electron source, which is a drawing skill as much as a chemistry one. The internal assessment needs a measurable variable and honest uncertainty treatment.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume is the problem rather than the difficulty. Students who revise by rereading lose marks on command terms, because 'outline' and 'explain' are scored against different mark allocations. Statistics in the internal assessment are usually the weakest section of an otherwise good investigation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry the paper. A correctly labelled diagram with the shift arrow and the new equilibrium annotated earns marks that prose cannot recover. HL quantitative questions are a separate skill, and the three commentaries need real published articles with clear theory links.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen non-literary analysis under time pressure, and the individual oral asks for a global issue traced through two works. Students who write beautifully about meaning but never discuss how form creates it cap themselves well below the top bands.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are applied, not described. A SWOT that lists items without evaluating which matters most to the stated firm earns little. HL adds the research project, which stands or falls on whether the student secured real primary data from an actual organisation early enough.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition requires three objects answering one prompt, and the essay responds to one of six prescribed titles. The usual failure is writing about the world rather than about knowledge: examples without a knowledge question attached score in the lowest bands regardless of how well written they are.

subjects.name: MYP Integrated Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion B and C carry the investigation: variables identified, method replicable, data processed, conclusion referenced to the hypothesis. Students who do good practical work and then write a thin conclusion lose half the available marks in a single paragraph.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in Al Mamzar is actually asking
paragraphs: The literal answer first. In-home IB tuition does exist in this part of Dubai, charged by the market at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel folded in, usually on a minimum of ninety minutes. IB Gram does not sell it. Our UAE delivery is one-to-one over live video, and home visits are an India-only service. If a tutor at the dining table is the only arrangement you will consider, this page will still be useful to you, because it tells you what the market charges and what to ask before you book anyone.

What most parents in Al Mamzar actually want is narrower than the phrase suggests. They want the hour after the bus to be supervised, productive and taught by somebody who knows the Diploma. The word "home" in the search is carrying the idea of convenience rather than the idea of a visitor. Once you separate the two, the question becomes which arrangement delivers a Diploma specialist into that hour most reliably, and in a district where IB households are thinly spread, the answer is not the one that depends on a car.

There is a second thing hidden in the search. Families in Deira often have more than one child, in more than one curriculum, in more than one school. A single travelling tutor gets booked for two hours to cover two children, and the second child invariably gets the tired half. Splitting that into two separate online bookings with two subject specialists costs about the same and gives both children a real teacher. That is a boring, practical point, and it is the one that changes outcomes most often.

So the honest framing for this page: take the home-tutoring question seriously, price it properly, then show what the same money buys when the travel comes out. The next two sections do exactly that, starting with the clock, because in Al Mamzar the clock is the binding constraint.
bullets: In-home IB tuition in Dubai: market rate roughly AED 180-500 per hour, travel included
IB Gram's UAE delivery: live one-to-one video, no home visits anywhere in the Emirates
Two children, two subjects, two specialists beats one tutor for two hours

sections.heading: The Al Mamzar school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: Nearly every school-age child in Al Mamzar leaves the district to go to school. The buses head south to Al Garhoud and Oud Metha, east to Al Qusais and Al Nahda, or out to Mirdif. Return times vary by thirty to fifty minutes depending on route length, and the Damascus Street and Al Ittihad Road queues add to that on any day with weather or an incident. A tutoring slot that ignores this gets cancelled in week three.

The table below is built from published school finish times and the realistic bus return for an Al Mamzar address, then works forward to the earliest hour a lesson can honestly start. It is not a promise about any particular bus; routes change each August. It is a planning tool, and it is the thing competitor pages for this neighbourhood do not give you.

The pattern it shows is consistent. Primary children are home first and should be taught first, while they still have attention left. Secondary students are home between 3.45pm and 4.30pm, which makes 4.30pm or 5.00pm the sensible Diploma slot, and 6.30pm the latest hour at which a Year 13 student will do real work rather than perform attendance. Families who try to squeeze a session into 3.30pm for a secondary child spend the first ten minutes waiting and the next ten unpacking a bag.

One more timing note that matters locally. Al Mamzar sits on the route out of Dubai towards Sharjah, and the evening outbound flow from 4.30pm onwards affects anything that has to move. An online session is indifferent to it. A travelling tutor is not, and this is where the comparison stops being theoretical.

sections.heading: What tuition costs in this corner of Dubai, in AED
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure, because that is the number a family actually budgets. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate work puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240 to 600 a month for a budget tutor, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-range qualified subject teacher, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for a specialist in an exam year. Packages sold in this market cluster around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Converted to an hourly view, the published figures line up into clear bands. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 for its cheapest online tiers, which buys a university student or a general tutor. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work. BartyED sits at AED 650 for a named premium tutor. In-home visits across Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, and that spread is mostly travel.

Three of the six best-ranking pages for Dubai tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays school fees in. That is why the table below exists. These are market bands gathered from competitors' own published rates and from the Bestimate survey, read in October 2026. They are not an IB Gram price list, and nothing on this page should be read as one. Our own rates depend on subject, level and session length, and the free trial lesson comes before any payment.

Where the money is wasted is worth saying out loud. It is wasted on a cheap general tutor for a Higher Level subject, because the tutor cannot mark the work. It is wasted on two-hour blocks for a Year 9 student, because the second hour produces nothing. And in Al Mamzar it is wasted on travel: at the top of the in-home band, a meaningful share of an hourly rate is paying for a car to sit on Al Ittihad Road.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for an Al Mamzar address
paragraphs: Set the two arrangements side by side on the things that actually differ, and the picture is less about ideology than about logistics. The tutor pool is the first difference. Restricting a search to people willing to drive to Al Mamzar on a weekday evening narrows the field to whoever lives nearby and has a free car. For a common subject at Standard Level, that may be enough. For Physics HL, Chemistry HL or a Mathematics AA exploration, it usually is not, and the family ends up accepting a generalist because they were available.

The second difference is the shape of the hour. An online session begins at the stated minute. An in-home session begins when the tutor finds parking, which in the Corniche towers can take ten minutes on its own. Across a term of weekly hours, that is a measurable amount of teaching lost, and the family paid for all of it.

The third is what survives the session. Board work from a video lesson is saved and can be reread the night before a test. A whiteboard in a living room is wiped. That sounds minor until a student is revising in March for a May paper and wants the worked example from October.

Against all that, in-home tuition has two honest advantages. A physically present adult keeps a distractible younger child on task in a way a screen does not, and some families simply prefer it. Neither advantage is imaginary. They are just rarely worth the travel premium for a Diploma subject in a district this far from the city's tutoring supply.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and the Al Mamzar week
paragraphs: Dubai private schools shorten the day during Ramadan, and the whole tutoring pattern in Deira shifts with it. Buses come back earlier, families eat late, and the hours between Iftar and midnight become the productive part of the evening for older students. A tutor who can only offer a 5pm slot is close to useless for a month. An online tutor who can move to 9pm for four weeks is not.

This matters more in Al Mamzar than in some western Dubai neighbourhoods because the district's rhythm is tied to the Deira community and to the Sharjah crossing. Evening movement in Ramadan around Al Mamzar and Al Nahda is heavy in the hour before Iftar and heavy again afterwards. A travelling tutor's reliability drops exactly when a Year 13 student has internal assessment deadlines to meet.

The practical plan we use with families here is to agree a Ramadan timetable in advance rather than week by week. Two post-Iftar sessions a week, usually between 8.30pm and 10.00pm, shorter than the normal hour, focused on one thing each. Younger students move the other way, to a late-morning or early-afternoon slot on the weekend, because an eleven-year-old at 9pm is not learning anything.

The same flexibility covers prayer times, Friday timings and the long summer break. Sessions can be booked around Jummah, and students who travel in July and August can keep a reduced schedule from wherever they are, since the lesson follows the student rather than the address. Families who leave the UAE for six weeks and come back cold in September are the ones who lose the most ground.

sections.heading: The assessment year, counted backwards
paragraphs: Almost nothing published for Dubai tutoring queries mentions an exam session at all. That is a strange omission, because the session is the only fixed point in the year and every sensible tutoring plan is built backwards from it. UAE schools sit the May IB session. Cambridge offers its February and March series to India only, so a Cambridge candidate in Dubai works to the June series with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

The dates that can be stated with confidence are the Pearson ones, because Pearson publishes them. Its November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking facts a parent can check. Future windows should always be read off the live official timetable rather than from any page like this one, because provisional timetables get revised.

For the IB, we do not publish session dates. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a wrong date in an FAQ is worse than no date, so the right source is your child's IB coordinator. What can be said is the shape of the year: internal assessment deadlines cluster in the autumn of Year 13, the Extended Essay is finished before them, mocks land in the winter, and the spring term is past papers.

One Cambridge detail worth knowing, because it bites every year. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the school which zone it sits in before you plan a single revision week.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the line that separates a tutor from a problem. IB academic honesty rules make the student the author of every piece of assessed work, and a breach is investigated as malpractice with consequences that reach the whole Diploma, not just the one subject. At least one site ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed internal assessments outright. Buying one puts a student's entire Diploma at risk, and no grade is worth that.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria, letter by letter, with the mark allocation for each. A tutor may discuss whether a proposed research question is answerable in the word count. A tutor may read a draft the student wrote and say which criterion is underserved and why. A tutor may ask the questions an examiner would ask and let the student find the answers. A tutor may teach the statistics, the referencing convention or the lab technique the work needs.

What a tutor may not do is write, redraft to completion, supply text to paste, or hand over a worked exploration for adaptation. IB Gram tutors do not produce assessed work for students, and a request to do so is declined. That is a plain commercial statement as much as an ethical one: the review is only worth paying for if the work being reviewed is genuinely the student's.

A practical consequence for Al Mamzar families on a deadline. The most useful internal assessment coaching happens before the first draft, not after it. A student who has understood criterion wording in week one writes a better exploration in week four than a student who writes something and then pays somebody to repair it. Book the criteria session early; it is the cheapest hour in the whole process.
bullets: Allowed: teaching criteria, scrutinising a research question, feeding back on the student's draft
Not allowed: writing, completing, rewriting or supplying text for assessed work
Official syllabus documents and mark schemes are linked, never reproduced or supplied
Earliest sessions are the valuable ones; repair work after a draft is the expensive kind

sections.heading: KHDA, the tutor permit, and what an Al Mamzar parent can verify
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the published report for your child's school is a free, detailed read on the authority's own site. It is the most useful document most parents never open.

KHDA does not license individual tutors, and no tutor should be described as approved by it. What KHDA issues is an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, a process that begins with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requires renewal at least thirty days before expiry. Anyone claiming regulator approval for an individual tutor has misunderstood which permit does what.

The permit that does apply to an individual is federal. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists a two-working-day completion time and is applied for through the ministry's app, website or e-services. Working without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Three things an Al Mamzar parent can check before paying anybody. Ask to see the MoHRE permit. Ask which exam board and specification the tutor teaches, by code, not by name. And ask who marks the work: a tutor who cannot mark a past paper against the published mark scheme is supervising homework, which is a reasonable service at a reasonable price but is not subject tuition. Abu Dhabi families should also note that ADEK's ethics rules bar school staff there from paid tutoring of pupils at their own school, which is a rule worth understanding wherever you live.
bullets: KHDA inspects schools; it does not license individual private tutors
The MoHRE private tuition permit is free and valid for two years

process.description: Weekly slot, subject sequence, and the school's own internal assessment and mock dates written in. Ramadan timings are agreed in advance rather than improvised, and the plan is adjusted when the school changes its calendar.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not a radius
whyPoints.description: Matching by subject and level rather than by neighbourhood is the whole point. In a district where IB families are thinly spread, a search bounded by driving distance from Al Mamzar returns a short list of generalists; a search bounded by subject returns the teacher the paper needs.

whyPoints.title: Sessions timed to the bus
whyPoints.description: Slots start from 4.00pm Gulf Standard Time and move to the half hour. Ramadan, exam weeks and travel are planned for rather than apologised for, which is why these bookings survive past week three.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the rate
whyPoints.description: An online hour carries no driver's hour. The AED comparison table on this page shows where the in-home premium sits, and in a district on the Sharjah-bound evening route that premium is paid almost entirely in traffic.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not produce internal assessments, Extended Essays or TOK essays. That line protects the Diploma, and we would rather lose a booking than cross it.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the competitor or survey that published it, with the month it was read. We publish no satisfaction statistics, no star ratings and no grade promises, because none of those could be evidenced.

whyPoints.description: If no specialist covers a niche Higher Level subject at your hour, we say so and give you the realistic wait rather than booking somebody unsuitable. A disclosed gap is worth more to a parent than a filled slot.

faqs.question: Can I actually get a home tutor who comes to our flat in Al Mamzar?
faqs.answer: In-home tutoring does exist in Dubai, at market rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel folded in, usually on a ninety-minute minimum. IB Gram does not sell it anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Our Al Mamzar lessons are one-to-one over live video, which means the tutor is picked for the subject rather than for living near the Corniche. If a physically present adult is non-negotiable for you, use the questions in the regulator section of this page to vet whoever you hire.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session realistically start in Al Mamzar on a school day?
faqs.answer: Four o'clock is the earliest honest answer for a secondary student, and 4.30pm is safer. Almost every child in Al Mamzar is bussed out of the district, to Al Garhoud, Al Qusais, Al Nahda, Mirdif or Oud Metha, and the return leg runs thirty to fifty-five minutes depending on the route. Add ten minutes for a bag and a drink. Primary children come back earlier and should be taught earlier, around 3.45pm to 4.15pm, while their concentration is still there.

faqs.question: Which schools near Al Mamzar actually offer the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The nearest Diploma centres are in Al Garhoud, roughly fifteen minutes away off-peak: Deira International School and Universal American School Dubai. Uptown International School in Mirdif runs the full continuum from Primary Years through to the Diploma and draws from the northern Dubai belt. Al Ittihad Private School Mamzar sits inside the district itself. Only about seven per cent of Dubai's private-school pupils follow the IB, which is why a neighbourhood-level search for a Diploma tutor so often comes back nearly empty.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book online tuition than a tutor who drives to Deira?
faqs.answer: On published market figures, yes, and the gap is mostly travel. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one in Dubai at AED 180 to 350 an hour, independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, while qualified online subject tutors are published from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB by Unitors. Monthly, that is the difference between packages around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits. Figures read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers who published them.

faqs.question: How does the evening traffic towards Sharjah affect our tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: It affects anything that has to move. Al Mamzar sits on the outbound route towards the Sharjah border at Al Khan, and the flow through Al Mamzar and Al Nahda is heavy from about 4.30pm until 7.00pm on weekdays. A travelling tutor's arrival time becomes a guess, and the guess is worst in the exact window a Year 12 or 13 student should be working. An online session is unaffected: it starts at the booked minute, and it can be moved to the half hour if your own evening changes.

faqs.question: My child is at a school in Al Qusais but we live in Al Mamzar. Does that matter for tutoring?
faqs.answer: It matters for the timetable rather than the teaching. A bus from Al Qusais to Al Mamzar runs thirty-five to fifty minutes in the afternoon, so a day ending at 2.30pm puts your child home nearer 3.30pm. That pushes a sensible start to 4.00pm or later. It also means the tutor needs the school's scheme of work, not a generic syllabus plan, because Dubai Scholars, Westminster and Apple International all sequence topics differently within the same specification.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both my children if they are in different year groups?
faqs.answer: We would rather not, and the reason is honest. A single tutor booked for two hours to cover two children usually gives the second child the tired half, and if the children are in different programmes the tutor is a specialist in at most one of them. Two separate bookings with two subject specialists cost about the same in this market and produce better work. If budget is the constraint, it is usually better to run one child's subject weekly and the other fortnightly than to split one tutor.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge exam series will my child in Dubai sit?
faqs.answer: June, with November available as the resit route. Cambridge offers its February and March series to India only, so a candidate sitting in the UAE should never be planning around those dates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. One Cambridge administrative detail is worth checking with the school: every centre is allocated to one of six zones, Cambridge says it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and it states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: Do tutors coming to an Al Mamzar address need a permit, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE free of charge, and is valid for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time. Ask any tutor to show you theirs. Working without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no official fine schedule is published, so treat a quoted figure sceptically.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Mathematics AA exploration without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful help comes early. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria with their mark allocations, test whether a proposed question is actually mathematical rather than a survey with regression attached, read a draft your daughter has written and name which criterion is underserved, and teach any statistics or notation the work needs. A tutor cannot write it, redraft it to completion or supply text to paste in. IB Gram declines requests to produce assessed work, because a malpractice finding reaches the whole Diploma.

faqs.question: How do Ramadan timings change a weekly tutoring arrangement here?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, families eat late, and the productive hours for older students move after Iftar. We agree a Ramadan timetable in advance rather than improvising: usually two shorter sessions a week between about 8.30pm and 10.00pm for Years 11 to 13, each focused on one thing. Younger students go the other way, to a weekend daytime slot, because an eleven-year-old at 9pm learns very little. Sessions can also be booked around Jummah and prayer times on request.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor before paying for a first session?
faqs.answer: Four questions sort most of it. Can you show me your MoHRE private tuition permit? Which specification do you teach, by code rather than by name? Will you mark a past paper against the published mark scheme and show me where the examiner stopped awarding credit? And what will you not do with my child's internal assessment? A tutor who answers the fourth question clearly is usually sound on the rest. Any claim of regulator approval for an individual tutor is a reason to walk away.

faqs.question: Is online teaching workable for a student who says they learn better in person?
faqs.answer: Often, though not always, and the distinction is age rather than preference. A Year 12 or 13 student working on a shared screen with a specialist who can annotate their own marked script usually gets more from the hour than from a generalist sitting beside them. A distractible nine-year-old may genuinely need a present adult, and we will say so. The practical test is the free trial lesson: one real session on current work tells you more than any argument on a web page.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for a niche Higher Level subject at our hour?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we give a realistic wait rather than filling the slot. Niche Higher Level subjects, some language A options and a few of the less common sciences have genuinely thin cover at 4pm Gulf Standard Time, because that hour is busy. Usually the fix is a later slot, a weekend session, or a fortnightly arrangement with a stronger specialist instead of a weekly one with a weaker match. A disclosed gap is more useful to you than a booking that quietly disappoints.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mamzar.closingHeading: Start with the hour, then pick the teacher
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mamzar.closingBody: If your child is bussed out of Al Mamzar every morning and back in the late afternoon, the hour after that bus is the only reliable teaching window you have. Spending it on a tutor who is still on Al Ittihad Road is the most common mistake families here make. Tell us which school the bus comes from, what time it lands, and which subject is causing the trouble, and we will match a Diploma or Middle Years specialist to that exact slot. The first lesson is free and works on something real from the current unit, so you can judge the teaching before any money changes hands.

intro.heading: What an hour of IB tutoring is really worth in Al Manara
paragraphs: Al Manara sits between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Thanya Street, a low-rise villa district with no school inside its own boundary. That single fact sets the price of tutoring here. Every family on this grid drives out of it twice a day, and anyone hired to teach in your sitting room drives in. The drive is billable time in every quote you will receive, whether or not the invoice itemises it. Once the travel component is separated from the teaching component, the cost question in this neighbourhood becomes much easier to answer honestly.

The numbers themselves are not secret, they are simply scattered. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour. Tutopiya quotes from AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. BartyED charges AED 650 for a named examiner. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with specialist exam-year tutors running AED 200 to 450 and above. Five providers, five pricing logics, and almost no page in this search result that sets them side by side.

The spread is not random. It tracks three things: how specialised the teacher is, how much of the hour is spent travelling, and whether you are buying a single session or a block. A university student revising algebra costs a fraction of a Diploma Chemistry teacher who has marked the paper. An in-home arrangement adds thirty to fifty minutes of driving around a sixty-minute lesson, and somebody pays for that time. A monthly package smooths the headline rate but commits you before you know whether the match works for your child.

What this page does not contain is an IB Gram price list. Our rate depends on the subject, the level and the number of sessions, and it is quoted after a free trial lesson rather than before one. Publishing a single headline figure would repeat the trick the AED 45 advertisements play: a real number attached to a tutor your child will never actually be given. Every figure below belongs to the open market and carries the name of whoever published it, so you can check it yourself.

The last point before the tables start is the one that matters most. The money is usually not lost at the hourly rate. It is lost in the number of hours bought, the weeks they were bought in, and the gap between what the tutor knows and what the paper asks. A family paying AED 180 an hour for forty sessions of general maths has spent more, and gained less, than one paying AED 300 for twelve sessions aimed squarely at Paper 3. That arithmetic is the spine of this page.
