dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-manara.programmesIntro: Al Manara children sit across the whole IB continuum, because the schools either side of the district run different parts of it. The notes below are about cost and hours rather than curriculum theory: how much tutoring each programme typically absorbs, and at which point in the two years the spending actually concentrates.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme is transdisciplinary and reported against learner-profile strands rather than subject grades. Tutoring at this stage is almost always about English reading fluency or number sense, booked in thirty or forty-minute blocks because attention, not content, is the limiting factor. Market rates for primary support sit at the bottom of the band, and the honest advice for most Al Manara parents is fewer sessions than an agency will try to sell you.
programmes.countryNote: Raffles International School in Umm Suqeim and Al Ittihad Private School, Jumeira both run PYP within a short drive of Al Manara. A Dubai primary day ends between 2pm and 3pm, so a session can start at 3.30pm without eating into dinner. At that hour a tutor driving in from Al Barsha is sitting in Umm Al Sheif traffic, which is precisely what an in-home travel premium pays for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years grades run 1 to 8 against four published criteria per subject. Most of the money Al Manara families spend in MYP4 and MYP5 goes on maths and the sciences, where the jump into Diploma standards is steepest. The useful spend here is diagnostic: one or two sessions to find which criterion is pulling the grade down, then a short block aimed at that strand rather than at the subject as a whole.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah Baccalaureate School in Al Safa and Raffles World Academy in Umm Suqeim both carry Middle Years cohorts that Al Manara addresses feed. Parents often buy middle-school tutoring at Diploma intensity and Diploma prices, which is the most common overspend at this stage. Two sessions a month, reviewed each term against the criterion grades, usually achieves more than a weekly standing slot nobody ever cancels.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where the spend concentrates and where it is most often misdirected. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and an Internal Assessment in nearly every course. Paper weightings differ by subject, so an hour of general revision is worth less than an hour on the component carrying 35 per cent of the grade. Costed properly, a Diploma year is a sequence of short targeted blocks rather than a twenty-four-month subscription.
programmes.countryNote: GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh and Dubai American Academy in Al Barsha both run the Diploma, and both sit the May session. The expensive months for an Al Manara family are the Internal Assessment deadline run late in DP1 and the final eight weeks before the May papers. Spreading the same budget evenly across two years spends it at the wrong time, which is a quieter waste than overpaying per hour.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. It is far rarer in Dubai than the Diploma, and tutoring demand follows that scarcity. Where a family does need support, the cost question is almost always about the Diploma subjects inside the programme rather than the career-related component, which the school supervises directly and which no outside tutor should be shaping.
programmes.countryNote: Very few schools near Al Manara offer this programme, so a family needing help here is already looking outside the neighbourhood and well outside any sensible in-home radius. That is the clearest case in this district for live video delivery: the pool of people who have actually taught a reflective project is small, and it is not distributed by postcode or by driving distance.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-manara.subjectsIntro: The subject notes below are written from a cost angle: what each one typically absorbs in hours, and which component those hours should go to. Hourly rates do not vary much by subject in this market, but efficiency does. A Physics hour aimed at Paper 3 data analysis buys more than four hours of general Physics review.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 3 is Higher Level only and carries 20 per cent of the grade across two extended problem-solving questions. It is also where Dubai candidates lose the most marks, because school teaching frequently runs out of term before Paper 3 technique has been practised under time. Hours aimed here are the best-value maths hours in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: This route rewards modelling, statistics and graphical calculator fluency. Standard Level candidates often arrive assuming it is the easy option and discover the Paper 2 technology work is unforgiving about method marks. Three sessions on calculator discipline usually shift a grade further than ten sessions on algebraic manipulation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The practical scheme of work and the Paper 3 data questions are where marks disappear. Uncertainty arithmetic and gradient work from a drawn graph are cheap to fix and expensive to leave alone. Mechanics is usually sound by DP2; fields, circuits and the option topic usually are not.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry most of the lost marks at Higher Level. The Internal Assessment is 20 per cent of the grade and is the clearest legitimate use of paid hours, because feedback on a student's own draft is permitted under IB rules and raises the mark without crossing any line.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide Biology grades more than content recall does. Outline, explain and evaluate demand different answer lengths, and a student who writes an essay where outline was asked loses the minutes needed for the long-answer section. Two sessions on command terms is the cheapest useful intervention in this subject.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries built on published news articles form the Internal Assessment. Diagram accuracy and the depth of evaluation decide the marks. Higher Level adds Paper 3 quantitative work, which is formulaic and therefore the fastest part of the whole course to improve with a short block of hours.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, the Individual Oral is internally assessed, and Higher Level adds the HL Essay. Students here rarely need more content. They need a repeatable way into an unfamiliar text under timed conditions, which takes practice rather than reading lists.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The Higher Level extension and the research project carry the difference between grades. Markbands reward applying a tool to a specific context rather than reciting its definition, so sessions built around one case study are worth considerably more than sessions built around a glossary.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 2 covers the Higher Level option and the solution-development work inside the Internal Assessment absorbs most of the time. Pseudocode fluency is a cheap, high-return target: it appears in both papers and it is purely a practice problem rather than a comprehension one.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Theory of Knowledge is graded against a published rubric and affects the bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. A tutor may question an argument and point at a rubric strand. A tutor may not supply the exhibition or the essay. Hours spent here are coaching hours, and they should be billed and understood as such.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Al Manara costs, tier by tier
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Manara is quoted somewhere between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour, and the range is that wide because five different products are being sold under one phrase. At the bottom sit online platforms using university students: EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. In the middle sit qualified subject tutors working online, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. At the top sit named examiners, where BartyED quotes AED 650.

In-home delivery occupies its own band, because the quote has to absorb the journey. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. The same teacher, selling the same hour, prices it differently depending on whether a car is involved. That gap is the single most useful number in this whole search result, and almost nobody publishes it next to the online figure for comparison.

Read the table below as a market survey rather than a menu. Each band carries the name of a provider who published it, with the month it was read. IB Gram's own rate is not in the table, because it depends on the subject, the level and the number of sessions, and because quoting a single figure before a trial lesson tells you nothing useful. What the table does let you do is recognise an outlier when one lands in your inbox.

sections.heading: The travel premium, counted in minutes and dirhams
paragraphs: A sixty-minute in-home lesson in Al Manara is never sixty minutes of a tutor's afternoon. It is the lesson plus the drive in, plus the drive out, plus the margin they leave for Sheikh Zayed Road being Sheikh Zayed Road. A tutor living in Al Barsha and teaching one Al Manara student at 5pm has committed closer to two hours. The quote reflects that, as it should, and the honest question for a parent is what the extra dirhams are buying.

Set against the rate gap, the arithmetic is not subtle. If a qualified subject tutor is AED 200 an hour online and AED 300 an hour in person, the AED 100 difference is paying for the journey. Over a forty-session Diploma year that is AED 4,000 spent on driving. Nobody would write a cheque with that memo line, but it is what the invoice says once you separate the two components out.

There is a second cost that never appears on an invoice. The pool of tutors willing to drive to Al Manara at 5pm on a Tuesday is much smaller than the pool who can teach the subject. Hiring by driving radius means hiring from that smaller pool, and in narrow Higher Level subjects it can mean hiring nobody suitable at all. Al Manara families who insist on a local visit are, in practice, choosing availability over specialism without being told that is the trade. Over video that trade disappears, because the shortlist is drawn from whoever teaches the subject best rather than from whoever can reach Umm Suqeim Road before the traffic does.
bullets: Ask how far the tutor is travelling and what the journey adds to the rate

sections.heading: Four ways Al Manara families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: The first waste is buying a tutor instead of buying a diagnosis. A parent sees a 4 in Chemistry and books a weekly hour for a year. Nobody has established whether the 4 came from the Internal Assessment, from organic mechanisms, from timing on Paper 2 or from reading the command terms wrongly. Each of those has a different fix and three of the four are short. Two sessions spent working out which one it is pays for themselves several times over.

The second is paying Diploma prices for Middle Years problems. Families around Al Manara often start intensive weekly tutoring in MYP4, two years before any external paper exists. The grades are criterion-based and the gaps at that stage are usually habits rather than knowledge. Spending AED 250 an hour weekly for two years before the Diploma even starts leaves nothing in the budget for the eight weeks when it would genuinely matter.

The third is the standing slot nobody reviews. A weekly session booked in September is still running in March, charged in full, attended out of habit. The fourth is subject spread: funding all six Diploma subjects at once, lightly, rather than two properly. Grades move when a specific component improves. Six shallow hours a month move nothing and cost more than two deep ones. None of these four is about the hourly rate, which is why comparing rates alone is a poor way to control what you spend.
bullets: Buy a diagnosis before you buy a block of sessions
Match the intensity to the year, not to the worry
Put a review date on every arrangement and keep it
Fund two subjects properly rather than six subjects lightly
Decide in advance what evidence would make you stop

sections.heading: A two-year Diploma, costed end to end
paragraphs: Parents rarely get to see tutoring set against the other numbers in a Dubai school year, which makes a rate feel either outrageous or trivial depending on the day. Context helps. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are therefore a known quantity this year, which makes the variable spending easier to plan around.

The table below costs a two-year Diploma the way a family would actually buy it: light in DP1, heavier around the Internal Assessment deadlines, heaviest in the final eight weeks. The monthly figures come from Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions, which put budget support at AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-range at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. The pattern matters more than the totals.

What the table should make obvious is how much of a two-year budget disappears into the quiet terms if the arrangement is a subscription rather than a plan. A family spending AED 900 a month every month for twenty-four months has committed AED 21,600, much of it in terms where no assessment was pending. The same money concentrated into the Internal Assessment run and the pre-exam block buys roughly three times the sessions at the moments they change a grade. Written down two years ahead, that difference is the single largest controllable number in a Diploma budget, and it is decided by the calendar rather than by the hourly rate.

sections.heading: What an AED 45 hour actually contains
paragraphs: The cheapest advertised rates in this market are real, and understanding what sits behind them is more useful than dismissing them. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. At that price the teacher is usually a university student or a recent graduate, often teaching several subjects, almost always working from the textbook rather than from the assessment. That is a legitimate product. It is homework supervision, and homework supervision has a place.

What it is not is component-level teaching. Nobody at AED 45 an hour has the Chemistry Higher Level markbands in their head, knows that Paper 3 carries 20 per cent in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, or can tell you which criterion a Middle Years science investigation lost its marks against. Those things take years to learn and the people who know them charge accordingly. The error is not buying the cheap hour. The error is buying forty of them and expecting a Higher Level grade to move.

The useful way to think about it is cost per useful minute rather than cost per hour. An AED 45 hour where thirty minutes go on re-explaining what the textbook already said costs AED 1.50 per useful minute. An AED 250 hour spent entirely on timed Paper 3 technique with a teacher who has marked it costs AED 4.17 per useful minute, but the minutes are aimed at 20 per cent of the grade. For a DP2 student eight weeks out, the second is plainly the better purchase. For a Year 7 student who will not open a book, the first may well be.

sections.heading: What you are paying a tutor to do with an IA, EE or TOK essay, and what they must refuse
paragraphs: This is the part of the budget where families are most exposed, because the internally assessed components carry real weight and the market contains people who will simply write them. One agency in this search result sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying that is not an expensive shortcut, it is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the seller. No amount of money makes that a sensible purchase.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial, and it is worth paying for. They may help a student narrow a research question until it is actually answerable. They may question whether the data supports the conclusion. They may point at a criterion and ask the student to find where in their own draft that criterion is addressed. They may teach the difference between description and analysis, which is where most Internal Assessment marks are lost. All of that raises marks and none of it crosses any line.

What they must refuse is equally clear. They may not draft a section, rewrite a paragraph into their own prose, choose the topic for the student, or supply the Theory of Knowledge exhibition objects. IB Gram tutors work on the student's own writing and the student's own data, and say so when asked. Priced per hour, process coaching on the Internal Assessment is usually the best-value spending in the whole two years, because the component is worth 20 per cent in most sciences and the student keeps the skill.

sections.heading: Budgeting backwards from the exam series
paragraphs: Almost no competitor page in this search result names an exam series at all, which is strange, because the calendar decides when tutoring money is worth spending. The sequence runs the other way from how families plan it: results day sits at the end, but the decisions that control the grade sit nine to eighteen months earlier, in entry deadlines and internal coursework dates nobody circles on a kitchen calendar.

For the boards involved, the published positions are clear. Cambridge International runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, with Cambridge stating that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and in November; the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session, and the specific dates should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taken from any tutoring page, including this one.

Read the table as a spending schedule rather than a revision plan. The two rows that cost the most if missed are the entry deadline, where a tier chosen wrongly commits a whole year, and the mock window, which is the only honest diagnostic a parent gets before the real thing. Everything else on the list is downstream of those two. Always open the live official timetable on the board's own site, because provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and dates get revised.

sections.heading: The permit, the regulator and the cost of getting this wrong
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a parent in Al Manara paying AED 300 an hour has a straightforward right to ask about it. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone offering private tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no figure is quoted here.

The eligibility list is wider than most parents expect. It includes teachers working in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The permit is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, a tutor who has not obtained one has no economic excuse for the omission.

Two further points matter for spending decisions. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also restricts serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, so hiring your child's own teacher privately is not the easy win it looks like. Separately, a tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different instrument from an individual's permit and should never be implied by either party. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of either kind and does not describe itself as having one.

sections.heading: Equivalency, attestation and why neither changes your tutoring budget
paragraphs: Families in Al Manara planning on a UAE university sooner or later meet the Ministry of Education equivalency process, and the market around it contains a quantity of confident misinformation. One page currently ranking tells UAE parents their child must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced rule is five. Getting this wrong by one subject is an expensive planning error, and it is exactly the kind of thing a tutoring page should get right rather than guess at.

For the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. For the American track, English proficiency is satisfied by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB, no points threshold appears in the source consulted, so none is stated here: verify it on moe.gov.ae.

The budget implication is smaller than families fear. Equivalency is a documentation process, not an examination, and no tutoring is required for it. IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency or attestation, and no tutoring page should present itself as a route through a regulatory process. What tutoring can usefully do is make sure the five subjects your child is relying on are actually the five likely to clear the grade bar, which is a conversation to have in Year 10, not in Year 13.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: Start with the specific thing that is going wrong: a Paper 3 mark, an Internal Assessment criterion, a mock grade that dropped. A subject name alone leads to a generalist and a long arrangement. A named component leads to a specialist and a shorter one, which is cheaper and usually works better.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson before any payment
process.description: The trial lesson costs nothing and needs no card details. Use it as a diagnostic rather than a demonstration: ask the tutor what they would change first and why. If the answer is generic, the match is wrong, and finding that out before you have paid for a block is the whole point of the trial.

process.title: Agree the number of sessions and the review point
process.description: Decide together how many sessions the specific problem should take and what evidence would show it is fixed. Write the review date down. An arrangement with no end condition drifts into a subscription, and a subscription is how a reasonable hourly rate turns into an unreasonable annual total.

process.title: Schedule around the real Al Manara afternoon
process.description: Dubai school days end between 2pm and 3.30pm depending on the school, and the drive home from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh eats the next hour. Pick a slot that survives a bad traffic day, usually 5pm or later, and keep it consistent so the session becomes a habit rather than a negotiation.

process.title: Concentrate the spending where the calendar says it counts
process.description: Light support in the settling terms, heavier through the Internal Assessment deadlines, heaviest in the final eight weeks before the papers. The same budget spent in that shape buys roughly three times the sessions at the points where a grade actually moves. Spread evenly, most of it lands in terms where nothing was due.

process.title: Review against the mock paper, then stop or continue
process.description: The mock is the only independent evidence a parent gets before the real series. Read the paper itself rather than the grade, and decide from that whether to extend, redirect or end the arrangement. Stopping when a problem is fixed is a legitimate outcome, and the best tutors say so first.

whyPoints.description: Each AED figure names the provider who published it and the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. A number you can check is worth more than an adjective you cannot.

This one puts the round trip from six origins into a table with the effect on the quote. You may still decide the premium is worth paying, but you will be deciding it with the number in front of you.

whyPoints.description: IB Gram delivers one-to-one lessons over live video to UAE families. Home visiting is a service the platform runs in India, not here, and this page says so plainly rather than leaving the URL to imply otherwise. Knowing what is not on offer is part of knowing what is.

whyPoints.title: Specialism beats proximity on Higher Level subjects
whyPoints.description: Hiring by driving radius means hiring from the much smaller pool who will come to Al Manara at 5pm. Over video the constraint disappears, which is why a family here can work with a Chemistry Higher Level specialist instead of whoever lives nearest Al Thanya Street and is free on a Tuesday.

whyPoints.description: Tutors review and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not draft Internal Assessments, Extended Essays or Theory of Knowledge essays, and they say so when asked. One agency in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice risk carried entirely by the student.

whyPoints.description: The trial is one lesson, before any payment, with no card details taken and no obligation afterwards. The condition is on this screen rather than buried in terms, because a free offer with an unstated string attached is not really free and is not worth the goodwill it borrows.

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor in Al Manara actually cost?
faqs.answer: Market quotes for Al Manara fall into bands rather than onto a single figure. Online tutoring from budget platforms starts at AED 33 to 65 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at AED 150 to 300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel, per Bestimate's 2026 rate table. IB Gram quotes its own rate after a free trial lesson, because it depends on the subject, the level and the number of sessions.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tutoring quoted higher in Al Manara than in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Because there is no school inside Al Manara's boundary and most Dubai tutors live inland. A tutor coming from Al Barsha commits roughly 1.7 hours of their afternoon to deliver a sixty-minute lesson here, once the round trip at 5pm is counted; from Al Sufouh or Dubai Marina it is closer to two hours. That time has to be paid for by somebody, and it appears as a higher hourly rate rather than as a separate travel line. Families in Umm Suqeim, five minutes away, are quoted noticeably less for the same teaching hour.

faqs.question: Is an AED 45 online tutor a realistic option for Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: It is a real product, but it is a different product. At that rate the tutor is usually a university student or recent graduate working from the textbook, which is useful for homework supervision and content review. It is not component-level teaching: nobody at AED 45 an hour has Chemistry Higher Level markbands in their head or can tell you which criterion a Middle Years investigation lost marks against. For a Year 7 student who needs structure, the cheap hour is sensible. For a DP2 student eight weeks from the papers, forty cheap hours cost more and achieve less than twelve specialist ones.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an Al Manara villa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service the platform runs only in India, where tutor distribution and economics are different. UAE lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing for past papers and a shared whiteboard. The practical gain is specialism: instead of choosing from tutors willing to drive to Al Thanya Street at 5pm, an Al Manara family can work with whoever actually teaches the component their child is losing marks on.

faqs.question: How many tutoring hours does a DP2 student from this area usually need?
faqs.answer: There is no single answer, but the shape is more predictable than the total. Most families who spend well buy two to four diagnostic sessions after the mocks, then a block of six to ten sessions on one or two components in the eight weeks before the papers. That is roughly twelve to fourteen hours per subject being supported, concentrated rather than spread. The families who spend badly buy one hour a week for twenty-four months, which is around ninety hours, much of it in terms when nothing was due and nothing was measured.

faqs.question: Should I buy a monthly package or pay for sessions one at a time?
faqs.answer: Monthly packages in Dubai are commonly advertised at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. A block makes budgeting predictable and sometimes lowers the effective rate, which is a genuine benefit. The risk is that it commits you before you know whether the match works. A reasonable compromise is a free trial lesson first, then a short block with a written review point tied to mock results rather than to how many months have passed.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Dubai rise as the May session gets closer?
faqs.answer: Rates themselves move less than availability does. What changes in the final term is scarcity: the tutors who genuinely know a Higher Level component are booked, so the choice narrows to whoever is still free, and premium providers like BartyED, quoting AED 650 an hour, look more reasonable simply because fewer alternatives remain. The practical consequence is to secure a specialist early rather than to budget for a price rise. Families who leave it until eight weeks out usually pay a scarcity premium in quality rather than in dirhams.

faqs.question: Does a tutoring quote in Dubai include VAT, and should I ask?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask in writing. UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees depends on the provider's status and is not something a tutoring page should state as settled fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, so this page does not. What you can reasonably require is clarity about the specific quote in front of you: whether the figure is inclusive or exclusive, whether it is per hour or per session, and whether a tax registration number appears on the invoice. A provider unwilling to answer those three questions has told you something useful.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my child's six Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is often cheaper, but it should be the consequence of a match rather than the reason for it. Mathematics and Physics pair reasonably well because the Higher Level content overlaps. Chemistry and Biology look adjacent and are not, at Higher Level. The real test is whether the tutor can name the paper weightings and the Internal Assessment criteria for both subjects without hesitating. If they cannot, you are buying one specialism and one generalist hour at the specialist rate.

faqs.question: What does Internal Assessment support cost, and what should it include?
faqs.answer: Internal Assessment coaching is quoted at the same hourly rates as subject tutoring, so AED 150 to 300 online at the qualified tier, higher for a named specialist. The component is worth 20 per cent of the grade in most sciences and in mathematics, which makes those hours among the best-value in the two years. What you should be buying is process coaching: narrowing the research question, testing whether the data supports the conclusion, and mapping the student's own draft against each criterion. What you must not buy is anybody writing or editing the work itself.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write or finish my child's Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider offering to is selling your child a serious risk. One agency in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; submitting purchased work is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate. What a tutor may legitimately do is coach the research question, teach citation properly, read a draft the student has written and question its argument, and explain what the criteria actually reward. That work raises marks. IB Gram tutors operate on the student's own writing and say so plainly when asked.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a UAE permit, and does it cost us anything?
faqs.answer: They need a private tutor work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE app, website or e-services system under Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. It costs you nothing and costs the tutor nothing, so there is no excuse for not holding one. Tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here.

faqs.question: What happens if we stop after the free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Nothing happens. The trial is one lesson, taken before any payment, with no card details collected and no obligation to continue afterwards. That condition is stated here rather than in terms elsewhere, because a free offer with an unstated string attached is not genuinely free. If the match is wrong, say so and ask for a different tutor or walk away. Using the trial as a diagnostic rather than a demonstration is the single cheapest way to avoid a bad arrangement, and it is why it exists.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until the papers. Is tutoring still worth the money?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough for technique and not enough for content, so the spending has to be aimed accordingly. Pick the one or two components carrying the most marks, work exclusively from timed past papers, and ignore the rest of the syllabus. Bestimate's estimates put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 a month and above for weekly hours, so a focused block is real money. It is usually better value at this point than the same sum spread across two quiet terms, because the student can use the work immediately.

faqs.question: Do two children in the same Al Manara household get a lower rate?
faqs.answer: Shared sessions are quoted below one-to-one on a per-student basis, which makes them attractive on a budget. They only work when both students are genuinely at the same point in the same syllabus with the same board, and two siblings a year apart in the Diploma almost never are. Ask the tutor directly how they split attention when the two diverge mid-term, and compare the per-student group rate against half of a one-to-one hour rather than against the whole hour. Often sequential individual sessions turn out to be better value.

faqs.question: How does the KHDA school fee freeze change what I should budget for tutoring?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For planning, that means the largest line in a Dubai education budget is a known quantity this year, which makes the variable tutoring line easier to size and easier to concentrate where it matters. It does not mean tutoring is cheaper. It means the money you were holding against a fee rise can be directed at the eight weeks when a grade actually moves.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-manara.closingBody: The useful first conversation about an IB home tutor in Al Manara is not about price. It is about which component is losing marks, what evidence says so, and how many sessions that specific problem should take. Once those three things are written down, a rate becomes something you can judge rather than something you have to guess at. Take the free trial lesson, ask the tutor what they would change first, and ask them to name the weighting of the component in question. Then set a review date. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, so the whole hour goes on teaching rather than on Al Thanya Street.

Check the subject and level, then check the availability window, because a plan built backwards from a deadline only works if the slot actually exists every week.

intro.heading: The calendar is the thing that decides what tutoring can do
paragraphs: Parents in Al Mankhool rarely search for a tutor in September. They search in late October when the first real assessment comes back, in January when the mock results land, or in March when the May session has stopped being abstract. Each of those moments gives a tutor a different amount of room, and the honest conversation starts with how much room is left rather than with an hourly rate. A plan that ignores the calendar is a plan that spends a term teaching the wrong half of the course.

Count what is actually available. A Dubai term runs roughly eleven or twelve weeks, of which eight or nine are usable for tuition once the first settling week, the assessment week and the week before a break are removed. At one session a week that is eight or nine hours. Eight hours is enough to rebuild one topic properly, or to fix answer structure across a paper, or to get an internal assessment from a bad research question to a defensible one. It is not enough to cover a year of content, and any tutor who says otherwise is selling hours.

The second thing the calendar decides is which deadlines matter. The May session is the public one, but it is not the one that bites first. Your child's school sets internal deadlines for internal assessments, the extended essay and the theory of knowledge essay, and those arrive months earlier than families expect. School mock weeks sit in between. A tutoring plan written backwards from the school's own calendar beats one written forwards from today, every time, and the school calendar is free to obtain.

On the phrase in the search: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and lessons for Al Mankhool families are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a calendar-driven plan this is an advantage rather than a compromise. A session that depends on somebody driving through Bur Dubai at 5pm is a session that is occasionally late and sometimes cancelled, and an eight-week block cannot absorb two lost weeks. A video slot starts when it says it starts.

What follows is the working. It sets out what a term can achieve week by week, counts the Diploma year backwards from the session, explains how Dubai term dates and Ramadan change when revision actually happens, answers the starting-late question honestly, prices the Al Mankhool market in AED with attribution, states what any private tutor in Dubai must hold under MoHRE rules, and draws the academic-honesty line that matters most when a deadline is close. Cambridge and Pearson dates carry their sources. IB dates do not appear, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mankhool.programmesIntro: Each IB stage has its own calendar pressure, and the useful tutoring block is different in each. These are the stages, described by what their deadlines do rather than by what their brochures say.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No public examinations and no fixed external deadlines, which means the calendar pressure is entirely internal to the school. Units run for several weeks and conclude with a presentation or a reflection. The useful tutoring block here is short and skill-based: reading fluency, written structure, number facts. There is nothing to revise for and nothing to cram.
programmes.countryNote: Al Mankhool families with primary-age children are usually within ten minutes of school, so the practical question is homework routine rather than exam timing. A four-session block on written structure in Year 5 is worth more than a year of weekly support in Year 6, and costs a fraction of it at the AED 150 to 300 qualified online band.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed continuously against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with the Personal Project arriving in MYP5. The calendar pressure is a series of unit deadlines rather than one exam, which means a tutoring block should be timed to the start of a unit rather than to the week after a disappointing mark.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision reachable from Al Mankhool sits mainly in Al Jaddaf and across the Creek. Ask the school whether it enters MYP5 students for the IB's on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, because that single answer changes whether the final year rewards timed practice or sustained drafting. It is a school-level decision and rarely explained in a prospectus.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years with three distinct calendar phases: a content phase in DP1, a coursework phase spanning DP1 term three to DP2 term one, and an examination phase in the final two terms. Families who buy tuition in the wrong phase pay full price for the wrong work. Internal assessments, the extended essay and the theory of knowledge essay all sit in the middle phase.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No IB session, upload or results date appears on this page: ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB. Confirm every one with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before planning around it, and treat any page that restates one, including this one, as a pointer rather than a source.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses paired with a career-related study and a reflective project. The DP components carry the same deadlines as a full Diploma, so the calendar work is identical, while the surrounding load is lighter and usually means fewer total hours are needed.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in Dubai is thin and Al Mankhool families generally choose between the full Diploma and a British post-16 route. If the CP is on the table, ask the school which DP subjects it actually timetables rather than which it lists, because a course in a brochure is not always a course running in September.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mankhool.subjectsIntro: Subjects differ in how much a short block can move, and that is a calendar fact rather than a difficulty one. These are the Diploma subjects we teach, each with what eight weeks can realistically achieve in it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Eight weeks moves technique, not content. Algebraic fluency, calculus method and timed paper discipline respond quickly. A full topic rebuild, such as all of calculus from scratch, does not fit in a term and should not be promised.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics content responds faster than the pure content, because much of it is procedure. A block before mocks is usually best spent on the statistical tests and on the exploration rather than on re-teaching functions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Rearrangement and unit discipline can be fixed in a handful of sessions and pay across every paper. Conceptual rebuilds in fields and in quantum content take longer and belong in DP1, not in the final term.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics sign conventions and organic mechanism sequences are the two blocks that fit a term. Both are practice-heavy rather than explanation-heavy, so eight sessions with homework between them moves marks measurably.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Experimental design and extended-response structure are the term-sized jobs. Content recall is large and is better handled by the student against the school's own material, which is why a tutor spending eight weeks on recall is poor value here.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation structure are the quick wins, and both are technique. The commentary portfolio is a coursework-phase job and should be timetabled, not left to collide with revision.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study technique and the application of tools to unseen material respond fast. A block aimed at the command terms, distinguishing analyse from evaluate in practice, often lifts marks more than content coverage does.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Timed writing is the term-sized target. Students who draft well and write slowly lose marks that look like analysis problems and are pace problems, and pace responds to eight weeks of timed practice with feedback.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Study recall and the structure of an evaluation paragraph are the two things worth a block. Precision about method and ethics in named studies is where marks are won, and it is learnable material rather than insight.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Essay and exhibition, both on school-set internal deadlines that arrive earlier than families expect. Support is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafting; no tutor may write or complete any part of it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mankhool.igcseSubjectsIntro: Many Al Mankhool households have an IGCSE sibling on a published timetable while the Diploma student works to internal deadlines. These are the IGCSE courses we cover, with the dated series that applies to them.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Sat in Pearson's May/June and November series. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, which makes the preceding eight weeks the planning unit for a resit candidate.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge runs its IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates. The mole concept and electrolysis are the two blocks that fit an eight-week window usefully.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and waves dominate lost marks and respond well to a short block, because most of the loss is unit handling rather than concept. Confirm the school's zone timetable before planning the final fortnight.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
igcseSubjects.description: Answer length against the mark allocation is the term-sized fix. The content reads easily, so a block spent on recall is usually a block spent on what the student already has.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language (Pearson 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Timed writing and the comprehension technique are both eight-week jobs. Results timing matters for post-16 applications: Pearson's June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026.

igcseSubjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
igcseSubjects.description: Papers move between the three sciences without warning, so a block aimed at switching speed and at shared method vocabulary is better value than one aimed at a single science.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mankhool.regionsIntro: What changes between these neighbourhoods is the school run, and the school run decides what time a weekly session can realistically hold for eight weeks running. That reliability is the whole point of a calendar-led plan.

regions.name: Al Mankhool

regions.name: Bur Dubai
regions.note: The Creek-side core immediately north. Several long-established schools sit within minutes, which means short runs and few scheduling surprises, but also a tutoring pool spread thinly across three or four different curricula.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: East across Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Road, compact and apartment-dense. The shortest runs in the belt and the tightest parking, which is why an evening slot that does not depend on anybody finding a space is worth more here than the rate difference suggests.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: South along Oud Metha Road, with Red Line stations and the Healthcare City approach. Families here often cross to Al Jaddaf or Festival City for IB provision, which pushes a reliable session start towards 5pm.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: The nearest full IB continuum provision, a few minutes down Oud Metha Road. The shortest IB school run available to this cluster, and the only part of it where a 4pm session is genuinely realistic on a weekday.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Over the Creek beside the airport, and the approach to Festival City schooling. Al Garhoud Bridge is the variable that breaks weekly slots: the same pickup lands home anywhere between 3.45pm and 4.30pm depending on the day.

regions.note: Out along the Green Line towards Sharjah. The longest inbound commute in this cluster, so a session before 5.30pm is unreliable and a block built on one will lose weeks it cannot afford.

regions.note: Coastal, near the Sharjah border, with two established schools minutes away. Cohorts are small, which means a named Diploma subject specialist is scarce locally and the eight-week block is best protected by booking online.

sections.heading: What a home tutor means in Al Mankhool, and what we actually deliver
paragraphs: The phrase home tutor in Dubai usually means one of two things, and they have different prices. The first is an independent tutor who travels to the apartment, advertised in this market at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors quoting up to AED 500. The second is a tutor who teaches from their own desk to the child's, live over video, quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour for an equivalently qualified person. The difference is largely a car.

IB Gram delivers the second. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. That is stated plainly because the alternative, implying a tutor will arrive at an Al Mankhool address, would be a promise we do not keep. What the online format buys for a family on a deadline is the reliability the calendar needs, plus a tutor pool that is not limited to people who can cross Bur Dubai at 5pm.

There is a genuine case for in-home support, and it is worth naming. A young child who cannot stay at a desk without an adult beside them benefits from physical presence in a way video cannot replicate, and families with that need should buy it. For a Diploma student working to internal deadlines, the need is a specialist in one named subject at a fixed hour every week for eight weeks. That is the job the online format does better, and it does it at the lower of the two published bands.

sections.heading: What the next eight weeks can honestly achieve
paragraphs: Eight sessions is the realistic size of a Dubai term once the settling week, the assessment week and the week before a break are taken out. That is eight hours of teaching plus whatever homework the student actually does, and it is enough for exactly one well-chosen objective. Families who ask for three objectives get a third of each, which is the commonest reason a term of tuition produces no visible change.

Some objectives fit and some do not. Rebuilding answer structure across a paper fits. Fixing unit handling and rearrangement in Physics fits. Getting an internal assessment from a vague research question to a defensible one with a sound method fits, comfortably. Teaching a year of Chemistry content does not fit, and nor does raising every grade on a report at once. The skill in buying tuition is choosing the objective that fits and that also happens to be worth the most marks.

The week-by-week shape below is what a sound eight-week block looks like from the inside. Notice that week one contains no teaching and week four contains a decision. Both are deliberate. A block that never diagnoses is a block aimed by guesswork, and a block with no mid-point review runs to its end whether or not it is working, which is how a term becomes a year. Week eight is also where the next block gets decided, or decided against: a block that has met its objective should end rather than roll on out of habit, and that conversation is far easier to have when the objective was written down in week one and the mid-point note says whether it moved.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, and the right way to plan is from the session towards today rather than the reverse. No IB date appears here. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session, upload or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family acts on must come from the school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly. What can be planned without a date is the order and the size of each phase.

Working backwards from the session: the final four to eight weeks are timed full papers and error-log work, at the highest intensity and therefore the highest cost. The term before that is answer structure and the remaining content gaps. Before that sits the coursework phase, where internal assessments, the extended essay and the theory of knowledge essay are decided, and it is the phase families most often underfund because none of it looks like revision. DP1 is for content and for the method skills the coursework phase will need.

For an IGCSE sibling the dates exist and are sourced, which makes the household calendar easier to build. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; the February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to UAE candidates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, since it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

sections.heading: Term dates, Ramadan and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: The Dubai academic calendar shapes a tutoring plan more than most families allow for. Terms are punctuated by breaks that fall differently from the exam calendar, and the weeks immediately after a long break are among the least productive of the year. A block that starts the week before a holiday loses its momentum at exactly the point where homework should be compounding, which is an avoidable waste of the first two sessions.

Ramadan shifts the day. School hours shorten, afternoons are quieter and evenings reorganise around Iftar, and a 5pm session that worked in January is often the wrong slot entirely. The practical answer is to move sessions to post-Iftar timings, which we do on request, and to accept that the fortnight either side of Eid is not a revision window. Planning around it rather than through it is the difference between a block that finishes and a block that fades.

There is a second calendar pressure specific to Dubai private schools. Every school here teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of its licensed curriculum, and KHDA's guidance required these to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes. Those lessons occupy real timetable space, which is one reason a Diploma student's homework evenings are tighter than a parent expects.
bullets: Get the term calendar and the mock weeks from the school in writing
Do not start an eight-week block in the week before a long break
Move sessions to post-Iftar timings during Ramadan
Treat the fortnight around Eid as unavailable, not as optional
Allow for mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons in the weekly load

sections.heading: Starting late: the honest answer to the six-week question
paragraphs: Families ask whether six weeks before an exam is too late, and the answer is that it depends entirely on what the six weeks are spent on. Six weeks cannot deliver a year of content. Six weeks can reliably move three things: question selection and timing, the structure of extended answers, and the specific errors a student makes repeatedly. In most subjects those three together are worth more marks than any content block of the same length, because they apply to every question on the paper rather than to one topic.

So the plan changes shape when time is short. There is no diagnostic week in the ordinary sense; the diagnostic is a full past paper sat cold in the first session, marked without mercy, and turned into an error log. Then every subsequent session is a timed section plus the two errors that appeared most often. Content is taught only where the error log demands it, which is a different and much narrower selection than the syllabus would suggest.

What a late start cannot rescue is coursework. An internal assessment with a weak research question six weeks before submission is in trouble, because the question determines the ceiling and changing it means collecting data again. This is the strongest argument for the coursework-phase scheduling described above: the work is cheapest, fastest and most effective when the question is challenged before anything else happens. A family that spends two sessions in DP1 term three on a research question avoids six in DP2 on the consequences.

sections.heading: What a home tutor costs in this market, and what the premium buys
paragraphs: The travel premium in Bur Dubai is unusually easy to see because both formats are advertised monthly. A Dubai provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, close to AED 100 a session. In-home packages are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions, which is AED 200 to 225 an hour. The teaching in both can be identical. The second figure includes a car crossing Al Mankhool twice a week, and a scheduling risk the first does not carry.

The hourly bands tell the same story. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, is advertised from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. In-home one-to-one is AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 table, with independents to AED 500. Specialist IB and IGCSE support is AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes.

For a family on a calendar, the premium buys one thing worth having and one thing that costs them. It buys physical presence, which matters for young children. It costs reliability, because an eight-week block cannot absorb two sessions lost to traffic, and it narrows the specialist pool to people who live nearby. None of these are IB Gram prices; ours follow a free trial lesson. For wider context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai do not rise for 2026-27, so the tutoring line is the one a family can still size deliberately.
