sections.heading: What any private tutor in Dubai must hold
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a family about to commit to eight weeks should check it in week one rather than week six. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, the website and the e-services system. Because the permit is free, a tutor who cites a permit cost as a reason for a higher rate has it wrong. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you either.

One further rule matters for families in Dubai who are tempted by the obvious shortcut. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document before relying on the exact wording. The sound position either way is not to arrange your child's own class teacher as a paid private tutor. On regulators generally: KHDA oversees private education in Dubai, ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA regulates Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge regulates Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by any of them and claims nothing of the kind.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when a deadline is close
paragraphs: Pressure is where this line gets crossed, and the crossing is almost always the parent's decision rather than the student's. An internal assessment is due on Sunday, the draft is thin, somebody offers to tidy it up, and a family that would never cheat on principle agrees to it on a Thursday evening. The IB does not read it that way. The student signs a declaration that the work is their own, and the consequence falls on the student's record and can reach the whole Diploma.

So the boundary is worth stating before the deadline rather than during it. A tutor may challenge a research question, interrogate a method, teach uncertainty handling or source evaluation, explain what a criterion is asking for, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite, complete or supply any part of an internal assessment, extended essay, theory of knowledge essay or any other assessed work. IB Gram does not do it in any subject, at any level, at any point in the calendar.

This is also a market warning. One operator found during research for this project sells completed internal assessments outright at AED 3,750. That is not a premium tutoring tier; it is a malpractice trigger with a price on it. The calendar answer is the better one: schedule the coursework phase deliberately, challenge the question early, and the Thursday-evening temptation never arrives. Families who front-load the question work almost never find themselves in the position where somebody offers to finish it for them.

process.title: Send the deadline, not just the subject
process.description: A message that says Chemistry HL, school internal IA deadline in February, mock week in January is actionable immediately. A message that says needs a tutor requires three exchanges before anything useful can be planned. The school calendar and the internal deadline list are the two documents to have in front of you.

process.title: Free trial lesson as a cold diagnostic
process.description: The tutor sets work across the whole paper rather than the current topic, or a full past paper if time is short, and reports what the errors actually are. If the match is wrong you say so and nothing is owed. One trial lesson per student, and it is where the objective for the block comes from.

process.title: An objective and an end date, in writing
process.description: You receive the objective, the number of sessions, and the date the block ends. One objective, not three. A block without a stated objective cannot be judged, and a block without an end date renews itself by default, which is how eight weeks becomes two years.

process.title: A weekly slot that survives a term
process.description: Lessons run live over video on Gulf Standard Time at a time chosen around the Bur Dubai school run, usually 4.30pm to 7pm. Nobody drives, so the slot holds for eight consecutive weeks. Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timings on request.

process.title: Week four review, then a real recommendation
process.description: At the midpoint we check the objective against evidence and say whether to continue, re-aim or stop. At week eight you get the assessment and a recommendation that may be to stop. A tutor who always recommends continuing is selling hours rather than reporting progress.

whyPoints.title: Plans built from your school's calendar
whyPoints.description: Internal deadlines and mock weeks decide what a term can achieve, and they are set by the school rather than by the IB. We ask for them first and build the block backwards from them, because a plan written forwards from today usually aims at the wrong phase of the year.

whyPoints.title: One objective per block
whyPoints.description: Eight usable weeks support one well-chosen objective. Families who ask for three get a third of each, which is the most common reason a term of tuition shows no visible change on a report. Choosing the objective is the work; the sessions are the easy part.

whyPoints.title: Dates carry their source, or they are not published
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page name their source. No IB date appears at all, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and nothing in this project has been confirmed from the IB. A wrong date a family acts on is worse than no date, and it has been published to UAE parents before.

whyPoints.title: A slot that actually holds
whyPoints.description: An eight-week block cannot absorb two sessions lost to Bur Dubai traffic. Lessons are delivered live over video, so the session starts when it says it does, which is the specific reason the online format suits a calendar-led plan better than the in-home alternative.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line stated before the deadline
whyPoints.description: A tutor challenges, teaches and gives feedback on the student's own work. IB Gram does not write, draft or complete an internal assessment, extended essay or theory of knowledge essay, in any subject. Stating that in week one is what stops the question being asked in week seven.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we cannot cover
whyPoints.description: If no specialist in your subject is free in the window your block needs, we say so and say when one will be. Filling the slot and hoping costs a family a term, and no competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Can lessons take place inside our Al Mankhool apartment?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for an Al Mankhool family is one-to-one and live over video, on Gulf Standard Time, at a slot chosen around the Bur Dubai school run. The reason is not only cost, although the market gap is real: Bestimate's 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online. It is that a weekly slot which depends on crossing Bur Dubai at 5pm cannot be relied on for eight consecutive weeks.

faqs.question: My child has exams in six weeks. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the six weeks are spent on the right things. Six weeks cannot deliver a year of content. It can reliably move question selection and timing, the structure of extended answers, and the specific errors a student repeats, and in most subjects those three are worth more marks than any single content block of the same length. The method is to sit a full paper cold in session one, mark it without mercy, build an error log, and then spend every remaining session on a timed section plus the two commonest errors. What six weeks cannot rescue is a coursework question.

faqs.question: How many weeks of tutoring does one Dubai term actually give us?
faqs.answer: Eight or nine, not eleven or twelve. Once you remove the settling week at the start, the assessment week, and the week before a break when nothing lands, a term yields eight or nine usable sessions. That is enough for one well-chosen objective with homework between sessions. It is not enough for three objectives, and families who ask for three receive a third of each. The practical step is to get the term calendar and the mock week dates from the school office in writing before deciding what the block should aim at.

faqs.question: When should we start thinking about the internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Earlier than almost anyone does, and the reason is that the research question sets the ceiling. An internal assessment with a vague or unmeasurable question cannot score well however good the later work is, and changing the question late means collecting data again. The cheapest and most effective support is therefore two sessions in the term when the question is chosen, spent challenging it hard before anything else happens. Families who do that rarely need the six sessions of rescue work that a weak question produces in the term before submission, and they avoid the pressure that leads to worse decisions.

faqs.question: Can you tell me the dates of the next IB exam session?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and we will not publish one. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session, upload or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session, and that much is safe to say. For the actual dates, ask your child's IB coordinator or check ibo.org directly, and treat any page restating an IB date, including this one, as a pointer rather than a source. A date a family builds a revision plan around has to come from the authority that sets it.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE siblings in the same household sit their exams?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to UAE candidates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson's June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Work from the school-issued timetable.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge publish several versions of the same timetable?
faqs.answer: Because the same paper is sat at different local times around the world. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a timetable per zone. Its guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Your child's school in Al Mankhool or Bur Dubai knows its zone. If anyone in the household is revising from a timetable found online rather than the school's own, check the zone first.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a weekly tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: It usually moves it. School hours shorten, afternoons go quiet and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so a 5pm session that worked in January is often the wrong time entirely. We move sessions to post-Iftar timings on request. The second adjustment is to the plan rather than the clock: the fortnight either side of Eid is not a productive revision window, and a block that tries to run through it loses momentum it cannot recover. Plan around it, finish the block before it, or restart after it.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost in Al Mankhool?
faqs.answer: Dubai market rates reviewed October 2026 run from AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya's budget online tier and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik's, typically delivered by university students. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing from AED 200 for IB. Specialist IB support is AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home one-to-one is AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's table. None of those are our prices; IB Gram sets pricing after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is a standing weekly slot across two years a good idea?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is the most expensive arrangement in this market. A slot with no stated objective and no end date runs for two years and nobody involved has to judge whether it worked, which is precisely why it keeps running. At the AED 150 to 300 qualified band, two years at one hour a week is somewhere between AED 9,000 and AED 36,000. Three defined blocks, timed to the coursework phase and the exam run, usually cost a fraction of that and produce more movement, because each one is pointed at something specific and can be stopped.

faqs.question: Which schools near Al Mankhool run the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Not many inside Al Mankhool itself, which is why the school run is the scheduling problem it is. Swiss International Scientific School in Al Jaddaf runs a full IB continuum a few minutes down Oud Metha Road. Across the Creek, Deira International School and Universal American School in Dubai Festival City offer the Diploma, reached via Al Garhoud Bridge, and Hartland International School and GEMS Modern Academy sit further out. Within Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai the provision is largely British and Indian curriculum. Check the current KHDA inspection report and the school's own subject list before any transfer.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit, and does it cost us anything?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it costs the tutor nothing. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted at you.

faqs.question: Can we arrange my child's own school teacher as a private tutor?
faqs.answer: It is not a good idea and in Abu Dhabi it is barred. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported, so verify the exact wording against the current ADEK policy document before treating it as settled. The sound position in any emirate is to keep the two roles separate, because a teacher who marks your child's work and is paid by you is in a conflict nobody benefits from.

faqs.question: What happens at the end of an eight-week block?
faqs.answer: You receive a timed assessment, the error log as it now stands, and a written recommendation. The recommendation may be to stop, and for many students after a well-aimed block it should be: the specific weakness has closed and the money is better spent on a different subject, or not spent at all. If the evidence says continue, the next block gets its own objective and its own end date rather than drifting on from the last one. A tutor whose recommendation is always to continue is reporting their own interest, not your child's.

faqs.question: Do you supply past papers, mark schemes or IB subject guides?
faqs.answer: No. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright material, and reproducing or distributing them is infringement. A tutor works with material the student legitimately holds through their school, cites the official source and links to it: ibo.org for the Diploma, cambridgeinternational.org for Cambridge qualifications and qualifications.pearson.com for Pearson Edexcel. The school is also the holder of the correct zone timetable and the internal deadline list, both of which matter more to a calendar-led plan than any copy circulating online.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mankhool.closingHeading: Bring the calendar, and we will work backwards
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mankhool.closingBody: Ask the school office for two documents: the term calendar with the mock weeks marked, and the internal deadline list for coursework. Send them with your enquiry. Take the free trial lesson and let the tutor set work across the whole paper, or a full past paper if the exam is close, and read the error log that comes back. Then agree one objective and an end date, and judge the block at week four rather than at week eight. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, timed around the Bur Dubai school run, moving to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan. If nobody is free in the window your block needs, we will say so.

intro.heading: Home tutoring in Al Mizhar: the honest answer, then the useful one
paragraphs: Start with the question as asked. Can you get an IB home tutor in Al Mizhar? Yes, from the local market, and it costs more than most parents expect. Published Dubai rates put in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertised between AED 200 and 500. Monthly in-home packages in this market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Al Mizhar sits beyond Mirdif, which means a tutor coming here is driving out and back through Algeria Street or Tripoli Street, and a meaningful part of that rate is recovering the journey rather than paying for teaching.

IB Gram does not sell that service. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one to one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service offered only in India. We are not going to pretend that is a sacrifice you should make for our convenience, so here is the actual argument: the Diploma Programme is not one subject. It is six subjects at two levels plus three core elements, each with its own Internal Assessment and its own mark scheme, and the thing that moves a grade is somebody who knows the specific component your child is losing marks on. The number of such people within a twenty-minute drive of Al Mizhar is small. The number teaching that exact component somewhere in the world is not.

So this page is written from the subject rather than from the neighbourhood. What the six groups actually assess. Where the mark schemes catch students out, group by group. What each Internal Assessment really is and what proportion of the grade it carries. What Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay demand. And what a past-paper session looks like when it is done properly rather than as a worksheet handed over.

The scheduling point is worth making once, because it is the reason the comparison is not close for most households here. Al Mizhar students travel to schools in Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais on collecting bus routes that can run the better part of an hour. A tutor driving to your villa for a 5pm start is leaving home at 4.15pm and arriving somewhere between 4.50pm and 5.30pm depending on the traffic, and the hour you paid for shrinks accordingly. A video lesson at 5.30pm begins at 5.30pm.

What follows assumes you want the detail rather than the pitch. If your child is in DP1 and drifting, or in DP2 with a predicted grade that blocks an offer, the useful next step is a free trial lesson with a specialist in the weakest component, working on a past question from their own subject and level.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mizhar.subjectsIntro: The Diploma is six separate examinations with six separate failure modes. These are the subjects Al Mizhar families ask about, with what the assessment actually rewards in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic technique, proof and pure mathematics, expected by most engineering and physical science degrees. The non-calculator paper exposes fluency gaps directly, and Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers and vectors. Marks are lost to method not shown rather than to method not known.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and data with technology assumed throughout and a heavier statistics load. Not an easy option, and the recurring loss is interpretation: a correct calculation with no sentence explaining what it means in the context the question set up.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes covering motion, matter, waves, fields and nuclear and quantum physics, with Higher Level extensions throughout. Fields is where Higher Level students most often break, because three analogous models have to be held apart under time pressure without merging their equations.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised into structure and reactivity, with the mole underpinning everything. A student who understands mole arithmetic but cannot execute it in fifteen seconds loses marks across every paper, and equilibrium is the largest conceptual hurdle in the course.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume plus precision. Extended responses want specific terminology in a specific order, and a general paragraph about a process scores poorly however accurate it is. Data-based questions are the second reliable loss, because they reward analysis rather than recall.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the marks. A correctly labelled diagram with the shift drawn the right way earns credit no surrounding prose can recover, and the evaluation marks at the end of extended responses are the commonest thing students leave behind.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus material rather than recall of theory. A textbook answer about motivation that never mentions the organisation in the case is capped, and that pattern repeats across every paper in the subject.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing how a text produces an effect, not summarising what it says. The individual oral and the comparative work reward close reference to specific passages, and students who read widely still lose marks for writing around a text rather than into it.

subjects.name: English B and language acquisition
subjects.description: Comprehension, productive writing and oral components, with the level chosen by the school and occasionally mismatched to the student. Knowing which course your child is registered for matters before any tutoring is booked, because the components differ.

subjects.name: History and Global Politics
subjects.description: Argument and source handling. Marks go to a sustained line of reasoning supported by evidence, and the source-based questions reward provenance and limitation analysis that students treat as preamble rather than as the question.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition, contributing to the core points. The essay rewards precise handling of knowledge questions rather than general philosophising, and it is the component students most often leave until it is too late to think properly about.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent research essay in a subject of the student's choice, with a word limit and a supervised process. The research question decides most of the mark, and the reflections on the process are assessed alongside the essay itself rather than as paperwork.

sections.heading: In-home against online for an Al Mizhar villa, with the numbers
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search is really asking for, so here it is with figures rather than adjectives. Every rate below was read on the provider's own public page and is attributed to them; none is an IB Gram price.

In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is quoted between AED 180 and 500 an hour. Bestimate's rate table runs AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The gap between those two bands is not a quality difference. It is a journey, and from Al Mizhar it is a long one in the wrong direction at the wrong time of day.

There are things the in-home option genuinely wins, and a page that pretended otherwise would not be worth reading. Physical presence works better for a restless younger child, it requires no device or connection, and some families simply prefer it. Against that, the pool of available tutors shrinks to whoever will drive out past Mirdif, the session start time becomes hostage to traffic, and specialist subjects at Higher Level often have no local candidate at all.

IB Gram's position is straightforward: we do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and that service exists only in India. So the comparison in the table is between market options, with our own model named as one of them. Read it and decide. For most Diploma families in these villa communities the deciding factor is not the rate but the specialist, because at Higher Level the right person is rarely the nearest one.

sections.heading: What the Diploma actually assesses, group by group
paragraphs: Families often buy IB tutoring as though the Diploma were a single qualification with a single difficulty. It is six subjects plus three core elements, and the reason a student is losing marks in Higher Level chemistry has nothing in common with why they are losing marks in English A.

That has a direct consequence for how you choose. A general IB tutor can be competent across several subjects at Standard Level and is rarely the right purchase at Higher Level, where the distinctive content and the specific mark-scheme conventions matter. When a parent asks for an IB tutor, the useful follow-up question is always which subject, at which level, and which component.

The table sets out what each group's assessment rewards. Read it alongside a marked paper, because the shape of the loss usually identifies the group's characteristic trap: unexplained method in mathematics, unstated assumptions in the sciences, undrawn or mislabelled diagrams in economics, summary instead of analysis in language and literature.

Confirm current structures, weightings and internal deadlines with your school's IB coordinator rather than from any third-party page. Subject guides are revised, and we do not reproduce or supply IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes; those belong to the IB and reach you properly through the school.

One cross-group observation is worth the money it saves. In four of the six groups the largest recoverable gain is not content at all but command-term discipline: answering the verb the question used, and no other. A student who writes an evaluation when the question said describe has produced more work for fewer marks, and a student who describes when the question said evaluate has capped themselves at the bottom of the band. That is a single habit, correctable in a term of weekly feedback, and it pays in every subject on the timetable at once.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment, subject by subject
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internally assessed work, and in the sciences and mathematics it commonly accounts for around a fifth of the final grade. That makes it the largest single component outside the written papers, and it is also the one most often left until there is no time to do it properly.

What the Internal Assessment is differs completely between subjects, which is why generic advice about it is useless. A mathematical exploration is an independent piece of written mathematics. A science investigation is experimental or data-based work with a research question and an evaluation. An economics portfolio is a set of commentaries on real-world articles. A language oral is a timed spoken analysis. The criteria, the lengths and the deadlines are different in each case.

The common factor is that the decisive step happens early. In almost every subject the choice of topic, question or article sets the ceiling, and no amount of careful writing afterwards raises it. Four sessions in DP1 spent on criteria and on choosing properly protect a fifth of the grade at ordinary rates. A rescue block in the final weeks costs more, arrives at exam-year rates, and cannot change the choice.

The boundary is the same everywhere and it is not negotiable. A tutor may teach the criteria, model method on a different example, question the student's draft and point out where a claim is unsupported. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit to completion any part of a submission. One page in the researched competitor set sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; that is a malpractice route and the student carries the finding, not the seller.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay: the points nobody plans for
paragraphs: The two core components contribute points to the Diploma total, and they are the two things students in this corridor most often postpone, partly because neither has weekly homework attached. Postponing them is expensive in a way that is invisible until the deadline.

The Extended Essay lives or dies on its research question. A question too broad produces a survey with nothing argued; one too narrow produces a page and a half. The supervised process also includes reflections, which are assessed rather than administrative, and a student who writes them retrospectively loses marks that cost nothing to earn along the way. A tutor's useful role here is interrogating the question early and responding to drafts with questions.

Theory of Knowledge rewards precision about knowledge claims rather than general opinion, which is an unfamiliar discipline for most sixteen year olds. The essay is written on a prescribed title and the exhibition requires objects connected to a knowledge prompt. Students who approach the essay as an opinion piece lose marks in exactly the places the criteria concentrate, and the fix is explicit instruction in handling a knowledge question.

Both components sit under the same honesty rule as everything else. A tutor teaches method, questions a draft and points out unsupported reasoning. A tutor does not write, draft or complete any part of a Theory of Knowledge essay, an exhibition commentary or an Extended Essay. Ask to see the feedback: questions your child must answer are right, sentences they could paste in are not.

sections.heading: What a past-paper session looks like when it is done properly
paragraphs: Past-paper work is the phrase every tutor uses and the thing most of them do badly. Handing a student a paper, waiting while they attempt it and then reading out the answers is not teaching; it is invigilation with commentary. A session that moves marks looks different, and a parent can recognise the difference from the written note afterwards.

The sequence that works is narrow. One question, attempted under something close to timed conditions. Then marking against the published mark scheme, with the student holding the scheme and identifying where their answer diverged from what it rewarded. Then the diagnosis, named out loud: this was method not shown, or an unstated assumption, or the wrong command term answered. Then a second question of the same type immediately, to prove the diagnosis.

That produces one or two questions per session rather than a whole paper, and parents sometimes read that as slow progress. It is the opposite. A student who has genuinely understood why four marks left a specific question will keep those marks in every future question of that shape, where a student who has been shown twelve correct answers has learned twelve answers.

You can test for this on the trial lesson. Ask the tutor how many questions they expect to cover in forty minutes. An answer of one or two with the mark scheme open is the right answer. An answer of a whole paper is a sign of the other approach, which is cheaper to deliver and worth less to buy.
bullets: One or two questions per session, not a whole paper

sections.heading: Higher Level or Standard Level, and when to change
paragraphs: Three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard is the usual shape, and the decision about which is which is made early and revisited rarely. It deserves revisiting, because it is the single biggest lever on both workload and university options.

Higher Level is not Standard Level with more questions. In most subjects it adds distinctive content, an extra component or substantially greater depth, and the step up is steeper than the timetable suggests. A student carrying three Higher Levels where one of them serves no purpose in their university plans is spending a great deal of time on a subject that will never be asked about.

The decision has to be made against destination rather than comfort. Engineering and physical sciences commonly expect Higher Level mathematics in the Analysis and Approaches route and often Higher Level physics; medicine-adjacent routes commonly expect Higher Level chemistry and often biology. Requirements vary by university and change between admission cycles, so read each target course's own entry page rather than any general rule.

If a change is being considered, the window is early and the conversation is with the school's coordinator rather than with a tutor. What a tutor can usefully contribute is evidence: whether the marks in that subject reflect a content gap that work would close, or a genuine mismatch between the student and the level.

There is a middle option families in this corridor often miss. Rather than dropping a Higher Level, buy a defined block of support in it for one term and then decide, with marks from that term as the evidence. Six to ten sessions on the specific extension content causing the trouble costs far less than two years of struggling through a level that was never the problem, and far less than discovering in DP2 that a required subject was dropped for comfort in DP1. Either outcome of that term is useful, which is what makes it a reasonable thing to buy.

sections.heading: Scheduling from Al Mizhar, including Ramadan and travel
paragraphs: A session that does not happen costs what one that does. For families out here that is the whole scheduling argument, because the bus routes serving Al Mizhar from Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais can run the better part of an hour and students arrive home late.

Set the slot from the arrival home on a bad afternoon rather than a good one, and add recovery time. For most households here that means 5.30pm at the earliest and 6.30pm or 7pm for students on the Al Warqa and Al Khawaneej routes. Families who cannot make a weekday evening work are usually better served by a weekend morning, where the comparison is a rested student against an exhausted one rather than one hour against another.

Plan the exceptions before they arrive. During Ramadan school days are shortened and household routines move towards the evening, so the usual slot shifts to after iftar; because no tutor is travelling anywhere, that change costs a message. Holiday weeks suit a short defined block on one component better than a weekly slot limping along while the family is away.

Travel is a standing feature of households in these communities. Online lessons follow a student to another time zone if the slot is adjusted, which no arrangement tied to a villa address can do. Send the dates in advance and sessions move rather than vanish; the thing to avoid is letting a trip become a four-week gap, because the restart costs more than the sessions missed.

sections.heading: Starting, and the limits we will tell you about
paragraphs: Send four things: the subject and level, which component is losing marks, a photograph of a marked paper or the latest report, and the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. The second item is the one that turns a broad request into a narrow brief, and the fourth is the one that decides whether the arrangement survives to February.

The free trial lesson runs about forty minutes on a past question from your child's own subject and level, with your child working and the tutor teaching. Ask the tutor how many questions they plan to cover; one or two with the mark scheme open is the right answer. Afterwards you get a written read on the loss pattern and the weeks it implies, and nothing is owed if you stop there.

Sometimes the answer is that nobody suitable is free. Higher Level specialists in narrow components, minority languages, and late-evening Gulf Standard Time slots are the three that run short, and a request made a fortnight before final papers is the hardest of all. We give a realistic match time rather than filling the hour with a generalist, because the wrong tutor costs the fee and then the weeks.

What we ask for is limited to what matching needs: subject, level, component, school if you want its sequence followed, and a contact for scheduling. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history across every subject. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs the data we hold, and the privacy link on this page sets out what is kept and how to have it deleted.

process.description: Whatever the subject, the choice of topic, question or article sets the ceiling, and it happens in DP1. Four sessions on criteria and choosing properly costs a fraction of a rescue block in the final weeks, which cannot change the choice anyway.

whyPoints.description: The Diploma is six examinations with six failure modes. We ask which subject, which level and which component before shortlisting anybody, because at Higher Level the right tutor is a component specialist rather than a general IB tutor.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram send a home tutor to our villa in Al Mizhar?
faqs.answer: No. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India. The local market does provide in-home tutoring, at a published AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online, and a substantial part of that difference is the drive out past Mirdif in afternoon traffic. We would rather state the position plainly and make the argument for online delivery than imply something we do not sell.

faqs.question: What does in-home IB tuition cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures, each read on the provider's own page: Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages in this market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions, against roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those two monthly numbers describe different products rather than different prices, so compare the session count and the session length before comparing the totals.

faqs.question: Why would a specialist matter more than a tutor who can come to us?
faqs.answer: Because the Diploma is six separate examinations. The reason a student is losing marks in Higher Level chemistry has nothing in common with why they are losing marks in English A, and at Higher Level the distinctive extension content and the subject's own mark-scheme conventions decide the grade. A general IB tutor can be genuinely competent at Standard Level. For a single weak component at Higher Level, the pool of people who have taught it is spread across the world rather than clustered within driving distance of Al Mizhar.

faqs.question: How many questions should a past-paper session actually cover?
faqs.answer: One or two, with the mark scheme open and in your child's hands. The sequence that moves marks is: attempt the question under something close to timed conditions, mark it against the published scheme, identify precisely where the answer diverged from what was rewarded, name the error out loud, then do a second question of the same type immediately to test the diagnosis. A tutor who expects to cover a whole paper in forty minutes is reading out answers, which is cheaper to deliver and worth much less.

faqs.question: What is the Internal Assessment in my child's subject?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the subject, which is why generic advice about it is useless. Mathematics sets an independent exploration. The sciences set an experimental or data-based investigation. Economics sets commentaries on real-world articles. Business Management sets a project on a real organisation. Languages set oral and written tasks. The criteria, lengths and deadlines differ in each case, and in the sciences and mathematics the component commonly carries around a fifth of the final grade. Confirm your child's specifics with the IB coordinator.

faqs.question: When does Internal Assessment work need to start?
faqs.answer: In DP1, because the decisive step is early in every subject. The choice of topic, research question or article sets the mark ceiling, and no amount of careful writing afterwards raises it. Four sessions on the criteria and on choosing properly protects roughly a fifth of the grade at ordinary rates. A rescue block in the final weeks costs more, arrives at exam-year rates, and cannot change the choice that was already made. For travelling households this matters doubly, because an early lost fortnight is survivable.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child complete an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Not complete it, no. A tutor may teach the criteria, model the method on a different example, question your child's draft and point out where a claim is not supported by evidence. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit to completion any part of a submission. The test a parent can apply requires no subject knowledge: feedback as questions your child must go and answer is correct, feedback as sentences they could paste in is not. One page in this search result sells finished Internal Assessments outright.

faqs.question: What do Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay actually need?
faqs.answer: Early thinking rather than late effort. The Extended Essay turns on its research question: too broad produces a survey with no argument, too narrow produces a page and a half, and the process reflections are assessed rather than administrative. Theory of Knowledge rewards precision about knowledge claims rather than general opinion, with an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition. Neither responds to a sprint, which is exactly how most students approach them. Both sit under the same rule: method coached, nothing written for the student.

faqs.question: Should my child really be carrying three Higher Levels?
faqs.answer: Only if all three serve a purpose. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra questions; in most subjects it adds distinctive content or an additional component, and the step is steeper than the timetable suggests. A third Higher Level that no university requirement asks for is the most expensive subject on a Diploma timetable. Check each target course's own entry page, because requirements vary by institution and between admission cycles, then take evidence from marked papers to the school's coordinator if a change is worth considering.

faqs.question: What time can a lesson start for a student on an Al Warqa bus route?
faqs.answer: Realistically 6.30pm or 7pm, or a weekend morning. The collecting routes serving Al Mizhar from Al Warqa and Al Qusais are among the longest in this part of Dubai and can run the better part of an hour, so a student is home late and tired. Set the slot from the worst afternoon with recovery time added, rather than from the earliest hour that has ever worked, because a slot that fails every third week stops existing by the second term. Weekend mornings give a rested student and a full session.

faqs.question: Can the lessons follow us when we travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the slot adjusted for the time difference. Households in these villa communities travel often, and an online one-to-one lesson is the format that survives it; no arrangement tied to a villa address can. Send the dates in advance and sessions move rather than disappear. What to avoid is letting a trip become a four-week gap, because in a sequential subject the restart costs more than the sessions missed. A short catch-up block on return usually settles it in a fortnight.

faqs.question: My child's predicted grade is below a university offer. What changes?
faqs.answer: The work moves from content to components. A predicted grade a band low usually reflects two or three repeating errors across past papers rather than a general gap, and one diagnostic session with a marked paper in front of a specialist finds them. From there, two sessions a week to the final series spent almost entirely on timed past-paper work, marked against published criteria, is the shape that moves marks. Tell the school as well, since predicted grades are theirs to revise on evidence rather than on request.

faqs.question: Can you send us a folder of IB papers and schemes to work through?
faqs.answer: No. Those belong to the IB and reproducing or distributing them is not ours to do. We teach against the subject and level your child is registered for and point you to the official route, which is the school or the IB's own site. That is the more useful answer as well as the lawful one, because official material is current while files circulating in parent groups are frequently from a superseded guide and will quietly send a student to question styles that no longer appear.

faqs.question: Is a group class a cheaper way to get IB support out here?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per student, and only worthwhile when the whole group shares the same gap. A group class works for revising a topic a class is collectively weak on. It works poorly for the situation most Diploma families are actually in, where one student is losing marks on a specific component that the others handle fine, because the hour then runs at the group's pace. It also means two journeys into Mirdif or Al Qusais, which for an Al Mizhar family is a real cost in time.

faqs.question: What should we send before booking a first IB lesson from Al Mizhar?
faqs.answer: Four things. The subject and the level. Which component is losing marks, which is what turns a broad request into a narrow brief. A photograph of a marked paper or the most recent report. And the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon, which sets the slot. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history across every subject; UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs what is held and the privacy link explains it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mizhar.closingHeading: Buy the component, not the commute
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mizhar.closingBody: The honest summary for an Al Mizhar family is this. Home tutoring exists locally and costs AED 180 to 500 an hour, with a real part of that paying for a drive out past Mirdif. IB Gram does not sell it at any price in the UAE, and delivers one-to-one Diploma tuition over live video instead. What that trade buys is a tutor matched to the component your child is actually losing marks on, which at Higher Level is rarely somebody within driving distance. Send us the subject, the level, the component and a marked paper, pick a slot that survives a bad bus day, and take the free trial lesson. Ask the tutor how many questions they plan to cover.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-muteena.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors who teach Diploma and Middle Years subjects to families in Al Muteena, Hor Al Anz and Al Nahda. Each one works to a single subject and level rather than covering everything, which is the whole point of matching by syllabus instead of by postcode.

intro.heading: Two streets apart, the same answer
paragraphs: Al Muteena sits in the older spine of Deira, a dense grid of apartment blocks between Abu Baker Al Siddique Road and Al Muteena Street, a short hop from Salah Al Din and Union metro stations. Families here are mostly in flats rather than villas, often with two or three children sharing one study space, and almost none of them attend a school inside the neighbourhood itself. The children travel out: to Al Garhoud, to Al Mamzar, to Oud Metha, to Al Qusais. That daily outward journey is the fact that shapes every tutoring decision made in this area.

Walk ten minutes in any direction and you are in Hor Al Anz, Al Rigga or Naif. Drive fifteen and you are in Al Nahda or Al Garhoud. Parents in each of those places type a slightly different search into Google, and they all get served a page that promises a tutor will drive over. So it is worth comparing them honestly. Put Al Muteena next to Deira proper, next to Al Nahda, next to Al Garhoud and next to Karama, and look at what actually differs: the drive time at four in the afternoon, the IB schools inside a twenty-minute radius, the size of the local tutor pool, the earliest hour a session can realistically start. Four of those five columns change. The fifth does not.

The column that does not change is the one that matters. An IB Diploma student needs a tutor who teaches their exact course — Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is not the same subject as Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, and a Chemistry HL student working on an Internal Assessment needs someone who has marked against criteria lettered A to E rather than someone comfortable with general science. The number of people within driving distance of Al Muteena who teach that precise combination is small in Al Muteena, and it is small in Al Nahda, and it is small in Al Garhoud. Proximity does not solve a specialisation problem. It only limits the shortlist.

That is why IB Gram delivers tuition to Al Muteena as one-to-one online lessons over live video. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service that exists only in our India operation, and pretending otherwise on a Dubai page would be a promise we do not keep. What the online model buys is a wider shortlist: a subject specialist for the course your child actually sits, available at a time that works after a Deira school run, without a single minute of the hour paid for being spent in traffic on Al Ittihad Road.

This page answers the home-tutoring question properly first — what the Dubai market charges, what a travel premium buys, how families compare the options — and then makes the case for the online format on the numbers rather than on adjectives. It also covers the things a Deira parent asks that nobody else writes down: which schools the area feeds, what a KHDA inspection band means for a Diploma cohort, how the exam calendar counts backwards from the May session, where a tutor's help stops being teaching and starts being malpractice, and what the MoHRE permit rules say about who may legally tutor your child at all.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-muteena.programmesIntro: An IB home tutor in Al Muteena is usually wanted for one of four things: a Diploma subject in trouble, a Middle Years student heading for Diploma choices, a Primary Years child who needs reading or number work, or the Diploma core — the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the Internal Assessments that sit outside any single subject.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the three core elements. Final grades run 1 to 7 per subject with up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix, for a 45-point maximum. Most of the teaching pressure lands in DP1 term two, when Internal Assessment work starts running alongside new content, and again in the ten weeks before the May session.
programmes.countryNote: Al Muteena families reach Diploma teaching at Deira International School in Al Garhoud, Universal American School, Al Ittihad Private School in Al Mamzar and, further out, GEMS Modern Academy. Each school runs a different subject menu, so two neighbours on the same street can be sitting completely different Higher Level combinations. That is precisely why matching by subject beats matching by distance.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 0 to 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade by published boundaries. There is no final external exam in most schools, so the grade a student carries into Diploma selection is built entirely from internal assessment. MYP 4 and 5 are where a weak criterion — usually criterion C or D in sciences and mathematics — quietly caps a child's options two years early.
programmes.countryNote: Deira-area MYP students often arrive from a CBSE or British primary and meet criterion-based marking for the first time at eleven or twelve. The gap is rarely knowledge; it is not knowing that a Middle Years answer is marked on communication and on reflection as well as on the correct result. Al Muteena parents tend to notice it when a child who was strong at arithmetic comes home with a 4.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, organised around transdisciplinary themes, with the Exhibition in the final year. Assessment is continuous and descriptive rather than numerical, which makes it harder for a parent to see a specific weakness forming. The two areas where targeted one-to-one help genuinely moves a Primary Years child are reading fluency and number sense, both of which respond well to short, frequent sessions.
programmes.countryNote: Primary Years children from Al Muteena mostly travel to Al Garhoud or Al Mamzar, which in a Deira afternoon means a tired child home at half past four. Thirty or forty minutes of focused online work at six, three times a week, does more for a seven-year-old than a ninety-minute block at the end of a long commute.

programmes.name: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the Internal Assessments
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent research piece supervised inside school. Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an exhibition of three objects and a prescribed-title essay. Every subject also carries its own Internal Assessment, marked against lettered criteria by the school and moderated externally. Together the core and the Internal Assessments account for a substantial share of the final grade in most subjects, and they are the work that most often slips.
programmes.countryNote: Deira schools set their own internal deadlines for these, usually well before any external upload date, and they rarely align between schools. A tutor's role here is bounded by IB academic-honesty rules: teaching method, reading a draft and giving feedback on the student's own writing, and coaching the research process. A tutor does not write any part of it, and this page says so because the alternative is an expulsion risk for the student.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-muteena.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and Middle Years subjects Al Muteena families ask for most, with the places marks are actually lost. The list is deliberately specific: a tutor matched to Physics HL and a tutor matched to Biology SL are not interchangeable, whatever a general science listing suggests.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and complex algebra at Higher Level. Marks go on unjustified steps, on sloppy notation in differentiation and integration, and on Paper 1 being sat without a calculator after a year of practising with one. Al Muteena students switching from a CBSE background usually have the algebra and need the written reasoning.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-heavy work. The common failure is treating it as the easier route and then meeting hypothesis testing and regression unprepared. Several Gulf engineering programmes list Analysis and Approaches specifically, so the route choice needs checking against a named university before DP1 begins.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry most of the lost marks. Higher Level adds depth rather than extra topics, so a Standard Level student who moves up mid-course meets unfamiliar rigour in familiar chapters. The Internal Assessment is marked on personal engagement, exploration, analysis, evaluation and communication.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields are where Deira students most often stall, usually because a free-body diagram is skipped and the algebra then hides the error. Paper 3 includes data-analysis and an option section. Uncertainty handling in the Internal Assessment is the single most recoverable band of marks in the subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content defeats more students than difficulty does. Command terms decide the mark: outline, explain, discuss and evaluate each expect a different shape of answer, and writing a good explanation when the question said outline wastes time without gaining credit. Statistics in the Internal Assessment is routinely underdone.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis; Paper 2 is comparative. Higher Level adds the written essay on a studied text. Students lose marks by summarising content rather than analysing how meaning is built, and by preparing the Individual Oral as a presentation instead of an argument about a global issue.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the quickest gain available: an axis mislabelled or a shift drawn the wrong way costs marks the written answer cannot recover. Higher Level adds quantitative paper work. The three commentaries must each use a different key concept and a recent news article, and they are routinely started too late.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A tool-heavy course where students quote frameworks without applying them to the stimulus. Higher Level adds extension topics and the pre-released case study. The Internal Assessment differs by level — a research project at Higher, a stimulus-based commentary at Standard — and the two are frequently confused in DP1.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Al Muteena students often arrive fluent in Python and unready for the paper's pseudocode and abstract data structures. Higher Level adds resource management and a case study. The solution-development Internal Assessment is marked on documented process as much as on working code.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics and Integrated Sciences
subjects.description: Marked against four criteria out of eight each. Criterion C, communicating, and criterion D, applying to real-life contexts, are where most Deira students lose grade points while knowing the content perfectly well. Fixing a criterion is a technique problem and usually takes weeks rather than terms.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: A KHDA-mandated subject in every Dubai private school regardless of curriculum, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Non-Arab Al Muteena students often treat it as a side subject until it appears on a report, and the recovery work is vocabulary and script fluency rather than grammar theory.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by the exhibition of three objects and the prescribed-title essay. The commonest problem is writing about the world rather than about knowledge: a strong essay argues about how a claim can be known, using the student's own examples, and that framing can be taught quickly once it is named.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in Al Muteena is really asking
paragraphs: The literal question is whether somebody qualified to teach the IB Diploma will come to a flat in Al Muteena. The underlying question is different: can my child get one-to-one help from someone who knows this exact course, at a time that works after the school run, at a price I can commit to for a term. Those are two separate problems, and treating them as one is why so many Deira families end up with a tutor who is convenient rather than correct.

In-home tutoring genuinely exists in Dubai and plenty of families use it. Published market rates put an in-home one-to-one visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Monthly packages advertised in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. So the travel premium is real and it is substantial, and the honest way to think about it is to ask what the premium buys.

What it buys is physical presence and a shorter shortlist. What it costs, beyond money, is choice. The people willing to drive to Al Muteena on a weekday evening are the people who live near Al Muteena, and the chance that one of them teaches Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and has marked that subject's Internal Assessment is simply low. Widen the radius to Al Nahda or Al Garhoud and it stays low. The constraint is not geography; it is that the Diploma splits into dozens of subject-and-level combinations and each one needs its own specialist.

IB Gram's answer is to drop the geography constraint entirely. Lessons to Al Muteena are delivered one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with shared screens and a shared whiteboard, and the tutor is chosen for the course your child sits. There are no home visits in the UAE at all — that is an India-only part of our service — and this page will not suggest otherwise. What follows is the arithmetic that makes the online format the better buy for a Deira family, laid out so you can check it rather than take it on trust.

sections.heading: Al Muteena against the next neighbourhood over
paragraphs: This is the comparison nobody publishes, so here it is. Five neighbourhoods a Deira family might live in or move between, compared on the four things that actually change a tutoring plan: how long the drive takes in the late afternoon, how many IB schools sit inside a twenty-minute radius, what the local in-home tutor pool realistically looks like, and the earliest hour a weekday session can start without a child arriving exhausted.

Read the table and the pattern is clear. Drive times vary by a factor of three. School access varies from none inside the neighbourhood to two within a short hop. Session start times vary by a full hour depending on which school your child attends and which road the bus takes home. Everything about the logistics is local, specific and worth knowing.

And then the last thing does not vary. In every one of these areas, the pool of people who will travel to a home and who also teach one named Higher Level subject is small. A family in Al Mamzar with a school on the doorstep faces the same shortage as a family in Al Muteena with a twenty-five minute commute. The Diploma is specialised enough that distance stops being the deciding factor long before the shortlist gets interesting.

Which is why the recommendation is the same on either side of Abu Baker Al Siddique Road: choose the tutor by the subject and level your child is examined in, accept that the lesson happens over video, and spend the saved travel premium on a second session a week instead. The one genuine advantage Al Muteena has over the villa districts is that an apartment makes a quiet study corner easy to set up — a desk, a headset and a door that closes is the whole technical requirement.

sections.heading: What Dubai charges, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Most pages in this market either refuse to publish a price or publish one in US dollars, which is not the currency a Deira family budgets in. So start at the bottom of the market and work up, because that is the order a parent weighing a monthly commitment actually thinks in.

At the cheapest end sit online sessions with university students and generalist tutors: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52. These rates are real and they have their uses — a Middle Years student who needs homework structure rather than syllabus expertise can be well served here. What they do not buy is someone who has taught a named Higher Level course against its mark scheme. A step up, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which is roughly where the qualified subject band begins.

Above that, specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and beyond; TutorChase lists AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 plus. In-home visits sit in their own band at AED 180 to 500 an hour because the figure absorbs travel. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 for named premium or examiner-led teaching. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 plus for specialist exam-year work.

Every one of those figures belongs to the provider named beside it, read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price. We publish them because a parent in Al Muteena deciding between a neighbour's cousin at AED 100 and an agency at AED 400 deserves to know what the bands are and what separates them. For IB Gram's own figure, the free trial lesson and the consultation that follows are the honest route — the price depends on subject, level and how many sessions a week the plan actually needs.

sections.heading: What the travel premium actually buys an Al Muteena family
paragraphs: Compare in-home and online on the hour you pay for rather than the rate you are quoted, and the gap widens. A ninety-minute in-home booking in Deira often delivers somewhere near seventy-five minutes of teaching, because the tutor arrives into Al Muteena's parking, settles, and then leaves early enough to beat the traffic back. That is not dishonesty on anyone's part; it is what a visit costs in a dense apartment district with contested street parking.

An online session starts at the minute agreed. The screen share is already up, last week's worked problems are already on the shared board, and a past-paper question can be annotated by both people at once. Ninety minutes booked is close to ninety minutes taught. Set that against a rate that is lower to begin with and the cost per hour of real teaching diverges sharply from the headline comparison.

There is a second, larger difference. An in-home booking in Al Muteena draws from the people who will drive to Al Muteena. An online booking draws from everyone teaching that subject at that level who is free at that hour in Gulf Standard Time. For a Chemistry HL student three weeks from an Internal Assessment deadline, that distinction decides whether the help is relevant at all. A generalist who can reach your door is not a substitute for a specialist who knows what criterion D rewards.

The honest counter-argument deserves stating. Some children do work better with a person in the room, and a very young child — Primary Years, below about eight — often does. For those families the market's in-home option may genuinely be the right purchase, and it is available in Dubai from providers who sell it. IB Gram does not; our UAE delivery is online, and the free trial lesson exists so that an Al Muteena family can test whether the format works for their child before committing to a term of it.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is odd, because the calendar is what decides whether tutoring starts in time to matter. UAE IB schools sit the May session, and the work that determines a final grade happens months before anyone opens an exam paper. Counting backwards from the exams rather than forwards from today is the only way to see which deadline is actually next.

Work back from the May window and the shape is this: the exams themselves, then roughly six to ten weeks of past-paper and command-term work before them, then mock exams in the preceding term, then the school's internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and the subject Internal Assessments, then the Theory of Knowledge exhibition, then the DP1 term in which Internal Assessment topics are first chosen. A student who starts tutoring eight weeks before the May session has already passed four of those milestones with whatever marks they earned.

Precise IB dates are not published here on purpose. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so every session and results date in this project is unverified, and an unverified date that a parent plans around is worse than no date. Confirm your child's exact windows with the school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, and treat the school's internal deadlines as the ones that bind — they usually sit well before any external upload date and they differ between Deira schools.

For Cambridge qualifications the picture is firmer and worth stating, because many Al Muteena students sit IGCSE before the Diploma. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate sits June, with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the day after, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong zone timetable — so always read your own school's version.

sections.heading: KHDA, inspection bands and what a Deira school report means
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. For an Al Muteena family the relevant body is KHDA, and its inspection reports are published and free to read.

The inspection band is useful and limited. It rates the school on a six-point scale and it reports on whole-school performance, which means a school rated well overall can still have a thin Higher Level cohort in one subject, and a school rated lower can have an outstanding Physics department. The number that matters to a Diploma parent is not the headline band; it is whether the subject your child sits is taught by a stable, experienced team this year. That is a question for the school directly, and it is a reasonable one to ask.

Scale context helps too. The Dubai Media Office reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen curricula, with UK provision at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three IB — creating 16,846 new places. IB provision in Dubai is growing from a small base, which is exactly why specialist Diploma teaching is thin on the ground in older districts like Deira.

One thing to be clear about: IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge, and holds no partnership with any of them. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with physical premises, and we do not claim it. Any tutoring page that advertises regulator-approved tutors is making a claim it almost certainly cannot show you the paperwork for, and in this emirate that is the single most misleading phrase available.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child in Al Muteena
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a surprising number of pages in this market imply otherwise. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced private tuition work permits, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so this page does not quote an amount — figures circulating online could not be verified against any official source and repeating them would be guesswork presented as fact. The official application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit – Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, listed with a two-working-day completion time and no fee.

There is a second rule Al Muteena parents should know, and it cuts against a common instinct. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct likewise bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than read from the policy document, so verify it against the current ADEK text before relying on it. The practical point stands either way: hiring your child's own classroom teacher privately is not the shortcut it looks like, and no reputable service should offer it.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again — that needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram operates no premises in the UAE and holds no such permit. What a parent can do is simple: ask any individual tutor whether they hold a current MoHRE private tuition work permit, and ask to see it. It is free to obtain, so there is no good reason for a working tutor not to have one.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may touch and what they may not
paragraphs: This is the line that matters most and the one this market crosses most often. One page found during research sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller — a withdrawn diploma is not a refundable purchase. Al Muteena parents should know what a legitimate tutor will and will not do before they ask for help with coursework.

A tutor may teach the subject content the assessment draws on. A tutor may explain each lettered criterion and what it rewards, so a student knows that criterion B asks for something different from criterion C. A tutor may help narrow a research question until it is answerable with the data a student can actually collect. A tutor may read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning does not hold, where the evaluation is thin, where the communication loses a reader. A tutor may coach the process: planning, timekeeping, referencing conventions, how to record a method so it can be followed.

A tutor may not write any part of the work. Not a paragraph, not an introduction, not a conclusion, not a rewritten method section. A tutor may not supply a topic that comes pre-answered, edit a draft into something the student could not have produced, or hand over a worked model to be adapted. A tutor may not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables — those are cited and linked to on their official sites, never copied.

Saying this plainly is a competitive advantage rather than a disclaimer. The Extended Essay and the Internal Assessments are the parts of the Diploma most responsive to good teaching, precisely because most students have never been taught how independent research is assessed. Teach that properly and the marks follow from the student's own work, which is the only version that survives moderation.
