sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA's guidelines required this to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year — April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. No competitor page in this market has a section on it, which is strange, because it appears on every Al Muteena child's report card.

The organisational rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two more details are worth a parent's attention. Schools must ensure all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential you can ask about directly. And instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit; schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, with the advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, which constrains how any tutoring in these subjects can legitimately be described.

In practice this matters to Al Muteena families in one specific way. A non-Arab Diploma student carrying Arabic as an additional language alongside three Higher Level subjects has a genuine timetable problem, and the mandatory subject is usually the one that gets dropped from the revision plan. Support here is vocabulary, script fluency and reading speed rather than grammar theory, and because the content itself is fixed by the Ministry, the work is about building access to the prescribed material rather than substituting anything for it.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what an IB or IGCSE student needs for UAE universities
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that recognises a foreign secondary certificate for use in the UAE, and it is absent from almost every page in this market. Al Muteena families with children heading to a UAE university should understand the requirements early, because the subject choices that satisfy them are made at fifteen or sixteen, not at eighteen.

For the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. That five-subject rule is worth knowing precisely because at least one ranking competitor page tells UAE parents the requirement is six subjects, which would change a child's option choices for no reason.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no equivalency points threshold published here, because none has been read on a Ministry of Education source, and publishing an unverified threshold on a page a parent plans around would be irresponsible. Check the figure on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority.

Two boundaries on this. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation — we can explain the process and point you to the official channel, and that is where our role ends. And nothing about tutoring is required for equivalency, university admission or school progression; it is help with learning, not a gate anyone has to pass through. Any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Getting started from Al Muteena, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The process is short and deliberately unglamorous. You tell us the subject, the level, the board and the school; we propose a tutor who teaches that exact combination; your child has a free trial lesson; you decide. If the match is wrong after the trial, say so and we propose someone else rather than asking you to make it work. Nothing is taken before the trial, and the trial exists to answer the only question that matters, which is whether your child engages with this tutor in this format.

What happens when no specialist is free is the part nobody discloses, so here it is. Some subject-and-level combinations are thin — Computer Science HL, Music, a specific Physics option — and there are weeks in the Dubai school year, particularly either side of mock exams, when the tutors who cover them are fully booked. In that case you get told. The choice offered is a waiting slot with a named date, a different session time that is available now, or a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to Gulf Standard Time. What you will not get is a generalist quietly substituted into a specialist slot.

Scheduling from Al Muteena has its own rhythm and it is worth being realistic about it. A child commuting back from Al Garhoud is not ready to think at four o'clock. Five is workable, six is better, and three shorter sessions a week usually beat one long one for a Middle Years student. During Ramadan many families move sessions to after Iftar, and that is a normal request rather than a special arrangement. School exam weeks are worth pausing for; a tutor competing with a school's own revision timetable helps nobody.

One practical note on the technical side, because Al Muteena is an apartment district. The requirement is a quiet corner, a reliable connection, a headset and a device with a camera. A tablet works; a desk works better. If two siblings are tutored on the same evening, stagger them rather than running them in the same room — the shared whiteboard work needs a student who can talk out loud without an audience.

process.description: You see who is proposed and what they teach before anything is booked. If the available specialist does not match the exact combination your child sits, you are told that rather than offered a near-enough alternative dressed up as a match.

process.title: You decide, and you can change your mind
process.description: If the trial worked, a weekly slot is set against your child's school timetable. If it did not, tell us and a different tutor is proposed. A wrong match identified in week one costs nothing; a wrong match tolerated for a term costs a term.

process.title: Review on the school's calendar, not ours
process.description: Progress is reviewed around the school's own mock exams and internal deadlines, because those are the dates that decide grades. Sessions pause during school exam weeks and step up for the revision block before the May session.

whyPoints.description: An in-home booking in Al Muteena draws on tutors willing to travel to Al Muteena. For a narrow Higher Level combination, that is the difference between a specialist and whoever is nearest.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is the plan
whyPoints.description: Tutoring is built backwards from the May session and from your child's school deadlines for Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay, which usually fall well before any external date. A plan that ignores those dates is a plan that arrives after the marks are already set.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches method, explains lettered criteria and gives feedback on work the student wrote. A tutor does not write, rewrite or complete any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. In a market where completed coursework is openly sold, the line is worth drawing in public.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed, not concealed
whyPoints.description: When no specialist covers a combination in the week you need it, you are told, and offered a dated waiting slot, a different time, or a tutor outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus on Gulf Standard Time. Nobody is quietly substituted into a specialist slot.

faqs.question: Will an IB tutor actually come to our flat in Al Muteena?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Our UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE — that is a service we run only in India. Other providers in Dubai do sell in-home visits, at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and if having someone physically present is essential for your child that option exists. What we offer instead is a tutor matched to your child's exact subject and level, which in Deira is usually the harder thing to find.

faqs.question: Is tutoring in Al Muteena cheaper than in Al Garhoud or Al Mamzar?
faqs.answer: For online tuition the neighbourhood makes no difference to the rate, because there is no travel to price in. For in-home visits it does: market rates tend to sit at the higher end of the AED 180 to 500 band for areas that are slower to reach at five in the afternoon, and crossing the Sharjah line into Al Nahda can add a premium again. The more significant difference between these areas is not price but shortlist length, and on that measure all of them are short for any single Higher Level subject.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do Al Muteena children usually attend?
faqs.answer: There is no IB World School inside Al Muteena itself. Families typically travel to Deira International School or Universal American School in Al Garhoud, or to Al Ittihad Private School in Al Mamzar, with GEMS Modern Academy further out. Many Al Muteena children attend British or Indian-curriculum schools in Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Oud Metha instead and sit IGCSE at sixteen. These schools are named as context for the area's education ecosystem; no affiliation or endorsement is implied.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start after the Deira school run?
faqs.answer: Five in the evening is workable and six is better. A child travelling back from Al Garhoud through the airport tunnel at half past three is usually home by half past four and not ready to think for a while after that. Students at schools in Al Mamzar or Al Qusais often manage half past four. For younger children, three short sessions a week in the early evening tend to work better than one long block, and during Ramadan many Al Muteena families move the slot to after Iftar.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Diploma tutor cost in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: Published market rates, read in October 2026, run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour for budget online help, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 650 at the premium end. Those figures belong to the providers that publish them, not to IB Gram. Our own rate depends on subject, level and session frequency, and the free trial lesson comes before any quote.

faqs.question: Does my child need Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: It depends on where they are applying. Several engineering and quantitative degree programmes in the Gulf and beyond list Analysis and Approaches specifically, so the route choice should be checked against a named university's own entry page before DP1 starts rather than after. Applications and Interpretation is not the easy option — it carries statistics, modelling and hypothesis testing that catch out students who chose it expecting less work. If the plan is undecided, Analysis and Approaches keeps more doors open.

faqs.question: Do tutors visiting an Al Muteena flat need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced private tuition work permits through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any individual tutor to show you their permit — it costs nothing to obtain, so a working tutor has no reason not to hold one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help an Al Muteena student with the Chemistry Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the underlying chemistry, explain what each lettered criterion rewards, help narrow the research question to something answerable with available equipment, and give feedback on a draft your child has written. A tutor cannot write any part of it, rewrite it to completion, or supply a model to adapt. Coursework sold ready-made is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, so this boundary protects your child rather than limiting the help.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely as effective for an Al Muteena student?
faqs.answer: For Diploma and Middle Years subject work, generally yes, and often better, because the tutor is chosen for the syllabus rather than for the postcode. A ninety-minute online session delivers close to ninety minutes of teaching, where a visit to an apartment block in Deira loses time to parking, settling and an early exit before the traffic. The honest exception is young children, roughly below eight, who often do need a person in the room. The free trial lesson is there so you can test the format rather than assume it.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge exam series do UAE students actually sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate sits June with November as the resit route. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong zone timetable, so read your own school's version.

faqs.question: My child has mocks in six weeks. Is it too late to start in Al Muteena?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change shape. Six weeks is enough for exam technique and for two or three specific topics, not for a full syllabus. The first session should be diagnostic — a marked past paper that separates topic gaps from question-type errors — because a student losing marks to command terms needs something completely different from a student who has not covered a chapter. Expect two or three sessions a week in that window and timed practice under real paper conditions from the start.

faqs.question: What does my child need alongside the Diploma for Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of its licensed curriculum, and KHDA required this in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arabs. Using different or additional content without Ministry permission is prohibited, so support here means building access to the prescribed material rather than substituting anything for it.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does an Al Muteena child need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five, not six. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one ranking page in this market tells UAE parents the figure is six. Verify on moe.gov.ae before making option choices, and note that IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers my child's subject that week?
faqs.answer: You get told, plainly. Some combinations are thin — Computer Science HL, a particular Physics option, Music — and around Dubai mock-exam weeks the specialists who cover them fill up. The choices offered are a waiting slot with a named date, a different session time that is free now, or a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to Gulf Standard Time. A generalist is not quietly substituted into a specialist slot, because that wastes a term before anyone notices.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by KHDA or the IB for tutoring in Al Muteena?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with physical premises in Dubai, and we do not hold or imply it. Any tutoring page advertising regulator-approved tutors should be asked to produce the permit number, because in this emirate that phrase is the easiest one to get wrong.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach two of my children in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the subjects match their specialism, but stagger the sessions rather than running them together. Online one-to-one work depends on a student talking through their reasoning out loud and annotating a shared board, and a sibling in the same room changes that. In an Al Muteena flat the practical arrangement is usually one child at six and the other at half past seven, in the same quiet corner. If the two children need genuinely different subjects, two matched specialists will do more than one generalist covering both.

intro.heading: What a home tutor costs in Al Nahda, and what you are paying the premium for
paragraphs: The question is a fair one, so here is the arithmetic before anything else. Published Dubai in-home tutoring rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai table shows AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. Translated into the monthly commitments families actually sign, the market shows in-home packages of around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions, against about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Twice the money for half the sessions is the shape of the whole decision.

The premium is not teaching quality. It is a car, and in Al Nahda it is a particularly expensive car. This neighbourhood sits on the Dubai-Sharjah boundary, with Al Ittihad Road alongside it carrying one of the heaviest commuter flows in the country every evening. A tutor coming in from Barsha, the Marina or Jumeirah at 16:30 is budgeting forty to seventy minutes each way, and that is on a normal day. The published rate reflects that time, and the cancellation rate reflects it too.

What the premium does buy is real, and worth naming honestly rather than dismissing. A person in the room can see a page without it being photographed, can sit beside a younger child who will not stay on a call, and does not depend on a household's broadband. For some families those things decide it. If that is your decision, make it knowing what it costs and what it narrows: at AED 180 to 500 an hour the tutor has to be someone willing to drive to Al Nahda in the evening peak, and that willingness has nothing to do with whether they know Chemistry HL.

That narrowing is the part most families underestimate. IB Diploma subjects are not interchangeable - Mathematics alone is four separate courses, and Chemistry HL under the current guide is a different teaching job from Chemistry SL. Filter for tutors who will travel to Al Nahda and you are choosing from a short list defined by geography. Filter for the course, over video, and you are choosing from the whole Gulf evening. The second list contains the specialist; the first list contains whoever is closest.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and that is stated identically on every UAE page on this site so a reader can check it is policy rather than a line. What we deliver to Al Nahda is one-to-one tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched by course and level, with a free trial lesson first - one lesson with the matched tutor, with the fee discussed afterwards.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nahda.programmesIntro: Families in Al Nahda ask for home tutoring across all three IB programmes, and the cost case differs for each because the scarcity of the right tutor differs. Here is how the money works at each stage.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and internal assessments in most subjects. Each subject is examined in its own way, and at Higher Level the specialism is real: a tutor who is strong on Chemistry HL mechanisms is not automatically the person for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL.

Diploma Higher Level specialists are the scarcest match in the UAE market, and insisting one also drives to Al Nahda in the evening narrows the pool to almost nothing. Published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour buy proximity, not specialism.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject scored from 0 to 8, assessed through tasks rather than papers. The tutor requirement here is criterion literacy rather than advanced content knowledge, and that is a different scarcity: plenty of people can teach MYP 3 mathematics, far fewer can explain why a student scored 4 on investigating patterns.
programmes.countryNote: MYP cohorts near Al Nahda sit mainly in Al Mamzar, Al Garhoud and Festival City, so local in-home tutors have often never seen a criterion report. Ask any tutor to name the four criteria for your child's subject group before paying anything.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, with no external examinations. Support at this stage is usually about literacy, number fluency and confidence rather than about subject content, and short frequent sessions work better than long ones.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one age group where a parent's preference for someone physically present is hardest to argue with, and we say so. A six-year-old who will not engage with a screen is a genuine limit on online delivery, and we would rather tell an Al Nahda family that than sell them something unsuitable.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nahda.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Nahda families most often ask for when they search for an IB home tutor, with a note on how scarce the right person is and therefore how much the geographic filter costs you.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic and calculus-heavy route, with a non-calculator paper that examines manipulation directly. HL adds a third paper. The most requested Diploma subject in this area and the one where course-level matching matters most, because AA and AI are genuinely different courses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with a calculator permitted throughout. Marks sit in selecting the right test and writing a conclusion in context rather than in manipulation. A tutor strong on AA can be a poor fit here, and the reverse is equally true.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Six themes under Structure and Reactivity in the current guide, with two written papers and a scientific investigation. Higher Level organic mechanisms are the scarcest teaching skill in this subject, and no amount of local availability substitutes for it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, two papers with data-based questions inside Paper 1, and a scientific investigation. Physics needs longer unbroken sessions than most subjects, which makes the travel arithmetic worse: a ninety-minute in-home block is a two-and-a-half hour commitment for the tutor.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy with marks concentrated in precise written explanation and in data analysis. A common and comparatively well-supplied subject, which means the in-home premium is harder to justify here than in physics or HL chemistry.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams, definitions, evaluation and the internal assessment commentaries. Students lose marks by describing rather than evaluating, and by drawing a correct diagram without referring to it in the answer. Well supplied at SL, tighter at HL.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis, the individual oral, the learner portfolio and Paper 1 unseen commentary. The oral is the component students prepare least and panic about most, and it is one of the easier things to rehearse properly over video.

subjects.name: Internal assessments, TOK and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Supervision against published criteria, with the student writing every word. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate a research question and mark a draft against the descriptors; a tutor may not write, redraft to completion or supply content. This is a boundary, not a limitation.

sections.heading: The border premium: why in-home quotes to Al Nahda sit at the top of the range
paragraphs: Al Nahda's geography is the single biggest driver of what a home tutor charges to come here, and it is worth setting out properly because no competitor page does. The neighbourhood sits against the Dubai-Sharjah boundary, with Al Ittihad Road running alongside it as one of the busiest commuter corridors in the country. The flow is directional and predictable: heavy towards Sharjah in the late afternoon and evening, heavy towards Dubai in the morning. A tutor travelling in from New Dubai arrives against that flow in the afternoon and leaves into it at night.

Forty to seventy minutes each way is the realistic budget on a term-time evening, which means a one-hour lesson is a two-and-a-half hour commitment. At the published Dubai in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, a tutor pricing their own time rationally lands at the upper end for this neighbourhood rather than the lower. That is not opportunism; it is arithmetic. It also explains why in-home arrangements in Al Nahda tend to settle on Friday and Saturday rather than on school nights.

Weekend-only tutoring creates a second problem that families discover a month in. The gap between a lesson and the homework it was meant to fix becomes six days, and for cumulative subjects like mathematics and physics that gap is where the benefit leaks away. Frequency matters more than session length for repairing algebra or correcting method, and the in-home model in this neighbourhood systematically trades frequency for presence.

The third consequence is the one with the largest effect on outcomes. A tutor who will travel to Al Nahda at 16:30 is self-selected by willingness to travel, not by subject specialism. For a Year 8 maths catch-up that is a reasonable trade. For Chemistry HL organic mechanisms, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL, or an internal assessment three weeks from a school deadline, it is the wrong trade, and the published price does not reflect that it is the wrong trade.

sections.heading: The same budget, spent two ways: an Al Nahda worked example
paragraphs: Abstract bands are hard to act on, so take a single figure a family in this neighbourhood might actually commit and spend it twice. Call it AED 1,700 a month, which sits inside the published in-home package range of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Spent in-home, that buys eight contact hours a month in four sessions, one a week, with the tutor chosen largely from those willing to travel here at the time you need.

Spent online at the published qualified-tutor band of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, the same AED 1,700 buys somewhere between six and eleven contact hours depending on where in the band the match sits - and at the lower end it buys two sessions a week rather than one. The market's own packaged comparison makes the point more sharply: about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Roughly half the money for twice the number of sessions.

The second difference is what the hours can be spent on. Four long weekly in-home sessions suit content teaching and suit a student who needs a sustained push through a syllabus. Two shorter sessions a week suit diagnosis and correction - mark the work, name the error, drill it, check it next session - which is what actually moves a grade in mathematics, chemistry calculations and physics data handling. The shape of the week is not a detail.

The third is who you get. At AED 1,700 a month online, a family in Al Nahda can hold out for a Higher Level specialist in the exact course their child sits. At the same figure in-home, the constraint is the drive. sections.heading: Two regulators, one neighbourhood: what Al Nahda parents need to know
paragraphs: Al Nahda is one of the few places in the UAE where a tutoring or schooling conversation genuinely crosses an emirate line, and almost no page in this market mentions it. Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Across the boundary, Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which u.ae states regulates private education in that emirate.

The difference is not only who inspects. Sharjah's authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum and fee approval, not just inspection, sits with the emirate regulator. For a family comparing a Dubai-side school with a Sharjah-side one a few minutes away, that means two different approval regimes behind the prospectus, and inspection reports that are not directly comparable with each other.

The completeness of the map is worth having. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in that emirate. Sharjah sits with its own authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched in this market and Sharjah's authority by one, which is a strange gap given how many Gulf families move between emirates.

One federal rule applies throughout. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.

sections.heading: Is your tutor permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: Anyone considering a home tutor in Al Nahda should ask this before money changes hands, and the answer is public. Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Because the permit costs nothing and takes two working days, a tutor working regularly in this market has no financial reason to be without one. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

No fine schedule is published. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so a figure circulating online as the penalty should be treated as unverified, and we do not publish one. What a parent can do is ask the question and note the quality of the answer. A tutor who explains the permit, or who says plainly that they are applying, has told you something useful. One who changes the subject has told you something else.

A second boundary catches families out innocently. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct reported as barring the same arrangement. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document, but treat the principle as sound anywhere in the Emirates. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity again and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no claim to one.

sections.heading: What an Al Nahda family actually gets from us, stated plainly
paragraphs: One-to-one tuition over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a tutor matched to the exact course and level your child sits rather than to the subject name. A free trial lesson first: one lesson with that matched tutor, with the fee discussed afterwards rather than before. If the fit is wrong, you say so and we match again, because a student who does not want to talk to their tutor will not learn from them and that is better discovered in week one.

What we do not do, in plain terms. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We do not operate an office, centre or branch in the Emirates. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing on this page should be read as implying one. We publish no success rate, no star rating and no student headcount, because none of those could be produced on request.

On availability, which most providers leave vague. Demand for Higher Level specialists concentrates in the same two hours of the Gulf evening, and in October and in the weeks before mocks those hours fill. If no specialist in your child's exact course is free in your window, you are told at the match stage with three options: a different slot with the right specialist, a tutor with adjacent expertise starting now, or a wait with a date attached. A disclosed wait costs an Al Nahda family less than a mismatched tutor discovered in February.

And on coursework, which is the thing worth being unambiguous about. Internal assessments, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essays and the Personal Project must be the student's own work under IB academic-honesty rules. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate a research question, mark a draft against the descriptors and say a section is below standard. A tutor may not write, redraft to completion, choose the topic or supply the content. Research into this market found a provider publishing a price for completed Internal Assessments; the consequence of buying one falls on the student, potentially the diploma itself.

sections.heading: Cost in context: school fees, tutoring and what Al Nahda households actually control
paragraphs: Tutoring decisions are made inside a wider education budget, and the Dubai figures for that budget are published. The emirate's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with an enrolment split of 37% UK curriculum, 26% Indian, 14% US and 7% International Baccalaureate. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%.

KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For an Al Nahda family that is the useful anchor: the largest line in the education budget is flat for the year ahead, which makes the tutoring line the part still fully under the household's control.

That control is why the in-home versus online decision deserves five minutes of arithmetic rather than a default. The difference between about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits is, over a Diploma year, several thousand dirhams. Spent on an extra weekly session with the right specialist, that difference buys frequency and specialism. Spent on travel, it buys presence. Both are legitimate purchases and only one of them is usually examined.

Note also that a Sharjah-side family is working within a different fee-approval regime, since Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees as well as curricula. Any comparison of total education cost across the boundary should be made on each school's own published figures rather than on an emirate-wide assumption. We quote no price list on these pages; the free trial exists so a family can judge a tutor before the fee conversation happens at all.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what an IB or IGCSE student needs for a UAE university
paragraphs: Families in Al Nahda often come to tutoring with a destination in mind, and for those planning to study in the UAE the equivalency process matters. The Ministry of Education sets out what a secondary certificate must show before it is recognised, and the British-track requirements are published clearly. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

Two details inside that are worth knowing because a ranking competitor publishes them wrongly. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. And the requirement is five subjects, not six - at least one page ranking for these queries tells UAE candidates they must take six, which is the kind of error that causes a family to pay for an extra entry they did not need. Verify against the Ministry's own channel before acting on either figure.

For American-track students the requirements run differently: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For IB candidates there is no points threshold we are willing to publish, because none has been read on the Ministry's own site. Any figure you see quoted for IB equivalency should be checked against moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly.

Nothing about this process is something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not required for it. IB Gram does not handle equivalency, attestation or university applications on a family's behalf, and we would not describe tutoring as necessary for a regulatory process. What a tutor can do is make sure the grades a student is aiming at are the ones their destination actually requires, which is a planning conversation worth having in Year 11 rather than in Year 13.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor in Al Nahda through IB Gram?
faqs.answer: No, and it is better to say so on the page than after a deposit. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson we arrange is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The Dubai market does supply in-home tutors, at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, and this page sets out what that premium buys and what it narrows so you can judge the trade rather than guess at it.

faqs.question: Why do home tutors charge more to come to Al Nahda than to other parts of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because of where Al Nahda sits. The neighbourhood is on the Dubai-Sharjah boundary beside Al Ittihad Road, one of the heaviest commuter corridors in the country, and a tutor travelling in from New Dubai budgets forty to seventy minutes each way on a term-time evening. A one-hour lesson becomes a two-and-a-half hour commitment, so a tutor pricing their own time rationally lands at the top of the published AED 180 to 500 band rather than the bottom. Cancellation risk rises for the same reason.

faqs.question: What does AED 1,700 a month buy in Al Nahda, in-home against online?
faqs.answer: In-home, that figure sits inside the published package range of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits - eight contact hours a month in four weekly sessions, with the tutor drawn from those willing to travel here at your time. Online at the published qualified-tutor band of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, the same money buys roughly six to eleven hours and often two sessions a week rather than one. The market's own packaged comparison is about AED 799 monthly for eight online sessions.

faqs.question: Is online IB tutoring genuinely as good as having someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma and Middle Years work, yes, and for some of it better. Written work photographed and annotated live, a shared whiteboard and screen-shared papers reproduce the part of a lesson that matters. Where presence genuinely wins is with young children who will not engage with a screen, and with households where broadband is unreliable. We would rather name those cases than pretend they do not exist. For a Year 12 chemistry student, course-level specialism matters far more than physical presence.

faqs.question: Which part of Al Nahda am I in, and does it change the schooling?
faqs.answer: It changes it considerably. Al Nahda 1 and 2 on the Dubai side sit under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, while Al Nahda across the boundary sits under the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods as well as inspecting, so two schools minutes apart can sit under different approval regimes with inspection reports that are not directly comparable. Check which authority your child's school answers to before comparing anything.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a student in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: For well-supplied requests - Standard Level content, Middle Years mathematics and sciences, IGCSE bridging - usually within a few days. For Higher Level specialists in a named course, longer, because demand concentrates in the same two hours of the Gulf evening and those hours fill in October and before mocks. The honest version is that we tell you the position at the match stage with three options: a different slot with the right specialist, adjacent expertise starting now, or a wait with a date attached to it.

faqs.question: Do I need to check whether a home tutor in Dubai holds a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a fair question to ask anyone, including us. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, a working tutor has no financial reason to lack one. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher tutor them privately at home?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid, however convenient it looks. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring the same thing. Verify current wording against the authority's own policy document. The underlying principle - that the person assessing your child should not also be paid privately by you - holds across the Emirates.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects do Al Nahda families most often ask for?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, split across the four Diploma courses, then chemistry and physics, then economics and English A. Mathematics dominates because it is compulsory and because the four courses are genuinely different, so a mismatch is easy to make. Chemistry and physics requests cluster at Higher Level and are the hardest to staff. Internal assessment and Extended Essay supervision comes up heavily in Year 12 term two and Year 13 term one, around the school's own internal deadlines.

faqs.question: Will a tutor draft any part of my child's Internal Assessment or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: No, and anybody who says yes is putting your child at risk. Under IB academic-honesty rules that work must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the published criteria, interrogate a research question, explain why a section does not meet a descriptor, mark a draft and say plainly that it is below standard. A tutor may not write it, redraft it to completion, choose the topic or supply the content. Research into this market found a provider publishing a price for completed Internal Assessments; the consequence of that falls on the student.

faqs.question: What time can lessons start for a student living in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: School days across this catchment end between roughly 14:30 and 15:15, and buses put most students home between 15:00 and 15:45, later for those travelling to Al Garhoud or Festival City. That gives two realistic windows on a school night: about 15:45 to 17:00, and about 19:30 to 21:15 after the family has eaten. The mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies homework that all Dubai private schools set usually occupies the gap. Weekend mornings are the best long block of the week.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai fee freeze affect what we should spend on IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: It changes the household arithmetic rather than the tutoring choice. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. With the largest education line flat, the tutoring line is the part a family still controls - which is an argument for choosing between in-home and online deliberately rather than defaulting to whichever was easier to arrange.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Dubai a better option than a home tutor?
faqs.answer: For a different problem, yes. A centre or group class is the cheapest per hour and works for a student near a grade boundary who needs structured reminding across a syllabus. It cannot address an individual content gap, because the class cannot stop for one student. Note also that a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific authorisation - worth asking about if a centre describes itself in regulatory terms.

faqs.question: What happens if the trial lesson does not go well?
faqs.answer: You say so and we match again. The trial is one lesson with the matched tutor, with the fee discussed afterwards rather than agreed in advance, and its purpose is exactly this decision. Fit failures are common and usually have nothing to do with competence: pace, manner, how much the student is allowed to talk. A student who does not want to speak to their tutor will not learn from them, and that is far cheaper to discover in week one than in month three.

intro.heading: Al Quoz, Business Bay, Meydan: the comparison most parents are actually running
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Quoz is a search with a comparison hidden inside it. Al Quoz is a central district split between warehouses, art spaces along Alserkal Avenue, car showrooms on Sheikh Zayed Road, and residential pockets in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3. Families living there are rarely more than fifteen minutes from Business Bay, Downtown Dubai, Al Jaddaf, Meydan or Sobha Hartland. So when a parent types the phrase, the question underneath it is often comparative: does living in Al Quoz rather than Business Bay change what tutoring my child can get?

The short answer is that it changes the drive and nothing else that matters. The number of Diploma Programme teachers who happen to live within twenty minutes of Al Quoz 2 is a transport fact, not an educational one. What determines whether a tutor is any use to your child is whether that person has taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or has marked enough Chemistry Paper 2 responses to know that a student who writes a correct answer without a justification loses the mark anyway. Geography has no bearing on either.

This is where the in-home model breaks down in a district like Al Quoz. If you insist on someone physically arriving at a residential address off Latifa Bint Hamdan Street, rather than on a live online session into the same room, you are selecting from whoever is free, qualified, permitted and willing to cross Al Khail Road at half past five. In practice that is a short list, and it gets shorter the narrower the subject. Ask for Physics Higher Level with real Paper 3 experience and the list may be empty on the day you need it. Ask for the same specialist online and the constraint disappears entirely.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. For Al Quoz, and for every other Dubai district, lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled around your child's school day and the family's own evenings. That is stated plainly here because it is the first thing a parent needs to know, and because the comparison that follows only works if the premise is honest.

What this page does is run the comparison properly. It sets Al Quoz against the districts immediately around it, shows what the Dubai market charges in AED for each delivery format, counts the Diploma calendar backwards from the May session, explains what KHDA inspection bands actually mean when you read a school report, and sets out what a tutor is permitted to do with an internal assessment. If you finish it still unsure, the trial lesson exists so you can test the answer rather than take it on trust.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-quoz.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and Al Quoz families usually meet it in the middle. Most children in the district attend British or Indian curriculum primaries and then move into an IB school at Year 7 or Year 12. Each programme below is described with what it means for a family on this side of Al Khail Road.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Learning is organised into transdisciplinary units of inquiry, and the programme closes with the Exhibition in the final year, where a group of students research a question of their own and present it. Progress is reported against learner-profile attributes and approaches to learning rather than subject percentages, which is why PYP reports read so differently from the British curriculum reports many Al Quoz parents are used to.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Quoz and Al Barsha families run a British primary followed by an IB secondary, so the child meets inquiry-based reporting for the first time in Year 7. PYP tutoring in this district is mostly about English reading fluency and number sense, not exam technique, because there is no exam to prepare for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a 1 to 7 grade after a published conversion. MYP Year 5 students take on the Personal Project independently, an extended independent piece with its own criteria and process journal. The criterion language is the part families find hardest: a strong piece of writing can still sit at criterion C level 4 if the student never addressed what criterion C asks for.
programmes.countryNote: GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail in Al Quoz 2 and the IB schools along the central corridor run MYP, and the Personal Project lands in the same term as school mock weeks. Tutoring here is usually criterion translation: taking the published wording and showing the student what a level 7-8 response contains that a level 5-6 one does not.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the Creativity, Activity, Service requirement. Subject grades run 1 to 7, with up to three further points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix, for a maximum of 45. Each subject also carries an internal assessment marked by the school and moderated by the IB, which for most sciences is 20 per cent of the final grade.
programmes.countryNote: This is where almost all Al Quoz tutoring demand sits. The pattern is consistent: a student arrives from IGCSE in Year 12, meets Higher Level Mathematics or Chemistry, and discovers the step in abstraction is larger than anyone warned. Support in the first DP1 term is far cheaper than repair work in DP2.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two Diploma Programme subject courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning element, personal and professional skills, and a language development requirement. It suits a student who wants IB subject rigour alongside an applied qualification rather than the full six-subject Diploma. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools rather than being widely available.
programmes.countryNote: CP is rare across Dubai, so an Al Quoz family on this route is usually travelling further for school than a Diploma family would. Tutoring demand on the CP comes from the DP courses inside it, which are assessed identically to the same courses in the full Diploma.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-quoz.subjectsIntro: Al Quoz sits near both British-curriculum and IB secondaries, so requests arrive from Diploma students in the second year and from Year 11 students who have just chosen their DP subjects. These are the courses most often asked for, described by what they assess rather than by how interesting they are.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency. The Higher Level paper set includes Paper 3, a longer two-part investigation worth 20 per cent of the grade, and it is the component students have least practice with because schools often reach it late. Most lost marks are notation and justification rather than method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use. Students are expected to work fluently with the graphical display calculator and to interpret output in context. The common failure is a technically correct calculation presented without the sentence that answers the question actually asked.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is multiple choice plus data analysis, Paper 2 extended response, and Paper 3 covers experimental work and the option. Marks go missing on uncertainty treatment, graph gradients used without units, and explanations that describe a phenomenon rather than applying a named principle to it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium carry the most Higher Level weight. The internal assessment is 20 per cent, and the usual problem is a research question too broad to be measured properly in a school laboratory, which then caps the analysis and evaluation criteria.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the grade here more than content recall does. Students who write everything they know about a topic in response to an 'explain' question score less than students who answer only what was asked. Statistical treatment in the internal assessment is where Higher Level candidates most often fall short.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, correct axis labelling and evaluation that reaches a judgement rather than listing both sides. The internal assessment is three commentaries on published news articles, each with a strict word limit, and students routinely lose marks for choosing an article that does not actually illustrate the syllabus concept they wanted.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works, and the Individual Oral links a global issue to two texts. Weak scripts summarise the text; strong ones analyse how meaning is constructed and sustain that argument across the whole response.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application under time pressure, and an internal assessment based on a real organisation. The research project needs genuine primary or secondary evidence, and students who pick a company they cannot get data about discover the problem far too late to change it.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking, pseudocode conventions and the internal assessment solution for an identified client. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and resource management. Most mark loss comes from pseudocode written in a language the student knows rather than in the IB's own notation.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together these supply up to three points on the Diploma matrix. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words with a required reflection process, and TOK is assessed by an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. Both reward a narrow, arguable question and punish a broad topic.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in Al Quoz is really asking
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Quoz means, to most parents typing it, one-to-one Diploma or MYP teaching that fits into a weekday evening at home. The home part is about convenience and supervision, not about the tutor's physical presence. IB Gram meets that need with live one-to-one video lessons into Al Quoz homes, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and does not send tutors to UAE addresses at all.

It is worth separating the two things the phrase bundles together. The first is a place: your child works at the kitchen table or in their room, at a time that does not require another car journey after a long school day. That part is delivered exactly as searched. The second is a person physically in the room, and that is the part where the market in Dubai works against you rather than for you, because it narrows your choice of teacher to whoever can reach Al Quoz at the hour you need.

Al Quoz makes this unusually clear. The district is largely industrial by land area, with housing concentrated in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3, so the pool of qualified Diploma subject teachers who both live nearby and are free at 5pm is small by construction. A family in Sobha Hartland has a different small pool. Neither pool is the right size for a Higher Level Physics request, which is why the sensible move is to stop drawing circles on a map and start selecting on subject and level.

That is the argument this page makes, and it is made with numbers rather than adjectives in the sections below: what the market charges, what travel costs you, what the calendar demands, and what a tutor is allowed to do with coursework.

sections.heading: Al Quoz against the next neighbourhood over
paragraphs: The comparison most parents run is between their own district and the one they almost moved to. For Al Quoz that is usually Business Bay, Meydan, Al Jaddaf or Sobha Hartland. The table below sets out what actually differs, and the pattern is consistent: the housing stock changes, the drive changes, the realistic session start time changes by an hour or so, and the question of which subject specialist your child needs does not change at all.

Session timing is the one genuinely local variable. In Downtown and Business Bay, children are bussed out of the district to school and arrive home late, so the earliest workable weekday slot is nearer 6pm. In Sobha Hartland, where two schools sit inside the community, 4.30pm is realistic. Al Quoz lands in between, and depends heavily on whether the school run goes towards Al Barsha or across Al Khail Road.

Everything else in the table is logistics. None of it tells you whether the person teaching your child understands why a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches candidate keeps losing Paper 3 marks on notation. That is a property of the teacher, and once lessons are online it is the only property you need to select on.

One more difference is worth naming, because parents notice it and then draw the wrong conclusion from it. Districts with schools inside them, such as Sobha Hartland, feel better supplied with tutors simply because teachers working at those schools live nearby. That is a residential accident, and in Abu Dhabi it would also raise a professional-ethics question, since ADEK's rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school and the MoHRE permit carries a comparable code of conduct. Proximity is not the same thing as suitability, and sometimes it is the opposite of it.

sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same in Al Quoz and in Business Bay
paragraphs: Run the comparison to its conclusion and it collapses. If the deciding factor were local tutor supply, then moving from Al Quoz to Meydan would improve your child's Chemistry grade, which is obviously false. The deciding factor is the match between the teacher's subject expertise and the specific component where marks are being lost, and that match is made from the whole pool or from a geographic slice of it.

An in-home arrangement forces the slice. The tutor must be qualified in the subject, free in the slot, willing to drive, and in possession of the MoHRE private tuition work permit that Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 requires of individuals offering private lessons. Each condition is reasonable on its own. Stacked, they produce a very short list, and the list is shortest exactly where demand is most specialised: Higher Level Physics, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, Chemistry internal assessment supervision.

The table below compares the formats on the things a parent is actually buying. The travel column is where the in-home premium lives: market rates for a home visit in Dubai run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 per hour according to Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The gap is not teaching quality. It is a car on Al Khail Road at the busiest hour of the day, billed to you.

There is a scheduling consequence too. A tutor who drives can usually fit two or three sessions into an evening; a tutor who does not can fit four or five, and can take the 9pm slot a family in a different time zone needs. That is why online availability is better at precisely the hours Al Quoz parents find hardest to fill.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs around Al Quoz, and where the money goes
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in. So here are the AED bands, attributed, with the caveat that these are market rates rather than IB Gram's own. Our pricing is discussed on the consultation call after the free trial, because it depends on subject, level and how many sessions a week the plan actually needs.

Start from the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number that hits the household budget. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 per month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 per month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The waste is rarely in the hourly rate. It is in buying general tutoring when the problem is one component. A DP2 Chemistry student losing marks on organic mechanisms and nowhere else does not need two years of weekly Chemistry; that student needs six focused sessions on mechanisms and past-paper marking, and then to stop. Paying a premium rate for broad revision of content the student already knows is the most expensive mistake available in this market, and it is far more common than paying too much per hour.

sections.heading: The Diploma calendar counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session. Working backwards from it is the single most useful planning exercise a DP family can do, and no competitor page in this market does it. Note one thing first: IB session and results dates in this project are not independently verified, because ibo.org blocks automated access. Confirm every specific date with your child's IB coordinator, who holds the school's own version of this calendar.

The milestones that matter are internal before they are external. Internal assessment drafts, the Extended Essay reflection sessions, Theory of Knowledge exhibition submission and the school's own mock window all fall well before the examination papers, and they are set by the school rather than by the IB. That is why two Al Quoz students at different schools can be in completely different states of panic in the same week.

For a family starting from zero, the practical rule is that anything you want to influence through tutoring needs about eight weeks of runway. Six focused sessions on one component, spread across eight weeks with the student's own practice in between, changes outcomes. The same six sessions compressed into the fortnight before a paper mostly produce a tired student. The table sets the sequence out so you can see where your child currently sits.

For the IGCSE side of the same household the calendar is different and better documented. Cambridge International runs its examinations in a June series and a November series, with the February and March series offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate sits June with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Both publish provisional timetables ahead of a series and both revise them, so the rule is to read the official timetable rather than a date on a tutoring page. As checkable reference points: Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, Extended Essay or TOK essay
paragraphs: This market contains operators who sell completed internal assessments. One researched competitor advertises them at AED 3,750. Buying one is an academic honesty breach that can cost a student the entire Diploma, and the risk sits with the student, not with the seller. IB Gram does not write, complete, edit to completion or supply coursework of any kind, and no tutor working through us is permitted to.

What a tutor does instead is teach the assessment. That means explaining what each criterion asks for in the IB's own words, asking the questions that expose a research question too broad to measure, reviewing the student's own draft and saying where it sits against the criteria and why, and teaching the skills the draft reveals are missing. The student writes every word. The tutor's fingerprints are on the student's understanding, not on the document.

The boundary is easier to hold than parents expect, because it maps onto an ordinary teaching relationship. A good school supervisor does the same thing: reads, questions, returns. If anyone offers to do more than that, the offer is not a service, it is a liability with an invoice attached. We also do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; those are the boards' copyright and we link to the official source instead.

Parents sometimes ask where the line falls on proofreading. A tutor may point out that a paragraph does not address the criterion it was written for, and may teach the student how to recognise that themselves. A tutor may not sit with the document and fix the sentences. The test is simple: after the session, could the student explain and defend every change made to their own work? If not, the line has been crossed, and the school's academic honesty policy is the document that will decide what happens next.

sections.heading: KHDA inspection bands, and what a school report actually tells you
paragraphs: Every private school an Al Quoz child attends is regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band. Parents read the band, and often read more into it than it supports.

A band is a whole-school judgement across many measures. It does not tell you whether the Higher Level Chemistry teaching in Year 13 is strong this year, which is the only question that matters if your child is sitting Higher Level Chemistry. A school can sit at a high band and still have a subject-level gap, usually caused by nothing more sinister than a mid-year staff change. Conversely a school in a middle band may teach your child's particular subject very well.

Use the band as context and the subject report as evidence. The useful signals are component-level: which paper the marks are falling on, whether the internal assessment draft is scoring well against the criteria, and whether the gap is content or technique. Dubai's private sector is large enough that the numbers are worth knowing as background: 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, 17 curricula, with 7 per cent of students on an IB programme and KHDA confirming in May 2026 that there would be no fee increase for the 2026-27 academic year.

The supply side is also moving, which matters if you are weighing a school change against tutoring. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four British curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. A new school in a middle band in its first inspection cycle is a different proposition from an established school in the same band, and the inspection report itself will usually say so.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market has a section on this, which is odd, because it affects every Dubai private school pupil. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisation rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; non-Arabs are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold appropriate KHDA approval.

For families, two practical consequences follow. First, these subjects sit on top of a full IB load, so timetable pressure in MYP and DP1 is real and a child struggling in Arabic is often simply out of hours. Second, the content is tightly controlled: KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, so any support in these subjects works within the school's own material rather than around it.

The federal position behind all of this is straightforward. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. KHDA then sets the detail for Dubai, including instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools free to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met and a recommended minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what IB and IGCSE students need for UAE universities
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that converts a foreign school certificate into something a UAE university or employer will accept, and it is absent from most competitor pages. It is a process the family completes through the official channel. IB Gram does not perform it, cannot expedite it, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

The British-track rules are published and specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must show either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That five-subject count is worth noting: one competitor page ranking in this market tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong.

The American track runs on test scores instead. English proficiency is satisfied by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold published in the source we read, so no figure appears on this page. Check the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before you plan around it.

sections.heading: Getting started from Al Quoz, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the subject, the level, the school and what the last two assessments looked like. We read that and match a specialist in the component where marks are going. The trial lesson is free and happens before anything is paid for, and its purpose is diagnostic as much as commercial: a good tutor can usually name the actual problem inside forty minutes.

Then the honest part, which the rest of this market tends to skip. Sometimes no specialist is available for a very narrow request at the exact hour a family wants, especially in the weeks before the May session when every DP2 student in Dubai wants the same 6pm slot. When that happens we say so, offer the nearest workable alternative, and tell you when the slot you wanted is likely to open. We do not fill the gap with a generalist and hope.

Two more things that are true and are worth stating. Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; it is granted free of charge for two years, and those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so we quote no figure. And we hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because an independent tutoring platform does not, and any page telling you otherwise is telling you something it cannot show you.
