faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who comes to our villa in Al Quoz?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one IB tuition to Al Quoz homes as live online lessons, and we do not send tutors to any UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. Other providers in Dubai do offer home visits, and market rates for them run roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour according to Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, with travel built into the price. What you gain by going online is the ability to choose a tutor by subject and level rather than by who can reach Al Quoz at 5pm. What you give up is a person in the room.

faqs.question: Does living in Al Quoz rather than Business Bay change what tutoring my child can get?
faqs.answer: It changes the drive and the realistic session start time, and nothing else. Business Bay children are bussed out of the district and arrive home later, so 6pm is often the earliest workable slot, while Al Quoz families usually manage 5pm to 5.30pm depending on which direction the school run goes. The teacher your child needs is defined by the subject and the component where marks are being lost, not by the district. Once lessons are online, both families are selecting from the same pool of specialists.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Quoz children usually attend?
faqs.answer: The district itself is largely industrial, with housing in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3, so children travel short distances in several directions. The nearby cluster includes Safa Community School, GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail, GEMS Our Own Indian School in Al Quoz, Delhi Private School Dubai, Kings' School Al Barsha, Repton School Al Barsha, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha and Nord Anglia International School Dubai. All are regulated by KHDA. We name them as market context only; IB Gram has no relationship with any of them and none is a client.

faqs.question: What does an online IB tutor cost per hour in Dubai at the moment?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor online run roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour, and for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist roughly AED 200 to 450 or more. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase shows AED 270; BartyED quotes AED 650 at the premium end. Budget tutors start lower, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. These are other providers' published figures as at October 2026, not our price list. Ours is discussed on the consultation call after the free trial.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Diploma student in Al Quoz start with?
faqs.answer: One a week for a single subject is the usual starting point, moving to two in the weeks before a mock or the May session. More than two a week in a subject rarely helps during term, because the student needs time between sessions to practise independently, and that practice is where the learning consolidates. If two subjects are in trouble at once, one weekly session each works better than two in whichever subject feels most urgent this week. The plan is reviewed after the next school assessment.

faqs.question: Is my child's Al Quoz school report enough to diagnose the problem?
faqs.answer: It is a start, but it rarely goes deep enough. A report tells you the grade and often a general comment; it seldom tells you that the marks are going on justification in Paper 1 rather than on content. What helps far more is the last two marked scripts, because a specialist reading them can usually name the failing pattern inside one session. That is also what the free trial lesson is for: diagnosis before anyone commits to a block of paid teaching.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child write the Chemistry internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the criteria, question whether the research question can actually be measured in a school laboratory, and give feedback on the student's own draft against each criterion. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of it, and no tutor working through IB Gram is permitted to. Some operators in this market sell completed internal assessments; one advertises them at AED 3,750. Buying one is an academic honesty breach that puts the whole Diploma at risk, and the risk falls on the student.

faqs.question: When do UAE IB students actually sit their examinations?
faqs.answer: UAE IB schools sit the May session. Your child's school will have its own internal calendar of coursework deadlines, mock weeks and upload dates sitting well before that, set by the school rather than by the IB, which is why two students at different Dubai schools can be under very different pressure in the same week. IB session and results dates are not independently verified in this project, because ibo.org blocks automated access, so confirm specifics with your child's IB coordinator rather than taking a date from any tutoring website.

faqs.question: Is the tutor teaching my Al Quoz child legally permitted to do it?
faqs.answer: They need to be, and the requirement is specific. Individuals offering private lessons need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Apply or verify through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing.

faqs.question: A provider says KHDA has approved it. Should that reassure me?
faqs.answer: No, and the claim itself should make you more careful rather than less. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes that hold premises in Dubai, with initial approval, a maximum six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no permit, approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We explain what those bodies do; we do not imply any of them endorses us.

faqs.question: What do the KHDA inspection bands actually mean for choosing a tutor?
faqs.answer: KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak. It is a whole-school judgement, so it does not tell you whether Higher Level Chemistry in Year 13 is being taught well this year, which is the only question that matters if your child sits Higher Level Chemistry. Use the band as background and the subject-level evidence as the decision: which paper the marks are falling on, how the internal assessment draft scores against the criteria, and whether the gap is content or technique.

faqs.question: How does my child manage Arabic and Islamic Education on top of a full IB load?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, so they sit on top of six IB subjects plus the core. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Content is tightly controlled: KHDA states that different or additional material needs prior Ministry of Education permission, so support works within the school's own material.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or when we travel out of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. Ramadan timetables change the shape of the day, and sessions commonly shift to post-Iftar slots for the month; that is agreed with the tutor rather than imposed. Travel is simpler still, because nothing is tied to a Dubai address: if the family is in Europe for three weeks the session moves to a time that works in both zones. Many Al Quoz families use the summer and the long winter break for the steady work that term-time schedules do not allow.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks before an assessment. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to change one component, which is usually what needs changing. Six focused sessions spread across eight weeks, with the student's own timed practice in between, will shift a specific failing pattern such as justification in Paper 1 or uncertainty treatment in Physics. The same six sessions compressed into a fortnight mostly produce fatigue. What eight weeks will not do is rebuild two years of missing content, so the honest plan targets the component with the most marks attached to it.

faqs.question: What do you do when nobody covers my child's exact subject and level?
faqs.answer: We say so, which is not what most of this market does. Narrow requests at popular hours are genuinely constrained in the weeks before the May session, when a large share of Dubai's DP2 students want the same early-evening slot. In that situation you get the nearest workable alternative, an estimate of when the slot you wanted is likely to open, and the choice to wait. What you will not get is a generalist quietly substituted for the specialist you asked for.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-quoz.closingHeading: Start with the component, not the postcode
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-quoz.closingBody: If you have read this far comparing Al Quoz with Business Bay or Meydan, the useful conclusion is that the comparison does not decide anything. What decides your child's grade is whether the person teaching them understands the component where marks are being lost. Send us the subject, the level, the school and the last two marked scripts, and take the free trial lesson; it is diagnostic before it is anything else. You will finish it knowing what the actual problem is and roughly how many sessions it should take, and you can decide from there. Lessons run live online into your Al Quoz home, on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Price is the question, so price comes first
paragraphs: Three of the six highest-ranking pages for IB tutoring in Dubai publish no price at all. One of them runs an FAQ that asks what a tutor costs and then declines to say. Two quote in US dollars, a currency no family in Al Quoz 4 pays a tutor in. So before anything else: a qualified subject tutor working online in this market is quoted between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour, an in-home visit including the tutor's travel runs AED 180 to AED 500, and a named specialist at the top of the market has published AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, read in October 2026, and each is attributed in the table below.

What that spread means in practice is that the hour itself is not the expensive part. The expensive parts are travel, mismatch and timing. A tutor who drives from Al Barsha to Al Quoz 4 at five in the afternoon is paid for the Al Khail Road slip road as surely as for the teaching, and the premium sits inside the hourly rate where you cannot see it. A generalist booked for "science" when the student needs Chemistry HL is a term of sessions that never touches the grade. A package bought six weeks before a paper is peak-season pricing with the least possible time to use it.

Al Quoz 4 makes the travel arithmetic sharper than most Dubai neighbourhoods. It is a residential pocket wedged between the Al Quoz industrial strip, Al Khail Road and the Umm Al Sheif boundary, so a tutor coming in from Mirdif or Silicon Oasis crosses the city at exactly the wrong hour. Families here are typically dividing their attention between Safa Community School, the Al Barsha IB and British schools, and the Hartland and Nad Al Sheba cluster a short drive east. The tutor pool that can physically reach the villa by 4:30pm is small; the pool that can teach Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is small for a different reason. Those two small pools barely overlap.

IB Gram resolves that by not asking them to. Lessons are delivered as live one-to-one video, screen shared, recorded on request, scheduled against Gulf Standard Time and against the student's own school deadlines. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is stated plainly because the alternative is to let a parent assume otherwise, and because the online format is what makes the specialist match possible at all.

The rest of this page is built to be used rather than admired. There are three tables: the market's AED bands by tier with sources, the same decision expressed as a monthly figure, and a leak audit showing where a tutoring budget disappears without buying anything. After that come the parts of the cost picture nobody puts on a pricing page: the MoHRE permit position, the KHDA fee context your tutoring sits inside, what a tutor is allowed to do with an Internal Assessment, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that decides whether the qualification counts at a UAE university.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-quoz-4.programmesIntro: An IB education in Dubai is four distinct programmes with four different cost profiles. Primary Years support is light and diagnostic. Middle Years is criterion-based and cheap to fix early. The Diploma is where hours concentrate, because the Internal Assessments and the final papers arrive together. The Career-related Programme is rarer in Dubai and needs a tutor who has read its reflective project requirements.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units rather than subject syllabuses, assessed continuously by the class teacher against learning outcomes the school sets. There is no external examination, so there is no paper technique to drill. Support at this stage is about number fluency, reading stamina and the habit of explaining reasoning out loud, which is the single transferable skill the Middle Years Programme will later mark you on.
programmes.countryNote: Al Quoz 4 and the surrounding Al Barsha and Umm Al Sheif streets feed several PYP primaries, and the common pattern here is a family moving in mid-year from a British or Indian curriculum. The spend that actually pays off is six to eight diagnostic sessions to find the gap, not a standing weekly booking. At market rates that is a one-off AED 900 to AED 2,400 rather than an open-ended commitment.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, each criterion scored out of 8 and converted to a 1-7 grade by the school's own boundaries. A student can be strong at content and still sit at a 4 because Criterion D, which rewards reflection and evaluation, has never been taught as a skill. That is diagnosable in one session and fixable in a term.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP cohorts in this corridor often split at Year 11, with some students sitting IGCSE alongside MYP and others going straight to MYP eAssessment. The cost consequence matters: a student doing both is carrying two assessment systems at once, and families in Al Quoz 4 regularly underestimate it by a full term of support. Ask the school which route the child is on before you buy any hours.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly 20 to 25 per cent of its grade, and all of them fall due inside the same few months of DP2. The final papers then test command terms as much as content: a student who knows the material but writes to "describe" when the paper says "evaluate" loses marks that no amount of extra content covers.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Al Quoz 4 budgets concentrate, and where the leak table below bites hardest. A DP2 family buying two subjects at two hours a week from January is looking at AED 1,200 to AED 2,400 a month at the qualified-tutor band. The cheaper path is to start in DP1 while the content is being taught, when one hour a week on each weak subject does the same work for roughly half the total outlay.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills core. It is offered by a handful of UAE schools rather than most, and it needs a tutor who understands that the reflective project is assessed on process evidence, not on a polished final document.
programmes.countryNote: Few schools in the Al Quoz and Al Barsha catchment run the Career-related Programme, so local tutor supply is close to nil and the in-home option effectively does not exist at any price. This is the clearest case on the page for online matching: the constraint is not distance, it is that the number of people in the emirate who have taught the reflective project is very small.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-quoz-4.subjectsIntro: Rates track specialism, not subject glamour. A tutor who can teach Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and mark against the paper's own command terms sits at the top of the qualified band; a tutor who can supervise homework in any subject sits at the bottom. The descriptions below name what each course assesses so you can tell which one you are buying.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus, proof and algebraic manipulation, sat without a calculator in Paper 1. The Higher Level course adds complex numbers, vectors and deeper integration techniques. Marks are lost most often on unjustified steps: the answer is right, the method is not shown, and the mark scheme awards the method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and financial mathematics, calculator-permitted throughout. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding regression work. The common failure is treating it as the easy route; the Higher Level paper is genuinely hard and some university programmes will not accept it for engineering.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, waves, electricity, magnetism and nuclear physics, with Higher Level extending into rigid-body rotation and quantum phenomena. Paper 3 tests experimental and data-analysis skill rather than recall, which is why students who revise content alone plateau at the same grade.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, redox and organic chemistry. Organic and energetics account for a disproportionate share of lost marks, usually because mechanisms are memorised as pictures instead of as electron movement.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cell biology, molecular biology, genetics, ecology, evolution and human physiology, with Higher Level adding plant biology and animal physiology. Grades turn on command-term discipline more than on memory: "outline" and "explain" carry different mark allocations and students answer both the same way.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and the three-commentary Internal Assessment built from published news articles. Higher Level adds quantitative questions and a policy paper. Diagram accuracy is where marks go: an unlabelled axis costs the same as not knowing the theory.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business organisation, human resource management, finance and accounts, marketing and operations. The Internal Assessment differs by level, and Higher Level students must build theirs on primary research, which takes planning time most families do not budget for.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis across literary and non-literary forms, assessed by two written papers, an Individual Oral and, at Higher Level, an essay. The Individual Oral is the most coachable component on the Diploma and the one most students walk into unprepared.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language-acquisition course for students who are strong but not first-language in English, assessed on reading, listening, writing and an individual oral based on a visual stimulus. The listening paper is the component Dubai students most often underestimate because practice material is harder to find.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Al Quoz 4 actually costs
paragraphs: A qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai is quoted at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. An in-home one-to-one visit, with the tutor's travel priced into the hour, is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500. A named specialist at the top of the market has published AED 650. Those are the three numbers a family in Al Quoz 4 needs before any other conversation, and the table below shows who publishes each of them.

The bands come from providers' own public pages and from a Dubai rate survey, all read in October 2026. They are the market, not IB Gram's price list. The reason to publish them anyway is that a parent cannot judge a quote without a reference range, and the pages currently ranking for this search either refuse to give one or quote in dollars. If a provider asks AED 420 an hour for Maths SL, you should be able to see immediately that it sits above the specialist band and ask what justifies it.

Read the right-hand column as carefully as the rate column. The gap between AED 60 an hour and AED 250 an hour is not a gap in politeness or punctuality. It is the difference between someone who can supervise homework and someone who can look at a Paper 1 script and say which mark the student lost, why the mark scheme withheld it, and what to practise this week so it is not lost again. For an IB Diploma student in DP2, that distinction is the whole purchase.

One more line on the in-home band. The AED 180 to AED 500 figures are what the Dubai market charges for a tutor to travel to a residence, and quoting them is the argument for buying the hour differently. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at any price, and the comparison in the next sections is built on that.

sections.heading: The same decision, read as a monthly number
paragraphs: Hourly rates hide the commitment. Families do not experience AED 220 an hour; they experience a figure that arrives every month next to the school fee and the nursery invoice. Converting the bands into monthly totals changes which option looks sensible, and it is the conversion almost no tutoring page performs.

At the qualified-tutor band, one online hour a week lands between AED 600 and AED 1,200 a month. Two hours a week doubles it. One in-home hour a week, at the travel-inclusive band, runs AED 720 to AED 2,000 a month for a quarter of the contact time of the two-hour online plan at its lower end. Advertised monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is a useful sanity check on any bespoke quote.

The planning consequence for an Al Quoz 4 family is straightforward. If the budget is fixed, and for most families it is, the choice is between fewer in-home hours and more online hours. Two online hours a week with a subject specialist does more for a DP Physics grade than one in-home hour with a generalist, and at the mid-band it costs roughly the same. That is the trade the table makes visible.

A note on exam years. A Diploma student sitting the May session with two weak Higher Level subjects needs more contact time from January, and the specialist band at weekly frequency reaches AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 a month on published Dubai estimates. Budgeting for that in DP1, when the hours are cheaper and the content is still being taught, is the single largest saving available on this page.

sections.heading: Where a tutoring budget leaks in Al Quoz 4
paragraphs: Most families who feel they overpaid for tutoring did not pay an unreasonable rate. They paid a reasonable rate for hours that could not have worked. Five leaks account for the majority of it, and four of the five are decided before the first lesson happens.

The first is travel. Al Quoz 4 sits behind the industrial strip with access off Al Khail Road, which is a comfortable approach from Al Barsha and an unpleasant one from the eastern suburbs between four and seven in the evening. Any in-home rate quoted to an address here has that journey priced into it, and the portion of the yearly bill that buys movement rather than teaching is substantial. The second is mismatch: a booking that names "maths" rather than Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is a booking nobody can plan.

The third is session length. Two-hour blocks look efficient on an invoice and rarely are for a fourteen-year-old, because the second hour is low-attention time charged at full rate. Two separate sixty-minute sessions on different days cost the same and retain more. The fourth is timing: starting six weeks before a paper means paying peak-season rates with the least remaining time to use them. The fifth is the absence of any written record, which makes it impossible to tell whether week nine repeated week three.

None of these leaks is fixed by finding a cheaper tutor. They are fixed by naming the subject and level before you book, buying sixty-minute slots, starting in the term the content is taught, and asking for one paragraph of notes after each lesson. The table puts rough annual figures against each so the fix can be weighed against the cost.

sections.heading: Why the online hour is cheaper here, honestly stated
paragraphs: The cost argument for online delivery is not that video is a cheaper medium. It is that the two things driving the in-home premium, travel and scarcity, both disappear when the tutor does not have to be within driving distance of Al Quoz 4 at half past four on a Tuesday.

Travel is the visible half. A tutor crossing from Mirdif or Silicon Oasis to Al Quoz 4 in the evening peak spends an hour of working time getting there and another getting home, and that time is paid for inside the hourly rate. No provider itemises it, which is precisely why the in-home band sits AED 30 to AED 200 above the online band for the same teaching.

Scarcity is the half that costs more and is harder to see. The number of people in Dubai who can teach Chemistry at Higher Level to a Diploma standard is not large. The number who can do that and who live close enough to reach this part of Al Quoz by early evening is smaller again. When a family insists on proximity, they are not buying convenience at a premium; they are selecting from a much smaller pool and often accepting a generalist as the price. The honest version of the trade-off is in the table.

What a family gives up by going online is real and should be named: a physical presence in the room, a tutor who can see the student's body language without a camera, and for younger children the structure that someone arriving at the door provides. For a Diploma student working on past papers and an Internal Assessment, screen sharing and a shared document are closer to how the work is actually done than a kitchen table is.

sections.heading: What the fee does not buy: the permit a tutor must hold
paragraphs: A rate tells you nothing about whether the person charging it is permitted to teach privately in the UAE, and that is a question an Al Quoz 4 parent can settle in one message before any money changes hands.

Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the official service listing is "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing" on mohre.gov.ae, with a two-working-day completion time and applications through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

Two consequences follow for a budget. The first is that nobody can justify a higher rate on the grounds of permit costs, because the permit costs nothing. The second is that a tutor who cannot tell you their permit status is a risk you are paying for: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody.

There is a related boundary worth knowing in Abu Dhabi, and worth knowing in Dubai because families move. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than read from the policy document, so treat it as a question to ask rather than a settled fact. Either way, "your child's own teacher, privately" is not a product any responsible provider should offer.

sections.heading: The fee context your tutoring budget sits inside
paragraphs: Tutoring is a second education bill arriving next to the first, and the first one is large. Reading them together changes how much a family is willing to spend on the second, which is why this section exists on a page about cost.

Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula. By enrolment, UK curriculum accounted for 37 per cent, Indian 26 per cent, US 14 per cent and International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. That last figure is the one Al Quoz 4 IB families should sit with: the IB cohort in Dubai is a minority of a very large market, which is exactly why specialist IB tutors are thin on the ground in any one neighbourhood.

On fees, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family planning tutoring spend, a flat school fee for the year is a genuine planning input: the tutoring budget is not competing with a fee rise this cycle.

Supply is moving too. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. Three new IB schools in one intake means more Diploma students, more Internal Assessments falling due in the same weeks, and more competition for the same small pool of local specialist tutors. If you are planning a Diploma two years out, book the specialist early rather than cheap.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment
paragraphs: This is a cost section disguised as an ethics section, because the most expensive thing a family can buy in this market is work that gets the student's Diploma withdrawn. One provider found in this search results page sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger, and it is worth understanding the boundary precisely so you can recognise when it is being crossed.

Every IB Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Middle Years Personal Project must be the student's own work, submitted with the student's and supervisor's authentication. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain how the published criteria are applied, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short of a criterion, and ask the questions that make a student notice their own gap. A tutor may not produce any part of the submission, rewrite passages into final form, supply the data, or select the research question on the student's behalf.

The practical test is whether a stranger reading the finished piece would be reading the student's thinking. If the tutor's sentences are in it, the line has been crossed, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the person who was paid. Feedback keyed to criterion letters is both the legitimate service and the more useful one: a Maths Internal Assessment marked against each criterion in turn tells a student exactly which two marks are reachable this week.

There is a separate boundary around materials. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright. A tutor should reference them and point you to the official source, not hand over a folder of redistributed PDFs. A provider who supplies unreleased material is a problem you do not want attached to your child's candidature.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the five-subject rule nobody budgets for
paragraphs: A qualification only pays off if it converts. For a UAE university place, that conversion runs through Ministry of Education equivalency, and the British-track rules are published and specific enough to plan a subject choice around.

On the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently ranking for Dubai tutoring queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic education.

On the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB route specifically, no points threshold should be quoted to you that has not been read on moe.gov.ae or confirmed by the emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram does not publish one, and you should treat any tutoring provider that does with scepticism until they cite the source.

Why this belongs on a cost page: a family that discovers in DP2 that a subject combination will not satisfy equivalency is buying emergency tutoring at peak rates to fix a problem that cost nothing to avoid in Year 10. Equivalency is also a process the family completes with the authority, not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or shortcuts, and no amount of tutoring is a requirement for it.

faqs.question: What should I expect to pay an IB home tutor in Al Quoz 4?
faqs.answer: Dubai market rates, read in October 2026, put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and an in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180 to AED 500, with travel priced inside the hour. A named specialist at the top of the market has published AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, attributed on this page. IB Gram delivers one-to-one teaching live over video rather than at a UAE address, so the travel component is not part of what you pay for. Ask any provider to confirm the rate, the session length and whether the level is specified before you book.

faqs.question: Is the in-home premium in Al Quoz 4 worth paying for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma students it is not, because the premium buys proximity rather than specialism. The AED 30 to AED 200 an hour gap between the online and in-home bands pays for the tutor's journey across Al Khail Road in the evening peak. Spent differently, that money buys a second session each week with a tutor who teaches the exact subject and level your child is sitting. For a student working on past papers, an Internal Assessment and a shared document, screen sharing is closer to how the work actually happens than a kitchen table is.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should an Al Quoz 4 family budget for?
faqs.answer: One sixty-minute session a week per weak subject, started in the term the content is being taught, is the plan that gives the most grade movement per dirham. At the qualified band that is AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month per subject. Two sessions a week is justified in an exam year or when a student is behind on a Higher Level subject, and that doubles the figure. Two-hour blocks are usually false economy for anyone under sixteen, because the second hour is low-attention time charged at the full rate.

faqs.question: Does a cheaper tutor rate mean a worse lesson?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but the bands describe different products. At AED 45 to AED 150 an hour you are generally buying homework supervision and worked examples from a university student. At AED 150 to AED 300 you are buying someone who knows the paper structure, the component weightings and the command terms, and who can tell you which mark was lost and why. For Primary Years support the cheaper band is often sufficient. For a Diploma Higher Level subject with an Internal Assessment attached, it usually is not, and the saving gets spent twice.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with Al Quoz 4 families need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time on the official service listing. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Are Dubai tutoring rates higher close to exam season?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, and that is one of the five budget leaks set out on this page. Demand concentrates in the weeks before a paper, intensive blocks are priced above standing weekly slots, and the student has the least remaining time in which to use what the sessions produce. A family that starts in the term the content is being taught pays a lower rate, buys fewer total hours and gets more out of each one. Starting late is the most expensive scheduling decision available in this market.

faqs.question: What does the AED 799 monthly package advertised in Dubai actually include?
faqs.answer: Advertised online packages in this market at around AED 799 a month typically cover eight sessions, which works out near the lower end of the qualified-tutor hourly band. In-home monthly packages are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Before signing either, confirm three things in writing: the session length in minutes, whether the named tutor teaches your child's specific subject and level, and what happens to unused sessions. Package pricing is a useful sanity check on a bespoke quote rather than automatically better value.

faqs.question: How does a free trial lesson work if there is no card taken?
faqs.answer: One free trial lesson is offered per family, held live over video, with no card details collected beforehand and no obligation afterwards. The condition is simply that it is one lesson per family rather than one per subject. Use it as a diagnostic rather than a sales call: hand the tutor a question your child recently lost marks on and ask them to explain exactly which mark the scheme withheld and why. A tutor who can do that in twenty minutes is worth the qualified band; one who cannot is not.

faqs.question: Will school fees in Dubai rise on top of what we spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For planning purposes that means a tutoring budget set this cycle is not competing with a fee rise. It is a one-year position announced by the regulator rather than a permanent rule, so check the current KHDA announcement before committing to a long tutoring plan.

faqs.answer: The scarce ones rather than the hard ones. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Physics at Higher Level, Chemistry at Higher Level and the less common language B courses have the thinnest local supply, so the in-home rate quoted for them sits near the top of the band if a tutor can be found at all. Economics and Business Management are easier to staff locally. Online matching flattens this, because availability stops being a function of who lives within driving distance of Al Quoz 4.

A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain how each published criterion is applied, read a draft the student has written and identify where it falls short, and ask the questions that make a student notice their own gap. A tutor may not produce any part of the submission, rewrite passages into final form, supply the data or choose the research question. faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One page currently ranking for Dubai tutoring searches states that six subjects are required, which is wrong. For the IB Diploma, the sourced material available does not include a points threshold, so IB Gram publishes none. faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is available for the subject an Al Quoz 4 family needs?

When that happens the honest options are a wait for the right match, a different session pattern, or a referral elsewhere. Each one works to a named syllabus and a named assessment component rather than to a general idea of helping with homework, and each teaches on screen rather than travelling.

intro.heading: The real question behind "IB home tutor in Al Qusais"
paragraphs: Al Qusais sits along the Dubai-Sharjah corridor, between Al Twar and Al Nahda, with the Red Line running through it at Stadium, Al Qusais and Dubai Airport Free Zone. Families here are close to a dense cluster of schools and a short drive from Al Garhoud and Oud Metha. What they are not close to is a deep bench of IB Diploma subject specialists. An IB home tutor in Al Qusais, interpreted literally, means somebody who can drive to your building and who also happens to teach your child's exact subject at your child's exact level. Those two conditions rarely meet in the same person.

Consider what the Diploma actually demands. A DP2 student might need Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Chemistry HL, English A Language and Literature SL, Economics SL, Arabic B SL and Visual Arts SL. Six subjects, each with its own internal assessment, its own command terms and its own paper structure. A general maths tutor who covers Years 7 to 11 is not the same person as someone who has marked Paper 3 responses on a Higher Level option. The gap between those two is usually two grades.

So the honest answer is this. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai; home visits are something we run only in India. For UAE families, every lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school day. That is not a compromise forced on us by logistics. It is what lets an Al Qusais family work with a Chemistry HL specialist who understands the 2023 syllabus structure, rather than with whoever is willing to sit in Ittihad Road traffic for an hour each way.

This page does four things. It sets out what the Dubai market charges for IB support and names the sources for every figure. It compares an in-home hour against an online hour on cost, travel, tutor pool and rescheduling. It explains how to check whether a tutor advertising privately holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. And it states plainly what a tutor may and may not do with an internal assessment, because that boundary is where several providers in this market quietly cross a line.

Dubai's private-school sector carried 387,441 pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment and the UK curriculum 37%, according to the Dubai Media Office. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees would not rise for 2026-27. Both facts matter to a tutoring decision: the IB cohort is a minority of a very large market, which is exactly why subject-level specialists are thin on the ground in any one neighbourhood, and a frozen fee bill means the tutoring line in a family budget is the one that can still move.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-qusais.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the three school-age IB programmes that Dubai schools near Al Qusais run. The teaching problem is different in each, and so is the kind of tutor who helps.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations and no syllabus to drill. Learning is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry, with the exhibition in the final year acting as the first piece of sustained independent work a child produces. Tutoring at this stage is about number fluency, reading stamina and the habit of asking a question that can actually be investigated.
programmes.countryNote: Al Qusais and Al Twar families often move a child into a PYP school from a CBSE or Ministry-curriculum primary, where the shift from textbook exercises to inquiry units unsettles strong pupils as much as weak ones. A term of structured reading and arithmetic work usually settles it faster than a year of waiting.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP runs five years across eight subject groups and is assessed against criteria A to D rather than a mark scheme. Grades land on a 1 to 8 scale. The Personal Project in MYP 5 is assessed on its process as much as its product, and MYP 5 students at some Dubai schools sit eAssessment for an externally validated certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Al Qusais run MYP to Year 9 and then switch to IGCSE, which means a child can meet criterion-referenced assessment and then a linear examined course within eighteen months. Knowing which route your school takes changes what a tutor should be drilling in Year 9.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Each subject carries an internal assessment worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade, marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The core adds up to three bonus points on a 45-point total.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai IB schools sit the May session, which puts internal assessment deadlines through the autumn and winter of DP2 and makes October to February the pressure window for an Al Qusais family. Starting support in March of DP2 leaves almost no coursework left to influence.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-qusais.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Dubai families ask for most often. Each entry says what the assessment actually tests and where marks tend to go, because that is what a tutor should be working on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries the whole course. At Higher Level, Paper 3 is an extended problem-solving investigation where students lose marks for abandoning an unfamiliar context rather than for weak technique. Proof by induction, complex numbers and the Maclaurin series are the usual pressure points.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-heavy and modelling-led. Marks go missing in interpretation rather than computation: a correct regression with no statement of what the gradient means in context earns part credit. Graph theory and the chi-squared test are the topics most often under-taught in school.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The 2023 syllabus groups content into themes A to E across both levels, with additional Higher Level material inside each theme. Students lose marks on vector reasoning in fields and on uncertainty propagation in the internal assessment. Paper 2 extended response needs structured reasoning, not a formula.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Split into Structure and Reactivity, with the HL extensions sitting inside each. Organic mechanisms and energetics are where Higher Level grades separate. The internal assessment is marked on research design and analysis, so a well-run experiment with no uncertainty treatment still caps out in the middle bands.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Organised around unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and continuity. The content volume is the trap: students revise descriptive recall and then meet data-analysis questions in Paper 2. Command terms matter here more than anywhere else in the group 4 subjects.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two papers, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay on a studied text. Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, which rewards a method rather than knowledge. Most lost marks come from summarising a text instead of analysing how it produces its effect.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal assessment commentaries drawn from published news articles, each capped at 800 words, plus papers that reward diagram accuracy and explicit evaluation. Higher Level adds quantitative questions. Students routinely lose evaluation marks by describing a policy rather than weighing it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as Ansoff, SWOT and break-even analysis are easy to name and hard to apply to a case. Paper 1 uses a pre-released case study. The internal assessment differs by level, and Higher Level students need primary research handled properly rather than a questionnaire bolted on late.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Assessed across five prescribed themes with a written paper, listening and reading comprehension and an individual oral. Non-native speakers at Dubai schools often carry strong spoken Arabic and weak formal register, which the written paper punishes immediately.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-qusais.regionsIntro: Students taught through IB Gram live across the Dubai-Sharjah corridor and the older districts around it. The notes below are about what each area does to a tutoring timetable, which is the only thing a tutor can actually plan around.

regions.name: Al Qusais

sections.heading: What this search returns today, and what it should return
paragraphs: Type "IB home tutor in Al Qusais" into Google and you get three kinds of result. There are agency pages that list every district in Dubai and name no school in any of them. There are classified listings from individuals, most of whom teach a broad age range and none of whom state a syllabus code. And there are blog posts about the IB in general that mention Al Qusais once, in a list. None of these answers the question a parent actually has.

The question is narrower than the search box suggests. A parent typing it has usually already had a conversation at a parents' evening. A teacher has said the word "predicted" about a subject, and the parent has gone looking for someone who can teach that specific thing. What they need to know is whether the person they are about to pay has taught the Higher Level option their child sits, has seen that internal assessment marked, and knows which Paper the lost marks are coming from.

Geography does not help with any of that. It helps with one thing only, which is travel. If a provider can send someone to a building in Al Qusais, that provider has restricted itself to people who live close enough to make the journey worthwhile at the rate quoted. In a district where the IB cohort is a minority of a minority, that filter removes almost everybody who is genuinely specialised.

The honest reframing is to drop the radius and keep the specialism. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, and says so before a parent asks. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen because of what they teach rather than where they sleep. The rest of this page is the evidence for why that trade is worth making, including the costs on both sides.

sections.heading: Does anybody near Al Qusais teach your child's exact subject at the right level?
paragraphs: Work the arithmetic through from the school roll rather than from a marketing claim. Dubai had 227 private schools in 2024-25 and the IB accounted for 7% of pupils. The Diploma sits in the final two years of that, so the DP cohort in any one district is small. Split it by subject and level and the numbers get smaller again: a school with sixty DP students might have twelve taking Chemistry HL and four taking Physics HL.

Now ask who teaches those four. In practice it is one teacher, possibly two, both employed full time at the school and both barred by the MoHRE permit code of conduct from tutoring their own enrolled students. Abu Dhabi's regulator ADEK sets out the same prohibition in its professional-ethics rules for school staff. So the pool of people near Al Qusais who know Physics HL inside out and can legally tutor your child is not the pool of people who teach it locally.

That leaves independent tutors, and the question becomes how to tell a specialist from a generalist. The test is specific and takes two minutes. Ask which assessment components the subject has and what each is worth. Ask what the internal assessment is marked against. Ask which topic the student most recently lost marks on and what the command term in that question was. A specialist answers without hedging. A generalist talks about confidence and rapport.

Online delivery changes the arithmetic because it removes distance from the equation entirely. The constraint stops being who lives within twenty minutes of Damascus Street and becomes who is free at 17:30 Gulf Standard Time. That is a far larger set of people, and it is the only way an Al Qusais family reliably gets a tutor who has taught the exact Higher Level option their child sits.

sections.heading: What IB support costs around Al Qusais, and who published each figure
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest thing on the market and work upwards, because that is the order a budget actually gets built in. University-student and entry-level online tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 65 on EdFlik and from roughly AED 33 to 52 on Tutopiya. Those rates buy homework supervision and a second explanation of what the teacher already said. For MYP consolidation that can be enough. For a Diploma internal assessment it is not, and a family that pays it for DP work usually ends up paying twice.

The next band up is where most Diploma tutoring actually happens. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutoring at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED advertises AED 650 at the examiner-led end. Monthly packages seen in this market run from about AED 799 for eight online sessions to AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. Compare the middle of that range against the middle of the online qualified band and the gap is roughly AED 80 to 150 an hour. That gap is the travel premium. It does not buy more teaching time, better subject knowledge or a tighter match to the syllabus. It buys the tutor's journey along Ittihad Road, paid for by you.

None of these are IB Gram's prices and none should be read as such. They are what other providers in this market publish, quoted so that a parent in Al Qusais can see the shape of the market before anyone quotes them anything. For what IB Gram charges, start with the trial lesson and the consultation, where the subject, level and session length are known and a figure can be given against them rather than against an average.

sections.heading: An in-home hour against an online hour, line by line
paragraphs: A fair comparison has to hold the teaching constant and look at everything around it. Assume the same tutor, the same subject and the same sixty minutes of instruction. What changes is the cost, the travel, the size of the pool you are choosing from, and what happens when a Tuesday falls apart.

Travel is the item parents underestimate. A tutor coming into Al Qusais from Deira or Bur Dubai at 17:00 is looking at twenty-five to forty minutes each way on Ittihad Road or Damascus Street during term time. That hour and a bit is priced into the rate whether anyone names it or not, and it caps how many students that tutor can see in an evening, which pushes the rate up again. A 17:30 online session starts at 17:30.

Rescheduling is the second item. An in-home slot that gets cancelled because a child has a late football fixture is usually lost, because the tutor cannot refill a journey at short notice. An online slot moves to Thursday. Over a two-year Diploma that difference is worth several sessions, which at AED 250 an hour is real money as well as real teaching.

The third item is the one that actually decides grades: the pool. An in-home requirement narrows your choice to people who can reach your building. Online, the choice is everyone free at that hour. For Mathematics at Standard Level the difference may not matter much. For Chemistry HL option work or a Physics internal assessment with messy uncertainty data, it is the whole decision. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and the table below is the argument for why that is the right position rather than an apology for it.

sections.heading: Check the permit before you check the price
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page, "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE app, website or e-services system.

The consequence matters. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure you see quoted for this should be treated with scepticism. What a parent can do is ask directly whether the person teaching their child holds the permit, and ask when it was issued. A legitimate tutor answers in one sentence.

There is a second rule that catches families by surprise. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars a teacher from tutoring students affiliated with their own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school. So the arrangement many parents instinctively want, their child's own subject teacher privately in the evening, is the one arrangement to avoid.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again. That requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and runs no centre in the UAE, which is why you will not find a Dubai address on this page. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one.

sections.heading: Which schools Al Qusais children attend, and what that changes
paragraphs: Al Qusais itself is well served for British and Indian curriculum schooling. For the Diploma specifically, most families in the district travel. The nearest dense IB provision sits in Al Garhoud, Oud Metha, Festival City and Al Jaddaf, with further options towards Nad Al Sheba and Academic City. That journey is the single biggest determinant of when a tutoring session can start.

A child leaving a school in Al Garhoud at 15:30 and travelling back into Al Qusais by bus is rarely home before 16:20, later if the route serves Mirdif first. Add a change of clothes and something to eat and 17:00 is the earliest honest start. For a child at a school with a 14:45 finish and a short route, 16:00 works. These are not small distinctions. A session booked at the wrong hour gets cancelled twice and then quietly abandoned.

The regulator question comes up constantly in this corridor. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes inspection ratings on a six-band scale. Families living in Al Nahda on the Sharjah side but schooling in Dubai are inspected by KHDA for school purposes, while Sharjah private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate and also approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods.

Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. For an IB student, that means these subjects run alongside the Diploma, and a tutoring plan that ignores them tends to come apart in the spring.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the clearest line in IB tutoring and the one most often blurred in this market. The internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay and Personal Project must be the student's own work. A tutor does not write any of them, does not edit one to completion, and does not supply a finished piece for a student to submit. One provider found in this SERP sells completed internal assessments outright; that is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger for the student, not a shortcut.

What a tutor can do is substantial, and it is where most of the available marks sit. A tutor teaches the criteria. For a science internal assessment that means explaining what the research design criterion actually rewards, why a vague research question caps the whole piece, and how uncertainty propagation turns a mid-band analysis into a top-band one. For an Economics commentary it means working on the 800-word limit, diagram accuracy and explicit evaluation against a published article the student chose.

Feedback on a draft is legitimate and expected. The IB's model assumes a supervisor reads drafts and comments. A tutor can do the same thing in parallel, marking against the published descriptors and saying which criterion is losing marks and why. What the tutor returns is a commentary, not a rewritten paragraph. If a tutor hands back prose the student can paste in, the line has been crossed.

There is also a sequencing point. Most internal assessment marks are lost before any writing starts, in a research question that cannot be answered within the word limit or a method that generates data nobody can analyse. The most useful hour a tutor spends on an internal assessment is usually the first one, weeks before the draft deadline. Families who come to this in the final fortnight are paying for damage limitation instead of design.

sections.heading: What happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider in this market has availability gaps, and almost none of them say so. The pattern a parent in Al Qusais will recognise is being told yes to everything, then being matched with somebody who teaches a neighbouring subject and hoping it works out. A Physics HL request answered with a general science tutor is the most common version of this.

The honest version is a disclosed answer. For common Diploma subjects at both levels, matching is usually quick and the first trial lesson can often sit inside the same week. For narrow Higher Level options, for less common group 2 languages and for subjects where the student needs a specific exam board at IGCSE as well, it can take longer. In those cases we say how long, and if the right tutor is not available we say that rather than substituting someone close enough.

The second half of that disclosure is about where the tutor is. Because delivery is online, a tutor teaching an Al Qusais student may be based in the UAE or elsewhere. We say which, before the trial, because a family has a right to know who is teaching their child and from where. Several providers in this market route UAE parents to overseas numbers without mentioning it, which is a trust failure before it is anything else.

If a subject genuinely has no specialist free, there are two useful fallbacks and we name them. One is a tutor in an adjacent subject who can carry the shared skills, which works for maths-heavy sciences and not for language acquisition. The other is a shorter, narrower engagement on the component where marks are actually being lost, rather than a full weekly slot on the whole subject. Both are better than a mismatch that burns a term.

faqs.question: Is there an IB home tutor in Al Qusais who actually teaches my child's Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: Probably not within driving distance, and that is the honest answer. The Diploma cohort in any one Dubai district is small, Higher Level options split it further, and the teachers who know those options best are usually employed full time and barred by the MoHRE permit code of conduct from tutoring their own school's students. IB Gram solves it differently: your child is matched to a subject specialist who teaches that exact level and the lesson happens one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The radius disappears and the specialism stays.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram not send a tutor to our flat in Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: Because it would make the teaching worse. Requiring a tutor to travel to a UAE address restricts the choice to people who live close enough to justify the journey at the rate quoted, which in a district with a small IB cohort removes almost every genuine specialist. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. For UAE families every lesson is one-to-one over live video, which means the tutor is chosen for what they teach rather than for where they live, and no part of your fee pays for time spent on Ittihad Road.

faqs.question: How do I check that a private tutor advertising in Al Qusais holds a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and ask when it was issued. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's app, website or e-services system under the service "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing". Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published. A tutor operating properly will answer the question in a sentence; hesitation is the signal.

faqs.question: What do Dubai providers publish as their hourly rate for IB Diploma support?
faqs.answer: Working upwards: Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the entry level. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level work at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED advertises AED 650. These are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices. Ours are quoted against a known subject, level and session length after a trial.

faqs.question: Our building in Al Qusais has slow evening Wi-Fi. Does that rule out online lessons?
faqs.answer: Rarely. A one-to-one video lesson with a shared whiteboard needs far less bandwidth than streaming video, and the usual fix is turning the student's camera down rather than abandoning the session. What helps most is a wired connection or sitting closer to the router, and agreeing a fallback in advance so a dropped connection costs two minutes rather than the lesson. The trial lesson is the right place to test this, because it shows you what your actual connection does at the hour you plan to use it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both Maths AA and Physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking because the overlap is real. Vectors, calculus and uncertainty handling appear in both, and a tutor comfortable with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level often teaches Physics to a good standard. Where it breaks down is at the top of Higher Level, where Paper 3 in each subject rewards quite different habits. For a student chasing a 6 or 7 in both, two specialists usually beat one generalist. For a student stabilising a 4, one tutor across both is efficient and cheaper.

faqs.question: Is a teacher from my child's own school allowed to tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the arrangement parents most often ask for. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled there. Beyond the rule, there is a practical problem: the person who predicts a grade should not also be paid to raise it. An independent specialist who knows the same syllabus avoids both issues.

faqs.question: How much of an IB Diploma grade comes from work done during the course?
faqs.answer: Enough that leaving it late is the most expensive mistake available. Each Diploma subject carries an internal assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB, typically worth somewhere between a fifth and a quarter of the subject grade, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together contribute up to three points of the 45. For a Dubai school sitting the May session, those deadlines fall across the autumn and winter of DP2. Support that starts in March of the final year arrives after most of that has been banked.

faqs.question: Where exactly does Extended Essay support stop being legitimate?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor teaches the assessment criteria, helps narrow a research question until it can be answered in 4,000 words, questions the method, and marks a draft against the published descriptors. A tutor does not write the essay, does not rewrite paragraphs and does not supply text to paste in. The school supervisor's role and deadlines stand. What comes back from a session is a commentary on what is losing marks, which is also where most of the available marks actually are.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 at a school near Al Garhoud and has slipped in two subjects. How many sessions a week is sensible?
faqs.answer: Two subjects at sixty minutes each, on different evenings, is the usual starting point in DP1. That is enough to stay ahead of the class in both without eating the evening a student needs for their own work. Taking three or four subjects at once early in DP1 tends to produce attendance problems by half term. The sequencing matters too: start with the subject where the internal assessment deadline falls first, because that mark is fixed earliest and is the hardest to recover later.

faqs.question: Which IB exam session do Dubai schools sit, and when should revision actually begin?
faqs.answer: Dubai IB schools sit the May session. Specific IB exam and results dates are set by the IB and should be confirmed with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taken from any tutoring site, including this one. What is safe to plan around is the shape of the year: internal assessments and the Extended Essay fall through the autumn and winter of DP2, mocks usually land in the new year, and serious past-paper work needs to be running by then rather than starting after it.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still apply to an IB student at a Dubai private school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes. These subjects run alongside the Diploma, so a tutoring plan built only around six IB subjects has left something out of the week.

faqs.question: What happens if no IB specialist is free for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: We say so, and give a realistic wait rather than a yes. Common Diploma subjects at both levels usually match quickly, often with a trial inside the same week. Narrow Higher Level options and less common languages can take longer. Where the right tutor is not available, the two honest alternatives are a shorter engagement on the specific component losing marks, or a tutor in an adjacent subject who can carry the shared skills. A near-enough substitute on a full weekly slot costs a term and then has to be unwound.

faqs.question: Does my child need tutoring to get UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a documentary process run by the Ministry of Education, not something tutoring delivers or that IB Gram performs. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. No IB points threshold should be quoted without reading it on moe.gov.ae, so verify your own case through the official channel.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to Al Rashidiya enquiries are priced by what they specialise in rather than by how far they would drive, and the figure is agreed after the free trial rather than before it.

intro.heading: A price range of twenty to one, and what explains it
paragraphs: The published rates for IB tutoring in Dubai run from AED 33 an hour to AED 650 an hour. That is a twenty-fold spread for something described by every provider in roughly the same words, and no page in this market explains it. So before any discussion of what to buy, here is what each tier of that range actually contains, starting at the cheapest, because that is where most families in Al Rashidiya begin looking.

At the bottom, roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour as published by two providers, you are buying a university student or recent graduate who knows the subject. That is genuinely useful for homework supervision and for a younger student who needs company and momentum. It is not reliable for anything involving the Diploma's assessment model, because assessment literacy is the thing that tier does not include and nobody at that price should be expected to supply it.

In the middle, roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, you are buying a trained teacher who knows the syllabus, with one Dubai agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is where most Diploma tutoring should transact. Above it, roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, sit specialists in a single subject at a single level, with one UK agency publishing AED 270. At the top, AED 500 to 650 and above, one provider publishes AED 650 for examiner-branded provision, and what that buys is scarcity and brand rather than a demonstrably different outcome.

Separately, in-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, where Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table gives 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertise 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in this market are AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those two monthly figures, placed side by side, are the clearest statement of what the travel component costs that this market produces.

On delivery, so you are not comparing the wrong things: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. For an Al Rashidiya family we match a specialist to the exact course and level and teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a free trial lesson before anything is charged. Our own figure is agreed at the consultation, because a first-year weekly slot and an eight-week pre-session block are not the same product and one number would mislead most readers.

One structural point before the detail, because it governs everything that follows. The Diploma total is six subject grades out of 7 plus up to three points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix, and a point counts the same wherever it comes from. That single fact is why a cost-led approach outperforms a worry-led one: the point a family can buy most cheaply is frequently not in the subject keeping them awake.
