dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.programmesIntro: Diploma spend behaves very differently across the two years and the preceding ones. Planning it as a whole is what keeps the total down.

programmes.name: Diploma, first year
programmes.description: Six subjects begin, three at Higher Level, with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay process starting alongside. Internal assessment questions are chosen in this year in most subjects. Nothing is examined externally, which is why families postpone spending and why that postponement is expensive.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest and most effective year in which to buy support, and the least popular. Work done here is foundational and transfers to both years. An Al Rashidiya family who buys one bounded block in the first year typically spends less across the Diploma than one who buys nothing until the second.

programmes.name: Diploma, second year
programmes.description: Internal assessments are completed and submitted, mock examinations run, and the written papers arrive at the end. The available work narrows to technique, triage and submission deadlines. Published monthly estimates for specialist exam-year support run roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for a weekly hour.
programmes.countryNote: Where most demand arrives and where the cost per point recovered is highest. Bought as a bounded block against a stated target it is good value; bought as three open-ended weekly slots in the spring it is the most expensive configuration available in this market.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of 8 and converted to a 1-7 grade. No terminal examination unless the school uses eAssessment. Rates sit at the lower end of the published bands because the specialism required is less than for Diploma assessment work.
programmes.countryNote: Spending here is unglamorous and cheap, and it removes problems before they become Diploma problems. Teaching a student to read a criterion descriptor and write deliberately against it costs very little and pays across five years.

programmes.name: The year before the Diploma
programmes.description: Subject and level choices are made, and in mathematics the route between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation is decided. These decisions shape the entire Diploma and are effectively irreversible after the first year.
programmes.countryNote: The single highest-value hour available to an Al Rashidiya family is a free one: checking the actual entry requirements of the intended universities before the subject choices are locked. We cover it at the consultation, and a family that gets it right rarely needs the expensive second-year rescue.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.subjectsIntro: Cost per point recovered varies by subject. These are the Diploma courses Al Rashidiya families name, with an honest note on how expensive each tends to be to improve.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Good value per hour because the losses are specific and diagnosable: unstated methods, unlabelled sketches, premature rounding. A student losing marks that way is visibly better in six weeks, which makes a bounded block the right purchase.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Similar value, with the recurring loss being a calculator result left without interpretation. Teaching the sentence that must follow every statistical answer is quick work and worth a predictable number of marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mid to expensive, and the cost depends entirely on diagnosis. Graph meaning and uncertainty work are cheap; rebuilding fields from a weak algebraic base is not. Higher Level also carries a scarcity premium because fewer tutors cover it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The most expensive Diploma science to repair once organic mechanisms have been learned as memorised sequences, because the unlearning takes longer than the learning. Cheap if the gap is command terms or data handling.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Often the best value of the three sciences, because the losses are usually command-term precision and reading unfamiliar methods rather than content. Both respond within a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Evaluation technique and diagram labelling are quick wins. The portfolio of commentaries is where real money goes if the articles were chosen before the concepts were understood, because the work then has to start again.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Mid-range. Tool application to a specific stimulus is teachable in a short block; the Higher Level research project is longer work and should be quoted separately rather than folded into a weekly slot.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Expensive if the student needs to build reading stamina, cheap if the issue is essay structure or the Higher Level essay's four criteria. Diagnose before buying, because the two differ by a factor of several.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Carries a scarcity premium in this market because specialists are thin. Essay structure against command terms is efficient work; the experimental study needs attention at the design stage or not at all.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source provenance reasoning is a short, high-yield block. Content recall with figures attached is slow work and is largely the student's own to do, so paying for it by the hour is poor value.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Among the cheapest sources of Diploma points, because the essay is judged out of 10 and feeds a matrix worth up to three points. Most students receive no targeted help with it at all.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Marked out of 34 with Critical thinking alone carrying 12. A small number of sessions aimed at that criterion while the essay is still in draft is the best-value core work available on the Diploma.

sections.heading: The published rates, lowest first, with what each tier contains
paragraphs: Here is the market in order, cheapest to most expensive, with the provider that published each figure and an honest statement of what the money buys. All of it was collected in October 2026 and none of it is ours. We publish it because three of the six strongest competitor pages in this cluster quote no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Dubai household transacts in.

The useful way to read this table is from the bottom up, deciding where to stop. For homework supervision and momentum, stop at the first row. For a Middle Years student learning to write against a criterion, the second row is sufficient. For Diploma assessment work, internal assessment coaching or Higher Level technique, you need the third or fourth. The fifth row buys scarcity and a name, and we would not advise a family in Al Rashidiya to start there.

The in-home rows are the comparison most families on this page actually want. Four two-hour visits a month at the published AED 1,599 to 1,799 is eight hours for roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour, against an online package of eight sessions at AED 799, which is roughly AED 100 a session. The gap is not teaching quality. It is a car, a driver's time, and the arrival risk that goes with the airport road at six in the evening.

Our own position sits in the qualified-specialist part of this table. We publish no rate card on these pages because the right figure depends on the subject, the level, whether the work is a weekly slot or a bounded block, and what the marked work says is actually wrong. The trial lesson is free, nothing is charged before it, and the figure is agreed at the consultation with the whole plan attached rather than as a headline.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys from an Al Rashidiya address
paragraphs: Al Rashidiya is better connected than most of the eastern suburbs. It has a metro station on the Red Line, a major bus interchange, and it sits beside Dubai Festival City and the airport roads. In principle that should make in-home tutoring cheap here, and to an extent it does: a tutor based in Festival City or Garhoud faces a short journey and quotes accordingly.

The complication is the hour. The tutoring slot a Diploma family wants is between five and eight in the evening, which is exactly when the airport approaches, Al Rebat Street and the Garhoud crossings are at their worst. A tutor is pricing not the distance but the risk of a twenty-minute delay, and the ones who accept a six o'clock booking in this area are either very local or charging for the uncertainty. Neither of those is a statement about their teaching.

The table sets the two formats against each other on the things that change a grade rather than on atmosphere. Read the row on delivered teaching minutes carefully, because it is the one nobody quantifies: a quarter-hour of arrival slippage on a weekly sixty-minute booking is roughly a quarter of the teaching you paid for, and across thirty weeks that is seven and a half hours, or more than a full term's worth of lessons.

Against that, be fair about what in-home genuinely provides. An adult in the room, which for a child under about eleven or a student with real attention difficulties is a service and not a luxury. No dependence on a household's internet. And no need for a quiet room with a closing door, which not every home can offer. If those apply to your situation, the premium is buying something real and we would say so.

sections.heading: The five places Diploma money disappears
paragraphs: None of these is the hourly rate, and together they account for most of the overspending we see in this part of Dubai. First, buying the subject the parent is most worried about rather than the subject where a point is cheapest. The Diploma total is built from six subject grades plus up to three matrix points, and a point is a point. Forcing a Higher Level grade from 5 to 6 is often the most expensive point on the board, while a Standard Level 5 to 6 or a matrix point sits there unbought.

Second, ignoring the core. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34 with Critical thinking worth 12, and the Theory of Knowledge essay is judged out of 10; together they feed a matrix worth up to three points. A handful of sessions aimed at those while the drafts are open is the cheapest point-recovery available on the Diploma, and almost no family buys it.

Third, starting in the second year. By the spring the internal assessments are submitted, the content window has closed, and only technique work remains, at the point in the demand curve where specialist rates and scarcity are highest. The same intervention bought twelve months earlier costs less and has more to work with.

Fourth, buying hours before a diagnosis. The same symptom, a dropping grade, can mean a four-session technique fix or a two-term rebuild, and those differ by an order of magnitude in cost. A marked script tells a specialist which it is in minutes. Fifth, renewing monthly without a review point. An engagement nobody is measuring gets extended out of uncertainty, and at the published monthly estimates of AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support, uncertainty is an expensive habit.

sections.heading: A two-year Diploma budget, planned backwards
paragraphs: Families budget tutoring monthly and then discover the Diploma has cost several times what they expected. The alternative is to plan the whole two years once, at the start, with specific purchases attached to specific windows and nothing bought outside them. It is a less comfortable conversation and it reliably produces a lower total.

The table below is that plan, with indicative figures from the published qualified and specialist bands. It assumes one subject at a time and bounded blocks rather than continuous weekly slots, which is the configuration we would recommend to an Al Rashidiya family and the one that costs least per point recovered. A family following it typically spends somewhere between AED 6,000 and AED 14,000 across the full Diploma, against the AED 15,000 to 30,000 that two years of three-subject weekly support would reach.

Note where the money sits. The largest single item is the first-year subject block, because foundational work transfers to both years. The cheapest items with the best return are the mathematics exploration or science investigation question, and the Extended Essay criterion work. The item most families actually buy, an open-ended second-year weekly slot, does not appear at all, because its job is done better and earlier by two of the other rows.

Treat the figures as planning ranges rather than quotes. They are derived from other providers' published rates, collected in October 2026, and our own figure is agreed at the consultation once the subject, level and diagnosis are known. The structure is the point: decide what you will buy and when, before the first panic, and the total stops being a surprise.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach here, and what does that cost?
paragraphs: A question with a free answer, which is why it belongs on a page about money. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. If a tutor tells you the permit costs money, they have not applied for one.

Eligibility is wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, available through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days and no published fee.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the ministry's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and a figure circulating online could not be verified, so any provider quoting you a specific dirham penalty is repeating something they cannot evidence.

There is a related distinction worth knowing before you pay anybody. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor: it requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. A tuition centre should be able to evidence that. An individual needs the MoHRE permit. Neither of those is something IB Gram holds or claims, and no tutoring provider should be describing itself as KHDA-approved without showing the permit.

sections.heading: The cheapest way to lose everything: paying for assessed work
paragraphs: This belongs on a page about cost because it is marketed on price. One provider found in the research for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at a published figure. Framed as a purchase it looks efficient: a fixed sum, a finished document, a problem solved. Framed accurately it is the most expensive thing available in this market, because what it risks is the Diploma itself.

Work submitted for IB assessment must be the student's own. Buying it is an academic-honesty breach that triggers malpractice procedures against the student rather than against the seller, and the consequence lands on a seventeen-year-old who may lose the award. There is no refund available for that outcome and no provider offers one.

The legitimate alternative costs far less and is genuinely useful. A tutor may teach the content, explain what a criterion descriptor is asking for, interrogate a research question or an essay's argument, and read the student's own draft and say precisely which descriptor is not yet met. A tutor may not write, draft, restructure or edit to completion any part of the submitted work, supply data, or perform the analysis.

The test after any session is simple and costs nothing to apply: has the document changed, and if so, who typed the changes? If the answer is the tutor, you have bought something you did not want. A good session leaves the student holding three specific problems and the file untouched. We will not produce assessed work at any price, and we state that here rather than in terms and conditions because the families most at risk are the ones under time pressure.

sections.heading: IB provision within reach of Al Rashidiya, and what it tells you
paragraphs: Al Rashidiya sits unusually close to Diploma provision by the standards of the eastern suburbs. Dubai Festival City is adjacent and holds two of the nearest IB schools, one of them running the full continuum. Mirdif, a short drive east, adds continuum provision, and Nad Al Sheba is within the realistic school-run radius. For a family weighing the cost of the whole education rather than just the tutoring, that proximity is worth real money in fuel and in time.

The free document nobody reads is the KHDA inspection report. Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by the UAE government as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and it inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, publishing subject-level and phase-level findings. If you are deciding whether a difficulty is a provision issue or an individual one, that report answers the question better than any tutoring consultation.

Context on the market: Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with UK provision at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and International Baccalaureate at 7%. Seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, were announced for the 2026-27 intake, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

The budgeting implication of that last point is direct. For a household with two children in private school, a flat fee year genuinely changes what is available for everything else, and it is the right year to plan a two-year Diploma support budget deliberately rather than reactively. The planning is free; only the tutoring costs anything.

sections.heading: What to send to get an honest quote first time
paragraphs: Four things, and they are the same four regardless of who you ask. The exact course title and level as the school writes it, because Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level are different tutors at different rates. The most recent marked script or report. The predicted grades and the university offer if there is one. And the two evening slots that genuinely survive your school run.

With those, any competent provider can tell you whether this is a bounded block or a term's work, which is the difference between roughly AED 1,500 and roughly AED 9,000. Without them, you will be quoted a weekly slot by default, because a weekly slot is the safe thing to sell when nobody knows what is wrong. That default is how families in this area end up spending several times what the problem required.

Ask three questions back. What specifically will my child be able to do after this block that they cannot do now? Is work set between sessions, and is it marked, and is that inside the quoted figure? And what is the cancellation notice in writing? The first tests whether there is a plan, the second tests whether you are buying teaching or company, and the third protects you when a Dubai family inevitably needs to move a session.

And ask one more that most providers dislike: is there a cheaper thing I should buy instead? Sometimes the honest answer is the school's own revision clinic, which is free and aligned to the school's entries. Sometimes it is a conversation with the IB coordinator about whether a Higher Level subject should be stabilised rather than pushed. Sometimes it is nothing at all. A provider who will give one of those answers is more likely to be worth the figure when they do quote one.

whyPoints.description: Six subject grades plus up to three matrix points make the Diploma total, and a point costs very different amounts depending on where it comes from. We start from the predicted grades and the offer, which often points somewhere the family was not looking.

whyPoints.title: Travel is not inside the figure
whyPoints.description: The published in-home band of AED 180 to 500 includes a drive, and from Al Rashidiya at six in the evening that drive crosses the airport approaches. Online delivery means the whole figure buys teaching and the full hour is delivered.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered for free
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free of charge and valid two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. No fine schedule is published, so nobody can quote you a penalty figure, and no provider should call itself KHDA-approved without the permit to show.

whyPoints.title: We will name the cheaper option
whyPoints.description: The school's own revision clinic is free and aligned to its entries. A conversation with the IB coordinator costs nothing. Sometimes the right recommendation is one of those, and we would rather give it and lose the booking than sell a block that was never needed.

faqs.question: What should an IB home tutor cost around Al Rashidiya?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates for in-home one-to-one visits run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, where Bestimate's 2026 table gives 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertise 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour visits have been published at AED 1,599 to 1,799, which is roughly AED 200 to 225 per teaching hour. Qualified tutors working online sit lower, roughly AED 150 to 300, with one Dubai agency publishing IB from AED 200. Those are other providers' figures, collected October 2026, not ours.

faqs.question: Why does the Dubai tutoring market have a twenty-fold price range?
faqs.answer: Because the tiers contain genuinely different things. At roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour you are buying subject knowledge and homework momentum from a student or recent graduate, with no assessment literacy expected. At AED 150 to 300 you are buying a trained teacher who knows the syllabus and its papers. At AED 200 to 450 and above you are buying single-subject depth and internal assessment expertise. Above AED 500 you are buying scarcity and brand. The step that reliably changes a Diploma lesson is from the first tier to the second.

faqs.question: How much should a whole IB Diploma cost in tutoring?
faqs.answer: Planned properly, somewhere between roughly AED 4,000 and AED 12,000 across both years, using the published qualified and specialist bands. That assumes bounded blocks: a first-year subject block, a few sessions on the internal assessment question, a few on the Extended Essay's Critical thinking criterion, a mock diagnostic, and a second-year technique block only if the mocks justify it. Bought instead as three open-ended weekly slots across two years, the same support reaches AED 15,000 to 30,000, which is where most unplanned Diploma spending ends up.

faqs.question: Which Diploma points are cheapest to buy help for?
faqs.answer: Usually the matrix points and a Standard Level grade. Six subject grades reach 42 and the final three come from a matrix combining the Theory of Knowledge grade with the Extended Essay grade. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34 with Critical thinking alone carrying 12, and the Theory of Knowledge essay is judged out of 10, so a handful of sessions while those drafts are open can move the total. Forcing a Higher Level grade from 5 to 6 is generally the most expensive point on the board.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying more for an examiner-branded tutor?
faqs.answer: We would not advise starting there. One provider publishes AED 650 an hour for examiner-branded provision, which is roughly twice the specialist band and more than ten times the budget tier. What it reliably buys is scarcity and a name. We also will not describe any tutor as a current IB or Cambridge examiner unless that status can be evidenced, and no provider should be implying examiner status gives access to marking, boundaries or paper content. Ask what specifically changes in the lesson at that price.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Dubai need a licence, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: They need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services with a stated two-working-day completion. If a tutor tells you the permit has a fee, they have not applied for one. No fine schedule is published, so treat specific penalty figures online as unverified.

faqs.question: Why are monthly in-home packages so much more expensive?
faqs.answer: Because they include a car. Four two-hour in-home visits a month at the published AED 1,599 to 1,799 works out around AED 200 to 225 per teaching hour, against an online package of eight sessions published at AED 799, roughly AED 100 a session. The difference is the journey, the driver's time and the risk of arriving late. From Al Rashidiya at six in the evening that journey crosses the airport approaches, which is precisely why the quote carries a premium rather than a discount for a short distance.

faqs.question: How much teaching time does a late tutor actually cost us?
faqs.answer: More than families estimate. A quarter of an hour of arrival slippage on a weekly sixty-minute booking is a quarter of the lesson, and across a thirty-week school year that is seven and a half hours, which is more than a full term's worth of sessions. It is also not refunded, because the tutor was present for the booking. An online session starts when the clock says so, which is the least glamorous and most measurable argument on this page for the format we actually sell.

faqs.question: Should we buy a block of twenty hours for the discount?
faqs.answer: Not before you know the match works. Bulk hours at a reduced rate are a saving only if all of them are the right hours, and they make leaving expensive, so families persist with a tutor they would otherwise have changed in week two. That is the most costly outcome in this market. Take the free trial, buy a small bounded block with a stated target, review it on marked work, and only then commit further if you want to. We do not sell bulk discounts for exactly this reason.

faqs.question: Is buying a finished Internal Assessment ever worth the money?
faqs.answer: No, and it is the most expensive purchase available in this market however low the price looks. Work submitted for IB assessment must be the student's own, and buying it triggers malpractice procedures against the student rather than the seller, with the award itself at risk. One provider found in the research for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments at a published figure. No refund exists for the outcome. The legitimate version, a tutor questioning a research design and naming the descriptor a draft does not meet, costs far less and is genuinely useful.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time to start Diploma support?
faqs.answer: Before it starts, with a free conversation about subject and level choices and the mathematics route, because those decisions are effectively irreversible after the first year and getting them wrong is the most expensive mistake on the whole Diploma. After that, the first-year autumn, where foundational work transfers to both years. The most expensive window is the spring of the second year, when internal assessments are submitted, only technique work remains, and specialist rates and scarcity are both at their peak.

faqs.question: What should we ask before paying a Dubai tutor anything?
faqs.answer: Four things in writing. What specifically will my child be able to do at the end of this block that they cannot do now. Is work set between sessions, is it marked, and is that inside the quoted figure. What is the cancellation notice period, because a Dubai family will need to move sessions. And does the figure include VAT, which you are entitled to ask and nobody should be vague about. A provider who answers all four plainly is more likely to be worth the rate.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai fee freeze affect what we can spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: It changes what is available rather than what is wise. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a household with two children in private school that is genuine capacity. The sensible use of it is a planned two-year Diploma support budget with specific purchases in specific windows, rather than a larger monthly commitment nobody is measuring.

faqs.question: Would you ever tell us to spend nothing?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the three-session diagnostic exists partly so that it can end that way. If the school runs its own revision clinic in the subject, it is free and aligned to the school's own entries, and competing with it wastes your money. If a Higher Level subject should be stabilised rather than pushed while points are recovered elsewhere, that is a conversation with the IB coordinator and it costs nothing. And no tutoring is required for a university application or for Ministry of Education equivalency, whatever any provider implies.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.closingHeading: Plan the total, then buy one block
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.closingBody: The families in Al Rashidiya who spend least across a Diploma are the ones who decided at the start what they would buy and when. One free conversation about subjects and levels, one bounded block in the first year, a few sessions on the internal assessment question and the Extended Essay, a diagnostic on the mocks, and a second-year technique block only if the scripts justify it. Send us the course and level, the most recent marked script and the predicted grades, and we will tell you which of those your child actually needs and what it costs. A free trial lesson comes first, and nothing is charged before it.

intro.heading: The Diploma is six subjects and eleven or twelve separate assessments
paragraphs: A parent in Al Safa searching for an IB home tutor normally has one sentence of diagnosis to work from: the school says Chemistry is a concern, or Maths has slipped. The Diploma does not work at that resolution. Each subject is assessed by two or three written papers plus an Internal Assessment, each component carries its own percentage of the final grade, and each is marked by different criteria. A student can be comfortable on Paper 1 and losing a grade on Paper 2, and the report card will say the same thing either way.

So the first job of a useful IB tutor is subtraction. Which component is actually costing marks? Before any teaching happens, that question has a cheap answer: look at the mock breakdown by paper. If the school does not provide one, ask for it. A Diploma mock paper set is three to four separate scripts in most subjects, and the component-level numbers tell you more than the aggregate grade does. Almost every plan we write for an Al Safa family starts there.

The second job is the Internal Assessment, which is where the marks are most predictably available and most commonly neglected. Each IA is marked against lettered criteria with explicit mark allocations: in the sciences the scientific investigation carries 24 marks across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation; in mathematics the exploration carries 20 marks across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Those are published numbers. A student who has read them and written to them does better than a student who wrote a good piece of work and hoped.

Third comes the core, which decides up to three points of the final 45. The Extended Essay is marked against five criteria totalling 34 marks, with a 4,000-word maximum, and Theory of Knowledge contributes an essay and an exhibition. Al Safa families routinely underweight this: three points is the difference between a conditional offer met and missed, and it sits in two pieces of work that are supervised rather than taught, which means nobody is chasing the student weekly.

On how we deliver, say it plainly. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we offer only in India, and the in-home market in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour by other providers if that is the format a family wants. Our Al Safa tuition is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and the mark scheme on a shared screen. On component-level work that is the right tool, because both people need to be looking at the same question.

The pages beside this one in Al Safa take other routes: the maths, physics and chemistry pages go deeper into single subjects, and the IGCSE pages cover the years before this one. This page is the architecture of the Diploma, because that is the part Al Safa parents are most often working without.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-safa.programmesIntro: Al Safa households meet the IB at different points, and the three stages need genuinely different help. Naming the stage before booking saves both money and a term of mismatched sessions.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard, graded 1 to 7 for a subject maximum of 42, plus up to 3 points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combined, giving 45. Each subject carries written papers and an Internal Assessment, and the component weightings differ by level. Most of our Al Safa work sits here, and most of it is component-specific rather than subject-wide.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Safa schools run A Level rather than the Diploma after IGCSE, so a family wanting the DP sometimes moves a child at sixteen. A student arriving in DP1 from a different school and a different curriculum carries two adjustments at once, and the first term is where that shows.

programmes.name: IB Career-related Programme and course candidates
programmes.description: Not every student in an IB school takes the full Diploma. Course candidates take individual subjects and receive certificates rather than the Diploma, and the Career-related Programme combines DP courses with career-related study. The assessment for the individual subjects is identical, so the tutoring is the same work, but the pressure profile is different because there is no 45-point total and no core requirement.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Safa this comes up most where a student has moved from a British school mid-sixth-form, or where a school advises against the full Diploma after a difficult DP1. The subject papers and the IA still need the same component-level preparation, and that is what we work on.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme, the run-up
programmes.description: Five years assessed against four lettered criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, with no percentages and no terminal examinations except through optional eAssessment. The skills it builds are inquiry, documentation and reflection. The skills the Diploma then assumes are recall under time pressure and technical fluency, which is why the transition catches strong MYP students out.
programmes.countryNote: Al Safa has both continuum IB schools and British-curriculum schools, so some students reach DP1 from MYP 5 and others from IGCSE. The two arrive with opposite strengths, and a tutor who does not ask which route a student came by will misdiagnose the first term.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside the Diploma
programmes.ageRange: All year groups in Dubai private schools
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and these subjects sit alongside the six Diploma subjects rather than replacing any of them.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Safa Diploma student this is the reason the week has less slack than the IB subject count suggests. Six subjects plus the core plus mandatory subjects is a full timetable, and tutoring has to fit a smaller evening window than a UK-based plan would assume.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-safa.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Al Safa families ask for most, named with the component that usually carries the loss. The point of this list is to help you say something more specific than the subject name when you enquire.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At SL the two papers carry the bulk of the grade with the exploration at 20%; at HL a third paper adds extended problem-solving. Marks are lost on algebraic manipulation under time pressure and on the non-calculator paper, where fluency rather than understanding is what is being tested.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology-rich and modelling-led, with statistics carrying real weight. Students who choose it to avoid algebra discover that the interpretation demands are high: a correct calculation with no comment on what it means scores poorly against the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two written papers plus the scientific investigation at 20%. Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics are the recurring difficulties, and the investigation is where the most predictable marks sit because its four criteria are published with mark allocations attached.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mathematical modelling under time pressure is the real demand, not conceptual difficulty. Students who can state a law lose marks deriving from it, and the data-based questions in Paper 1 reward careful graph and uncertainty work that is rarely practised enough.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume plus command-term precision. An answer that describes when the verb asked for an explanation earns nothing, however accurate it is, and HL students routinely underestimate how much of the grade sits in extended response rather than recall.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the grade. HL adds a quantitative paper that surprises students who chose the subject as an essay option, and the Internal Assessment is a set of commentaries on real published articles rather than a single piece of research.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The guided textual analysis paper rewards close reading of an unseen text under time pressure, and the comparative essay rewards planning. HL carries an additional written essay. Strong readers lose marks by narrating the text instead of analysing how a choice produces an effect.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source evaluation on the prescribed subject paper, essay writing on the world history topics, and at HL a third regional paper. The IA is a historical investigation marked against three criteria totalling 25 marks, with source evaluation carrying a specific allocation of its own.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application and evaluation under case-study conditions. Students memorise frameworks and then apply them generically; the marks sit in applying one tool precisely to the stimulus provided, which is a technique rather than a knowledge gain.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together worth up to three points of the 45. The Extended Essay has a 4,000-word maximum and five criteria totalling 34 marks; TOK carries an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition. Both are supervised rather than taught, which is why they are the most commonly neglected marks in the Diploma.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Al Safa is really being asked to do
paragraphs: The phrase people search is "IB home tutor in Al Safa", and the intent behind it is almost never about the home. It is about proximity as a proxy for reliability: somebody nearby, who knows the schools here, who can be held accountable. Those are reasonable wants and they are worth answering directly rather than redirecting.

On proximity, the honest position is that IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and Al Safa tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video. The in-home market in Dubai is real and is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel by Bestimate and by independent home tutors; if a family wants somebody physically present, that market exists and this page will not pretend otherwise.

On reliability, the thing that matters is whether the tutor can work at component level. A Diploma student losing marks on Chemistry Paper 2 needs somebody who can read the mark scheme for an extended-response question and explain why a correct-sounding answer earned two of four marks. Geography has nothing to do with whether a tutor can do that, and insisting on physical presence narrows the pool to people willing to drive to Al Safa at 4.30pm on a Tuesday.

On accountability, what replaces proximity is documentation. A written diagnosis after the first session, a named component to be fixed, a halfway review against the same question types, and a session recording the parent can watch. That is more checkable than somebody sitting at a kitchen table, and it is available regardless of where the right subject specialist happens to live.

sections.heading: Component weightings: which paper is actually deciding the grade
paragraphs: The single most useful document a Diploma parent can obtain is the component breakdown of their child's mock results. Not the grade, the breakdown. In most subjects a Diploma mock comprises two or three written papers plus an IA mark, and the papers do not carry equal weight. A student who is five marks off a boundary may be losing all of it in one component that carries 44% of the grade, which makes the next eight weeks very easy to plan.

Weightings also differ between Higher and Standard Level in the same subject, which parents consistently find surprising. In mathematics, Standard Level is two papers plus the exploration, while Higher Level adds a third paper and redistributes the percentages. In the sciences, the exploration-equivalent investigation is 20% at both levels, but the written papers divide the remaining 80% differently from, say, History, where the IA share and the paper count both change with level.

There is one caution to attach to any table of weightings, including the one below. The IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle, and the current guide for your child's cohort is the authority. Ask the subject teacher or the Diploma coordinator which guide applies and what the component percentages are for that version, and treat anything published on a third-party page as a prompt to check rather than a fact to act on.

Used properly, the weightings change the plan in a specific way. If the heaviest paper is also the weakest, the whole block goes there. If the weakest component is the IA and the IA window is still open, that is the cheapest grade movement available in the entire Diploma, because the criteria are published and the work is not timed.

sections.heading: IA criterion letters and mark allocations, which nobody else publishes
paragraphs: Internal Assessments are marked against lettered criteria with explicit mark allocations, and those allocations are published in each subject guide. We checked the pages ranking for Dubai IB tutoring searches: not one of them names a single criterion. That is a strange gap, because the allocations tell a student exactly where to spend their effort.

Take the sciences. The scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each carrying 6 marks. A student who writes a thorough method and then a two-line conclusion has thrown away a quarter of the available marks for reasons of pacing rather than ability. Knowing the allocation is enough to prevent that, and it takes five minutes to read.

Mathematics works differently. The exploration is marked out of 20 across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and the last of those carries the largest share. Students pick topics they find interesting but mathematically thin, score well on engagement and poorly on the heaviest criterion. The topic choice conversation, held before any work starts, is worth more than every session afterwards.

The Extended Essay follows the same logic at larger scale: five criteria totalling 34 marks, with critical thinking carrying the heaviest allocation by a wide margin. Students spend their time on knowledge and understanding, which is comfortable, and underinvest in argument, which is where the marks are. Reading the allocation table before choosing a research question changes the question a student picks.

sections.heading: Command terms, and why a correct answer can score nothing
paragraphs: The most common conversation in a first Diploma tutoring session goes like this. The student has written something true and relevant and received one mark out of four. They conclude the marking is harsh. The mark scheme says otherwise: the question asked them to evaluate and they described, or it asked them to justify and they stated.

IB command terms are defined in the subject guides and grouped by the depth of thinking they require. Terms like state, list and identify ask for recall and nothing more. Describe, outline and explain ask for progressively more development. Analyse, evaluate, justify, discuss and to what extent ask for argument, weighing and judgement. A student who treats all of them as invitations to write everything they know will underperform in every paper of every subject.

This is coachable quickly, and it is the highest-return early work available. Take ten past-paper questions in the student's own subject, cover the answers, and have them say only what the verb requires before writing anything. Then mark against the official scheme. Most students see the pattern within two sessions, and the improvement shows up across subjects rather than in one.

The reason it goes untaught is that it sits between subjects. The Chemistry teacher teaches chemistry, the History teacher teaches history, and nobody owns the verb list. A tutor working with one student across their whole Diploma profile is well placed to own it, and for an Al Safa student juggling six subjects plus the core that cross-subject view is often the most valuable thing a weekly hour provides.

sections.heading: The three core points, and why Al Safa families leave them on the table
paragraphs: Six subjects give a maximum of 42 points. The remaining three come from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together, through a published matrix combining the grades awarded for each. Three points is a large amount in a system where university offers are set in whole numbers, and it is routinely the least prepared part of the Diploma.

The structural reason is supervision. Subjects are taught weekly by a teacher who sets work and chases it. The Extended Essay is supervised, usually with a small number of scheduled meetings across a year, and TOK sits in a thin timetable slot. A student who is managing their own time well does fine. A student who is not has no weekly mechanism catching them, and the first visible sign is a missed internal deadline.

What helps is treating both as projects with milestones rather than as essays with deadlines. For the Extended Essay that means a narrowed research question months before the first draft, a method that genuinely fits the question, and an explicit plan for criterion C, critical thinking, which carries the heaviest allocation of the 34 marks. The 4,000-word maximum is a constraint on scope, and a question too broad to answer in 4,000 words is the commonest root cause of a weak essay.

The honesty boundary here is firm and worth repeating. A tutor may teach research method, interrogate a question, explain what a criterion requires, and read a student's own draft and say where it falls short. A tutor may not write, rewrite to completion or dictate any part of an Extended Essay, TOK essay or Internal Assessment. There is at least one provider in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at a published price; that is an academic-integrity breach, and the risk falls on the student rather than the seller.

sections.heading: Online versus in-home IB tuition from an Al Safa address
paragraphs: Lead with the number a family can check. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, per Bestimate's 2026 rate table and independent home-tutor listings. Qualified online subject tutors are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. The difference between those bands is roughly AED 100 to 200 an hour, and what it buys is a journey.

For an Al Safa household the journey is short but badly timed. The neighbourhood sits inside its own school catchment, so a tutor living nearby has a quick run; a tutor living anywhere else is crossing Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Wasl Road at pick-up. In practice that limits the realistic in-home pool to a small number of people with the right availability, and availability is not the same as being the right specialist for Chemistry Paper 2.

The pool argument is the real one. Diploma requirements are narrow. A student needs Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or History Paper 3 on a specific regional option, or an Extended Essay supervisor who understands the criteria in a subject their school does not teach. Accepting live video means choosing from everyone who can do that. Requiring physical presence means choosing from everyone who can do that and lives within twenty minutes.

The trade-offs deserve naming. A student who will not work without somebody in the room benefits from a person being there. A household with an unreliable connection should establish that on the free trial rather than in week three. And handwritten mathematics working needs to be visible, so a document camera or a well-placed phone is worth setting up before a paid session. Online is the better tool for most Diploma work, not for all of it.

sections.heading: What IB tuition costs in Dubai, and what the premium actually buys
paragraphs: Begin with what a parent can verify independently rather than with a rate. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are flat this year; tutoring rates are not, which makes the tutoring line more visible in a household budget than it has been.

The published bands, each attributed to its source, run as follows. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

What rises as you move up those bands is specificity, not generic quality. The budget band can supervise homework. The qualified band can teach a syllabus accurately. The specialist band can read a mark scheme for an extended-response question and explain the gap between three marks and five. For Diploma work that last skill is the one being bought, and it is why a cheaper tutor who does not have it can be worse value at a third of the price.

One caution on the top band. Examiner status is frequently claimed and rarely evidenced. We do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners unless current status can be shown, and no examiner claim should be taken to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. If a provider leans on examiner status at AED 650 an hour, ask what evidence exists before paying for it.

sections.heading: KHDA, ADEK and the regulator map Al Safa parents can use
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools annually. For an Al Safa family the practical use is simple: the current published inspection band on KHDA's own listing is the figure worth reading, not a rating quoted on a third-party page that may be two cycles old.

The rest of the country is regulated differently, which matters if a family relocates within the UAE. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there; both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the emirate regulator controls more than inspection. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

On mandatory subjects, the federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes strictly prohibited.

Dubai's market context is worth holding too, because it affects availability. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, and the enrolment split by curriculum was UK 37%, Indian 26%, US 14% and International Baccalaureate 7%. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More IB provision is arriving, which over time widens Higher Level subject choice in this part of the city.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and what IB Gram is not
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount a parent sees online should be treated as unverified. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor. It needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit and does not operate premises in the UAE, and no page of ours should ever imply a regulator or an examination board has approved, accredited or licensed us, because none has.

What we are is an online matching platform. We do not perform or expedite Ministry of Education equivalency or attestation, which is a process the Ministry and the emirate authorities run and which parents should pursue through the official channel. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and the mock breakdown
process.description: The component-level mock marks are what make a plan possible. Subject and level alone leave a tutor guessing between Paper 1 technique, Paper 2 extended response and an IA that has not been started. If the school has not provided the breakdown, ask for it before you book.

process.title: Free trial lesson on a real past-paper question
process.description: The trial runs on an actual question from the component in question, not as an introductory chat. You see how the tutor explains the gap between the student's answer and the mark scheme. No payment, no card, and if the fit is wrong we will try another tutor.

process.title: A written diagnosis naming the component
process.description: After the first paid session you get a short note: which component is costing marks, whether the cause is content, technique or timing, and what the first four sessions will do about it. That note is what the block is judged against later.

process.title: Criteria read before any IA or Extended Essay work
process.description: For Internal Assessment and core work, the first session reads the criterion letters and their mark allocations with the student. Most students have never seen the allocation table, and seeing it changes what they choose to write about.

process.title: Fixed slots on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are booked on GST around the Al Safa school run, usually from 4.30pm on weekdays with weekend mornings available for longer Extended Essay work. Ramadan slots shift later, including post-Iftar timings, agreed in advance rather than week by week.

process.title: A halfway review against the same question types
process.description: Midway through a block we re-test the diagnosed component with comparable questions and compare the marks. If nothing has moved, the plan or the tutor changes. Continuing unchanged because sessions are booked is how families pay for comfort instead of progress.

whyPoints.title: We match on component, not on subject name
whyPoints.description: Chemistry Paper 2 extended response and the scientific investigation are different pieces of work needing different teaching. Asking which component is costing marks before matching a tutor is the single biggest determinant of whether a block works.

whyPoints.title: Criterion letters and allocations named explicitly
whyPoints.description: Not one of the pages ranking for Dubai IB tutoring names an IA criterion. We publish the letters and the mark totals because they tell a student where the available marks actually sit, and because a parent can verify them in the subject guide.

whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work. Nobody writes an IA, Extended Essay or TOK essay. We say so plainly, because at least one provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price.

faqs.question: What should I ask the school for before hiring an IB tutor in Al Safa?
faqs.answer: The component breakdown of the most recent mock, not the grade. A Diploma mock is two or three written papers plus an Internal Assessment mark in most subjects, and the papers carry different weights. A student five marks off a boundary is often losing nearly all of it in one component, which makes the next block easy to plan and cheap to buy. Ask also which subject guide the cohort follows, because the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle and component percentages differ between versions.

faqs.question: How is the IB score of 45 actually made up?
faqs.answer: Six subjects, each graded from 1 to 7, give a maximum of 42 points. The remaining three come from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together, awarded through a published matrix that combines the grades for each. Students normally take three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard. The practical consequence is that the core is worth more than most families treat it as: three points is a large margin in a system where university offers are stated in whole numbers, and the core is the least supervised part of the programme.

faqs.question: What are the IB Internal Assessment criteria and how many marks does each carry?
faqs.answer: They differ by subject and are published in each subject guide. The sciences scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6 marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The History historical investigation totals 25 across identification and evaluation of sources, investigation and reflection. Read the allocation table for your child's subject before any work starts; it changes what topic a sensible student chooses.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Al Safa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Al Safa lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and mark scheme on a shared screen and a recording available afterwards. We target the home-tutor phrase because that is what parents search for, then answer it honestly. The in-home market in Dubai exists and is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel if you want somebody physically present.

faqs.question: Why does my child write a correct answer and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Usually because the command term was not answered. IB command terms are defined in the subject guides and grouped by required depth: state, list and identify ask only for recall, describe and explain ask for development, and analyse, evaluate, justify and discuss ask for argument and judgement. A student who writes everything they know in response to a low-depth verb wastes time, and one who states facts in response to evaluate earns very little. Two sessions of verb drill against official mark schemes usually shifts the pattern across every subject at once.

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor in Al Safa cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market bands in Dubai, each attributed to its publisher: budget online and student tutors AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650, BartyED publishing AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel. None of these is an IB Gram price; we quote against a plan after the free trial.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Extended Essay without writing it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the only version worth buying. A tutor can interrogate the research question, explain why a question too broad for 4,000 words cannot be answered well, teach research method, explain what each of the five criteria totalling 34 marks requires, and read the student's own draft and say which criterion a section fails. A tutor cannot write, rewrite to completion or dictate any part of it. Any provider offering a completed essay is offering an academic-integrity breach whose consequences fall on your child, not on them.

faqs.question: Which Extended Essay criterion should my child worry about most?
faqs.answer: Critical thinking, which carries the heaviest allocation of the 34 marks by a wide margin. Students spend their time on knowledge and understanding because reading is comfortable, and underinvest in argument, which is where the marks sit. The practical implication arrives early: a research question that invites description cannot score well on critical thinking however much work goes into it. Narrowing the question so that it demands weighing and judgement is the single highest-value decision in the whole process, and it is made months before any writing.

faqs.question: My child has arrived in DP1 from IGCSE and is struggling. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always fluency rather than content. IGCSE rewards accuracy on shorter structured questions; the Diploma assumes algebraic manipulation is automatic and asks for sustained argument under time pressure. In Mathematics Analysis and Approaches the non-calculator paper exposes this immediately. A six to ten session landing block in the first term, aimed at algebra, command terms and timed written response rather than new content, resolves most of it. Separating content gaps from fluency gaps from timing problems is the first session's job, and it is usually possible in one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one Diploma subject for the same student?
faqs.answer: For a cross-subject problem, yes, and often better than two specialists. Command terms, essay structure under timed conditions and IA criterion reading are the same skills in every subject, and one tutor holding the whole Diploma profile can fix them once. For deep content work in a specific Higher Level subject, a specialist in that subject is the right choice. Start from the diagnosis: if the pattern of lost marks is the same shape in three subjects, buy the cross-subject work first.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session start for an Al Safa household?
faqs.answer: Al Safa sits inside its own school catchment, so arrival home is earlier than in most Dubai communities and a 4.30pm start is usually workable. From Jumeirah 2 and Jumeirah 3 the realistic first slot is 5pm because of Beach Road congestion at pick-up. Diploma students carry the heaviest homework load in a household, so a 60-minute focused session beats a longer one that eats the evening. Slots are booked on Gulf Standard Time and move later during Ramadan, including post-Iftar timings, arranged in advance.

faqs.question: Is online IB tutoring as effective as having someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For component-level Diploma work it is usually better, because the work is document work. The past paper, the mark scheme, the student's script and the criterion table can all be on a shared screen at once, with the tutor's cursor on the exact phrase that lost the mark. The pool argument is stronger still: narrow requirements such as a specific History regional option or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level need the right specialist, not the nearest one. The exception is a student who genuinely will not work without physical supervision.

faqs.question: Does my child's Higher Level choice matter for UAE university admission?
faqs.answer: It can, and it is worth checking directly with the universities on your child's list rather than relying on general advice. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are treated differently by some engineering and economics programmes, and Higher Level science requirements vary by faculty. Ask the admissions office for the stated requirement in writing. Separately, Ministry of Education equivalency is a distinct process from admission, run by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authorities, and no IB points threshold for it should be trusted unless you have read it on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Which Al Safa schools run the Diploma, and does it matter which one?
faqs.answer: Al Safa and its immediate neighbours contain both IB continuum schools and British-curriculum schools that run A Level after IGCSE, which is why some families move a child at sixteen to get the route they want. Where it matters most for tutoring is Higher Level provision: a school running one HL Physics group with very few students in it offers a different experience from one running a full class. KHDA publishes an annual inspection band for each school, and the current band on KHDA's own listing is the figure to read.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory UAE subjects affect a Diploma timetable?
faqs.answer: They sit alongside it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Six Diploma subjects plus the core plus mandatory subjects is a genuinely full week, which is why one protected weekly hour on a diagnosed component outperforms an ambitious multi-session plan a household cannot sustain.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is available for my child's Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than putting a generalist in the slot and hoping. Narrow Diploma combinations genuinely run out: specific History regional options, some Group 2 languages at Higher Level, and particular Extended Essay subjects. Where the right specialist for a component is based outside the UAE, the lesson is still one-to-one over live video and we say upfront where the tutor is. No competitor page we examined in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without mentioning it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-safa.closingHeading: Get the component breakdown, then book a trial
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-safa.closingBody: One request to your child's school changes everything that follows: ask for the mock results broken down by component rather than as a grade. With that in hand you will usually be able to name the paper or the Internal Assessment that is costing the marks, and a block of tutoring becomes a narrow, finishable piece of work instead of a vague commitment. Then book a free trial lesson on a past-paper question from that component and watch whether the tutor can explain the gap between your child's answer and the mark scheme. Lessons run online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, around the Al Safa school run.

intro.heading: The Al Satwa timetable problem, stated honestly
paragraphs: Al Satwa has almost no international school inside it. That single fact shapes everything about tutoring here. Families living between Satwa roundabout and 2nd December Street commute outward every morning, to Jumeirah, to Al Safa, to Oud Metha, to Al Sufouh, and then back again in the afternoon. By the time a child is through the door, changed and fed, the usable study window is narrower than in almost any other part of old Dubai.

That is why the search is for a home tutor. It is not a preference for a particular pedagogy. It is an attempt to remove one journey from a day that already contains two. The logic is sound, and it is worth saying plainly that online delivery removes the same journey more reliably, because a tutor crossing Dubai at 16:00 is subject to exactly the traffic the family just sat in, and arrives late for the same reasons.

The second thing Al Satwa families run into is the shape of the IB Diploma itself. Internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service do not arrive evenly. They cluster. A student can coast for six weeks and then face three internal deadlines in ten days, and the week that breaks is usually the week the family discovers their tutoring arrangement has no flexibility in it.

So this page is built around time rather than around a list of subjects. It names the schools Al Satwa children actually attend and when those schools finish. It sets out which slots in the week work and which do not. It gives the market's published dirham rates for both online and in-home provision so you can see what the travel premium costs. It covers Ramadan and the UAE term calendar, because revision timing shifts with both. And it explains the permit position, because a parent hiring privately in the UAE is entitled to know what the law requires of the person they are hiring.

On delivery: IB Gram teaches Al Satwa students one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen and a tutor matched on the subject rather than on geography. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and the pages for every other country we serve say the same. For an IB Diploma subject at Higher Level that constraint matters less than it sounds, because the specialist you need for Physics Paper 3 or Economics Paper 2 is unlikely to be the person with a free afternoon near Satwa roundabout. The rest of this page is written to let you price that trade yourself rather than take our word for it, which is why the market's own published rates appear in full further down, each attributed to the provider that published them, and why the school-finish table gives the times as they are rather than as a timetable claims.
