dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-satwa.programmesIntro: An Al Satwa family may be in any of the three IB programmes, and the timetable pressure differs sharply between them. Below is what each programme demands of an evening, which is the practical question when you are choosing a slot.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment is largely external, with one internal assessment per subject. The workload is not evenly distributed across the two years; it concentrates into deadline clusters, and those clusters are what determine how much tutoring a student needs in any given month.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools sit the May session, which places the heaviest internal deadlines in the preceding autumn and winter terms. For an Al Satwa family that means the squeeze lands in the same months as the shortest usable evenings, since winter after-school activity schedules in Dubai are fuller than summer ones. Booking a fixed weekly slot from September is worth more than reacting in January.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria each, marked nought to eight. Work is continuous rather than terminal, so the demand on an evening is steadier and lower than the Diploma's. Year 5 adds the Personal Project and, in schools that enter it, externally validated on-screen assessment. Shorter and more frequent sessions suit this programme better than long blocks.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools within the Al Satwa commute run the Middle Years Programme, including continuum campuses that take students straight through from the Primary Years Programme. Because schools design their own units, the task sheet in your child's bag is the reference point rather than any generic scheme, and the fortnightly rhythm of those tasks sets the useful session frequency.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry without formal grades, closing with the Exhibition in the final year. Demand for tutoring is lowest here and is usually about reading fluency, number confidence or settling a child who has arrived from a different system mid-year. Thirty to forty-five minutes is the right length, and it must happen before the child is tired.
programmes.countryNote: For primary-age children in Al Satwa the school run is the whole constraint, because a tired seven-year-old cannot use a 19:00 slot. Weekend mornings work far better than weekday evenings at this age, and most families in this part of Dubai settle on a Saturday morning once they have tried both.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-satwa.subjectsIntro: Demand from Al Satwa concentrates in the Diploma subjects where the internal assessment and the final papers pull in different directions. Below is what each one asks for and the sort of session length it needs.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with a Paper 1 sat without a calculator at both levels. Students lose marks on method presentation rather than on answers. Needs a full hour minimum, because a problem set cannot be worked through in thirty minutes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with graphical calculator work assessed throughout. The exploration carries a substantial share of the grade and is where most of the tutoring time goes. Better suited to fortnightly longer sessions than weekly short ones.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, fields and, at Higher Level, a heavier quantitative load. Paper 3 rewards experimental technique and data analysis that classroom time rarely covers properly. Students need to work problems live rather than watch them worked, which makes a shared screen essential.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity, with organic mechanisms the recurring obstacle. Marks are lost on state symbols, significant figures and incomplete explanations of why rather than what. Short regular sessions beat long infrequent ones in this subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy recall alongside data analysis and experimental design. The internal assessment demands a genuinely independent investigation, and students tend to choose topics that cannot generate enough data. Early topic conversations save months.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, real-world examples and evaluation under timed conditions. The internal assessment commentaries must each use a recent news article and apply a specific part of the syllabus, which is a skill separate from understanding the economics.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis across literary and non-literary forms, plus the individual oral and, at Higher Level, the essay. Students who read well still lose marks on structuring an argument to a question rather than summarising a text.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, frameworks and case-study application, with a research project at Higher Level built on a real organisation. The common failure is description where evaluation was asked for, which is a command-term habit that can be trained quickly.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, both assessed on the quality of knowledge questions rather than on content. Students with strong subject grades often score poorly here because the mode of thinking is unfamiliar and unpractised.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent research essay in one subject, supervised at school. Tutoring is process coaching only: narrowing a research question, planning a method, reading a draft the student has written. The writing has to be theirs for the work to be submissible.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Al Satwa can and cannot be
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Satwa, as the market offers it, is an independent tutor or agency-supplied teacher who drives to your building, teaches for an hour or two and leaves. In this part of Dubai that model has specific problems. Parking around Satwa roundabout and along 2nd December Street is tight, the afternoon traffic a tutor must cross is the same traffic the family has just sat in, and the hour is billed from the agreed start time whether or not the tutor arrived on it.

There is also a selection problem that families discover second. The pool of people willing to drive to Al Satwa for a single hour on a weekday afternoon is small, and it is not selected for subject expertise. If your child needs Physics at Higher Level, or Economics Paper 2 evaluation, or help structuring a Mathematics exploration, the binding constraint is finding someone who has taught that component to that level. Geography narrows that pool hard, and the narrower it gets the more likely you are offered a generalist.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. That is a limit, stated plainly, and not a negotiation: home visits are a service we run only in India. Al Satwa students are taught one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen so working is written and seen rather than described, and with a tutor matched on the subject and level your child is sitting. The honest comparison is in the table further down this page, with the market's own published rates in both columns, so you can see what the travel premium costs and decide for yourself.

sections.heading: The Al Satwa school run: where children actually go and when they get back
paragraphs: Al Satwa itself holds very little international schooling, so the question of when tutoring can start is really a question about somebody else's postcode. The table below sets out the schools Al Satwa families most commonly commute to, the programmes they run, the broad weekday finish and the earliest point at which a child is realistically ready to work. The finish times are the published school day rather than the moment a car leaves the gate, which in Dubai are different things by fifteen to twenty-five minutes.

Two patterns show up immediately. Westward commutes to Jumeirah and Al Safa are short in distance and slow in practice, because Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road absorb every school in the strip at the same moment. Eastward commutes to Oud Metha and Bur Dubai are longer but move more predictably once past Al Mina Road. The result is that a Jumeirah family and an Oud Metha family can both be home at 16:10 having travelled very different distances.

The practical rule that emerges is this: a 16:00 weekday session is a bad idea for almost every Al Satwa family, and a 17:30 or later session is fine for nearly all of them. Families who book the earlier slot do it because it looks tidier on paper, and then spend a term rescheduling. Booking honestly against the table below is worth more than any amount of flexibility promised afterwards, because a rescheduled lesson is rarely a rescheduled lesson; it is usually a cancelled one.

sections.heading: Why the 16:00 slot fails here and the 18:30 slot works
paragraphs: The 16:00 weekday slot is the one families ask for and the one that collapses. The reason is not traffic alone. It is that 16:00 sits inside the handover, the twenty minutes where a child is out of uniform, looking for food and still carrying the school day. A lesson placed there spends its first fifteen minutes on logistics and its last fifteen on a student who has not eaten since 11:30. The parent paid for sixty minutes and received thirty of attention.

The 18:30 slot works because everything else has already happened. Dinner is done, the bag is unpacked, and the student arrives with a specific question rather than a vague tiredness. For Diploma students in particular this is the first point in the day where sustained work on a problem set or a draft is genuinely possible. The 19:30 slot works equally well for families commuting from Oud Metha or Al Qusais, and is the normal choice for households where a parent is also getting home from Business Bay or DIFC.

There are two exceptions worth naming. Primary-age children cannot use a 19:00 slot, however convenient it is for the adults, because the attention is gone. Weekend mornings are the right answer for them, and also for any internal assessment or Extended Essay work at Diploma level, where ninety uninterrupted minutes achieves more than three rushed weeknight hours. The second exception is the deadline cluster, where a student genuinely needs extra contact for three weeks and then does not need it again until the next cluster.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or group: what each costs from Al Satwa
paragraphs: The cheapest way to see what the travel premium is worth is to put the published rates side by side. Budget online provision in this market advertises from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to AED 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one, travel included, is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's Dubai figures at AED 180 to AED 350. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

Set against those hourly figures, the monthly view is what a household actually plans with. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for one weekly hour give AED 240 to AED 600 at budget level, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to beyond AED 2,000 for specialist examination-year support. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. The in-home package is roughly double the online one for the same number of contact hours.

What that doubling buys, in Al Satwa specifically, is a tutor's travel time across a congested city at the worst hour of the day, plus a candidate pool restricted to people prepared to make that trip. It does not buy more subject expertise, and in a narrow component like Physics Paper 3 or a Mathematics exploration it frequently buys less. Every figure quoted here is a market rate published by the provider named, not an IB Gram price. Our arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and the quote follows the subject and the level.

sections.heading: Fitting the Diploma week around the school run
paragraphs: The Diploma does not generate steady weekly homework in the way a British Year 11 does. It generates clusters. Internal assessments across six subjects, the Extended Essay draft stages, Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay deadlines, and Creativity, Activity, Service reflections are each set by the school on its own calendar, and three of them will land in the same fortnight at least twice a year. A tutoring schedule built for the average week will fail in those fortnights.

The sensible structure for an Al Satwa family is a light permanent spine plus planned surges. One fixed weekly slot in the subject that most needs it, a weekend block when internal assessment work is live, and extra sessions booked in advance for the weeks the school's published deadline list already identifies. That costs less across a year than a heavy standing schedule and covers the moments that actually matter. It also means the family is not paying for contact hours in the quiet weeks of February when a Diploma Year 2 student is mostly working through past papers alone, which is the period when standing schedules get cancelled and then quietly abandoned.

The table below is a worked week for a Diploma Year 2 student commuting to Jumeirah, with a Mathematics exploration in progress. It is not a prescription; it is an illustration of what fits once the school run is taken seriously. Note that nothing sits before 17:00 on a weekday and that the longest piece of work happens on a weekend morning, which is the pattern nearly every family in this area arrives at independently after a term of trying something tidier.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and the UAE term calendar
paragraphs: Tutoring schedules in the UAE have to bend twice a year, and both bends are predictable. During Ramadan school hours shorten, working hours shorten, and family routines move around iftar. The practical effect on tutoring is that the useful slot moves from early evening to after iftar, often as late as 21:00, and that attention in the late afternoon drops substantially for fasting students. Families who move their slot a week before Ramadan rather than a week into it lose nothing.

The second bend is the shape of the UAE academic year itself. The long summer break is longer than in the United Kingdom, winter and spring breaks land at different points from European terms, and Dubai families travel heavily in both. A Diploma student with an internal assessment due in January and three weeks abroad in December has a problem that is obvious in October and insoluble in January. Sessions during travel work when they are planned, because online delivery follows the student, which is the one logistical advantage that is genuinely unanswerable.

Daily prayer times matter for scheduling too, and the accommodation is simple: avoid slots that collide with Maghrib, which shifts through the year, and confirm the preferred band at the start of each term rather than assuming last term's slot still works. Al Satwa households are more likely than most in Dubai to want this considered, and it is a thirty-second conversation that prevents a term of awkward rescheduling.
bullets: Move the slot before Ramadan starts, not after it has begun
Post-iftar sessions are the productive ones for fasting students

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to teach your child privately in the UAE
paragraphs: A parent hiring privately in Dubai is entitled to know what the law asks of the person they are hiring, and the answer is specific. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone quoting you a permit fee has misunderstood something. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, available through its smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

Eligibility is broader than families expect. The permit covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. What matters more than the category is the condition attached: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. The ministry has not published a fine schedule, so any specific amount circulating online is unverified and should be treated as such.

There is one further boundary worth knowing. In Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK before relying on it. The reason it matters in Dubai is that families sometimes ask for their child's own classroom teacher privately, and that is the one arrangement to avoid.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the deadline is tomorrow
paragraphs: The Diploma's internal assessments and the Extended Essay must be the student's own work, and the pressure point is exactly the moment a family is most tempted. A draft is due, the student is behind, and a tutor is in the room. The line a tutor must hold is that they can read what the student has written, ask what a paragraph is trying to do, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the data, and teach the skill again on a different example. They cannot supply sentences, restructure the piece into its final form, or add the sources the student did not find.

This market makes that line harder to hold than it should be, because pages in this niche openly advertise completed Internal Assessments for a fee. That is an academic-integrity breach, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the provider. An Al Satwa family under deadline pressure deserves to hear the distinction clearly rather than to be sold a convenient alternative, and the test to apply is simple: could the arrangement be described to the school supervisor without discomfort?

The practical version, on a Saturday morning with a draft due Monday, looks like this. The tutor reads the draft cold. They ask four or five questions about the parts that are not doing their job. The student takes notes, and then writes the revision themselves during Sunday. That sequence is slower than having the problem fixed in the session, and it is the only sequence that leaves a student able to do the same thing unaided in the final examination series.

faqs.question: Can I get a home tutor who comes to our apartment in Al Satwa?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Independent tutors and local agencies do provide them, at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel. Before booking one in Al Satwa, consider the two practical problems: parking near Satwa roundabout and along 2nd December Street is tight, and a tutor crossing Dubai at pick-up hour is subject to the same traffic you just sat in. Our lessons run one-to-one over live video instead.

faqs.question: What time should an Al Satwa family book an IB session for?
faqs.answer: On a weekday, 18:30 or 19:30. Al Satwa has little schooling inside it, so almost every family commutes outward and back, and a 16:00 start lands inside the handover when a child is changing, eating and still carrying the school day. Families commuting from Jumeirah or Al Safa can sometimes hold 17:00. Families commuting from Oud Metha, Al Qusais or Al Sufouh should assume 18:00 at the earliest. Primary-age children do better on a weekend morning, whatever the weekday convenience.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring really as effective for an IB student as someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For Diploma subjects the evidence that matters is whether the tutor has taught the specific component. A shared screen lets a problem be worked jointly, a draft annotated live and a mark scheme read side by side, which covers most of what physical presence provides. What online delivery adds is access to a specialist in a narrow component rather than whoever is willing to drive to your area on a Tuesday. For a primary-age child, presence matters more, and that is worth saying honestly.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an IB Diploma student usually need?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one, in the subject causing the most trouble, and that is usually right. The Diploma generates work in clusters rather than evenly, so the better structure is a single weekly slot plus extra sessions booked in advance for the fortnights when several internal deadlines land together. Two permanent weekly slots in different subjects make sense for a student carrying two Higher Level subjects they are struggling with, but adding hours before diagnosing which component is failing tends to produce cost without movement.

faqs.question: What does IB tutoring cost per hour in Dubai, and who publishes those rates?
faqs.answer: Published market rates split into tiers. Budget online runs AED 45 to AED 150, with EdFlik listing AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to AED 300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500, Bestimate giving AED 180 to AED 350. Specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270, with premium examiner-led provision at AED 650 from BartyED. Those are market figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Do tutoring times change during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They move later. School and working hours shorten, routines organise around iftar, and the productive window for a fasting student shifts to after the meal, often as late as 21:00. Late-afternoon attention drops noticeably. The advice we give Al Satwa families is to change the slot in the week before Ramadan rather than a week into it, because a slot that stops working is usually abandoned rather than adjusted. Prayer times should also be checked against the chosen band each term, since Maghrib moves through the year.

faqs.question: Can we keep sessions going while we travel over the winter break?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the one logistical advantage of online delivery that has no counter-argument. Lessons follow the student, so a Diploma Year 2 student with an internal assessment due in January can keep working through three weeks abroad in December. What makes it work is planning in October rather than improvising in December: agree which sessions run, at what local time, and what the student will have produced before the family returns. Time-zone changes need confirming in writing, not assuming.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a licence, and is there a fee?
faqs.answer: They need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone quoting you a permit fee is mistaken. Applications go through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service via its smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: My child's internal assessment is due in ten days and nothing is written. What can a tutor actually do?
faqs.answer: Teach, question and give feedback on what the student produces, which in ten days is still a great deal. A realistic sequence is one longer session to narrow the scope to something the available data can support, a second to read a rough draft and ask what each section is failing to do, and a third to check the structure before submission. What a tutor cannot do is write any part of it, restructure it into its final shape, or supply sources the student did not find, because the work must be the student's own.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools do Al Satwa children usually attend?
faqs.answer: Mainly schools in Jumeirah, Al Safa, Al Sufouh and Oud Metha, since Al Satwa holds very little international provision itself. The westward run reaches IB continuum campuses and long-established British-curriculum schools; the eastward run reaches Oud Metha's Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools. Finish times across both clusters land roughly between 14:30 and 15:20, with arrival home typically fifteen to twenty-five minutes later than the bell. Those two numbers together are what determine which tutoring slot will survive a full term.

faqs.question: Do you teach Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay as well as subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, as process coaching rather than content delivery. Theory of Knowledge is assessed on the quality of knowledge questions rather than on knowing things, so the work is practising how to frame and test a claim, usually in ninety-minute blocks rather than hourly slots. The Extended Essay work is narrowing a research question until it is answerable, planning a method, and reading drafts the student has written. In both cases the school supervisor signs off the process, and a tutor's involvement should be describable to them without discomfort.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We say so. For a narrow component at Higher Level the honest answer is sometimes that nobody suitable is available at 18:30 on a Tuesday, and the choices are a different band, a different day or a wait. Offering a generalist into a specialist slot is how families end up paying for a term and seeing no movement, so we do not do it. Where coverage is genuinely thin, we say what the realistic wait is and what the alternative band would be, before any trial lesson is booked.

faqs.question: Is a small group cheaper than one-to-one, and is it worth it?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per student, and it is worth it for a narrow set of cases: content revision where every student in the group sits the same paper at the same level and is at a similar stage. It stops being worth it as soon as the students diverge, because the pace follows the group rather than your child. For internal assessment work, Extended Essay process coaching or a specific weakness in one component, group format does not work at all, and the saving is illusory.

faqs.question: How will I know whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: By looking at the thing that was supposed to change. At the start we name a specific weakness, in a specific component, and what evidence would show movement: marks on a particular paper section, a draft that no longer needs restructuring, a problem type the student can now start unaided. A written note after each session records what was covered. If the named evidence has not appeared after six to eight sessions, the diagnosis or the match was wrong, and we change one of those rather than adding hours.

It is which school the child attends and when the car actually leaves the gate, because that decides whether 17:00, 18:30 or a Saturday morning is the slot that will still be running in March. intro.heading: The one neighbourhood where proximity is actually on the table
paragraphs: Most pages about home tutoring in Dubai are written for families who live some distance from where the teaching happens. Al Sufouh is the exception. The strip between Sheikh Zayed Road and the coast holds school campuses, Dubai Knowledge Park, Internet City and Media City within a few minutes of each other, which means the people who teach IB subjects in this city are often working inside your own postcode. If the argument for an in-home tutor were ever going to hold anywhere, it would hold here.

So this page takes the argument seriously rather than dismissing it. It sets out what living in the school district genuinely solves - short journeys, teachers nearby, a parent who may well work three minutes from the gate - and then explains why none of those things is what decides a Diploma grade. The honest answer is that proximity solves logistics and the Diploma is not a logistics problem. It is a problem of six subjects, three Higher Level, two years of internal deadlines, and an Internal Assessment in nearly every subject that most students leave in a mediocre band because nobody showed them the criteria.

IB Gram's position does not change for this neighbourhood: tuition into Al Sufouh is delivered one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer in India only. In an area where in-home tuition is plainly practical, that deserves a reason rather than a policy statement, and the reason is in the comparison table further down. In short, the specialist you need for Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches is unlikely to be the specialist who happens to live in Knowledge Park, and the Diploma does not reward settling.

The rest of the page is built around the Al Sufouh afternoon and the Diploma year. There is the gate-by-gate timing picture including the tram and the Media City working parent, a comparison of delivery models with the published rates attached, the Diploma year counted from internal deadlines rather than from exam dates - which is the calendar that actually governs a DP student's life - the Internal Assessment arithmetic per subject, and the regulatory position stated plainly.

One framing note. International Baccalaureate schools account for 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, in a market of 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula. Al Sufouh is one of the places where that 7% is concentrated, which means local IB knowledge here is better than almost anywhere in the emirate - and still thin for any specific Higher Level subject in any specific week. Al Sufouh therefore makes a useful test case for the whole argument. If the nearest-tutor approach were going to work anywhere in the UAE it would work on this strip, and the families who have tried it here are the ones who report the same outcome as families forty minutes away: a pleasant, competent tutor, a term of sessions, and a predicted grade that did not move because nobody ever identified which component was costing the points.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-sufouh.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma subjects most requested from Al Sufouh, with the component structure that determines where a grade is won or lost. Use them to test any tutor you speak to, including ours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At SL the two papers carry 40% each with the Internal Assessment at 20%. At HL there are three papers at 30%, 30% and 20% plus the IA at 20%. Paper 3 at HL is an extended investigation unlike anything in the textbook and is the component HL students most consistently under-prepare.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and technology-led, with the same component pattern. The AA or AI decision affects university prerequisites for engineering, economics and some science courses, so check the target course rather than relying on a school's default recommendation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 at 36% with a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, Paper 2 at 44%, Internal Assessment at 20%. Organic mechanisms and energetics calculations are the predictable Higher Level losses, and the IA is where the most marks are recoverable by legitimate coaching.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44%, Internal Assessment at 20%. Marks go missing less on the physics than on extended written answers where a chain of reasoning has to be visible, and on uncertainty handling in the practical write-up.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The heaviest content load of the three sciences on the same 36, 44 and 20 split. Command words decide grades: outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each demand a different structure, and a correct fact in the wrong structure earns nothing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: At SL Paper 1 is 30%, Paper 2 is 40% and the Internal Assessment portfolio is 30%. At HL a quantitative third paper carrying 30% joins Papers 1 and 2 with the IA at 20%. The portfolio of commentaries on real news articles is where organised students gain the most ground.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: At SL the two papers carry 35% each with the Individual Oral at 30%. At HL Paper 1 is 35%, Paper 2 is 25%, the HL Essay is 20% and the Individual Oral is 20%. The HL Essay is a formal written task and a frequent source of academic-honesty confusion.

subjects.name: Business Management and Psychology
subjects.description: Both carry substantial internally assessed components and both reward structured evaluation over content recall. They are also the subjects where a student who writes everything they know most reliably sits in the middle bands with full knowledge of the course.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through the exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, contributing to the core points on the 45-point scale with the Extended Essay. Tutoring here is argument construction and precise use of real-world examples; the essay must be entirely the student's own work.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay in a chosen subject, supervised at school. A tutor may teach research method, question formulation, structure and referencing and may ask the questions a supervisor will ask. A tutor may not research it, draft it, rewrite it or edit it into shape.

sections.heading: What living in the school district actually solves
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Sufouh is a reasonable thing to want, and the usual objections to in-home tuition carry less weight here than anywhere else in Dubai. The journeys are short. The teaching population is local, because the campuses and Knowledge Park are local. A parent working in Media City or Internet City can be home before a 5pm session starts. None of that is imaginary, and a page that pretended otherwise would not be worth reading.

What it solves is logistics. A tutor arriving at an Al Sufouh address is not fighting Al Khail Road for fifty minutes, so the session is likelier to start on time than the same arrangement in a far suburb. The cost of the travel premium is also easier to justify when the travel is five minutes rather than forty-five. For a family that specifically wants a person in the room - a younger child, a student who will not work without supervision - this neighbourhood makes that choice practical rather than aspirational.

What it does not solve is the Diploma. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay, an Internal Assessment in nearly every subject and two years of internal deadlines are not a scheduling problem. They are a problem of knowing which component is costing the grade and what the criteria for it actually say. The person best placed to answer that for Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches is whoever has taught the component repeatedly, and the chance that they also live within five minutes of your villa is a coincidence, not a plan.

That is the whole of the reason IB Gram delivers into Al Sufouh over live video rather than in person. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. In a district where in-home tuition is genuinely feasible, the honest case has to be made on merit rather than on necessity, and the comparison in the next section is where it is made.

sections.heading: The Al Sufouh afternoon: gates, the tram and the working parent
paragraphs: The timing picture here is better than in most of Dubai and still narrower than families expect. Secondary year groups across the Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Marina corridor release between roughly 2:45pm and 3:30pm. Al Sufouh Road and the tram take the local traffic; Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road take everyone travelling inland. A student living in Al Sufouh and attending an Al Sufouh gate is home within fifteen minutes. A student living in Al Sufouh and attending an Al Barsha or Emirates Hills gate is not.

The second variable is the working parent, and it is more relevant here than elsewhere because so many Al Sufouh households work inside the same few square kilometres. Knowledge Park, Internet City and Media City finish later than the schools, which produces the common local pattern: a child home by 3:30pm with a nanny or alone, a parent back between 5:30pm and 6:30pm, and a window in between that is either used well or lost entirely. A session placed inside that window is supervised by the arrangement itself, which is one of the few genuinely useful scheduling observations for this neighbourhood.

The third is the Diploma's own calendar, which eats evenings in bursts rather than evenly. Creativity, Activity, Service commitments take one or two. Internal Assessment draft deadlines cluster. Mock weeks remove everything. A tutoring plan that assumes a stable weekly hour across two years will survive the first term and then collapse, which is why the sensible arrangement here is a fixed slot plus explicit permission to pause for a named week rather than a vague promise of flexibility.

The table below gives the pattern by gate cluster. Times are ordinary-day observations rather than published bell times - check your own school - but the shape holds, and the recommendation for most Al Sufouh Diploma students is a 4:45pm or 5:00pm start, before the parent is home and before the evening fills.

sections.heading: Home tutor or online, in a district where both are possible
paragraphs: This is the comparison that matters in Al Sufouh, because both options are real. Published Dubai rates for an in-home one-to-one visit with travel included run AED 180-500 an hour, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200-500. A qualified subject tutor working online runs AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists sit at AED 200-450 and upwards, TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500-650, BartyED publishing AED 650. Budget online starts at AED 33-52 from Tutopiya and AED 45-65 from EdFlik.

In most of Dubai the in-home premium is mostly mileage. In Al Sufouh it is less so, which changes the arithmetic honestly in favour of the in-home option on cost grounds - a five-minute journey does not justify the same premium as a forty-five minute one, and some local tutors price accordingly. What does not change is selection. Requiring the tutor to be within a short drive means choosing from the people who are both qualified in your subject at your level and available in your slot and nearby. For Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches in the weeks before the May session, that intersection is frequently empty even here.

The second thing that does not change is what the money buys. The in-home band overlaps the online specialist band across almost its whole range, so the premium is not purchasing a different quality of teaching. It purchases presence, which is worth paying for in specific cases: a student who will not sit down without an adult there, a younger child whose attention over video is short, or a household with poor bandwidth. For a Diploma student working on an Internal Assessment draft or a Paper 3 technique, presence adds nothing a shared screen does not provide, and a shared screen is a better way to annotate a draft than reading it upside down.

All figures above are other providers' published rates read during the October 2026 research round, quoted as market context rather than as an IB Gram price list. For context on the household budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private-school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Tutoring is the uncapped part of that budget, which is a reason to buy it by component diagnosis rather than by the hour.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted from internal deadlines, not exam dates
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in this market that mentions the calendar mentions exams. That is the wrong calendar for a Diploma student. The dates that govern two years of a DP student's life are set by the school: first draft of the Internal Assessment, final IA submission, Extended Essay research question approval, Extended Essay interim and final drafts, the reflection sessions, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay deadlines, mock weeks, and the predicted-grade point that determines university offers. Those deadlines arrive in clusters and they are the ones a student actually misses.

This page publishes no IB session or results dates, deliberately. UAE schools sit the May session, and ibo.org or your school's IB coordinator are the only places to confirm specifics. Several pages in this market quote IB dates from secondary sources with confidence they have not earned, and a date a parent plans around is not a detail to approximate. What can be said safely is the structure: internal deadlines come months before external assessment, coursework is finished long before papers are sat, and a student who hits the internal calendar has a far easier final term than one who does not.

The practical planning consequence for an Al Sufouh family is to build the tutoring arrangement around the school's internal calendar rather than around a generic revision timeline. Ask the coordinator for the year's deadline list at the start of DP1 and put it on a wall. Then place tutoring where it is useful: Internal Assessment coaching in the weeks before a draft deadline, component work after mocks when the diagnosis is fresh, and nothing at all in the week a major submission is due, because adding a session to that week makes things worse.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks are actually recoverable
paragraphs: A Diploma grade is made of parts, and the parts are not equally recoverable at any given moment. The Internal Assessment is the most recoverable, because it carries around a fifth of most subject grades and remains in the student's hands until the submission deadline. A student predicted a 5 in a Higher Level science with an Internal Assessment sitting in a low band is carrying a capped grade regardless of how well the papers go, and that cap can be lifted by legitimate coaching on the criteria. That is the first place to look, always.

The second is the component that is unlike the rest of the course. Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3 at 20% is an extended investigation rather than a set of questions. The Higher Level Essay in English Language and Literature at 20% is a formal written task. Higher Level Economics Paper 3 at 30% is quantitative. Higher Level History Paper 3 demands regional depth beyond Paper 2's breadth. Students arrive at these with no practice because they do not resemble what they have been doing, and a short component block often moves more than a term of general subject work.

The third is command-word and structure discipline on the main papers, which transfers across subjects. A student who learns how an extended-response mark scheme awards points gains on every subsequent question of that type in every subject. This is the cheapest improvement available in the Diploma and it is almost never bought deliberately, because it does not sound like a subject.

What is not recoverable late is content never learned, and the honest service at that point is triage rather than rescue. Eight weeks before external assessment, a student with large content gaps is better served by securing the topics with the heaviest mark allocation and the Internal Assessment marks already banked than by attempting the whole syllabus. A provider who promises otherwise is selling reassurance. We would rather say which marks are reachable and work on those.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and what "approved" cannot mean
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map for UAE private schools, and ADEK in particular is named by almost nobody in this market.

KHDA regulates schools, inspects them annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises - a permit requiring initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. It is a licence for an organisation with a physical location. No individual online tutor holds it, and the phrase KHDA-approved tutor is the single most misleading claim available in this market.

The permit that applies to individual tutoring is MoHRE's. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any amount circulating online is unverified.

One further rule shapes who you should not hire. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify it against current policy, but the direction is unambiguous, and in a district like Al Sufouh where teachers and families live side by side it is worth knowing. IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and holds none.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Sufouh, and what we will not do
paragraphs: Send four things: the subject, the level, the current predicted grade and where the Internal Assessment stands. Add a marked paper if you have one and the school's internal deadline list if you can get it. From those we can tell you whether the useful purchase is subject teaching, Internal Assessment coaching or a component block, and those are three different jobs rather than three sizes of the same one.

Then: we match on subject and level, you take a full-length trial lesson at no cost with your child's own work on screen, and you decide. Sessions run weekly in Gulf Standard Time, usually 4:30pm for a student at an Al Sufouh gate and 5:00pm or later for one commuting back from Al Barsha or Emirates Hills. Timings move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan. Sessions pause in the week a major submission is due, which should be in the plan from the start rather than negotiated each time.

The disclosure. Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches in the run-up to the May session is the hardest request in the set to fill. Some group-two languages, Theatre, Music, Global Politics and Design Technology are thin year-round. A late request in a rare Higher Level subject may be answered with a waiting position rather than a tutor, and we will say so rather than place somebody learning the component alongside your child at specialist rates. No competitor page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all.

And the fixed limits. No home visits anywhere in the UAE - home visits are an India-only service, and in this district that is a choice we have explained rather than a constraint we are hiding. No claimed approval or partnership from any regulator or examination board. No writing, drafting, rewriting or editing of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed work. No supplied or reproduced past papers, mark schemes or subject guides; we reference the official sources and work from your school's materials. No grade promises, and no statistics about our own results, because we cannot publish the sample, date and method that would make such a figure mean anything.

process.title: Get the school's deadline list
process.description: Ask the IB coordinator for the year's internal deadlines at the start of DP1: Internal Assessment drafts, Extended Essay milestones, mock weeks, predicted grades. That list governs the next two years far more than any external date, and almost no family requests it.

process.title: Send the four facts

process.description: One marked mock or past paper with the marks visible shows whether losses are content, structure, command words or timing. The grade looks identical in all four cases and the remedies are completely different, so this single document shortens diagnosis by weeks.

whyPoints.description: Al Sufouh is the one district in Dubai where a short local journey makes in-home tuition genuinely practical, so we show the published rates and name what presence buys and costs. The argument for online here rests on selection rather than on traffic.

whyPoints.title: Planning built on the school's internal calendar
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessment drafts, Extended Essay milestones and mock weeks are what a Diploma student actually misses. We build the arrangement around that list, including scheduled pauses, rather than around a generic revision timeline.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level together

whyPoints.title: Internal Assessment treated as the first place to look

faqs.question: We live in Al Sufouh, where tutors are local. Why would we choose online lessons?
faqs.answer: Because proximity solves logistics and the Diploma is not a logistics problem. Al Sufouh genuinely makes in-home tuition practical - campuses, Knowledge Park and Media City are minutes apart and local tutors price a five-minute journey differently from a forty-five minute one. But requiring the tutor to be nearby means choosing from whoever is qualified in your subject at your level, free in your slot and local. For Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches in the weeks before the session, that intersection is often empty even here. IB Gram delivers over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: Which internal deadlines should an Al Sufouh Diploma family actually be tracking?
faqs.answer: Ask the IB coordinator for the whole list at the start of DP1 and put it on a wall: Internal Assessment topic approval, IA first drafts, IA final submissions by subject, Extended Essay question approval, EE interim and final drafts, the reflection sessions, Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay deadlines, mock weeks and the predicted-grade point. Those are the dates students miss. External assessment dates matter far less day to day and should be confirmed with the coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taken from any tutoring page.

faqs.question: My child's Internal Assessment draft came back poorly. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: It is usually the most fixable thing on the list, which is why it is the first place to look. The Internal Assessment carries around a fifth of most Diploma subject grades and remains in the student's hands until the final submission. A low draft band is often a criteria problem rather than a capability problem - a research question too broad, a method not justified, data handled without an analysis plan, or a conclusion that overstates the evidence. A tutor may teach the criteria, question the design and show where the draft falls short. Every word of the rewrite must be the student's own.

faqs.question: Does the HL third component really need separate work?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because it does not resemble the rest of the course and it arrives late. Higher Level Mathematics adds a Paper 3 worth 20% that is an extended investigation rather than a set of exercises. Higher Level English Language and Literature adds an HL Essay worth 20%, a formal written task on a studied text. Higher Level Economics adds a quantitative Paper 3 worth 30%. Students who are competent across the shared content arrive at these components with no practice at all, and a block of two to six focused sessions often returns more than a term of general subject tuition.

faqs.question: How early in the afternoon can a session start if our gate is in Al Sufouh itself?
faqs.answer: 4:30pm is realistic, which is earlier than almost anywhere else in Dubai. Al Sufouh gates release secondary year groups roughly between 2:50pm and 3:20pm, and a student living in the same district is home within fifteen minutes, often by 3:20pm. Allow for changing and food and the window opens at about 4:30pm. If your child attends an Al Barsha or Emirates Hills gate instead, the return leg pushes that to 5:00pm or 5:15pm. A session placed before a working parent gets back from Knowledge Park or Media City is also supervised by the arrangement itself.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying a local Al Sufouh tutor the in-home premium?
faqs.answer: Only if presence is the thing you need. The premium is smaller here than elsewhere because the journey is short, which is an honest point in its favour. But published Dubai in-home rates of AED 180-500 an hour overlap the online specialist band of AED 200-450 almost entirely, so the money is not buying different teaching quality. Presence is genuinely worth paying for in three cases: a student who will not work without an adult in the room, a younger child whose attention over video is short, or a household with unreliable bandwidth. For Internal Assessment or Paper 3 work it adds nothing a shared screen does not.

faqs.question: What should we ask a Diploma tutor before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things. What is each component worth at my child's level - a specialist gives the percentages without hesitating. What is the Internal Assessment worth and what are its criteria. What exactly will you do and not do on that Internal Assessment - the boundary should be stated before you ask. And what do you need from us before lesson one - the right answer is a marked paper and the school's deadline list. A tutor who wants nothing in advance intends to teach a generic scheme, which is competent work aimed at the wrong target.

faqs.question: Can a tutor be IB accredited or IB certified?
faqs.answer: No. The IB authorises schools to deliver its programmes and does not approve, accredit or certify private tutors or tutoring companies. Nor do KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Education approve individual tutors. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, which requires initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the steps and annual renewal at least 30 days before expiry. The permit relevant to an individual tutor is MoHRE's private tuition work permit. IB Gram claims none of these and holds none of them.

faqs.question: We are eight weeks from external assessment. What is realistic now?
faqs.answer: Triage rather than coverage. In eight weeks a student can change paper technique, secure the topics carrying the heaviest mark allocation, and make sure every coursework mark already achievable is banked. What cannot happen is learning two years of content that was never learned. The honest plan names which marks are reachable and works on those, which usually means the Internal Assessment if it is still open, the highest-weighted paper, and command-word discipline that transfers across questions. A provider offering a full-syllabus rescue in eight weeks is selling reassurance rather than a plan.

faqs.question: Should the AA or AI Mathematics decision be made on the school's advice?
faqs.answer: Take the school's advice seriously and check it against the target university course yourself, because the two sometimes diverge. Analysis and Approaches is the more abstract and proof-oriented route; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and technology-led. Several engineering, economics and science courses specify one or the other, and a school recommending on the basis of current performance may not be optimising for an admissions requirement two years away. Where a student is capable of Analysis and Approaches but currently weak, a term of focused work in DP1 sometimes keeps a route open that would otherwise close.

faqs.question: How does a Creativity, Activity, Service commitment affect the tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: It removes an evening, usually permanently, and it should be designed into the plan rather than discovered. A commitment in Al Quoz, Al Barsha or the Marina takes the whole evening because of the double journey, not just the hours of the activity itself. The practical approach is to build around three usable weekday evenings rather than five, place the tutored session on the best of the three, and keep extended work - a full timed paper, a long Internal Assessment session - for a weekend morning when there is genuinely time for it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle two Diploma subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but the honest limit is two adjacent subjects at most. Chemistry and Physics share mathematical handling and practical write-up conventions. Economics and Business Management share evaluative structure. Mathematics and Physics share rearrangement and graph work. Beyond adjacency, a tutor claiming four Diploma subjects at Higher Level is claiming something improbable. In practice, a student whose problem is structure or command words rather than content is often lifted across several subjects by work in one, which is cheaper and more effective than multiple weekly sessions.

faqs.question: What would make you tell an Al Sufouh family not to book?
faqs.answer: Several things, and we would rather say them. A student who understands the content and is not doing the work needs supervision, which a weekly online hour does not provide - and in this district a local in-person arrangement genuinely might. A student weak across five subjects has a load or wellbeing problem that more sessions worsen. A single dip in a previously strong subject deserves one more data point before any spending. And a rare Higher Level subject requested weeks before the session, where we have nobody genuinely qualified, gets a no rather than a generalist at specialist rates.

faqs.question: Do you work with students at the schools in Al Sufouh and Knowledge Park?
faqs.answer: Students we support attend IB schools across the Al Sufouh, Marina and Al Barsha corridor, and tutors are matched by subject and level rather than by school. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership, endorsement or client relationship with any school or school group, and we would be wary of a provider implying otherwise - several in this market list dozens of schools as though they were clients. What actually matters at the first session is your child's marked work and the school's own deadline list, not a tutor's claimed familiarity with the gate.

faqs.question: How do we judge progress when the next external assessment is a year away?
faqs.answer: Component by component, against marked evidence, every six to eight weeks. Agree at the start which component is the target - the Internal Assessment band, Paper 2 extended responses, Paper 3 - and compare the same component before and after. A predicted grade can stay still while a component improves, which is still progress and worth continuing. If the target component has not moved after a full block, the sensible responses are a change of focus, a change of tutor, or stopping. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we will recommend it when it applies.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-sufouh.closingHeading: Buy the component, not the postcode
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-sufouh.closingBody: Al Sufouh gives you short journeys and local teaching staff, and neither of those decides a Diploma grade. What decides it is knowing which of six subjects and which component inside it is costing points, and whether the Internal Assessment is still recoverable. Get the school's internal deadline list, send the subject, the level, the predicted grade and the Internal Assessment stage, and take a free trial lesson on your child's own work. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, from 4:30pm for a local gate.

intro.heading: What does an IB home tutor in Al Twar really cost over a year?
paragraphs: Think in months rather than hours, because that is how the bill arrives. The Dubai market advertises in-home packages of four two-hour sessions at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month, and online packages of eight sessions at around AED 799. Bestimate's 2026 rate survey puts monthly spend on a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. For a Diploma student taking two subjects seriously through DP2, the realistic annual figure in this market sits in the tens of thousands of dirhams, and almost nobody plans it as an annual figure.

That matters in Al Twar specifically, because this is a villa district with household budgets already committed to school fees, and the tutoring line tends to accumulate by the hour rather than get decided once. A family that agrees to two hours a week at AED 250 in September has committed roughly AED 2,000 a month without ever seeing the number written down. The same budget, planned deliberately, buys a different and usually better shape: fewer, sharper hours on the subjects where marks actually move, plus a dated block before mocks.

The second thing worth knowing is where the in-home premium comes from. It is not a quality premium. A tutor driving to Al Twar from anywhere in central Dubai spends forty to sixty minutes in the car across an evening peak, and that time is paid for inside the hourly rate whether it appears as a line item or not. Published figures make the gap visible: Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500, against qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300. The difference is logistics, not teaching.

There is a third cost that never appears on an invoice: the restriction of the tutor pool. An in-home arrangement in Al Twar can only use tutors willing to drive to Al Twar at 6pm. For a Standard Level subject with plenty of supply that is a minor constraint. For Higher Level physics, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or an Extended Essay supervisor in a specific subject, it can mean paying a premium rate for the only person available rather than the right person. That is the most expensive mistake in this market and it is invisible on the receipt.

So the honest position. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Diploma and MYP tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the reason we make that trade is the one above: dropping the travel requirement removes the premium and removes the pool restriction at the same time. The free trial lesson lets you test whether the format works for your child before any money moves.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-twar.subjectsIntro: Not every subject repays the same rate. These are the ones Al Twar families ask for, with an honest note on where the money works hardest in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The highest-demand subject in this district and the one where specialist rates pay off soonest. Higher Level proof and calculus are where students fall behind irrecoverably if the first term of DP1 is left unaddressed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistically weighted, with a strong technology component. Often better value to tutor than Analysis and Approaches, because the marks lost are usually in interpretation and presentation rather than in deep technique.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Few facts, heavy technique. Most lost marks trace to unit handling, to rearranging an equation after substituting, and to skipping the diagram. All three are cheap to fix and expensive to ignore.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics sign conventions, equilibrium reasoning and organic mechanisms absorb the hours. The Scientific Investigation carries about a fifth of the grade and is the component families resource last.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and easy to revise inefficiently. The best return comes from data-based question practice rather than from re-reading notes, which is also the cheapest intervention available.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline and the internal assessment commentaries drive the grade. A handful of sessions on labelling and justifying a shift is worth more than a term of content review.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-driven and heavily dependent on applying tools to an unseen context. Students lose marks by describing a framework rather than using it, which is a technique fix rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay and the individual oral. The individual oral is routinely under-prepared and is one of the best-value targets for a short block of sessions.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive components each need separate practice. Families often buy generic Arabic tutoring when the gap is specifically in the interactive assessment.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the essay. Three or four sessions on framing a knowledge question properly tend to outperform a term of discussion, which makes it unusually cheap to support well.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Supervision is coaching on the student's own research. The single highest-value hour in the Diploma is the one that narrows an unanswerable question into an answerable one, and it comes early or not at all.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a developed solution, and scoping it realistically is where tutoring earns its fee. Over-ambitious projects are the standard failure and they cost a grade.

sections.heading: What Al Twar families pay per month, and for what
paragraphs: Monthly is the unit that makes sense, because it is the unit a household budget uses. The advertised packages in this market are clear enough to compare directly: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those two numbers buy the same total contact time in very different shapes, and they differ by roughly a factor of two in price. The in-home figure includes the tutor's travel across Dubai twice a week; the online figure does not include travel because there is none.

Underneath the packages, Bestimate's 2026 survey gives monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session: roughly AED 240 to 600 for budget tutoring, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A Diploma student in DP2 taking two subjects at the specialist band is therefore looking at somewhere between AED 2,000 and 4,000 a month on tutoring alone, which is a figure worth seeing in writing before the term starts rather than discovering in February.

The shape matters as much as the total. Eight shorter contact points across a month give a tutor eight chances to catch an error early; four long ones give four. In subjects where the learning happens in between, through practice, frequent shorter sessions outperform fewer longer ones at the same spend. The exception is coursework work, such as an internal assessment or an Extended Essay draft, where a longer uninterrupted block genuinely helps.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it quietly costs
paragraphs: The in-home premium is real and it is measurable. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 350 according to Bestimate, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. Qualified online subject tutors over the same period are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The gap between those bands is the cost of a car in Dubai traffic, paid by the hour, and in Al Twar it is not a small journey: the district sits behind Al Qusais, and a tutor coming from central Dubai at six in the evening is committing well over an hour of driving to deliver one hour of teaching.

What the premium genuinely buys is presence. A tutor in the room can see a seven-year-old stop concentrating, can take a pen out of their hand, and can be supervised by a parent in the next room. For a young child those things matter and are worth paying for. For a sixteen-year-old working through Higher Level calculus on a shared screen, they matter considerably less, and most of what the premium pays for is a benefit the student is not using.

What the premium quietly costs is choice. An in-home arrangement in Al Twar draws from the set of tutors willing to drive to Al Twar on a weekday evening, which is a much smaller set than the set of tutors who teach the subject. For a Standard Level humanity that is fine. For Higher Level physics, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or an Extended Essay supervisor in a specific discipline, the shortlist can collapse to one name, and a shortlist of one is the most expensive thing in tutoring. You end up paying a premium rate for availability rather than for expertise.

This is the whole argument for the online format, and it is an argument about value rather than about convenience. Removing the drive removes the premium and widens the pool in the same move. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For an Al Twar family the practical effect is that the tutor is selected for teaching the subject at the right level and then scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, rather than selected for geography and hoped to be right.

sections.heading: A two-year Diploma budget, phase by phase
paragraphs: Most families decide tutoring spend monthly and regret it annually. The better approach is to plan the two Diploma years as a whole and distribute the money where it does the most work, because the value of an hour is not constant across the programme. Three phases dominate: the first term of DP1, the internal assessment window from DP1 summer into DP2 autumn, and the final revision run before the examination series.

The first term of DP1 is the highest-value and lowest-spent phase. This is where a weak foundation in a Higher Level subject sets, and where a student who is quietly lost becomes a student who is permanently behind. A single weekly hour in the subject that is going wrong, started in October rather than in March, repeatedly costs less in total than the rescue operation it prevents. Families consistently underspend here because nothing has gone visibly wrong yet.

The internal assessment window is the second. In most subjects the internal assessment carries a meaningful share of the grade, and the work is produced to school deadlines over several months. Supervision here is questioning and feedback on the student's own work. It is also the phase families most often buy in a panic, at the most expensive rate available, in the final fortnight before a deadline, which is both the worst value and the point at which a tutor can legitimately do least.

The final revision run is the third, and it is the one most families already plan for. A dated block of eight to twelve sessions aimed at paper technique rather than content, scoped honestly against what is recoverable, is a defensible purchase. What is not defensible is a year of low-intensity, undirected weekly sessions in five subjects, which is how a household spends AED 40,000 across two years and arrives at the examination series with the same technique problems it started with.

sections.heading: Four ways Al Twar families waste IB tuition money
paragraphs: The first is paying specialist rates for supervision. A tutor at AED 300 an hour watching a student complete homework they could have completed alone is a babysitting arrangement priced as expertise. If the problem is that the work does not get done, the cheapest honest solution is a budget-tier tutor or a structured study routine, not a Higher Level subject specialist. Separating the two problems, will not and cannot, is the single most useful conversation to have before booking anything.

The second is buying five subjects at once. A Diploma student with six subjects and a household budget tends to end up with four or five low-intensity weekly sessions, none of which produces enough practice between lessons to change anything. The same money concentrated on one or two subjects, with the others left alone, consistently produces more. This is counter-intuitive and it is the advice families push back on hardest.

The third is the late internal assessment panic. A supervisor can do a great deal with an unanswerable research question three months out and very little with a nearly-finished draft three days out, because at that point the only remaining help would cross the academic-honesty line. We will not write, draft or complete any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay, and a service that offers to is selling your child a malpractice risk rather than a rescue. The money spent at that point buys almost nothing legitimate.

The fourth is paying the premium band at MYP level. A tutor priced for Diploma Higher Level work is not automatically better at MYP criterion coaching, and frequently has never marked an MYP task against a descriptor. For an MYP 3 or MYP 4 student the better purchase is a mid-band tutor with real MYP experience. Paying more here buys seniority rather than relevance, and it is the commonest overspend we see in villa districts like Al Twar.

sections.heading: Tutoring in the context of an Al Twar education budget
paragraphs: Tutoring is one line in a bigger number, and it is worth placing. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For an Al Twar household that means the largest education line is flat this year, which is precisely the moment to decide the second-largest line deliberately rather than by accumulation.

The wider market context is a sector still growing. Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26 per cent, US 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More IB provision means more IB students competing for the same specialist tutors, which is a supply argument for not relying on whoever lives nearby.

Against that, the tutoring decision should be sized honestly. If the household can commit roughly AED 1,000 a month to tutoring, the question is not which subject to spread it across but which single subject will repay it, and the answer is usually the Higher Level subject where the student is furthest from where they need to be. If the figure is AED 3,000, two subjects plus a core block is realistic. Deciding the figure first and the allocation second is the discipline that prevents the February surprise.
