sections.heading: Hidden extras, receipts and what to ask before paying a term up front
paragraphs: Several costs in this market do not appear in the headline rate. Ask whether the price is per hour or per lesson, because a fifty-minute lesson billed as an hour is a twenty per cent difference that compounds across a year. Ask what happens to a session cancelled with a day's notice, and what happens when the tutor cancels. Ask whether materials are included or billed, and whether marking time between sessions is charged. Each is a reasonable thing to charge for and an unreasonable thing to discover in month three.

Ask about VAT explicitly, and expect a straight answer about whether a quoted figure includes it. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as settled fact on this page, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than a tutoring company's opinion. What any provider can and should tell you is whether the number they quoted you is the number you pay. Get it in writing before the first invoice.

Be cautious about paying a term up front for a discount. The discount is real and so is the risk: the commonest failure in tutoring is a mismatch between tutor and student, and it reveals itself in weeks two to four. A family that has pre-paid twelve sessions will usually persist with a poor match rather than write off the balance, which costs far more than the discount saved. Our arrangement is a free trial lesson first and a change of tutor at no cost if the match is wrong, which addresses the same risk from the other direction.

Finally, ask about the permit, because it is free and therefore a pure honesty test. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. A tutor who tells you the permit is expensive, optional or unnecessary has told you something checkable and wrong. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific amount you are quoted.

sections.heading: What an Al Twar parent can establish free before any money moves
paragraphs: Three free checks will improve the purchase more than any amount of comparing websites. The first is the school. Your child's IB coordinator will confirm the subject levels, the internal assessment deadlines and the mock window, and will often tell you frankly which subject is the real problem. That is the diagnostic information a tutoring plan should be built on, and it costs an email. Families who skip it buy tutoring in the subject the student complains about rather than the subject that is costing the grade.

The second is the regulator. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes inspection outcomes on its own site. If your child attends school across the boundary in Sharjah, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education there and also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Read ratings from the regulator rather than from an agency page, including this one.

The third is the claim check, and it is the cheapest protection available. Nobody offering you private tutoring in Dubai is accredited, approved or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson to do it. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with physical premises, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such accreditation and occupies no UAE premises. If a provider claims regulator approval, ask for the permit number; the request is free and the answer is decisive.

Finally, use the free trial for what it is actually good for. Not for watching a tutor explain something well, which almost all of them can do, but for watching what happens in the thirty seconds after your child gets something wrong. The tutor who asks a question there, rather than re-explaining, is the one worth paying for at any band.

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor in Al Twar cost per month?
faqs.answer: The market's own advertised figures are the clearest guide. In-home packages of four two-hour sessions are listed at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month, against around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. On an hourly basis Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500. For a Diploma student taking two subjects at the specialist band, Bestimate's monthly estimates imply AED 2,000 to 4,000 a month. These are market rates read in October 2026, attributed to their publishers, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our villa in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Diploma and MYP tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We make that trade for two reasons that both show up in the price: the published in-home premium pays for a car in Dubai traffic rather than for better teaching, and an in-home arrangement limits you to tutors willing to drive to Al Twar on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tutoring in Dubai so much more expensive than online?
faqs.answer: Because a tutor driving to Al Twar from central Dubai at six in the evening commits well over an hour of travel to deliver one hour of teaching, and that time is paid for inside the hourly rate whether it is itemised or not. Published figures make the gap visible: Bestimate quotes in-home at AED 180 to 350 and independents up to AED 500, while qualified online subject tutors are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. The difference is logistics rather than teaching quality.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor ever the right choice for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For some jobs, yes. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52. That band can genuinely handle recall drilling, homework supervision and keeping practice ticking over between specialist sessions. What it rarely buys is diagnosis, which is the ability to identify the actual fault in one attempt instead of three. Many families get the best result by mixing bands rather than buying entirely at one end.

faqs.question: Where do Al Twar families most often waste tuition money?
faqs.answer: Four places. Paying a specialist rate for homework supervision, when the problem is that work does not get done rather than that it cannot be done. Spreading a budget across five subjects at an intensity too low to change any of them. Buying emergency internal assessment help in the final fortnight, when the only remaining help would cross the academic-honesty line. And paying premium Diploma rates for MYP criterion work, where a mid-band tutor with real MYP experience is worth considerably more.

faqs.question: Should I pay for a whole term up front to get a discount?
faqs.answer: Be careful. The discount is real, and so is the risk it creates. The commonest failure in tutoring is a mismatch between tutor and student, and it usually becomes clear in weeks two to four. A family holding twelve pre-paid sessions tends to persist with a poor match rather than write off the balance, which costs far more than the discount saved. Our arrangement addresses the same risk differently: a free trial lesson before any payment, and a change of tutor at no cost if the match turns out wrong.

faqs.question: When in the two Diploma years is tutoring money best spent?
faqs.answer: Three phases dominate. The first term of DP1, because a weak Higher Level foundation sets permanently and a single weekly hour started in October costs less than the rescue it prevents. The internal assessment window from DP1 summer into DP2 autumn, where scheduled supervision beats panic buying. And a dated block of eight to twelve sessions before the examination series, aimed at paper technique. Families consistently underspend in the first phase, because nothing has visibly gone wrong yet, and overspend in the last.

faqs.question: Is the quoted tutoring rate per hour or per lesson?
faqs.answer: Ask, because it varies and the difference compounds. A fifty-minute lesson billed as an hour is a twenty per cent difference across a year. While you are asking, settle three more things in writing: what happens to a session you cancel with a day's notice, what happens when the tutor cancels, and whether materials and marking time between sessions are inside the rate or billed separately. Each of those is a reasonable thing to charge for and an unreasonable thing to discover in month three.

faqs.question: Does a tutoring quote in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as settled fact here, because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than a tutoring company's assertion. What any provider can tell you is simply whether the figure they quoted is the figure you will pay. If the answer is vague, treat that as information. The relevant question is never the tax rule in the abstract; it is whether your invoice will match your expectation.

faqs.question: Is it better to fund one subject properly or spread the budget wider?
faqs.answer: One or two, almost always, and this is the advice families resist hardest. A Diploma student with six subjects and a limited budget tends to end up with four or five weekly sessions at an intensity too low to produce the practice that actually drives improvement. The same spend concentrated on one or two subjects reliably produces more movement. Choose the subject the coordinator identifies rather than the one the student complains about, because those are frequently different and only one of them is costing the grade.

faqs.question: Can we pay a tutor to finish my son's internal assessment?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honest will. IB academic-honesty rules require the work to be the student's own, and a malpractice finding falls on the student, potentially costing the whole Diploma rather than a few marks. Legitimate supervision is questioning the research question until it is answerable, challenging an uncontrolled variable, teaching conventions in general terms, and giving feedback on the student's own draft including flagging unsupported claims. We will not write, draft, edit to completion or supply any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay.

faqs.question: How does the Dubai school fee freeze affect what we should spend?
faqs.answer: It gives you an unusually clear year to plan. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. With the largest education line flat, this is the right moment to decide the second-largest line deliberately: name the monthly tutoring figure, then allocate it, rather than letting hours accumulate until a February statement delivers the total you never agreed to.

faqs.question: Is a small group cheaper than one-to-one for Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and whether it is better value depends entirely on how closely matched the group is. Two or three students at the same level, on the same paper, with the same specific weakness, can learn well together and share the cost. A group assembled because three families live nearby and all want maths help will move at the pace of its weakest member while being billed for everyone. For diagnosis of an individual error pattern, one-to-one is the only format that works.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor before paying anything in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: Six questions. Which subject and level do you teach, and how many students at that level do you currently have? What would you do in the first three sessions? Per hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson? What are the cancellation terms, both ways? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid two years? And can we do a trial session before any payment? Hesitation on the permit question or the cancellation terms is the most informative answer you can get.

faqs.question: Do I get a refund if the tutoring does not improve my child's grade?
faqs.answer: We do not offer outcome-linked refunds, and we would be cautious about anyone who does. A grade depends on the student's own work, the school, the subject, the examiner and the paper, so a promise tied to it is either carefully hedged in terms you have not read or not meant seriously. What we offer instead is a free trial before any payment, a change of tutor at no cost if the match is wrong, and scoped blocks that end on their agreed date rather than rolling on.

faqs.question: Does the permit cost anything, and why should I ask about it?
faqs.answer: It costs nothing, which is exactly why the question is useful. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. A tutor who tells you it is expensive, optional or unnecessary has said something checkable and wrong. Individuals tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

intro.heading: The Al Warqa IB budget, written out in full
paragraphs: A household in Al Warqa'a 2 or 3 deciding whether to buy Diploma support is making a two-year commitment whether or not anybody says so out loud. Weekly tutoring in one subject from the start of Year 12 to the May examinations is roughly seventy sessions. At market rates that is a four-figure monthly line and a five-figure total, and almost nobody is shown that arithmetic before the first invoice. This page does the arithmetic first and the persuasion second.

Al Warqa makes the calculation unusually clear, because the community is a long way from where Dubai's tutoring supply lives. The school run goes north to Al Qusais, west to Mirdif, or down Ras Al Khor Road towards Festival City and Academic City. A tutor driving in from Jumeirah or Business Bay at five in the afternoon is in the car for the best part of an hour each way, and that hour is paid for by somebody. In this postcode the travel premium is not a rounding error, it is the difference between two sessions a week and one.

The second thing the arithmetic exposes is which marks are cheap. Diploma grades are built from external papers sat in the May session and from internal assessment completed across the two years. The internal assessment is worth a fixed, published share of every subject grade, it is marked against criteria the student can read, and it is finished months before anyone sees an examination paper. Marks lost there are lost quietly and permanently. Marks gained there are the least expensive grade points available in the whole programme, and they are the ones a tutor can legitimately help with by teaching and reviewing the student's own work.

The delivery position has to be stated before any of this is useful. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Al Warqa lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We are not pretending that is identical to a tutor at the kitchen table. We are saying that for a family whose nearest Diploma school is a twenty-five minute drive away, the choice is between a subject specialist on a screen and a generalist who was willing to make the journey, and that the specialist is usually the better purchase.

Everything below is written to be checked. The rate bands name their sources. The context table puts tutoring next to Dubai school fees and examination entry costs so the figure has a scale. The academic-honesty section states what a tutor will not do, because the providers in this market who blur that line are putting a student's IB registration at risk in exchange for a short-term grade. And where coverage is thin, the page says so instead of promising a specialist in every subject at every hour.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-warqa.programmesIntro: Al Warqa students reach three IB programmes, all of them by car. The notes below cover what each stage costs in support terms and what a tutor can change inside it, with the local detail that decides whether buying now or waiting a term is the better call.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Most of each subject grade comes from external papers sat in the May session UAE schools use; the rest comes from internal assessment completed during the course. Higher Level carries extra syllabus content and, in several subjects, an extra paper, so the hours required are genuinely different rather than nominally so.
programmes.countryNote: Al Warqa Diploma students mostly travel to Deira International School or Universal American School via Festival City, or to Uptown International School in Mirdif. That journey is the practical argument for fixing a tutoring slot at 17:30 or later and keeping it: a 16:30 booking looks fine on a calendar and fails the first time Ras Al Khor Road backs up.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, each marked against four criteria scored 0 to 8. There is no external examination, so reports convert criterion totals into a 1 to 7 grade. The cost implication is that general revision is close to worthless here: marks move when the weak criterion is identified and practised, and not otherwise.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Warqa family the MYP years are where support is cheapest and most effective, because the diagnosis made in MYP 4 is the one that prevents an expensive Higher Level mistake in Year 12. Uptown International School is the nearest full continuum school, so MYP criterion language is familiar to some households here and entirely new to others.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than separate subjects, with reporting written against learner-profile attributes and no criterion marks or examinations. Useful paid support at this stage is narrow: number fluency, reading stamina and the beginnings of written structure. Anything broader is supervision rather than teaching, and should be priced at the bottom of the market band.
programmes.countryNote: Few Al Warqa families buy PYP tutoring and fewer should. The exception is a child moving from a CBSE or British primary into an IB continuum school, where the shift from marks to inquiry-based reporting is disorienting for a term and a short block of sessions genuinely helps.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is assessed through a mix of DP external papers and course-specific coursework, and suits a student who wants IB depth in a few subjects alongside an applied qualification.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is available at a small number of Dubai schools and rarely drives a tutoring enquiry from this area. It is worth naming because a student drowning in the full six-subject Diploma has routes other than abandoning IB, and a tutor who sells more hours instead of mentioning them is not advising honestly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with Higher Level adding a third paper. The exploration is the internal assessment. Marks are lost in HL on the unseen-structure questions in Paper 2 and on mathematical communication in the exploration, where correct work scores poorly because it is never justified.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving. Standard Level suits most social-science and business routes, but several engineering and mathematics degrees specify Analysis and Approaches. Checking a university's own prerequisite page before Year 12 is free and saves an expensive route change later.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level carries additional content and a longer examination load. The predictable losses are uncertainties and error propagation, graph gradients with units, and extended explanation questions where command terms are ignored. The scientific investigation is the internal assessment and rewards a controlled, well-justified design.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most dropped marks, along with the data-based questions that look like reading comprehension and are not. Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth, which makes targeted work on two or three topics unusually effective.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of terminology is the visible problem; the real one is applying it to unfamiliar contexts under timed conditions. Students who can recite a process often cannot answer a question that presents it in a new organism. Past-paper work with command-term discipline is the fix.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the grade. Higher Level adds quantitative content and a policy paper. Internal assessment commentaries are a common place to lose marks cheaply, because students summarise an article rather than applying a single clearly identified concept to it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are easy to learn and hard to apply. Marks are lost where a student lists a framework without using the case material, and in the internal assessment where the research question is too broad to answer with the evidence gathered.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis under time pressure, the individual oral, and the HL essay. Strong readers lose marks summarising content instead of analysing how a writer's choices produce an effect, which is a technique problem with a short fix.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies are remembered; critical evaluation is not. The grade sits in weighing methodology, ethics and cultural generalisability, and in the internal assessment's statistical reporting, which students frequently treat as an afterthought.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The core contributes to the overall Diploma total and is where organised students gain ground. A tutor may teach argument structure, question a research question that cannot be answered in the word limit, and comment on the student's own draft. Nobody here produces either piece of work.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-warqa.regionsTitle: Al Warqa and the communities on the same school run
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-warqa.regionsIntro: These are the pockets whose IB families share Al Warqa's constraints: a long drive to the nearest Diploma school, a late return, and almost no resident subject specialists. The notes are practical rather than scenic.

regions.name: Al Warqa'a 1
regions.note: Closest to Al Qusais and the Metro Green Line, with the shortest runs to Westminster and Apple International. Children home by about 15:45, which makes a 16:30 start workable here and nowhere else in the community.

regions.name: Al Warqa'a 2 and 3
regions.note: Villa plots towards Al Khawaneej Road. Longer runs to Mirdif and Festival City schools push a realistic weekday start to 17:15 or 17:30, and activity schedules compete for exactly those slots.

regions.name: Al Warqa'a 4 and 5
regions.note: The newest edge of the community, nearest Al Awir Road. Families here often drive to Academic City, adding a further twenty minutes in each direction, so one later session holds better than two early ones.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Where much of the local school supply actually sits, including Uptown International School on the IB continuum. Mirdif-schooled children can start at 16:00, which is why siblings at different schools need different slots.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: Dense school cluster to the north, mainly CBSE and British. Diploma students travel out of it rather than into it, and pickup traffic around Damascus Street is the variable that breaks an early booking.

regions.name: Al Mizhar and Al Khawaneej
regions.note: Villa communities east of Al Warqa feeding the same Mirdif schools. Short commutes but heavy after-school sport, so two fixed weekday slots prove easier to protect than four flexible ones.

regions.name: Nad Al Hamar
regions.note: Between Al Warqa and Al Rashidiya with fast access to Ras Al Khor Road. Very few resident specialists in any Diploma subject, which is precisely the gap online delivery closes.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Deira International School and Universal American School sit here, drawing Diploma students out of Al Warqa daily. Return traffic across the creek is the reason a 17:30 session survives and a 16:45 one does not.

schoolClusters.note: The schools immediately around the community. The local supply is mostly CBSE and British rather than IB, which is why Al Warqa Diploma families drive, and why a tutor who happens to live nearby is unlikely to be a Diploma subject specialist.

modes.title: One subject, one weekly hour, two years
modes.description: The standard Diploma arrangement and the one worth costing properly, because it is roughly seventy sessions from the start of Year 12 to the May examinations. It works where a single subject is clearly the problem and the internal assessment in that subject is approached early rather than in the final term.

modes.description: Where two subjects are weak, alternating a single weekly hour between them costs half what two slots cost and works surprisingly well in the months when Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are eating the student's evenings. sections.heading: What two years of Diploma support in Al Warqa adds up to
paragraphs: Start from the month rather than the hour, because the month is what a household actually feels. Bestimate's Dubai rate table estimates a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages circulating in this market put eight online sessions at around AED 799 a month, and four two-hour in-home sessions at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Those are published figures from the Dubai market, not IB Gram prices.

Now multiply by the programme. A Diploma runs two academic years, so a single subject at one session a week is roughly seventy sessions before the May examinations. At the middle band that is a total somewhere between AED 12,000 and AED 25,000 for one subject across the whole Diploma. Two subjects doubles it. Nobody shows parents that number at the enquiry stage, which is why so many families drift into a rolling monthly commitment they would have questioned had it been quoted as a total.

The useful conclusion is not that tutoring is expensive. It is that the shape of the spend matters more than the rate. The same total buys either a thin layer of weekly support across two years, or concentrated blocks at the three points where Diploma marks are genuinely decided: the internal assessment in each subject, the transition into Higher Level content in the first term of Year 12, and the final revision run. Families who plan the shape spend less and get more than families who simply start a weekly hour and keep paying.

sections.heading: The travel premium, priced in teaching minutes
paragraphs: The gap between the online band and the in-home band is roughly AED 100 to 200 an hour. It is tempting to read that as a convenience charge. It is better read as the cost of a tutor's unpaid commute, because that is what it is, and in Al Warqa the commute is long. A tutor coming from central Dubai at the hour a school child is free spends forty to sixty minutes each way on Ras Al Khor Road or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road.

Convert it into the only unit that matters. At AED 200 an hour online, AED 1,000 buys five hours of teaching. At AED 400 an hour in-home, the same AED 1,000 buys two and a half. The in-home arrangement also constrains when teaching can happen, because a tutor making a ninety-minute round trip will only accept a slot that justifies it, which in practice means fewer available times and a booking that collapses the first time traffic does.

There is a second cost that never appears on an invoice: the pool. The set of tutors willing to drive to Al Warqa'a 4 on a Tuesday evening is small, and nothing about willingness to drive predicts knowing why Diploma Chemistry students lose marks on energetics. Online, the constraint is only the clock. A specialist free at 17:30 Gulf Standard Time is available regardless of where they sleep, and that is the whole argument for the format rather than any claim about screens being better than rooms.

sections.heading: Internal assessment is the cheapest grade point in the Diploma
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internal assessment worth a published share of the final grade, completed during the course and marked by the school against IB criteria before external moderation. In the sciences it is the scientific investigation; in Mathematics it is the exploration; in Economics it is a set of commentaries; in the languages it is an oral and, at Higher Level, an essay. The share differs by subject and level, and the school will tell you the exact figure for each of your child's six.

Two features make these the least expensive marks in the programme. They are produced without time pressure, over weeks, with the criteria visible to the student from the start. And they are finished long before anyone sits a paper, so a weakness addressed in the first year cannot resurface in May. A student who treats internal assessment as homework and the examinations as the real event has given away a fixed percentage of six subject grades for nothing.

What a tutor may legitimately do here is specific and worth writing down, because this is exactly the territory where the worst providers in this market operate. A tutor may teach the method, explain each criterion in the words the examiner uses, challenge a research question that cannot be answered within the word limit, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. No tutor at IB Gram supplies text, data, analysis or a finished section for an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. One Dubai provider found during research sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence lands on the student, not the seller.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai fees, entry fees and the 2026-27 freeze
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means nothing without a scale beside it. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by 6 per cent.

The number that changes a household budget is the fee decision. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For an Al Warqa family that means the tutoring line is not competing with a fee rise this year, which is a genuinely unusual position and a sensible moment to plan the two-year shape rather than drift into monthly payments.

The other context is examination entry, which parents in Dubai routinely forget until a school invoice arrives. Entry fees are set by the school or, for private candidates, by the examination centre, and they are separate from tuition and from tutoring. Nobody should publish a single figure for them because they vary by centre and by subject count. The point for budgeting is simply that the two-year Diploma total includes a school fee, an entry cost and, if you choose it, a tutoring cost, and only the third is optional.

sections.heading: Where the Diploma money should go first
paragraphs: Families almost always buy tutoring in response to a grade, and the grade is the least informative thing on a Diploma report. A 4 in Higher Level Chemistry can mean a content gap in two topics, an inability to read a data-based question, or a student who understands the chemistry and writes answers that ignore the command term. Those are three different purchases, and only one of them is a weekly hour for two years.

The cheapest diagnostic is marked work. Two recent papers with the examiner's or teacher's annotations on them show the pattern within a session, and a competent tutor will ask for them before quoting anything. If a provider quotes a package before seeing any of the student's work, they are selling hours rather than diagnosing a problem, and the price is the only thing they can differentiate on.

The table below is the triage we actually use. It maps what a report or a paper looks like to the likely cause and the first thing worth buying, with a rough duration. None of it is a promise about a grade. No tutor, however experienced with Diploma mark schemes, can promise a Diploma score, and a provider who does is telling you something about their marketing rather than their teaching. The durations are honest estimates from the pattern in the work, and they are the figure to hold a tutor to at the six-week review rather than a vague sense that things feel better. A content gap that was supposed to take four sessions and is still open after ten is a signal that the diagnosis was wrong, which is useful information and considerably cheaper to act on than another term of the same arrangement.

sections.heading: Two children, two timetables, one Al Warqa evening
paragraphs: A detail that matters more in this community than the rate does: Al Warqa households commonly run two or three children at different schools on different timetables. One is collected from Al Qusais at 14:45, another from Festival City at 15:30, a third does sport until 17:00. A single visiting tutor cannot serve that household without someone waiting, and the waiting is usually the younger child doing nothing useful for an hour.

Online scheduling dissolves the problem rather than solving it cleverly. Two children can be taught on the same evening at different times by different subject specialists, from the same house, with no second journey and no overlap. A sibling who needs MYP Sciences and a Year 13 who needs Higher Level Mathematics are two different tutors, and in-home delivery forces a household to choose between them or pay two travel premiums.

The same flexibility handles the parts of the Dubai year that break fixed arrangements. Ramadan shifts the whole evening, and sessions move to post-Iftar timing without anyone renegotiating a driving commitment. Families travelling during the long summer keep the slot by changing the clock rather than cancelling the block. School examination weeks, when a student needs three sessions one week and none the next, are a scheduling change rather than a contractual one. The same applies to the stretch of the Dubai year when Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay deadlines collide with mock papers and a household genuinely cannot hold a fixed hour. Moving a slot by ninety minutes costs nobody anything when there is no journey attached to it, and that single fact removes most of the friction that makes families abandon tutoring halfway through Year 12.
bullets: Two children, two subject specialists, one evening, no second journey

sections.heading: The honesty line that protects your money and your child's registration
paragraphs: This market contains providers who will finish a student's coursework for a fee. Research for these pages found one selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is not an aggressive form of tutoring, it is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the sanction falls on the candidate: a malpractice finding can cost the Diploma itself. Any parent weighing a cheap route to a finished IA should price in that risk, because the provider does not carry it.

The legitimate boundary is not vague. A tutor teaches the method, explains the criteria in the examiner's own language, questions whether a research question can be answered within the word limit, and comments on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not supply text, data, analysis, a structure the student could not have produced, or edits so heavy that the authorship changes. On the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay the same line holds, and so does the student's declaration of authenticity.

Two related claims are worth refusing on sight. Nobody should describe themselves as approved or accredited by KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson unless they hold the specific permit and can show its number; IB Gram holds none of those and does not claim them. And no provider should promise a grade, a score or an improvement. A tutor can make a weakness visible and teach the technique that fixes it. What the student does in the examination hall in May is not a product anyone can sell.
bullets: A tutor teaches, questions and reviews; the student writes every word

sections.heading: What to ask before paying, and what a good answer sounds like
paragraphs: Five questions separate a tutoring purchase from a subscription. First: what did you see in my child's marked work? An answer that describes a pattern in the papers is worth more than any qualification list. Second: what will you do that the school is not already doing? A school gives twenty-five students the same explanation; the value of one-to-one is that it does not have to.

Third: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because it is free and fast, there is no good reason not to hold it, and asking costs nothing.

Fourth: what will you not do with the internal assessment? The right answer is immediate and specific. Fifth: how do we stop? An arrangement with no review point becomes a standing order. Six weeks, then a check against the school's own reporting, then extend or end, is the shape that keeps a two-year Diploma budget under control. At IB Gram the trial lesson is free, there is no fixed term, and if we cannot staff a subject at the level you need we will say so rather than improvise. A sixth question is worth adding where a provider is quoting a monthly package: what is the total across the Diploma at this rate? Hearing that number out loud changes how families choose, which is presumably why so few pages in this market print it.
bullets: Ask what they saw in the marked work, before any package is quoted
Ask for the MoHRE permit; it is free and takes two working days

process.title: Send two marked papers
process.description: Not the report card, and not a description of the worry. Two recently marked pieces of work in the weakest subject show the pattern faster than any conversation, and they let a tutor tell you whether you need four sessions or forty before anybody quotes a package.

process.title: Fix the slot around the real school run
process.description: For most Al Warqa addresses that means 17:15 or later on a weekday, earlier at the Al Qusais end of the community, and later again for families driving to Academic City. Choosing the time before the tutor prevents the usual quiet failure of a good match in an impossible slot.

process.title: Use the free trial as a diagnostic
process.description: By the end of it you should have a named weakness, an explanation of why marks are lost there, and an estimate in weeks. If you instead get a sales conversation and a monthly figure, change the match. The trial costs nothing and is the only cheap way to test a tutor.

process.title: Plan the two-year shape, not just this month
process.description: Decide now where the concentrated work goes: the internal assessment in each weak subject, the first term of Higher Level content, and the final revision run. Families who plan the shape spend less across the Diploma than families who start a weekly hour and let it run.

process.title: Review against the school's marks, then decide
process.description: After six weeks compare the school's own assessment data, not the tutor's impression. Extend, switch subject, or stop. A review date agreed in advance is what turns an open-ended monthly cost back into a decision.

whyPoints.description: One subject at a weekly hour is roughly seventy sessions across the Diploma. We publish that total in dirhams alongside the monthly figure, because the monthly figure is how families end up committing to an amount they never agreed to.

whyPoints.description: Al Warqa lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service. You will not discover the format after booking.

whyPoints.title: Internal assessment treated as the priority it is
whyPoints.description: A fixed published share of every subject grade is decided before anyone sits a paper. We schedule that work in the first year, teach the criteria in the examiner's language, and review the student's own drafts without ever writing them.

whyPoints.title: No accreditation claims, no grade promises
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval and claims none. No page here promises a score, a grade improvement or a refund tied to a result, because none of those is a thing a tutor can deliver.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Where no specialist is free in a subject at the level you need, you get a time estimate, a named alternative, or an honest decline. Nobody is matched quietly to a tutor outside their subject and left to find out in week three.

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor in Al Warqa cost per month?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures put a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, according to Bestimate's Dubai rate table. Packages in this market show eight online sessions at around AED 799 a month and four two-hour in-home sessions at AED 1,599 to 1,799. IB Gram quotes after a free trial rather than from a price list, because the sensible figure depends on how many subjects are actually weak.

faqs.question: What does two years of IB tutoring in Al Warqa cost in total?
faqs.answer: One subject at one session a week from the start of Year 12 to the May examinations is roughly seventy sessions. At the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 an hour that is somewhere between AED 11,000 and AED 21,000 for a single subject across the whole Diploma, and roughly double for two. Almost nobody is shown the total at the enquiry stage, which is how families drift into a rolling monthly commitment. Planning where the concentrated work goes usually costs less than letting a weekly hour run untouched for two years.

faqs.question: Is there an option for a tutor to visit our Al Warqa villa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every Al Warqa lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In this community that is usually the better arrangement regardless: a tutor driving from central Dubai at the hour your child is free spends forty to sixty minutes each way and prices that into the rate, and the pool shrinks to tutors willing to make the journey rather than tutors who know the subject.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home tutor in Al Warqa so much more expensive than online?
faqs.answer: Because you are paying for the commute. The gap between the bands is roughly AED 100 to 200 an hour, and Al Warqa sits far enough east that a tutor from central Dubai spends most of an hour in each direction. Converted into teaching, AED 1,000 buys between three and seven hours online and between two and five and a half in-home. The hidden cost is the smaller choice of tutors: willingness to drive to Al Warqa'a 4 on a Tuesday tells you nothing about whether someone can teach Higher Level Chemistry.

faqs.question: Which part of the IB Diploma gives the best return on tutoring spend?
faqs.answer: Internal assessment, by a clear margin. Every subject carries it, it is worth a published share of the final grade, it is produced over weeks without time pressure, and it is finished long before any examination. A weakness fixed there cannot return in May. Students who treat it as homework hand back a fixed percentage of six subject grades. A finite block of six to eight sessions, started before the school's first internal deadline, is usually better value than a year of general weekly support.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with my child's IB internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the method, explain each criterion in the examiner's own wording, challenge a research question that cannot be answered within the word limit, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. That is the full list. No tutor should supply text, data, analysis or a finished section, and no tutor should edit so heavily that authorship changes. One Dubai provider found during research sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Under IB rules that is malpractice, and the sanction falls on the candidate rather than the seller.

faqs.question: What time can an Al Warqa IB lesson realistically begin on a school night?
faqs.answer: It depends which end of the community you live in. Al Warqa'a 1 families, with short runs to Al Qusais schools, can usually hold 16:30. Al Warqa'a 2 and 3 should plan for 17:15 or 17:30, because the run goes to Mirdif or Festival City. Al Warqa'a 4 and 5 families driving to Academic City often need 17:45. Fixing the time before choosing the tutor matters: the commonest reason a good match quietly fails is a slot that never actually worked on a Tuesday.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two Diploma subjects for the same Al Warqa student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Mathematics and Physics is a common and genuine pairing; so is Chemistry and Biology. Economics and Business Management overlap less than they appear to. What you should resist is a single tutor covering four unrelated subjects, which usually means general school support rather than subject teaching. Where two subjects are both weak, alternating one weekly slot fortnightly costs half as much as two slots and works well in Year 12, though not in the final term.

faqs.question: Does my child's Diploma school in Dubai set the examination entry fees?
faqs.answer: Entry is arranged through the school for enrolled candidates, or through an examination centre for private candidates, and the cost sits separately from both school fees and tutoring. Amounts vary by centre and by how many subjects are entered, so no single figure is worth publishing. For budgeting, the point is that a two-year Diploma carries a school fee, an entry cost and an optional tutoring cost, and the school's finance office can give you the first two precisely. IB Gram has no role in entry or registration.

faqs.question: Are Dubai school fees going up, and should that change our tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For an Al Warqa household that means the tutoring line is not competing with a fee rise this year. It is a reasonable moment to plan the full two-year shape of Diploma support deliberately, rather than starting a weekly hour and discovering the total eighteen months later.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child needs four tutoring sessions or forty?
faqs.answer: Marked work tells you, and nothing else does reliably. Good classwork with poor timed papers is technique and pacing, usually six to eight sessions. Marks lost across every answer type in one topic is a content gap, three to five sessions. Correct method with low marks is a command-term problem, four to six. Falling in several subjects at once is almost always workload and organisation rather than subject knowledge, and buying four subjects of tutoring makes it worse. Any provider quoting a package before seeing the work is selling hours.

faqs.question: We have two children on different school timetables. Does that work?
faqs.answer: It works considerably better online than with a visiting tutor. Al Warqa households commonly run children at Al Qusais, Mirdif and Festival City schools with pickups spread across ninety minutes. Two children can be taught on the same evening at different times by two different subject specialists from the same house, with no second journey and nobody waiting. An in-home arrangement forces you to choose one child's subject or pay two travel premiums, which is a poor use of the same budget.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or when we travel over the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the practical advantages of the format. Ramadan shifts the whole evening, and lessons move to post-Iftar timing without renegotiating anyone's driving commitment. Families travelling during the long holidays keep their slot by changing the clock rather than cancelling the block. Examination weeks, where a student wants three sessions one week and none the next, are a scheduling change rather than a contractual one. None of that is possible when a tutor's journey is part of the arrangement.

faqs.question: Can anyone promise my child a higher IB score if we pay for tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and you should treat the promise itself as the warning. A tutor can make a weakness visible, teach the technique that addresses it, and build the past-paper habit that converts knowledge into marks. What a student does in the examination hall in May is not a product. Equally, nobody in this market should describe themselves as approved or accredited by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson without the specific permit number to show. IB Gram holds none of those and claims none.

faqs.question: What if there is no tutor available for my child's subject at the level we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, with an estimate of how long a match is likely to take. Higher Level Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and English are well covered. Less commonly requested subjects, and some language options, take longer and are occasionally declined outright. Where a near alternative is genuinely useful it is offered as an alternative and named as one, not quietly substituted. Where neither applies, declining the booking is the right answer, and it is cheaper for you than three weeks with the wrong tutor.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-wasl.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects to students on the Jumeirah side of Dubai. Each is matched to one subject at one level, because a Chemistry HL paper three and a Maths AA paper one reward entirely different teaching.

intro.heading: Al Wasl, Al Safa, Jumeirah 3: the search looks local, the answer is not
paragraphs: An Al Wasl parent types "IB home tutor near Al Wasl" and gets a list sorted by proximity. That list is answering a question about traffic, not a question about teaching. The useful comparison is not Al Wasl against some distant suburb. It is Al Wasl against Al Safa, against Jumeirah 2, against Al Manara and Umm Suqeim 1, all of which sit within a short run along Al Wasl Road or Jumeirah Beach Road. Run that comparison honestly and the same conclusion appears four times over: the pool of people who will drive to your villa for a 5pm Diploma lesson is small, and it shrinks to almost nothing once you specify Higher Level, once you specify a subject, and once you specify a tutor who has marked that subject's assessment.

This page is written as that comparison. It sets Al Wasl beside its neighbours on drive time, school cluster, realistic session start and what the in-home premium actually costs, and then explains why the answer lands in the same place in every one of those communities. The conclusion is not a sales line. It is arithmetic. A specialist in a subject taken by a minority of Diploma candidates is not going to live fifteen minutes away from you, and a generalist who lives fifteen minutes away is not going to lift a Physics HL grade in the eight weeks before the exam.

The second thing worth saying early, because it decides whether the rest of the page is useful to you: IB Gram does not send a tutor to a villa in Al Wasl or anywhere else in the UAE, and does not run home visits in Dubai. Home tuition at an address is a service offered only in India. For Al Wasl the delivery is live one-to-one video, one tutor and one student, scheduled around the school run and homework. That is stated here rather than buried, because the alternative is a parent paying for a trial and then discovering it.

What that buys is worth naming. A student at a Jumeirah-side Diploma school taking Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level alongside Chemistry HL is sitting two of the most demanding courses in the programme. The in-home market in Dubai will offer that student whoever covers maths and science generally. Online, the same student gets one tutor for the AA paper three optional topic and a different tutor for the Chemistry internal assessment, and neither of them needs to be within range of Safa Park at half past four.

The rest of this page does five things. It compares Al Wasl with the four communities that border it, so you can see the data rather than take the claim. It publishes what Dubai actually charges, in AED, with the source of each band. It counts the Diploma calendar backwards from the May session so the eight weeks in front of you have a shape. It sets out exactly what a tutor may and may not touch on an internal assessment or an Extended Essay, which is the line the essay mills in these search results cross. And it says plainly what happens when no specialist is free, because concealing that is how families end up with the wrong match.

Nothing here requires you to buy anything to be useful. The rate bands, the regulator detail, the permit position and the assessment weightings are published so that an Al Wasl parent can interrogate any provider in Dubai, including this one, with the right questions.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-wasl.programmesIntro: An Al Wasl family may have children in three different IB phases at once, and the tutoring that helps a Year 5 PYP student has almost nothing in common with what a DP2 candidate needs in February. These are the programmes we cover and what each one actually asks of a student in Dubai.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units rather than subject syllabuses, so there is no paper to revise for and no mark scheme to drill. Support at this stage is about the mechanics underneath the inquiry: number fluency, reading stamina, and writing that holds a line of argument for more than three sentences. A PYP exhibition in the final year is the first piece of extended independent work most children produce.
programmes.countryNote: Several of the primary schools serving Al Wasl and Al Safa run a British Early Years and Key Stage 1 model instead of the PYP, which means children on this side of Dubai often transfer into an IB school at Year 7. That transfer is where gaps appear, because a child arriving from a phonics-and-objectives curriculum into inquiry units is not weaker, only differently prepared.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, and converts to a 1-7 grade through subject-specific boundaries. Students lose marks because they answer the task rather than the criterion. A Sciences criterion C response needs analysis and evaluation of data, not a longer method. The Personal Project in the final year carries a process journal that is assessed as heavily as the product.
programmes.countryNote: Al Wasl families choosing MYP at Year 7 are usually choosing against IGCSE, and in Dubai that choice is reversible later but expensive in effort. An MYP student moving to IGCSE in Year 10 arrives without two years of past-paper technique; an IGCSE student moving to the Diploma arrives without criterion-based writing. Both gaps are closeable in roughly a term of focused work.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment worth between 20 and 30 per cent of the grade, marked by the school and moderated by the IB. The core contributes up to three bonus points. Most of the damage to a final score happens in the internal assessments, not the written papers, because they are drafted while five other subjects are also making demands.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah-side Diploma candidates sit the May session, which is the one UAE schools are built around. The practical consequence for an Al Wasl family is that the internal assessment deadlines fall in the winter term of DP2, weeks before any exam revision starts, and a student who arrives at January with three unfinished drafts has already lost points that no amount of paper practice recovers.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a language development strand and a personal and professional skills course. It is far less common in Dubai than the full Diploma. Support typically focuses on the Diploma-course component, because those are marked against the same external criteria as a full Diploma subject and carry the same internal assessment load.
programmes.countryNote: Very few schools serving the Jumeirah and Al Safa corridor offer the CP, so an Al Wasl family considering it is usually looking across town. Worth knowing before you plan: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency treatment of the CP is not something to assume, and should be confirmed with the ministry's own channel rather than with a tutoring provider.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-wasl.subjectsIntro: A Diploma student does not need a tutor for the Diploma. They need one for the component that is costing them marks. These are the subjects most requested by families along the Al Wasl and Al Safa corridor, with what each actually assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof. At Higher Level the paper three optional question runs for an hour on one extended investigation, and students who have drilled routine questions find it unfamiliar territory. Marks go missing in the non-calculator paper one, where careless manipulation costs method marks that the answer would otherwise have earned.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use throughout. Both papers permit a graphical calculator, which students read as easier and then under-prepare. The commonest loss is writing down an answer without the statistical reasoning that justifies it, because the examiner is marking the inference, not the number the calculator produced.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, waves, fields and nuclear. Paper two is where extended response marks are lost, usually because a student describes a phenomenon when the command term asked them to explain it. The internal assessment needs a measurable independent variable and real uncertainty treatment, which is where most drafts fail criterion B.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic. Organic mechanisms and the HL-only topics are the usual pressure points. In paper one the multiple-choice distractors are built from specific misconceptions, so reviewing wrong answers by misconception beats re-reading the topic.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy on terminology precision and on data-based questions. Students who know the content still lose marks by writing loosely: an examiner marking a question on membrane transport wants the named process, not a description of movement. The internal assessment struggles most on controlling confounding variables in a living system.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and development. Diagrams are marked for accurate labelling and for the explanation that accompanies them. HL adds a quantitative paper three. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on recent news articles, each with a strict word limit, and over-length work is penalised.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are the risk here: a student who can define a SWOT analysis but cannot apply it to the stimulus firm will not score in the top bands. HL paper three works from unseen material under time pressure. The internal assessment at HL is a research project on a real organisation, which needs primary or secondary data secured early.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two papers plus an individual oral and, at HL, an essay on a studied work. Paper one is guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, which rewards students who can read a visual or a column for its construction rather than its content. The individual oral needs two extracts and a global issue that actually connects them.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with written commentaries, and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. TOK is marked on the quality of knowledge questions, not on general thoughtfulness. Students lose marks by writing an opinion piece. Support here is about structuring an argument and selecting examples that do real work.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in one subject, supervised at school. The research question is where essays are won or lost: too broad and there is nothing to argue, too narrow and there is nothing to find. Support is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts, never drafting on their behalf.

sections.heading: Al Wasl against the four communities that border it
paragraphs: The comparison below is the reason this page exists. An Al Wasl parent assumes that choosing a tutor is a local decision, and that a neighbour in Al Safa or Jumeirah 2 has a materially different set of options. They do not. The drive times vary by a few minutes, the school clusters overlap almost completely, and the people willing to teach a Diploma subject in somebody's living room are drawn from the same small pool regardless of which of these five communities you live in.

What does vary is the premium. A tutor travelling to Umm Suqeim 1 in the afternoon peak charges more than one travelling to Al Safa, because the drive is longer and because the return leg eats a slot they could have sold. That premium is real money and it buys nothing academic. It is the price of a car being in a particular place at a particular time, and the market in Dubai quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, according to the published rates of the agencies operating here and Bestimate's Dubai rate table.

The second variable is the realistic session start. A student finishing at a Jumeirah Beach Road school at 3pm is home by 3.40pm on a good day. A tutor finishing a lesson in Al Barsha at 4pm does not reach Al Wasl before 4.45pm in term time, and reaches Umm Suqeim 1 later still. That is why in-home Diploma lessons on this strip cluster at 6pm or later, after the student's useful concentration has already gone into homework.

Read the table as a single argument. Across five communities with different drive times, different premiums and different school clusters, the specialist you actually want is not in any of them, and the delivery that reaches you is the same in all five.

sections.heading: What the travel premium actually buys, line by line
paragraphs: Strip the in-home rate down and ask what each component of it delivers to a Diploma grade. The honest audit is uncomfortable. A chunk of the premium pays for fuel and Salik. A chunk pays for the tutor's unsold time in the car. A chunk pays for the risk that a session is cancelled late and the journey is wasted. None of those three improve a student's paper two extended response.

The part of the premium that does have academic value is small but real. A tutor in the room can see a student's written working develop in real time on paper, can watch posture and attention, and can intervene before a misconception is written down. Those are genuine advantages. They are also almost entirely reproducible on a shared digital whiteboard with a graphics tablet, which is why the online market has converged on that setup rather than on a talking-head video call.

Against that, the premium costs something academic as well as financial. Every kilometre of acceptable travel radius you demand removes tutors from your shortlist, and the ones it removes first are the specialists, because specialists are rarer and therefore less likely to be nearby. An Al Wasl family that insists on an in-home Chemistry HL tutor is choosing from whoever is both free and local. An Al Wasl family that accepts live video is choosing from everyone who teaches Chemistry HL.

Bestimate's Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and notes home tutors quoting up to AED 500. Monthly packages advertised in this market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, against roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published figures, quoted here with their source, not an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: Why the specialist is never fifteen minutes away
paragraphs: This is the mechanism behind every row of the comparison table, and it is worth stating as arithmetic rather than as assertion. Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7 per cent of that enrolment. Take any one Diploma subject at Higher Level and you are looking at a slice of that 7 per cent. Take a specific demanding combination and the slice narrows again.

Now impose a geographic filter. The tutors who teach that subject at that level are distributed across the whole emirate, and a good proportion of them are not in the UAE at all. Asking for one who will drive to Al Wasl at 5pm on a Tuesday does not reduce the pool proportionally. It reduces it to the handful who happen to live in range and happen to have that slot free, and it does so before you have asked a single question about whether they can teach the paper three optional topic.

The counter-argument a parent reasonably makes is that a competent maths teacher can handle Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level regardless. Sometimes that is true. It stops being true at the point where the student is sitting at a 5 and wants a 7, because the gap there is not content coverage. It is command-term discipline, timing under exam pressure, and knowing which of the four paper three optional topics the school has taught and how it has historically been examined. A generalist does not carry that, and no amount of proximity substitutes for it.

Across Al Wasl, Al Safa, Jumeirah 2, Al Manara and Umm Suqeim 1, the same answer applies. That is not a coincidence or a convenient conclusion. It is what happens when a small specialist population meets a hard geographic constraint, and it is the reason this comparison lands in the same place in every community on the list.

sections.heading: Reading a Jumeirah-side school report before you buy anything
paragraphs: Before you compare providers, compare what the school has already told you. A Dubai report usually carries a working grade, a target grade and an effort or attitude indicator, and the relationship between those three decides what kind of help is useful. The mistake is treating the gap between working and target as a single number that tutoring closes.

A working grade of 4 against a target of 6, with strong effort, means the student is doing the work and the work is not converting. That is a technique problem. It responds quickly to past-paper practice, command-term work and mark-scheme reading, and six to ten lessons often move it. A working grade of 4 against a target of 6 with weak effort is a different problem entirely, and adding a weekly lesson to a student who is not completing the existing work usually produces a more expensive version of the same outcome.

Read the subject comments for the word that describes the failure rather than the level. Comments that say "does not show working", "answers the question asked in class rather than on the paper" or "strong recall, weak application" are naming diagnosable faults. Comments that say "should aim to participate more" are naming a classroom observation and will not tell you what to buy. Bring the specific comments to a first lesson. A tutor who reads them will produce a sharper diagnosis in forty minutes than a general assessment produces in three sessions.

One Dubai-specific note. KHDA inspects private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and a school's band describes the school, not your child's progress within it. A student can be drifting in an Outstanding school and thriving in a Good one. Use the inspection report to understand the context your child is learning in; use the report card to decide what to fix.

sections.heading: The Diploma calendar counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools build their Diploma around the May session, and the single most useful thing a parent can hold in their head is that the examinations are not the first deadline. The internal assessments are, and they fall months earlier, set by the school rather than by the IB. A DP2 student in Dubai is typically finalising science and mathematics internal assessments in the winter term while also being taught new content in every subject.

Counted backwards, the shape is this. The school's internal deadlines for the internal assessments and the Extended Essay land through the autumn and winter of DP2. Mock examinations usually follow in the winter or early spring, and the mock grade is what predicted grades and university offers lean on. Only after that does revision for the written papers begin in earnest, and by then every mark available from the internal assessments has already been banked or lost.

This is why the eight-week question matters more than it looks. A family arriving in February asking for help with Physics papers is often asking too late about the wrong thing: the internal assessment, worth a fifth of the grade, has gone. A family arriving in October of DP2 can still change both. The practical advice is unglamorous. Find out from the school, in writing, what its internal deadlines are for every one of your child's six subjects, and work from that list rather than from the exam timetable.

On dates themselves, this page deliberately publishes none for the IB. The IB sets its own session and results dates and revises them, and a wrong date acted on by a parent is worse than no date at all. Confirm every Diploma deadline with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. For the Cambridge and Pearson qualifications an Al Wasl family may also be sitting, the UAE series are June and November, and the live official timetables are the only thing worth relying on.

sections.heading: Where the line sits on an internal assessment or Extended Essay
paragraphs: This is the part of the Dubai market that should worry a parent most, and it is the easiest thing to get wrong by accident. One provider found in these search results sells completed internal assessments outright. Buying one is not a shortcut with a risk attached. It is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

The line is clearer than the marketing around it suggests. A tutor may teach the method: how to formulate a research question, how to design an investigation with a measurable independent variable, how to treat uncertainty, how to structure an argument, how to read the published criteria. A tutor may read what the student has written and give feedback against those criteria. A tutor may explain why a paragraph does not score and leave the student to fix it. A tutor may not write, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of the text, and no reputable tutor will offer to.

In practice the useful work is criterion-by-criterion. Most internal assessments are marked against lettered criteria with published mark allocations, and a student who has never read those criteria is writing blind. Reading them together, then marking the student's own draft against them as an examiner would, is the single highest-return hour available in the whole programme. It is also the hour that essay mills cannot sell, because the output is a better student rather than a finished document.

A practical safeguard for an Al Wasl parent: ask any provider, directly, what they will do with a draft. An answer that includes improving, polishing, fixing or finishing the text is an answer to walk away from. The school supervisor signs an authenticity declaration, and the student signs one too.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit, and how to check a Dubai tutor
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. For an Al Wasl family the relevant body is KHDA, and its annual inspection reports are published and readable.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately, through a work permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Two consequences for a parent on this strip. The permit is free, so any tutor who tells you their rate is higher because of licensing costs is not describing the actual position. And individuals providing private lessons without a permit are, in the government's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with suspicion.

One more boundary worth knowing. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document here, and worth verifying against the current rules. Either way, a parent should not be arranging their child's own classroom teacher as a paid private tutor.
