sections.heading: Starting from Al Wasl, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The process is deliberately short. You describe the subject, the level and what the school has said. A first lesson is free and is used as a diagnosis rather than a sales call, which means the tutor spends it finding out where the marks are going. You get that diagnosis in writing afterwards, including the uncomfortable version if the uncomfortable version is true. Then you decide whether to carry on.

Sometimes the answer is that tutoring is not the right purchase. A student who is not completing set work does not need another hour of instruction. A student three weeks from a paper with no internal assessment problem may need six focused lessons rather than a term. A student whose difficulty is organisational rather than academic is better served by fixing the organisation first. Saying that costs a booking and saves a family money, which is the correct trade.

The harder honesty is availability. Not every subject at every level has a tutor free in the slot an Al Wasl family wants, and a demanding minority combination at Higher Level in the weeks before the May session is exactly when supply is tightest. When that happens you will be told, with a realistic date, rather than matched to the nearest available generalist. A bad match in a subject under time pressure is worse than a two-week wait.

Lessons run on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school run, prayer times and training commitments, and can shift to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan. Reschedules move a lesson rather than lose it. All of it happens over live video, one tutor to one student, because that is how this is delivered in the UAE and this page would rather say so twice than have you find out after paying.

process.title: Tell us the subject and the component
process.description: Not "maths help" but "Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, losing marks on paper one non-calculator". The more precisely the problem is named, the more precisely the match can be made. Bring the school report comments if you have them; they shorten the diagnosis considerably.

process.title: Matched on subject and level
process.description: A tutor is proposed because they teach that subject at that level, with experience of the assessment the student will sit. Location does not enter the decision, which is the whole point of delivering over live video to Al Wasl rather than driving along Al Wasl Road.

process.title: A free first lesson used as a diagnosis
process.description: Forty to sixty minutes of actual teaching, with the tutor working out where marks are going. No payment and no card held. You and the student both form a view of whether this particular person is the right fit, which is not something a profile page can tell you.

process.title: A written diagnosis and a plan with an end point
process.description: What the problem is, what the sequence of work will be, and roughly how many lessons it should take. Where the honest answer is that tutoring is not the fix, that is what you are told. A plan with a stated end point is harder to let drift than an open-ended booking.

process.title: Weekly lessons with notes, reviewed each term
process.description: A fixed slot, notes to the parent after each session, and a review at the end of each term against the original diagnosis. If the plan is not working, the tutor changes or the plan does. Continuing out of habit is the commonest waste of money in this market.

whyPoints.title: The comparison is published, not asserted
whyPoints.description: This page puts Al Wasl beside Al Safa, Jumeirah 2, Al Manara and Umm Suqeim 1 on drive time, cluster, session start and premium, and shows the working. You can disagree with the conclusion, but you can see what it rests on, which is more than any competing page in these results offers.

whyPoints.title: Rates with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or table that published it, with the market band stated as a band. Three of six ranking pages in this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Matching by specialism, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level subject specialist is rare by definition, and insisting they live near Safa Park removes precisely the people worth hiring. Live video removes the constraint, so the shortlist is everyone who teaches the subject rather than everyone free and nearby.

whyPoints.title: A stated position on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Internal assessments, Extended Essays and Theory of Knowledge essays are taught, reviewed and fed back on. They are not written, rewritten or supplied. One provider in this search sells completed internal assessments; the exposure from buying one lands on the student.

whyPoints.title: No regulator borrowed as a credential
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE and the Ministry of Education are explained here because an Al Wasl parent needs to know what each one does. None of them endorses IB Gram, and this page does not suggest otherwise. There is no UAE office and no centre to visit.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free in the slot you want, you hear that with a realistic date instead of being matched to whoever is available. Concealed coverage limits are how families in this market end up with a generalist in a Higher Level subject eight weeks before a paper.

faqs.question: Does an Al Wasl family have better tutor options than an Al Safa family?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the finding this page is built on. Al Wasl, Al Safa, Jumeirah 2, Al Manara and Umm Suqeim 1 draw on the same pool of people willing to drive to a villa for an evening lesson, and the drive times between them vary by minutes rather than meaningfully. What changes between these communities is the travel premium a tutor quotes and the earliest realistic start time. What does not change is that the Higher Level specialist in a given subject is unlikely to live in any of them. Delivering over live video makes the question irrelevant in all five.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a tutor to our villa on Al Wasl Road?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at an Al Wasl address. In-home tuition at a family's address is a service offered only in India. For UAE families the delivery is live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, one tutor and one student, with a shared digital whiteboard so written working is visible in real time. This is stated plainly and early because the alternative is a parent booking a trial on an assumption and finding out afterwards, which wastes everybody's evening.

faqs.question: How much more does an in-home tutor cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures from providers operating in Dubai put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table gives AED 180 to 350, with home tutors quoting up to AED 500. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Monthly packages advertised in the market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published numbers, cited with their source, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: What does the extra money for a home visit actually get my child?
faqs.answer: Honestly audited, most of it buys transport rather than teaching. Fuel, Salik, the tutor's unsold time in the car and the risk of a wasted journey are all priced into the hourly rate, and none of them improves a paper two extended response. The one genuine academic advantage is a tutor watching handwritten working develop in real time and intervening before a misconception is written down. That advantage is largely reproducible on a shared whiteboard with a graphics tablet, which is why serious online tutoring uses one rather than a plain video call.

faqs.question: My child takes Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Does proximity matter for that?
faqs.answer: It matters in the wrong direction. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level includes a paper three that runs for an hour on a single extended investigation, and the four optional topics mean schools teach different content. A tutor who knows how that paper is set and which optional topic your school covers is worth considerably more than one who lives nearby. Insisting on a local in-home tutor removes exactly those specialists from the shortlist first, because rarer expertise is less likely to be geographically convenient. Live video keeps them on the list.

faqs.question: Which schools do children living in Al Wasl usually attend?
faqs.answer: The schools immediately around Al Wasl and Al Safa are predominantly British curriculum and heavily weighted towards primary and through-school provision, which is why many families on this strip sit IGCSE at sixteen before considering the Diploma. Diploma provision sits further out, towards Umm Suqeim, Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and across to Al Jaddaf and Nad Al Sheba. Students we support attend schools across that spread. Those schools are named on this page as context for the local market only, with no affiliation, partnership or endorsement implied in either direction.

faqs.question: What time can a weekday lesson start if my child finishes school at 3pm?
faqs.answer: Online, a 4pm start is comfortable and a 4.30pm start is the common choice, after a snack and before homework fatigue sets in. In-home, the realistic figure on this strip is 5.30pm or later, because a tutor finishing elsewhere in Dubai at 4pm does not reach Al Wasl before 4.45pm in term time and usually later. That difference is not trivial. An hour of Higher Level content at 4.30pm is worth noticeably more than the same hour at 6.30pm, after a full school day and a round of homework.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone providing private lessons without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the internal assessment without crossing an IB rule?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the method: formulating a research question, designing an investigation with a measurable independent variable, handling uncertainty, structuring an argument, and reading the published criteria. A tutor may read the student's own draft and give feedback against those criteria. A tutor may not write, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of the text. One provider in these search results sells completed internal assessments; that is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student. Ask any provider directly what they will do with a draft.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting in February if the papers are in May?
faqs.answer: It can be, but it narrows what is achievable. By February the internal assessments are usually finished or very nearly, and those carry twenty to thirty per cent of each subject grade, so the marks available there have largely been settled. What a focused block from February can still change is examination technique: command-term discipline, timing, mark-scheme reading and the specific question types a student keeps dropping. Six to ten targeted lessons on one paper is a realistic brief. A full recovery across six subjects in twelve weeks is not, and a provider who promises one is not being straight with you.

faqs.question: How do I tell a technique problem from an effort problem on a report?
faqs.answer: Read the working grade, the target grade and the effort indicator together rather than separately. Strong effort with a two-grade gap is usually technique, and it responds quickly to past-paper work, command terms and mark-scheme reading. Weak effort with the same gap is a different problem, and adding a weekly lesson to a student who is not completing existing work tends to produce an expensive version of the same result. The subject comments are the most useful part. Phrases like "strong recall, weak application" name a fault a tutor can diagnose in one lesson.

faqs.question: Does a KHDA Outstanding rating mean my child does not need support?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the band describes the school as a whole, not any individual student's progress inside it. A student can drift in an Outstanding school and thrive in a Good one, because class size, subject staffing and a particular teacher matter more to one child than the overall judgement does. Use the inspection report to understand the context, and use the report card and subject comments to decide what actually needs fixing.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor on the roster covers my child's subject?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a realistic date, rather than matched to whoever happens to be free. Supply is tightest for demanding minority combinations at Higher Level in the weeks before the May session, which is exactly when families most want them. A bad match in a hard subject under time pressure is worse than a short wait, because the student loses confidence as well as time. No competitor page found in this search discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE parents to non-UAE numbers without saying where delivery happens.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan or around travel?
faqs.answer: Yes. Slots can shift to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan, which many families on this side of Dubai prefer because the evening is calmer and the student is not being asked to concentrate at the hardest point of the day. Because delivery is over live video, a family travelling between Dubai and abroad keeps the same tutor and the same slot adjusted for the time difference, rather than pausing for a month. Reschedules move a lesson rather than cancel it, and a term plan can be paused around mocks and coursework crunch weeks by agreement.

faqs.question: Should I pick a tutor who teaches at my child's own school?
faqs.answer: No, and in parts of the UAE it is explicitly ruled out. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct with a comparable restriction. That is press-reported, so verify it against the current policy document. Beyond the rules, the arrangement is a bad idea on its own terms: the person marking your child's internal work should not also be paid by you to improve it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-wasl.closingHeading: The comparison ends in the same place in every community on Al Wasl Road
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-al-wasl.closingBody: Set Al Wasl beside Al Safa, Jumeirah 2, Al Manara and Umm Suqeim 1 and the differences are minutes of driving and a travel premium that buys no marks. The constant is that the Higher Level specialist your child needs is unlikely to live in any of them. IB Gram matches on subject and level and teaches over live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, with the rate bands, the regulator position and the assessed-work boundary published above so you can question any provider in Dubai with the right information. The first lesson is free and is used to diagnose, not to sell. If the honest answer is that tutoring is not what your child needs, that is what you will be told.

None of them is matched on where they live, because that is not what a Higher Level course needs. Tell us the subject, the level and the evening you want, and we will say honestly who is free.

intro.heading: The same search, run from six different Dubailand villas
paragraphs: A family in Arabian Ranches types the phrase at the top of this page. A family three roundabouts away in Arabian Ranches 2 types it with a 2 on the end. In Dubai Hills Estate, Motor City, Mudon and Town Square the same thing happens with a different community name in the middle. The results are nearly identical, and the reason is not laziness on the part of the agencies. It is that the thing being searched for, a teacher who can take a student through Higher Level Chemistry or Analysis and Approaches, is not distributed by community at all.

Dubai's Diploma specialists cluster near the schools that employ them, which in this part of the city means Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim, Dubai Hills and Nad Al Sheba. They are also barred from privately tutoring students enrolled at their own school by the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition work permit. What remains available in-home is a small travelling pool, and that pool serves the whole Dubailand belt rather than any single community inside it. The address you type changes nothing about who is actually free.

That is why this page is written as a comparison. It sets out what in-home tuition costs around Arabian Ranches, what the premium over an online rate pays for, how long the return drive takes from the schools these communities feed at four in the afternoon, and which Diploma subjects are genuinely scarce to staff. Then it gives the same answer for all ten communities, because the honest answer really is the same: choose the teacher on subject depth and run the lesson over live video.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai. Sending tutors to houses is a service we operate in India, and the UAE side of the business is one-to-one online teaching, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing for working, past papers and internal assessment drafts. Saying that plainly matters on a page targeting this phrase. A parent searching for in-home tuition deserves the costs and the trade-offs laid out properly, not a change of subject halfway down the page.

What you gain in exchange is the part of the comparison nobody advertises. An in-home booking in Arabian Ranches selects from the teachers willing to drive to Arabian Ranches at the hour you want. An online booking selects from everyone who can teach the subject at that hour. For a Standard Level Business Management student the two pools may be equally good. For Higher Level Physics, Economics or Analysis and Approaches in the second Diploma year they are not remotely the same, and that gap is worth considerably more to a student than a short drive is worth to a parent.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches.programmesIntro: Families across the Dubailand communities reach the Diploma from three directions: an IGCSE Year 11 at a British school, an MYP 5 year at a continuum school, and occasionally an American high-school track. The notes below are written for a student living in Arabian Ranches making that move, with what each route demands on this side of the city.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Subject grades run from 1 to 7 and the core adds up to three points, so 45 is the ceiling. Higher Level courses carry more teaching hours and deeper content, and they are where private tuition demand concentrates, because the internal assessment and the final papers both sit on top of two years of accumulated material.
programmes.countryNote: From Arabian Ranches the nearest Diploma places sit in Dubai Hills, Al Barsha, Nad Al Sheba and Umm Suqeim, so a second-year student is frequently on a bus home after four. The courses this belt is shortest of are Higher Level Physics, Economics and Analysis and Approaches, and that scarcity is the whole reason an online match beats a local one here.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, and assessment against four criteria marked out of eight rather than percentages. There is no external examination in the first four years, so pressure arrives through internal task deadlines and the report cycle instead. The Personal Project lands in the final year. Students leaving the continuum at that point sit IGCSE, which is a common pattern across the Dubailand communities.
programmes.countryNote: Several families in Arabian Ranches and Mudon use a continuum school for the middle years and then move to a British school for IGCSE and A Level, while others stay for the Diploma. Either way the decision is taken during MYP 4, and it is worth taking with the current criterion profile in front of you rather than on reputation alone.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study and a core of personal and professional skills, a reflective project, service learning and language development. A small number of Dubai schools license it. For a student strong in two or three academic subjects and keen on an applied qualification, it is a genuine alternative to carrying six.
programmes.countryNote: Worth knowing about from Arabian Ranches mainly because option blocks close early in MYP 5 and Year 11. Check the licensed programme list on each school's own KHDA page, since licences differ between neighbouring schools in Dubai Hills and Al Barsha and change between academic years.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary years with no external examination, closing with the PYP Exhibition. Reporting describes learner-profile attributes and approaches to learning rather than marks, which families arriving from a British or Indian primary school often find unfamiliar for a term. Support at this stage is about reading fluency and the habit of recording a method, both of which the middle years assume from day one.
programmes.countryNote: Primary places inside the Dubailand communities are strong and plentiful, which is precisely why the comparison between communities matters so little at six and so much at sixteen. The primary school is a five-minute drive from most of these villas. The Diploma school usually is not.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches.subjectsIntro: Diploma demand on this belt is lopsided. Three courses account for most enquiries and nearly all of the scheduling difficulty, and the rest are straightforward to staff. The list names what each subject assesses and where the marks go, so you can judge whether your child needs a specialist or a strong generalist. Give the level as well as the subject when you enquire.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 and Paper 2, plus Paper 3 at Higher Level, with the exploration as internal assessment. Marks go on reasoning and method rather than arithmetic: a correct final answer with no justification scores badly. This is the hardest course to staff on the Dubailand belt at Higher Level, which is the practical argument against hiring by distance.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy work, with its own exploration. It suits students heading towards business, psychology or design rather than engineering. Several engineering courses expect Analysis and Approaches instead, so the route choice should be checked against the admissions pages of the universities actually in view, not against general advice.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Assessed across written papers plus a scientific investigation. Students who scored highly at IGCSE often drop sharply in the first Diploma year, because the course assumes algebraic fluency and asks for uncertainty handling that IGCSE never required. Fields and circular motion are where Higher Level marks reliably disappear.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Written papers plus the scientific investigation. Organic mechanisms and energetics carry most of the lost marks, and the investigation punishes a student who collects data without a defensible method. Higher Level adds content depth that cannot be caught up in a final term, which is why the first Diploma year is the economical time to start.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Papers plus the investigation, with command terms doing more work here than in any other science. A student who writes everything they know about a topic scores less than one who answers exactly what outline, explain and evaluate demand. Weak statistics in the investigation is common and entirely fixable in a few sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Papers plus three internal assessment commentaries built on recent news articles. Diagram accuracy and precise evaluation carry the marks, and Higher Level adds quantitative work that surprises students who chose the subject to avoid mathematics. Another course that is scarce to staff locally at Higher Level, particularly in an evening slot.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral and, at Higher Level, the essay. The commonest fault is summarising a text where the question asks for analysis of the writer's choices, and that habit usually arrives intact from IGCSE English Language and needs naming before it can be broken.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Papers plus a written commentary at Standard Level and a research project at Higher Level. Case-study technique and the ability to apply a tool rather than describe it carry the grade. One of the more straightforward courses to staff in this part of Dubai at either level, which is useful to know before you pay a scarcity premium.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and internal assessment
subjects.levels: Core, taken by every Diploma student
subjects.description: The core carries up to three points and takes a disproportionate share of first-year time. A tutor may teach structure, question framing and argument, may review the student's own drafts, and may give written feedback. A tutor may never produce any part of the work. That boundary is the whole of the honesty rule, and it is not negotiable.

regions.note: Townhouse communities along Al Qudra Road with young populations and a rising number of Year 10 and Year 11 students. Demand here is still mostly IGCSE rather than Diploma, which changes which subjects are hard to staff at five o'clock.

regions.note: The most affordable community on the belt and the least served by travelling tutors, which shows up directly in quoted in-home rates. Online delivery removes that penalty completely, and this is the community where the difference between the two models is largest.

Programme licences and inspection outcomes are published by KHDA and change between years, so check the regulator's own listing rather than a prospectus.

sections.heading: What changes between Arabian Ranches and the community next door, and what does not
paragraphs: Set two searches side by side: this page's phrase, and the same phrase with Dubai Hills Estate, Motor City or Mudon in place of the community name. The agencies that appear are the same agencies, the subject lists are the same lists, and in several cases the page is the same page with one noun swapped. A parent could reasonably conclude the whole category is marketing. The more useful conclusion is narrower than that: the inputs which vary between these communities are not the inputs that decide whether tutoring works.

Three things genuinely differ. The drive, because DAMAC Hills 2 is a long way from Al Barsha and Dubai Hills is not. The school mix, because primary provision inside the villa communities is strong while Diploma places mostly sit outside them. And the quoted in-home rate, because a travelling tutor prices distance, so the same person charges more into Remraam than into Dubai Hills Estate. Those are real differences, and this page puts numbers on all three rather than waving at them.

One thing does not differ at all: who can actually teach Higher Level Physics at seven on a Tuesday evening. That pool is small, it is not resident in any of these ten communities, and it does not grow because your villa sits nearer the Hessa Street exit. Which is why the recommendation at the end of every comparison on this page is the same recommendation, and why it is fairer to state it at the start. Choose the teacher on the subject, and run the lesson over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; that is an India-only service, and pretending otherwise on a page about in-home tuition would be the easiest sale available and the wrong one to make.

sections.heading: What an in-home IB tutor costs across this belt, cheapest first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market and work upwards, because the cheap end is where most families start and where most of the disappointment lives. Tutopiya publishes online rates from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. At that level you are buying a university student with the syllabus open in another window. For Year 8 maths practice that can be perfectly adequate. For a second-year Diploma internal assessment it is not, and the hour is cheap because it has to be.

The next band is where most Diploma work actually happens. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts a qualified subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, and the named-examiner end of the market, at BartyED, reaches AED 650. Monthly, Bestimate's estimate for one weekly hour runs AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for exam-year specialist help.

Then the in-home column. Bestimate quotes AED 180 to 350 for a one-to-one visit with travel included, independent providers advertise up to AED 500, and monthly packages appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits against roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Read those two monthly figures next to each other: the in-home package costs around twice as much for half as many sessions. The difference is a car, a parking space and a radius. It is not a teaching difference, and on this belt the radius is the part that costs you most, because it decides which teachers exist for you at all. Every figure here belongs to the provider named, on the date its own page carried that rate; IB Gram quotes no rate card on this page and the first lesson is free.

sections.heading: The drive at four o'clock, community by community
paragraphs: The drive is the one input that really does change between these communities, so it is worth putting numbers on it. The relevant journey is not the morning run, which moves reasonably well in both directions along Al Qudra Road, but the return at four in the afternoon, when Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Hessa Street and the Al Barsha interchanges all work against you at once. A tutor driving in from the schools is making that journey in exactly the same traffic as the school buses.

The figures below are indicative rather than measured, and any parent on this belt will recognise them. What they show is how a sixty-minute lesson becomes a two-hour commitment for a travelling tutor, and why somebody pricing by the hour has to price the travel into it somewhere. They also show why the earliest realistic start time varies by half an hour or more between communities that look adjacent on a map and are not adjacent in traffic.

Read the last column as the operational constraint it is. A second-year Diploma student home at 16:15 needs to eat, and a lesson starting at 16:30 is worse than one starting at 17:00. Push the start to 17:00 or 17:30 and the travelling tutor's window narrows further, because they can now fit one booking into the evening rather than two. An online slot at 19:30 costs nobody a drive, which is why evening availability is wider online by a margin that grows the further out a community sits.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition: the arithmetic from a Dubailand villa
paragraphs: Put the three delivery models in one frame and the decision stops being a matter of preference. Each one buys a different thing. One-to-one online buys the widest possible choice of teacher at the exact hour your child is free. In-home buys a person in the room, paid for with a narrower choice and a travel premium. A group class buys content coverage at a lower price per student, paid for with the loss of the hour being yours.

For some students the in-home option is genuinely the right one. A Year 7 child who will not sit still without an adult beside them is a case for a person in the room, and no amount of arithmetic changes that. For a Diploma student working on a Physics investigation or a Mathematics exploration, the opposite is true: the work is already on a screen, the draft is already a shared document, and a tutor annotating it live from anywhere is doing the job better than one reading it over a shoulder in a kitchen.

The last row of the table is the one most families actually choose and nobody plans. Doing nothing through the first Diploma year and then buying six weeks of specialist help before the papers costs the top of the market, gets the worst slots, and arrives after the internal assessment marks are already submitted. The same money spent across the first year, when there is still time to change how a student writes, buys a different outcome entirely.

sections.heading: Why the same answer serves all ten communities
paragraphs: Here is the comparison that matters, and it has nothing to do with addresses. Diploma teaching capacity in Dubai is distributed by subject and level, not by community. Standard Level Business Management is easy to staff anywhere. Higher Level Physics in an evening slot is hard to staff at all, and it is equally hard whether the student is in Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills or Town Square. Any page that implies otherwise is selling a map when the constraint is a timetable.

Disclosing that limit is unusual in this market, and it should not be. No competitor page researched for this project publishes a coverage limit or a fallback policy; several route UAE parents to numbers in other countries without saying so. The table below is our version, written as the answer to a question a parent should be asking: what happens when the specialist you need is not free, and what will you be offered instead?

The practical consequence for a family on this belt is a short checklist. Name the subject and the level before you name your evening, because the level decides whether there is any flexibility at all. Ask for a stated match time rather than a promise of availability. And ask what the fallback is, in writing, before the first payment. A provider that answers those three questions concretely is telling you more about itself than any testimonial on the page, and a provider that deflects all three is telling you something too.

sections.heading: KHDA inspection bands, and reading them across two neighbouring schools
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are inspected annually by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and the outcome is published on a six-band scale. Families comparing communities usually end up comparing school bands too, and the bands are more slippery than they look. A band is a judgement about a whole school across many measures, and your child attends a department inside it for two years.

That gap matters in a specific way for Diploma families. A school can sit in a high band on the strength of its primary phase, its attendance, its leadership and its inclusion provision, while the department teaching your child's Higher Level subject has lost two staff in eighteen months. The band will not tell you that. Nor will it tell you how many students took the subject at Higher Level last year, which is the single most informative number a parent can ask for and one every school knows.

Dubai's private sector is also expanding fast, which keeps moving the comparison. Seven new private schools are opening for 2026-27, four British curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion. Use the table to read a band for what it is, then ask the department-level questions it cannot answer.

sections.heading: What the UAE Ministry of Education requires for equivalency
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step families forget until it blocks something, and no competitor page researched for this project mentions it at all. If your child intends to use a school qualification for a UAE university place or for certain government processes, the certificate has to be recognised by the Ministry of Education, and the requirements differ by curriculum. They are published, they are specific, and they are worth reading two years before they are needed rather than two weeks.

For the British track the numbers are clear. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. At least one page ranking for queries like this one states that six IGCSE subjects are required; the sourced figure is five.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. For the IB Diploma we publish no points threshold, because none appears in the sources available to us and an unsourced number here would be worse than silence. Verify on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform equivalency, does not submit it on your behalf, and tutoring is not required for it.

sections.heading: Where the line sits on internal assessment, and who may legally tutor
paragraphs: Two boundaries are worth knowing before you hire anyone on this belt, and both have checkable answers. The first is academic honesty. Every Diploma internal assessment, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the skill, discuss the research question, explain what a criterion rewards, read the student's own draft and give written feedback on it. A tutor may never produce any part of the submitted work, and a provider offering to do so is offering your child a malpractice finding.

That matters here more than it should, because this search result contains operations selling completed internal assessments outright at prices in the thousands of dirhams. The consequence of buying one falls on the student, not the seller. Our position is deliberately dull: feedback in writing as comments on criteria, never edits inside the submitted file, and every draft kept and dated so the development of the work is visible if a coordinator ever asks to see it.

The second boundary is legal. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with no fee and a stated two-working-day completion time on MoHRE's own service page. Teachers in government or private schools, public and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 may all apply. People tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published, so treat any figure you see quoted with suspicion. A centre with premises and staff needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute instead, which is a different thing entirely.

sections.heading: Booking from Arabian Ranches, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The practical sequence is short. Send the subject, the level, the school and the evening window that works after the bus arrives. Attach the last report and, if there is one, the marked internal assessment draft. That is enough to decide whether we have the right teacher free, and it takes a few minutes rather than a consultation call. The trial lesson is free, with the condition stated plainly: one session, before any payment, with written feedback afterwards so the teaching can be judged on its own.

If the match is wrong, we change the teacher rather than asking you to persevere. If the right specialist is not free for the slot you need, you get told that, along with the options: a different evening, a short wait, or a teacher whose subject depth we describe accurately before you decide anything. On a page comparing ten communities it is worth being explicit that this is the one variable your address does not improve. A villa in Dubai Hills does not make a Higher Level Physics specialist appear on a Tuesday at seven.

Scheduling flexes with the UAE year in two predictable ways. Ramadan shortens school hours and families across the Dubailand communities move an afternoon slot to after Iftar; an online lesson absorbs that without renegotiating a drive. The long summer empties much of this belt, and a student in London, Mumbai or Toronto in July keeps the same teacher and the same slot, time-converted. Both of those are ordinary requests here, and neither of them works at all when the arrangement depends on somebody's car.

process.title: Send the subject and the level, then the evening
process.description: Name the course and whether it is Higher or Standard Level first, because that decides whether there is any scheduling flexibility. Then give the window that works once the bus has arrived in your community. A subject without a level produces a shortlist that collapses the moment the real requirement appears.

process.title: Attach the report and any marked draft
process.description: The last school report and a marked internal assessment draft tell a teacher more in two minutes than a phone call does in twenty. They show which component is losing marks rather than which topic feels hard, and those are frequently different things in the second Diploma year.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson on its own terms
process.description: One lesson at no charge, booked before any payment and with no card details taken beforehand. It is a working session: the teacher looks at the draft, teaches one component and sends written feedback. Judge it on whether your child understood something new, not on how the call felt.

process.title: Fix the slot for the term, then let it move
process.description: Lessons run live online on Gulf Standard Time, so the slot is held for the term and can shift for Ramadan, mock examinations or a trip without changing teacher. Families on this belt use that more than they expect to, because nothing in the arrangement depends on traffic on Al Qudra Road.

process.title: Review on the next report, and stop if it is not working
process.description: The test is the grade and the teacher's comment on the next school report, not a feeling after four sessions. At that point we continue, change the teacher, or stop. If no specialist is available for your subject and slot, you are told so rather than quietly handed somebody approximate.

whyPoints.title: The comparison is run with numbers, not adjectives
whyPoints.description: Travel times, published AED rates and monthly package figures are set out on this page with the provider that published each one. Three of the pages ranking for queries like this publish no price in any currency, and two quote US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject scarcity, not on your address
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Physics, Economics and Analysis and Approaches are the courses this belt is short of, and no community within it has more of them than another. Matching across the whole pool and teaching over video is the only move that actually widens your choice.

whyPoints.title: The coverage limit is published
whyPoints.description: There is a table on this page naming which subjects are thin, what the typical match time is, and what you are offered when nobody is free. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a foreign phone number.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what in-home tuition is and is not
whyPoints.description: The in-home market is described here with its real rates because that is what the search phrase means. IB Gram does not sell it in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. Saying so on this page rather than in a footnote is the point of writing it honestly.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits on coursework and on claims
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reviews the student's own drafts and gives written feedback. No part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is produced for a student, and no grade is promised by anyone here. Both limits are stated rather than implied.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a home tutor to a villa in Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending tutors to houses is a service we operate in India only. Teaching for families in Arabian Ranches is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so working, past papers and internal assessment drafts are visible to both sides. The practical gain is the size of the pool: instead of choosing from teachers willing to drive out to Al Qudra Road at five o'clock, you choose from everyone who can teach the course at the hour your child is actually free.

faqs.question: Is it easier to find an IB tutor in Arabian Ranches or in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: Marginally easier in Dubai Hills, and only for in-home tuition. Dubai Hills sits closer to the schools that employ Diploma teachers, so a travelling tutor can reach it inside twenty-five minutes at four in the afternoon and can fit two bookings into an evening. From Arabian Ranches the same trip is twenty-five to forty minutes and usually means one booking. For online teaching the difference is zero: the same teachers are available to both communities at the same times, which is why this page gives both the same recommendation.

faqs.question: What does an in-home IB lesson cost in Dubai once travel is priced in?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour with travel included, and independent providers advertise up to AED 500. Monthly packages appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits, against roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Set those two monthly figures side by side and the in-home option is around twice the money for half the sessions. The gap pays for a car and a radius rather than for better teaching, and those are the providers' own published numbers, not ours.

faqs.question: We are moving from Arabian Ranches to Mudon. Does the tutoring arrangement change?
faqs.answer: Not at all, which is one of the quieter advantages of online delivery on this belt. The teacher, the slot and the plan carry over, because nothing in the arrangement depends on which community the villa sits in. An in-home booking would change: the drive from the Al Barsha schools to Mudon runs thirty-five to fifty minutes at four in the afternoon rather than twenty-five to forty, which usually means a later start, a higher quoted rate, or a tutor who declines the booking altogether once they see the postcode.

faqs.question: Which IB schools serve Arabian Ranches and the Dubailand communities?
faqs.answer: Diploma places within reach sit mostly in Dubai Hills, Nad Al Sheba, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim, including GEMS International School Al Khail, North London Collegiate School Dubai and GEMS World Academy Dubai, with Fairgreen International School inside the Dubailand area itself. Primary provision inside the communities is far stronger, which is the asymmetry this page is about. Programme licences change between academic years, so confirm what each school is licensed to offer on its own KHDA listing. IB Gram has no affiliation with any school named here.

faqs.question: How long is the drive from Al Barsha to Arabian Ranches at four in the afternoon?
faqs.answer: Indicatively twenty-five to forty minutes, against fifteen to twenty in the morning, because Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Hessa Street and the Al Barsha interchanges are all busy at once. For a travelling tutor that turns a sixty-minute lesson into a two-hour commitment, which is why the travel appears in the hourly rate. It also pushes the earliest realistic start for a student arriving home around 16:00 to roughly 17:00, once eating is accounted for. An online slot at 19:30 removes the constraint entirely for both sides.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who lives in Motor City better than one who does not drive at all?
faqs.answer: Only if they teach the right course well. Proximity is a scheduling convenience, not a qualification, and on Higher Level courses the two things pull in opposite directions: the nearer the pool, the smaller it is. The sensible test is to ask both candidates the same subject question. For a Physics investigation, ask how they would handle uncertainty propagation in the student's own data set. The answer separates a physics graduate from somebody who has taught the current Diploma course, and distance has nothing to do with it.

faqs.question: Why do in-home rates vary so much between neighbouring Dubai communities?
faqs.answer: Because the tutor is pricing the return journey. A travelling tutor living near the Al Barsha or Dubai Hills schools can reach Dubai Hills Estate quickly, Arabian Ranches less quickly, and Remraam or DAMAC Hills 2 only by giving up a second booking that evening. The rate rises to cover the booking they cannot take. That is a rational way to price a car, and it is also the clearest signal that what you are paying for at the top of the in-home range is distance rather than expertise.

faqs.question: Can two children in one Arabian Ranches villa share a single IB session?
faqs.answer: Rarely usefully, unless they are in the same year taking the same course at the same level. Diploma subjects diverge quickly, and an hour split between a Higher Level Chemistry student and a Standard Level Economics student gives neither child a proper lesson. Consecutive one-to-one slots on the same evening work better: one quiet room, one evening disturbed, two specific lessons. Where both children genuinely sit the same course, a paired session is reasonable and we will say so rather than selling two hours.

faqs.question: Does a higher KHDA inspection band mean my child needs less support?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. A band is a judgement about a whole school across many inspected areas, and your child attends one department inside it for two years. A school can sit in a high band on the strength of its primary phase, leadership and inclusion provision while the department teaching a Higher Level subject has lost staff. The more useful questions are specific: how many students sat that subject at Higher Level last year, who teaches it now, and what support exists around internal assessment deadlines.

faqs.question: What does the UAE Ministry of Education require from an IB student for equivalency?
faqs.answer: We do not publish a figure, and that is deliberate. The British-track requirements are sourced and specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No IB points threshold appears in the sources available to us, so publishing one would be guesswork on a page thousands of families read. Verify on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority, and note that tutoring is not required for equivalency.

faqs.question: Do my child's IGCSE grades count towards UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Yes, on the British track. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. One page ranking for queries like this states that six subjects are needed; the sourced figure is five, which is the kind of error worth checking at the source rather than inheriting. The requirement sits alongside the Advanced Level condition, so a student on a pure IGCSE route still has an A Level or AS Level step to satisfy.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma internal assessment may a tutor touch?
faqs.answer: The line is the text itself. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, discuss whether a research question is answerable, teach the statistical or analytical technique the task needs, read a draft the student wrote and give written feedback on it. A tutor may not write sentences that end up in the submission, restructure the work by rewriting it, or supply data. Keep every draft dated and keep feedback as comments on criteria rather than edits inside the file, and the distinction stays visible to anyone who asks.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working in Arabian Ranches need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services system. School teachers, public and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 may all apply. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since the permit costs nothing there is no excuse for not holding it.

faqs.question: What if nobody is free for Higher Level Economics on a Sunday evening?
faqs.answer: You get told, with options. Higher Level Economics is one of the courses this belt is genuinely short of, and the honest answers are a different evening, a short wait for a slot to open, or a specialist outside the UAE whose time zone we state before you agree to anything. What we will not do is fill the hour with a strong generalist and let you discover the gap from the next report. Disclosing that in advance is unusual in this market and it is the policy anyway.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a Motor City centre better value than one-to-one online?
faqs.answer: For content coverage in a shared syllabus, often yes: the price per student is lower and a well-run group moves faster than a lone student will. For a specific weakness or an internal assessment, no, because the hour belongs to the group and your child's particular gap may never come up. There is also the drive each way to count. Centres operating with premises and staff need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is worth asking to see before enrolling.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches.closingHeading: One answer for ten communities, and the numbers behind it
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches.closingBody: If you are weighing an in-home tutor in Arabian Ranches against the same search in Ranches 2, Dubai Hills, Mudon or Remraam, the figures on this page should settle it. intro.heading: The school run is the reason this search exists
paragraphs: Arabian Ranches 2 sits between Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Al Qudra Road, south of the original Arabian Ranches and north of Mudon and Arabian Ranches 3. It is a villa community with a souk at its centre, a British-curriculum primary school inside the gates and no Diploma Programme provision within walking distance of any of it. For a family with a DP1 or DP2 student, that geography sets the shape of the week before anyone discusses tutoring: the child leaves early, returns late, and the first usable academic window opens somewhere after five.

That window is what a search for an IB home tutor in Arabian Ranches 2 is really about. Parents here are not shopping for a venue. They are trying to recover the hour that the drive to Al Barsha South, Dubai Sports City or the Sustainable City removes from the afternoon, and the obvious way to recover it looks like booking somebody who turns up at the gate. That is one answer. In this part of Dubailand it is rarely the quickest one, and the research below shows it is not the cheapest either.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one tuition over live video. We do not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; door-to-door tutoring is a service offered only in India. The reason is not administrative tidiness. A Diploma student taking Chemistry at Higher Level needs a teacher who has taught Chemistry at Higher Level, and the number of those inside a twenty-minute radius of Ranches Souk is small enough that most families settle for a capable generalist who is reading the subject guide on the way over.

Online changes what you are choosing between. Instead of the tutors who happen to live near the Ranches, the choice becomes the tutors who teach your child's exact course: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level rather than maths, Biology Higher Level rather than science, Economics Standard Level with the commentary deadline already in view. Lessons are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, the screen and the working are shared both ways, and the work a student submits stays the student's own. Nothing travels, so nothing is billed for travel, and a five o'clock slot does not require somebody to leave somewhere else at twenty past four.

The rest of this page is written from the clock rather than from a brochure. Which schools this neighbourhood actually feeds, roughly what time each of them finishes, what the return leg does to the afternoon, and where in the evening a sixty- or ninety-minute session can sit without colliding with homework, a swim squad at Dubai Sports City, or a Friday that finishes at lunchtime. Every AED figure quoted is a market rate from a named source, never a price list of ours.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-2.programmesIntro: Arabian Ranches 2 families arrive at the Diploma by two routes: through the Middle Years Programme at an IB continuum school, or through IGCSE at a British school followed by a switch at sixteen. The three programmes below are the ones that matter for this neighbourhood, each with a note written from a Dubailand villa rather than in general terms.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subject syllabuses, and it closes with the Year 6 Exhibition. There is no external examination, which means a parent's only reliable signal is the school's own reporting against learning outcomes. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining a method out loud, because those are what the Middle Years Programme will start grading.
programmes.countryNote: Arabian Ranches 2 children in the PYP are mostly bussing to continuum schools in the Sustainable City or Al Barsha South, so the day is long for an eight-year-old. A thirty-minute online slot twice a week lands better here than a single hour, and it fits after the bus and before dinner without turning the evening into a second school day.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP grades each subject against four criteria, A to D, on an eight-point scale, and converts the total to a 1-7 subject grade using published boundaries. Criterion wording is the thing students misread: a task asking them to analyse is not asking them to describe. Year 11 ends with the Personal Project, which is assessed on its process journal and the student's own reflection as much as on the product.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Arabian Ranches 2 parents most often discover a gap, because MYP reporting looks reassuring until the DP1 maths and sciences start. Families with a child in MYP 4 or 5 are the ones who benefit most from booking a subject-specific review before the DP subject choices are locked, usually in the spring term of Year 11.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment set and marked in school against published criteria and then externally moderated. The Higher Level papers are longer, carry additional content and, in several subjects, add a third paper that Standard Level candidates never sit. UAE schools sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Arabian Ranches 2 are travelling to JESS Arabian Ranches, Fairgreen International School, North London Collegiate School Dubai, Nord Anglia International School Dubai or Dwight School Dubai. That spread is why the evening slot matters so much here: a DP2 student back at 16:15 from Al Barsha South cannot sensibly start Higher Level content before five, and the honest answer is to protect two fixed evenings rather than four scattered ones.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-2.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects below are the ones Arabian Ranches 2 families book most often, with a note on what each one actually assesses and where marks go missing. Availability is confirmed before you pay, and where a Higher Level specialist is not free in Gulf Standard Time we say so rather than substitute somebody from a neighbouring subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-and-proof route, with a no-calculator Paper 1 that catches students who have learned to lean on a graphics calculator. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a two-part extended investigation worth 20 per cent of the grade. Most lost marks are notation and unjustified steps rather than genuine gaps in method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with a graphics calculator permitted in every paper. Students who chose this expecting an easier course find the Higher Level statistics and the regression work demanding. Marks go in interpretation: a correct value with no sentence saying what it means in context scores less than students expect.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level carries additional content Standard Level candidates never sit, and organic mechanisms plus energetics are where the grade is usually decided. The Internal Assessment is a single scientific investigation of the student's own design, assessed on research design, data analysis and conclusion, which is where most of the avoidable marks sit.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics is taught first and examined last, so DP2 students often arrive at the paper with the oldest topic least secure. Uncertainties and significant figures quietly remove marks in the data-analysis questions. Higher Level fields and the extended topics are what separate a 5 from a 7 in practice.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume of defined terminology makes this a recall-plus-application subject rather than a reading subject. Command terms matter: outline, explain and evaluate carry different mark allocations for the same content. The investigation needs a measurable, controllable variable, and a poorly chosen one costs more marks than weak writing ever will.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries drawn from published news articles, each tied to a different unit of the course, form the Internal Assessment. Diagrams carry marks on their own: axes labelled, equilibrium shifted, the change explained in the student's own words. Higher Level adds quantitative questions that trip students who treated the subject as essay-only.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under timed conditions, which rewards a repeatable approach far more than wide reading. The Individual Oral links a global issue to two texts and is internally assessed. Higher Level adds the HL Essay, a formal 1,200 to 1,500-word piece on one text studied.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based rather than theory-based: students are expected to apply named frameworks to a real organisation and justify the choice of tool. The Internal Assessment is a research project on a genuine business issue. Marks are lost in evaluation, where answers summarise findings instead of weighing them against the question asked.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition in DP1 and the prescribed-title essay in DP2, graded A to E and contributing to the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. Students treat it as an opinion piece and lose marks for unexamined claims. Supply of specialist tutors is genuinely thin, and we say so when it is.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: A tutor can help a student narrow a researchable question, test whether the sources exist before the writing starts, and read a draft against the assessment criteria. A tutor cannot draft, rewrite or finish it. That boundary is set by IB academic-honesty rules and it is not negotiable at any price.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in Arabian Ranches 2 actually gets you
paragraphs: It gets you one-to-one Diploma Programme teaching delivered live online, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor matched to the exact course and level your child sits. It does not get you somebody at the villa door. IB Gram does not operate home visits in the UAE, and saying so on the page is more useful than letting a parent discover it on a phone call.

The phrase itself is worth taking seriously rather than correcting. Families type home tutor because they want the lesson to happen where the child already is, without another car journey at the end of a long day. That requirement is real and it is the one thing online delivery satisfies completely: the lesson happens in the room the child is already sitting in, and the only travel involved is from the kitchen to wherever the laptop lives.

What changes is the pool. A tutor who has to reach Arabian Ranches 2 by road is drawn from whoever lives in Dubailand, Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Al Barsha and has a free evening. A tutor who teaches over live video is drawn from everyone who teaches that subject at that level in a compatible time zone. For Standard Level support in a broad subject the difference is modest. For Chemistry Higher Level, Analysis and Approaches Higher Level or Theory of Knowledge, the difference is the whole decision.

One more practical consequence. Because nobody drives anywhere, a cancelled or moved session costs nothing in wasted travel, which is why rescheduling by notice is straightforward rather than a negotiation. Families in this community reschedule more than they expect to, usually for a sports fixture or a school trip, and a format that absorbs that without a surcharge is worth more over a term than a slightly lower hourly rate.

sections.heading: The Arabian Ranches 2 school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: Arabian Ranches 2 has a primary school inside the community and nothing above it, so almost every secondary student here commutes. The table below sets out the schools this neighbourhood actually feeds, their approximate road distance from Ranches Souk, a typical weekday finish and the earliest hour at which a tutoring session is realistically worth starting. Finish times vary by year group and by term, so treat them as the shape of the day rather than a timetable.

Two features of the Dubai school week matter more than distance. The private-school week runs Monday to Friday with a short Friday, which means Friday afternoon is the single most underused academic slot available to a Diploma student in this community. And the afternoon peak on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Al Qudra Road overlaps exactly with school dismissal, so the return leg is consistently slower than the same trip at eleven in the morning.

The earliest realistic session column is deliberately conservative. It assumes the child gets through the door, eats something and sits down, which in practice takes longer than parents allow for when they book a slot. A session that starts fifteen minutes late every week loses most of a lesson over a term, so the better move is to book the later slot and keep it than to book the earlier one and apologise for it.

For families running two children on different buses, the arrival spread is usually thirty to forty minutes. Where that is the case, the workable pattern is one fixed evening per child on different days rather than two sessions stacked on the same evening, because the second one always lands in homework time and the student is already done.

sections.heading: Why a quarter past four is the wrong start time for a DP2 student here
paragraphs: Parents book the earliest slot the schedule technically allows, because it leaves the evening free. For a Year 12 or Year 13 student coming off a long commute, that choice reliably produces the worst hour of the week. The student is physically present and cognitively finished, the tutor spends twenty minutes rebuilding attention, and the family concludes that tutoring is not working when the problem was the clock.

The Diploma load makes this sharper than it is at other levels. A DP2 student is carrying six subjects, four of which will have an Internal Assessment deadline inside the same eight-week window, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Their afternoon already contains obligations. Dropping a Higher Level session into the first available gap means it competes with the school's own deadlines rather than supporting them.

The pattern that works in Arabian Ranches 2 is a later start with a protected shape: arrive home, eat, thirty minutes of nothing, then a focused sixty or ninety minutes beginning between five and half past seven depending on the cluster and the sports schedule. Where a family runs co-curriculars at Dubai Sports City or Arabian Ranches Golf Club two evenings a week, the sensible answer is to accept a seven o'clock slot on the free evenings rather than squeeze a session in before the fixture.

Friday is the exception worth planning around. With a short school day across Dubai private schools, a Friday session sits on a rested student with no commute behind it and nothing scheduled after it. For Higher Level content and for Internal Assessment work, where thinking rather than drilling is required, a single Friday session frequently outperforms two weekday evenings.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition compared for a Dubailand villa community
paragraphs: This is the comparison the market avoids publishing. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this project quote no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family pays in. The figures below are AED market rates taken from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They describe what the market charges, not what IB Gram charges.

Read the travel column first, because in Arabian Ranches 2 it is the column that decides the others. An in-home rate of AED 180-500 an hour includes the tutor's travel, and it is quoted that way because the travel is real: crossing Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road or Al Qudra Road between half past three and half past six is not a fifteen-minute proposition. A tutor who can only fit two visits into an evening prices accordingly.

The second thing the table shows is where specialisation actually costs money. A budget online tutor at AED 45-150 an hour is a reasonable way to supervise homework and keep a Standard Level subject ticking. It is not a way to move a Chemistry Higher Level grade, because the person is usually not a Chemistry Higher Level teacher. The specialist band at AED 200-450 and above buys course-exact teaching, and for one or two subjects in DP2 that is the band most families end up in.

Group classes deserve one honest line. A monthly package advertised in this market at around AED 799 for eight online sessions looks like strong value until you notice it is a group rate and the group is not at your child's level. For topic revision where everyone is sitting the same paper, group teaching works. For a student who is losing marks for a reason specific to them, it does not.

sections.heading: The Diploma calendar counted backwards from a villa in Casa or Rosa
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, and the May session is not the deadline that bites first. The deadlines that shape a DP2 student's year are internal: the school's own submission dates for each Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay drafts and the Theory of Knowledge essay. Those sit months before any examination and they are set by the school, not by the IB, which is why two students in the same community can be working to different dates.

Precise IB session and results dates are deliberately not published here. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and a wrong date on a page like this is worse than no date. Ask your child's Diploma coordinator for the school's internal calendar and confirm the external dates with them or on ibo.org. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications, the published dates further down the IGCSE pages in this set are sourced and usable.

Working backwards is the useful exercise. If an Internal Assessment is due to the school in the second half of DP2 term one, the data collection has to be finished a month earlier, the research question has to be agreed a month before that, and the point at which a tutor can genuinely help is at the question stage, not at the draft stage. Families who book support in the week before a deadline are buying proofreading, which is both the least valuable and the most ethically constrained thing a tutor does.

The same logic applies to the Extended Essay. A 4,000-word piece needs its sources tested for existence before the student commits to the question. Half the Extended Essay problems a tutor sees are not writing problems; they are questions that cannot be answered with the material the student can actually reach from Dubai.
