sections.heading: Academic honesty: what an IB tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: A tutor may teach content, model a method, explain what a criterion rewards, read a student's own draft and say which criterion it is currently losing marks under. A tutor may not write, rewrite, draft, edit to completion or supply any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project. That boundary is set by the IB's academic-honesty framework and it applies to paid support exactly as it applies to a parent.

This is not a theoretical concern in this market. One site examined during research sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. A student who submits purchased work faces an academic-misconduct investigation and, where it is upheld, the loss of the qualification. No grade is worth that exposure, and no tutor who offers it is protecting your child.

The practical version of the rule is simple to police as a parent. Ask to see the feedback the tutor gave, not just the improved draft. Criterion-referenced feedback looks like a list of criteria with a note against each; completion looks like prose that suddenly sounds like somebody else. If the draft improves and the student cannot explain why, something has gone wrong regardless of what anybody intended.

We also do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those are the boards' copyright. Tutors reference them, cite them and point families to the official source, which is also the only version guaranteed to be current.

sections.heading: What a KHDA inspection band actually tells an Arabian Ranches 2 parent
paragraphs: KHDA is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, and under the UAE government's own description it is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. It inspects private schools annually and publishes an overall judgement on a six-band scale from Outstanding through Very Good, Good, Acceptable and Weak to Very Weak. That report is public and it is the only school-quality signal on this page worth reading.

What the band does not tell you is how your child's specific subject at Higher Level is taught. A school can hold a strong overall judgement while a particular department is thin, usually because of a mid-year staffing change. Conversely a school in a lower band may have an outstanding Physics teacher. Parents in this community occasionally make a tutoring decision on the strength of the inspection headline when the subject-level detail inside the report is the part that matters.

Dubai's private-school sector is large enough that these bands are the practical filter: KHDA figures for 2024-25 record 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. The IB share is small, which is exactly why IB specialist supply is thinner than general tutoring supply.

Two further facts are useful context for a family budgeting a year of support. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private-school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package the authority valued at AED 1.5 billion. And the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools in Dubai, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Read inspection reports on KHDA's own site, never from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: Tutor coverage for this neighbourhood, and what happens when a subject is not covered
paragraphs: No competitor page examined for this project discloses a coverage limit. Several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas phone number. The table below is the alternative: what we can usually staff for an Arabian Ranches 2 family, roughly how long a match takes, and what we do when the specialist a student needs is not available in Gulf Standard Time.

The honest position on a thin subject is to say so. Theory of Knowledge is the clearest example: demand concentrates in DP2 when the prescribed-title essay lands, supply is small because few teachers specialise in it, and substituting a subject teacher produces confident advice that does not match the assessment criteria. Where we cannot staff it, the useful answer is a referral back to the school's own Theory of Knowledge lead rather than a booking.

Where a specialist is not UAE-based, we widen the search to tutors teaching in a compatible time zone and tell you before you book. Gulf Standard Time is four hours ahead of UTC, which keeps an early-evening Dubai slot inside the working day for tutors across South Asia and comfortably inside the afternoon for tutors in the United Kingdom. The constraint is not geography but the student's own evening.

Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit in a separate category. KHDA requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects in Dubai schools, and the mandatory content itself may not be varied without prior Ministry of Education permission. For those subjects the first conversation belongs with the school, and we say that rather than taking a booking we should not take.

Then the honest earliest start time given your cluster in Arabian Ranches 2 and your child's school. Those two facts determine whether we can match a specialist, and they take about four minutes to supply.

process.title: We check availability before you commit to anything

We tell you which, name the tutor, state their qualification and board experience, and say if they are outside the UAE. If we cannot cover the subject at the level you need, you hear that instead of being matched with the nearest approximate person.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with no card details taken
process.description: One full lesson at no cost so the student meets the tutor before any money changes hands. The trial is a real lesson on real content, not a sales call: the tutor diagnoses where marks are going and says so at the end. No payment details are required to book it and there is no obligation afterwards.

process.title: Fix the slot and keep it for the term
process.description: The same evening each week with the same tutor, written into the family calendar next to the school run and the sports fixtures. Work is set between sessions and reviewed at the start of the next one. Sessions can be moved by notice without penalty, because nobody has made a journey that cannot be recovered.

process.title: Review against the school's own reporting
process.description: Every half term, compare what the tutor is seeing against the school's reports and the student's own marked work. If the two disagree, that is information worth acting on. If the subject no longer needs support, the sensible outcome is to stop that subject rather than to carry it to the end of the term.

whyPoints.title: The tutor matches the course, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Online delivery removes distance from the selection, so the question becomes who teaches Analysis and Approaches Higher Level rather than who teaches maths and lives near Dubailand. For Standard Level support the difference is modest. For Higher Level sciences and maths in DP2 it is the difference that shows up in the grade.

whyPoints.title: Timing built around the Dubailand school run
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time and set after the realistic arrival time for your child's school, not at the first slot the calendar allows. Friday's short school day is treated as the strongest revision window of the week rather than as an afterthought, because for Higher Level content it usually is.

whyPoints.title: No travel, so no travel in the price
whyPoints.description: Market in-home rates of AED 180-500 an hour include the tutor's road time across E311 or Al Qudra Road in the dismissal peak. Nothing travels in an online session, so the hour you pay for is an hour of teaching, and a session moved for a school trip costs nobody a wasted journey.

whyPoints.title: Clear academic-honesty boundaries, stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, model and give criterion-referenced feedback on the student's own work. They do not write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. In a market where completed coursework is openly sold, saying where the line sits is the most useful thing a tutoring page can do.

whyPoints.title: Figures and facts with their sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, every regulatory statement to the authority that issued it, and no IB examination date is published because the IB's own site could not be checked automatically. Numbers without a source are not reassurance, they are a liability.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed rather than hidden
whyPoints.description: Where a specialist is not available in Gulf Standard Time, you are told before booking, including whether the tutor is based outside the UAE. Theory of Knowledge and KHDA-approved Arabic and Islamic Education are the two areas we routinely decline, and declining is more useful to a family than an approximate match.

faqs.question: Can I book an IB home tutor who comes to our villa in Arabian Ranches 2?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; door-to-door tutoring is a service we offer only in India. What we provide for Arabian Ranches 2 is one-to-one Diploma teaching delivered live online, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, so the lesson still happens in the room your child is already sitting in. The practical gain is the tutor pool: instead of whoever can reach your gate between dismissal and dinner, you get the person who actually teaches your child's course at your child's level. The practical loss is that no adult is physically in the room, which matters more for a nine-year-old than for a DP2 student.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start if my child finishes school at 15:15?
faqs.answer: For a secondary student bussing back to Arabian Ranches 2 from Al Barsha South or the Sustainable City, 17:00 is the first slot that works properly and 17:30 is safer. The return leg overlaps the afternoon peak on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Al Qudra Road, and the student then needs to eat and decompress. For the schools closest to the community, including JESS Arabian Ranches at roughly three kilometres, 16:30 is usually achievable. Booking the earliest technically possible hour is the most common scheduling mistake families here make: a session that starts fifteen minutes late every week loses most of a lesson across a term.

faqs.question: Which schools do Arabian Ranches 2 children actually attend for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: There is no Diploma Programme provision inside the community, so Diploma students commute. The nearest option is JESS Arabian Ranches, which runs IGCSE and then the IB Diploma about three kilometres away. Beyond that, the cluster most used from here covers Fairgreen International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai in the Sustainable City, and Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Dwight School Dubai and Repton Al Barsha in Al Barsha South. A smaller group travels to Emirates International School Meadows or Sunmarke School. These schools are named as neighbourhood context; no affiliation is implied, and inspection reports should be read on KHDA's own site.

faqs.question: Is Friday actually a usable day for IB tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It is the best day of the week for it, and almost nobody uses it. Dubai private schools run a Monday to Friday week with a short Friday, so the student arrives home early, rested and with no commute behind them. For Higher Level content and Internal Assessment work, where the task is thinking rather than drilling, one Friday session frequently achieves more than two tired weekday evenings. Families in Arabian Ranches 2 who protect a Friday slot tend to keep it, because nothing else competes for the hour. The main constraint is family plans, since Friday afternoon is also when weekends start in practice.

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor cost per hour for a family in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not ours. A qualified subject tutor working online is commonly AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IB specialists sit at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table quoting AED 200-450+. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180-500 once travel is included. Budget and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45-150. Monthly packages around AED 799 for eight online sessions appear in this market, usually as group rates. IB Gram does not publish a rate card here; the free trial and the consultation are where our own pricing is discussed.

faqs.question: Does a 90-minute session work better than two 60-minute ones in DP2?
faqs.answer: For Internal Assessment work and Higher Level problem-solving, yes. Both need a run-up: the student has to reload where they were, and twenty minutes of a sixty-minute session can disappear into that. Ninety minutes gives one proper working block. For content catch-up, vocabulary-heavy subjects or anything that needs repetition, two shorter sessions on different evenings beat one long one, because spacing is doing the work. Most Arabian Ranches 2 families settle on ninety minutes for the subject causing the most trouble and sixty for the second subject. The deciding factor is usually the school run rather than the pedagogy.

faqs.question: My child is at Ranches Primary School — is tutoring sensible this early?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and rarely in the form parents imagine. At primary age the useful targets are reading fluency, number facts and the habit of explaining a method aloud, because those are what the Middle Years Programme will later grade against criteria. What does not help is a sixty-minute evening session after a long bus ride. Two thirty-minute online slots a week, early enough to be before dinner, fit this age group far better. If the school's own reporting is not flagging a gap, the honest advice is usually to wait and spend the money in Year 9 or 10 instead.

faqs.question: How do online lessons handle a maths question that needs working shown?
faqs.answer: Through a shared writing surface rather than a talking head. The tutor and the student both write on the same digital whiteboard, so the tutor sees the working develop line by line and can stop at the line where it goes wrong, which is the only place a maths correction is useful. Students photograph a handwritten page and drop it in when they prefer paper, which many Analysis and Approaches students do for proofs. The session is recorded on request so the student can revisit the method. For a no-calculator Paper 1 technique, this works at least as well as sitting side by side.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics HL and Mathematics AA HL for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking because the overlap is real: Higher Level Physics leans on calculus and algebraic manipulation that Analysis and Approaches teaches directly. A tutor comfortable with both can use one subject to reinforce the other. The risk is a tutor who is strong in one and adequate in the other, which produces a reasonable Physics hour and a weak maths hour at the same price. We tell you which subject the tutor's qualification and recent teaching actually sit in, and if the honest answer is that they should only take one of the two, that is what we recommend.

faqs.question: What exactly can an IB tutor do with my child's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, help narrow a research question before the writing starts, check whether the data or sources are actually obtainable, and read the student's own draft and say which criterion it is currently losing marks under. What a tutor must not do is write, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of it. One provider examined during research sells completed Internal Assessments outright; a student submitting purchased work risks an academic-misconduct finding and the loss of the qualification. Ask to see the feedback, not just the improved draft.

faqs.question: How does an Arabian Ranches 2 parent check a tutor has a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring is regulated through a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection band tell me about my child's school?
faqs.answer: KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, is responsible for overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects schools annually, publishing an overall judgement on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. The band is a reliable summary of the school and a poor guide to one subject at one level, because a single staffing change can leave a strong school with a thin department. Read the subject detail inside the report rather than the headline, and read it on KHDA's own site. No tutoring page, including this one, should be your source for a school's rating.

faqs.question: Can our session move later during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it usually should. School hours are reduced during Ramadan across the UAE, so the afternoon looks different and the evening is organised around Iftar. The pattern most Arabian Ranches 2 families move to is a later start after Iftar, or a daytime slot on the short school days, with a slightly shorter session length. Because nothing has to travel, moving the slot for the month costs nothing and reverts afterwards. Tell us at the start of the month rather than week by week, so the tutor's whole Ramadan schedule is set once and your slot is not the one that gets squeezed.

faqs.question: We travel over the winter break — can lessons follow the family?
faqs.answer: They can, with one caveat about time zones. An online session needs a stable connection and an agreed hour, both of which usually survive travel. The caveat is that Gulf Standard Time is four hours ahead of UTC, so a Dubai evening slot becomes an inconvenient afternoon or morning slot depending on where you go. The workable approach is to agree the holiday hours before you leave and to reduce frequency rather than attempt the normal pattern from a hotel. Many DP2 families use the break for a short Internal Assessment block instead, which travels better than content teaching does.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor is not the right fit for my child?
faqs.answer: You say so and we change the tutor, which is why the free trial exists before any payment. Fit at Diploma level is rarely about warmth; it is usually about pace and about whether the tutor explains in the register the student thinks in. A mismatch shows up inside two sessions, and the signal to watch for is a student who stops asking questions. When we re-match, the new tutor gets the previous diagnosis, so the term does not restart from zero. If the subject turns out not to need support at all, the useful recommendation is to stop it rather than to carry it.

Lessons are one-to-one and delivered live online in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the Diploma subjects Arabian Ranches 3 families ask for most: Mathematics at both routes, the three sciences at Higher Level, Economics, English Language and Literature, and core supervision for the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Each one teaches a named syllabus, not a general subject.

intro.heading: Arabian Ranches 3, the Diploma, and the gap a tutor is hired to close
paragraphs: Arabian Ranches 3 is a handover community. Families arrived with the school run already decided, because there is no secondary campus inside the gates and the Diploma is taught somewhere else: Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Nord Anglia International School Dubai in Al Barsha South, Dubai International Academy, GEMS World Academy Dubai. The bus leaves early and comes back late. By the time a DP2 student is through the door, changed and fed, the evening holds perhaps two usable hours, and one of those is already spoken for by whatever the school set that day.

That is the gap a parent is describing when they type IB home tutor in Arabian Ranches 3 into Google. The phrase is about place; the problem is time and specificity. A tutor living three communities away costs the family forty minutes of driving at each end and may still not teach the right syllabus. A tutor matched on syllabus instead, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level rather than the word maths, costs nothing in travel and starts the moment the student sits down.

So the honest position first. IB Gram does not send anyone to a villa in Arabian Ranches 3, or anywhere else in the UAE, and we do not make home visits in Dubai: those are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard the student writes on and a recording the family keeps. The keyword in this page's title is the phrase parents search. The delivery underneath it is online, and the rest of this page argues why that is the better buy for a Dubailand villa rather than a compromise a family tolerates.

The second thing worth saying early is that the Diploma is not six subjects. It is six subject grades out of seven, plus up to three points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge read together, plus a Creativity, Activity, Service requirement that awards no points at all and can still stop a diploma being issued. Families who hire a tutor for maths and leave the core alone are often leaving the cheapest points on the table. A student predicted 34 with a C and a C in the core sits in a measurably different place from the same student holding an A and a B.

This page is written from that structure outwards: what each component demands, where the marks actually leave, what the Dubai market charges for help with it in dirhams, and what a tutor is permitted to touch on work that has to be the student's own. Where a figure appears, the source is named. Where a date matters, an entry deadline or a results window, the page points at the board's own timetable rather than restating something that can be revised without notice.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.programmesIntro: Arabian Ranches 3 children are spread across the full IB ladder, because the Dubailand ring contains continuum schools, British schools that switch to the Diploma at 16, and American schools that offer it alongside Advanced Placement. The four programmes below are the ones families here are choosing between, with what each means for tutoring in Dubai specifically.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations and no published grades, which is exactly why parents find it hard to read. Progress is reported against transdisciplinary units and learner-profile attributes, so a report can say a great deal about attitude and almost nothing about whether a child can handle fractions. The programme ends with an exhibition in the final year, a group inquiry presented to the school community. Tutoring at this stage is diagnostic rather than remedial: finding out what a cheerful report is not telling you.
programmes.countryNote: Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City is the nearest PYP campus to Arabian Ranches 3, with Nord Anglia and Dubai International Academy reachable on the Al Barsha South run. Dubai parents moving in from a British primary often meet the PYP mid-stream, and the first thing they notice is that nobody has mentioned a reading age or a maths level. That is the gap a one-to-one session is useful for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks every subject against four criteria, A to D, each scored 1 to 8 and each measuring a different thing. A student can be strong on knowledge and weak on investigating patterns and still see one flat grade out of seven. The programme has no public examinations unless the school enters students for eAssessment, and it ends with a Personal Project in MYP 5. Tutoring that works at this stage names the criterion before it names the topic.
programmes.countryNote: Dubailand families often run a British primary and an IB middle school in the same household, because the inner ring mixes both. That produces the particular Arabian Ranches 3 situation where one child is doing IGCSE past papers and another is being marked out of eight, in the same room, at the same hour. Matching two tutors to two curricula is cheaper than asking one to do both badly.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7, plus the core. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are read together on a matrix that can add up to three points, and CAS must be completed for the diploma to be awarded at all. There are minimum-grade conditions that can withhold a diploma from a student whose total looks comfortable. Most tutoring requests from Arabian Ranches 3 arrive in DP1 term two, when the first set of real mock marks lands.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is a minority programme in Dubai by enrolment, which is why the campuses offering it are scattered rather than local. For a family in Arabian Ranches 3 that means the nearest school teaching DP Chemistry HL may be a thirty-minute drive, and the nearest tutor who has actually taught DP Chemistry HL may be nowhere nearby at all. Online matching removes that second constraint entirely.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning requirement, language development and a personal and professional skills course. It is not a reduced Diploma; it is a different award with its own requirements, and it suits a student with a clear vocational direction better than six academic subjects would. Few UAE schools run it, so parents often meet it for the first time as an option a counsellor has mentioned.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP provision in Dubai is thin, families in the Dubailand belt usually encounter the choice as a Diploma-or-nothing conversation, and then discover the CP late. The tutoring need is specific: the Diploma courses inside the CP are marked exactly as they are in the full Diploma, so a CP student taking Business Management SL needs the same paper technique as any other Business Management SL candidate.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Arabian Ranches 3 families request, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to leave. The description matters more than the subject name: a tutor who has taught Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL is not interchangeable with one who has taught Analysis and Approaches HL, even though both appear on a timetable as maths.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, examined without a calculator on one paper and with a graphic display calculator on the others. HL adds a third paper built from extended problem-solving, where marks go on sustained method rather than on recall. Most lost marks here are notation and unjustified steps, not wrong answers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, calculator-permitted throughout. Students who chose it to avoid algebra are often surprised by the volume of interpretation required: a correct regression line with no comment on what it means scores poorly. HL adds graph theory and complex numbers that schools commonly teach late in DP2.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Three written papers plus a scientific investigation. Paper 1 is multiple choice and data analysis; Paper 2 is extended response; Paper 3 covers the options and experimental technique. HL-only content on fields and induction is where the gap between a 5 and a 7 usually sits for Dubai students arriving from IGCSE.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and the quantitative paper carry the heaviest loss rates. The scientific investigation needs a measurable variable chosen early, which is where most Diploma chemistry students waste a term. HL adds depth on equilibria and acid-base theory that cannot be revised quickly from notes alone.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume of content is the obstacle rather than the difficulty of any part of it. Marks leave through imprecise terminology, command terms answered at the wrong depth, and data questions where the student describes the graph instead of explaining the biology. Precision in written answers is coachable in a few sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks of their own, and a correct diagram with unlabelled axes earns fewer of them than students expect. HL adds the quantitative paper and a heavier evaluation demand. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published articles, which rewards picking the article carefully before writing anything.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen analysis of non-literary text types, which is the component Dubai students find hardest because it cannot be revised from the texts studied in class. The individual oral links a global issue to two works. HL adds the essay. Technique transfers between texts and is the fastest thing to improve.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released case for one paper and quantitative tools that students either learn properly or guess at. The internal assessment differs between HL and SL in both length and research base. Application to the named business, rather than textbook theory in general, is where the marks are.

subjects.name: Spanish and French ab initio
subjects.description: Designed for genuine beginners, with themes, text types and a prescribed vocabulary range. Dubai students often arrive having studied the language a little, which makes them overconfident on productive skills and underprepared for the written assessment's text-type conventions. Regular short sessions beat long infrequent ones here.

subjects.name: Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Supervision rather than teaching. The essay needs a research question narrow enough to answer in 4,000 words and a method the subject recognises; the TOK exhibition needs three objects that let the student argue something. Both are graded A to E and combine for up to three points on the Diploma total.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.modesIntro: Three ways of buying Diploma support come up in Arabian Ranches 3, and they suit different situations rather than different budgets. What follows is what each one is for, with the honest limitation attached, so the choice can be made before a trial rather than after three months.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, same tutor, same slot
modes.description: The default and the one that moves grades. A single subject, a fixed evening, the same tutor across a term, with written notes after each session and the recording kept. The value is cumulative: by week four the tutor knows which topics the student fakes confidence on, which is information no first lesson produces.

sections.heading: What an Arabian Ranches 3 search for a home tutor actually returns
paragraphs: Search the phrase from inside the community and the results split three ways. There are classifieds listings from individuals offering to drive out to Dubailand, usually without naming a syllabus. There are agencies with a city-wide page that mentions Arabian Ranches 3 once, in a list of forty neighbourhoods. And there are platforms that quote a price in US dollars, which is a currency no UAE family transacts school fees or tuition in. None of those three answers the question a parent is actually asking, which is whether somebody who has taught this specification, at this level, can work with this child on a Tuesday evening.

The permit position is worth knowing before you ring anyone on a classified. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The ministry has not published a fine schedule, so any page quoting you an amount is guessing.

That rule has a second edge in Abu Dhabi, which matters to Dubai families with relatives across the border recommending somebody. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars the same thing. A tutor who offers to take your child because they already teach them in class is offering something they should not. It is a question worth asking in the first conversation rather than the fourth.

IB Gram's answer to the original search is narrower and more useful than a list of names: one tutor, matched to the syllabus and level, teaching live online on Gulf Standard Time into whichever phase of Arabian Ranches 3 you live in. No travel, no radius, no compromise on which Higher Level subject the tutor has actually taught. What follows is the structure of the qualification that tutor is being hired to work on.

sections.heading: How a Diploma total of 45 is assembled
paragraphs: Parents are told the Diploma is marked out of 45 and are rarely told how the 45 is built. It matters because the components are not equally expensive to improve. Six subject grades out of seven account for 42 of the points. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge contribute no points individually: their letter grades are read together on a matrix that awards up to three. CAS awards nothing and is still a condition of the award. And a set of minimum-grade rules can withhold a diploma from a candidate whose arithmetic total looks perfectly safe.

The practical consequence is a triage question. A student at 33 predicted who is sitting on a C and a C in the core is probably one grade band away from two or three extra points for a fraction of the work a subject grade would take, because the core is assessed on two pieces of writing rather than two years of content. A student at 38 with an A and a B in the core has already banked those points, and the only place left to look is the subject most likely to move from a 5 to a 6. Tutoring money spent without that triage tends to go into whichever subject feels worst, which is not the same thing as whichever subject is cheapest to lift.

The failing conditions are the part that surprises families most. A diploma can be withheld for a grade of 1 in any subject, for too many grades of 2, for an E in either core component, and for failure to complete CAS. Each of those is a cliff rather than a slope, and each is visible months in advance in the school's own reporting. A parent who knows the conditions reads a DP1 report differently: a single 2 in a Standard Level subject stops being a disappointment and becomes the thing that gets dealt with first.

The table below sets the structure out component by component. It is deliberately about what tutoring can and cannot move, because a page that lists the rules and stops has not helped anyone decide where to spend an evening a week.

sections.heading: The core: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS
paragraphs: The core is the part of the Diploma that most resembles university work and gets the least tutoring attention, usually because parents cannot see it on a report card. It is also where the limits are hard numbers rather than impressions. The Extended Essay runs to 4,000 words. The TOK exhibition is 950 words across three object commentaries. The TOK essay is 1,600 words on one of the IB's prescribed titles. None of those is a target to reach; each is a ceiling that forces a decision about scope, and the decision is where supervision earns its hour.

Most Extended Essays that disappoint were lost at the research-question stage, months before anything was written. A question that would take a book to answer produces an essay that summarises instead of arguing, and summary does not score. The fix is cheap and early: narrow the question until the student can state what evidence would settle it, then check the method against what the subject actually recognises. A history essay and a biology essay are graded on the same criteria and need completely different methods, which is why subject-matched supervision beats general essay coaching.

The reflection sessions are the component families most often treat as paperwork. There are three of them with the school supervisor, including the final discussion, and they are recorded on the reflection form that goes to the IB. Treated properly, the first one is where a weak question gets caught and the last one is where the student rehearses defending the work they did. Treated as a signature exercise, they add nothing and the essay goes in with its original flaw intact.

CAS sits outside all of this and still has the power to stop a diploma. It runs across roughly eighteen months, is checked by the school's CAS coordinator against the learning outcomes, and has no marks attached. No tutor should be writing CAS reflections, and any provider offering to is offering something that puts the student at risk rather than ahead.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, and what the extra hours cost
paragraphs: The difference between Higher and Standard Level is not difficulty in the abstract; it is taught hours and an extra paper. The IB builds a Standard Level course around roughly 150 hours of teaching across two years and a Higher Level course around roughly 240. That ninety-hour gap is content a student has to hold in mind simultaneously, and it is the reason a Higher Level catch-up takes proportionally longer than the same work at Standard Level rather than simply being harder per topic.

The extra paper is the part families underestimate. In most Higher Level subjects there is a third written component, built from options or extension material, and it rewards a different skill from the first two. Practising Papers 1 and 2 more does not prepare a student for it. This is a recurring pattern in Dubailand booking conversations: a student has revised conscientiously, improved on the papers they practised, and is still losing the same marks on the one paper they never set a timer for.

Route choice is the other place a Higher Level decision costs money later. A subject taken at Standard Level is rarely accepted where that subject is the degree, so a student who intends to read engineering and is sitting Mathematics at Standard Level has a problem that becomes expensive after DP1 and almost unfixable after the first term of DP2. One session with somebody who knows the entry requirements, held before the choice is locked, is the cheapest intervention on this entire page.

What does not change between the levels is the internal assessment. The same task, the same criteria, the same marks. A Higher Level and a Standard Level student can share a tutor productively for that piece of work and then need different people for the papers, which is a reasonable way to spend a limited budget.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Start with the question nobody else answers, which is what the extra money for a visit actually purchases. The in-home band in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour: Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. A qualified subject tutor working online is published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The gap between those two bands is not better teaching. It is a car, a driver's hour, and a tutor pool restricted to whoever is willing to drive to Dubailand on a weekday evening.

Below that sits a budget band of AED 45 to 150 an hour, where EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. It buys homework supervision and company rather than syllabus expertise, which is a reasonable purchase for a Year 7 who will not sit down alone and a poor one for a DP2 student losing marks on Paper 3. Above the qualified band, IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate reaching AED 450 or more. A premium tier exists above that again, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Monthly packaging is where the travel premium shows most plainly. The market shows online packages around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Set against school fees those are real numbers, and worth reading next to KHDA's confirmation on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package.

Every figure above is somebody else's published rate, cited so you can check it. IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages, because the rate depends on subject, level and how much of the core is involved; the free first lesson and the consultation exist so the number arrives with the tutor attached rather than as a band in a table.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks leave in the final six months
paragraphs: By DP2 term two the losses are rarely about not knowing the content. They are about the same four or five habits, and they are diagnosable from one marked past paper. The commonest is answering at the wrong depth: a question asking the student to outline gets three paragraphs, and a question asking them to evaluate gets a description with no judgement in it. The marks are allocated to the verb, and the verb is in the question, which makes this the cheapest thing on the list to fix.

The second is the internal assessment left at draft. Across subjects the internal assessment is worth a fifth to a quarter of the grade, and it is the one component where the student controls the conditions entirely. A draft that has had one round of criterion-level feedback and one revision reliably outperforms a draft submitted because the deadline arrived. This is also the component where the honesty line matters most, and it is drawn in the next section.

The third is time. Students who have never run a full paper against a clock discover in the exam that the last question carries as many marks as the first and gets a third of the attention. Running two timed papers in the eight weeks before a series changes the distribution of marks without changing what the student knows. The fourth is the Higher Level third paper, already discussed, which simply does not get practised. The fifth, in the sciences and mathematics, is mechanical: unlabelled axes, missing units, significant figures, a graphic display calculator used as an answer machine rather than as a check.

None of that list requires two years of tuition. It requires one marked paper, an honest conversation about which of the five is costing most, and six to eight weeks of narrow work. That is a different and cheaper purchase from a standing weekly booking, and a tutor who tells you so at the first lesson is worth more than one who does not.

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes and what we will not send you
paragraphs: Past-paper practice is the single most productive thing a Diploma student can do in the final two terms, and it has to be sourced properly. IB past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables are copyright material. IB Gram does not host them, email them or supply them as downloads, and a tutoring provider that offers you a drive full of papers is handing you a copyright problem and, where the material is unreleased, a malpractice exposure for your child. The legitimate routes are the school's own subscription, the IB's own store, and the coordinator, who can usually access more than parents expect.

What a tutor can do is work papers with the student rather than at them. There is a real difference between marking a completed paper and sitting beside a student while they attempt one, stopping at the point where the method goes wrong rather than at the point where the answer does. The second is slower and is where the learning is, because the error almost never happens in the last line. A session that covers one question properly can be worth more than one that covers a whole paper superficially.

The order also matters more than families expect. Working papers in reverse chronological order teaches a student the current style of question but hides the pattern; working them by topic until a topic is secure, then by paper once several are, produces fewer false positives. A student who scores well on a mixed paper after topic practice has learned something. A student who scores well on their fourth attempt at the same paper has learned that paper.

Cambridge and Pearson publish their own timetables and key-date documents openly, and those are the right thing to link when a date matters. IB session dates are a different case: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no exam or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Any page that gives you a precise IB date without saying where it came from is guessing, and the right source is your school's IB coordinator.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and the mandatory UAE subjects alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: A Diploma student in Dubai is not only studying six IB subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind the timetable squeeze every DP1 parent notices and few are told about.

The organisation rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length if the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

Two further constraints shape what tutoring in these subjects can honestly offer. Schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects, which is a school-level credential and not something a private tutor holds. And for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support in these subjects therefore means practice against the school's own scheme of work, not a parallel syllabus, and any provider promising their own Arabic programme alongside a Dubai school's is describing something the regulations do not allow.

For an Arabian Ranches 3 family the practical effect is scheduling. The mandatory subjects occupy real timetable minutes that are not available for Diploma content, which is one reason the evening hour matters here more than it would in a system with fewer required subjects.

sections.heading: Booking from Arabian Ranches 3, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The booking sequence is short. You describe the subject, the level and the evening that works; we propose one tutor with their syllabus and level stated; the first lesson runs free, with no card details taken, and you decide afterwards whether to continue. If the match is wrong, say so after the first lesson and a different tutor is proposed rather than argued for. That is the whole process, and it is deliberately one tutor rather than a shortlist, because a shortlist transfers the work of choosing back to a parent who has no way to assess it.

What matters more than the sequence is what happens when we cannot staff a request. Specialist Higher Level coverage is not uniform. Mathematics, the three sciences, Economics and English are reliably available on UAE evening hours. An ab initio language, a less common Higher Level option, or Extended Essay supervision in a narrow subject can take longer than a fortnight, and sometimes the honest answer is that nobody suitable is free. In that case we say so. Where the tutor who fits is based in India rather than the UAE, that is stated before any payment, and the lesson is scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so the student's evening does not move.

The disclosure matters because no competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without mentioning where the teaching happens. A page that tells you in advance which requests are hard to fill is more useful than one that promises everything and then delays. The table below is what we can actually commit to for this community.

On data: a tutoring enquiry for a Diploma student collects a child's name, school, year group, subjects and the levels they are sitting, because none of the matching works without them. We use it to propose a tutor and to run the lessons, we do not need a photograph or a report card to do that, and a request to delete it is honoured. The privacy policy linked from this page sets out the detail, under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection.

Those two details decide which tutors are even candidates, and getting them right in the first message removes a week of back and forth.

process.description: You receive a single match rather than a shortlist, with the specification they teach, the level they teach it at and their permit position. If the subject is one where coverage is thin, you are told that at this stage rather than after a fortnight of silence.

process.description: One session, held at the slot you asked for, with no card details taken beforehand. The student does the talking and the writing; the tutor diagnoses rather than presents. Afterwards you decide. There is no condition attached beyond it being one lesson with one tutor.

process.description: After the first lesson the tutor sets out which topics are being worked on, in what order, and what will be used to tell whether it is working: a marked past paper, a criterion-level improvement on an internal assessment draft, a timed section completed inside the time allowed.

process.description: Mid-term the plan is checked against the evidence rather than against how the sessions feel. Where the work is finished, we say so and the booking ends. An intensive block before a mock series is supposed to have an end date, and a provider that never finds one is selling a subscription.

whyPoints.title: The match is on syllabus, not on distance
whyPoints.description: A radius search around Arabian Ranches 3 returns whoever lives nearby. An online match returns whoever has taught the specification at the level your child is sitting. For a Higher Level subject with a third paper, that distinction is the whole difference between a tutor who can help and one who can only supervise homework.

whyPoints.title: Every rate on this page is somebody's published figure
whyPoints.description: The AED bands here are attributed to the provider or the rate survey that published them, so you can check them yourself. Three of the six main competitors in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars. A number you cannot verify is not information.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line on coursework is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: No tutor may write the Extended Essay, the TOK essay or an internal assessment for a student. Support means teaching, criterion-level feedback on the student's own draft, and process coaching. One operator in this market sells completed internal assessments; that is a malpractice trigger for the student, not a shortcut.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are published before you book
whyPoints.description: Some Higher Level options and ab initio languages are genuinely hard to staff on UAE evening hours. Where that is true you are told at the match stage, including whether the tutor who fits is based outside the UAE. No competitor page researched in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

whyPoints.title: No regulator is claimed as a sponsor
whyPoints.description: KHDA regulates private schools in Dubai and the MoHRE permit governs private tutors; neither endorses IB Gram, and this page does not suggest otherwise. A provider advertising KHDA-approved tutors is describing something that does not exist in that form, and it is the single most common claim in this market.

faqs.question: Is there any way to get an in-home IB tutor inside the Arabian Ranches 3 gates?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not send anyone to a UAE address; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. The market does offer them, at a published AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on the provider, and a family who wants that specifically should hire locally and ask to see the tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit. What we offer instead is one-to-one Diploma tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched on syllabus and level rather than on who is willing to drive to Dubailand on a Tuesday.

faqs.question: How do the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge add points to the Diploma total?
faqs.answer: Neither carries points on its own. Both are graded A to E, and the two letters are read together on the IB's core matrix, which awards up to three points toward the total of 45. A grade of E in either component is also a failing condition that can withhold the diploma regardless of the arithmetic. The practical consequence is that lifting the weaker of the two letters is often cheaper than lifting a subject grade, because the core is assessed on two pieces of writing rather than on two years of content. Your school's coordinator holds the current matrix.

faqs.question: What is the CAS requirement and can it really stop a diploma being awarded?
faqs.answer: Creativity, Activity, Service runs across roughly eighteen months of the Diploma, is recorded in a portfolio against the programme's learning outcomes, and carries no marks. Completion is nonetheless a condition of the award, so a student with a strong points total and an incomplete CAS record does not receive the diploma. It is checked by the school's CAS coordinator, not by an external examiner. No tutor should be drafting CAS reflections: the record has to be the student's own account of what they did, and a provider offering to write it is creating a problem rather than solving one.

faqs.question: How many of the 45 Diploma points can a tutor realistically influence?
faqs.answer: Honestly, fewer than most marketing suggests, and the number depends on where the student is. Six subject grades account for 42 points and move in whole bands, so a realistic weekly arrangement in one subject is aiming at one band in that subject. The core adds up to three points and is often the cheaper target because it rests on two pieces of writing. The reliable gains are technique rather than knowledge: command terms answered at the right depth, a revised internal assessment instead of a first draft, and a paper completed inside the time allowed.

faqs.question: Which Diploma campuses do Arabian Ranches 3 families usually drive to?
faqs.answer: There is no Diploma school inside Arabian Ranches 3, so students commute. The campuses that come up most in booking conversations are Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and Dubai International Academy in the Al Barsha South direction, GEMS World Academy Dubai, Dwight School Dubai and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai. Those are named as local context; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them. The commute is the reason a fixed online slot is easier to hold than an arrangement that depends on a second car journey in the same evening.

faqs.question: What does the Dubai market charge for Extended Essay supervision in dirhams?
faqs.answer: Providers rarely price the core separately, so it generally sits in the specialist band: published figures put IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 an hour and upward, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate reaching AED 450 or more. Supervision also tends to need fewer hours than a subject, concentrated at the research-question stage and again before each reflection session. IB Gram does not publish a rate on this page because it depends on the subject of the essay; the free first session exists so the figure arrives with a named supervisor attached.

faqs.question: My son is in Sun and finishes school at 15:30. When can a session realistically start?
faqs.answer: Allow for the bus rather than the bell. From most of the Dubailand campuses a 15:30 finish puts a child inside Arabian Ranches 3 somewhere between 16:15 and 16:45, and a secondary student needs food and twenty minutes before anything useful happens. A 17:00 start works for most households in the earlier phases; 18:00 is more reliable during heavy term weeks and noticeably easier in Ramadan. Because the lesson is online there is no second journey to absorb, which is what makes the later slot practical rather than theoretical.

faqs.question: What may an Extended Essay supervisor do that a tutor from outside the school may not?
faqs.answer: Your school's supervisor is the person who holds the three reflection sessions, records them on the reflection form and confirms the work is the student's own. An outside tutor cannot replace that and should not pretend to. What an outside tutor can do is narrow the research question, check the method against what the subject recognises, read the student's own draft against the published criteria and give feedback on it, and prepare the student for the final discussion. What nobody may do is write any part of it. That line is the student's protection, not a formality.

faqs.question: Are IB past papers and mark schemes something IB Gram can send us?
faqs.answer: No. IB past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables are copyright material, and we do not host, email or supply them. Any provider offering you a folder of papers is handing you a copyright problem, and where the material is unreleased it becomes a malpractice exposure for your child. The legitimate sources are your school's own subscription and your IB coordinator, who can usually access more than parents expect. A tutor's job is to work the papers with the student, which is a different thing from supplying them.

faqs.question: Does a Higher Level subject genuinely need more tutoring hours than a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a structural reason rather than a vague one. The IB builds a Standard Level course around roughly 150 taught hours across two years and a Higher Level course around roughly 240. That gap is content the student has to hold simultaneously, so catch-up is proportionally longer. Higher Level also usually adds a third written paper drawn from options or extension material, which rewards a different skill from the first two and therefore needs its own timed practice. Revising Papers 1 and 2 harder does not prepare anybody for it.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still have to run alongside the Diploma in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; combined classes are prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a DP1 timetable that means real minutes which are not available for Diploma content, which is what makes the evening hour matter.

faqs.question: How do we check that a private tutor in Dubai is legally permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. It is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system under the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Is the free trial lesson conditional, and what exactly are the conditions?
faqs.answer: It is one lesson, with one proposed tutor, at the slot you asked for, and no card details are taken before it runs. That is the whole condition. It is not a shortened demonstration and it is not a sales call with a student present: the tutor spends it diagnosing, usually on a real past paper or the student's current internal assessment draft, and you get the written notes afterwards whether you continue or not. If the match is wrong, saying so is the expected outcome and a different tutor is proposed.

faqs.question: We are early in DP1 with no crisis yet. Is it too soon to start?
faqs.answer: DP1 is the cheapest moment to intervene, which is the opposite of how most families use tutoring. Two things are decided in DP1 and expensive to change later: whether the Higher Level choices match the degree the student intends to read, and whether the Extended Essay research question is narrow enough to answer. A single session on each, held before the choices lock, costs less than a term of remedial work in DP2. If nothing is wrong, a diagnostic session that confirms it is a reasonable purchase and the honest answer afterwards is to wait.

faqs.question: What happens if no UAE-based tutor covers our Higher Level option?
faqs.answer: You are told before you book rather than after. Mathematics, the three sciences, Economics and English are reliably staffed on UAE evening hours. An ab initio language, an unusual Higher Level option or Extended Essay supervision in a narrow subject can take longer than a fortnight, and sometimes nobody suitable is free at all. If the person who fits the brief sits in India rather than the UAE, you hear that at the match stage, and the slot stays on Gulf Standard Time. Where there is genuinely nobody, we say no rather than send somebody unsuited.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.closingHeading: Start with one marked paper, not a subscription
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-3.closingBody: The useful first step for a Diploma student in Arabian Ranches 3 is small: one past paper, worked with a tutor who teaches that specification at that level, marked against the published criteria rather than against an impression. That single session tells you whether the problem is content, technique, timing or the internal assessment, and those four problems have different prices and different timescales. Tell us the subject, the level and the hour the bus gets back to your phase. We will propose one tutor, state their syllabus and permit position, run the first lesson free with no card details taken, and give you the notes either way.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-bluewaters-island.tutorsIntro: These are IB Diploma and Middle Years specialists teaching Bluewaters families online. Each is matched to one subject at one level, and we tell you honestly when the work in front of us does not require the most expensive tutor we have.

intro.heading: The problem here is not the budget, it is what the budget buys
paragraphs: Bluewaters Island is a small residential population in high-value apartments, connected to Dubai Marina and JBR by a single road bridge and a pedestrian link. It has no school on it. Children here are bussed or driven to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, The Greens, Jumeirah Park or Emirates Hills, and the households are, on the whole, able to pay whatever tutoring costs. That turns out to be the problem rather than the solution.

A note on what this page is not. It is not an argument that tutoring is expensive, or that Bluewaters families are being overcharged by anybody in particular. The rates published across this market are, on the whole, what the people charging them believe their time is worth, and several are reasonable. The failure is upstream of price: nothing in this search explains which kind of work needs which kind of tutor, so the match is made on marketing confidence rather than on diagnosis, and a confident page at the top of the market will always out-market a competent one in the middle of it.

When price is not a constraint, families default to the top of the market, because the top of the market is where the confident marketing is. Published Dubai rates run from AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 at the premium end, a fourteen-fold spread, and nothing on those pages explains which band a particular piece of work actually needs. So a student who needs forty minutes a week of someone checking their algebra gets an examiner-led specialist at AED 650, and a student who genuinely needs criterion-level Internal Assessment supervision gets a university student at AED 65 because the package looked reasonable.

Both are overspends. The second is worse, because it also wastes the term. The useful discipline is to diagnose the work first and then choose the band, which inverts how almost every tutoring purchase in this emirate is made.

So this page leads with money. What Bluewaters families actually pay per month, with the market sources. The six specific places the money gets wasted, named plainly. What each band genuinely buys and does not buy. The travel premium, which on an island with one bridge is not a rounding error. And the package structures that look economical and are not.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run in India only, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. On a cost page that fact is load-bearing rather than incidental: a substantial share of what an in-home hour costs in this market is the journey, and on Bluewaters the journey has one route on and off the island.

Every AED figure on this page was read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 Dubai rate table, and each is attributed. They describe the market, not our price list. We do not publish a price list on these pages, because the honest answer to what tutoring should cost depends entirely on what the tutoring has to do, and that is what a free trial lesson is for. A family that knows which band the work needs can judge any quotation in this market, including ours, which is a more useful thing to be given than a number.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-bluewaters-island.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes matter to Bluewaters households, and the cost profile of each is genuinely different. Knowing which one you are buying for prevents the most common overspend of all.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Six transdisciplinary themes, continuous assessment, no external examination. The support that pays off is narrow: number fluency, reading stamina, and writing a paragraph that answers the question asked. None of it requires examination expertise, which means none of it requires the specialist band.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Bluewaters families most often overpay. A PYP child needing reading practice and number facts is well served at the lower end of the market, and a premium specialist adds nothing a patient tutor at a third of the price would not provide. Short, frequent sessions also work better at this age than long ones, which reduces the bill further.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria scored one to eight, converted to a 1-7 grade. The highest-return work is criterion literacy: reading the published descriptor for the band above and redrafting one piece to meet it. That needs a tutor who will do it rigorously, not an examiner.
programmes.countryNote: MYP support sits comfortably in the qualified subject tutor band at roughly AED 150-300 an hour. The exception is the Personal Project in the final MYP year, where criterion-level feedback genuinely benefits from somebody who has assessed against the descriptors, and the bridging block before DP1, which is specialist work.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, with a maximum of 45 points. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly twenty per cent, and each has papers with their own mark-scheme conventions.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one stage where the specialist band earns its premium, and only for specific work: Internal Assessment supervision against the published criteria, Higher Level paper technique, and the third paper in subjects that have one. Content catch-up at Diploma level does not need it, and that distinction is worth several thousand dirhams across two years.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and language development. Provision is limited in the UAE, and where a student takes Diploma courses within it, those courses are taught and tutored identically.
programmes.countryNote: Families considering the Career-related Programme from Bluewaters are usually weighing a specific campus rather than a curriculum, since provision is thin. For the Diploma courses inside it, the same cost logic applies: pay the specialist band for internally assessed work and paper technique, and not for content revision.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-bluewaters-island.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects Bluewaters families request most, with a note on where the money in each one is well spent. The pattern is that internally assessed components justify specialist rates and content revision does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with a third paper at Higher Level worth roughly a fifth of the grade. Paper 3 technique is specialist work. Practising quadratics and logarithm rules is not, and buying the latter at AED 450 an hour is the commonest single overspend in this subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use, with the graphical calculator assumed throughout. Calculator fluency can be built by any competent tutor. Interpreting a regression in context the way the upper band requires is where mark-scheme familiarity starts to matter.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes with Higher Level extensions, assessed by two papers plus a scientific investigation at roughly twenty per cent. Uncertainty treatment and investigation criteria are specialist work. Revising kinematics is not, and the two are frequently sold at the same price.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity as integrated strands. Mechanism notation and investigation criteria justify the specialist band. Mole drill, which is the highest-return work in the subject, can be supervised competently at the budget end for a fraction of the cost.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: High content volume with precise terminology demands. Most of the lost marks are command-term and vocabulary precision, which is teachable by a good subject tutor. The investigation is where specialist criterion knowledge changes the outcome.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides most of the grade, plus a portfolio of three commentaries at 800 words each. Diagram drilling is mid-band work. Commentary feedback against the published criteria is specialist work, and the two are rarely distinguished when a package is sold.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral, and at HL a 1,200-1,500 word essay. Global issue selection for the oral is the one place where experienced judgement is worth paying for; essay structure practice is not.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools examined for application rather than recall, with a pre-released case study for Paper 1 and an 1,800-word research project at Higher Level. The research project justifies specialist support; case study familiarisation does not and is often sold as though it does.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition with 950 words of commentary, contributing up to three points with the Extended Essay. Prescribed title interpretation is genuinely specialist work and one of the better uses of a premium hour.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece supervised by the school. Research question narrowing in the first weeks is where external support has the greatest effect per hour, and where a few specialist sessions beat a term of general writing help.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: A single road bridge and a pedestrian link to JBR. No school on the island, so every child commutes. For an in-home tutor, the bridge is a bottleneck at exactly the hours a student is free, and the rate reflects it.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Directly across the bridge and the densest tower cluster in this part of Dubai. Visitor parking and building access add time to any in-home visit, which is priced into the market rate rather than itemised on it.

regions.name: JBR
regions.note: The beachfront strip immediately adjoining the Bluewaters link. Convenient on paper and slow in practice between five and seven, when The Walk traffic and the Marina exit interact badly.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, well served by metro and tram. A larger pool of tutors lives here than on Bluewaters, which matters only for in-home arrangements and not at all for online ones.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Low-rise apartments with Regent International School in The Greens. Shorter school runs than Bluewaters, and a community where families often compare notes on what tutoring costs.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Home to several established campuses including Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School. A short drive from Bluewaters off-peak and a slow one at school-run times.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Villa communities inland with Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Emirates International School Meadows. Where a number of Bluewaters Diploma students actually study, and a twenty-five to forty minute drive depending on the hour.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: The ring of established campuses most Bluewaters secondary students attend. A mix of British and IB provision, which is why a single household on the island can be paying for IGCSE support for one child and Diploma support for another in the same month.

schoolClusters.city: The Greens, Jumeirah Park and Emirates Hills
schoolClusters.note: The inland ring, 20 to 40 minutes from the island depending on the hour. Several IB Diploma providers sit here, and the drive at school-run times is the practical reason in-home arrangements from Bluewaters are expensive and fragile.
