sections.heading: What Bluewaters families actually pay, by month
paragraphs: Monthly is the right unit, because that is how the commitment is felt. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for weekly one-hour sessions put budget support at AED 240-600 a month, mid-tier at AED 600-1,200, and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more. A Diploma student with one weekly session in two subjects sits at the top of that range for most of DP2, which is where the annual figure starts to concentrate a family's attention.

Market packages tell the same story from a different angle. Monthly packages seen on competitor pages in October 2026 include AED 799 for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. The online package looks like excellent value per session, at just under AED 100 an hour, and the questions worth asking are who the tutor is, whether they teach that subject at that level, and what happens to the unused sessions when a school trip eats a fortnight.

The in-home package is instructive in another way. Four two-hour sessions at AED 1,599 is AED 200 an hour, which sits at the lower end of the published in-home band of AED 180-350. For a Bluewaters address, with one bridge on and off the island at school-run hours, a tutor pricing at the bottom of that band is either local, generous with their time, or unlikely to keep the arrangement for a full term.

What none of these figures tells you is whether the hours will do the job, which is the only question that matters. That is why we start with a free trial lesson and a diagnosis rather than a quotation.

sections.heading: The six places the money gets wasted
paragraphs: These are the six overspends we see most often in high-value Dubai communities, and all six are avoidable with a diagnosis. None of them involves a dishonest tutor; they are structural mismatches between what was bought and what was needed.

First, premium rates for procedural drill. A student practising quadratics, mole calculations or French verb endings needs supervision and patience, not examination expertise. At AED 650 an hour that is the single most expensive way to buy something available at AED 65. Second, open-ended weekly arrangements for a problem that was a six-session problem. The arrangement continues because nobody set an end date, and after week ten it is a habit rather than an intervention.

Third, three concurrent subject tutors when component marks would have identified one subject as the priority. Fourth, large session counts in holiday intensives, which usually produce a tired student and a flat January. Fifth, paying for hours in the final weeks before a session when the internally assessed twenty per cent of each grade is already fixed and only paper technique remains, which is real but narrow work.

Sixth, and most costly in a different currency, buying the cheap option for work that genuinely needed the specialist. Internal Assessment supervision from somebody who has never assessed against the published criteria is not a bargain; it is a term spent on a piece of work that will be marked against descriptors nobody in the room had read. That one is the expensive mistake, and it is the one price comparison cannot catch.

sections.heading: The travel premium, and what one bridge does to it
paragraphs: In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 table, with individual home tutors quoting up to AED 500 for specialist levels. Qualified subject tutors delivered online sit at roughly AED 150-300. The difference, somewhere between AED 50 and AED 150 an hour, is the journey, and it is the largest single line item in the comparison even though no invoice itemises it.

Bluewaters makes this unusually visible. The island has one road bridge. A tutor coming from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh at five in the afternoon faces Sheikh Zayed Road, then the Marina approach, then the bridge, then visitor parking in a residential tower. The segment that looks shortest on a map, the last kilometre, is frequently the slowest, and a tutor who teaches two island families in an evening spends a large part of the evening stationary.

There is a second cost that does not appear as money. A tutor who can reach Bluewaters in the window a Diploma student is awake is selected from a geographic pool rather than a subject pool. For Chemistry at Higher Level with Internal Assessment supervision, that filter removes most of the people who could actually do the job, and the family ends up paying a premium rate for a general science teacher.

IB Gram does not offer UAE home visits, so this is not a comparison between two things we sell. It is the reason we only sell one of them here. For a Primary Years child who needs somebody physically present, an independent local tutor can genuinely be the better choice, and we will say so.

sections.heading: What each band genuinely buys, and what it does not
paragraphs: The fourteen-fold spread between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour is real, and so are the differences behind it. What is missing from the market is any explanation of which work needs which, so here it is in plain terms.

The budget band, AED 45-150, buys supervision, repetition and a second pair of eyes. EdFlik lists AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. That is genuinely enough for mole drill, quadratic practice, vocabulary work, reading practice at Primary Years level, and checking a student's working. It is not enough for Internal Assessment criteria, Higher Level paper technique, or anything requiring knowledge of how a specific component is marked.

The qualified band, AED 150-300, buys a competent subject teacher who can teach the course properly, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is the working band for most students most of the time, and the one a family defaults away from too readily. The specialist band, AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270, buys mark-scheme fluency and criterion-level judgement, and it is worth the premium for internally assessed work, third papers and core essays.

The premium band, AED 500-650 and above, with BartyED at AED 650, buys narrow, specific expertise at the very top of a Higher Level subject. There are students for whom that is the right purchase: a candidate aiming at a 7 in a subject where they are already at a 6 and the remaining gap is specialised. For everybody else it is a rate without a matching problem, and we will say so rather than taking it.

sections.heading: Package structures that look economical and are not
paragraphs: A monthly package at AED 799 for eight online sessions works out at just under AED 100 an hour, which reads as a bargain against a specialist at AED 270. Whether it is depends entirely on three things the page does not tell you: who teaches the session, whether they teach that subject at that level, and what happens when life interrupts.

The expiry question is the one families regret. Eight sessions a month assumes eight usable weeks of attention a month, and a Dubai school year contains trips, exam leave, half-terms, Ramadan and family travel. A package that expires monthly turns every disrupted fortnight into forfeited value, and across a year that leakage can exceed the discount that attracted you.

The second issue is substitution. Large session counts at low prices are usually supported by a pool of tutors rather than one named person, and continuity is most of what makes tutoring work over months. A tutor who knows what your child misunderstood three weeks ago is doing something a new tutor each month cannot.

The third is scope. Eight hours a month of unfocused support is worse value than four hours aimed at a diagnosed problem, even at a higher hourly rate. The question to ask any provider is not what the hourly rate is. It is what the eight sessions are for, who teaches them, what happens to unused sessions, and whether they will tell you when fewer hours would do.
bullets: Ask who teaches the sessions, by name, and whether it is the same person each week
Ask what happens to unused sessions during exam leave, half-term or travel
Ask whether the tutor teaches that subject at that level, not just the subject
Ask whether the provider will ever recommend fewer hours
Compare total cost against a diagnosed block, not against an hourly rate

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, and what the freeze means
paragraphs: A tutoring decision reads differently depending on what else is moving. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a Bluewaters family, that means the largest education line in the household budget is flat for the year.

The sector context is worth knowing too. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. For 2026-27, seven new private schools are being added, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

Those figures matter for a cost page because they describe a market that is growing rather than tightening, with more IB provision arriving. More provision eventually means more teachers, which is the supply side of the tutoring market. It does not mean cheaper tutoring next term, but it does mean the scarcity argument used to justify premium rates deserves scrutiny.

What we would not do is suggest that tutoring is required. It is not required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. Tutoring is a purchase that should be justified by a diagnosed problem, and when there is not one, the honest recommendation is to spend nothing.

sections.heading: The one purchase never worth making
paragraphs: There is a part of this market that sells finished assessed work. One operator in our competitor research advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. On a page about where money is wasted, this is the clearest case: it is not a bad deal, it is a transfer of risk onto a child.

Submitting purchased work is academic malpractice under IB rules. The finding goes against the student, not the seller, and the consequences reach the Diploma itself rather than a single subject grade. No saving on hours justifies it and no deadline pressure makes it reasonable, which is why we state it on every page even though it is not a sales argument.

The legitimate version is clear and it is what we do. A tutor teaches the subject content the assessment rests on, explains each criterion and what the descriptors require, questions a research question until it is answerable, discusses method and whether the data will support a conclusion, reads a draft the student wrote and says where it falls short, and teaches referencing. That is teaching, and it is what the specialist band is genuinely worth paying for.

What a tutor must not do is write any part of the work, supply text, rewrite a paragraph to final form, generate data, or choose the topic on the student's behalf. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material. Where a school asks what external support a student received, we can provide a written record of sessions and what was taught.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and how to verify what you are buying
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspections published from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there; Sharjah has SPEA; Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Individual tutors need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services system. u.ae states that tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram does not hold one, has no UAE premises, and is not IB authorised, KHDA approved, ADEK approved or Cambridge accredited. Any provider describing itself as approved should be asked which permit it means.

On verification generally: never accept a star rating that cannot be traced to real, countable reviews. Two competitors in our research publish different review counts on the same page, and one shows five stars from twenty reviews beside a claim of 2,500 students. We publish no aggregate rating, because we have no audited one to publish.

process.title: Diagnose before quoting
process.description: Send the subject, the level, the school and a recent marked script. The script tells us whether the problem is drill, technique or criteria, and that determines which band the work needs. Choosing the band before the diagnosis is how a family ends up paying AED 650 an hour for quadratic practice.

process.title: One matched tutor at the right band
process.description: You get one named tutor who teaches that subject at that level, with their background, where they are based and the hourly band they sit in. If the work does not need our most expensive specialist, we say so, which is the only way the rest of this page means anything.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then decide
process.description: A real teaching hour on this week's sticking point, followed by a short written note on what the tutor found. No card is held and nothing renews. If you decide against continuing, that is the end of it, and if the match is wrong we rematch once at no charge.

process.title: Set an end date, not a subscription
process.description: Most problems are six to ten session problems. We write the finish into the plan so the arrangement concludes rather than becoming a standing cost, and we review at the halfway point. Open-ended weekly support that nobody reviews is the second most common overspend in this market.

process.title: Review the band as the work changes
process.description: A student who starts with content drill and moves to Internal Assessment supervision should change band, not just topic. Equally, a student who finishes criterion work and needs paper volume can usually move down. We re-check every four to six weeks and change the arrangement rather than the price.

whyPoints.title: We tell you when cheaper is correct
whyPoints.description: Mole drill, quadratic practice and reading support do not need a specialist at AED 200-450 an hour. Saying so costs us revenue on that session and is the only reason to believe anything else on this page. Three of the six main competitor pages in our research publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: Each band here names the competitor or rate table it came from and the month it was read. Two of the ranking competitors in our research quote US dollars, which is not a currency UAE families transact in, and one publishes prices that contradict its own structured data.

whyPoints.title: No packages that expire
whyPoints.description: A Dubai school year contains trips, exam leave, half-terms, Ramadan and travel. Monthly packages turn each disruption into forfeited value, which across a year can exceed the discount. We price by session with a written end date and no notice period, so nothing is lost to a fortnight you did not plan.

whyPoints.title: One named tutor, not a pool
whyPoints.description: Continuity is most of what makes tutoring work over months. A tutor who remembers what your child misunderstood three weeks ago is doing something a rotating pool cannot, and large low-cost session counts are usually supported by a pool rather than a person.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed before payment
whyPoints.description: If no specialist in your subject and slot is free, you get a date rather than a substitute. If the tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, you know before booking. Neither disclosure appears on any competitor page in our research.

whyPoints.title: No ratings we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: We publish no aggregate rating or review count, because we have no audited one. Competitors in our research show conflicting review figures on a single page, and one shows five stars from twenty reviews against a claim of 2,500 students. An unverifiable number is marketing, not information.

faqs.question: What should we expect to pay monthly for IB tutoring from Bluewaters?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A Diploma student with one weekly session in two subjects sits near the top of that range through most of DP2. Market packages seen in October 2026 include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those figures describe the market rather than our prices, and what they cannot tell you is whether the hours will do the job.

faqs.question: Is a tutor at AED 650 an hour ever worth it?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and for a narrow case. BartyED publishes AED 650, and that band buys very specific expertise at the top of a Higher Level subject. It makes sense for a candidate already performing at a 6 where the remaining gap is specialised, and for prescribed-title interpretation in Theory of Knowledge. It makes no sense for content revision, procedural drill or general support, where a qualified subject tutor at AED 150-300 does the same work. If somebody quotes that rate without asking what the work is, the rate is the product.

faqs.question: Where do families in high-value Dubai communities waste the most money?
faqs.answer: Six places, in rough order of frequency. Premium rates for procedural drill that a budget tutor could supervise. Open-ended weekly arrangements for a six-session problem. Three concurrent subject tutors when component marks would have named one priority. Large holiday intensives that produce a tired January. Heavy spending in the final weeks when the internally assessed twenty per cent is already fixed. And, most costly in a different sense, buying the cheap option for criterion-level work, which wastes the term rather than the money.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home tutor more expensive for a Bluewaters address?
faqs.answer: Because the journey is in the rate. Dubai in-home one-to-one runs roughly AED 180-350 an hour against AED 150-300 for the same tier online, and that AED 50-150 gap is travel time the tutor cannot teach in. Bluewaters sharpens it: one road bridge, the Marina approach, Sheikh Zayed Road and then visitor parking in a residential tower, all at the hours a student is actually free. A tutor teaching two island families in an evening spends a large share of that evening stationary and prices accordingly.

faqs.question: Is the AED 799 monthly package genuinely good value?
faqs.answer: It can be, and three questions decide it. Who teaches the sessions, by name, and is it the same person weekly? Do they teach that subject at that level, or just that subject? And what happens to unused sessions during exam leave, half-term, Ramadan or family travel? A Dubai school year contains several disrupted fortnights, and a package that expires monthly converts each into forfeited value. Eight unfocused hours is also worse value than four aimed at a diagnosed problem, even at a higher hourly rate.

faqs.question: Can a cheaper tutor really handle Diploma-level work?
faqs.answer: For some of it, yes. The budget band from AED 45 an hour buys supervision, repetition and a second pair of eyes, which is genuinely enough for mole drill, quadratic practice, vocabulary work and checking a student's working. What it does not buy is knowledge of how a specific component is marked, which matters for Internal Assessment criteria, Higher Level paper technique and core essays. The split is the useful discipline: pay the specialist band for criterion and mark-scheme work, and the lower band for everything that is really practice.

faqs.question: How many hours does a Diploma student actually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most packages assume, and targeted differently. A typical useful allocation across two years is three to five hours making a weak quantitative skill automatic, six to ten hours on Internal Assessment criteria and design, three to five hours on command-term and answer structure, and ten to sixteen hours of timed paper work in the final two terms. That is under forty hours spent where the marks are, against sixty to seventy for an unreviewed weekly arrangement across the same period, and it generally achieves more.

faqs.question: Should we book a tutoring intensive over the winter break?
faqs.answer: Usually not as a full programme. Families book ten to twenty hours across the long break with good intentions and produce a tired January, in a term where mocks are often close. At market rates that is AED 1,500-6,000 for a net negative. One or two targeted sessions on a single identified weakness, with real rest around them, achieves more. The spring break is different: by then content teaching has limited returns and timed paper work has high ones, so a short burst of papers over that break is usually sound.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school fee freeze change the tutoring calculation?
faqs.answer: It changes the context rather than the arithmetic. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family whose largest education cost is flat, a tutoring decision is a marginal one rather than part of a rising total. It does not make unnecessary tutoring worthwhile, and tutoring is not required for equivalency, university admission or school progression in any case.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish your own hourly price?
faqs.answer: Because the honest answer depends on what the work is, and quoting a single number invites exactly the mismatch this page is about. A student needing mole drill and a student needing criterion-level Internal Assessment supervision should not pay the same rate, and either figure would be wrong for one of them. What we publish instead are the market bands with their sources, so you can see where any quotation sits, and we start with a free trial lesson and a diagnosis before discussing hours at all.

faqs.question: Someone offered a completed Internal Assessment for AED 3,750. Is that an option?
faqs.answer: No, and it is the one purchase on this page that is never worth making at any price. One operator in our competitor research advertises exactly that. Submitting purchased work is academic malpractice under IB rules, the finding goes against the student rather than the seller, and the consequences reach the Diploma itself rather than one subject grade. The legitimate alternative is a specialist who teaches the criteria, questions the research question, and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote, which is a few hours of work rather than a transaction.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our apartment on Bluewaters Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. On a cost page that is load-bearing rather than incidental: the AED 50-150 hourly travel premium in the Dubai market is the journey, and on an island with one bridge at school-run hours it is a larger premium than most. Independent home tutors do work here, and for a Primary Years child who needs somebody physically present they can genuinely be the better choice.

faqs.question: How do we check a tutoring provider's claims before paying?
faqs.answer: Ask three things and watch what happens. Does the tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and when does it expire? Which specific component will they work on, and can they explain one lost mark from a real script in mark-scheme language? And will they ever recommend fewer hours? Separately, treat any star rating that cannot be traced to real countable reviews as marketing: two competitors in our research publish conflicting review counts on a single page. We publish no aggregate rating because we have none we could evidence.

faqs.question: Is three tutors for three subjects ever the right answer?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and only for a student genuinely weak in all three. The alternative costs roughly a third as much and usually works better. Ask the school for component marks across the subjects. If losses look similar everywhere, the problem is command terms and answer structure, which is one intervention of three to five hours paying in every paper. If one subject is clearly worse, buy a six to eight week block there and reassess. Three concurrent weekly arrangements at AED 150-300 each is a commitment that rarely matches the diagnosis.

faqs.question: What does the specialist band buy that the qualified band does not?
faqs.answer: Mark-scheme fluency and criterion-level judgement. A specialist can tell you which line of a script earned the method mark and which did not, what a particular criterion descriptor rewards in the band above, and what the examiner wants in the opening lines of an extended response. TutorChase publishes AED 270 in that band; Unitors publishes IB from AED 200 in the qualified band. For teaching the course properly the qualified band is sufficient. For internally assessed work, third papers and core essays, the premium is doing real work.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-bluewaters-island.closingHeading: Diagnose first, then choose the band
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-bluewaters-island.closingBody: Almost every tutoring overspend in a community like Bluewaters follows from choosing the rate before understanding the work. A student needing procedural drill is well served from AED 45 an hour; one needing criterion-level Internal Assessment supervision needs AED 200-450 and will waste a term at the lower rate. Send a recent marked script, take a free trial lesson, and get a written answer on which band the work needs and roughly how many hours it should take. Then buy that, with an end date, and nothing else.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-bur-dubai.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects to students across Old Dubai. Each one works to your child's own school deadlines — the coordinator's internal assessment dates, the mock window, the reporting cycle — rather than to a generic syllabus plan.

intro.heading: Why a Bur Dubai IB search is usually a question about time
paragraphs: A Bur Dubai parent types "IB home tutor" into Google at one of three moments. The first is October, when DP1 has turned out to be nothing like Year 11 and a child who collected level 7s in the Middle Years Programme has come home with a 4 in Higher Level Chemistry. The second is February, when mock results land and the gap between a predicted grade and a required offer becomes a number on a page. The third is six weeks before the May session, when the question is no longer whether tutoring helps but whether there is enough calendar left for it to.

All three are timing problems. The Diploma is not a syllabus a student can simply study harder at; it is a two-year schedule with roughly eleven fixed hand-in points, six subject grades, and three core pieces that each carry their own internal deadline. Miss the internal assessment draft date your coordinator set in November and the consequences arrive in July. That is why this page is built as a calendar rather than a subject list. It counts backwards from the exam session and shows where a Bur Dubai family can still intervene.

The second thing worth being blunt about is delivery. The phrase parents search is "home tutor", and the market in Dubai does sell exactly that: a tutor who drives to Al Mankhool or Oud Metha and teaches at a dining table for ninety minutes. Those visits are quoted at roughly AED 200 to 500 an hour in Dubai, and the upper half of that range is substantially travel. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE — that is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own past papers on screen, and a recording the student keeps.

For an IB family in Old Dubai that is usually the better trade rather than a compromise, and the reason is supply. There are not many Higher Level Physics specialists living within a twenty-minute drive of Al Raffa, and the ones who are will be booked by the families nearest to them. Online, the constraint disappears: your child is matched to a teacher who has marked that subject, not to whoever is geographically convenient at 5pm on a Tuesday. On a calendar-driven problem that matters twice over, because the specialist is the only person who can tell you honestly whether eight weeks is enough.

The rest of this page does four things. It lays out the Diploma year counted backwards, with who controls each date. It sets out what a realistic eight-week block looks like, week by week, with the evidence a parent should be able to see at each stage. It publishes what the Dubai market charges in dirhams, because three of the six pages currently ranking for this search publish no price at all. And it covers the Ramadan and school-run realities that decide when a Bur Dubai session can actually start.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-bur-dubai.programmesIntro: Bur Dubai and the wider Old Dubai district hold schools running all three IB programmes alongside British and Indian curricula. Each programme has a different calendar shape, and the kind of help that works in Year 7 is not the kind that works in DP2.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary teaching organised around transdisciplinary units rather than separate subjects. There is no external exam, so the calendar is driven by unit-of-inquiry cycles, the exhibition in the final year, and the school's own reporting dates. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the written and spoken explanation the programme asks for constantly.
programmes.countryNote: Several Old Dubai schools run PYP alongside a British primary phase, so a child moving between the two inside the same district can meet a different approach to the same mathematics. The PYP exhibition in the final primary year is the first time most Bur Dubai families see a long, self-directed project, and it usually arrives in the spring term.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of 8, with no public exam unless the school enters students for eAssessment. The calendar runs on summative task windows rather than a single exam, which means a weak term is visible in criterion scores long before any certificate. The Personal Project in the final year is the pressure point.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP-to-Diploma step is where most tutoring demand sits, because criterion marking does not prepare a student for the timed, mark-scheme-driven papers of DP assessment. A Bur Dubai student arriving in DP1 from MYP typically needs eight to twelve weeks to rebuild exam technique, and that block is best spent in Terms 1 and 2 of DP1.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries internal assessment worth 20 to 30 per cent of the grade and marked by the teacher before external moderation. The May session is the one Dubai schools sit; November exists mainly as a resit route for this hemisphere.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is the highest-stakes calendar a Bur Dubai family will manage, because the internal deadlines are invisible from outside the school. Ask your coordinator for the written internal assessment schedule in DP1 rather than DP2; by the time the Extended Essay draft date is a fortnight away, the room to plan has gone.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Offered by far fewer UAE schools than the Diploma, but a genuine option for students who want IB subject rigour without the full six-subject load and the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Dubai schools licence the Career-related Programme, so most Bur Dubai families meet it only when researching alternatives to a full Diploma. If your child is on it, check carefully which Diploma courses the school offers inside it, because the subject-level teaching and the internal assessment rules are identical to DP.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-bur-dubai.subjectsIntro: Requests from Old Dubai cluster around the Higher Level sciences, both mathematics routes and English A, with Economics and Business Management close behind. Each entry below names what the subject actually assesses and where the marks tend to leave.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency under time pressure, calculus to a depth most students have never met, and proof. Marks leave on method lines that are never written down: an unsupported answer in a six-mark question scores one. The internal assessment exploration needs a mathematical process the student can genuinely drive, not a survey with a graph attached.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy work. Students lose marks by treating the graphic display calculator as the answer rather than as a tool whose output must be interpreted in context. HL adds matrices, graph theory and Voronoi diagrams, which arrive late and unsettle students who coasted through SL content.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity dominate the early course and the early failures. The usual pattern is a student who can recite a definition but cannot select between two equations under exam conditions. Paper 1 multiple choice punishes exactly that, and the internal investigation needs a measurable, controllable variable chosen in week one rather than week six.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are where Higher Level separates from Standard. Marks go on arrow-pushing that is almost right, on significant figures, and on explanations that describe a trend rather than account for it. Data-based questions reward a student who has practised reading a table before reading the question.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where command terms decide the grade. "Outline", "explain" and "discuss" carry different mark expectations, and students who write the same paragraph for all three cap themselves in the middle bands. Statistical treatment of data in the internal investigation is the most common weak point.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two papers plus an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay on a studied text. The individual oral is where confident speakers still lose marks, because the global issue has to be argued through specific extracts rather than described. Timed comparative analysis is a trainable skill and most students never train it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the fastest grade change available. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram carries marks that prose cannot recover. The internal assessment commentaries need genuinely recent articles and a disciplined word count; students routinely lose marks for exceeding it or for choosing an article with no theory in it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study response under time pressure, with tools applied rather than described. Students who learn the frameworks but never practise selecting between them write generic answers. Higher Level adds the written commentary and a longer paper, and quantitative tools are a reliable source of easy marks for a student willing to drill them.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode under exam conditions, systems fundamentals and a developed solution as internal assessment. The solution is the time sink: students pick a project with no identifiable client and no testable success criteria, then spend the spring term writing documentation around it. Scope has to be fixed early.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, graded against a rubric most students never read closely. The essay fails on structure rather than ideas: a thesis that does not answer the prescribed title, examples that illustrate nothing, and no counter-position. One hour a week from October of DP2 is usually enough to fix it.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a chosen subject, supervised by a school teacher. The research question is the whole battle; too broad and the essay describes, too narrow and there is nothing to argue. A tutor can coach the question, the method and the reading, and must not write any part of it.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic regardless of the licensed curriculum, so almost every Bur Dubai student has Arabic on the timetable whether or not they take it for the Diploma. Non-Arab students sit a different course from first-language Arabic speakers, and KHDA requires the two groups to be taught in separate classes.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-bur-dubai.regionsIntro: Bur Dubai sits inside a tight district where a school five minutes away by map can be forty minutes away at 3pm. These are the surrounding communities Old Dubai families travel between, and what each one does to a weekday session plan.

regions.name: Al Mankhool
regions.note: Dense apartment blocks with several British and Indian schools within walking distance. Short school runs mean a 4pm start is realistic here, which is earlier than most of Dubai manages.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: Home to some of the district's largest schools, which means a concentrated exit at dismissal. Families here often prefer a 5.30pm or 6pm session to let the surrounding roads clear first.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: Compact flats and large households, so a study space is usually shared. Session length matters more than session count: fifty focused minutes beats a distracted ninety.

regions.name: Al Raffa
regions.note: Close to the creek and to the Bur Dubai abra crossings. Parents working on the Deira side arrive home late, so sessions that need an adult present are better placed at the weekend.

regions.name: Al Fahidi
regions.note: The historic quarter, with a mix of long-settled families and newer rentals. Small residential streets make parking a real constraint for any tutor who drives, which is part of why in-home rates here carry a premium.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Newer towers and one of the district's IB continuum schools. Residents here are often the first in the family to meet IB assessment language, so early explanation of criterion marking pays off.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Across the creek, with several IB and British schools and a well-established international community. The creek crossing is the variable: a 4.30pm session is optimistic if the child is collected at 3.15pm.

regions.name: Deira
regions.note: The oldest commercial district, with heavy afternoon congestion and a wide spread of curricula. Online delivery removes the crossing entirely, which for a Deira household is usually worth more than any rate difference.

regions.name: Oud Metha and Al Nasr fringe
regions.note: Sports clubs and training centres mean many students have fixed evening commitments three days a week. Session planning here starts from the activity timetable, not the school one.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: A large school cluster along the Sharjah road, with significant Indian-curriculum and British provision. Students commuting in from here lose the most time to traffic and benefit most from removing travel from the equation.

schoolClusters.city: Bur Dubai, Al Mankhool and Oud Metha
schoolClusters.note: The district's core school cluster: large Indian-curriculum schools alongside long-established British schools running IGCSE. Diploma provision is thinner here than in New Dubai, which is exactly why online matching matters for a Higher Level specialist.

schoolClusters.city: Al Garhoud, Al Jaddaf and Festival City

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-bur-dubai.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Bur Dubai request. The choice is usually dictated by where the calendar sits: a steady weekly slot in Term 1, an intensive block before mocks, and a short focused run on one assessed piece.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, same slot each week
modes.description: The default for a student who is coping but slipping. One subject, sixty or ninety minutes, the same evening each week so it survives contact with a Bur Dubai school timetable. The value is cumulative: a tutor who sees the same child weekly notices the pattern in errors long before a report card does.
bullets: Same tutor throughout, so diagnosis carries from week to week
Homework set from the student's own school material, not a generic workbook
Short written note after each session on what was covered and what was weak
Slot held through the term rather than rebooked each week

modes.title: Intensive block before mocks or the May session
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week for six to eight weeks, aimed at a specific window. The sequence is fixed: diagnose with a full past paper first, rank topics by marks lost rather than by difficulty, then work the top three until they stop costing marks. This is the format most Bur Dubai families ask for in January and February.
bullets: Opens with a timed past paper marked against the official mark scheme
Topic order set by marks lost, not by syllabus order
Weekly timed section under exam conditions to rebuild pacing
Clear stop date, so the block ends rather than drifting

modes.title: Assessed-piece coaching for IA, TOK and the Extended Essay
modes.description: Short, scheduled sessions attached to one internal deadline. The tutor works on the research question, the method, the structure and the rubric, and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. The student writes every word. Nothing is drafted, rewritten or produced for them, and we say so plainly because the alternative puts a student's whole Diploma at risk.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor search in Bur Dubai is actually asking
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Bur Dubai costs roughly AED 200 to 500 an hour if a tutor travels to the apartment, and roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working one-to-one online, on Dubai market rates published in 2026. IB Gram sits in the second group and sends nobody to a UAE address. The underlying question behind the search is rarely about the format, though. It is about whether there is still time.

That is a question with a real answer, and it depends on three variables a parent can actually check. The first is which assessed pieces are still open: an internal assessment not yet submitted is recoverable, one already moderated is not. The second is how many marks the student is currently losing and where, which a single marked past paper establishes in ninety minutes. The third is how many weeks remain before the next fixed point — a mock window, a draft deadline, the session itself.

Those three numbers turn an anxious search into a plan. A DP1 student in October with a 4 in Higher Level Chemistry and the whole internal investigation ahead of them is in a completely different position from a DP2 student in March with a submitted investigation and a predicted 4. Both searches look identical from the outside. The first needs a steady weekly slot for two terms; the second needs an intensive block on Paper 1 technique and an honest conversation about which universities are realistic.

The rest of this page is organised around that distinction, because a page that only tells you what tutoring costs has answered the easier half of the question. What follows is the Diploma year counted backwards, an eight-week block set out week by week, the market rates in dirhams, and the logistics that decide whether a Bur Dubai session survives the school run.
bullets: Check which assessed pieces are still open before deciding anything
Establish marks lost with one marked past paper, not with a conversation
Count the weeks to the next fixed point, not to the exam
Ask the coordinator for the written internal assessment schedule

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards, and who controls each date
paragraphs: Nobody in this search results page publishes a Diploma calendar. Across the competitor pages measured for this project, the word "November" returned zero hits, and not one named a registration deadline or a results date. That is a strange omission, because the calendar is the thing a parent most needs and the thing a school explains least clearly.

The table below counts backwards from the exam session a Dubai school sits, which is May. The important column is the third one. Some of these dates belong to the IB and are fixed internationally; some belong to your school and are set by the Diploma coordinator in a document most parents never see. Confusing the two is the single most common planning error. A parent who assumes the internal assessment deadline is set by the IB will believe it cannot move, and a parent who assumes it is purely internal will believe it can move further than it can.

One honest caveat. The IB does not permit automated collection of its published dates, so this project does not publish a specific IB exam window or results date on any page. Treat the session as May, and confirm every actual date with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org before you plan a flight, a holiday or a tutoring block around it. The Cambridge and Pearson dates referenced elsewhere on this site are sourced from those boards directly and are a different matter.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can genuinely move, week by week
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the block most Bur Dubai families actually buy, usually starting in January. It is enough to change a grade in one subject and it is not enough to change three. A tutor who tells you otherwise is selling, and the honest version is more useful: pick the subject where the most marks are available, work it properly, and leave the others on maintenance.

The sequence below is the one that works, and the order is not negotiable. Diagnosis comes first because a student's sense of their own weakness is reliably wrong — they report the topic they dislike, not the topic costing them marks. A marked past paper, scored against the official mark scheme with a breakdown by question and by topic, puts a number on each. From there the plan is arithmetic: the three topics with the largest losses get the time.

The last column of the table matters most for a parent paying for the block. Each fortnight has a visible output. If week four arrives and there is no marked timed section and no shrinking list of error types, the block is not working and you should say so rather than wait for the May session to tell you. Progress in an eight-week block is not a feeling, it is a number, and the number exists from week one onwards.

Two warnings about how these blocks go wrong in practice. The first is subject spread: a family that buys eight weeks and asks for three subjects inside it ends up with twenty minutes of practice per topic and no measurable change in any of them. The second is homework. A session a week generates two or three hours of work between sessions, and a student who does not do it converts the block into expensive tuition on the same three topics repeated. Where a Bur Dubai student is genuinely over-committed, the better decision is a shorter block on one subject rather than a wider one that cannot be serviced.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs in Bur Dubai, and what the calendar does to the bill
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number a household budget actually meets. A single weekly one-hour session with a qualified online subject tutor at Dubai market rates lands somewhere between AED 600 and AED 1,200 a month, on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring estimates. Move to twice weekly in an exam year with a specialist and the same source puts it at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upwards. Published monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Working down from the top rather than up from the bottom is also instructive. The highest published rate found in this market is AED 650 an hour at a premium named-tutor agency. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Unitors quotes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65, and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. The spread between the cheapest and the dearest is more than tenfold for what is described, on the surface, as the same service. The difference is almost entirely who is teaching: a university student revising alongside your child, or somebody who has taught and marked the subject.

The calendar moves this bill in one direction. Rates themselves do not rise before exams, but demand for the few genuine Higher Level specialists does, and availability in February is a fraction of availability in October. A family that starts a weekly slot in Term 1 of DP1 pays a lower total across two years than a family that buys an intensive block in the final term, and gets a better outcome, because the work is spread across the year the content is actually taught. None of the figures below are IB Gram prices; they are what the Dubai market charges, and our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the school run and when a Bur Dubai session can really start
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the Dubai calendar fails in week three. Bur Dubai dismissal times cluster between 2.30pm and 3.30pm, and the roads around Oud Metha and Al Mankhool absorb that exit badly. A child collected at 3.15pm from a school across the creek is not realistically ready to think at 4pm. Families in walking distance of their school can hold a 4pm slot; families crossing the creek should plan 5.30pm or later and accept it.

Ramadan reshapes the week more than any other factor. School hours shorten, the working day shifts, and the productive study window for many households moves to after Iftar. Online delivery handles this better than a travelling tutor does, because moving a session from 5pm to 9.30pm costs nothing in logistics. Families who plan for this in advance keep momentum through a month that otherwise costs them four weeks of a block they have already paid for.

Two smaller constraints matter in this district specifically. Shared study space is normal in Karama and Al Mankhool apartments, which argues for shorter, sharper sessions with headphones rather than long evening ones. And sports or activity commitments at the Oud Metha clubs often fix three evenings a week solid, so the honest order of operations is to build the tutoring slot around the activity timetable rather than hope the child will drop the activity. They will not, and nor should they — Creativity, Activity, Service is a Diploma requirement.

sections.heading: An in-home tutor in a Bur Dubai apartment against one-to-one online, on the clock
paragraphs: The case for a travelling tutor is real and worth stating properly. A young child who needs an adult physically turning the page learns better with somebody in the room. A student who will not engage with a screen is not going to be fixed by a better screen. And some parents simply want to see the lesson happening, which is a legitimate preference rather than a misunderstanding.

Against that, the arithmetic in this district is unkind. A tutor crossing from New Dubai to Al Mankhool at 5pm spends an hour each way and prices it in — which is why home visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 200 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online for comparable qualifications. The travel also caps the pool. The number of people who can teach Higher Level Physics, hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit and reach Bur Dubai within an hour is small, and in February it is smaller still.

There is a third difference that matters more than either. Online sessions produce a record. The whiteboard is saved, the session can be recorded, the marked past paper is a file rather than a page in a notebook that stays at the tutor's house. For a calendar-driven problem — eight weeks, measurable progress, a decision point at week four — that record is the thing that lets a parent judge whether the block is working. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and the comparison below is why we think that is the right way round for an IB family in Old Dubai.

sections.heading: Internal assessment deadlines are school deadlines, and that changes the plan
paragraphs: Internal assessment is worth 20 to 30 per cent of most Diploma subject grades, and it is marked by your child's own teacher before the IB moderates a sample. The dates, though, are set inside the school. The coordinator builds a schedule that staggers six subjects plus the Extended Essay so a student is not writing four investigations in one fortnight, and that schedule is the real calendar of DP1 and DP2.

Most parents never see it. Asking for it in writing, early in DP1, is the single highest-value thing a Bur Dubai parent can do, and it costs nothing. With it, a tutoring plan becomes obvious: the Chemistry investigation is due in March, so the method and data collection work happens in January, and the Economics commentaries sit in a different term so they do not compete. Without it, families buy tutoring reactively, a fortnight before each draft, at the point where the tutor can only tidy what exists.

The order inside a single internal assessment also matters. Students lose marks at the start, not at the end: a research question that cannot be answered in the word count, a variable that cannot be controlled, a dataset that does not support the analysis the criteria want. An hour spent on the question in week one saves ten hours of rescue in week six. That front-loaded hour is the cheapest tutoring available in the Diploma and the least often bought.
bullets: Request the written internal assessment schedule in DP1, not DP2
Front-load support onto the research question and the method
Spread subjects across terms so investigations do not collide
Treat the school draft date as the real deadline, because it is

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the deadline is close, and the line we will not cross
paragraphs: This is where the Dubai market is at its worst. One operator found in this search results page sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at around AED 3,750 each. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student: a withheld grade, or the Diploma itself. No tutor and no agency carries that risk on the student's behalf.

The boundary is not vague, and it is easier to hold when it is written down. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain the criteria and what each one rewards, help a student narrow a research question, discuss method and sampling, read a draft the student wrote and say where it loses marks against the published criteria, and teach the referencing convention. A tutor may not write any part of the piece, rewrite a paragraph into better prose, supply a worked dataset, or produce a plan so detailed that the student is transcribing rather than composing.

Near a deadline, pressure pushes at that line from both sides, and a parent paying by the hour is in the weakest position to police it. So we state it on the page rather than in the small print, and our tutors are briefed that feedback is returned as comments and questions on the student's own document. It is also, pragmatically, the better purchase. A student who has been taught to read a rubric can apply that to the next five pieces of assessed work. A student handed a finished essay has bought one grade and learned nothing that survives into the exam hall.
bullets: A tutor teaches, explains criteria and gives feedback on the student's own draft
A tutor does not write, rewrite or supply data for assessed work

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and the timetable hours they occupy
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the reports are published. Reading the one for your child's school is free and takes twenty minutes, and it will tell you more about teaching quality in a specific subject department than any tutoring agency can.

KHDA also sets a requirement that reshapes the Diploma timetable in every Dubai school. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; combined classes for both groups are prohibited.

For a Bur Dubai parent planning a tutoring block, that has a practical consequence. Those hours are already committed, so a Diploma student's free study time is narrower than the subject list suggests. It also means Arabic is a genuine tutoring need in this district rather than an afterthought, and that any material used for the mandatory subjects is constrained: KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited. We teach to the school's own stream and syllabus rather than substituting our own.

process.title: Tell us the date you are working towards
process.description: Not just the subject and level, but the next fixed point: a mock window, an internal assessment draft date, the May session. The date determines whether the answer is a weekly slot, an eight-week block or an assessed-piece engagement, and it changes which tutor is the right match.

process.title: Free trial lesson, used as a diagnosis
process.description: The first session costs nothing and is spent finding out where the marks are going. Where the student has recent school work or a past paper, the tutor works from that rather than from a generic placement test. You get a written summary afterwards whether or not you continue.

process.title: A plan with a visible checkpoint
process.description: Topic order ranked by marks lost, a stop date, and a defined output at the halfway mark. A plan without a checkpoint cannot be judged until it is too late, which is how families end up paying for six months of sessions that never moved a grade.

process.title: Weekly sessions, held on your timetable
process.description: The slot is fixed for the term and set around the Bur Dubai school run, activity commitments and Ramadan hours. Sessions run live over video, one-to-one, with the whiteboard saved and the session recorded for the student to revisit.

process.title: Review at the checkpoint, then change or stop
process.description: At the agreed point you see a like-for-like comparison with the diagnostic paper. If the numbers have not moved we change the tutor or the approach, and if the work is done we say so and stop rather than extend the block by default.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is the plan
whyPoints.description: Every engagement is built backwards from a date that exists in your school's own schedule. That is a different thing from a generic revision course, and it is why the first question we ask is about the deadline rather than the subject.

whyPoints.title: Subject specialists, not the nearest available tutor
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the Higher Level Chemistry teacher does not also have to live near Al Mankhool. For the three or four Diploma subjects where Bur Dubai supply is genuinely thin, that is the whole difference.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, our model explained
whyPoints.description: The dirham figures on this page are what the Dubai market charges, each attributed to the source that published it. Three of the six pages ranking for this search publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars to families who transact in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach, review and give feedback on the student's own writing, and we will not draft an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. This is stated on the page because the alternative is sold openly in this market.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can audit
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts, saved whiteboards, session recordings and a written note after each lesson. At the halfway checkpoint you are comparing numbers rather than relying on an impression of whether things feel better.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for a niche Higher Level subject in the window you need, we say so at the start rather than matching you to a generalist and hoping. A late answer on availability costs a family weeks it cannot get back.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks before the May session. Is it too late to start IB tutoring in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to change one subject grade and not enough to change three. Start with a full past paper marked against the official scheme, rank the topics by marks lost, and spend the block on the top three. Expect a measurable comparison at week eight against that first paper. What eight weeks cannot do is rescue an internal assessment already submitted and moderated, or rebuild two years of Higher Level content. Be clear which of those you are dealing with before you buy, because the honest answer changes the plan rather than the price.

faqs.question: Who sets my child's IB internal assessment deadlines, the school or the IB?
faqs.answer: Your school sets them. The Diploma coordinator builds an internal schedule that staggers six subjects plus the Extended Essay across DP1 and DP2 so investigations do not collide, and the IB sets only the final submission window the school works back from. Ask for that schedule in writing early in DP1. With it, tutoring can be placed where it earns most — on the research question and the method, months before a draft is due. Without it, families buy help reactively a fortnight before each hand-in, which is the most expensive and least effective point to start.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our apartment in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a Bur Dubai family that is usually the better arrangement: a travelling tutor in this district prices an hour of traffic into the lesson, and the pool shrinks to whoever can reach Al Mankhool before 6pm. Online, your child is matched to a teacher who has taught and marked that subject at the right level. You also get a saved whiteboard, a recording and marked scripts, which a dining-table session does not produce.

faqs.question: What does a weekly IB session cost per month in the Dubai market?
faqs.answer: One weekly hour with a qualified online subject tutor sits roughly between AED 600 and AED 1,200 a month on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates. Twice weekly with a specialist in an exam year runs AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upwards from the same source. Published monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are market figures rather than IB Gram prices; our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation about the date you are working towards.

faqs.question: Why is there a tenfold gap between the cheapest and dearest IB tutors in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the word tutor covers two different jobs. At the bottom of the market, AED 33 to 65 an hour buys a university student revising alongside your child, which can work for homework supervision in the Middle Years Programme. At the top, AED 500 to 650 buys somebody who has taught the course for years and knows the mark scheme. For Higher Level Diploma subjects the difference is not polish, it is whether the tutor can tell you which three topics are costing marks. Qualified subject tutors in the AED 150 to 300 band are where most Diploma families land.

faqs.question: Can sessions move after Iftar during Ramadan for a Bur Dubai household?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning that before Ramadan rather than during it is what keeps a paid block intact. School hours shorten, the working day shifts, and for many households the productive study window moves to late evening. Because lessons are delivered online, moving a slot from 5pm to 9.30pm costs nothing in logistics — no travel to re-plan, no tutor stuck in traffic. Families who agree the Ramadan timetable in advance usually keep momentum through the month, while those who do not tend to lose three or four weeks of a block they have already committed to.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a weekday session can realistically start in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school run rather than on the tutor. Dismissal across the district clusters between 2.30pm and 3.30pm. A child who walks home from a school in Al Mankhool can hold a 4pm slot comfortably. A child collected at 3.15pm from a school across the creek in Al Garhoud is not ready to think until closer to 5.30pm, and pretending otherwise produces a session that looks attended and achieves nothing. Online delivery removes the tutor's own commute from the equation, which is usually where the extra usable hour comes from.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line between coaching an IB internal assessment and writing it?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary worth knowing precisely. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each criterion rewards, help narrow a research question, discuss method and sampling, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write or rewrite any part of it, supply a dataset, or hand over a plan so detailed the student is transcribing. One operator in this market sells completed internal assessments at around AED 3,750; that is malpractice and the consequence falls on your child, not the seller.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects do Bur Dubai families most often ask for help with?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics come first, followed by Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at both levels, then English A and Economics. The pattern reflects supply as much as difficulty: Diploma provision in Old Dubai is thinner than in New Dubai, so the number of local specialists in the Higher Level sciences is small and they fill early. Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay support arrives later in the year and in shorter engagements, usually three to six sessions attached to a specific draft deadline the school has set.

faqs.question: What permit should I ask a Bur Dubai tutor to show me before the first paid session?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring privately without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with caution.

faqs.question: Does the IB Diploma meet UAE Ministry of Education equivalency requirements?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process and we are not the right source for the IB threshold. The British-track requirements are published: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. No comparable IB points figure has been verified from the ministry's own pages, so confirm it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate. Treat any agency that quotes you an IB points threshold without a ministry source sceptically.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a DP1 student in Bur Dubai start with?
faqs.answer: One a week in a single subject, held for a full term. DP1 is where content is taught, so steady weekly work on the subject that is slipping beats an intensive block, and it is cheaper across two years than the rescue engagement a family buys in DP2 instead. Two subjects at once early in DP1 usually means neither gets enough practice between sessions. The exception is a student arriving from the Middle Years Programme who needs exam technique rebuilt, where two shorter sessions a week for eight weeks sets up the rest of the course.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for a niche Higher Level subject in our window?
faqs.answer: We tell you at the start rather than matching your child to a generalist. For the less commonly taught Higher Level options, availability in February is a fraction of availability in October, and a family told in week three that the match is not working has lost weeks it needed. Where a UAE-timezone specialist is unavailable, the alternative is usually a tutor on a compatible timezone at a different hour, and we set that out plainly with the timing involved so you can decide rather than discover it later.

faqs.question: Can two children in a Bur Dubai apartment have sessions on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common arrangement in this district. Because there is no travelling tutor to schedule, two children in different year groups can work with two different specialists back to back, or at the same time if there are two devices and headphones. Where a household shares one laptop, the better plan is shorter sessions placed on different evenings rather than two long ones on the same night. Study space in Karama and Al Mankhool flats is usually shared, and fifty focused minutes with headphones beats a distracted ninety.

faqs.question: How will I know at the halfway point whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: By looking at a marked script rather than asking your child whether it feels better. Every block opens with a full past paper marked against the official scheme and broken down by topic, so at the agreed checkpoint there is something to compare against: a shorter list of error types, a timed section completed at a sensible pace, method marks appearing where they were previously missing. If none of that has moved by the checkpoint, say so. We change the tutor or the approach at that point rather than letting the block run to the end.

If a specialist is not available in your window, we will say so rather than fill the slot.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-business-bay.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors who cover Diploma Programme subjects for students living in Business Bay, Downtown Dubai and along the Dubai Water Canal. Each is matched to one subject at one level, because a Chemistry HL paper and a Maths AI SL paper are not the same job.

intro.heading: What the search for an IB home tutor in Business Bay is really about
paragraphs: Parents in Business Bay type "IB home tutor" into Google for a practical reason, not an abstract one. The district is a dense tower community sitting south of Downtown Dubai along the Dubai Water Canal, and it holds nurseries rather than K-12 campuses. The schools its families use are in Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf, Al Quoz, Al Safa and Al Barsha, which means a car journey at both ends of the day. By the time a Grade 11 student is home, changed and fed, the clock says 5.30pm and there are two Higher Level subjects waiting. A tutor who also has to drive across Sheikh Zayed Road to reach that living room is a tutor who arrives at 6.45pm or not at all.

So the honest answer to the query is that the thing families want from home tutoring is the one-to-one attention and the fit around the school run, not the physical presence of a stranger in the flat. IB Gram delivers that as one-to-one online teaching over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Saying so plainly matters more than winning the click, because a Business Bay parent who books expecting a doorbell has been misled, and the tutoring relationship starts in a hole.

What a Business Bay family gains in exchange is the thing the local-radius model cannot offer: subject-level matching. The Diploma Programme is six subjects assessed in six different ways. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is examined across three papers with a graphical calculator banned from one of them. Physics Higher Level puts 44 per cent of the grade on a single extended-response paper. History Higher Level adds a Paper 3 worth 35 per cent that no Standard Level student ever sees. A tutor who is strong in one of these is not automatically useful in another, and a 20-minute driving radius around Business Bay does not reliably contain a specialist in the particular combination your child is sitting.

This page is written from the syllabus outwards rather than from the neighbourhood inwards. It sets out which paper carries which share of the grade, which command terms quietly decide whether an answer scores, which criterion letters an Internal Assessment is marked against and what its word limit actually is, and what the past-paper work of the final two terms should look like week by week. It also publishes what the Dubai market charges in AED, with each figure attributed to the provider that published it, because three of the six pages currently ranking for this search quote no price at all.

The regulatory picture is here too, because it affects your planning. Dubai private schools answer to KHDA, which inspects them annually on a six-band scale and requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the licensed international curriculum. Private tutoring itself is permitted through MoHRE under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Those are checkable facts with sources, and they are the sort of thing a Business Bay parent is entitled to before handing over an hour of their child's week.
