dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-business-bay.programmesIntro: Business Bay families sit across the whole IB continuum, because the towers house everyone from a PYP Year 2 to a DP2 candidate three months from final exams. These are the programmes we cover and what each one specifically demands of a student living in this part of Dubai.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around six transdisciplinary themes rather than subject silos, and it is assessed by the school rather than by the IB. Tutoring at this stage is about the mechanics that the inquiry model assumes are already in place: number bonds, written methods for multiplication and division, fraction equivalence, reading fluency and the ability to write a paragraph that holds a single idea. Exhibition in Year 6 is where gaps in research and note-taking habits become visible.
programmes.countryNote: Business Bay PYP children are usually driven to Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf or Al Safa, so an online 4.30pm session fits where a travelling tutor cannot. Dubai schools must also run Arabic and Islamic Education from the primary years under KHDA requirements, and for non-Arab children that is often the first subject a parent asks about, because it is the one the family cannot help with at home.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against four criteria per subject, each scored 0-8, and converts the total to a 1-7 grade boundary set by the school. Students lose marks here for reasons that have nothing to do with knowing the content: not addressing a command term, not showing the reflection the criterion asks for, not following the task-specific clarification. MYP Year 5 ePortfolios and the Personal Project are the two moments where that catches up with a student.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP step is the single most common reason a Business Bay parent contacts us. A student who has been comfortable with criterion-based marking for five years meets Diploma Programme papers with timed mark schemes and discovers the two are scored on different logic. Eight to twelve weeks of structured work in the summer before DP1 closes most of that gap, and it is far cheaper than repairing it in DP2.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly 20 to 25 per cent of the grade and externally marked papers for the rest. The paper structures differ sharply by subject group, which is why generic tutoring underperforms at this level and paper-specific work does not.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and Business Bay DP2 students are typically working against school-set internal deadlines for the IA and Extended Essay that fall a long way before the IB's own upload dates. Confirm every IB date with your child's DP coordinator rather than with a tutoring website, including ours. Secondary sources disagree on IB session windows and the IB's own site blocks automated checking.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by a small number of Dubai schools and suits a student who wants Diploma-level rigour in two or three subjects alongside an applied qualification. Tutoring here concentrates on the DP courses taken and on the reflective project's research and referencing standards.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer Dubai schools run the CP than the DP, so a Business Bay family considering it is often choosing between two campuses on opposite sides of the city. Check what the chosen school's CP pathway means for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency before committing, and ask the school directly rather than relying on a general description of the programme.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-business-bay.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma Programme subjects Business Bay families request most, with what each one actually assesses and the specific place marks tend to disappear. The descriptions are deliberately paper-level, because that is the unit of work a tutor and a DP2 student can plan around.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Three papers at Higher Level. Paper 1 is sat without a graphical calculator, which turns algebraic fluency into a grade issue rather than a style preference. Paper 3 is two extended problem-solving questions, and the usual failure is abandoning a question at the first sub-part the student cannot see rather than working forward from the given result.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, with statistics, modelling and financial mathematics carrying real weight. Marks go on unstated assumptions, on reading a regression or chi-squared output without interpreting it in context, and on rounding that is correct arithmetically but wrong for the question's stated degree of accuracy.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-based section; Paper 2 carries the extended responses and the larger share of the grade. The recurring problem is not the mathematics but the explanation: a student who can calculate the field strength often cannot write the three-step causal chain the mark scheme wants for the word 'explain'.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics account for most of the lost marks at Higher Level. The scientific investigation needs a research question that is genuinely measurable with the school's apparatus, and students routinely choose something interesting that cannot generate enough data points to analyse properly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides this subject. 'Outline' and 'explain' carry different mark allocations and different expectations, and a full, well-informed paragraph written against the wrong command term scores a fraction of what it should. The data-analysis questions reward students who have practised reading unfamiliar graphs under time pressure.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries make up the portfolio, each limited to 800 words and each marked against the same criteria including diagram accuracy and the named key concept. Higher Level adds a quantitative paper. Most marks are lost on diagrams that are drawn but never referred to in the analysis, and on evaluation that lists two sides without reaching a judgement.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-released case study rewards early, structured preparation and punishes cramming. Students lose marks by describing a tool rather than applying it to the stated firm, and by answering a 10-mark question with the structure of a 4-mark one. Tutoring here is largely about answer architecture and timing.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis against a guiding question, and the guiding question is where most of the marks are decided. Higher Level adds the 1,200-1,500 word HL Essay on a studied text. The Individual Oral asks a student to connect a global issue to two texts, and weak choices made in Year 12 constrain what is possible in Year 13.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Reading and listening comprehension carry the largest external weighting, and the written assignment is judged on register and audience as much as on grammar. Students who have strong conversational English frequently underperform here because the paper tests text type conventions they have never been taught explicitly.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Paper 1 is source-based, Paper 2 is comparative essays, and Higher Level adds Paper 3 at 35 per cent on a single regional option. The historical investigation is 2,200 words and is marked substantially on the evaluation of sources rather than on the narrative, which is the opposite of what most students instinctively write.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title are assessed against published criteria, and the essay is marked on the quality of the argument rather than on the breadth of examples. Students who treat TOK as an afterthought lose points from the Diploma's bonus three, which is a cheap way to miss a university offer.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words, supervised by a teacher at the school, marked out of 34 across five criteria including engagement, which is assessed from the student's reflections rather than the essay itself. Subject choice and research question are the two decisions that determine the grade, and both are made before any writing starts.

These are the areas our Business Bay students share tutors and timetables with.

regions.note: High-density towers along both banks of the Dubai Water Canal, with nurseries but no K-12 campus inside the district. Every school run leaves the area, which pushes the earliest practical weekday session to around 5pm.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Immediately north across Al Khail and Sheikh Zayed Road. Shares the same school catchments as Business Bay and the same absence of on-site campuses, so the two communities behave as one tutoring market.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland

sections.heading: What a Business Bay family is actually buying when they search for a home tutor
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Business Bay, as the phrase is used by the families who search it, means one adult giving one child undivided attention on a specific subject at a specific level, at a time that fits around a school run that leaves the district. The word 'home' in the search is about privacy and convenience, not about transport. Once you separate those two things, the delivery question answers itself: IB Gram provides that teaching as one-to-one online tuition over live video, and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India.

The reason this is not a compromise comes down to arithmetic. The Diploma Programme has six subject groups, two levels, two mathematics routes and a different assessment architecture in each. The chance that a tutor who is genuinely strong in, say, Chemistry Higher Level organic mechanisms also lives within a workable evening drive of a particular tower on the Dubai Water Canal is low, and it gets lower the more specific the need. Removing the travel constraint does not reduce the pool of tutors by a little; it expands it by a lot, and the expansion is concentrated exactly where the scarcity is.

There is a cost argument sitting alongside it, and it runs in the same direction. Published in-home rates in Dubai sit between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is not a quality premium. It is travel time being paid for, plus the smaller supply that a radius creates. A Business Bay parent who pays the travel premium is buying a tutor's commute, and getting a narrower choice of specialist in return.

What this page does from here is unusual for the search term, and deliberately so. Rather than describing the neighbourhood and listing subject names, it sets out the assessment machinery your child is being marked by: which paper is worth what, which words in a question control the mark scheme, which criterion letters an Internal Assessment is scored against, and what the final two terms of past-paper work should look like. That is the material a tutor and a student spend an hour a week on, so it is the material you should be able to judge us by before booking anything.

sections.heading: The Diploma assessment map: which paper carries which share of the grade
paragraphs: Most Diploma students, and a surprising number of parents, cannot say what fraction of a subject grade each paper carries. That matters because revision time is finite and the papers are not equally weighted. A Physics Higher Level student who spends equal hours on Paper 1 and Paper 2 has misallocated effort against a 36 to 44 split. A History Higher Level student who neglects Paper 3 is ignoring 35 per cent of the subject. The table below is the map, and the first job of any serious tutoring block is to look at it with the student and decide where the hours go.

Read the internal assessment column carefully. Across almost every subject it sits at roughly a fifth to a quarter of the final grade, and it is the only component the student controls completely: unlimited time, access to resources, a known mark scheme and the chance to redraft. A student sitting on a predicted 5 who has produced a weak Internal Assessment has usually thrown away the cheapest marks available to them. Fixing that is often a better use of six sessions than another round of Paper 2 practice.

The other pattern the table exposes is where levels diverge. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra content bolted on; in several subjects it introduces a whole additional paper with its own question style. Maths AA Higher Level adds Paper 3, two long structured investigations that reward a student who keeps working forward from a given result rather than stopping at the first unfamiliar sub-part. History adds Paper 3. English A adds the HL Essay. Those additions are where Higher Level grades are won and lost, and they are frequently the components a school has least time to rehearse.

Weightings are taken from the current published subject guides and are stable across a teaching cycle, but the IB does revise them between syllabus versions. Check your child's exact combination with the Diploma Programme coordinator at their school before planning around any figure, including the ones here. The same applies to session and results dates: we do not publish IB exam dates on these pages, because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically and secondary sources disagree with each other.

sections.heading: Command terms are the mark scheme in disguise
paragraphs: The single most common reason a well-prepared Diploma student underscores is that they answered a different question from the one printed. IB papers are built on command terms, and each term carries an expectation that the examiner's mark scheme enforces strictly. 'State' wants a single fact with no working. 'Outline' wants a brief account. 'Describe' wants detail without causation. 'Explain' wants the mechanism, step by step, with each step connected to the next. 'Discuss' wants a balanced review with arguments on both sides. 'Evaluate' and 'Justify' want a judgement reached and defended. A student who writes an excellent description where the paper asked for an explanation has produced good work that cannot score.

This is diagnosable in a single session. Give a student a marked past paper and the official scheme, and ask them to say, for each question they lost marks on, which command term was used and what that term required. Most cannot do it for more than half the paper. That is not a knowledge gap and no amount of content revision closes it. It closes in two to four sessions of deliberate practice: same content, different command terms, marked against the real descriptors each time until the student can predict the shape of the answer before writing it.

The pattern is sharpest in the sciences and in Economics. In Physics and Chemistry, 'deduce' and 'determine' both expect working to be shown, but 'deduce' also expects a conclusion drawn from given information rather than from memory. In Economics, 'examine' and 'evaluate' both require two-sided treatment, but a question worth 15 marks expects a judgement that a 10-mark question does not. In Mathematics the critical term is 'hence', which signals that the previous result must be used; students who restart from scratch after 'hence' lose the method marks even when the final answer is correct.

For Business Bay students specifically, this is the highest-return work available in a weekly online session, because it needs nothing but a paper, a mark scheme and someone who knows how examiners read. There is no equipment, no travel and no lab. It also transfers across subjects: a student who learns to read command terms in Biology reads them better in History the following week. That is why a command-term audit is usually the first thing we do rather than the last.
bullets: 'Explain' requires a connected mechanism; 'describe' does not and scores less if that is all you give

sections.heading: Internal assessment, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component, and every one of them is marked against published criteria identified by letter with a fixed mark allocation per letter. Students are given this information by their schools and routinely do not use it. The most useful hour a tutor can spend on an Internal Assessment is the first one, before any writing exists: read the criteria aloud, decide what evidence each letter needs, and check whether the research question or chosen text can actually generate that evidence.

Word and page limits are enforced, and overshooting them costs marks mechanically rather than by judgement. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words. The History investigation is 2,200. A scientific investigation in Physics, Chemistry or Biology is 3,000. Each Economics commentary is 800, and there are three of them. The English A HL Essay sits between 1,200 and 1,500. A Mathematics exploration has no hard word count but a recommended length of roughly 12 to 20 pages, and examiners are explicit that a longer exploration is not a better one. Writing to the limit from the outset is easier than cutting 900 words out of a finished draft.

The boundary of what a tutor may do here is a real rule, not a disclaimer. Under IB academic honesty requirements the submitted work must be the student's own, authenticated by the supervising teacher at the school. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion is asking, question whether a method is sound, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the data, and mark a student's own draft against the published descriptors. A tutor may not supply text, draft sections, or edit a draft into a submission. We decline that work when it is requested, and it is requested, because at least one competitor in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright.

There is a practical reason beyond the ethics. The reflection and engagement criteria in several subjects are marked from the student's own record of how the work developed, and a student who did not do the thinking cannot produce credible reflections. Supervisors notice. The fastest route to a strong Internal Assessment mark is genuinely a well-coached student doing their own work early, because the criteria were designed to reward exactly that and to expose the alternative.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Business Bay, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Start with the monthly number, because that is the one a household budget is built on rather than the hourly rate. A single weekly 60-minute session with a qualified online subject tutor at published Dubai market rates lands somewhere around AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month. The same session with an in-home tutor lands closer to AED 800 to AED 2,000, and monthly in-home packages advertised in Dubai run from AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Online monthly packages in the same market have been published from AED 799 for eight sessions. That spread is wide enough to change which plan a family can sustain for two years, which is the relevant timescale for a Diploma.

Now the hourly view, by tier, with attribution. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, is advertised from AED 33 to AED 150. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted from AED 150 to AED 300. In-home one-to-one with travel included sits at AED 180 to AED 500. Named IB and IGCSE specialists are quoted between AED 200 and AED 450 and above, and premium examiner-led tutoring has been published as high as AED 650. These are market figures published by the providers named in the table, read in October 2026, not IB Gram's price list.

The useful question is what the in-home premium actually purchases. It is not more teaching time, because an hour is an hour. It is not better subject fit, because the pool is restricted to tutors within driving distance. What it buys is physical presence and the tutor's travel, and in a tower district with canal crossings at both ends of the drive, that travel is substantial and it is priced into every session. A parent paying AED 350 rather than AED 220 for the same hour of Chemistry teaching is, in most cases, paying AED 130 for a car journey.

What IB Gram's own arrangement looks like is simple enough to state without a price list: a trial lesson first so you can judge the tutor before committing, then blocks booked by the term with the slot held. If you want figures for your child's exact subject and level, ask on the consultation rather than reading a number off a page, because the honest answer depends on level, session length and frequency. Any provider quoting a single universal rate for 'IB tutoring' is quoting an average, and no family pays an average.

sections.heading: The past-paper sequence that actually moves a Diploma grade
paragraphs: Past papers are the most misused resource in the Diploma. The standard pattern is to work through them in chronological order, check answers against the mark scheme, feel reassured or alarmed, and repeat. That produces familiarity without improvement, because nothing in the loop forces the student to change behaviour. A sequence that works has four distinct stages and the student should know which stage they are in at any point.

Stage one is untimed, open-book, by topic. The purpose is diagnosis, not score: which sub-topics generate errors, and are they knowledge errors, method errors or command-term errors. Stage two is timed by question, still by topic, with the mark scheme used immediately after each question rather than at the end. This is where method marks get recovered, because the student sees exactly where the scheme awarded a mark they did not claim. Stage three is full papers to time, in the morning if possible, marked strictly by someone else. Stage four is targeted re-attempt: the failed questions only, four to six weeks later, cold.

An error log is what holds the sequence together. One line per lost mark: paper, question, command term, what went wrong, and the category. Within three weeks the pattern is visible, and it is almost never evenly spread. A typical Maths AA Higher Level log shows most losses concentrated in two or three places, often integration by substitution, complex number manipulation and the second half of Paper 3. Revising the whole syllabus for a student with that log is a waste of their remaining weeks, and the log is what makes that obvious to the student rather than just to the tutor.

Timing deserves its own treatment, because in several subjects it is the binding constraint rather than knowledge. History Paper 3 asks for three essays in two and a half hours, and students who know the content well still run out of time on the third. The fix is not more content; it is a fixed planning allowance per essay, practised until it is automatic. Physics Paper 2 rewards the same discipline on extended responses. These are habits, and habits need rehearsal under conditions, which is why the last six weeks before the May session should contain more marked full papers than new teaching.
bullets: Four stages: untimed by topic, timed by question, full paper to time, cold re-attempt
Use the mark scheme immediately after each question, not at the end of the paper
One line of error log per lost mark, categorised as knowledge, method or command term
In the final six weeks, marked full papers should outnumber new teaching hours

sections.heading: Business Bay has no school campus, and that decides your session time
paragraphs: This is the operational fact that shapes tutoring in the district more than anything else. Business Bay holds nurseries and early-years provision, but the K-12 campuses its families use all sit outside it: Sobha Hartland and Mohammed Bin Rashid City to the east, Al Jaddaf across the creek extension, Al Quoz and Al Safa to the west, Al Barsha further out. Every secondary student in the towers therefore travels, usually by car or school bus, through a road network whose afternoon flow is governed by the canal crossings and the Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail interchanges.

In practice that means a Diploma student leaving school at 3.00pm or 3.15pm is rarely settled and ready to work before 4.45pm, and often not before 5.15pm if the route runs through Al Quoz. Add a travelling tutor to that evening and you are negotiating two separate journeys against the same traffic, which is why in-home sessions in central Dubai so often get set at 6.30pm or later, and why they are the first thing to collapse when a school adds an after-school commitment. An online session can start at 4.30pm from a bedroom desk with the school bag still in the hall.

The day of the week matters too. Dubai schools run Monday to Friday with a shorter Friday, which concentrates the useful tutoring window into Monday to Thursday evenings plus the weekend. Saturday morning is the single most requested slot we see from central Dubai, because the student is rested and nothing competes with it. Sunday evening is the second, used as a setup session for the week ahead. For a DP2 student in the exam run, one weekday evening plus one weekend morning is a more durable pattern than two weekday evenings.

Ramadan changes the whole shape for a term. School hours shorten, energy profiles shift and families reorganise the evening around iftar. Sessions commonly move to the late morning or to after iftar, and that reorganisation is straightforward online and genuinely difficult with a travelling tutor in a city where the roads just before sunset are at their worst. We schedule around it rather than pausing, because for a DP2 student the Ramadan weeks usually sit close to the May session and are not weeks that can be given up.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: where a tutor stops
paragraphs: The IB treats authorship as a matter of fact rather than of degree. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own, and the supervising teacher at the school authenticates it. A breach is not a style issue; it triggers the IB's academic misconduct process, and the outcome for a student can be the loss of a subject grade or of the Diploma. That exposure sits with the student, not with the tutor, which is why a tutoring service that blurs the line is transferring risk to a sixteen-year-old in exchange for a fee.

The permitted territory is wide and genuinely useful. A tutor may teach the content the assessment rests on. A tutor may explain what a criterion requires and what evidence satisfies it. A tutor may say that a research question cannot be answered with the apparatus available, that a sample size will not support the statistical test chosen, that a conclusion overreaches the data, or that an argument in a Theory of Knowledge essay has no counter-position. A tutor may mark a student's own draft against the published descriptors and explain each mark. All of that is teaching, and all of it raises marks.

The prohibited territory is narrow and absolute. A tutor does not supply sentences for a submission, does not draft a section, does not rewrite a paragraph into its final form, and does not produce an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay, Personal Project or any assessed coursework on a student's behalf. Requests for exactly that arrive regularly in this market, and they are declined. One operator in this SERP advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; that is an academic integrity breach being sold as a service, and a family should treat any provider who offers it as unsafe for everything else too.

There is also a records question worth naming. We reference official syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes and point to the board's own pages for them. We do not host or hand out IB, Cambridge or Pearson materials, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. If a tutoring service offers you a library of downloadable mark schemes, that is a signal about how it treats rules in general.
bullets: Permitted: teaching content, explaining criteria, questioning method, marking the student's own draft
Not permitted: supplying text, drafting sections, or producing assessed work for the student
The school supervisor authenticates authorship, and reflection criteria expose work that is not the student's

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and the Diploma timetable squeeze
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Inspection outcomes run on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and a published band is a reasonable starting point for a parent comparing campuses, though it describes the school as a whole rather than the Diploma teaching of one subject. Ask a school directly how its Higher Level cohorts in your child's subjects have performed before drawing conclusions from a headline band.

Alongside the licensed international curriculum, Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, and KHDA's guidance is specific about how. Separate classes are required for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and any mandatory-subject lesson is advised to run at least 25 minutes. Schools also require appropriate KHDA approval for the teachers who deliver Arabic and Islamic Education.

The consequence for a Diploma student in Business Bay is a timetable squeeze that parents often do not see until DP1. Six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the mandatory UAE subjects have to coexist in the same week, and the components that lose out are usually the ones with no external paper attached: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the early stages of Internal Assessment work. That is precisely why so many Internal Assessments start late, and why an early block of online coaching in DP1 pays for itself in DP2.

Equivalency is the other thing worth planning early, because it affects UAE university applications rather than school progression. For British-track students the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects at IGCSE or GCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among the five, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One page currently ranking for these searches states six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong. For IB students we publish no points threshold, because none has been read on the Ministry's own site, and an unsourced number here would be a number a family acts on. Verify through the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation channel, and treat IB Gram's role as explaining the process rather than performing it.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the deadline
process.description: Not just 'IB maths'. Which route, which level, which paper is the problem, and what date is fixed: a school mock, an Internal Assessment submission, the May session. A Business Bay family that gives us the school name as well lets us anticipate the internal deadline calendar, which is usually tighter than the IB's.

process.title: We match by subject and level before anything else
process.description: The constraint we optimise is specialist fit, not postcode, because lessons are online and distance is irrelevant to delivery. If the exact combination is scarce we say so at this point and give you a realistic timescale rather than placing a near-match and hoping it holds.

process.title: A trial lesson, then you decide
process.description: One session before any paid block, so the student meets the tutor and you see how a lesson is run. It is a diagnostic as much as an introduction: by the end there should be a stated view on where the marks are going and what the first four sessions will address.

process.title: A written plan with the papers named
process.description: After the trial you get the plan in writing: which components, which weightings, which past papers, what gets set between sessions and how it will be marked. If an Internal Assessment is in scope, the criterion letters and the length limit are in the plan from the start.

process.title: Weekly sessions in a held slot
process.description: The same tutor in the same slot, booked by the term so it survives the school calendar. Notes go to the parent after each session, and the error log travels with the student rather than living in the tutor's notebook.

process.title: Review at six sessions, honestly
process.description: Six sessions is enough to judge whether the pairing works and whether the plan is landing. If it is not, we change the tutor or the plan and say which. A review that always concludes everything is fine is not a review.

whyPoints.title: Specialist fit instead of a driving radius
whyPoints.description: Online delivery removes distance from the matching problem, so a Business Bay student needing Chemistry Higher Level organic mechanisms gets someone who teaches that, rather than the nearest available generalist. On a six-subject, two-level programme, that difference compounds over two years.

whyPoints.title: Paper-level planning, not chapter-by-chapter
whyPoints.description: Sessions are organised around the components that carry the marks, with the weightings on the table in front of the student. A plan that names Paper 3 and the exploration is a plan a sixteen-year-old can argue with, which is the point.

whyPoints.title: Prices you can check against the market
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it and dated. We do not present market rates as ours, and we do not quote a single universal hourly rate for a programme with two levels and six subject groups.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach, question and mark against published criteria. We decline requests to produce an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, and we say so on the page rather than in the small print, because the risk of the alternative falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for a district with no school in it
whyPoints.description: Business Bay school runs leave the area in both directions, so sessions are set to start when a student is actually home and able to work. Ramadan timings, mock weeks and study leave are planned around rather than treated as interruptions.

whyPoints.title: Sourced facts, and silence where there is no source
whyPoints.description: Regulatory and equivalency statements here carry their origin. Where a figure could not be verified, including IB session and results dates and the Ministry of Education's IB points threshold, we leave it out and point you to the authority instead of guessing.

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor in Business Bay charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates for in-home one-to-one tuition run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to 500. Qualified online subject tutors are quoted lower, AED 150 to 300, with Unitors advertising IB from AED 200. Those are market figures from the providers named, read in October 2026, not IB Gram's price list. The gap between the two bands is mostly travel time rather than teaching quality. Ask for a figure for your child's specific subject, level and session length on the consultation, because a single universal rate for the whole Diploma is an average nobody actually pays.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an apartment in Business Bay?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Teaching for Business Bay families is one-to-one and delivered live online, over video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The URL you arrived on uses the phrase parents search, and we would rather target it honestly than imply a doorbell. The practical trade is a good one here: the towers have no K-12 campus, both ends of the school run cross the canal, and removing the tutor's journey means you can start a session at 4.30pm and choose a specialist in the exact subject and level rather than whoever lives nearby.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do Business Bay families usually drive to?
faqs.answer: Business Bay has nurseries but no K-12 campus, so secondary students travel. The nearest cluster with Diploma provision sits in Sobha Hartland and Mohammed Bin Rashid City, with Al Jaddaf across the creek extension and a larger, older cluster west and south in Al Quoz, Al Safa and Al Barsha. Schools named on this page are context for the communities we teach into; IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them. Check current programme offerings and the latest published inspection outcome on KHDA's own site rather than on a tutoring page, including this one, because provision changes between academic years.

faqs.question: What time can a Business Bay session realistically start on a school night?
faqs.answer: A Diploma student leaving school at around 3pm is rarely settled and ready to work before 4.45pm, and later if the route runs through Al Quoz. Online, 4.30pm to 5pm is achievable because there is no second journey to coordinate; in-home sessions in central Dubai commonly end up at 6.30pm or later for exactly that reason. Monday to Thursday evenings and Saturday morning are the slots that hold up best over a term. Saturday morning is the one we see requested most from the central corridor, because the student is rested and nothing else competes with the time.

faqs.question: How many Diploma papers does my child sit at Higher Level in Business Bay schools?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject rather than the school. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is three papers, with Paper 1 sat without a graphical calculator and Paper 3 worth 20 per cent. Physics and Chemistry Higher Level are two papers, weighted roughly 36 and 44 per cent with a 20 per cent investigation. History Higher Level is three papers, with Paper 3 alone worth 35 per cent. English A: Language and Literature has two papers plus an HL Essay and an Individual Oral. Confirm your child's exact combination with the Diploma Programme coordinator at their school, because weightings are revised between syllabus versions.

faqs.question: Where is the line between tutoring help and IB malpractice on the exploration?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. A tutor may teach the mathematics involved, explain what each criterion rewards, challenge whether the chosen topic can carry enough mathematics, point out where a method is unsound, and mark the student's own draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not supply text or produce the exploration. The reflection and engagement criteria are scored from the student's own account of how the work developed, so coached work that the student did themselves scores better than work they did not, quite apart from the misconduct risk.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost Business Bay students the most marks?
faqs.answer: 'Explain' is the biggest single loss, because it demands a connected mechanism and students supply a description instead. 'Hence' in a mathematics question is the second: it signals that the previous result must be used, and restarting from scratch forfeits method marks even when the final answer is right. In the sciences, 'deduce' expects a conclusion drawn from information given rather than recalled. In Economics, a 15-mark question expects a judgement that a 10-mark question does not. This is fixable quickly. Two to four sessions of deliberate command-term practice against real mark schemes usually recovers more marks than another full content pass.

faqs.question: Is Paper 3 worth tutoring separately for a Maths AA HL student in Business Bay?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because it is 20 per cent of the grade in a question style nothing else in the course rehearses. Paper 3 is two extended, structured investigations that build sub-part by sub-part, and the common failure is not a knowledge gap but abandoning the question at the first sub-part the student cannot see. Working forward from a given result is a learnable habit, and it needs practice on whole Paper 3 questions rather than on topic exercises. Schools often have the least timetable room for this component, which makes it one of the higher-return things a weekly online session can cover in the final two terms.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 near Business Bay and already behind. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: DP1 is the cheapest point in the programme to intervene, so no. Two things usually need attention at this stage, and neither is content. The first is the gap between criterion-based MYP marking and timed Diploma mark schemes, which is where most of the first-term shock comes from. The second is the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay timeline, which slips in DP1 because those components have no external paper attached and lose out to the ones that do. Eight to twelve weeks of structured work now costs considerably less than repairing the same gap under exam pressure in DP2.

faqs.question: Does a tutor living near Business Bay beat a specialist teaching online?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma subjects, no. Proximity helps with transport and nothing else, and transport is not part of the teaching. The Diploma has six subject groups, two levels and two mathematics routes, so the useful question is whether the tutor knows the exact paper structure your child sits. A radius of a 20-minute drive around a tower in Business Bay does not reliably contain that person, and paying the in-home premium narrows the choice further. Where proximity genuinely matters is practical laboratory work, and that is delivered by the school rather than by any tutor, in-home or online.

faqs.question: How can a Business Bay parent check that a private tutor holds the MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the private tuition work permit is issued by MoHRE free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you read online as unverified. MoHRE's own service page is the route to check the requirement.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards UAE equivalency for a Business Bay student?
faqs.answer: Not towards the five-subject count on the British track. The Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects at IGCSE or GCSE at no less than grade E or 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One page currently ranking for UAE tutoring searches states six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. The subjects still have to be taken, because KHDA requires them in Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum. Verify your child's position through the Ministry or your emirate's attestation channel before it matters.

faqs.question: Can Business Bay lessons move to post-iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they routinely do. School hours shorten during Ramadan, energy profiles change and families reorganise the evening around iftar, so sessions shift to late morning or to after iftar. Online scheduling makes that a calendar change rather than a logistics problem, which matters in a city where the roads immediately before sunset are at their most difficult. For a DP2 student the Ramadan weeks usually sit close to the May session, so pausing for a month is expensive. We plan the term around the shift instead, with the slot agreed before Ramadan starts rather than week by week.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers my child's Higher Level subject in Business Bay?
faqs.answer: We say so, with a timescale, rather than placing a near-match. Some combinations are genuinely scarce, particularly Higher Level subjects outside the common six and second languages at Higher Level. If we cannot cover it we will tell you at the matching stage, suggest what else would move the grade in the time available, and keep the request open. Because delivery is online, availability is not limited to tutors living within reach of Business Bay, which widens the pool considerably; it does not make it infinite. An honest no at the start is cheaper for your child than three wasted sessions.

faqs.question: How many weeks of IB tutoring do Business Bay families usually book?
faqs.answer: Three patterns dominate. A single problem subject in DP1 typically runs as a weekly session across a term, around twelve weeks, with a review at six. Internal Assessment or Extended Essay coaching runs shorter and denser, four to eight sessions timed to the school's own submission deadlines rather than the IB's. The exam run before the May session is eight to twelve weeks at two or three sessions a week across one or two subjects. We review at six sessions in every case and will say if the pairing or the plan is not working, which is a more useful conversation than a renewal reminder.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-business-bay.closingHeading: Start with the paper, not the postcode
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-business-bay.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB home tutor in Business Bay, the useful first step is to name the component rather than the subject: Paper 3, the exploration, the HL Essay, Paper 2 extended responses. Tell us that, your child's level and the date that is already fixed in the school calendar, and we will match a specialist in exactly that and run a trial lesson before anything is booked. Lessons are one-to-one and online, on Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE. What you get instead is the tutor who teaches that paper, at a time your child is actually home and able to think.

Each one teaches one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Four neighbourhoods, one shortlist
paragraphs: City Walk sits in an unusual position for this search. It is a low-rise, walkable district wedged between Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah, surrounded on three sides by established villa communities and on the fourth by the Downtown corridor. A parent living there who types 'IB home tutor in City Walk' will, within ten minutes, also have typed Al Wasl, Jumeirah 1 and probably Al Safa, because those are the areas the family knows and the drive between any two of them is under fifteen minutes. Four searches, four sets of results, and no way to tell whether the differences mean anything.

They do not. The reason is arithmetic rather than opinion. Dubai has 227 private schools serving 387,441 pupils, of whom roughly 7% are on International Baccalaureate programmes, and a Diploma subject at Higher Level is taught by a small number of teachers in any given part of the city. Narrow the field to people willing to drive to a specific district on a Tuesday at five o'clock and the shortlist for Higher Level chemistry or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches drops to a handful. That handful is almost exactly the same handful whether the address is in City Walk, Al Wasl, Jumeirah 1 or Al Safa, because the four districts share a road network and therefore share a catchment.

The second thing that does not change between the four is what in-home delivery costs. Read from the cheapest end, the Dubai market starts with budget online tutoring advertised from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, usually university students. Qualified subject tutors working online occupy AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one sits above that at AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500, and specialist Diploma tutors run AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. The step from the online band to the in-home band is a vehicle. It is not a better lesson.

IB Gram's position is stated at the top rather than buried. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. A City Walk family therefore gets a shortlist built from everyone who has taught the current Diploma syllabus in the subject they need, rather than from the subset who can reach Al Wasl Road before the evening traffic. That is the whole trade, and the comparison table further down puts both sides of it in the same frame so you can judge it rather than take it on trust.

What follows is the detail: the four neighbourhoods compared on the things that actually differ, what the in-home premium buys on this particular corridor, how the tutor pool narrows as the radius shrinks, which subjects have thin UAE coverage and what happens when nobody is free, how to verify that any tutor is legally permitted to teach in the UAE, and exactly what a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay.

This is the stage where subject specialism matters most and where a proximity-based search narrows the shortlist most sharply, because a Higher Level subject is a small market.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma schools a City Walk family reaches easily sit in Al Safa, Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim rather than in City Walk itself, which has no large secondary campus. That means every Diploma student from this district commutes, and it means the local tutor pool is shared across all four surrounding neighbourhoods. Al Wasl families, Jumeirah 1 families and City Walk families are competing for the same evening slots with the same people.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, assessed against four criteria per subject, each out of eight, with the total of 32 converted to a level from one to seven. Support at this stage is about reading the criterion breakdown correctly rather than about content, and the diagnosis is the same wherever the family lives.

Most campuses in this corridor are British-curriculum, so a Middle Years Programme family here is in a minority locally and will field a good deal of comparison with neighbours whose children sit Year 9 tests instead.

programmes.name: Year 11 qualifications before the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, taken at most of the British-curriculum schools in this corridor before students split into A Levels or the Diploma. Tiering, syllabus codes and board choice vary by school, and the content assumed at the start of a Diploma course is Extended or Higher tier.
programmes.countryNote: This is the most common route into the Diploma for families in City Walk, Al Wasl and Al Safa, simply because the schools nearby are predominantly British. It also means the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is the single most valuable support window available in this corridor, and it is the one almost nobody uses.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: IA, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: Internal assessments in each subject, a 4,000-word Extended Essay with a school supervisor, and Theory of Knowledge with a prescribed-title essay and an exhibition. All of it is the student's own work. A tutor may teach the criteria, question a research question and challenge an argument, and may not write, edit or supply any part of it.
programmes.countryNote: This is the part of the Diploma where the home-tutor market in Dubai is least trustworthy and where a parent in any of these four districts should be most careful. The risk of that purchase falls entirely on the student, and no convenience of location changes it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-city-walk.subjectsIntro: Proximity costs more in some subjects than in others, because the pool of teachers thins out sharply as the level rises. These are the Diploma subjects City Walk families ask for, with how scarce a genuine specialist is in a twenty-minute radius.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested subject in this corridor and the one where a proximity search fails most often. Higher Level requires fluent calculus, proof and complex numbers taught at speed; a tutor comfortable with Standard Level is not automatically comfortable with Higher Level, and the distinction is invisible from a listing page. Ask which Higher Level topics they have taught in the last two years.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led with graphing technology assumed throughout. Easier to staff locally than Analysis and Approaches because more general mathematics teachers can cover Standard Level competently. Higher Level, with its statistical inference and modelling content, is a genuinely different course and a much smaller pool.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Six themes across structure and reactivity, two written papers and one scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Organic mechanisms are the part that needs a specialist, because the marks turn on arrow placement and conditions rather than on understanding. Very thin local availability at Higher Level in any Dubai district.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, two written papers and one investigation, with no third paper in the current course. The scarcest science locally, and the one where families most often end up with a mathematics teacher covering physics. The data-based section of Paper 1 and the uncertainty arithmetic are the specialist parts.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Better covered locally than physics or chemistry, with a large volume of recall and the same investigation criteria as the other sciences. The specialist value is in command-term discipline and in teaching the student to answer the question that was asked rather than the one they revised for.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internally assessed commentaries plus examinations, with Higher Level adding quantitative content. Popular in this corridor given the household mix, and reasonably well covered by tutors locally, although the commentary work is where a specialist earns the rate by teaching the criteria rather than editing the writing.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay. The individual oral is the component families underestimate most. Widely available locally in principle, but the quality spread is large and a strong general English teacher is not the same as somebody who knows the assessment.

subjects.name: Language acquisition: French, Spanish and Arabic
subjects.levels: Higher Level, Standard Level and ab initio
subjects.description: Availability depends heavily on the language and the level. Arabic at a high level is better served in Dubai than in most markets; ab initio Spanish or French at short notice in a specific evening slot is harder. Oral components need a tutor who will conduct them properly rather than discuss them.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: A prescribed-title essay and an exhibition for Theory of Knowledge; a 4,000-word independent piece with a school supervisor for the Extended Essay. The scarcest thing here is not subject knowledge but somebody who will coach the process honestly and refuse to touch the writing, which is the opposite of what parts of this market sell.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-city-walk.regionsTitle: City Walk and the districts it is constantly compared with
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-city-walk.regionsIntro: These are the neighbourhoods a City Walk family will search alongside their own, and what each one genuinely offers that the others do not. The honest summary is that the differences are about housing and commute rather than about access to teaching.

regions.name: City Walk
regions.note: Low-rise apartments and townhouses, walkable, with no large secondary campus inside the district. Every secondary student commutes, mostly west into Al Safa and Jumeirah or north into Downtown. Short internal distances make a 17:00 session feasible once the school run is accounted for.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: Villas and compounds along Al Wasl Road, immediately adjacent. Families here sit closest to the Al Safa school cluster and have the shortest school run in this group, which is the only material advantage over City Walk. The tutor catchment is identical, because it is the same road.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: Established villa district running to the coast, with several long-standing British-curriculum schools and one IB continuum campus within a few minutes. The oldest school provision in this corridor and the strongest argument for staying put, but no additional local tutor supply at Higher Level.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: The densest school cluster in the group, with British-curriculum and IB provision side by side. A family living here has the shortest commute of all four and will still find that Higher Level physics and chemistry are taught by a very small number of people within a twenty-minute drive.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2 and Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Further west along the coast, quieter, with primary provision close by and secondary options a slightly longer run. Widening the search here adds housing options and does not add tutors, because the same teachers already serve the whole corridor.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Beyond Jumeirah 3, with two substantial campuses including an IB continuum school. This is where a City Walk Diploma student may be travelling to every morning, which makes the afternoon return the binding constraint on weekday session timing.

regions.name: La Mer and Pearl Jumeira
regions.note: Coastal, newer and residential rather than institutional, with no secondary schools of their own. Families here face the same pattern as City Walk: a commute out, a shared tutor catchment, and evening slots competing with three neighbouring districts.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: North across Al Wasl Road and Sheikh Zayed Road, dense and school-free at secondary level. Included because it is the fourth direction a City Walk family searches, and because it demonstrates the point: the pool is the city's, not the district's.

schoolClusters.city: Al Safa and Al Wasl campuses, the shortest run from City Walk
schoolClusters.note: This cluster is why the four districts in this comparison behave as one catchment. The schools sit between them, families from all four attend, and the tutors who serve those families serve all four equally. Confirm current programmes with each school rather than with any tutoring site.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Al Safa

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha campuses, a longer return leg
schoolClusters.note: The second ring, reached in fifteen to thirty minutes depending on the hour. Diploma provision here is substantial, and students from City Walk travel to it daily. The longer afternoon journey is the main reason weekday sessions for this group start at 17:30 rather than 17:00.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-city-walk.modesIntro: Three delivery shapes a City Walk family will be choosing between, two of which exist in this market and one of which IB Gram provides. The comparison is set out honestly because the decision is a real one and the costs differ.

modes.title: One-to-one online, what IB Gram delivers
modes.description: Live video, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and the student's working shared on screen. The shortlist is drawn from every tutor who has taught the subject at the level needed rather than from those who can reach Al Wasl Road by five o'clock. Market rate for qualified subject tutors working this way runs AED 150 to 300 an hour.

modes.description: Described here because it is what the search phrase means, not because IB Gram sells it. Published Dubai rates run AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 table, with independent tutors quoting AED 200 to 500 and monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. sections.heading: What a City Walk home-tutor search is actually asking
paragraphs: The phrase carries two separate questions and they have different answers. The first is practical: can somebody competent teach my child, in our home, at a time that works. The second is a proxy for the first: is there anyone near us who actually knows this syllabus. Parents in this corridor type the first because it is how tutoring has worked everywhere they have lived, and they are really asking the second. Separating them is the useful move, because the answer to the second is yes and the answer to the first, from IB Gram at least, is no.

The reason the two questions come apart in Dubai is that the supply of Diploma subject specialists is not distributed the way housing is. A district like City Walk has excellent housing, good access and no secondary school inside it. The teachers who can take a Higher Level chemistry student from a 4 to a 6 live wherever they live, work full days at schools across the city, and have a limited number of evening hours. Requiring one of them to spend forty to ninety minutes in a car to reach Al Wasl Road reduces the number who can help from a reasonable list to a very short one, and the short list is not chosen for teaching quality.

This page therefore does something that most pages competing for this search do not: it compares the options in the same frame, with the published prices attached and the limitation stated. IB Gram delivers one-to-one online tuition and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, because that is a service the business runs only in India. If an in-home tutor is genuinely what a family wants, the market rates further down will tell them what to expect to pay and what the premium represents, and the comparison is set out so a parent can disagree with the conclusion if they choose.
bullets: 'Home tutor' usually means 'someone who knows this syllabus', not 'someone nearby'
Specialist supply follows teachers' working lives, not residential districts
Both options are priced on this page so the comparison can be checked

sections.heading: City Walk against Al Wasl, Jumeirah 1 and Al Safa
paragraphs: Four addresses, fifteen minutes apart at worst, and four separate searches. The table below sets out what actually differs between them for a family buying Diploma support, and the honest finding is that the differences sit in housing type and school run rather than in access to teaching. Al Safa has the densest school cluster and the shortest commute. Al Wasl has villas and the same cluster a minute further on. Jumeirah 1 has the oldest provision and the longest-established community. City Walk has apartments, walkability and no campus of its own.

What does not vary is the last column. The pool of teachers who can take Higher Level mathematics, physics or chemistry and who are available on a weekday evening within a twenty-minute drive is small in all four districts, and it is substantially the same small group, because the four share Al Wasl Road, Jumeirah Beach Road and Sheikh Zayed Road. A family that moves its search from City Walk to Al Safa in the hope of a longer list of in-home specialists will find the same names, some of whom will now quote a slightly lower travel premium.

There is a related point about timing that families discover late. Because all four districts draw on the same evening hours, the useful slots between 17:00 and 19:00 are contested across the whole corridor rather than within one neighbourhood. A parent booking in September gets 17:00 on a Tuesday; a parent booking in late October finds it gone and is offered 20:00, which for a Year 12 student is a session that will be attended rather than used. Online delivery does not create more hours in the evening, but it does widen the pool competing for them, which is why a late booker has better options than they would otherwise.

sections.heading: What the in-home premium buys on the Al Wasl Road corridor
paragraphs: Begin at the cheapest end of this market, because that is where most families start and where the misunderstanding begins. Budget online tutoring is advertised from AED 33 to 52 an hour by Tutopiya and from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik, generally delivered by university students. That provision has a use: supervised homework, basic content and company while a student works. It is not what moves a Higher Level Diploma grade, and a family that buys it expecting mark-scheme diagnosis will conclude that tutoring does not work.

A step up, qualified subject tutors working online occupy AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE work from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270, and the premium examiner-adjacent tier reaches AED 500 to 650, where BartyED publishes AED 650. In-home one-to-one, the thing this search phrase describes, is quoted at AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and at AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Set those bands side by side and the in-home premium is visible as what it is. A tutor crossing from Al Barsha or Mirdif to City Walk for a one-hour lesson is committing between forty and ninety minutes of driving, and no professional prices their day without accounting for it. The money buys the journey. What it does not buy is a wider choice of teacher, better materials or a different syllabus; and in one respect it buys less, because the shortlist is now limited to people for whom that journey is worth making. The table sets out the four options a City Walk family is really choosing between, including what each one includes.

sections.heading: Why the shortlist narrows as the radius shrinks
paragraphs: This is the mechanism behind everything above, and it is worth setting out because it is checkable rather than rhetorical. Dubai's private sector had 387,441 pupils in 227 schools in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for about 7% of enrolment against 37% British curriculum. A Diploma Higher Level subject is therefore a minority product inside a minority curriculum. The number of people in the emirate who have taught Higher Level physics in the last two years is small; the number who are free at 17:30 on a Tuesday is smaller; and the number of those who will drive to City Walk is smaller again.

Each constraint multiplies rather than adds. A requirement for a specific subject at a specific level cuts the pool hard. A requirement for a specific weekday hour cuts what remains. A requirement for physical presence in a particular district cuts it again, and that third cut is the only one a family can remove without compromising on anything academic. Removing it is what online delivery does. The other two constraints stay, which is why this page also publishes what happens when even the online pool cannot cover a request, rather than implying that supply is infinite.

The practical test for any provider is to ask the question in reverse. Instead of asking whether they cover City Walk, ask how many tutors on their books have taught Higher Level chemistry in the last two academic years and are free between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf Standard Time. A provider drawing on the whole country can answer that; a provider drawing on a twenty-minute radius will change the subject. The answer tells a parent considerably more than a list of neighbourhoods on a landing page, and it works equally well on us.
bullets: IB programmes are about 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment; British curriculum is 37%

sections.heading: Subject coverage from this corridor, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: No competitor page found in this cluster publishes a coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas telephone number. The honest position is that availability varies sharply by subject and level, and a family is better served by knowing that before they pay than by discovering it in February. The table below sets out, by subject and level, how quickly a match is realistic, how thin in-home coverage is in this corridor, and what the fallback is when the first choice is not available.

Two patterns are worth stating in words. Higher Level sciences and Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches are the tight spots everywhere in the UAE, not just here, and a request for one of them in a narrow weekday window may take a week or more to fill properly. Language acquisition at ab initio level and the less common languages are similarly thin. Standard Level sciences, both mathematics courses at Standard Level, English A and economics are comfortable, and a match in two or three days is normal.

When the first choice is not available, there are three honest options and we name which one applies rather than quietly substituting. A different hour with the right specialist is usually the best outcome and the one families resist most. A different tutor whose specialism is adjacent, for instance a Standard Level physics specialist taking a Standard Level student while a Higher Level slot is waited for, is workable with the limitation stated. A short wait is sometimes simply correct. What we will not do is place a generalist in a Higher Level slot and let the family find out at the mock, which is the outcome that does the most damage and the one a proximity-driven search produces most often.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Only one competitor page in the researched set touches licensing at all, and it does so in a single subheading. This is the single most useful thing a parent in City Walk can check, it takes one question, and it applies to every provider including this one. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation introduced the private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service is named 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time listed.

Eligibility is broader than most parents assume. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students may all apply. There are conditions attached: the permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school. That particular rule is press-reported and worth verifying against the current ADEK policy document, but the principle is sound everywhere in the UAE and we do not arrange a teacher to tutor their own pupils privately.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published; a figure circulating online could not be verified, so none is quoted here. Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram does not hold one, does not operate premises in the UAE, and is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB organisation, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, Extended Essay or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is where the Dubai home-tutor market is least safe, and the risk does not change with the delivery format. Internal assessments carry fixed weightings across Diploma subjects, usually around a fifth of the grade in the sciences, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge carry points of their own. That concentration of marks in independently produced work has attracted providers who sell the work rather than the teaching. One in this cluster has been documented offering completed internal assessments at AED 3,750.

The boundary is not ambiguous and we state it rather than leaving it to be inferred. A tutor may teach what each assessment criterion rewards and what the descriptors mean. A tutor may question whether a research question is answerable with the data or sources it would generate, press on whether a conclusion follows from the evidence, point out that an evaluation has identified nothing systematic, and explain word and page limits and referencing conventions. A tutor may not write, edit, restructure or supply any part of the document, may not choose the research question, and may not produce the analysis or the argument.

Parents sometimes ask whether a tutor can supervise the Extended Essay instead of the school. They cannot, and the question is worth answering directly. Supervision is a school role: the supervisor is allocated by the school, holds the formal meetings, signs the declaration and is part of the authentication process. An external tutor sits outside that and can only coach. The useful division of labour is that the school supervises and authenticates while a tutor teaches the subject content and the assessment criteria, and both of those are legitimate at once. Where a provider offers to be the supervisor, something is being misdescribed.
bullets: Internal assessments carry roughly a fifth of the grade in most Diploma sciences
A tutor teaches criteria and questions reasoning; the student writes every word

sections.heading: Starting from City Walk, with the limits stated
paragraphs: The practical sequence is short. Tell us the school, the year group, the subject and level, and the two evening windows that are genuinely free once the return journey from Al Safa, Jumeirah or Umm Suqeim is accounted for. We shortlist tutors who have taught that subject at that level and who can take one of those windows, and the first fifty-five-minute lesson carries no charge with no card details taken. After it you get a short written note saying what kind of problem this is and what it will take to shift, including the possibility that it does not need paid tutoring at all.

The limits, in one place. Lessons are delivered online over live video, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the emirate. Higher Level sciences and Higher Level Analysis and Approaches may take up to a week to fill in a narrow weekday window, and when that is the case we will say so and name the alternative. No tutor can guarantee a grade, a point total or a university place, because the boards mark the papers and set the boundaries afterwards.

One more thing, which is the reason a comparison page is more useful than a sales page. If after the free lesson the tutor's view is that your child needs a timer, a mark scheme and six weeks of discipline rather than a weekly session, the note will say that and nobody will follow up with a package. The published rates above exist so that a City Walk family can decide between options on the numbers, and the coverage table exists so that the decision is made with the constraints visible. Both of those make a sale less likely in some cases, which is the point of publishing them.
bullets: Send school, year, subject, level and two genuinely free evening windows
First 55-minute lesson at no charge, no card details taken
