process.title: Name the subject and the level, not just the programme
process.description: 'IB help' is not a brief that can be matched. Higher Level chemistry, Standard Level Analysis and Approaches or Theory of Knowledge are. Add the school and the year group, because the school's own topic sequence determines what the first sessions should cover and Dubai campuses differ widely in the order they teach.

process.title: Give us two real evening windows
process.description: Not a preference, two windows that survive the return journey from Al Safa, Jumeirah or Umm Suqeim and whatever sport or music already occupies the week. Slots between 17:00 and 19:00 in this corridor are contested across four districts, so naming the real windows early is the difference between a good slot and a late one.

process.title: A free diagnostic lesson of 55 minutes
process.description: No charge, no card details. The tutor works through recent class material and one unfamiliar past-paper question, watching the working rather than the answers, and writes a short note classifying the problem. The note sometimes says that paid sessions are not the right purchase, and that is a legitimate outcome.

process.title: A written rate and a coverage position
process.description: You get the rate per session before anything is booked, and a straight answer on availability: matched now, matched within a week, or not coverable in that window with the alternatives named. Nothing is bundled, and no discount is conditional on committing to a term in advance.

process.title: Weekly sessions, written notes, and a review at the mock
process.description: Each session ends with two named priorities and specific past-paper questions. January and March mocks are the honest checkpoint: the marked paper is categorised by loss type and the plan continues, changes or stops. A plan that winds down because it worked is the intended outcome.

whyPoints.title: A comparison rather than a claim
whyPoints.description: This page publishes in-home market rates alongside online ones, names the companies that published them, and sets out what the premium represents. A family can read it and decide that in-home delivery is still what they want, in which case they now know what to pay. Three of the six researched competitors in this cluster publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: The shortlist built from the whole country
whyPoints.description: Subject, level and hour are real constraints. Location does not have to be. Removing it is the only one of the four that costs nothing academically, and it is what lets a City Walk family consider every tutor who has taught Higher Level chemistry rather than the two who will drive to Al Wasl Road.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits published
whyPoints.description: Higher Level sciences, Higher Level Analysis and Approaches and ab initio languages are thin, and the table on this page says so by subject with realistic match times. No competitor in the researched set discloses a coverage limit anywhere, and several route UAE parents to overseas telephone numbers instead.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered properly
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition permit, its two-year validity, its absence of a fee, the official application route and the categories eligible for it are all set out here so a parent can verify any tutor from any provider. We also state what IB Gram is not: not accredited by any regulator or board, and holding no UAE premises.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line drawn in public
whyPoints.description: Criteria taught, research questions interrogated, reasoning challenged, nothing written or edited. Extended Essay supervision is a school role and we say so. The parts of this market selling completed internal assessments are charging a premium for a risk the student carries alone.

whyPoints.title: Sessions that move without rearranging a journey
whyPoints.description: A school trip, a swimming gala or a family trip moves the lesson rather than cancelling it, because nobody has to be redirected across the city. Over a thirty-week year that difference is several sessions, which is a more significant saving than most hourly-rate negotiations produce.

faqs.question: Is there an IB home tutor in City Walk who will teach in the apartment itself?
faqs.answer: There are tutors in this market who make in-home visits, and published Dubai rates for them run AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 table with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. IB Gram is not one of them: we do not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. What we deliver to a City Walk address is one-to-one teaching over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the shortlist drawn from everyone who has taught the subject at the level needed rather than from those willing to drive to Al Wasl Road on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Does widening the search from City Walk to Jumeirah 2 or La Mer add any tutors?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is structural. Those districts sit on the same road network and share the same school cluster in Al Safa, Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, so they draw on the same group of teachers. What widening the search changes is the travel premium quoted, because a tutor coming from Al Barsha will price a journey to Al Safa slightly lower than one to La Mer. The pool of people who have taught Higher Level physics or chemistry within reach does not grow. That pool only grows when the requirement to be physically present is dropped.

faqs.question: What does the in-home premium on the Al Wasl Road corridor actually pay for?
faqs.answer: A journey. Published Dubai in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour sit above the AED 150 to 300 band for qualified subject tutors working online, and the difference is forty to ninety minutes of driving that no professional prices out of their day. It does not buy better materials, a different syllabus or a more qualified teacher. In one respect it buys less, because the shortlist narrows to those for whom the journey is worth making, and that criterion has nothing to do with how well somebody teaches the Diploma.

faqs.question: Over a Diploma year, which works out cheaper: an in-home tutor or an online specialist?
faqs.answer: Online, on the published figures. Bestimate's Dubai monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work, while advertised in-home monthly packages in this market run AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. There is also a hidden saving: an online session reschedules when a school trip or a family trip intervenes, whereas an in-home slot usually cancels. Across thirty weeks that is several sessions kept, which is worth more than most rate negotiations achieve.

faqs.question: How large is the pool of Higher Level Diploma tutors within a twenty-minute drive of City Walk?
faqs.answer: Small, and smaller than families expect. Dubai had 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate programmes at roughly 7% of enrolment against 37% British curriculum. A Higher Level subject is therefore a minority product inside a minority curriculum. Filter for people free at a specific weekday hour and willing to drive to this corridor, and Higher Level physics or chemistry comes down to a handful. The practical test for any provider is to ask how many of their tutors have taught your subject at your level in the last two academic years.

faqs.question: Does a City Walk address limit which IB subjects we can get support in?
faqs.answer: Not for online delivery, but availability still varies by subject and level and we publish where it is thin. Higher Level sciences and Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches can take up to a week to fill in a narrow weekday window. Ab initio languages and the less commonly taught languages are similarly tight. Standard Level sciences, both mathematics courses at Standard Level, English A, economics and history are comfortable, with a match usually possible in two or three days. The constraint is the specialist's calendar rather than your postcode.

faqs.question: What happens if the subject we need has no UAE-based specialist free?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and name which of three options applies. A different hour with the right specialist is usually the best outcome and the one families resist most. A tutor whose specialism is adjacent, with the limitation stated openly, is workable for some situations. A short wait is sometimes simply the correct answer. What we will not do is place a generalist into a Higher Level slot and let the family discover it at the January mock. No competitor page in the researched set publishes a coverage limit at all, which is why this one is written down and can be held against us.

faqs.question: How do we check that a private tutor in Dubai holds a valid permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see it, and ask who issued it. Private tuition in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service is called 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' and runs through the ministry's app, website and e-services system. Teachers, public and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 are all eligible. Tutoring without one exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published.

faqs.question: Can one tutor work with two children in the same City Walk household?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a caveat worth stating. Two children in different year groups should have separate sessions, because the content, the pace and the assessment are different and a shared hour becomes supervision rather than teaching. Two children in the same subject and year can share, and some families prefer it, but the individual mark-scheme diagnosis that moves a grade is diluted immediately: one child's habitual error is not the other's. Where a family wants both, the usual arrangement is two separate shorter sessions with the same tutor on the same evening, which online delivery makes trivial to schedule.

faqs.question: What may a tutor legitimately do with an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the criteria, explain what the descriptors mean, question whether a research question can be answered with the data or sources it would generate, challenge whether a conclusion follows from the evidence, point out that an evaluation has identified nothing systematic, and explain word limits and referencing. What a tutor may not do is write, edit, restructure or supply any part of the document, choose the research question, or produce the analysis. Internal assessments carry roughly a fifth of the grade in most Diploma sciences, which is exactly why parts of this market sell the work rather than the teaching. The student carries that risk, not the seller.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supervise the Extended Essay instead of the school?
faqs.answer: No. Supervision is a school role: the supervisor is allocated by the school, holds the formal reflection meetings, signs the declaration and forms part of the authentication process. An external tutor sits entirely outside that and can only coach. The workable division is that the school supervises and authenticates while a tutor teaches the subject content and the assessment criteria, which are both legitimate at the same time. If any provider offers to act as the supervisor, something is being misdescribed and it is worth asking the school's Diploma coordinator before going further.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a tuition centre near Jumeirah a reasonable substitute?
faqs.answer: For some needs, yes. A group can deliver content a student has genuinely not been taught, which happens after a staff absence or a mid-year move, and the cost per hour is lower. What it cannot deliver is the thing that shifts a Diploma grade in the final year, which is somebody reading one student's own written answers each week and naming the specific habit costing them marks. Those habits are individual. Ask how many students will be in the room before comparing rates, and use groups for content gaps rather than for examination technique.

faqs.question: How long does it take to start if we decide in the middle of term?
faqs.answer: For Standard Level subjects, English A, economics or history, two or three days is normal. For Higher Level sciences or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in a narrow weekday window, allow up to a week, and expect the first offer to be an hour you had not planned on. Mid-term starts in this corridor are harder than September ones for a specific reason: the 17:00 to 19:00 slots are contested across City Walk, Al Wasl, Jumeirah and Al Safa simultaneously. Being flexible about the hour by thirty minutes typically converts a week's wait into two days.

faqs.question: Do lessons pause during Dubai school holidays and family travel?
faqs.answer: They pause if you want them to and often should not. Dubai's winter and spring breaks are long enough for structural work, and a student with no school day behind them can concentrate for ninety minutes rather than fifty-five, which makes holiday blocks the most productive sessions of the year. Family travel is handled by moving the slot rather than cancelling it, since a time-zone change is a scheduling question rather than a logistical one. The one break worth taking in full is the fortnight immediately after the final papers.

faqs.question: What would make you tell us not to buy tutoring at all?
faqs.answer: Several things, and the diagnostic lesson exists partly to find them. A student already at a 6 who is losing marks to carelessness under time pressure needs a timer and a mark scheme, not a weekly session. A student whose school already runs clinics and past-paper marking for the subject may simply not be using them. A student three weeks from the final papers with a foundational gap cannot be rescued by hours and is better served by triage on two topics. In each of those cases the written note after the free lesson says so, and nobody follows up with a package.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-city-walk.closingHeading: Compare the options on the numbers, then decide
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-city-walk.closingBody: Send the school, the year group, the subject and level, and two evening windows that genuinely survive the return journey from Al Safa, Jumeirah or Umm Suqeim. You will get a written rate per session, a straight answer on whether that subject and hour can be covered now or within a week, and a free 55-minute diagnostic lesson with no card details taken. The rates on this page belong to the companies that published them, and they are here so a City Walk family can weigh in-home against online themselves rather than taking anyone's word for the comparison. If the honest answer after the first lesson is that no paid sessions are needed, the note will say exactly that.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-culture-village.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering the IB Diploma for families in Culture Village: matched to one subject at one level, working to your school's internal deadline calendar, and available in the early evening window a Creek-side commute allows.

intro.heading: Count the Diploma backwards, not forwards
paragraphs: The IB Diploma is twenty-two months long and almost nobody plans it as a whole. Families plan a term, react to a report, buy some hours, and discover the structure retrospectively. The structure is entirely knowable in advance, and the single most useful thing a parent in Culture Village can do is get the school's internal calendar and count backwards from the end. Everything else, including the choice of tutor, follows from that document.

The reason internal dates matter more than external ones is that they govern almost everything a tutor can affect. Every Diploma subject has an internally assessed component with its own school deadline. The Extended Essay has school-set draft deadlines well before submission. Theory of Knowledge has an essay and an exhibition with internal dates. Predicted grades, which university offers rest on, are produced by the school from the school's own evidence partway through Year 13. The external session is the last item on a long list, not the organising principle.

This is also why a plan that peaks in the spring of Year 13 wastes money. By then the internally assessed components are closed and moderated, the core is submitted and the predictions are issued. The only thing left to influence is examination performance, which is a real thing worth supporting, but it is one of several levers rather than all of them. Culture Village families who count backwards tend to spend the same amount and get two outcomes instead of one.

On the home-tutoring question, the honest version. Home tuition exists in Dubai at published rates of AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions appear in the market. IB Gram is not a visiting service: tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visiting exists only in our India operation.

There is a calendar reason that limit helps rather than hurts. Internal deadlines cluster, and they cluster at the same time across Dubai schools, because cohorts move through the programme together. In those weeks a visiting tutor bounded by driving distance is least likely to have a slot, and a replacement is hardest to find. An online match can be made or replaced inside the same week, which matters precisely when the calendar is tightest.

One honesty note before the detail. No IB session or results date appears anywhere on this page. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and an unverified exam date is something a family would plan a term of revision and a budget around. UAE schools sit the main May session. Your school's IB coordinator holds the calendar, and this page tells you which parts of it to ask for.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-culture-village.programmesIntro: Culture Village families come to us at four points in the Diploma calendar, and the useful work differs sharply at each. These are the stages we cover.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Forty-two points come from the subjects at a maximum of seven each, and up to three more from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination, for a maximum of 45.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the main May session. The dates that shape a tutoring plan are internal: the deadline for each subject's internally assessed component, the Extended Essay draft dates, the Theory of Knowledge submission window, the mock examination weeks and the point at which the school assembles predicted-grade evidence. Ask the IB coordinator for all five. None is published by the IB and all of them are set locally.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight and converted to a grade from one to seven. Most years have no external examination, so the reporting cycle rather than an exam calendar is what governs the work.
programmes.countryNote: Culture Village families with children in both programmes face two different calendars in one household. The Middle Years Programme runs on school reporting points with revisable tasks, and the Diploma runs on fixed internal deadlines with no resubmission. Treating them the same is the commonest planning error, because it leads parents to assume a Diploma deadline has the flexibility an MYP task had.

programmes.name: The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is an independent research essay limited to 4,000 words. Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an essay on a prescribed title limited to 1,600 words and an exhibition of three objects with a commentary limited to 950 words. Together they carry up to three of the forty-five points.
programmes.countryNote: The core is where the internal calendar bites hardest, because the school supervises it and sets the draft deadlines. It is also where early work is cheapest and late work is most expensive: an Extended Essay research question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words is visible at the question stage and unfixable once the writing is done. Ask for the draft dates in Year 12, not Year 13.

programmes.name: Creativity, Activity, Service
programmes.description: Not graded, but required for the Diploma to be awarded. Students complete experiences and at least one project, with reflections recorded and reviewed by the school's CAS coordinator at set interview points.
programmes.countryNote: Included here because it is a calendar item that can delay a Diploma and is routinely treated as optional until it is urgent. Tutoring does not touch it, and we will not pretend otherwise. What a plan should do is keep the CAS interview dates visible, so that a term already carrying an internal assessment deadline does not also acquire a CAS catch-up that nobody scheduled.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-culture-village.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Culture Village families ask for, each with the internally assessed component whose school deadline drives the work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, calculus and proof, with induction and complex numbers at Higher Level and Paper 1 sat without technology. The Exploration carries twenty per cent and has a school draft deadline usually in the first term of Year 13.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, regression, hypothesis testing and interpretation with a calculator permitted throughout. Same Exploration weighting and same five criteria, so the internal deadline matters just as much on this route.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, waves, electricity, magnetism and nuclear physics. The internally assessed investigation needs uncertainty analysis, which is where marks are lost, and it usually has the earliest internal deadline of the sciences.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium, redox and organic chemistry. The investigation is marked on exploration, analysis, evaluation and communication, with evaluation carrying the weight schools teach least.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cell and molecular biology, genetics, ecology, evolution and human physiology. Data-based questions on unfamiliar material are the discriminator, and the investigation deadline tends to sit alongside the Extended Essay draft.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with an internally assessed portfolio of commentaries on published news articles. The portfolio has staged internal deadlines across both years rather than one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisation, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with a Higher Level research project. Marks come from application to a real organisation, and the project needs scope control before any writing.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis, comparative essay, individual oral and a Higher Level essay. The individual oral is internally assessed with a school-scheduled date, which is frequently the earliest internal assessment of the whole Diploma.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title limited to 1,600 words and an exhibition of three objects with a commentary limited to 950 words. Both carry school-set internal deadlines and together with the Extended Essay are worth three points.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay in a chosen subject, supervised in school, with staged internal deadlines for question approval, first draft and final submission. Question scope decides the outcome before any writing begins.

sections.heading: The twenty-two months, counted backwards
paragraphs: Here is the Diploma written as a countdown rather than a syllabus. The useful direction of travel is from the end, because that is how deadlines actually constrain a student: each one has a latest moment at which work on it can still begin, and those moments stack. A plan built forwards from September keeps discovering that the next thing was due sooner than expected. A plan built backwards from the final paper knows in advance which terms are full.

The structure is stable across schools even though the dates differ. Internally assessed components sit in Year 13, with first drafts usually in the first term. The Extended Essay has staged internal deadlines beginning with question approval late in Year 12. Theory of Knowledge runs across both years with the exhibition and essay in Year 13. Mock examinations fall in Year 13, often immediately after the heaviest internal deadline period, which is why that term is the one that breaks students.

The item most often misplaced is the summer between Year 12 and Year 13. It is the only genuinely clear block in the whole programme: no commute, no competing deadlines, and enough length for sustained work. Families treat it as a holiday and then spend the autumn in overlap. Using even part of it for preliminary Extended Essay reading or Exploration mathematics removes the worst collision in the calendar, and it costs less than the emergency work it replaces.

The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and publishing an unverified date on a page a family plans around would be worse than publishing none. sections.heading: Internal deadlines beat external dates
paragraphs: The IB publishes session windows. The school sets everything else, and everything else is what a tutor can influence. That asymmetry is the single most useful thing to understand about planning Diploma support, and it explains why two families with identical children and identical budgets get different outcomes: one asked for the internal calendar and one planned around the exam.

Five internal dates matter and all five are free to obtain. The deadline for each subject's internally assessed component. The staged Extended Essay dates, beginning with question approval. The Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition submission dates. The mock examination weeks. And the point at which the school assembles predicted-grade evidence. A Culture Village parent who emails the IB coordinator for those five has done more for the outcome than a month of tuition typically achieves.

The predicted-grade point deserves separate emphasis because it reframes everything. Predictions come from the school, from the school's own evidence, and university offers rest on them. The external examination happens afterwards. That makes internal assessments evidence rather than practice, and it means money spent before the predictions buys two outcomes while money spent after buys one. A student treating a mock as a rehearsal has misread what the school is doing with it.

There is an operational reason this matters for a visiting arrangement in particular. Internal deadlines cluster at the same time across Dubai schools, because cohorts move through the programme together, and that is exactly when a tutor bounded by driving distance is least likely to have availability and hardest to replace. An online match can be made or changed inside the same week. The calendar argument and the delivery argument are the same argument.

sections.heading: The core, milestone by milestone
paragraphs: Three of the forty-five points sit on two written components, and both fail in ways that are visible months before the deadline. The Extended Essay is limited to 4,000 words and fails most often on question scope: a question that cannot be answered in that space produces a final fortnight spent cutting argument, and the criteria reward focus and method heavily. The Theory of Knowledge essay is limited to 1,600 words and fails most often by answering an adjacent question rather than the prescribed title as written.

Both failures are cheap to prevent and expensive to repair, which makes the core the clearest argument for a calendar-led plan. Two or three conversations at the question stage in Year 12 protect the Extended Essay. One session taking a prescribed title apart clause by clause protects the Theory of Knowledge essay. Twenty hours of editing in Year 13 protects neither, because by then the structural decision has been made and the criteria are judging that decision.

The Theory of Knowledge exhibition is a separate milestone and often the most rushed. Three objects with a commentary limited to 950 words means roughly three hundred words per object, so object choice does most of the work. A student who picks three objects that genuinely illustrate different aspects of a prompt writes a tight commentary. A student who picks three convenient objects writes three descriptions and scores accordingly.

The boundary on all core support needs stating before any of it begins. A tutor may question a research question, explain what a criterion rewards, and comment on the student's own draft. A tutor may not produce the essay, restructure it to a standard, or supply the argument. The school supervisor remains the supervisor. Providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price, which is a malpractice trigger whose consequence falls on the candidate.

sections.heading: What each missed window actually costs
paragraphs: Every window in the calendar has a price for missing it, and the prices are uneven. Understanding which ones are expensive changes how a Culture Village family allocates both attention and money, because the instinct is to worry most about the final term, which is in fact the window with the least left to lose.

The most expensive miss is the Extended Essay question. A badly scoped question cannot be repaired without starting again, and starting again in Year 13 is not practically available. The second most expensive is the internally assessed component started too late to be evaluated properly, because the criteria in every science reward evaluation substantially and a thin evaluation section caps the mark regardless of how good the experiment was. Both are matters of weeks, not hours, and both are visible in advance.

The cheapest miss is a single week of content teaching, which is also the thing families panic about most. Content can be caught up; a student who missed a fortnight of organic chemistry has a definable gap that a specialist closes in a few sessions. A student who missed the window for scoping an Extended Essay question has a structural problem that no number of sessions fixes. The asymmetry runs in exactly the opposite direction to most families' anxiety.

The middle case is the predicted-grade window, and it is the one where good information changes behaviour most. Because predictions are drawn from internal evidence partway through Year 13, work done before that point affects both the offer and the grade. Work done after affects the grade alone. Same hours, same rate, one outcome instead of two. Asking the school when predictions are assembled costs an email.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in Culture Village, and the calendar reason we do not offer it
paragraphs: Home tuition is a genuine option in this market and the prices are published. In-home one-to-one rates run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions circulate. Against that, a qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, and specialists from AED 200 to AED 450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Culture Village or anywhere else in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, and home visiting is a service we operate only in India. The usual argument for that is price and pool size, both of which are real. The calendar argument is less often made and matters more for the Diploma specifically.

Diploma internal deadlines cluster, and they cluster simultaneously across Dubai schools because cohorts progress together. In those weeks demand for subject specialists peaks in the same fortnight, and a tutor bounded by driving distance from Jaddaf Waterfront is both least likely to have a free slot and hardest to replace if the match is not working. Replacement inside the same week is possible only when the pool is national, and the week it matters is the week everything else is also happening.

There are cases where a visiting tutor is the right purchase, and they are worth naming honestly: a younger or easily distracted student who needs an adult present, primary work with physical materials, or a household with unreliable connectivity. A Year 13 Diploma candidate working on an internally assessed component three weeks before a school deadline is not one of them, and for that student the premium buys logistics rather than learning.

sections.heading: Culture Village's schools and the evening the calendar leaves
paragraphs: Culture Village is Jaddaf Waterfront: Dubai Wharf and the Creek-side towers, compact, with no private school inside the community. Every secondary pupil travels out, and the destinations are close by Dubai standards. Swiss International Scientific School Dubai sits in neighbouring Al Jaddaf running IB programmes. Across the Creek, Dubai Festival City holds further international provision. South along Al Khail Road sit Sobha Hartland, Mohammed Bin Rashid City, Meydan and Nad Al Sheba.

Because the nearest destinations are short runs, Culture Village is better placed than most Dubai districts for an early session. A student at a school in Al Jaddaf or across in Festival City is often home in time for a 16:30 start, which is the difference between a session that works and one that runs on fumes. A student travelling to Sobha Hartland is realistically 17:00, and to Nad Al Sheba 17:15 or later, at which point a weekend block is the better instrument for deadline work.

The Dubai context is worth one paragraph. KHDA reported 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with the International Baccalaureate at seven per cent of enrolment against thirty-seven per cent on UK curricula. Seven new private schools join for the 2026-27 intake, three of them IB, creating 16,846 new places, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that fees would not rise for that academic year.

The practical consequence of an expanding but still small IB share is that specialist supply lags locally while demand clusters in the same deadline weeks. For a Culture Village family that is the whole case for a national pool reached by live video: not that it is cheaper, though it is, but that it is available in the fortnight when everything is due at once.

sections.heading: The academic honesty line, and what happens to a draft
paragraphs: Because this page is built around deadlines, the honesty line needs setting out plainly: pressure near a deadline is exactly when it gets tested. Work submitted for IB assessment must be the student's own. A tutor who produces, completes, substantially rewrites or supplies any part of an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or internally assessed component creates a malpractice exposure for the candidate, and a finding can cost a Diploma.

The legitimate version is also the more useful version. A tutor can mark a student's own draft against the published criteria, which is the single most valuable thing available three weeks before a deadline. A tutor can explain what a criterion is asking for when the wording is opaque, which it frequently is. A tutor can model an evaluation or a reflection on an unrelated investigation and hand the student's own work back untouched. A tutor can teach referencing properly, which prevents more honesty cases than warnings do.

Providers in this market advertise completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. The advertising omits that the consequence falls on the sixteen or seventeen-year-old rather than on the seller. No deadline is worth that, and a family under time pressure deserves to be told so by the person they are paying rather than discovering it afterwards.

On materials, IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are copyright works. We reference and link them from the organisation's own site rather than reproducing or supplying them. We keep a short session note recording what was covered and whose work was in front of us, which is the document a parent can hand to a school if a question is ever raised.

sections.heading: Getting started, with the calendar in hand
paragraphs: Begin with the email that costs nothing. Ask your school's IB coordinator for five dates: the internal deadline for each subject's assessed component, the staged Extended Essay dates, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition dates, the mock examination weeks, and the point at which predicted-grade evidence is assembled. Those five turn a vague worry into a plan, and they are the difference between buying hours and buying outcomes.

Then send us the subject and level, which component is in progress, the internal deadline for it, and two evening windows that genuinely work from Culture Village after the school run. We match a subject specialist and run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep. One trial per student, nothing charged beforehand, no card details needed to book it, and the tutor writes a short note on what they found and which deadline they would work to first.

If no specialist is free in your window we say so, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing whoever is available. Scarcity concentrates in Higher Level sciences and mathematics, and in the deadline weeks themselves. Booking a slot before the cluster arrives costs exactly the same and secures a materially better match, which in a calendar-driven plan is the single largest free improvement available.

Two limits stated plainly. Nobody can promise a grade or a point total and this page does not. And nothing here implies that tutoring is required for the Diploma to be awarded, for university admission or for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency; those are institutional and regulatory processes with their own published rules, and the authority rather than any tutoring provider is where to verify them. IB Gram holds no approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

faqs.question: Which IB dates actually matter for planning tutoring in Culture Village?
faqs.answer: The internal ones, almost entirely. The IB publishes session windows; your school sets the deadline for each subject's internally assessed component, the staged Extended Essay dates, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition dates, the mock examination weeks, and the point at which predicted-grade evidence is assembled. Those five govern everything a tutor can influence and all five are free to obtain from the IB coordinator. A plan built from the external session date is built from the one item a tutor affects least.

faqs.question: Why does the Diploma need planning twenty-two months ahead?
faqs.answer: Because the expensive failures are structural and visible in advance. An Extended Essay question too broad to answer in 4,000 words cannot be repaired in Year 13, only restarted, which is not practically available. An internally assessed component started too late is capped by a thin evaluation section whatever the quality of the work. Both are matters of weeks rather than hours, and both are knowable a year out. Content gaps, which families worry about most, are the cheapest item on the list to fix.

faqs.question: When are IB predicted grades decided, and why does it change spending?
faqs.answer: They are produced by the school, from the school's own evidence, partway through Year 13, and university offers rest on them. The external examination comes afterwards. That makes internal assessments evidence rather than rehearsal, and it means an hour bought before the predictions affects both the offer and the final grade while the same hour bought afterwards affects only the grade. Same rate, one outcome instead of two. Ask the school when predictions are assembled; it costs an email.

faqs.question: What should my child be doing in the summer between Year 12 and Year 13?
faqs.answer: Preliminary reading for the Extended Essay and preliminary mathematics for an Exploration, if either applies. That summer is the only genuinely clear block in the whole programme: no commute, no competing deadlines, and enough length for sustained thinking. Families treat it as a holiday and then spend the autumn with the Extended Essay draft, the first internal assessments and new content all overlapping. Using even part of it removes the worst collision in the calendar and costs less than the emergency work it replaces.

faqs.question: How early should the Extended Essay research question be settled?
faqs.answer: Subject by the middle of Year 12 and question tested for scope by the end of it. The limit is 4,000 words and the dominant failure is a question that cannot be answered in that space, which produces a final fortnight spent cutting argument when the criteria reward focus and method heavily. Two or three conversations at the question stage protect the component. Twenty hours of editing later does not, because the structural decision has already been made and the criteria are judging it.

faqs.question: What makes the Theory of Knowledge exhibition go wrong?
faqs.answer: Object choice, almost always. The commentary is limited to 950 words across three objects, so each object gets roughly three hundred words, and a student who picks three convenient objects writes three descriptions. A student who picks three that genuinely illustrate different aspects of the prompt writes a tight argument instead. One session spent testing candidate objects against the prompt before anything is written does most of the work, and it belongs well before the school's submission date.

faqs.question: Can we get a tutor who comes to our apartment in Culture Village?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one tuition for UAE families online over live video on Gulf Standard Time and send no tutors to UAE addresses; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. Dubai agencies that do visit publish rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers. Beyond price, the calendar reason matters: internal deadlines cluster across Dubai schools, which is exactly when a locally bounded tutor has no free slot.

faqs.question: Which internal deadline week is the hardest one in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The term in Year 13 that carries internal assessment drafts, the Extended Essay deadline and mock examinations, usually in that order and often within a few weeks of each other. It is also the term during which predicted-grade evidence is being assembled, which raises the stakes on everything in it. It is entirely predictable from the school's calendar a year in advance, and relieving it means moving work earlier rather than buying more hours once it has arrived.

faqs.question: Is the final term before the exams worth heavy tutoring spend?
faqs.answer: Worth some, and less than instinct suggests. By then the internally assessed components are submitted and moderated, the core is in, and the predictions are issued, so the only remaining lever is examination performance. That is real and worth supporting with timed papers and command-term work. But it is one lever rather than all of them, and the same money spent two terms earlier would have moved both the grade and the offer. Book the final-term slot early; the price is identical and the match is better.

faqs.question: Why does this page avoid giving the May session dates?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified from the IB itself, whose website blocks automated checking. No IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and an unverified date on a page a family plans a term of revision and a budget around is worse than no date at all. UAE schools sit the main May session. Your school's IB coordinator holds the authoritative calendar, along with the internal deadlines that matter more to a plan than the external ones.

faqs.question: How does a tutor help three weeks before an internal assessment deadline?
faqs.answer: By marking the student's own draft against the published criteria, which is the most valuable thing available at that point, and by explaining what a criterion is asking for when the wording is opaque. A tutor can also model an evaluation or a reflection on an unrelated investigation. What a tutor cannot do is produce the work, restructure it to a standard or supply the argument, and deadline pressure is exactly when that line gets tested. We keep a note of whose work was in front of us.

faqs.question: Does CAS really affect the calendar, given it is not graded?
faqs.answer: It can delay a Diploma, which makes it a calendar item even though tutoring does not touch it. Creativity, Activity, Service is a completion requirement with school-scheduled interviews and at least one project, and it is routinely treated as optional until it becomes urgent. The planning point is to keep the interview dates visible, so a term already carrying an internal assessment deadline and an Extended Essay draft does not also acquire a CAS catch-up that nobody scheduled.

faqs.question: Which schools do Culture Village Diploma students attend?
faqs.answer: No private school sits inside Culture Village itself. Swiss International Scientific School Dubai is in neighbouring Al Jaddaf and runs IB programmes, which makes it the closest provision. Across the Creek, Universal American School Dubai and Deira International School sit in Dubai Festival City. South along Al Khail Road, North London Collegiate School Dubai and Hartland International School serve Sobha Hartland, with GEMS Modern Academy in Nad Al Sheba. Schools are named as market context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: What time can a Culture Village student realistically start a session?
faqs.answer: Often 16:30 if the school is in Al Jaddaf or across the Creek in Dubai Festival City, because those are short runs from Jaddaf Waterfront. A student travelling to Sobha Hartland is realistically 17:00 and one commuting to Nad Al Sheba 17:15 or later. Choose the slot for the worst normal weekday rather than the best. Where the commute is long and an internal deadline is close, a weekend block does more than two extra weekday evenings would.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold IB or KHDA authorisation?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. KHDA is Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; it regulates and inspects schools, and an inspection rating judges a school rather than any tutor. A KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises and staff, and we have no UAE premises.

intro.heading: A term has more deadlines than it looks
paragraphs: The Diploma is described to parents as two years ending in written papers, and that description causes most of the trouble. A Diploma year actually contains a sequence of school-set deadlines — internal coursework submissions, the mock window, option forms, supervision meetings — and every one of them arrives before the examinations do. Families in DAMAC Hills discover them one at a time, usually about a fortnight before each.

That matters more here than in communities with schools inside them. A student living in DAMAC Hills generally travels out to school, along Umm Suqeim Street extension or Sheikh Zayed bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street, and gets home after five. The usable working evening is short. Deadlines that collide inside it cost more than they would in a household where the student is home by half past three.

So the planning question is not how many hours of tutoring to buy. It is which fortnight to buy them in. The same eight sessions placed before a mock window produce a different result from the same eight placed after it, and the same coursework support placed a term before a submission produces a different result from the same support placed a fortnight before. Those are the decisions this page is organised around.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In this community that is less of a compromise than it sounds: a visiting tutor would be adding a journey to a day that already contains two, and a session that depends on the Hessa Street interchange at six in the evening does not start when it is supposed to.

What the online format changes practically is reliability and reach. A 5.30pm slot stays a 5.30pm slot. A session can move within the same week without a journey being rearranged on either side. And a student needing a specialist in a particular Higher Level subject is matched from everyone who teaches it rather than from those willing to drive to Dubailand on a Tuesday.

A note on dates before the detail. Dubai Diploma students sit the May session. This page publishes no IB session or results dates, because none could be verified from the IB directly, and a date a family plans around has to be right. The dates that actually bind are the school's own, and the Diploma coordinator holds them.

What follows is a term planned properly: the three deadlines that are not the exam, the commute arithmetic that decides when a session can run, a fortnight-by-fortnight plan, what the market charges for home tutoring against online, and where Diploma marks go when a term runs out of time.

IB Gram supplies exactly that, delivered live online over video in Gulf Standard Time rather than by somebody arriving at the villa. In-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and no UAE page on this site says otherwise.

The phrase persists because it describes a category rather than a method. Private tuition in Dubai meant a visitor with a folder for a long time, and the market for that still exists in Dubailand with a published rate attached. What has changed is the constraint it was built around. A tutor no longer has to live within reach of DAMAC Hills to teach a DAMAC Hills student, but driving there still takes the same amount of time it always did.

In this community the time argument is unusually strong. The student has already made two journeys that day. The tutor would be making two more, through the Hessa Street interchange or along Umm Suqeim Street extension at the worst hour. Removing all four leaves the student with a session that starts on time and an evening that still contains homework, which is the whole of what a parent is trying to protect.

What a family should expect is unglamorous and specific: a fixed slot at a realistic hour, a named specialist for one course at one level, a syllabus checklist that shortens, homework set from past papers and marked against the published scheme, and a written note after each session. Where no specialist is free for a course and level, the answer is a stated wait or a referral rather than a substitution.

sections.heading: The three deadlines that are not the exam
paragraphs: Ask a Diploma parent in DAMAC Hills when the important date is and they will name the examination session. Ask a Diploma coordinator and they will name three earlier ones. Those three are where the work actually gets decided, and they are all set by the school rather than by the board, which is why they are invisible to anyone searching online for a general Dubai calendar.

The first is the internal coursework deadline. Every Diploma subject has an internally assessed component with a school submission date, and those dates are usually clustered in the second year before the mock window. A student with six subjects can face four submissions inside a month, and the fortnight where that collides with mock revision is the one that produces the panicked February enquiry.

The second is the mock window itself. Mocks are a measurement, and most families treat them as an unavoidable weather event rather than as something to prepare for. Preparing for the measurement changes the measurement, and because predicted grades are informed by mock performance, the number matters beyond its diagnostic value.

The third is the option form, which belongs to the pre-Diploma year and closes earliest of all. Subject and level choices made on that form determine two years of work and, through prerequisites, what a student can apply for. The table below sets the three out with what should be true before each closes.

The practical step is to get all of them onto one page in September. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal deadline schedule, the mock window and the Extended Essay supervision dates, write them in one place, and look at where they cluster. The clusters are the fortnights to buy support in, and they are visible nine months early to anyone who asks.

sections.heading: The commute arithmetic, and when a session can actually run
paragraphs: Scheduling looks like a trivial problem until a term has lost four sessions to it. In DAMAC Hills the arithmetic is specific. A secondary student travelling to Al Barsha, Jumeirah or the Ranches leaves early and returns after five. Add the traffic on the Sheikh Zayed bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street and Hessa Street corridors in the late afternoon and the first genuinely workable slot is 5.30pm, with 6pm more reliable in the second half of term.

That has consequences for session design, not just timing. A student starting at six has less in reserve than one starting at four, so ninety minutes of new content is a worse use of the hour than sixty minutes of timed practice and review. Blocks for this community are usually built as two shorter sessions a week rather than one long one, with the heavier written work set for the weekend.

It also argues for weekend mornings, particularly for students at schools in Motor City or Sports City whose fixtures and training fill weekday evenings. A Saturday or Sunday morning session holds through a sporting season in a way that a Tuesday at six does not, and for coursework process work — discussion rather than drill — the longer weekend slot is genuinely better.

None of it would matter if a tutor were driving to the villa, because then the constraint would be the tutor's route rather than the student's energy. Online delivery is what makes the pattern choosable, which in a community with this commute is most of its value.

sections.heading: A term, planned fortnight by fortnight
paragraphs: A term is about six fortnights, and planning at that resolution is more useful than planning by week or by month. Weeks are too short to show progress and months are too long to correct. The pattern below is for a second-year Diploma student with a coursework deadline and a mock window in the same term, which is the standard DAMAC Hills situation.

The first fortnight is diagnostic and sets the target. The second and third are the coursework block, finishing the drafting before mock revision begins rather than alongside it. The fourth is timed-paper work, the fifth is mock revision proper, and the sixth is the mocks themselves plus the review afterwards. That sequence works because it never asks a student to do two kinds of work in the same fortnight.

The common alternative — coursework and revision running together for six weeks — fails for a predictable reason. Coursework is slow, open-ended work that expands to fill available time, and revision is bounded work that gets displaced by it. Running them in parallel means the coursework gets done late and the revision gets done badly, which is the February pattern families describe every year.

The adjustment for a first-year student is simpler: the coursework fortnights become foundation work, and the mock fortnights become a first timed sitting of each paper. The adjustment for a student with no coursework deadline that term is to extend the timed-paper work, which is the thing almost nobody does enough of. The table sets it out.

sections.heading: What home tutoring costs in DAMAC Hills, and what it costs in time
paragraphs: Begin with the packages, because that is how in-home tuition is usually sold in this part of Dubai. Monthly arrangements advertised in this market include around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, and around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those two figures describe the trade cleanly: eight hours at home against eight hours online, at roughly double the price.

The hourly bands behind them are published too. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors are quoted between AED 200 and 500 once travel is priced in. Qualified online subject tuition sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 at the premium named end. At the budget end Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65.

All of those are figures published by the providers named and read in October 2026. None is IB Gram's price list. They are printed because most pages competing for this search publish no price at all and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a DAMAC Hills family transacts in.

The time cost is the part no rate card shows. A visiting tutor in this community is budgeting thirty to forty-five minutes each way depending on the hour, and that time is inside the fee whether it is itemised or not. It also makes the tutor's availability thinner and cancellations more likely. For a family whose student is already home late, the arithmetic rarely favours adding two more journeys to the day.

sections.heading: Where the marks go when a term runs short
paragraphs: Every term runs short somewhere, and the question is where. Diploma marks are lost in a small number of categories, and in a compressed term the mechanical ones are both the largest and the cheapest to recover. That makes the triage decision clearer than families expect: fix the habits, rebuild two topics, and leave the rest alone on purpose.

The categories are consistent. Content genuinely not known. Content known but not retrieved under time pressure. Command term misread, so correct knowledge answered a different question. Working not written down, so method marks were unavailable. Arithmetic, units or significant figures. And questions not attempted because the clock ran out.

Three of those six are mechanical and respond within three or four weeks: command terms, written method, and unit and significant-figure discipline. One — retrieval under time — responds to timed practice rather than teaching. Only two are slow, and both are content problems that in a short term should be reduced to the two most examinable topics rather than attempted in full.

Doing this properly needs the marked papers, not the report. A report gives a grade and a comment; the script shows which category each lost mark fell into. Any DAMAC Hills family can run the sort themselves in an evening, and the result tells them whether the next block should be a technique block or a content block, which is the single most useful thing to know before paying for either.

sections.heading: The shape of the Dubai academic year
paragraphs: Dubai schools run three terms with a winter break, a spring break and a long summer, and the Diploma calendar sits inside that structure awkwardly. The second-year pressure lands in the terms either side of the winter break, which is also when the breaks interrupt the continuity that coursework needs. Planning that uses the breaks deliberately rather than treating them as pauses is worth real marks.

The winter break is the best coursework window in the year for a second-year student. There is no new teaching to keep up with, the days are free, and a draft finished there removes the February collision entirely. Families who treat it as recovery time and then spend February in crisis have made a predictable trade without noticing they were making it.

Ramadan falls at a different point each year and changes the shape of the school day: shorter hours and lower afternoon concentration. For online lessons the useful adjustment is simply to move the slot after Iftar, which produces more work than the same hour in the afternoon and needs no journey rearranged on either side. The period suits coursework discussion better than timed papers.

The long summer between the two Diploma years is the single largest block of uncommitted time a student has, and it sits exactly where first-year gaps are still cheap to close. Six sessions in July and August aimed at two named topics is the most efficient purchase in the entire two years, and it is the one almost nobody makes because nothing appears to be wrong in July.

sections.heading: Coursework, honesty and the line that does not move
paragraphs: Every internally assessed component in the Diploma is marked against published criteria, and roughly half the available marks on most of them concern process and communication rather than the result. That is why coursework support is high-value work: the criteria are published, the mark ceilings are known, and almost no student has read either document before being told to.

What a tutor does with coursework is therefore specific. Explain each criterion and what it rewards. Question whether the research question or method can actually be answered in the space available. Discuss whether the evidence supports the conclusion. Have the student self-mark their own draft against each criterion and justify the mark they have given themselves. Then give feedback on what the student has written.

What a tutor does not do is write, complete, draft or produce any part of the submission. That is an IB academic-honesty rule rather than a house style, and work a student did not produce becomes a malpractice finding against the student rather than against whoever supplied it. Providers in this market sell completed internal assessments; the risk in that transaction lands entirely on the candidate.

The practical consequence for timing is that coursework support has to arrive early to be worth much. A tutor can teach criteria and review a draft in the final fortnight, which helps a little. A tutor cannot make an unworkable research question workable at that point, and that is the failure that actually costs the marks.

sections.heading: The regulator, the fees context and the permit
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A DAMAC Hills parent reading an inspection report is reading a KHDA document.

The market context explains why Diploma cohorts here are small. KHDA reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai in 2024-25 offering 17 curricula, with the IB accounting for 7% of pupils and the UK curriculum the largest by enrolment. Seven new private schools arrive for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 places, after six opened during 2025-26 with enrolment up 6%. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Separate classes are required for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. For revision planning that means a Diploma student is timetabled beyond the six IB subjects.

On the tutoring side, private tuition is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE.

faqs.question: Will an IB tutor come to our villa in DAMAC Hills?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Every UAE lesson is delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In this community that is also the more practical arrangement: a visiting tutor adds two journeys through the late-afternoon corridors to a day in which the student has already made two. Published in-home market rates here run AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is counted, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject teaching.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a session can realistically start in DAMAC Hills?
faqs.answer: Usually 5.30pm, and 6pm is more reliable in the second half of term. Secondary students here generally travel out to Al Barsha, Jumeirah or the Ranches and arrive home after five once the Sheikh Zayed bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street and Hessa Street corridors are busy. Because the student is tired by then, two shorter sessions a week work better than one long one, with heavier written work set for a weekend morning slot instead.

faqs.question: Which Diploma deadlines matter before the exams?
faqs.answer: Three, and all are set by the school rather than the board. Internal coursework submissions, which carry a fixed share of each subject grade and usually cluster in the second year. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge deadlines, which together affect up to three diploma points. And the mock window, which produces both diagnostic data and the information behind predicted grades. The option form in the pre-Diploma year closes earliest of all and decides two years of work.

faqs.question: Should coursework and mock revision run at the same time?
faqs.answer: No, and running them together is the most common reason February goes badly. Coursework is open-ended work that expands to fill whatever time exists; revision is bounded work that gets displaced by it. Sequencing them so each fortnight has a single job — two fortnights on coursework, finishing the draft, then two on timed papers and revision — means both get done. It costs nothing and it is a scheduling decision rather than an academic one.

faqs.question: Is the winter break a good time for Diploma work?
faqs.answer: It is the best coursework window in the year for a second-year student. There is no new teaching to keep up with, the days are free, and a draft finished there removes the collision with mock revision entirely. Families who treat it purely as recovery and then spend February in crisis have made that trade without noticing. Three or four sessions across the break, aimed at a coursework draft, is a disproportionately efficient purchase.

faqs.question: How much does a month of IB tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published monthly packages in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour-long sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. All are provider-published figures read in October 2026 and none is IB Gram's price list.

faqs.question: My child's mocks are in three weeks. Is a block worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the target is the mock rather than the syllabus. Three weeks is enough for timed single papers with immediate mark-scheme review, which measures and improves the thing the mock will measure. It is not enough to rebuild content, and a block sold on that basis will disappoint. Preparing for a measurement changes the measurement, and since predicted grades are informed by mock performance, the number has consequences beyond diagnosis.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do with an Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Question whether the research question can be answered in 4,000 words, help narrow it until it can, explain what the assessment criteria reward, discuss whether the argument is supported by the sources, and give feedback on what the student has written. A tutor cannot write, draft or complete any part of it. The highest-value session is the first one, on the question itself, because an unworkable question discovered in month four cannot be rescued by extra sessions.

faqs.question: How should the summer between the two Diploma years be used?
faqs.answer: On the two topics the student already knows they never understood. It is the largest block of uncommitted time in the two years and it sits where first-year gaps are still cheap to close. Six sessions across July and August, aimed at named topics rather than at general revision, removes a problem that otherwise reappears in a February mock. Reading ahead instead usually leaves the gap in place with more content stacked on top of it.

faqs.question: Can lessons move after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Diploma students the later slot usually produces more work. School days shorten and afternoon concentration drops, so a session after Iftar is more productive than the same hour at four o'clock, and because the lesson is online no journey has to be rearranged on either side. The period suits coursework discussion and criterion review better than full timed papers, which are worth scheduling either side of it.

faqs.question: Does a school report tell me enough to plan a term?
faqs.answer: Rarely. A report gives a grade and a comment, and neither says which component produced the grade or which category the lost marks fell into. The marked script does. A student can hold a 5 with strong coursework and weak timed papers, or the reverse, and those two situations need opposite blocks. Sorting the marked papers by cause takes an evening, costs nothing, and tells you whether to buy technique work or content teaching.

faqs.question: Why are Higher Level specialists hard to book after mock results?
faqs.answer: Because demand across every Dubai cohort peaks in the same fortnight. Higher Level Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics are minority subjects inside Diploma cohorts that are themselves small, so the pool of tutors who have taught the extensions is thin, and every school's mock results land within a few weeks of each other. Booking before the mock window rather than after it is the practical response and costs nothing to arrange early.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week suit a student who gets home at five?
faqs.answer: Two shorter ones rather than one long one, for most students in this community. Sixty minutes at 5.30pm twice a week produces more than ninety minutes once, because concentration rather than teaching time is the limit after a commute. The most resilient pattern here is one weekday evening plus a weekend morning, with the longer weekend slot used for written work and discussion rather than for drill.

faqs.question: What happens if the four-session review shows no progress?
faqs.answer: One of three things changes, at no cost: the diagnosis, the tutor or the frequency. A target that has not moved by the halfway point of a block usually means the wrong problem was identified, and that is fixable. What should not happen is the block running quietly to its end because changing felt awkward. Families who never review a block are the ones who pay for a term and then describe tutoring as something that did not work.

intro.heading: Is there an IB tutor near DAMAC Hills 2 who knows the Diploma?
paragraphs: The short answer is that the number of people living within fifteen minutes of DAMAC Hills 2 who have taught a specific IB Diploma course to final grade is very small, and for some subjects it is zero. That is not a criticism of the community. It is arithmetic. DAMAC Hills 2 is a villa development on the Dubailand side of the city, built out well after the school belt it sits beside, and the professional tutoring supply in Dubai is concentrated where the oldest international schools are. Asking for an IB home tutor in DAMAC Hills 2 and expecting a Chemistry HL specialist to live two streets over is asking a lot of a residential map.

What usually happens next is the compromise nobody plans for. A family that cannot find a Diploma specialist nearby hires a general science graduate who is willing to drive out, and pays the travel premium for the privilege. The tutor is capable and the sessions are pleasant, and three months later the student is still losing the same marks in the same place, because the problem was never explained content. It was that nobody had read the subject guide and knew which assessment objective Paper 2 was testing.

IB Gram was built to break that trade-off, and the way it does that is unglamorous: lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, and it is assessed continuously by the class teacher against learning outcomes rather than by examination. Children document thinking in portfolios and finish Year 6 with the PYP Exhibition, a self-directed inquiry presented to the school community. Support at this stage is about building the reading fluency, number sense and written explanation that the later programmes assume.
programmes.countryNote: DAMAC Hills 2 families often arrive mid-primary from a different system, and the shift to inquiry-led learning is the shock. A child who was strong on drilled arithmetic can look weak in a PYP classroom because the task asks them to explain a method, not produce an answer. KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools from the start of primary, running alongside the PYP.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks every subject against four criteria, each on a 0-8 scale, and the criteria differ by subject group. Mathematics marks knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying maths in real-life contexts. Sciences mark knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Year 11 adds the Personal Project, assessed against its own criteria.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP years are where DAMAC Hills 2 parents most often tell us the school report has stopped making sense.
