Our MYP tutoring works criterion by criterion, which is also the only honest preparation for the Diploma that follows.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The final score runs to 45, with up to three bonus points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. UAE schools sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: This is where DAMAC Hills 2 families search hardest for a home tutor, and where the local-supply problem is sharpest, because a Diploma subject at Higher Level is a narrow specialism rather than general secondary teaching. A Physics HL student needs somebody fluent in Paper 3 and the practical scheme of work. The chance that such a person lives in the Dubailand belt and has a free weekday evening is not high.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning component, personal and professional skills, and a language development requirement. It suits a student who wants Diploma-standard academic subjects without the full six-subject load, and who has a clear applied direction such as business, hospitality or engineering technology.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by only a handful of Dubai schools, so most DAMAC Hills 2 families meet it as a mid-sixth-form option rather than a Year 11 choice. Where it matters for tutoring is the DP courses inside it: those are marked to exactly the same standard as a full Diploma candidate's, so a CP student taking Business Management SL needs the same depth of support as anybody else in that exam hall.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.subjectsIntro: These are the IB Diploma and MYP subjects DAMAC Hills 2 families request most, with the part that actually costs marks. Availability varies by level and by session, and the trial lesson is where you confirm the match rather than take our word for it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries this course. Marks go missing in proof, in calculus applications at HL, and in the unstructured Paper 2 questions where no scaffold tells the student which technique applies. The Exploration is a fifth of the grade and is lost on weak personal engagement far more often than on weak mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Lighter on proof, heavier on modelling, statistics and the graphical calculator. The common failure is treating it as the easy option and then meeting hypothesis testing and regression with no statistical vocabulary. HL adds matrices, graph theory and complex numbers, which surprises students who chose AI to avoid abstraction.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 punishes loose definitions, Paper 2 rewards structured working, and Paper 3 tests experimental technique and data analysis in a way textbook practice never prepares a student for. Uncertainty propagation and graph linearisation are where DAMAC Hills 2 students most often arrive stuck.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the two walls. Students who can recite reagents still lose marks because they cannot explain why a nucleophile attacks where it does. The Internal Assessment needs a question with a measurable variable and enough repeats to say something about uncertainty.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap, not the difficulty. Command terms decide the mark: outline, explain, discuss and evaluate each want a different shape of answer, and a well-informed student writing the wrong shape scores low. Statistical treatment in the IA is routinely thin.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams must be drawn, labelled and then used in the prose, not decorated beside it. The three commentaries carry the internal mark and are assessed on application of a named real article, so the choice of article decides the ceiling before any analysis is written.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as SWOT and Ansoff score nothing on their own; the marks sit in applying them to the case material and reaching a supported judgement. HL adds the research project, which needs a live organisation and a question narrow enough to answer in the word limit.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure, and most lost marks come from summarising the text rather than analysing how it produces meaning. The Individual Oral needs a global issue and two works prepared properly, and improvised attempts are audible.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The written papers test architecture, networks and abstract data structures as much as code. Students who are comfortable programming still lose marks on tracing algorithms by hand. The solution project needs a real client, documented criteria for success and evidence of testing.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Every argument must be anchored in a named study with its method and findings, and vague recall of a famous experiment scores little. The HL extensions and the Internal Assessment experiment with its inferential statistic are where structured support changes the grade most.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK is assessed by the exhibition of three objects and the prescribed-title essay, and it contributes to the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. The essay fails when it becomes general opinion rather than a claim-and-counterclaim argument grounded in specific areas of knowledge.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a chosen subject, marked against five criteria. Most grades are decided by the research question: too broad and nothing is answered, too narrow and there is no argument. A tutor coaches the question, the method and the reflection — the writing stays the student's own.

sections.heading: What searching for an IB home tutor in DAMAC Hills 2 actually turns up
paragraphs: Type it into Google and you get three categories of result. Agencies with a Dubai landing page and no named neighbourhood. Marketplaces quoting prices in US dollars, which is not a currency any family in DAMAC Hills 2 pays school fees in. And classified listings from individuals, most of whom are general tutors rather than Diploma specialists, and a proportion of whom will not be able to tell you their permit position if you ask.

What almost none of them tell you is how the supply actually works. Private tutoring in Dubai clusters around the old school corridors — Jumeirah, Al Barsha, the Greens, Mirdif — because that is where the tutors live and where the density of clients justifies the driving. DAMAC Hills 2 is a long way from all of them. A tutor based in Al Barsha quoting you a home-visit rate is quoting a rate that has forty minutes of Al Qudra Road baked into it each way, and that time is being paid for by you whether the invoice itemises it or not.

So the honest answer to the parent's real question is layered. Yes, there are tutors who will come to DAMAC Hills 2. No, there is not a deep bench of them who have taught your child's specific Diploma course at your child's specific level. And the gap between those two sentences is where most of the wasted money in Dubai tutoring sits: families pay a travel premium for proximity and then discover proximity was never the thing in short supply.

IB Gram's position on this is deliberately plain. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — that service exists only in India. For DAMAC Hills 2 we deliver one-to-one lessons over live video, which means the specialist pool is the whole of our teaching roster rather than the subset willing to drive to the Al Qudra corridor at 6pm. You lose the tutor in the room. You gain the one who has taught the course.

sections.heading: Counting the local specialist pool, subject by subject
paragraphs: It helps to replace the feeling of scarcity with a number. Dubai had 387,441 private-school pupils in 2024-25 across 227 schools, and the International Baccalaureate accounted for 7% of them. That is a meaningful Diploma population, but it is spread across the entire emirate, and only the final two years of it sit the Diploma at all. Now narrow to one subject at one level — Chemistry HL, say — and then to the fraction of that cohort living in or near DAMAC Hills 2.

The tutor side narrows faster. A person qualified to teach Chemistry HL to grade is typically either a current Diploma teacher at a Dubai school, a former one, or a graduate who has trained specifically on the course. Current school teachers are the largest group and the most constrained: Abu Dhabi's ADEK ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct carries the same restriction, so your child's own teacher is not the answer even where they are willing.

The table below is an estimate of the structure of that scarcity, not a census. The point of it is not the exact figures; it is the shape. For broad, early-years support, local supply is adequate. For a named Diploma subject at Higher Level, it collapses. That collapse is the whole reason online matching exists, and the reason a DAMAC Hills 2 family should stop optimising for distance and start optimising for whether the tutor has read the subject guide.

sections.heading: What home tutoring costs in this part of Dubai, and what the travel buys
paragraphs: Start with the monthly number rather than the hourly one, because that is the figure a household budget actually feels. Bestimate's Dubai rate research puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240-600 a month for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for mid-tier, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in the Dubai market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those two in-home figures are the interesting ones. Four two-hour visits a month at AED 1,699 works out near AED 212 an hour, and for a community as far out as DAMAC Hills 2 a tutor pricing that honestly is covering eighty minutes of driving per visit inside it. That is the travel premium, and it is worth being clear about what it buys: a person physically present, which matters for a young child who cannot self-manage, and almost nothing for a Diploma student who needs correct explanation of Paper 3 technique.

On the hourly view, the Dubai market splits into bands that the published sources broadly agree on. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for qualified online tutors. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180-500 including travel, per Bestimate and the home-tutor listings. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists sit at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one versus a tutor in your living room: the DAMAC Hills 2 version
paragraphs: This comparison is usually written as a list of online advantages. It deserves better, because in-home tutoring genuinely wins on some things and a parent should know which. A tutor in the room can see a child fidget and intervene before the attention goes. They can take a phone off the table. For a primary-age child with no self-regulation, that physical authority is worth real money, and any page that pretends otherwise is selling rather than advising.

What in-home loses on, from DAMAC Hills 2 specifically, is the pool and the clock. The pool, because you are choosing from the people willing to drive out here on a weekday evening, which for a Higher Level Diploma subject may be nobody. The clock, because a 4:30pm arrival home from a school in Motor City or Sports City plus a tutor fighting Al Qudra Road means a session that starts at 6pm and ends when a tired student has stopped absorbing anything.

Online removes both constraints and adds a few of its own. Screen sharing makes past-paper marking visible in a way a shared notebook does not. Sessions are recorded or notes are shared, so revision three months later has something to work from. Nothing is lost to travel, so a cancellation costs nobody ninety minutes of road. Against that: a weak internet connection ruins a lesson, and a student who will not engage with a screen will not engage with ours either. The trial lesson exists to find that out before you pay for a term.

sections.heading: Is the tutor coming to your villa legally permitted to teach?
paragraphs: Most parents in Dubai have never been told that this is a regulated activity, and the people who most benefit from that silence are the ones operating without a permit. Private tuition in the UAE sits under a work-permit regime introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. The permit is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time.

The eligibility list is broader than parents expect. It includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. So a university student tutoring your Year 9 child can hold a perfectly valid permit. What matters is whether they actually do. MoHRE states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the amounts, so treat any figure you see circulating as unverified.

There is a second restriction that catches well-meaning families. The permit's code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and press reporting on Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules describes the same prohibition for private and charter school staff there. The marketing line 'your child's own teacher, privately' is therefore not something any reputable provider should offer. If it is offered to you, that is information about the provider.

One more distinction worth holding. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE permit. An organisation running tutoring from premises in Dubai with staff is a different legal entity and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds neither a KHDA institute permit nor any form of KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership, and you should be sceptical of any provider claiming otherwise without showing you the permit number.

sections.heading: Where a DAMAC Hills 2 Diploma student actually loses marks
paragraphs: Parents usually describe the problem as the subject. The student says Chemistry is hard. The report says more effort needed in Physics. Neither statement tells a tutor anything useful, because a Diploma grade is not lost across a subject; it is lost in identifiable places, and those places repeat across students with remarkable consistency.

The first is command terms. The IB publishes them, every subject guide lists the ones that apply, and they are instructions rather than synonyms. State wants a bare answer. Outline wants a brief account. Explain wants causation. Discuss wants a balanced consideration. Evaluate wants a judgement supported by the balance. A student who understands the content and answers discuss with a list of facts will be marked down by somebody who can see that they understood it. This is the cheapest grade on the page to recover.

The second is Paper 3 and the practical scheme of work in the sciences. It is a different skill from the content papers: processing raw data, propagating uncertainty, linearising a graph, spotting that a method cannot answer the question it was set. Schools teach it, but they teach it inside a crowded practical timetable, and students who miss a few weeks of it rarely recover the technique from a textbook.

The third is the Internal Assessment, and it is the single largest recoverable block in most Diploma subjects. Marks are lost at the design stage, before any data exists — a research question with no measurable variable, too few repeats to say anything about reliability, an Exploration with mathematics that is technically fine and personal engagement that is absent. A tutor who reads the criteria with the student at week one is worth several who read the draft at week ten.
bullets: Command terms decide the shape of the answer, and the shape decides the mark
Paper 3 and practical technique are a separate skill from content revision

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This matters more in the UAE market than almost anywhere, because the search results for Dubai IB help include operators who sell finished coursework. One of them advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is not a shortcut with a cost; it is an academic-honesty breach that puts the student's entire Diploma at risk, and the IB withdraws awards for malpractice.

The boundary itself is not vague, and it is easier to apply than parents fear. A tutor may teach the subject content the assessment rests on. They may explain what a criterion is asking for and what the mark allocation rewards. They may help narrow a research question until it is answerable. They may review a method and point out that it will not generate usable data. They may read a draft the student has written and give feedback on it. All of that is ordinary teaching and all of it is permitted.

What a tutor may not do is produce the work. Not write a section. Not supply a paragraph to insert. Not rewrite the student's prose into their own. Not provide a template that only needs numbers dropped in. Not edit a draft to a finish so the submitted text is substantially the tutor's. The student's own authorship has to be real, because they will sign a declaration saying so and the supervisor signs alongside them.

IB Gram's tutors work inside that line, and we say so in writing because in this particular SERP it is a differentiator rather than a disclaimer. We also do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those are the awarding bodies' copyright. We reference them, we link to the official source, and we teach from them.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the IB Diploma in the May session. The useful way to think about a Diploma year is therefore backwards from there, because almost every deadline that decides the grade falls months earlier and most of them are internal to the school rather than published by the IB.

One honesty note first. The IB does not permit automated retrieval of its pages, so no specific IB exam window or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org. We therefore write about the May session as the one UAE schools sit, and we do not publish a specific date. Get the exact dates from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly — they are the only sources worth acting on, and a tutoring website is not one of them.

For IGCSE siblings in the same household, the Cambridge position is published and is worth stating precisely because it is widely got wrong. Cambridge runs its International GCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series. The February/March series is offered to India only; UAE candidates sit June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

sections.heading: What happens when no specialist is free for your subject
paragraphs: No tutoring provider covers every IB subject at every level at every hour, and the ones that imply otherwise are the ones you should distrust. Theory of Knowledge at short notice, Higher Level Computer Science, a less-taught Group 2 language, Music or Film — these are genuinely scarce, and a DAMAC Hills 2 family asking for one in March deserves a straight answer rather than a holding pattern.

So here is ours. If we have a specialist free who matches the subject and level, we propose them and you take a free trial lesson with that person. If the only available specialist works from a different time zone, we say so and offer the slots that exist, which for most of our roster means early morning or evening in Gulf Standard Time. If nobody suitable is free at all, we say that too, and we would rather lose the enquiry than put a general tutor in front of a Higher Level candidate eight weeks before a session.

There is one substitution we will never make, and it is worth stating because the market does make it: we do not offer a home visit in the UAE as a fallback when the online match is hard. There is no UAE visiting service to fall back on. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and nobody on our roster will arrive at a DAMAC Hills 2 address. Everything we deliver here is one-to-one over live video.

If the match is wrong once it starts, say so early. A mismatch between a competent tutor and a particular student is common and is nobody's failure; it is a reason to change tutor, not a reason to spend a term hoping. Tell us in the first fortnight and we rematch.

process.title: Tell us the school, the subjects and the levels
process.description: Not just 'IB maths'. Which school in or near DAMAC Hills 2, which course, which level, and what the last report or mock actually said. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL and Applications and Interpretation SL need different tutors, and the school's scheme of work decides the order topics are taught in.

process.title: A diagnostic on real questions
process.description: Before any plan is written, the student works through past-paper questions at their own level while a specialist watches. That conversation is where the actual problem surfaces, and it is usually narrower than the school report implies — a command term misread, a technique never taught, a topic missed during a term abroad.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the tutor who would continue
process.description: Not a sales call and not a different person. The specialist proposed for your child teaches a full session, and you and the student judge the fit afterwards. If it is not right, nothing has been spent and we propose somebody else. This is the only part of the process that tells you anything reliable.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: We set the time around the school run from Motor City, Sports City or wherever your child is enrolled, and around prayer times and family commitments. Most DAMAC Hills 2 sessions settle between 4:30pm and 9pm. The slot stays the same week to week, because a moving slot is the main reason tutoring quietly stops.

process.title: Review against the criteria, not against a feeling
process.description: Every few weeks the tutor reports in terms of the published assessment criteria and the marks they carry: which criterion has moved, which paper technique is now reliable, what is still weak. If progress stalls, that review is where we change the plan or change the tutor rather than carrying on.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the course, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: The constraint on good tutoring in DAMAC Hills 2 was never distance; it was whether anybody nearby had taught your child's specific Diploma course. Online delivery removes distance from the equation entirely, so the match is made on subject, level and assessment experience.

whyPoints.title: We say plainly that we do not visit UAE homes
whyPoints.description: Several providers leave the delivery model vague until a parent has paid. Ours is on every page: one-to-one over live video for the UAE, with home visits offered only in India. You will never be surprised by it, and you will never be waiting at the door.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with the source named
whyPoints.description: Three of six ranking competitors publish no price at all and two quote US dollars. We publish the Dubai market bands in AED with each figure attributed to the provider that published it and the month it was read, so you can check them. None of them is presented as our rate.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line stated in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains criteria, reviews method and gives feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor does not write, rewrite or finish coursework. In a search result that contains operators selling completed Internal Assessments, publishing that boundary is the useful signal.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership, and does not imply one. Every number on this page carries its source and its date. We publish no self-generated star ratings and no satisfaction percentages.

whyPoints.title: The trial decides, not the brochure
whyPoints.description: A free trial lesson with the tutor who would actually teach your child tells you more in sixty minutes than any amount of copy. If the fit is wrong, you have spent nothing and we propose somebody else. That is the whole of our argument.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who comes to our villa in DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one IB tuition to DAMAC Hills 2 families online, over live video, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — in-home visiting is a service we run in India only. Other providers in Dubai do offer home visits, at published market rates of roughly AED 180-500 an hour including travel. From the Al Qudra corridor that rate carries a long drive inside it. Our view is that for a Diploma subject the scarce thing is a specialist who has taught the course, not a person in the room, so we optimise for the specialist.

faqs.question: Are there really no IB Diploma specialists living near DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: There are some, and for broad MYP or primary support the local pool is adequate. It thins sharply for a named Diploma subject at Higher Level. Dubai's Diploma population is about 7% of 387,441 private-school pupils spread across the whole emirate, only the final two years of which sit the Diploma, so any single course at a single level is a small cohort citywide and smaller still in one community. Add that serving school teachers may not tutor students enrolled at their own school, and the realistic local supply for something like Chemistry HL is often zero.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for IB tutoring from DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Dubai market rates, read from published provider pages in October 2026: qualified online subject tutors run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270; in-home visits run AED 180-500 including travel. Monthly packages advertised include around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are market figures from the named providers, not IB Gram prices. Take the free trial lesson and get a direct quote, because the right number depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks remain.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a DAMAC Hills 2 family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any individual charging for private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website or e-services. Eligible applicants include school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Ask any tutor directly for their permit and verify it through MoHRE. MoHRE states that tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published, so ignore figures circulating online.

faqs.question: Which schools do DAMAC Hills 2 children usually attend?
faqs.answer: Jebel Ali School sits in neighbouring DAMAC Hills, and families commonly travel to Fairgreen International School, South View School, The Aquila School, Ranches Primary School and JESS Arabian Ranches on the Al Qudra side. For secondary, many go towards Motor City and Dubai Sports City — GEMS Metropole, Victory Heights Primary, GEMS United, Bradenton Preparatory Academy, Dunecrest American School and Lycée Français Jean Mermoz. We name these to describe the local landscape; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them. The school matters to us because it sets the scheme of work and the pickup time.

faqs.question: What time can lessons realistically start given the DAMAC Hills 2 school run?
faqs.answer: Most families here are collecting from schools ten to twenty-five minutes away, and in the evening peak that becomes longer, so a 3:30pm bell often means a 4:30pm arrival home. Because nobody is driving to you, an online session can start at 4:30pm or 4:45pm with no further wait. In practice DAMAC Hills 2 slots settle between 4:30pm and 9pm Gulf Standard Time, set around prayer times and other commitments. We fix the slot and keep it, because sessions that move every week are the ones that quietly stop happening.

faqs.question: How much help with an IB Internal Assessment is actually allowed?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help your child do it; a tutor cannot do it for them. Permitted support is teaching the underlying content, explaining what each criterion asks for and what marks it carries, helping narrow the research question until it is answerable, reviewing whether a method will produce usable data, and giving feedback on a draft your child has written. Not permitted: writing any part of it, supplying text to insert, rewriting the prose, or editing it to a finish. Operators in this market sell completed IAs. That is an academic-honesty breach and it puts the whole Diploma at risk.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring actually effective for an IB student who prefers face to face?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma students, yes, and for some younger children, no. The honest split is about self-regulation. A Year 12 or 13 student working through past-paper questions with a specialist on a shared screen loses nothing to the format and gains marking they can see annotated in real time. A primary-age child who needs a phone taken off the table benefits from physical presence. If your child is in the second group, be sceptical of any online provider, including us. The free trial lesson is how you find out which group they are in without spending anything.

faqs.question: When do IB and IGCSE exams happen for students in DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the IB Diploma in the May session. We deliberately publish no specific IB date, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and we will not put an unverified exam date in front of a parent — get it from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. For Cambridge, the position is published: International GCSE and O Level run in a June series and a November series, and the February/March series is offered to India only, so UAE candidates sit June and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

faqs.question: Who regulates my child's school, and does that affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: Dubai private schools, including every school a DAMAC Hills 2 family uses, are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects annually from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. None of them regulates or approves private tutors — that is MoHRE's permit. Treat any provider that implies a regulator endorses its tutors with real caution.

faqs.question: Do DAMAC Hills 2 pupils take Arabic and Islamic Education as well as the IB?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These subjects sit alongside the Diploma, not inside it, and they still appear on the school report.

faqs.question: What do the MoE equivalency rules ask of a British-track student here?
faqs.answer: For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. For the American track, English proficiency is IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 in reading and writing, and mathematics requires at least SAT Math 450. No IB points threshold has been verified, so we publish none — check moe.gov.ae. IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a DAMAC Hills 2 family?
faqs.answer: For common Diploma subjects at Standard Level and most MYP work, we usually propose a specialist and a trial slot within a few days. Higher Level sciences, Higher Level Computer Science, Theory of Knowledge at short notice and smaller language options take longer and sometimes cannot be covered at all in a given term. We tell you which case you are in rather than holding the enquiry open. If the only matching specialist is in another time zone, we say so and offer the slots that genuinely exist before you commit to anything.

faqs.question: What happens if we take the trial lesson and the tutor is not right?
faqs.answer: Nothing has been spent and we propose somebody else. A mismatch between a capable tutor and a particular student is common and is not a failure on either side — pace, explanation style and personality all matter more than credentials once a basic competence threshold is passed. If it only becomes clear two or three sessions in, tell us in the first fortnight and we rematch. The thing not to do is spend a term hoping it improves, which is how families lose both the money and the term.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two subjects for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single tutor who sees the whole workload can balance an IA deadline in one subject against a mock in another. Maths and Physics overlap enough that one specialist often covers both credibly. Chemistry and Biology less so at Higher Level, where the content depth pulls apart. What we will not do is stretch one tutor across subjects they do not genuinely teach to save you a match — two competent specialists beat one generalist in every Diploma scenario we have seen.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or the school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most DAMAC Hills 2 families do move them. During Ramadan, school days shorten and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so sessions commonly shift to late morning, early afternoon or post-Iftar slots, and some families pause for part of the month and resume with a heavier block afterwards. Over summer and the winter break, we keep sessions running for students who are travelling, because the time zone of the tutor is already part of the arrangement rather than an obstacle to it. Tell us the new pattern and we reset the slot rather than cancelling.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-deira.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects to students in Old Dubai. Each one works to the student's own school deadline sheet, not a generic scheme of work, and the first lesson is a free diagnostic rather than a sales call.

intro.heading: Where a Deira Diploma student actually is this term
paragraphs: A search for an IB home tutor in Deira almost never happens in September. It happens in the second half of a term, after a mock paper has come back, or after a Diploma coordinator has emailed about an Internal Assessment draft that has not arrived. By then the question is no longer whether tutoring helps in general. It is whether the weeks still on the calendar are enough to move a 4 to a 5, or hold a 6 that is slipping, and what has to happen in each of those weeks for that to be true.

That is the frame this page uses. Deira is one of the oldest residential districts in Dubai and one of the most densely built, running from the creek up through Al Muteena and Hor Al Anz towards Al Mamzar. The schools its families use are spread wide: Deira International School sits in Dubai Festival City, Rashid School for Boys in Al Garhoud, several of the large Indian-curriculum schools in Oud Metha and Al Qusais. A Deira student can easily spend fifty minutes a day in a car without leaving a six-kilometre radius, and that single fact decides how many usable study hours a week actually contains.

The Diploma Programme is unforgiving about those hours because its deadlines are internal before they are external. The written papers in the May session are the visible endpoint, but a Diploma student in Dubai meets eight or nine school-set deadlines before them: a Maths Exploration draft, a Chemistry or Physics investigation, a TOK exhibition or essay plan, an Extended Essay first full draft, the reflective sessions that go with it, plus two rounds of mocks. Each of those is a fixed date on a sheet the school issued months earlier. Tutoring that ignores the sheet produces pleasant lessons and no change in grades.

IB Gram works the other way round. The first thing a tutor asks a Deira family for is the school's assessment calendar, and the first session maps the remaining weeks against it: which deadline is closest, which one carries the most marks, which one the student is furthest from meeting. Only then does subject content get chosen. If there are eight weeks until a mock, eight weeks is the plan, and the plan says what each week does. If there are eighteen months until the first paper, the work is different and slower, and the Extended Essay gets started properly rather than rescued.

Lessons are taught online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that is a service offered only in India. For a Deira family this is usually the better arrangement rather than a compromise, and the sections below set out why in numbers: what the in-home market around Al Garhoud charges once travel is priced in, how much of a 60-minute paid hour a crossing of the creek consumes, and how much wider the pool of HL specialists becomes once the twenty-minute drive stops being a constraint.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-deira.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the three IB programmes a Deira family is likely to meet, and the support looks different in each. What follows describes what the programme assesses and then what it means specifically for a student living in Old Dubai with a long school commute.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Assessment is continuous, organised around transdisciplinary themes and a Year 6 Exhibition that asks a child to run a small inquiry and present it. Tutoring at this stage is about literacy fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining reasoning out loud, because the Middle Years Programme assumes all three. The common gap we see is a child who can compute accurately but cannot yet say why a method works, which is precisely what MYP criteria reward.
programmes.countryNote: Deira families often move a child into a PYP school from a national-curriculum primary where marks came from recall. The adjustment takes a term. Sessions in the late afternoon work better here than evening ones, because a Year 4 or 5 child who left Al Mamzar at seven in the morning is finished by six. Thirty to forty-five minutes twice a week does more at this age than a single long block, and the school's own portfolio comments are the best guide to what needs work.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks every subject against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, and converts the total to a 1-7 grade on a published boundary table. Students lose marks for not answering the command term rather than for not knowing content: a question asking them to evaluate gets described instead. MYP Year 5 ends with the Personal Project, which is externally moderated. Tutoring works best when it is criterion-led, taking one criterion at a time against the student's own marked work.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma step is the sharpest transition a Dubai student makes, and Deira schools run it at different speeds. A student arriving in DP1 from MYP Mathematics Extended is usually fine; one arriving from Standard has a real algebra and function gap to close in the first ten weeks of DP1. We check this in the trial lesson with four past MYP-style questions, because finding it in October of DP1 is recoverable and finding it in February of DP2 is not.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly 20 to 25 per cent of the final grade, marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The written papers in the May session decide the rest. The Diploma rewards students who treat the IA as a graded piece of coursework with criteria, and punishes those who treat it as an essay to finish the week before it is due.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and that shapes the whole Dubai Diploma calendar: mocks in the winter and early spring terms, IA deadlines clustered before them, Extended Essay final submission earlier still. A Deira DP2 student with a long commute has roughly twelve usable weekday evening hours a week for all six subjects plus core. Tutoring that adds hours without removing anything fails. We plan which subject gets the hour and what the student stops doing to free it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-deira.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and MYP subjects Deira families request most often, with a note on what each one actually assesses and where marks go missing. The description is deliberately about assessment rather than topic lists, because that is where a tutored hour earns its place.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: AA is the proof-and-algebra route. SL sits Papers 1 and 2; HL adds Paper 3, a two-question extended investigation worth 20 per cent of the HL grade and the component HL students are least prepared for. Marks are lost on unjustified steps and on calculator work shown without method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is modelling and statistics led, with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout. The frequent failure is treating it as the easy route: AI HL statistics and the HL Paper 3 investigation are demanding, and several engineering courses still expect AA. Route choice belongs in DP1, not DP2.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields carry the paper weight; HL adds depth rather than new habits. Students lose marks in Paper 2 by giving a numerical answer without the relationship it rests on, and in the investigation by collecting data before deciding what the uncertainty analysis will look like.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are where HL grades separate. The scientific investigation needs a measurable, controllable variable chosen in week one; most weak IAs are weak because the research question was unanswerable, not because the write-up was poor.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where recall is necessary but not sufficient. Extended-response marks come from using the command term exactly, and data-based questions reward students who read the axes and the control before the trend. HL biochemistry and genetics need spaced revision from DP1.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry the marks. A correctly labelled and explained diagram answers most of a Paper 1 question; an unlabelled one answers none of it. The three commentaries use published news articles and are marked on application of theory, not on the quality of the journalism chosen.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided textual analysis of unseen non-literary text, which is a trainable skill rather than a talent. The Individual Oral links a global issue to two texts and is internally assessed, so it rewards rehearsal against the criteria far more than it rewards a clever topic.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as the Ansoff matrix and break-even analysis must be applied to the stimulus, not recited. HL students are assessed on a research project built on primary or secondary evidence about one real organisation, which needs a focused question agreed early in DP2.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The TOK exhibition and the prescribed-title essay together contribute to the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. Essays fail when they describe a knowledge question instead of arguing about it. Coaching here is structural: claim, counterclaim, real example, implication.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay in one subject, with three recorded reflective sessions. A tutor can help narrow a research question, test whether the sources exist and review structure and argument against the published criteria. The essay itself has to be the student's own writing.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Close to Rashid School for Boys and a short run to Dubai Festival City. Families here often manage a 4:30pm start on three days a week, which makes Al Garhoud one of the easier Deira sub-areas to schedule around.

regions.name: Al Mamzar
regions.note: Northern edge of Deira against the Sharjah boundary. Al Ittihad Private School sits here. Evening sessions after six are more realistic than late-afternoon ones, because the return leg crosses the Sharjah commuter flow.

regions.name: Hor Al Anz
regions.note: Dense mid-Deira residential grid with a mix of Indian, British and IB school destinations. Siblings often attend different schools in different districts, so household scheduling rather than traffic is the binding constraint here.

regions.name: Al Muteena

regions.name: Al Qusais

schoolClusters.note: This cluster carries most of the IB and British-curriculum demand on the Deira side of the creek. sections.heading: What a Deira parent is actually asking in week eight of term
paragraphs: Searching for an IB home tutor in Deira is usually a question about time, not about tutoring. The real question is whether the weeks left before the next school-set deadline are enough, and what has to happen inside each of them. The honest answer depends on two things a parent can check in ten minutes: which deadline comes next on the school's assessment calendar, and how far the student's last marked piece of work sat from the grade they need.

Those two facts decide everything else. A DP1 student eleven months from any external paper, sitting two grades below target in HL Chemistry, has room to rebuild the subject from the foundations up, and should. A DP2 student six weeks from a mock with the same gap does not have that room, and spending those six weeks on foundations would be a mistake. The work there is narrower and more mechanical: find the four topics that account for most of the lost marks, repair those, and spend the rest of the time on how the paper is answered.

This is also why the first session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson. A tutor reads the student's most recent marked paper or IA draft, the school's deadline sheet and the mark breakdown per question, then says what the remaining weeks can realistically deliver. Sometimes that answer is less than a parent hoped. Saying so at the start is more useful than discovering it in April, and a Deira family losing fifty minutes a day to the bridges cannot afford to spend a term finding out.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the first paper
paragraphs: Almost no competitor page for this search names a single deadline. That is the gap worth filling, because the Diploma is a sequence of internal dates long before it is an examination. UAE schools sit the May session, so a Dubai Diploma calendar runs from the written papers backwards through two mock windows, a cluster of Internal Assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay final submission and the TOK components. Every one of those dates is set by the school, published in advance, and recoverable only if it is seen coming.

The table below counts the DP2 year backwards in relative weeks rather than in calendar dates, because each school in Dubai sets its own internal deadlines and a date copied from another school's sheet is worse than no date at all. IB examination and results dates are not published here: ibo.org is the only authority for those and should be checked directly with the school's IB coordinator, who holds the confirmed session timetable for the cohort.

Read the table as a planning instrument. The point of counting backwards is that it tells a family when tutoring stops being able to change an outcome. Work on an Internal Assessment is valuable up to the school's submission date and worth nothing after it, and the IA carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade. A family that starts in the autumn still has every component in play. A family that starts after the final IA submission has only the written papers left, which is a smaller lever.

sections.heading: What in-home IB tutoring costs around Deira, and what the travel pays for
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest option and work up, because that is the order a budget actually gets built in. University-student and generalist online tutors advertise from the bottom of the Dubai market: EdFlik publishes rates from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online is the next band up, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that sit IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and a premium named or examiner tier reaching AED 650 at BartyED.

In-home one-to-one is priced differently, and the difference is travel. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoting 200 to 500 once the journey is included. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, 600 to 1,200 mid-market and 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

A Deira parent can verify most of this without taking anyone's word for it. Ask two local providers for a written hourly figure, ask whether it includes travel, and ask how long the tutor expects the journey to take at half past four. The arithmetic that follows is the useful part: a tutor crossing Al Garhoud Bridge in the afternoon school peak is pricing a round trip of forty to seventy minutes into the hour, and that cost appears either as a higher rate or as a shorter taught hour. Figures here are market rates from the sources named, not IB Gram prices; our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation.

sections.heading: A tutor in a Deira flat against one-to-one online
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, so this comparison is not a sales device; it is the reason the service is built the way it is. A Deira family choosing between the two formats is really choosing between proximity and specialism, and in a district shaped by two bridges and a creek those two things pull hard against each other.

Consider what the geography does to a tutor's catchment. A tutor willing to travel to an apartment in Hor Al Anz for a 5pm session has to be somewhere between Al Mamzar and Oud Metha at four. That is a small pool, and it gets smaller the more specific the requirement becomes: not just a maths tutor but an AA HL tutor comfortable with Paper 3, or a Chemistry tutor who has supervised investigations through moderation. Online delivery removes the drive from the equation entirely, and the pool becomes every specialist available at that hour in Gulf Standard Time.

The format also changes what a session can contain. Marked work, a past paper and the student's IA draft can be on a shared screen with annotation, saved and sent after the lesson, which means the next session starts where the last one finished rather than with twenty minutes of re-establishing context. A recorded explanation of a worked Paper 1 question can be rewatched the night before a mock. None of that is possible across a dining table, and it matters more in the Diploma than in earlier years because the volume of written feedback is so much larger.

sections.heading: Mock season in Dubai IB schools, and what a mock actually tells you
paragraphs: Dubai Diploma schools usually run two mock windows in DP2, and parents tend to read the grade and nothing else. The grade is the least useful part. What matters is the per-question mark breakdown, because that is the only thing that tells you whether marks were lost to missing content, to misread command terms or to running out of time, and each of those needs a different fix over the following weeks.

The pattern repeats across subjects. A student who scores well on the first two-thirds of a paper and collapses on the last third has a timing problem, and no amount of extra content teaching will touch it. A student scattering small losses across every question is usually losing method marks: an answer without working, a unit omitted, a graph without labelled axes. A student who fails whole questions on two specific topics has a content gap that is genuinely repairable in a fortnight. The first lesson after a mock should be spent diagnosing which of those three is happening rather than reteaching the paper.

Mock grades also sit lower than final grades more often than not, because the full syllabus may not be finished and because the student has not yet done the volume of past papers that the final run-in produces. That is worth knowing in both directions: a disappointing mock is not a prediction, and a comfortable mock is not a guarantee of anything. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone selling a specific number from a mock result should be questioned closely. What a tutor can do is convert the mark breakdown into a weekly plan with a named target per week.

sections.heading: The eight weeks that decide an Internal Assessment
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly 20 to 25 per cent of the grade, marked in school and moderated by the IB. Most weak IAs are decided in the first fortnight, not the last. A research question that cannot be answered with the data a Dubai school student can actually collect produces a mediocre mark however well it is written up, and the single most valuable hour of coursework coaching is the one spent testing feasibility before anything else begins.

A workable eight-week shape looks like this. Week one: three candidate research questions, each tested for whether the data or sources exist and whether the method is controllable. Week two: method fixed, variables and uncertainties decided in advance of collection. Weeks three and four: collection or research, with a mid-point check that the data is usable. Week five: analysis against the criteria. Week six: first full draft. Week seven: criterion-by-criterion feedback, with the letter named, and revision by the student. Week eight: final checks on referencing, word count and presentation, submitted before the school deadline.

What the tutor does not do is also a plan. The tutor does not collect the data, write any section, or edit the prose into its final form. That boundary is not a disclaimer; it is what keeps the mark valid and the student out of a malpractice investigation. Feedback is given as a question about a criterion: what evidence supports this conclusion, which uncertainty dominates here, why is this source reliable for this claim. The student answers it in their own words, in their own file, and the mark stays theirs.

sections.heading: Where a tutor must stop on the IA, Extended Essay and TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the line that separates tutoring from the essay services visible in the same search results. One provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments for sale. Buying one is academic misconduct under IB rules, it puts the student's entire Diploma at risk, and it is an easy thing for a teacher who knows the student's written voice to spot. A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback. A tutor does not produce the work.

In practice the boundary is clear once it is written down. A tutor may explain what a criterion rewards, show an exemplar published by the IB, ask why a conclusion follows from the data, point out that a section is descriptive where the criterion asks for evaluation, and check that referencing follows the subject guide. A tutor may not supply a research question as a finished product, write or rewrite paragraphs, carry out the analysis, or hand over a document the student then submits. The same applies to the Extended Essay and the TOK essay, where the reflective sessions and the supervisor's own comments form part of the assessment record.

IB Gram also does not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables. Those belong to the boards. Tutors reference them, link to the official source and work from material the school has legitimately provided. Published subject guides and assessment criteria are where feedback language should come from, and students are better served by learning to read those documents themselves than by receiving a summary of them.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the shortened school day and the Deira revision block
paragraphs: Ramadan falls inside the Diploma run-in, and in Dubai it changes the shape of a school day rather than pausing it. Hours shorten, the afternoon is quieter, and the productive study window for a fasting student usually moves to after Iftar. A tutoring plan written in September without that in it will collide with it, and the collision lands in exactly the weeks before the second mock window when there is least room to lose time.

The practical answer is to plan the term in two halves. Before Ramadan, front-load the heavy cognitive work: new content, the hardest topics, the IA analysis that needs sustained concentration. During Ramadan, shift to shorter and later sessions, more past-paper technique and less new material, and accept that two 45-minute sessions after Iftar will do more than one 90-minute block in the late afternoon. Deira families with long Sharjah-side commutes often find the post-Iftar slot is the only genuinely quiet hour in the household.

The UAE academic calendar matters in the same way. Winter and spring breaks are when a determined student can gain real ground, and also when families travel; a plan that assumes four uninterrupted weeks in January will not survive contact with reality. Online delivery helps here, since a booked slot can follow a student to another time zone if the family agrees the adjusted hour in advance. What does not work is leaving the break unplanned and hoping, then arriving at the second mock three weeks behind.

sections.heading: Starting mid-term in Deira, and what happens if the slot you want is gone
paragraphs: Most Deira families start tutoring in the middle of a term, which means the first job is triage rather than a curriculum plan. The sequence is short: send the student's most recent marked work and the school's assessment calendar, take a free trial lesson that functions as a diagnostic, then agree a written plan in weeks with a named target for each. If the plan does not survive the first fortnight, it gets rewritten; a plan nobody revises is a plan nobody is using.

Availability is where most providers go quiet, so here is the honest position. Weekday slots between four and six in the afternoon Gulf Standard Time are the most contested hours on the platform, because every Gulf family wants them. Common Diploma subjects are usually matchable within a few days. Niche combinations take longer: HL Further Mathematics, a less-taught Group 2 language, or a specific subject at HL combined with a narrow slot can mean a wait, a different hour, or an honest recommendation to look elsewhere. We would rather say that than place a general tutor in a specialist seat.

If no specialist is free for the hour a family needs, there are three routes and all three get offered openly: take an adjacent hour, start with a diagnostic block and a planned handover once the specialist opens up, or wait. The one route we do not take is assigning whoever is available and describing them as a specialist. A Deira parent eight weeks from a mock has no time to discover in week three that the match was wrong, and the cost of that discovery is not measured in dirhams.

The tutor works through two or three questions from the student's own paper to locate where marks are going, then says what the remaining weeks can realistically achieve. If the match is wrong, this is where it is caught.

It also names what the student stops doing to free the hour, because a Deira weekday evening is already short. After each lesson the parent gets a short note on what moved and what did not. Annotated screens and worked solutions are saved, so revision in the final fortnight draws on the student's own corrected work.

process.description: Every school-set deadline is a checkpoint: did the plan deliver what it promised, and what changes for the next block. After a mock the per-question breakdown is read properly and the plan rewritten around it. At the end of a block the honest options are continue, reduce or stop, and stopping is a legitimate recommendation.

whyPoints.title: A written line on academic honesty
whyPoints.description: Coursework coaching is defined in writing before it starts: what the tutor will read, question and feed back on, and what stays entirely the student's own work. faqs.question: We are eight weeks from the next mock and live in Deira. Is it worth starting IB tutoring now?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to move marks, but only if the plan is narrow. In that window the work is not rebuilding a subject; it is finding the three or four topics where most marks are being lost, repairing those, and spending the rest of the time on how the paper is answered. The trial lesson looks at the student's last marked paper and says which of those two problems is dominant. If the gap is wide and spread across the whole syllabus, we say so rather than sell a block that cannot deliver.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IB home tutor to a flat in Deira or Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For families in the UAE every lesson is one to one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The URL you arrived on uses the phrase parents search for, and this page answers the in-home question honestly, including what the local market charges for a visit. The practical trade is proximity against specialism, and in a district split by the creek, specialism usually wins.

faqs.question: What does an in-home IB tutor charge around Deira and Dubai Festival City?
faqs.answer: Market figures, not ours. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors quote AED 200 to 500 once travel is included. In-home monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions appear in the same market. Online specialist rates published by others sit at AED 200 to 450, with TutorChase at AED 270. Ask any provider in writing whether travel is inside the quoted hour; the answer explains most of the gap.

faqs.question: How many weekly sessions does a DP2 student usually need in the run-in to the May session?
faqs.answer: Two or three a week in a single subject is typical for an intensive block, and one a week for maintenance in a subject that is already close to target. The constraint in Deira is rarely money and almost always evening hours: a student losing fifty minutes a day to the bridges has roughly twelve usable weekday evening hours for six subjects plus core. Adding sessions without removing something else produces a tired student and no gain, so the plan names what stops as well as what starts.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work to our school's own Internal Assessment deadlines rather than a generic plan?
faqs.answer: That is the starting point rather than an option. The first thing a tutor asks for is the school's assessment calendar, because Dubai schools set their own internal deadlines and they differ by weeks between institutions. The term plan is then written backwards from the nearest date on that sheet. It also tells us when a component has closed: once an IA has been submitted, no amount of tutoring changes that mark, and the hour is better spent on a paper that is still in play.

faqs.question: When should a Deira Diploma student start thinking seriously about the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most do. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words of independent research in one subject with three recorded reflective sessions, and in a Dubai school the final submission usually falls early in DP2, before the first mock window. Starting it in DP1 means the research question can be tested for feasibility while there is still time to change it. Starting it two months before submission means writing around whatever sources happen to be available, which is the most common reason a capable student lands a C.

faqs.question: Can a tutor review my daughter's Maths Exploration draft without breaching academic honesty?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, show an IB-published exemplar, ask whether a conclusion follows from the working, and point out where a section describes instead of analysing. A tutor may not write or rewrite any part of it, supply the research question as a finished product, or do the mathematics on the student's behalf. Feedback is given as questions about named criteria, which the student answers in her own file. That boundary keeps the mark valid and the Diploma safe.

faqs.question: What time can an online IB session realistically start for a family near Al Mamzar?
faqs.answer: For most Al Mamzar and Al Nahda households, after six works better than four thirty. The return leg from schools on the Bur Dubai side or in Oud Metha crosses the Sharjah-bound commuter flow, and a 4:30pm slot becomes a 4:50pm start on two days in five. Al Garhoud families, closer to Festival City, manage earlier slots more easily. Because delivery is online there is no tutor sitting in the same traffic, so the only variable is when the student is actually home and fed.

faqs.question: Do mock results at Dubai IB schools predict the final Diploma grade?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and in both directions. Mocks often sit below final grades because the syllabus may not be finished and because the student has not yet done the volume of timed past papers the final run-in produces. A comfortable mock is equally not a guarantee. The useful part of a mock is never the grade; it is the per-question mark breakdown, which shows whether marks went to missing content, misread command terms or poor timing. Those three need completely different work over the following weeks.

faqs.question: How do Ramadan hours change an IB revision plan for a fasting student in Old Dubai?
faqs.answer: Plan the term in two halves. Before Ramadan, front-load the demanding work: new content, the hardest topics, the IA analysis that needs long concentration. During Ramadan, move to shorter, later sessions after Iftar, favour past-paper technique over new material, and accept that two 45-minute blocks will achieve more than one 90-minute one in the late afternoon. For many Deira households the post-Iftar hour is the only genuinely quiet one, and booking it in advance is what keeps it.

faqs.question: Is a specialist HL Physics or HL Chemistry tutor available for a Deira student, or only general science tutors?
faqs.answer: Specialists, and that is the main reason delivery is online. A tutor who has to reach Hor Al Anz by five comes from a pool bounded by the afternoon traffic; a tutor joining over video comes from everyone free in that Gulf Standard Time slot. For HL sciences this matters because the investigation and the HL extension topics need someone who has taken that subject through moderation. If no HL specialist is free for the hour you want, we say so and offer an adjacent hour rather than substituting a generalist.

faqs.question: Which permit must a private tutor in Dubai hold under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by that resolution. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app and e-services. Never describe a tutor as KHDA approved, because KHDA does not approve individual tutors.

faqs.question: What happens to our booked sessions if the family travels out of Dubai during the winter break?
faqs.answer: The slot can follow the student, provided the adjusted hour is agreed in advance rather than improvised. This is one of the practical advantages of online delivery: a Deira family spending three weeks abroad can keep two sessions a week at a time that works in the new zone, or pause deliberately and resume on a stated date. What causes damage is leaving the break unplanned, because the weeks after it usually contain a mock window and arriving three weeks behind is difficult to recover.

faqs.question: Will an IB Diploma satisfy UAE Ministry of Education equivalency requirements?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is decided by the Ministry of Education, not by a tutoring provider, and the published numbers differ by curriculum. For the British track the requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. No IB points threshold is published here because we have not read one on moe.gov.ae. Verify your child's position with the Ministry directly.

The free trial lesson is a diagnostic: a specialist tutor works through two or three questions from that paper, locates where the marks are going, and tells you what the remaining weeks can realistically achieve. Lessons run one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school run. If the honest answer is that the window is too narrow for the target, you will hear that first.

intro.heading: The question behind the search, answered without flattery
paragraphs: The phrase an IB home tutor in DIFC gets typed into Google by a parent who has already worked out that the school is not going to provide what they need, and who assumes the next step is to find a competent person who lives nearby. That assumption is worth examining before any money is spent, because it is the part of the plan most likely to fail. DIFC is a financial district of towers and offices. It contains no school. The children who live here travel out every morning, and the adults who live here are overwhelmingly not Diploma subject teachers.

So the honest answer to is there anyone near me who knows this syllabus is: for Mathematics at Standard Level, probably. For History, Economics or Biology, possibly. For Chemistry at Higher Level, Physics at Higher Level, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, a less common language or any of the Diploma core components, the local pool shrinks to something close to nobody with the right combination of subject depth and availability at seven in the evening on a Tuesday.

That is not a sales argument, it is arithmetic. A Dubai IB school typically carries one or two teachers per Diploma subject, and those teachers are prohibited in some emirates from tutoring their own enrolled students and are in any case not available at scale. The people with genuine Higher Level depth in a narrow subject are scattered across the world. A family that insists on proximity is choosing from a pool of a few; a family that accepts live video is choosing from a pool of many, and the difference is not convenience, it is whether the person can teach the thing.

This page therefore takes the home-tutoring question seriously instead of sidestepping it. Below you will find what an in-home arrangement in DIFC actually involves in practice — building access, visitor passes, travel windows, the cancellation problem — what the market charges for it with each figure attributed, what the premium is really buying, and the permit rules that govern who may legally give private lessons in the UAE at all. There is also a subject-by-subject account of where availability is tight and what happens when it is.

The position is stated once and then not hidden. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson is delivered live online, one-to-one, over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The search phrase is a home tutor because that is what parents type, and the right response is to answer the question, show the comparison, and let a family decide with the numbers in front of them rather than pretend to sell something we do not.
