programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria rather than examination papers, with the Personal Project in MYP 5. Supply is easier here because the work is about reading descriptors and building habits rather than deep subject specialism, so a capable generalist can be genuinely effective.
programmes.countryNote: Several central Dubai schools run the full continuum, so a DIFC child may move from the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma without changing building. The practical consequence is that the family's first experience of scarce tutor supply arrives suddenly in DP1, having never been a problem before.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses combined with a career-related study and a separate core. A student takes the same papers and the same internal assessment as a Diploma candidate in the subjects they retain, so the tutoring need in those subjects is identical even though the qualification is not.
programmes.countryNote: A smaller number of Dubai schools offer this route, usually attached to business or engineering pathways. DIFC families sometimes find it after the full Diploma has proved too broad, and the relevant point for support is that the retained subjects' deadlines are still set by the school's IB coordinator.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-difc.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects DIFC families most often ask about, with a note on where local availability tends to be tight and why.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level includes Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper that rewards sustained reasoning rather than recall. Local availability for genuine Higher Level depth is the tightest of any subject in this district, and it is the commonest reason a DIFC family ends up looking beyond Dubai.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-led work, with its own Paper 3 at Higher Level. Easier to staff locally at Standard Level, considerably harder at Higher Level, and frequently confused with the Analysis route by families comparing tutor profiles.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The most mathematically dependent science. Higher Level students stall on the algebra rather than the physics, and a tutor who can diagnose that distinction in one session is a specialist rather than a generalist. Thin local supply at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two written papers plus a scientific investigation. Marks concentrate in energetics, equilibrium, acid-base calculation and the organic mechanisms. Higher Level availability within any one Dubai district is limited, which is the practical case for looking further afield.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, with marks lost mainly on command-term discipline rather than on knowledge. Easier to staff locally than the other two sciences, and a reasonable subject to start with if a family is testing whether tutoring helps at all.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three papers plus a portfolio of commentaries built on published news articles. The portfolio is where most marks are recovered, and it is work a tutor can support legitimately by questioning the diagram choice and the evaluation.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: An individual oral, a paper on unseen non-literary texts and, at Higher Level, an essay. The oral is the component students most often under-prepare, and rehearsing it is among the clearest returns available in the Diploma.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work, essay papers and a historical investigation. The investigation is marked internally and moderated, and the commonest failure is a question too broad to be answered in the word limit rather than weak knowledge.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay with a supervisor at school. A tutor may question the research question and give feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not research it, draft it or edit it to completion.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. The essay rewards a register most Diploma students have never been taught, and a small amount of focused support on argument structure goes a long way here.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-difc.regionsIntro: DIFC sits at the centre of a corridor of districts that share the same problem and the same answer. These are the neighbourhoods and what each actually offers a Diploma family.

regions.name: DIFC
regions.note: Offices, towers and residential blocks in the Gate District and around it. No school, strict building access for visitors, and an evening that starts late because every pupil commutes out of the district.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Immediately adjacent and equally campus-free. The same outward commute, the same late afternoon, and the same scarcity of Higher Level subject specialists living within a short drive.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Across the water, towers either side of the canal. Families here face the same supply question and often share bus routes with DIFC children to the creek-side and Al Barsha schools.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf and Culture Village
regions.note: Creek-side pockets, one with an IB continuum school. A short commute for a minority of students, which buys evening time but not access to a narrow subject specialist.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Two established schools inside the community, both drawing DIFC and Downtown families. The earliest afternoon finish in the corridor and the most common destination for Diploma students here.

regions.name: Meydan and Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Villa communities to the south-east with long runs in both directions. Diploma families here usually build the week around a weekend morning session rather than two weeknights.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Khail
regions.note: Mixed residential and industrial with several large schools nearby. A second direction DIFC buses turn, and a cluster that produces a high proportion of British-curriculum sixth-form students.

schoolClusters.city: Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf and the creek side
schoolClusters.note: The nearest cluster to DIFC and the most common destination. Between them these schools run the IB continuum and the Diploma after a British Year 11, which means two DIFC neighbours can be on quite different internal assessment calendars.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Quoz and Al Khail
schoolClusters.note: The second direction from DIFC, with several large schools offering the Diploma or International A Levels after Year 11. The afternoon return from here is the reason many DIFC Diploma sessions start at six rather than five.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: Reached along Al Wasl Road and Sheikh Zayed Road, a mix of IB continuum schools and British sixth forms. The slowest term-time return of the three directions out of the district.

sections.heading: How many people near DIFC can actually teach a Diploma subject
paragraphs: Begin with the supply side, because every other decision depends on it. A Dubai IB school typically carries one or two teachers per Diploma subject, sometimes a single teacher for a Higher Level course with a small cohort. Those teachers are employed full time, are not generally available for private work at scale, and in Abu Dhabi are barred by the regulator's professional-ethics rules from paid tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school. The MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction.

Strip those out and ask who else within a short drive of DIFC could teach Higher Level Chemistry to examination standard. Retired teachers, a small number of specialist freelancers, some university postgraduates, and a much larger group of capable general tutors who will offer the subject and discover its depth in the third session. That last group is the actual risk in this market, because their advertising is indistinguishable from a specialist's and the difference only becomes visible after a parent has paid for a month.

The table below is a qualitative map rather than a count, because nobody can publish a defensible headcount of subject specialists in a Dubai district and any page that does is inventing it. What it shows is the shape: broad subjects at Standard Level are staffable locally, narrow subjects at Higher Level are not, and the Diploma core sits somewhere in between because it needs academic judgement rather than subject depth.

Read the final column as the actual argument of this page. Online delivery does not make the lesson better by itself. It makes the choice of teacher better, by removing the geographic filter that was discarding the people who can do the job. For a Standard Level subject that filter costs a family little. For Higher Level Physics at seven o'clock on a weeknight it costs them the specialist entirely.

sections.heading: What an in-home arrangement in DIFC actually involves
paragraphs: It is worth being concrete about the thing parents are picturing, because the picture is usually a quiet hour at the dining table and the reality includes a good deal of friction specific to this district. DIFC towers run managed access. A visitor needs to be registered, met or issued a pass, and parking in the Gate District at six in the evening is not a trivial problem. None of that is insurmountable; all of it has to happen every single week, and it is work somebody in the household does.

Then there is the travel window. A tutor crossing the city in evening traffic to reach DIFC is committing ninety minutes of unpaid time around a sixty-minute lesson, and that cost is inside the rate whether or not it is itemised. It also makes the arrangement fragile. A lesson that depends on a car arriving through Sheikh Zayed Road traffic at 18:00 is a lesson that gets cancelled or shortened more often than a parent expects, and rescheduling a specialist is harder than rescheduling a generalist.

The comparison table sets both options against the things that actually differ for a DIFC household. The honest reading is that in-home visits buy presence in the room. For a young child, or a student who will not engage with a screen, presence can be worth paying for, and parents should not be told otherwise. For a Diploma student working on past papers and internal assessment drafts, presence changes nothing that gets written in the examination, while the travel premium and the fragility remain.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. The comparison is published here anyway, including the parts of it that favour an in-home arrangement, because a parent weighing AED 350 an hour against AED 250 an hour deserves to see what each actually includes rather than a one-sided case.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and what the in-home premium pays for
paragraphs: The published figures are worth setting out before any interpretation. Independent home tutors and agencies in Dubai quote in-home one-to-one work at AED 180 to 350 according to Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with home tutors going as high as AED 500. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits circulate in this market, against online packages advertised around AED 799 a month for eight sessions.

On the online side, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the generalist end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for a qualified subject tutor. TutorChase quotes AED 270 and Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Each figure belongs to the provider named beside it; none of them is an IB Gram price, and our own pricing is handled through a free trial lesson and a consultation rather than a public rate card.

Now the interpretation a DIFC parent actually needs. Subtract the online specialist band from the in-home band and the difference is roughly AED 100 to 150 an hour. That difference is not buying better teaching, because it is frequently the same calibre of teacher either way. It is buying a car journey across Dubai and the risk that the journey fails. For a Diploma student it is therefore the least productive money in the whole arrangement.

Where the premium does earn its keep is narrow and worth naming: a young child who cannot hold attention on a screen, a student with a specific need that benefits from physical presence, or a household where supervision rather than teaching is the actual requirement. Those are real cases. They are not the case of a DP2 student six weeks from a Higher Level paper, which is what most DIFC searches for a home tutor actually turn out to be.

sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to give private lessons in the UAE
paragraphs: This is the part of the market most pages skip, and it is the part a DIFC parent can actually verify. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. MoHRE's own service page for it is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any specific amount quoted to you — and figures do circulate — is unverified.

Two further rules matter in practice. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs an educational services permit from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority for a training institute. And in Abu Dhabi, the regulator's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Never arrange paid lessons with your child's own class teacher.

The practical version for a DIFC household is three questions. Does this person hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it? Are you charging me a fee for the permit, in which case what is it for, since the official route is free? And is the person teaching my child employed at my child's school? IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office.

sections.heading: The Diploma core: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, and where a tutor stops
paragraphs: The core is where DIFC families most often want help and where the boundary is tightest. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word piece of independent research supervised by a teacher at school. The Theory of Knowledge course produces an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. Both are assessed, both are substantial, and both must be the student's own work in a sense the IB defines precisely and enforces.

A tutor can do a great deal inside that boundary. On the Extended Essay: question whether a research question is answerable in four thousand words, point out that a methodology section describes nothing measurable, ask where the counter-argument is, and read a draft the student has written and say what a reader will not follow. On Theory of Knowledge: teach the register the essay rewards, which is argument with concession rather than assertion, and rehearse the exhibition commentary against the objects chosen.

What a tutor must not do is also precise. Not choose the research question. Not supply sources. Not write, draft, restructure by rewriting, or edit to completion. Not produce the knowledge claims for a Theory of Knowledge essay. Providers in this market do sell completed internal assessments and essays, at four-figure prices; buying one exposes the student to an academic-honesty investigation and the consequence falls on them, not on the seller.

Creativity, activity and service does not need tutoring and should not be sold as if it did. What occasionally helps is a conversation about evidencing it — what a reflection should contain and why a list of activities is not a reflection — and that is a single session, not a programme. Any provider offering a service around the core should be willing to put the no-writing boundary in writing before the work starts, and a reluctance to do so is the most useful piece of information a parent will get.
bullets: Extended Essay: question the research question, read the student's draft
Theory of Knowledge: teach argument with concession, rehearse the exhibition
Never: choosing a question, supplying sources, drafting, editing to completion
Creativity, activity and service needs reflection advice, not tutoring
Get the boundary in writing before any core work begins

sections.heading: Availability, and what happens when the specialist is not free
paragraphs: No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is strange given that every one of them has limits. A narrow Higher Level subject at a single weekday hour is a specific ask, and some weeks the answer is no. Saying so costs a booking and saves a family a wasted term, which is a trade worth making, and it is the easiest way for a parent to tell a serious provider from a confident one.

The honest set of options when a specialist is not available is small. Move the slot, which is usually the answer and usually works. Wait for a named tutor, where the wait is stated in days rather than implied. Take a different weekday. Or accept a short bridging arrangement with a generalist for the content that does not need specialism, on the explicit understanding that the Higher Level work waits. What should never happen is a general tutor presented as a specialist, which is the market's most common quiet failure.

This is also why the first lesson matters as a test. A specialist in a Diploma subject will, within forty minutes and with a marked paper in front of them, name a specific pattern of mark loss and the question types that expose it. A generalist will ask the student what they find difficult and build a plan from the answer. The difference is visible to a parent sitting in the room and does not require any subject knowledge to spot.

For a DIFC family the availability question has a timing dimension too. The usable window is narrow — most children here are home between four and five, and a Diploma student has homework as well — so a request is effectively for one or two specific hours rather than for any evening. Asking about availability at the hour you actually need, rather than in general, is the question that gets a useful answer.
bullets: A narrow Higher Level subject at one fixed hour is a real constraint
Options are a different slot, a stated wait, or a different weekday
A bridging generalist is acceptable only if labelled as one
Judge a specialist by whether the first lesson diagnoses anything

sections.heading: Equivalency and attestation for a family that may not stay
paragraphs: DIFC households move. A posting ends, a company relocates, and a Diploma that was going to be completed in Dubai is completed somewhere else or used to apply to a UAE university instead. That makes the Ministry of Education's equivalency process worth understanding early rather than discovering in the final year, and it is a topic almost nobody in this market covers at all.

The sourced position for the British track is specific: a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. At the post-16 stage the same route requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with at least 450 in SAT Mathematics.

For the IB there is no points threshold published in any source available here, so no figure should be taken from a tutoring page, including this one. Check the Ministry's own pages or the emirate's attestation authority before acting on anything you are told. Equivalency is also not a service a tutoring provider performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not a requirement for it — any suggestion otherwise is manufactured urgency about a regulatory process.

The practical planning point is unglamorous and it is the thing to act on. Keep the documents: statements of entry, certificates, transcripts, and the school's own records of internal assessment. Families who leave the UAE mid-Diploma and then need attestation two years later spend months reassembling paperwork that took five minutes to save. Ask the school's registrar what they will issue and when, before the move rather than after it.
bullets: British route: five subjects at grade 3 or E minimum, Arabic and Islamic education excluded
Post-16: one A Level at E, or two AS Levels at E
American route: IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61, or SAT 450 reading and writing, plus SAT Maths 450
No sourced IB points figure exists; verify with the Ministry
Collect certificates and transcripts before a relocation, not after

sections.heading: Getting started from DIFC, and the limits stated plainly
paragraphs: Send three documents before anything is booked: the most recent marked paper in the subject, the school's internal deadline calendar for the year, and the subject and level written exactly as the school records it. Those three let a tutor arrive at the first lesson with a hypothesis instead of a questionnaire, and they are the difference between a trial lesson that diagnoses and one that introduces.

Then book the free trial lesson at the hour you actually need rather than the hour that is easiest to offer. If the usable window in your household is 18:30 on a Tuesday, that is the slot to test, because availability at six on a Saturday tells you nothing about the term ahead. Use the lesson to judge one thing: did the tutor name a specific pattern in your child's work, or did they ask your child what they find hard?

After that the plan should be explicit about how many sessions go where — subject teaching, timed paper work, internal assessment or core components — and it should name an end point or a review date rather than running until somebody cancels. A reassessment after a marked mock is the honest checkpoint, and it should be allowed to conclude that the arrangement can stop.

The limits, once more and without softening. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are an India-only service, and every UAE lesson is live online, one-to-one, over video. No grade, score or improvement is promised by anyone here at any price. No accreditation, licence or partnership is held from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and none is implied. No part of a student's Extended Essay, internal assessment or coursework is written, drafted or edited to completion for them. And if the specialist you need is not free at the hour you need, you will be told.
bullets: Send the marked paper, the deadline calendar and the exact subject level
Test the trial lesson at the hour you genuinely need
Judge the tutor on whether they diagnosed or asked
Agree a review date rather than an open commitment

process.title: Say the subject and the level exactly
process.description: Higher Level and Standard Level are different courses with different papers, and Mathematics has two routes that are frequently confused when families compare tutors. Writing it as the school records it prevents the single most common mismatch between what is asked for and what is supplied.

process.title: Send a marked paper and the deadline calendar
process.description: One marked paper shows where the marks are actually going, and the school's internal deadline calendar shows what the term has to achieve. Together they let a tutor plan a sequence rather than start with general revision and adjust later.

process.title: Free trial lesson at your real hour
process.description: A full session with the specialist you would keep, booked at the time your household can actually sustain. The test is whether the tutor names a specific pattern of mark loss from the evidence, rather than asking the student what they find difficult.

process.title: Agree the split and a review date
process.description: The plan states how sessions divide between subject teaching, timed paper work and any core component, and sets a date to reassess, normally after the next marked mock. Arrangements with no review date tend to continue past the point of usefulness.

process.title: Hear the availability answer before committing
process.description: If the specialist for your subject and hour is not free, you are told the wait or offered a different slot. A bridging arrangement with a generalist is only ever offered as exactly that, labelled, and never described as specialist support.

whyPoints.title: The supply question answered, not dodged
whyPoints.description: This page says plainly that the local pool for Higher Level sciences and mathematics near DIFC is thin. That is the honest basis for choosing online delivery, and it is more useful to a parent than a claim that everything is available everywhere.

whyPoints.title: In-home compared fairly, including where it wins
whyPoints.description: The comparison table names the cases where physical presence is worth paying for — a younger child, a student who will not engage with a screen. A one-sided comparison is easy to write and easy for a parent to see through.

whyPoints.title: Rates attributed to whoever published them
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure carries the provider or rate table it came from, so it can be checked. Three of the six researched competitors in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: The permit rules set out in full
whyPoints.description: The resolution that created the private tuition permit, its two-year validity, the fact that it is free, who may apply, and the three questions a parent can ask to verify it. No fine amounts are quoted, because no schedule has been published.

whyPoints.title: A hard boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and internal assessment support is questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is researched, written or edited to completion, and that is agreed in writing before any core work begins.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: A narrow Higher Level subject at one fixed weekday hour is not always available. You are told the wait or offered another slot, rather than matched to a generalist described as a specialist and discovering it in week three.

faqs.question: Is there anybody in DIFC who actually teaches the IB Diploma syllabus?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics at Standard Level and the broader humanities, quite possibly. For Higher Level Chemistry, Physics or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, realistically no — DIFC has no school inside it, and the handful of people with genuine Higher Level depth in a narrow subject are not clustered in a financial district. School teachers are employed full time and are restricted from tutoring their own pupils. That is the honest arithmetic behind online delivery: it replaces a district-sized pool with a much larger one, which matters most precisely where the subject is narrowest.

faqs.question: What does an in-home tutor in Dubai charge, and what is the premium paying for?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one work at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits circulate in this market. Set against online specialist bands of roughly AED 200 to 450 — TutorChase at AED 270 — the difference is about AED 100 to 150 an hour. That difference buys a car journey across the city and the risk of it failing, not better teaching. All figures belong to the providers named.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IB home tutor to an apartment in DIFC?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson is delivered live online, one-to-one, over video, on Gulf Standard Time. The search phrase is a home tutor because that is what parents type, and the right response is to answer the question rather than imply something different. In a DIFC tower online delivery also removes the weekly business of visitor registration, passes and evening parking, which is not a small consideration in this district.

faqs.question: Who is legally allowed to give private lessons in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Anyone holding the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so treat any amount quoted to you as unverified.

faqs.question: Can I verify a tutor's private tuition permit myself?
faqs.answer: You can ask to see it, and you should. The permit is a document issued through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system, and a tutor holding one can show it without difficulty. Two warning signs are worth knowing: anyone charging you a fee for their permit is describing something other than the official route, which is free; and anyone quoting you a specific fine figure for tutoring without one is guessing, because no schedule has been published. Also ask whether the person is employed at your child's own school, which is a separate problem.

faqs.question: May a tutor help with the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary, yes, and the help can be substantial. A tutor may ask whether a research question is answerable in four thousand words, point out that a methodology describes nothing measurable, ask where the counter-argument is, and tell a student which parts of their own draft a reader will not follow. A tutor may not choose the question, supply sources, draft any section, or edit to completion. The supervisor at school remains the authority on the task. Ask for that boundary in writing before the work starts.

faqs.question: What can a tutor usefully do about Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Teach the register. The prescribed-title essay rewards argument that concedes and then answers, with knowledge claims examined rather than asserted, and most Diploma students have never been taught to write that way in any other subject. A tutor can also rehearse the exhibition commentary against the objects the student has chosen and ask whether each object does real work. What a tutor cannot do is generate the knowledge claims or write the essay. A small amount of focused support here has an unusually good return.

faqs.question: Does creativity, activity and service need tutoring at all?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should sell it as though it did. What occasionally helps is one conversation about evidence: what a reflection should contain, why a list of activities is not a reflection, and how to record something while it is happening rather than reconstructing it in the final term. That is a single session at most. If a provider offers a programme around this component, ask what they think is being assessed, because the answer will tell you whether they have read the requirements.

faqs.question: How many spare hours does a full Diploma student in DIFC actually have?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families assume. A DIFC student commutes out of the district and back, arriving home between four and five in term time, and then has school homework, internal assessment work and the core to fit in. Dubai schools also carry the emirate's mandatory subjects — Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies — within the timetable, so the school day itself leaves less subject study time than the course list implies. In practice two tutored hours a week is a real commitment, and three is usually displacing something that mattered.

faqs.question: What happens when the Higher Level subject we need has no tutor free?
faqs.answer: You are told, with the wait stated. The options are a different slot, which usually solves it; waiting a stated number of days for a named specialist; a different weekday; or a short bridging arrangement with a generalist for content that does not need specialism, labelled as exactly that. What should not happen is a general tutor presented as a specialist. No competitor researched in this market publishes any coverage limit at all, so asking the question directly is a fair test of whoever you are speaking to.

faqs.question: Our posting may end mid-Diploma. What should we plan for now?
faqs.answer: Two things. Documents first: ask the school's registrar what they will issue and when — statements of entry, transcripts, records of internal assessment — and collect them before a move rather than reassembling them from abroad two years later. Second, the subject choices. A Diploma is portable between IB schools, but Higher Level combinations and internal assessment progress are easier to carry if the receiving school teaches the same options. Ask the current coordinator which parts of the work transfer and which restart, in writing, early.

faqs.question: Does my child need Ministry of Education equivalency if they study the IB in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on what they do next, and it is a question for the Ministry rather than for a tutoring service. The sourced British-track requirements are five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. For the IB route no points threshold appears in any source available here, so do not act on a figure from any tutoring page. Equivalency is not something a tutor performs, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who lives in DIFC better than one teaching from another country?
faqs.answer: Only if they are the better teacher, which is a question about them rather than about where they sit. The Diploma syllabus is set internationally and is identical wherever it is taught, so residence adds nothing to subject knowledge. What does matter is the time zone: a tutor must be able to teach at a Gulf Standard Time hour that survives the DIFC school run, and some genuinely cannot. Ask about the hour rather than the address, and judge the first lesson on whether it diagnosed anything specific.

faqs.question: How do we build a weekly schedule that survives a DIFC commute?
faqs.answer: Start later than feels necessary and consolidate. Most DIFC students are home between four and five, and a session booked at 17:00 will be missed or rushed often enough to matter. A single 18:30 weeknight slot plus a longer weekend morning session is more robust than two squeezed weeknight hours, and the weekend session is where timed paper work belongs because the student is not exhausted. Hold the arrangement for a fortnight before judging it, then move the slot once rather than renegotiating weekly.

faqs.question: What should we send before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Three things, and nothing else is needed. The most recent marked paper or piece of internal assessment feedback, because that is where the actual pattern of mark loss is visible. The school's internal deadline calendar for the year, so the plan is built around real dates rather than assumptions. And the subject and level exactly as the school records it, since Higher Level and Standard Level are different courses and Mathematics has two routes that are easy to confuse. A tutor with those arrives with a hypothesis rather than a questionnaire.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-difc.closingHeading: Ask the supply question first, then book a trial lesson
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-difc.closingBody: The useful question for a DIFC family is not who is nearest but who can actually teach this course at the hour our evening allows. For a broad subject at Standard Level the local answer may be fine. For a Higher Level science or mathematics it usually is not, and that is the reason to look beyond the district rather than any claim about technology. Send the marked paper, the deadline calendar and the exact subject level, and book a free trial lesson at your real hour. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. No grade is promised and no accreditation is claimed.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-discovery-gardens.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors a Discovery Gardens family is matched with for Diploma work. Each is matched to a subject and level, and each works from the student's marked papers rather than from a syllabus checklist.

intro.heading: What is actually going wrong in the subject
paragraphs: Diploma grades slip for a small number of reasons and content ignorance is rarely the main one. The usual causes are specific: answering a command term with the wrong shape of response, treating an Internal Assessment as a writing task rather than a criteria-matching exercise, practising past papers without ever having one marked against the real scheme, and revising topics in isolation when the papers deliberately combine them. All four are diagnosable from one marked paper.

That is the premise of this page. Rather than describe tutoring in general, it sets out the assessment machinery of the Diploma: what each component actually rewards, which command terms require which structure, where Internal Assessment marks sit across the subject groups, and what proper past-paper work looks like as opposed to the version most students do alone. A parent who understands those can judge any tutor in about five minutes.

Discovery Gardens adds a practical dimension of its own. It is a high-density apartment community of 291 buildings laid out in themed districts, immediately north of Al Furjan and beside Ibn Battuta, with its own Route 2020 metro station. Almost nobody here has a spare study, which is why the common setup is a desk in a shared room with headphones. That works well for online sessions and poorly for a visiting tutor.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30; home visiting is a service we run only in India. The search phrase is still the right one to target because it is what parents type, but the honest answer belongs in the first screen rather than in a phone call three days later.

What online delivery buys a family here is specific to the problem this page describes. Proper syllabus work means a marked paper on screen, a mark scheme beside it, and both people looking at the same annotation. That is easier to do well over a shared screen than across a kitchen table, and it means the tutor is chosen for knowing the component rather than for living within a twenty-minute drive of Ibn Battuta.

One note on dates before the detail. UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session. We do not publish specific IB exam or results dates anywhere on this site, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date in front of a parent who acts on it is worse than none. Your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal deadline calendar, which is the document to request in September. With six subjects carrying six internal components, those deadlines cluster rather than spreading evenly across the year, and knowing where the cluster falls is worth more than any single session bought after it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-discovery-gardens.programmesIntro: The Diploma is one programme with several distinct assessment machines inside it. These are the parts a Discovery Gardens family will need to understand.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, the six subjects
programmes.description: Six subjects from different groups, usually three at Higher Level and three at Standard, each with external papers and an internally assessed component. The grade in each runs 1 to 7, and the Higher Level papers differ from Standard not only in content but in the length and structure of response expected. Command-term discipline is what separates students with similar knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Discovery Gardens travel out of the community for school, mostly to Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Al Khail, so they are home from about 16:30 and book sessions at 18:00 or later. Six subjects in one household also means prioritising: the useful choice is the subject where marked papers show a pattern, not the one the student dislikes most.

programmes.name: Internal Assessment, every subject
programmes.description: Each subject carries an internally assessed component, typically worth 20 to 30 per cent of the grade and marked in school against published criteria before moderation. The forms differ: a scientific investigation, a mathematical exploration, economics commentaries, an individual oral, a research project. What they share is that criteria compliance matters more than polish.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most Diploma marks are quietly lost in this community, because several deadlines land in the same weeks and students write to length rather than to criteria. One session per subject spent reading the criteria against a draft is worth more than three spent on content. Tutors give written feedback on the student's own work and write no part of any submission.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge comprises an exhibition commentary on three objects and an essay from prescribed titles. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words of supervised independent research in a chosen subject. Together they contribute the bonus points. Both are decided early: by the choice of objects and title, and by the research question respectively.
programmes.countryNote: Families here most often ask for core support late, when the Extended Essay is half written on a question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words. One early session interrogating the question costs an hour and prevents that. A tutor questions the question and gives feedback on the student's own drafts; the tutor does not write, outline or rewrite any part.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, before the Diploma
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria out of eight in every subject group, with published descriptors. The habits built here, stating a method, processing data, documenting a process, evaluating honestly, are precisely what Diploma Internal Assessments assume. A student who arrives in Diploma 1 without them meets four unfamiliar demands at once.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years students in Discovery Gardens are home earlier than Diploma students, often by 16:00, so a 16:30 session fits. This is the cheapest point at which to build the criteria habits the Diploma will later assume, and it is the stage families in this community most often skip before arriving with a Diploma 2 problem.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-discovery-gardens.subjectsIntro: What follows is what each commonly requested subject actually assesses, and where its marks are typically lost. This is the level of detail a tutor should be able to supply before you book anything.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, calculus and proof, with one paper sat without a calculator and, at Higher Level, Paper 3 worth twenty per cent as an extended investigation. Marks go to method shown and to notation; a correct answer lifted from a calculator with no working forfeits most of a multi-step question.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-led methods, with the graphic display calculator central. The specific trap is answering with a number where the question asks for interpretation in context: a gradient is not an answer until it is expressed as a rate of change in the units of the problem.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes with Paper 1 split into multiple choice and a data-based section, Paper 2 carrying extended response, and a scientific investigation worth twenty per cent. Uncertainty propagation and reading gradients from a line of best fit cost more marks across a cohort than any single theme.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Built around structure and reactivity with a data booklet provided in the exam. Energetics sign conventions, mechanism notation and chemical tests answered as a list rather than as observation plus conclusion are the three reliable losses, and all three are notational rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Organised around unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and continuity. The subject penalises imprecise language above all: naming a mechanism and a direction is required, and an answer stating that something increases earns nothing. Statistical treatment of data is reliably under-taught.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with diagram-led extended response and three Internal Assessment commentaries on published news articles. Students draw a correct diagram and then never refer to it in the analysis, which forfeits the marks the diagram was meant to earn.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers using tools such as break-even, investment appraisal and Ansoff, plus a Higher Level research project requiring a real organisation and primary data. Arranging organisational access takes longer than writing the project, which is why late starts fail here.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the Individual Oral linking a global issue to two texts, and at Higher Level a 1,200 to 1,500 word essay. Weak responses summarise the text; strong ones argue from how the text is constructed.

subjects.name: Language B: Arabic, French, Spanish
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and an individual oral from a visual stimulus. Dubai private schools must teach Arabic to all pupils under KHDA rules, in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. The trainable gaps are vocabulary breadth and speaking for the full duration without prompting.

subjects.name: Psychology and Geography
subjects.description: Both reward command-term precision and studies or case material used as evidence rather than recited. In psychology the standard loss is describing a study without using it to support an argument; in geography it is case studies with no specific detail attached.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word exhibition commentary on three objects and a 1,600-word essay from prescribed titles. Students fail by writing opinion essays. The marks go to the quality of the knowledge argument and to real, specific examples rather than general claims about science or history.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of supervised independent research in one subject. Failure is nearly always a research question too broad to answer in the word count, and the diagnosis takes one honest session months before the deadline rather than a rescue in the final term.

sections.heading: Command terms, and why they decide the grade
paragraphs: Every IB subject guide publishes a list of command terms and what each requires, and almost every Diploma student has read that list once and never used it. Yet it is the mechanism by which marks are awarded. A question beginning describe wants an account without reasons. Explain wants the reasons. Evaluate wants judgement supported by both sides. Compare wants similarities and differences. A knowledgeable answer in the wrong form earns a fraction of the marks available.

The reason this persists is that students are rarely marked on it. Classroom feedback often comments on content accuracy, and a student whose content is accurate concludes they are doing well. The paper then awards marks for a structure they never produced. Proper past-paper work, with annotation against the real scheme, exposes this in one session, which is why it is the first thing we look for in a marked paper.

The fix is mechanical and quick. Write an answer, mark it against the command, rewrite it once. Three cycles of that in a subject usually establishes the habit, after which the student reads a question and asks what shape is required before beginning. It is slower work for a tutor than talking through content, which is part of why many tutors avoid it and many students never meet it.

The table below sets out the common command terms and the typical error for each. It is worth printing and keeping beside past-paper work. Taken with the mark scheme for any paper your child has sat, it converts a vague sense of underperformance into a specific, fixable list.

sections.heading: Where the Internal Assessment marks sit in each subject
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component, typically worth somewhere between twenty and thirty per cent of the grade, marked in school against published criteria and then moderated. Most families know this in the abstract and underestimate it in practice. A student with six subjects is carrying six internal components, and in aggregate that is a very large share of the final points total.

The forms differ considerably, which is why generic advice about internal work is useless. The sciences require a scientific investigation. Mathematics requires an exploration marked on five criteria including personal engagement and reflection. Economics requires three commentaries on published articles. Languages require oral components. Business Management at Higher Level requires a research project on a real organisation with primary data.

What they share is that criteria compliance beats polish. In every case the published criteria name specific behaviours, and the student who addresses each strand deliberately outscores the student who writes well in general. This is the most common and most expensive misunderstanding in Diploma internal work: students treat these as writing tasks and are marked on them as evidence-matching exercises.

The practical consequence for a Discovery Gardens family is a sequencing one. Six internal deadlines do not arrive evenly; they cluster, usually between the autumn of Diploma 2 and the following winter. Asking the coordinator for the school's internal deadline calendar in September, and planning around the cluster rather than discovering it, is worth more than any individual session.

sections.heading: Past-paper work done properly, and the version that does nothing
paragraphs: Almost every Diploma student does past papers and most get far less from them than they should. The version that does nothing is familiar: the student works through a paper with the answers beside them, checks off what they got right, and feels reassured. No timing, no marking against a scheme, no record of what kind of error occurred. That builds recognition of question types and very little else, which is why students who have done many papers still plateau.

The version that works has four parts. The paper is attempted under timed conditions, in one sitting, without notes. It is then marked against the actual mark scheme, line by line, with marks awarded strictly. The errors are categorised by cause rather than by topic: command term, method not shown, misreading, arithmetic, timing. Then one or two of those categories are targeted before the next paper.

The categorisation step is what makes it diagnostic. A student who loses nine marks across a paper usually has two causes, not nine problems. Six marks lost to command-term errors and three to timing is an entirely different plan from six lost to a topic and three to arithmetic. Students cannot usually do this categorisation for themselves because they see the question they got wrong rather than the behaviour that caused it.

This is also where online delivery is genuinely better rather than merely adequate. A marked paper, a mark scheme and both people annotating the same screen is a cleaner setup than two people leaning over one sheet of paper. In a Discovery Gardens apartment, where the study space is often a desk in a shared room, it is also the more practical arrangement by some distance.
bullets: Timed, in one sitting, without notes, or it proves nothing
Marked strictly against the real scheme, not self-assessed

sections.heading: Studying in a Discovery Gardens apartment
paragraphs: Practical constraints shape outcomes more than most tutoring pages admit. Discovery Gardens is a high-density community of 291 buildings, predominantly studios and one and two bedroom apartments arranged in themed districts. A dedicated study is rare. Most Diploma students here work at a desk in a shared living space, or at the dining table, with family life continuing around them.

That has two consequences worth planning for. The first is noise, which is manageable: over-ear headphones with a microphone turn a shared room into a workable session space, and most families here already own them. The second is interruption, which needs a household agreement rather than equipment. A session that is treated as a timetabled lesson by everyone in the flat runs properly; one treated as homework does not.

It also makes a visiting tutor impractical in a way that has nothing to do with cost. Hosting an adult for an hour in a shared living space, in the evening, with other family members present, is a genuine imposition in a one or two bedroom apartment. Several families in this community cite that rather than price as the reason they stopped looking for someone to come to the home.

IB Gram does not visit homes anywhere in the UAE, so the question does not arise with us: every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30, and home visiting is a service we offer only in India. What the setup needs at your end is modest: a desk, headphones, the marked work to hand, and an hour nobody walks into.
bullets: Over-ear headphones with a microphone solve the noise problem

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, decided early
paragraphs: The two core components carry the bonus points and both are decided by choices made long before the writing. For the Extended Essay it is the research question: four thousand words is a narrow space, and a question too broad to answer in it produces an essay that surveys rather than argues. Students usually realise this at the halfway point, by which time months of reading have been organised around the wrong frame.

Diagnosing it takes one honest session. The test is whether the question can be answered, with evidence, inside the word count, and whether the student can state what the answer is likely to be. If they cannot, the question is a topic rather than a question. Narrowing it in Diploma 1 costs an hour; rebuilding the essay in Diploma 2 costs several and still scores lower than a well-framed question would have.

Theory of Knowledge has a parallel structure. The exhibition requires three objects linked to a prompt, and the essay requires a title chosen from prescribed options. In both cases the choice determines the ceiling, because some objects and some titles simply offer more room for a knowledge argument than others. Students who choose on interest alone frequently find they have nothing to argue by the third paragraph.

What a tutor can legitimately contribute here is questioning and feedback. Reading the criteria with the student, interrogating the question or the title, supplying real examples from their own subjects, and giving written feedback on the student's own drafts. What a tutor must never do is write, outline for completion, or supply content. At least one provider in this market sells completed essays; the malpractice exposure from that falls on the student.
bullets: The Extended Essay question sets the ceiling, not the writing
If the student cannot state a likely answer, it is a topic not a question

sections.heading: Mark-scheme traps by subject group
paragraphs: Each subject group has characteristic ways of losing marks that have nothing to do with understanding, and a tutor who knows the group can name them before seeing any work. In mathematics it is method not shown and loose notation: equals signs used as connectives, missing differentials, limits omitted from integrals, calculator answers presented bare. These feel unfair to students because the mathematics was correct, and they are among the fastest things to fix.

In the sciences it is uncertainty and graph handling, plus describing where explanation was required. Gradients read from plotted points rather than from a line of best fit, units misplaced, significant figures chosen by habit rather than justified by the uncertainty. In chemistry specifically, sign conventions in energetics and mechanism notation account for a large share of the gap between understanding and score.

In the humanities and social sciences it is evidence used as decoration. A psychology answer that describes a study without using it to support the argument, an economics answer with a correct diagram never referred to in the prose, a geography case study with no specific detail attached. The content is present and the marks are not, because the scheme awards the use of evidence rather than its presence.

In languages and literature it is summary in place of analysis. Paper 1 unseen analysis rewards explaining how a text creates its effect; students describe what the text says. The Individual Oral rewards a genuine global issue; students bring a theme. These are structural habits, and three marked attempts with rewriting usually changes them for good.

sections.heading: Why topic-by-topic revision underperforms on IB papers
paragraphs: Most Diploma students revise by topic because that is how the syllabus is printed and how the school taught it. The papers do not work that way. A physics question uses wave behaviour inside a fields context; a biology question needs statistics applied to an ecology scenario; an economics question requires a microeconomic diagram inside a macroeconomic argument. Students who revised the topics separately recognise the content and cannot assemble it.

What works better is revising the recurring ideas that cross topics, then practising whole questions that combine them. In the sciences those recurring ideas are energy, proportionality, graphical relationships and uncertainty. In mathematics they are function behaviour, rates of change and proof structure. In the humanities they are the command terms and the use of evidence. None of them belongs to a single unit.

The practical method is to work from marked papers rather than a syllabus checklist. A checklist produces coverage, which feels productive and tells you nothing about whether the student can answer a composite question. A marked paper shows exactly where assembly failed, and that is the information a revision plan should be built from. This is the difference between a plan and a timetable.

There is an exception worth stating. Where a marked paper shows genuine content gaps in a specific area, teach that area. The argument is not against content teaching but against content teaching as a default when the evidence points elsewhere, which is the commonest reason a term of tutoring produces no grade movement despite everyone working hard.
bullets: IB papers combine topics deliberately, so topic revision underprepares
Revise the recurring ideas, then practise composite questions
Build the plan from marked papers, not from a syllabus checklist
Teach content where the evidence shows a real gap, not by default

sections.heading: Delivery, limits, and what we will not do
paragraphs: IB Gram delivers one-to-one online across Discovery Gardens and the whole UAE. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the UAE. Those are limits rather than selling points, and stating them before a parent spends time on an enquiry is the only reasonable way to handle a page that targets a home-tutor search phrase.

On availability, the honest position is that Mathematics and the three sciences at Standard Level and Middle Years are usually matched within a few days, while Arabic B, Design Technology, Music and the smaller Higher Level options take longer. In January and February, when every Diploma 2 family in Dubai wants the same evening slots, everything takes longer. If we cannot cover a subject and slot, we say so rather than substituting a tutor one level below the student.

On internal work the boundary is fixed. Tutors read criteria with the student, question a research question or hypothesis, teach the technique the work requires, model how published work is structured, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts. Tutors do not write, rewrite, outline for completion, or supply content. Feedback is given in writing so a school asking what support was received gets an answer that holds up.

On materials and claims: we do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, and we cite and link official sources instead. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and claim none. We do not guarantee grades, and we do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence of current status.

process.title: Send a marked paper and name the component
process.description: Not the subject in general, but the paper or criterion where marks are going. Add the level and the earliest time your child is at the desk after school. Diploma students in Discovery Gardens travel out of the community, so 18:00 is the common starting point on a weekday.

process.title: We match a subject specialist and name them
process.description: You are told who will teach, at which level, and which components they have taught or marked, before any session. If the exact level cannot be matched we say so rather than offering someone a level below and letting the gap appear in week six.

process.title: Free trial built on the marked work
process.description: Bring the paper and ask what pattern connects the lost marks. A specialist answers at component level: command-term errors in extended response, uncertainty omitted throughout, a diagram never referenced in the prose. No payment is taken and there is no obligation afterwards.

process.title: Set up the session space once
process.description: A desk, over-ear headphones with a microphone, the marked work to hand, and an hour the household treats as a timetabled lesson. In a shared Discovery Gardens apartment that agreement matters more than the equipment, and it takes one conversation at the start.

process.title: Work from papers, categorised by cause
process.description: Timed papers, marked strictly against the real scheme, with errors grouped by command term, method, reading and timing rather than by topic. Two causes targeted before the next paper. This is what turns past-paper practice from familiarity into marks.

process.title: Get the internal deadline calendar in September
process.description: Six subjects means six internal components, and they cluster rather than spreading evenly. The coordinator holds the school's internal deadline calendar. Planning around the cluster, with criteria sessions scheduled before each draft, protects more marks than anything available later.

whyPoints.title: Command terms treated as the main event
whyPoints.description: A knowledgeable answer in the wrong form earns a fraction of the available marks, and most students are never marked on it. We look for that pattern in the first marked paper, because it is the fastest grade movement available in several subjects.

whyPoints.title: Internal Assessment as criteria matching
whyPoints.description: Internal components typically carry twenty to thirty per cent of a subject grade, and the marks go to criteria compliance rather than to writing quality. Students treat them as writing tasks. Reading the criteria against the draft is where the recoverable marks are.

whyPoints.title: Past papers marked, not just attempted
whyPoints.description: Unmarked practice builds recognition and little else. We run papers under timing, mark them strictly against the real scheme, and group the errors by cause, because nine lost marks usually come from two causes rather than nine problems.

whyPoints.title: Online suits the work and the apartment
whyPoints.description: A marked paper, a mark scheme and shared annotation on one screen is a better setup than two people over one sheet. In a Discovery Gardens apartment it is also far more practical than hosting a visiting tutor in a shared living space.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not the nearest available tutor
whyPoints.description: Delivering online means the tutor is chosen for knowing the component rather than for living near Ibn Battuta. For Higher Level subjects in this corridor, where local supply is thin, that is the difference between a specialist and a near miss.

whyPoints.title: Limits and boundaries stated upfront
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE, no UAE office, no written coursework, no reproduced mark schemes, no accreditation claims and no grade guarantees. Knowing the limits before you pay is worth more than a page implying there are none.

faqs.question: Will an IB tutor come to our apartment in Discovery Gardens?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video; home visiting is a service we run only in India. In a community of mostly one and two bedroom apartments that is often the preferred arrangement anyway, since hosting an adult for an hour in a shared living space in the evening is a real imposition. Several families here cite that rather than cost as the reason they stopped looking for a visiting tutor. What the online setup needs is a desk, headphones and the marked work to hand.

faqs.question: My child knows the content. Why is the mark still low?
faqs.answer: They are the instruction words at the start of every IB question, and the subject guides publish what each requires. Describe wants an account without reasons; explain wants the reasons; evaluate wants a judgement weighing both sides; compare and contrast wants similarities and differences together. A knowledgeable answer in the wrong form earns a fraction of the available marks. Most students have read the list once and are never marked on it, which is why it is the fastest grade movement available in several subjects.

faqs.question: How much of an IB subject grade comes from internal work?
faqs.answer: Typically twenty to thirty per cent, depending on the subject, marked in school against published criteria and then moderated. With six subjects a student is carrying six internal components, which in aggregate is a very large share of the final points total. The forms differ: a scientific investigation, a mathematical exploration, economics commentaries, oral components, a business research project. What they share is that criteria compliance matters more than polished writing.

faqs.question: Why does my child plateau despite doing lots of past papers?
faqs.answer: Because the papers are almost certainly not being marked. The common version is working through a paper with answers beside it, checking what was right, and feeling reassured, which builds recognition of question types and little else. The version that works is timed, in one sitting, without notes, then marked strictly against the real scheme, with errors grouped by cause: command term, method not shown, misreading, arithmetic, timing. Nine lost marks usually come from two causes, not nine topics.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment in any subject?
faqs.answer: Within a fixed boundary, yes, and it is where most recoverable marks are. A tutor may read the published criteria with the student strand by strand, question a research question or hypothesis until it works, teach the technique the component requires, show how published work is structured, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write, rewrite, outline for completion or supply content. Feedback is given in writing, so a school asking what help was received gets a clear answer.

faqs.question: What time can Diploma sessions run for a student living in Discovery Gardens?
faqs.answer: Usually 18:00 or later on weekdays. Diploma students here travel out of the community for school, mostly to Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Al Khail, so they are home from about 16:30 and often later with a Creativity, Activity, Service commitment or a fixture. Middle Years students are home earlier, often by 16:00, which makes a 16:30 start workable for them. Sessions run to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time, and a missed one moves to the next evening rather than the next week.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child's Extended Essay question will work?
faqs.answer: Ask them to state, in one sentence, what the answer is likely to be. If they cannot, it is a topic rather than a question, and four thousand words will produce a survey instead of an argument. Narrowing it in Diploma 1 costs about an hour; rebuilding an essay in Diploma 2 costs several sessions and still scores below a well-framed question. Students usually discover the problem at the halfway point, after months of reading has been organised around the wrong frame.

faqs.question: Why does topic-by-topic revision not work well for IB papers?
faqs.answer: Because the papers combine topics deliberately. A physics question uses wave behaviour inside a fields context, a biology question applies statistics to an ecology scenario, an economics question needs a microeconomic diagram inside a macroeconomic argument. A student who revised topics separately recognises all the content and cannot assemble it. Better to revise the recurring ideas that cross topics, energy, proportionality, graphs, command terms, evidence use, then practise whole composite questions and mark them.

faqs.question: What does a good first session look like with a new IB tutor?
faqs.answer: It starts with your child's marked work, not with a syllabus overview or a diagnostic quiz. Within twenty minutes the tutor should be naming a pattern: extended responses describing rather than explaining, method not shown in multi-step work, a diagram never referenced in the analysis, uncertainty omitted throughout. By the end there should be a stated number of sessions and a specific first target. A first session spent on introductions and a general plan has told you nothing.

faqs.question: Which subjects are hardest to find a Diploma specialist for in this corridor?
faqs.answer: Arabic B at Diploma level, Design Technology, Music and the smaller Higher Level options. Mathematics and the three sciences at Standard Level and Middle Years are usually matched within a few days. Availability tightens sharply in January and February, when every Diploma 2 household in Dubai is looking for the same Higher Level specialists in the same evening window. If we cannot cover your subject and slot we will say so rather than offering a tutor one level below your child.

faqs.question: How should a student revise in a shared apartment with family around?
faqs.answer: With over-ear headphones and a household agreement, in that order of cost and reverse order of importance. The equipment solves noise and most families here already own it. The agreement solves interruption, which equipment cannot: a session treated as a timetabled lesson by everyone in the flat runs properly, and one treated as homework does not. Discovery Gardens is predominantly studios and one or two bedroom apartments, so this is the normal setup rather than a compromise.

faqs.question: Does Theory of Knowledge really affect the final points?
faqs.answer: Yes. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute the bonus points, and both are decided by early choices. For Theory of Knowledge that means the three objects for the exhibition and the title chosen from the prescribed list, because some objects and titles simply allow more room for a knowledge argument than others. Students who choose on interest alone often find they have nothing left to argue by the third paragraph, and by then the choice is made.

faqs.question: My child's teacher says the content is fine. What else could be wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly the form of the answers. The classic pattern is accurate content assembled in the wrong structure: describing when the command asked for explanation, presenting evidence without using it to support an argument, drawing a correct economics diagram and never referring to it in the prose. Teachers often comment on accuracy, so a student with accurate content concludes they are doing well. The paper then awards marks for a structure they never produced. One marked paper exposes it.

faqs.question: Are IB exam dates published on this site?
faqs.answer: No. UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session and we write about that session, but we publish no specific IB exam or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date in front of a parent who acts on it is worse than no date. Your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal deadline calendar, including the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay deadlines, and that is the document worth requesting in September.

faqs.question: Can you supply past papers and mark schemes for us to work through?
faqs.answer: No, and nor should any tutor. We do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we cite and link official sources and work from what the school has issued to the student. Reproducing published board material is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure for the student. Ask the school what it can release, since most will provide papers relevant to the student's own entry.

faqs.question: Which single change moves an IB grade fastest?
faqs.answer: Having papers marked against the real scheme and the errors grouped by cause. It sounds procedural rather than transformative, and it is the step almost no student takes alone. It reveals whether the problem is command terms, method not shown, misreading, timing or genuine content gaps, and those need four different plans. Everything else on this page follows from knowing which of the five you are dealing with, which is why the free trial is built around a marked paper.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-discovery-gardens.closingHeading: Send one marked paper and we will tell you what is wrong

Send the subject, the level, the component where marks are going and the earliest time your child is at the desk. We will match a subject specialist, name them before the lesson, and run a free trial reading the paper against the mark scheme so you can hear exactly where the marks went. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address, and nothing is paid until you have judged the match.

intro.heading: Two products, one search phrase, very different prices
paragraphs: The phrase you typed describes two things. The first is a person who drives to your tower, parks, registers at a security desk, waits for a lift and teaches in your living room. The Dubai market prices that at AED 180 to 350 an hour according to Bestimate, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200 to 500, travel included, and monthly packages published at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. The second is one-to-one teaching delivered into your home over live video, which published rates put at AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor.

IB Gram sells the second one. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is stated in the second paragraph rather than buried, because the alternative is a family discovering it after a phone call. What we provide is the same hour of teaching, reaching the same apartment, with the paper, the criteria and the student's own draft shared on screen between tutor and student.

What makes the price difference unusually stark in Downtown Dubai is the access overhead, which is real and specific rather than a rhetorical device. This is a district of towers rather than villas. A visiting tutor registers with a security desk, some buildings require resident authorisation for each visit, visitor parking is limited or valet-only at several addresses, and the lift journey in a tall tower is not trivial at six in the evening. The exits off Sheikh Zayed Road into the Financial Centre Road and Boulevard approaches are among the slowest in the city at that hour, and during major Downtown events the approach roads are restricted outright.

None of that improves or degrades the teaching. It simply means that a meaningful share of what the in-home premium buys in this particular district is the logistics of arriving, and the premium is being paid every week. For a Diploma family that money has alternative uses inside the same subject, which is what the rest of this page is about: converting tutoring spend into the only unit that counts for a Diploma student, which is points.

That unit is the whole argument here. Six subjects graded 1 to 7 give 42, and the Extended Essay with Theory of Knowledge add up to three more through a published matrix, giving 45. The Diploma requires 24 points plus the core requirements. A family deciding where to spend should know which route to a point is cheapest, and the answer is reliably not the one most families buy. Confirm all structural detail with your school's Diploma coordinator, and note that no International Baccalaureate examination date appears here, because none in this project has been confirmed from the IB's own site.
