dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-downtown-dubai.programmesIntro: A Diploma spending decision depends on the stage and on which component is costing points. These are the four that matter in Downtown Dubai households.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Year One
programmes.description: The cheapest year to buy help in, because content taught properly now does not need re-teaching later and a mid-market rate covers it. It is also where the Extended Essay research question is chosen, which is the single most consequential decision in the core and the one most often made casually. A DP1 hour is worth more than a DP2 hour and costs less.
programmes.countryNote: Downtown and the central corridor feed campuses in several directions, from Sobha Hartland and Nad Al Sheba to Al Jaddaf and Al Quoz, running both the Diploma and A Level pathways. A DP1 cohort here commonly mixes students arriving from the Middle Years Programme and from IGCSE, with opposite weaknesses.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Year Two
programmes.description: Internal Assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and then the examinations, with the components colliding in the same weeks. Spending here should be concentrated into blocks timed to those deadlines rather than spread as a weekly retainer, which pays for quiet months and runs short in busy ones.
programmes.countryNote: Internal school deadlines arrive well before anything the International Baccalaureate sets and are what actually binds a term. Your Diploma coordinator publishes them, and a plan built from that list is materially cheaper than one built on a general assumption about when the year gets difficult.

programmes.name: The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: Up to three points from a published matrix combining the two grades, each awarded A to E. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34 across five criteria, with critical thinking carrying 12 of them. Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an exhibition and an essay. A grade E in either is a failing condition regardless of the subject total.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the cheapest points in the Diploma sit, and where Downtown families most often spend nothing. The step from a C to a B in the Extended Essay is usually a smaller piece of work than moving a Higher Level subject grade, and it is worth the same or more in the matrix.

programmes.name: Creativity, Activity, Service
programmes.description: Not graded and worth no points, but a completion requirement: the Diploma is not awarded without it. Worth naming on a cost page because it consumes time rather than money, and because the time it consumes is the time a Downtown student would otherwise spend on an Internal Assessment. Sequencing it early is free and saves a crowded DP2.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students often have rich activity portfolios already, through school and community commitments, and the administrative work of recording and reflecting on them is what gets left late. That is a scheduling problem rather than a tutoring one, and no tutoring budget should be spent on it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-downtown-dubai.subjectsIntro: A Diploma student has six subjects and a finite budget. These are the ones Downtown families most often ask about, with a note on whether tutoring them is usually good value.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Usually good value, because the weaknesses are specific and diagnosable. At Higher Level, Paper 3 structured problems are the least-practised component and respond quickly to short deliberate work. At Standard Level, the no-calculator paper exposes algebraic fluency that no amount of content revision addresses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Good value where the problem is technology use or interpretation rather than content. Marks go on producing a correct figure without saying what was entered or what the statistic means in context. That is a habit, which makes it cheap to fix relative to teaching a new topic.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Good value in fields and electricity, which are the costliest areas to repair and the ones an under-powered pre-16 route leaves thin. Poor value in mechanics for most students, which they largely met before 16 and can revise from past papers without paying a specialist rate for it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Good value if the diagnosis finds the earliest broken step rather than the latest topic. Chemistry has the longest chain of dependent calculations of the three sciences, so sessions on buffers for a student with hesitant mole handling are competent and wasted. Organic mechanisms also respond well to short, drawing-led work.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Often poor value for content and good value for command terms. The subject is high-volume and most students can read more; what they cannot do unaided is tell outline from describe from explain from evaluate, each of which has a different mark allocation and a different expected answer structure.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Reliably good value, because the marks sit in a template: diagram accuracy, an explained shift, a stated consequence and a judgement. At Higher Level, Paper 3 is quantitative and the most under-prepared component in the subject. A short block on structure usually produces more than a term of content work.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Mixed. Paper 1 guided analysis of an unseen text responds well to a method taught over a few sessions. The comparative essay and the Individual Oral improve more slowly, because they rest on reading habits rather than on a technique, and a family should expect a longer timescale there.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Good value on Paper 1, where source evaluation for origin, purpose, value and limitation follows a teachable structure that separates grades. The Higher Level regional option in Paper 3 is content-heavy and expensive to repair late, so it belongs in DP1 spending rather than DP2.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Good value in question technique. Students know their named studies and lose marks by describing them without linking to the question's demand, and by omitting the critical-thinking element in extended responses. Both are structural fixes rather than content gaps, which makes them cheap relative to their effect.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: The cheapest points in the Diploma and the component Downtown families most often leave unsupported. Marked out of 34, with critical thinking worth 12. Most lost marks trace to a research question too broad to answer in 4,000 words, which is a DP1 decision with DP2 consequences and costs one session to test properly.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through an exhibition of three objects with commentaries and an essay on a prescribed title, each marked out of 10. Good value for a short block, because students write abstractly about knowledge in general where the assessment rewards specific grounded examples and a visible line of argument.

subjects.name: Internal Assessments generally
subjects.description: The best value across the whole programme, whichever subject they sit in. A fifth to a third of a subject grade, produced over months with teacher feedback available and no clock running. Every mark lost there was available under near-perfect conditions, which makes it the cheapest place in any subject to buy points.

paragraphs: Here is the published market, every figure credited to the provider that published it and read in October 2026, none of it IB Gram's price list. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with travel inside the figure. Monthly in-home packages in this market are published at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits.

On the online side, budget and university-student tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International Baccalaureate from AED 200. Specialists across the International Baccalaureate, IGCSE and A Level run AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED publishing AED 650. Published monthly online packages include AED 799 for eight sessions.

Read across those two sets and the structural point becomes visible. The published in-home band substantially overlaps the specialist online band, which means a family paying an in-home rate is frequently paying specialist money for a tutor selected from whoever will travel to their tower. That is not a criticism of any individual; it is what happens when the selection pool is bounded by a drive. For a Higher Level Diploma subject, where the scarce thing is somebody who has taught that specific component, the bounded pool is the expensive part of the arrangement.

The sensible way to use these numbers is not to decide which product is better in general. It is to decide what you are buying. If your child genuinely will not engage with a screen, the in-home premium is buying something real and you should pay it. If the requirement is a Higher Level physics specialist or somebody who has marked an Extended Essay to the criteria, the premium is buying travel, and the same money spent online buys a wider selection plus the ability to add sessions in the weeks before a deadline.

sections.heading: Why the access overhead is larger here than in most districts
paragraphs: This is not atmosphere, it is a cost component, and in Downtown Dubai it is unusually large. The district is towers rather than villas. A visiting tutor has to reach the building, find somewhere to leave a vehicle, register at a security desk, in some buildings be authorised by the resident for that specific visit, and then travel up a tall tower at the busiest hour of its day. Each of those steps is small and the sum of them is not.

The approach is the first part. The exits off Sheikh Zayed Road onto the Financial Centre Road and the Boulevard approaches are among the slowest in the city between five and seven, and Dubai Mall traffic runs into them. During major Downtown events the approach roads are restricted outright, which in practice means a cancelled or relocated session rather than a late one. A family with a fixed weekly in-person appointment in this district will lose or move several of them a year for reasons nobody controls.

The second part is the building. Visitor parking in Downtown towers is limited, and at several addresses the practical option is valet, which adds both time and cost. Security registration varies by building and can require the resident to be present or to have pre-authorised the visit. Lift waiting in a fully occupied tower at six in the evening is genuinely several minutes. None of this is exotic; it is simply the ordinary texture of visiting a Downtown apartment on a weekday evening.

The honest conclusion is narrow. These overheads do not make in-home tutoring bad. They make the travel share of an in-home rate larger in this district than in a villa community, which matters because a family paying AED 350 an hour is entitled to know what proportion of it is teaching. An online session has none of these overheads, starts at the stated minute, and can be moved to a different evening without anybody rearranging a route across the city.

sections.heading: Cost per Diploma point, by route
paragraphs: This is the table that should govern a Diploma spending decision and that nobody publishes. Six subjects graded 1 to 7 give 42 points, and the Extended Essay with Theory of Knowledge add up to three more through a published matrix, giving 45. The Diploma requires 24 points plus the core requirements, and a grade E in either core component is a failing condition. So a point is a point, whichever component it comes from, and the components cost wildly different amounts to move.

The cheapest routes are the core and the Internal Assessments, and the reason is the same in both cases: the work is produced over months with feedback available and no clock running, and the criteria are published. A student who has never read the Extended Essay criteria is unlikely to be writing to them. Reading them with a tutor for a few sessions, testing the research question and attacking the critical-thinking criterion is a small, cheap, bounded intervention, and the matrix pays up to three points for it.

The most expensive route is moving a Higher Level subject grade late. Grade boundaries at the top of a Higher Level subject are narrow precisely because the cohort is strong, and the work required is specialist, at AED 200 to 450 an hour or more, over a sustained period. It is sometimes the right purchase, particularly when a university offer rests on a specific subject grade. It is rarely the cheapest available point, which is a different question from whether it is necessary.

The table also contains the route families most often buy, which is weekly general support across several subjects. That route produces a reassuring arrangement and the vaguest relationship to points of anything on the list, because the hours are distributed by anxiety rather than by where marks sit. Nothing on this page argues against spending on tutoring. It argues for spending it in the order the table suggests rather than the order worry suggests.

sections.heading: Six subjects, one budget: the portfolio decision
paragraphs: A Diploma student has six subjects and a family has one budget, which makes this a portfolio problem rather than a subject problem. The most common and most expensive error in DP2 is tutoring five subjects eight weeks before the examinations, because the hours available per subject fall below the level at which anything changes. A student tutored in five subjects eight weeks out is being tutored in none of them.

Choosing which two takes evidence rather than instinct, and the evidence is in marked scripts. Marks sitting close to a grade boundary are cheap to move; marks a band away are not. A subject where the losses are concentrated in method, command terms and timing is cheap; a subject where whole questions are unanswered is not. Those two tests, applied to two or three marked papers, settle the portfolio question in half an hour at a kitchen table and cost nothing.

The second portfolio insight is that the core belongs in the budget alongside the subjects, not outside it. Three points is the difference between a 38 and a 41, which is frequently the difference between two university offers. Yet the core is treated as administrative, supervised by the school, and funded by nobody. Putting a four-session Extended Essay block into the same budget as a subject block is the single most common improvement we suggest to Downtown families.

The third is that Internal Assessments cut across all six subjects and are all produced in favourable conditions. A family that does nothing else should make sure every Internal Assessment is written against its published criteria, because those marks are available with feedback and no time pressure. The table above ranks this high for exactly that reason, and it is uncomfortable to notice how often the hours go instead into examination revision for a component worth less.

sections.heading: What the in-home premium buys, honestly assessed
paragraphs: It would be easy to write this section as an argument. It is more useful as an inventory, because some of what the premium buys is real and a family deciding between products deserves to see both columns rather than one. The published premium, on Dubai figures read in October 2026, is the gap between AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel included.

What it genuinely buys: a person in the room, which matters for a student who will not engage with a screen and for a family that wants visible adult presence during a session. A fixed physical appointment, which some households find easier to protect than a video call. No dependence on a connection. And for a younger sibling in the same house, a single visit can sometimes serve two students consecutively, which changes the arithmetic materially.

What it does not buy: a wider selection of tutors, because the pool is bounded by who will drive to your address. Flexible rescheduling, because moving a session means moving a route across the city. The ability to double the hours for the eight weeks before an assessment and then stop, which is the shape most Diploma families actually need. And in Downtown specifically, it does not buy punctuality, because the approach roads and the tower access are outside anybody's control at six in the evening.

Set against that, what the online format buys is specific and short: the whole tutor pool rather than the drivable subset, sessions that start at the stated minute, hours that flex up and down with the deadline calendar, and a shared screen on which a paper, a mark scheme and a draft can sit side by side. For Internal Assessment and Extended Essay work, where the document is the subject of the session, that last point is a practical advantage rather than a consolation.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of a Downtown household
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means little in isolation, so here is some context from the emirate's own numbers. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment and the UK curriculum for 37%. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after enrolment rose 6% during 2025-26.

On fees, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. For a Downtown family already committed to private fees, a frozen year is the moment a defined tutoring block becomes affordable without a new conversation about the household budget.

The relevant comparison inside that is between a defined block and an open arrangement. Four to six sessions on an Extended Essay, at published qualified rates of AED 150 to 300 an hour, is a bounded, one-off number that a family can decide on in an evening. A weekly in-home arrangement at AED 350 an hour across a Diploma year is a different order of commitment, and it is usually entered into without the total ever being written down.

So write it down. Multiply the rate by the session length, by the number of weeks, by the number of subjects, and look at the figure. Then compare it to the table earlier on this page, which ranks routes to a Diploma point by cost. Families who do that arithmetic almost always rearrange their spending, usually towards the core and the Internal Assessments and away from broad weekly support. That is the single most useful thing this page can produce.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, the permit question and our status
paragraphs: A page about money has to cover the things that should not be bought at any price. Research for this project found a provider selling completed Internal Assessments outright at a published figure. That is not tutoring. It is an academic-integrity breach that triggers malpractice proceedings against the student rather than the seller, and a family buying it is paying for a risk to their child's entire Diploma.

The legitimate boundary is easy to apply. A tutor may teach content, explain assessment criteria, model how a question type is answered, discuss a student's own research question, point out where an argument is missing, mark the student's own draft against published criteria, and coach planning and revision. A workable test is whether your child's own school supervisor could do the same thing openly in a scheduled meeting.

A tutor may not write, draft or complete any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or exhibition commentary, dictate sentences for transcription, or edit text until the words stop being the student's. Nor may anybody legitimately distribute International Baccalaureate subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary documents as downloads, because those are the IB's copyright. We reference them and link to the official source.

On status and on the law: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, and claims none of those relationships. We run no office, centre or branch in Downtown Dubai or anywhere in the UAE. Private tutoring here is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule.

sections.heading: Booking, and the arithmetic we will do with you
paragraphs: Send the subject, the level, the component, and whichever of these you have: a marked script, a draft Internal Assessment, or the Extended Essay research question. That last one is often the most valuable document in a DP1 household, because a question too broad to answer in 4,000 words caps the whole essay and the fix takes one session.

The first session is free and is spent on that real material with the student working. You then get a short written note: the component, the criterion or the cause of the lost marks, the smallest effective block, and a session count. We do not quote an hour count before that, because a figure produced before anybody has seen the evidence is invented, and it is usually invented upward. If the answer is four sessions on the Extended Essay rather than a term of physics, the note will say that.

We will also, if you want it, do the arithmetic with you: rate times session length times weeks times subjects, set against the routes-to-a-point table on this page. It is a five-minute exercise and it changes most families' plans, usually towards the core and the Internal Assessments. We do it knowing it frequently reduces the size of the booking, because a family that spends well comes back and a family that spends badly does not.

Two practical limits. Higher Level specialists for a specific weekend hour are among the thinner combinations we staff, and we will give you a date rather than take a booking and hope. And if no UAE-based tutor is free for your combination, we will say whether a tutor based elsewhere can cover your hour in Gulf Standard Time, and you may decline. IB Gram runs no home visits in Dubai; every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, and during Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar slots for families who want them there.

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Downtown Dubai cost?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai in-home band, read in October 2026, is AED 180 to 350 an hour from Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, with travel inside the figure, plus monthly in-home packages published at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Qualified one-to-one online subject tutors are published at AED 150 to 300, and specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Those bands overlap heavily, which means price is rarely the honest deciding factor. None of these figures is IB Gram's price.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to apartments in Downtown Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the paper, the published criteria and the student's own draft shared on screen between tutor and student. We state this before any booking rather than after a call, because the phrase families search is the phrase families search and you deserve to know what arrives. The exchange is a wider tutor pool and sessions that start at the stated minute.

faqs.question: Why is the travel premium larger in Downtown than elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Because the district is towers rather than villas and the access steps add up. A visiting tutor negotiates the approach off Sheikh Zayed Road, which is among the slowest in the city between five and seven, finds limited or valet-only visitor parking, registers at a security desk that in some buildings requires resident authorisation per visit, and then waits for a lift in a fully occupied tall tower at its busiest hour. During major Downtown events the approach roads are restricted outright, which means a moved session rather than a late one.

faqs.question: What does the in-home premium genuinely buy?
faqs.answer: Four real things. A person in the room, which matters for a student who will not engage with a screen. A fixed physical appointment, which some households protect more easily than a video call. Independence from a connection. And, where two siblings are in the same house, one visit can sometimes serve both consecutively, which changes the arithmetic materially. What it does not buy is a wider tutor pool, flexible rescheduling, or the ability to double hours for eight weeks before a deadline and then stop.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to gain a Diploma point?
faqs.answer: Almost always the core. Up to three points sit in the published matrix combining the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge grades, the Extended Essay is marked out of 34 with critical thinking carrying 12 of those marks, and both components are produced over months with feedback available and no clock running. A step from a C to a B in the Extended Essay is usually a smaller piece of work than moving a Higher Level subject grade, and it is worth the same or more. Most families spend nothing here.

faqs.question: Why is an Internal Assessment such good value to support?
faqs.answer: Because it is worth a fifth to a third of a subject grade and is produced under near-perfect conditions: months of time, teacher feedback available, published criteria, and no examination clock. Every mark lost there was available in ideal circumstances and was given away. A student who has never read the criteria for their own Internal Assessment is unlikely to be writing to them, and four to six sessions reading them, testing the framing and strengthening the evaluation is a bounded, cheap, measurable intervention.

faqs.question: Should we tutor all six Diploma subjects before the exams?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most expensive common error in the second Diploma year. Hours split across five or six subjects fall below the level at which anything changes, so a student tutored in five subjects eight weeks out is effectively tutored in none. Choose two, using marked scripts: fund the subjects where marks sit within a few of a boundary and where losses are concentrated in method, command terms and timing rather than in whole unanswered questions.

faqs.question: How do I decide which two subjects to fund?
faqs.answer: Two tests, applied to two or three marked papers at a kitchen table. First, distance to the boundary: marks within a few of the next grade are cheap to move, a band away is a term of work. Second, cause of the lost marks: concentrated in method, working, command terms and timing means a technique block of four to six sessions, whereas whole unanswered questions mean a content gap and a longer, costlier plan. Half an hour with the scripts settles it and costs nothing.

faqs.question: Is moving a Higher Level grade worth paying specialist rates for?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and necessity is a different question from efficiency. If a university offer rests on a specific Higher Level subject grade, fund it even at the published specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour or more, because no other point substitutes for that one. If the goal is a higher total rather than a named grade, it is rarely the cheapest available point: boundaries near the top of a Higher Level subject are narrow because the cohort is strong, and the work is sustained rather than short.

faqs.question: What should we write down before agreeing to weekly tutoring?
faqs.answer: The total. Rate, times session length, times number of weeks, times number of subjects. Most families never produce that figure, which is how a weekly in-home arrangement at the top of the published band becomes a commitment nobody consciously made. Then compare it against the routes-to-a-point ranking: core work and Internal Assessment coaching at the cheap end, a two-subject technique block next, and moving a Higher Level grade late at the expensive end. Most plans get rearranged after that exercise.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school fee freeze affect this decision?
faqs.answer: It makes a defined block easier to fund. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. For a household already committed to private fees, a frozen year is a reasonable moment to pay for a bounded Extended Essay or Internal Assessment block, and a poor moment to start an open-ended weekly arrangement.

faqs.question: Which Diploma components do Downtown families most often leave unfunded?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, almost without exception, followed by the Internal Assessments. All three are supervised by the school, produced over months, and treated as administration rather than as marks. Together they represent the cheapest points available anywhere in the programme: three from the core matrix, plus a fifth to a third of each subject grade from the Internal Assessments. Meanwhile the hours go into examination revision for components with less available upside per dirham.

faqs.question: How far can paid help on an Extended Essay legitimately go?
faqs.answer: Yes, within firm limits. A tutor may explain the criteria, test whether the research question can be answered within 4,000 words, discuss the student's own argument, point out where an essay reports rather than evaluates, and mark the student's own draft against the published criteria. A tutor may not write, restructure the prose, or supply the argument that the critical-thinking criterion exists to reward. The school holds the supervisor, the student declares authenticity, and a breach is a malpractice finding against your child.

faqs.question: When should Downtown Diploma sessions run?
faqs.answer: Most families in this corridor settle on 17:30 or 18:00 on a weekday, with Extended Essay and Internal Assessment work moving to weekend mornings, which suits sustained writing better than an evening after a full school day. Students travel outward to campuses in several directions, from the creek corridor to Nad Al Sheba, so arrival times vary more than the distances suggest. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar slots for families who want them there, with the same tutor keeping the same student.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot staff the subject and slot we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a date, rather than taking the booking and hoping. Higher Level specialists for a specific weekend hour are among the thinner combinations we staff, and demand concentrates in the second term when Internal Assessment deadlines arrive together across subjects. If no UAE-based tutor is free for your combination, we will say whether a tutor based elsewhere can cover your hour in Gulf Standard Time, and you are free to decline. No competitor researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

intro.heading: Academic City, the neighbourhoods either side of it, and the same answer in all of them
paragraphs: Dubai International Academic City is a planned education free zone off Al Ain Road, built around university branch campuses rather than around schools. Families living in and beside it — in Dubai Silicon Oasis, Academic City's own residential blocks, Al Warqa, Nad Al Hamar and International City — share a problem that families in Jumeirah do not have. The IB schools they use are not next door. Dubai English Speaking College sits inside Academic City itself but runs the British route to IGCSE and A Level. The nearest IB Diploma provision is a drive away: GEMS Wellington Academy in Silicon Oasis, Uptown International School in Mirdif, GEMS Modern Academy and North London Collegiate School in Nad Al Sheba, Universal American School in Al Warqa.

That geography shapes what a search for an IB home tutor in this area actually returns. A tutor who lives in Academic City and happens to teach Diploma Chemistry is a coincidence, not a market. The pool of adults within a 20-minute drive who can teach Chemistry HL to a May candidate, and who hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is small enough to count. Parents discover this the slow way, after three WhatsApp enquiries and one tutor who turns out to teach GCSE Combined Science.

So this page is written as a comparison. Academic City against Silicon Oasis. Silicon Oasis against Mirdif. Mirdif against International City. Four neighbourhoods, four school catchments, four different drive times — and one answer, because the constraint is not distance. The constraint is how many Diploma subject specialists exist in Dubai at all, and a car does not change that number. Online delivery does, by making every specialist in the network reachable from every one of those four neighbourhoods on the same terms.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. We say that plainly here because the phrase you searched is the phrase parents use, and pretending otherwise would waste your evening. What we do instead is one-to-one tuition over live video, at a time that fits after the school run, with the tutor picked for the subject and level rather than for living near Dragon Mart.

Below you will find what in-home tutoring genuinely costs in this market, attributed to the providers publishing those rates; what the drive premium buys and what it does not; the Diploma year counted backwards from the May session; what KHDA inspects and what it does not; where the line sits between coaching an Internal Assessment and writing one; and what Ministry of Education equivalency asks of an IB graduate heading to a UAE university. Nothing here is a sales pitch dressed as information.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-academic-ci.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and Academic City families often start in one programme and finish in another because their school changes or their commute does. These are the three stages tutoring is actually requested for, with what each means for a family living behind the university campuses.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external exams. Learning is organised into transdisciplinary units of inquiry, and reporting is against learner-profile attributes and approaches to learning rather than subject percentages. Tutoring at this stage is mostly about the two things the PYP does not drill: number fluency and written fluency in English. A child who cannot recall multiplication facts under time pressure will meet that gap again in MYP mathematics, and the gap is cheaper to close at nine than at fourteen.
programmes.countryNote: Universal American School in Al Warqa and Uptown International School in Mirdif both run the PYP within reach of Academic City, and both report in the IB's own language. Parents moving in from a CBSE or British primary are often startled by a report with no marks on it. A tutor's first job for an Academic City family is usually translation: what the report says, what it does not say, and which specific skill to work on this term.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP subjects are graded 1-8 against four criteria, each with published strands and a maximum of eight marks. In sciences the criteria are Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science. Marks are lost on criteria B and C far more often than on A, because students who know the content still design weak investigations and process data without evaluating it. That is diagnosable work, and it is what MYP tutoring should be about.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma step is the one that bites in this part of Dubai. A student finishing MYP 5 at Uptown International School or Universal American School moves into a Diploma year where Mathematics AA HL assumes algebraic fluency the MYP never tested under exam conditions. Families who book tutoring in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 spend far less than those who book it in the February of DP1.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked by the school and moderated by the IB. The Diploma is scored out of 45, with up to three points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. HL papers are longer, carry more content and include components SL candidates do not sit at all.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates near Academic City sit the May session, which is the session UAE schools use. The practical consequence for a family here is that the crunch is not May. It is the January and February window when four Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay final draft and the TOK essay all land within a few weeks of each other, in the same term as mock exams. That is when tutoring demand in Dubai peaks and availability is tightest.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study and a core of personal and professional skills, service learning, a reflective project and language development. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and is sometimes the right route for a student who wants Diploma-level depth in two subjects without carrying six. Tutoring requests for CP students almost always concern the Diploma courses inside it.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision near Academic City is thin, and most families asking about it are comparing it against the British route available at Dubai English Speaking College on their doorstep. If your child is weighing CP against A Levels, the question to put to the school is which specific university courses in the UAE and abroad accept the CP certificate for the subject they want, and get the answer in writing before Year 12 begins.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-academic-ci.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Academic City and Silicon Oasis families request most. The description for each names what the assessment actually tests and where marks go missing, because that is what a tutor has to fix rather than the syllabus title.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic manipulation, calculus and proof. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers, vectors and far heavier integration. Marks are lost on method presentation: a correct answer with no working scores a fraction of the marks available, and students trained on calculator-first methods lose the analytic ones.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-based problem solving. The common failure is interpretation, not computation — a student finds the regression line and then cannot say what the gradient means in context. HL adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical inference.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is multiple choice and short response, Paper 2 extended response, Paper 3 experimental and option material. Students lose marks explaining phenomena in everyday language rather than with the defined quantity, and on uncertainty treatment in the Internal Assessment, which is where most IA marks are quietly forfeited.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics, equilibrium and acids and bases carry the heaviest mark loads. The recurring problem is mechanism drawing: curly arrows from the wrong origin, missing lone pairs, no charges shown. HL adds further organic synthesis routes and more quantitative equilibrium work.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the grade. 'Outline' and 'explain' earn different mark allocations and students answer both as 'describe'. Data-based questions in Paper 2 reward reading the axes and the error bars before writing anything, a habit that is teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams must be labelled, titled and referred to in the prose to score. HL adds calculation-heavy Paper 3. The Internal Assessment is three commentaries on recent news articles, each 800 words, and most mark loss is in the evaluation paragraph rather than the theory.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The toolkit — Ansoff, SWOT, decision trees, break-even — is applied, not described. Case-study papers reward candidates who use the stimulus material's own numbers. HL candidates sit an additional paper based on pre-released stimulus material issued ahead of the session.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis on unseen non-literary extracts, a comparative essay, the Individual Oral on a global issue, and for HL the HL Essay of 1,200-1,500 words. Marks are lost on the global issue being too broad — 'inequality' is not a global issue, a specific manifestation of it is.

subjects.name: Mathematics for the MYP transition
subjects.description: A short, targeted programme covering the algebra, indices, surds and function notation that Diploma Mathematics assumes on day one. Most students arriving from MYP 5 can do these operations slowly; the Diploma expects them automatic, and the gap only shows up under timed conditions in DP1.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition in DP1 and the 1,600-word essay in DP2, scored together with the Extended Essay for up to three Diploma points. The exhibition fails when the three objects are illustrations of the prompt rather than evidence for a claim about knowledge. Tutoring is Socratic questioning on the student's own objects and drafts.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A supervised independent research essay in one subject, assessed on focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation and engagement. Most failures are structural and early: a research question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words, or no method at all. A tutor interrogates the question, never writes the essay.

subjects.name: Chemistry and Physics Internal Assessment coaching
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is a single piece of work worth a fifth of the subject grade. Coaching covers research-question framing, control of variables, uncertainty propagation and the evaluation section, all on the student's own data. The student designs, measures, writes; the tutor questions and gives feedback.

Here is what each of those neighbourhoods actually looks like for an IB family, and what changes between them.

regions.note: Villa and low-rise, with Uptown International School running the full IB continuum and Star International School Mirdif on the British route. Mirdif families have the shortest IB school run of the four and still face the same specialist shortage at HL.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in Dubai International Academic City is actually asking
paragraphs: It is asking two questions at once, and they have different answers. The first is 'can my child get one-to-one IB help without me driving anywhere', and the answer is yes. The second is 'will a qualified IB Diploma tutor physically come to my flat in Academic City', and the honest answer from IB Gram is no — we deliver one-to-one lessons live online and reserve home visits for our India service. Saying so in the first eighty words is more useful than burying it.

The reason the first question matters more than the second is the Academic City map. This is a free zone built around university campuses, with one British-curriculum secondary inside it. The IB Diploma schools its families use are in Silicon Oasis, Mirdif, Nad Al Sheba, Al Warqa and Al Garhoud. A tutor who lives within a short drive of your building is not thereby a tutor who lives within a short drive of an IB school, and the two facts have almost nothing to do with each other.

What a parent in this district is really optimising is the gap between the school bus arriving and bedtime. That gap is roughly three hours on a weekday, and an in-home session consumes between twenty and fifty minutes of it in travel at each end — the tutor's travel, which you pay for, and the dead time around it, which you absorb. An online session starts when the laptop opens. For a family doing two sessions a week across a Diploma year, that difference compounds into something like forty hours.

So the rest of this page treats the question as a comparison rather than a yes or no. Academic City against the neighbourhoods either side of it, in-home against online, and the real numbers for each. The conclusion is the same in Silicon Oasis, Mirdif and International City as it is here, and the next section shows why.

sections.heading: Academic City against Silicon Oasis, Mirdif and International City: four neighbourhoods compared
paragraphs: The four neighbourhoods in this cluster look different on a map and behave almost identically in practice. What changes between them is the school run and the time a session can realistically begin. What does not change is the number of IB Diploma subject specialists available within driving distance, because that number is set by the Dubai labour market and not by your address.

Mirdif has the shortest IB school run of the four, because Uptown International School runs the full continuum within the district. Silicon Oasis has GEMS Wellington Academy on its doorstep. Academic City has neither — its own secondary is British route — so Diploma families here commute. International City has the longest run of all, with no international school inside the district at all, which is why sessions for children living around the clusters tend to start after six.

Read the table as a logistics table, not a quality table. None of these neighbourhoods is a better place to be an IB student than another. The commute differences are real and worth planning around; the tutor-pool differences are not real at all once delivery is online, which is the point the last column makes.

One more thing the table cannot show: traffic direction. A session timed at 4.30pm for a child travelling from Nad Al Sheba back to Academic City is a session that starts at 4.50pm two days out of five. Families who schedule for the worst case rather than the average stop losing the first ten minutes of every lesson to a parked car on Al Ain Road.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in this market, and what the drive premium buys
paragraphs: Start with the monthly number, because that is the one a family actually budgets. A single weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor, online, works out at roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month on Bestimate's 2026 estimates for mid-tier tutoring, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more a month for specialist exam-year support. Published monthly packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Working back to an hourly figure, the market splits into clear bands. University-student and budget online tutors advertise from AED 45 to AED 150 — EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one, travel included, runs AED 180 to 500, per Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. Named and examiner-led tutors go higher: TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650.

The gap between the online and in-home bands is the travel premium, and it is roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour. It is not a markup for greed; a tutor crossing Dubai at 5pm is spending ninety unpaid minutes to deliver sixty paid ones, and that has to be priced in. The question for an Academic City parent is simply what those AED 50 to 150 an hour buy. They buy a person in the room. They do not buy subject depth, and in this district they actively reduce the pool you can choose from.

None of these are IB Gram's prices. They are the market, attributed to whoever published them, as read in October 2026. For our own rates, start with the free trial lesson and the consultation that follows it, where the figure is quoted against your child's actual subjects and level rather than against a table.

sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same in all four neighbourhoods
paragraphs: Here is the arithmetic that makes the comparison collapse. Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, and the International Baccalaureate accounted for 7% of that enrolment. Seven per cent of a market that size is a substantial number of students, but it is spread across every programme from PYP to DP and across the whole emirate. The subset sitting Chemistry HL in any given May session, in the eastern suburbs specifically, is small.

Now apply the supply side. A tutor who can teach Chemistry HL to Diploma standard needs the subject at degree level, familiarity with the current assessment model, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Filter that population by willingness to drive to Academic City at 5pm on a Tuesday and the list gets shorter again. In Mirdif the list is slightly longer; in International City slightly shorter. In none of the four is it long enough to let you choose between three candidates on merit.

That is why distance is the wrong variable to optimise. If the binding constraint were travel time, moving from International City to Mirdif would solve the problem, and it does not. The binding constraint is the size of the specialist pool, and the only lever that changes it is removing the travel requirement — which is what online delivery does. A family in Al Khawaneej and a family in Silicon Oasis then face the same choice of Chemistry HL tutors, which is a larger choice than either had before.

The honest caveat: this is not infinite. Some combinations remain hard to staff at short notice — Diploma Further Mathematics, less-taught Group 2 languages, Music, Film. When that happens we say so at the consultation rather than filling the slot with a generalist, and we tell you what the realistic wait is.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Almost no tutoring page in this market names a session, a deadline or a results date. That absence is strange, because the calendar is the single most useful thing a parent can be handed. UAE IB schools run the May examination session. Working backwards from it produces a plan rather than a panic, and the pressure point is not where most families expect.

The crunch is the January-February window of DP2. Internal Assessments in four or five subjects, the Extended Essay final submission, the TOK essay and the school's mock examinations all land inside a few weeks. A student who has done nothing on the Extended Essay by the October of DP2 is not behind on the Extended Essay; they are about to be behind on everything else, because the hours have to come from somewhere.

Specific IB session and results dates are deliberately not published here. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a wrong date on a page a parent plans around is worse than no date. Confirm every date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. What is safe to publish is the shape of the year and the order of the milestones, which does not move.

For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications, the dates are sourced and the rule is different. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates — the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For reference on how far ahead deadlines sit: the Pearson November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: KHDA, the inspection bands, and what a school report does not tell you
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Every school your child might attend from Academic City — in Silicon Oasis, Mirdif, Al Warqa or Nad Al Sheba — is inspected by KHDA and given a published rating on a six-band scale. The reports are public and worth reading before a school visit rather than after.

What the bands tell you is school-level quality across many measures. What they do not tell you is how a specific department performs in a specific Diploma subject in a specific year. An Outstanding school can have a Physics HL cohort that lost its specialist in September; a Good school can have the strongest Mathematics department on this side of Dubai. Read the inspection report's subject-level commentary, not just the headline band, and then ask the Diploma coordinator directly about staffing in the two subjects your child cares about most.

KHDA is also the body that sets the mandatory-subject rules, and it is worth knowing that it regulates schools rather than private tutors. A private individual tutoring in Dubai operates under the MoHRE private tuition work permit, not under KHDA. A tutoring business with premises and staff needs a separate KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit and is not KHDA approved — the phrase appears on competitor pages and it means something specific that most of them do not hold either.

Context for fees: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Dubai's 2026-27 intake also adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places. For families in this cluster weighing a school move against tutoring, that supply change is relevant.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor may not cross on an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This matters more in these search results than in most, because at least one page competing for the same query sells completed Internal Assessments. That is not tutoring. Under IB academic-honesty rules, submitting work that is not your own is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student: a subject grade withheld, or the Diploma itself. No tutor is exposed by it. The sixteen-year-old is.

So the boundary needs stating in operational terms rather than as a disclaimer. A tutor may teach the subject content the assessment rests on. A tutor may question a research question until it is answerable. A tutor may explain what criterion C asks for and what a top-band response looks like in general terms. A tutor may read the student's own draft and give written feedback on it. A tutor may teach referencing, data handling and uncertainty treatment as skills.

A tutor may not supply text that ends up in the submission. May not rewrite a paragraph into better English. May not choose the Extended Essay topic. May not generate the data, process it, or produce the graphs. May not draft a TOK knowledge claim for the student to adopt. The test is simple: if the student could not explain, in their own words and without notes, why a sentence in their submission says what it says, that sentence should not be there.

Practically, this makes IA coaching look like a conversation rather than a correction. The tutor asks what the independent variable actually controls, why the uncertainty was estimated that way, what the evaluation section concedes. The student goes away and rewrites. That is slower than the alternative and it is the only version that survives moderation, and it is also the version that teaches the student something they keep.
bullets: Coaching allowed: subject teaching, questioning, criteria explanation, feedback on the student's own drafts
Not allowed: supplied text, rewritten paragraphs, chosen topics, generated or processed data
The consequence of malpractice falls on the student, not on the tutor
We do not publish or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes or boundary tables — we cite and link the official sources

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA's own guidance states that these requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For an Academic City family, this is the part of the timetable nobody explains at the open day, and it is a common source of surprise when the first report arrives.

The rules are specific. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. There is also a hard constraint on content: for these subjects, the use of any different or additional material without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Schools must ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects.

What that means for tutoring is narrower than parents expect. Support for Arabic as an additional language is ordinary language teaching and entirely available. Support for the mandatory Islamic Education and Social Studies content is constrained by the Ministry's rule on material, so the right first step is to ask the school what it will and will not accept. For the Diploma itself, note that MoE equivalency for the British track explicitly excludes Arabic and Islamic Education from the five-subject count.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency and what an IB graduate from this cluster needs for a UAE university
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that converts a foreign school certificate into something a UAE university can admit against. It is not something a tutoring company performs, and no tutoring is required for it. It is worth understanding in DP1 rather than discovering in DP2, because the subject choices that satisfy it are made early.

For the British track the requirements are published and specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, excluding those two.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB specifically, we publish no points threshold, because no IB equivalency figure in this project has been read on a Ministry of Education source. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate, and treat any page quoting an IB points number without that citation with suspicion.

The practical sequence for a family in Academic City: confirm with your child's school which of its qualifications are listed as accredited, check the university's own admission page for the specific programme, then approach the Ministry channel for attestation with the documents they ask for. Build the subject choices around that in DP1 and the paperwork in DP2 is administrative rather than urgent.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach privately in Dubai?
paragraphs: This is the question with the clearest answer on the page, and almost nobody competing for this query addresses it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you by anyone.

The permit is granted free of charge for two years. That is worth repeating because it removes a line of argument: a tutor cannot charge you more on the grounds of permit costs, because there are none. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

One restriction matters for Academic City and Silicon Oasis families in particular, where several schools sit close together. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Marketing 'your child's own teacher, privately' is something to decline rather than to seek.

How you verify it as a parent: ask directly whether the individual teaching your child holds a current MoHRE private tuition work permit, and ask to see it. A tutor who holds one will show you without hesitation. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; IB Gram has no premises in the UAE and does not hold one, and no page of ours should ever suggest otherwise.

process.title: Tell us the subjects, levels and session
process.description: Not just 'IB Maths'. Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, HL or SL, which school, which May session, and what the last piece of marked work came back as. Five minutes of specificity here is what makes the match a match rather than a guess.

process.title: We check the specialist pool honestly
process.description: We look for a tutor who teaches that exact subject at that exact level, and we tell you what we find. If the combination is one of the genuinely hard ones to staff at short notice, you hear that at this stage, with a realistic timeframe, rather than after a disappointing first lesson.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one-to-one, online
process.description: A real lesson on real content, not a sales call. Your child works; the tutor diagnoses. Afterwards you get a plain summary of what the tutor found and what they would do over the next eight weeks. If it is not right, say so and nothing further is owed.

process.title: Agree the rhythm around the school calendar
process.description: One or two sessions a week in term time, a finite block for Internal Assessment coaching, or an intensive before the May session. We schedule on Gulf Standard Time and around the school run from whichever of these neighbourhoods you are travelling from.

process.title: Review against the school's own marking
process.description: Progress is measured against the work the school marks, not against our own impression. Every few weeks you get a short written note: what has moved, what has not, and what changes next. If the tutor is not the right fit, we change the tutor rather than defending the choice.

whyPoints.title: Geography stops deciding who teaches your child
whyPoints.description: From Academic City, a 20-minute drive radius is a weak filter on IB subject expertise. Online delivery replaces that filter with the only one that matters: does this tutor teach Chemistry HL, or Mathematics AA HL, to Diploma standard. The same pool is available from Al Khawaneej as from Mirdif.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium in the price
whyPoints.description: In-home rates in this market carry roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour of travel cost, which is reasonable for the tutor and buys you presence rather than expertise. Removing the drive removes the premium and the dead time either side of the lesson, which is the part no invoice shows.

whyPoints.title: We state what we are not
whyPoints.description: Not KHDA approved, because that is a permit issued to training institutes with premises and we have none. Not partnered with any named school. No published star rating we cannot evidence with countable reviews. Every AED figure on this page is attributed to whoever published it and dated.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support that will not cost your child the Diploma
whyPoints.description: On an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay, the student writes and we question. No supplied text, no rewritten paragraphs, no chosen topics. It is slower than what the essay mills in these results offer and it is the only version that survives IB moderation.

whyPoints.title: The calendar, counted backwards, before you need it
whyPoints.description: The Diploma pressure point is the January-February window of DP2, not May. Families who plan from that date backwards buy fewer hours than families who react to it. The exam-session table on this page exists because no competitor page in this cluster names a session at all.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, cumulative work
whyPoints.description: Same tutor every week, working from your child's own marked papers and the school's assessment calendar. A rota of tutors restarts the diagnosis every session, which is the most expensive way to buy tuition that exists.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor in Dubai International Academic City?
faqs.answer: You can get one-to-one IB tutoring for a child living in Dubai International Academic City, and with IB Gram it is delivered live online rather than by a tutor travelling to your address. Home visits are a service we run in India only, not in the UAE. The Dubai market does include tutors who travel, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel according to published rate tables. What that premium buys is presence in the room. Given how few IB Diploma specialists live within a short drive of Academic City, online delivery widens the choice of tutor considerably rather than narrowing it.

faqs.question: Is Academic City or Silicon Oasis better placed for finding an IB Diploma specialist?
faqs.answer: Silicon Oasis is marginally better placed, because GEMS Wellington Academy sits inside the district and the school run is shorter, which makes a 4.45pm session realistic rather than hopeful. But the difference is logistical, not substantive. The number of adults in Dubai who can teach Chemistry HL or Mathematics AA HL to Diploma standard is set emirate-wide, and a ten-minute difference in drive time does not change it. Once lessons are online, both neighbourhoods draw from the same pool on the same terms, and so do Mirdif, Al Warqa, Nad Al Hamar and International City.

faqs.question: What does in-home IB tuition cost around Academic City compared with online?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's rate table at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising 200 to 500. Qualified online subject tutors sit lower, around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market rates from the providers named, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: How late can a weekday session start if my child comes home from school in Silicon Oasis?
faqs.answer: From Silicon Oasis or Mirdif, where the school sits inside the district, 4.45pm is realistic. From Academic City to a Silicon Oasis school, 5pm. From International City, where children travel out to Al Warqa or Mirdif, 6pm is the honest answer. From Nad Al Hamar to a Nad Al Sheba school, around 5.30pm. Schedule for the worst case rather than the average journey: a 4.30pm slot booked against a good day becomes a 4.50pm start twice a week, and ten minutes lost from every lesson across a Diploma year is a substantial amount of paid time.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do families in this part of eastern Dubai actually use?
faqs.answer: Academic City's own secondary, Dubai English Speaking College, runs the British route to IGCSE and A Level rather than the IB. Diploma families in this cluster most often name GEMS Wellington Academy in Silicon Oasis, Uptown International School in Mirdif, Universal American School in Al Warqa, and GEMS Modern Academy, North London Collegiate School Dubai and Repton School Dubai in Nad Al Sheba, with Deira International School in Al Garhoud as a further option. Those schools are named as local context; IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them, and each is inspected and rated by KHDA.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit, and can I check it?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted to you as unverified. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so no tutor can price it into their rate. Ask the individual teaching your child directly whether they hold a current permit and ask to see it. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Chemistry IA without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the chemistry the investigation rests on, question the research question until it is answerable, explain what each assessment criterion asks for, and give written feedback on your daughter's own draft. A tutor cannot design the experiment for her, generate or process her data, produce her graphs, or supply any text that ends up in the submission. The test we use is whether she could explain, unprompted and without notes, why every sentence says what it says. Submitting work that is not her own is malpractice, and the consequence falls on her, not on the tutor.

faqs.question: Which IB Diploma subjects are hardest to find a tutor for near Academic City?
faqs.answer: By residence, almost all of them at Higher Level — the specialist pool in the eastern suburbs is thin, which is the whole reason this page is written as a comparison. Once delivery is online, the genuinely difficult combinations narrow to Further Mathematics, less commonly taught Group 2 languages, Music and Film, and occasionally Physics HL at short notice in the weeks before mocks. If your child's combination is one of those, we tell you at the consultation and give a realistic wait, rather than filling the slot with a generalist and letting you discover the mismatch in lesson two.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Diploma families in this cluster usually start with?
faqs.answer: One session a week per subject is the usual starting point, and most families begin with one subject rather than three. That is enough to establish whether the diagnosis was right and whether the tutor and student work well together, and it keeps the monthly figure in the AED 600 to 1,200 band that Bestimate's 2026 estimates give for mid-tier weekly tutoring. Two sessions a week makes sense in the final eight to ten weeks before the May session, or during the January and February window when Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and mocks collide.

faqs.question: My son says he learns better face to face. Will online lessons actually work for him?
faqs.answer: Often the objection is not about the screen but about attention, and the fix is structural rather than geographic. One-to-one over video, with a shared document, the student's own marked paper on screen and the tutor watching the working as it appears, gives less room to drift than a group class and roughly the same as a person at the table. What makes it fail is a laptop in a living room with a television on. Give him a door that closes and a wired connection if you can, and judge it on the free trial lesson rather than in advance.

faqs.question: What does KHDA actually regulate, and does that include private tutors?
faqs.answer: KHDA regulates private schools in Dubai; u.ae describes it as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. It inspects schools, publishes ratings on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and sets the mandatory-subject requirements. It does not license individual private tutors — that is MoHRE's permit. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram has no UAE premises and holds no KHDA permit, so the phrase 'KHDA-approved tutors' is not one we use and is worth questioning wherever you see it.

faqs.question: Do IB students in Dubai need Ministry of Education equivalency for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is the process that converts a foreign school certificate into something a UAE university can admit against, and it is administered by the Ministry of Education rather than by any tutoring company. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. For the IB specifically we publish no points threshold, because no IB figure in this project has been read on a Ministry source. Verify it on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority.

faqs.question: Do session times change during Ramadan for families in Academic City?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families in this cluster ask for it. School days shorten during Ramadan, which frees the afternoon, but concentration in the late afternoon is usually poor and a session scheduled then is often wasted money. The two slots that work are mid-morning at weekends and after Iftar on weekdays. Because tutors are not travelling, a post-Iftar slot is a scheduling question rather than a logistics one. Tell us in advance which pattern you want for the month and we fix the slot before Ramadan starts rather than rearranging week by week.

faqs.question: We tried one lesson and it did not click - can we swap tutors?
faqs.answer: You say so and we change the tutor. The free trial lesson exists precisely so that this decision is made before any money moves, and nothing further is owed if the trial does not convince you. If a mismatch surfaces later, after three or four sessions, we would rather reassign than defend the original match, because a tutor the student does not want to talk to teaches nothing. What we will not do is rotate tutors as a matter of course: a different person each week restarts the diagnosis every time, which is the most expensive way to buy tuition.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic and Islamic Education at an IB school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidance states these requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on 40-minute lesson units. For these subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so ask your school what tutoring material it will accept.

faqs.question: When should we start if the May session is six weeks away?
faqs.answer: Six weeks is not too late, but it changes what the sessions are for. There is no time to build missing content from scratch across a whole syllabus, and any tutor promising that is not being straight with you. What six weeks does buy is substantial: timed past-paper practice, command-term discipline, and systematic work on the two or three question types the student keeps dropping marks on. That is often worth several marks a paper. The first session is diagnostic, and at the end of it you get an honest statement of what the remaining weeks can realistically achieve.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-academic-ci.closingHeading: Start with a trial lesson, from whichever of these neighbourhoods you are in
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-academic-ci.closingBody: If your child is on an IB programme and you live in Dubai International Academic City, Silicon Oasis, Mirdif, Al Warqa, Nad Al Hamar or International City, the practical next step is the same one. Tell us the exact subject and level, the school, and what the last marked piece of work came back as. We check whether a specialist in that combination is free, say plainly if one is not, and put a free trial lesson in the diary at a time that survives the school run. Lessons are one-to-one and online, on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the subject rather than the postcode.
