dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-creek-harbo.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects for families across Dubai Creek Harbour. Each one works to Gulf Standard Time, holds a fixed weekly slot set from the student's actual arrival home, and sizes practice to a commuting student's evening rather than an ideal one.

intro.heading: Almost nobody here walks home, and that changes everything about the timing
paragraphs: Dubai Creek Harbour is a new waterfront district, and new districts have apartments before they have schools. The practical consequence for a Diploma family is that almost every student here commutes out: to Al Jaddaf, to Dubai Festival City, to Nad Al Sheba, to Al Quoz or further. Nobody is home at ten past three having walked across the community, which is the quiet assumption behind most tutoring advice and it does not hold here.

That makes the transport decision the dominant variable in a tutoring plan, and it is one that almost no family thinks of as an academic decision. A student collected by car at the bell can be home within twenty-five to forty minutes depending on the direction. A student on a school bus is subject to a route: the bus loads, waits, and works through its stops, which commonly puts the drop forty-five to sixty minutes after the bell and sometimes more. Those two students live in the same tower and have evenings that begin an hour apart.

Once you see that, the rest follows. A bus-riding Diploma student at a school in the western cluster may not be through the door until a quarter to five, and after the twenty minutes anybody needs to stop being in transit, the session starts at five. That is still a usable hour for a seventeen-year-old, but it is one hour rather than two, and it has to be spent on the right thing rather than on whatever the tutor had planned.

This is where a near-me search actively misleads. The tutors who answer it are the ones prepared to drive here, and Creek Harbour is reached by a limited number of access roads with the Ras Al Khor crossings carrying the load. A tutor coming from the city's teaching concentrations at four in the afternoon arrives late, and arrives late into an evening that was already shortened by the bus. The journey is not a detail; it is the second hour removed from the same evening.

IB Gram delivers Diploma tuition to Dubai Creek Harbour as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the session begins when your child is actually home rather than when a tutor has crossed the creek. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The sections below compare bus and car properly, work out the start time by school, and show what a single usable hour should be spent on.

Nothing here promises a grade. It sets out the scheduling decisions a commuting household controls, which in a district built before its schools were is the part that decides whether tutoring works at all.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-creek-harbo.programmesIntro: The commute affects each stage differently, because a younger child loses more to a long bus route than an older one does. These are the three contexts that matter for a household here.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three core components and homework on most evenings. For a commuting student the practical issue is that the Diploma assumes an evening it may not have: a bus-riding student arriving at a quarter to five has perhaps three usable hours before the work becomes unproductive, and a tutoring session takes one of them. That means the session has to replace homework time rather than being added to it.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision is not inside Dubai Creek Harbour, so students here travel to it. Which school a family has chosen therefore determines the evening more than where in the district they live, and it is why we ask for the school and the transport arrangement before proposing a slot.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed with tasks arriving in bursts rather than homework nightly, and a usable evening window that closes earlier than a Diploma student's. For a bus-riding MYP student the window can be very narrow indeed, which argues for shorter sessions placed as early as the drop allows and for one session per task cycle rather than one per week.
programmes.countryNote: Families in this district frequently have both an MYP and a Diploma child on the same bus route, arriving home together into a single narrow window. Giving the younger child the earlier slot is usually right, because their capacity falls away sooner.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The age most affected by a long commute and the age where tutoring should be smallest. A primary child who has spent fifty minutes on a bus is not available for a formal session at half past four, and the honest advice is a short defined block scheduled at the weekend rather than a weekday arrangement that fights the bus timetable.
programmes.countryNote: New districts attract young families, and local tutoring supply follows, often scheduled late because that is when a tutor finishes elsewhere. A seven-year-old taught at six in the evening after a bus journey is being taught at the wrong time, and no tutor quality compensates for it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-creek-harbo.subjectsIntro: With one usable hour rather than two, the subject placed in it matters. These are the courses we cover for this district, noted for whether they suit a student who has just come off a bus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Needs an alert student, because Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and the work is timed practice. For a bus-riding student this is the subject to place on the shortest commute day, or at the weekend.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: More forgiving after a commute than Analysis and Approaches, because the modelling and interpretation work is discursive, though calculator practice still needs concentration.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation sections need alertness; investigation criteria and feedback discussion survive a post-commute slot well. Worth splitting the two kinds of work across different weeks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Problem solving needs the better hour; definitions, uncertainty discussion and practical write-up feedback are manageable later, which makes Physics unusually schedulable with planning.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most forgiving science after a long journey, because terminology precision and command-term work is discussion-led rather than computational.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram work and evaluation practice both survive a later start, which makes it a sensible subject for a household whose bus arrives at a quarter to five.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis discussion and Individual Oral preparation suit a post-commute hour. Timed writing does not, and should be set as practice at the weekend instead.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study analysis is discussion-led and survives a late slot, which makes it the easiest Diploma subject to schedule in a commuting household.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Genuinely fine late in the evening, which is fortunate because tutors covering it are scarce and their free hours are often the ones nobody else wants.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Question-narrowing and draft feedback are conversations rather than exercises, so they fit anywhere in the window. The reading and writing happen in the student's own time regardless.

sections.heading: Bus or car: the variable nobody treats as academic
paragraphs: In a district with few schools inside it, how a child gets home is the largest single determinant of what their evening can hold, and it is a decision almost always made on convenience and cost rather than on its academic consequences. Those consequences are substantial, and they are worth seeing laid out before a tutoring slot is agreed.

Car pickup at the bell puts a student home in twenty-five to forty-five minutes depending on the destination school, which for a Creek Harbour family means somewhere between a quarter past three and a quarter past four. A school bus is a route rather than a journey: it loads at the end of the school day, waits for its full complement, and works through its stops. Fifty minutes between bell and drop is unremarkable, an hour is common on longer routes, and the drop time varies day to day in a way a car journey does not.

The variability matters as much as the average. A weekly tutoring slot set to the best case will be missed whenever the route runs long, and a slot missed twice stops being defended. A slot set to the realistic worst case is kept, and the student occasionally has twenty spare minutes, which is a far better failure mode. We therefore ask for the latest usual drop time rather than the scheduled one.

The table sets out the comparison. Read the final column as the practical conclusion: for the longest routes, the sensible answer is not to find a later tutor but to move the demanding work to a weekend morning and keep the weekday hour for discussion-led subjects. That costs nothing, and it is the single most useful scheduling decision available to a commuting household in this district.

sections.heading: When a session can start, by school and by transport
paragraphs: The chain is the same as anywhere and the numbers are specific to this district, because every row involves a journey. When the school day ends, how the student travels, when they are actually through the door, the twenty minutes anybody needs to stop being in transit, and therefore when a session can begin without being half wasted.

The table applies that to the destinations Creek Harbour families actually use. The pattern is that a car-collected student at a creek-side school has a genuinely early evening and can do timed work at four. A bus-riding student at an inland or western school is starting at five, which is still a usable hour for a Diploma student but is one hour rather than two, and it should be spent on something that works at five.

The right-hand column is the comparison a near-me search never shows. An in-home tutor crossing the creek at four in the afternoon arrives after your child does, and the Ras Al Khor crossings carry the whole district's traffic at once. Adding a tutor's journey to a bus route that already consumed an hour leaves a session starting at half past five or later, which for a seventeen-year-old is the hour where attention begins to fall and for a younger child is past the point of value.

Set the slot from the realistic worst case, then choose the tutor. In a commuting district that order matters more than it does elsewhere, because the variability is higher: a slot that only works on a good day will be renegotiated twice and then abandoned, and a household will conclude the tutoring did not help when what did not work was the timetable.

sections.heading: One usable hour: what to spend it on
paragraphs: A commuting Diploma student often has a single hour in which real work is possible, rather than the two or three a scheduling plan assumes. That is not a disaster, and it does change what should happen inside the hour. The rule is to put the work that cannot be done alone into the session, and to leave the work that can be done alone to the student.

What cannot be done alone is diagnosis and correction: working through a marked script and finding why marks were lost, having a method questioned, getting feedback on a draft, being told that an internal assessment question will not produce enough data. These need a second person who has marked the paper, and they are the proper content of a scarce hour.

What can be done alone is practice, reading and drafting, and in a narrow evening these should not be happening inside a paid session. A tutor who spends the hour watching a student complete exercises has used the scarcest resource in the week on the thing the student could have done on the bus. For a commuting household that is the most expensive error in this market, and it is invisible because the hour looks productive.

The practical shape, then, is a session that arrives with last week's practice already marked, names the pattern, teaches it, and sends the student away with a small amount of work to apply it. Short pieces rather than a long weekly task, because a commuting student's evening absorbs fifteen minutes and cannot absorb ninety. Ask any prospective tutor what they will set and how they will mark it; a tutor who intends to be the practice rather than to set it has not understood the constraint.

sections.heading: The Diploma week in a commuting household
paragraphs: A Diploma week is full before tutoring is added, and in a commuting household it is fuller still, because an hour a day goes to transport. A plan that treats the evening as open ends up displacing school homework, which is the work the student's own teachers mark and the work that shapes predicted grades.

The table below sets out a plausible week for a bus-riding DP2 student in this district. It is an illustration rather than a prescription, and the method is what matters: map the transport first, then the fixed commitments, then find the hour that is both free and usable, and put the session there rather than in the first gap a tutor offers.

Two features of the week are worth noticing. The first is that the shortest-commute day, if the school runs a varied timetable or the student is collected on a particular day, is the one to use for demanding work. Households rarely identify which day that is. The second is that the weekend is comparatively empty and almost completely unused, which for a commuting family is the obvious place to put a whole timed paper.

The third point is about internal assessment weeks, which should be left empty rather than filled. Internal assessment deadlines cluster across subjects and sit near the Extended Essay deadline, so those evenings are already spoken for. In a household where the evening is an hour long, adding a session in those weeks guarantees something else gets dropped.

sections.heading: Counted backwards from the May session, in usable weeks
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session, and for a commuting household the useful way to count backwards is in weeks the evenings can genuinely absorb. Remove the mock fortnight, the internal assessment deadline weeks, the final fortnight when nothing new sticks, and any holiday the family travels through, and the number of usable weeks is smaller than the calendar implies.

Two cautions before using the table. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB holds those, and your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal versions, including the internal assessment and Extended Essay deadlines that actually constrain an evening. Confirm every date with the coordinator rather than with a tutoring website, including this one, and treat an internal deadline as firm from the moment it is announced.

Read for a commuting household, the calendar produces one unusual recommendation: use the holidays. School holiday weeks are the only period when the commute disappears entirely, and for a family in this district that is worth more than it is elsewhere, because the hour a day normally lost to transport becomes available. Three to five sessions across a holiday week, with a rested student and no journey, address a foundation gap properly.

The other recommendation is to book the week after the DP2 mock early. It is the most valuable tutoring week of the year in any district, because for the first time there is a marked script to diagnose from, and it is the most contested. A household that reserves it in October gets it; one that asks in February chooses from what is left, which in a narrow evening window is a quality cost rather than a price one.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and the day that is fuller than it looks
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspection on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. For a household choosing a school from a district with little provision of its own, those published reports are the most useful free document available, and the departmental commentary is worth more than the headline band.

The sector is also growing, which matters here more than in established districts. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. New provision closer to a new district eventually shortens the commute this page is built around.

The scheduling fact is the mandatory UAE subjects, which run alongside the Diploma rather than instead of it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit.

The effect for a commuting Diploma student is fewer free periods in the school day, so more work comes home into an evening already shortened by the journey. On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, and does not claim to be, since a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and why a short evening raises the stakes
paragraphs: There is a connection between a narrow evening and an integrity problem that this market does not discuss. A student with an internal assessment due tomorrow, an hour a day lost to a bus and no free evening left is the student most exposed to an offer they should refuse, and at least one operator ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. The consequence falls on the student, who can lose the Diploma, not on the website that took the money.

The boundary does not move with the timetable. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the language the examiner uses, question a research question until it is answerable with the resources available, warn that a method will generate too little data, teach the underlying content, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. That is substantial help and it is what the sessions on this page are for.

What a tutor may not do is choose the question, supply the method or the data, write any part of the text, or edit a draft into its final form, nor hand over a worked example close enough to the student's own task that copying becomes the obvious next step. We state this to the student in the first session rather than in small print, because in a household where time is already short the pressure arrives early and a boundary explained at the deadline is explained too late.

The scheduling remedy is to place the valuable sessions early and protect the deadline weeks entirely. A question-narrowing conversation in September costs one hour and removes most of the risk. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to the official source, which is both lawful and more useful since the official version is the current one.

sections.heading: Getting started, and the four things we ask first
paragraphs: Four pieces of information decide the slot, and we ask for them before proposing anyone. Which school your child attends. Whether they travel by bus or are collected by car. The latest usual time they are actually through the door, not the scheduled one. And what fixed commitments sit in the week, including CAS, sport and music.

Then the subject, the level, the latest grade and the teacher's last comment quoted rather than summarised, with a photograph of a marked paper if you have one. That decides who we propose. The slot and the tutor are separate decisions and in a commuting district they should be made in that order, because an excellent tutor in an hour the bus regularly overruns produces nothing but frustration.

We run a free trial lesson at the time you would actually use, on a normal school day rather than a convenient weekend. That matters more here than in most districts: a Saturday trial tells you nothing about whether your child can work at five o'clock after fifty minutes on a bus. Afterwards, ask for a written account of what is costing marks, and ask what will be set as practice and how it will be marked.

And the honest part. The five o'clock Gulf Standard Time slots this district needs are popular and fill early, and some Diploma areas are thin everywhere: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay supervision, Higher Level mathematics with Paper 3 experience, and second languages beyond the common ones. When what you need is unavailable we say so and offer another hour, a weekend morning, or a tutor based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time. We will not hold a slot we cannot reliably keep.

faqs.question: Why does the school bus matter so much for tutoring in Dubai Creek Harbour?
faqs.answer: Because almost no student here walks home. The district has little school provision inside it, so nearly every child commutes out, and a bus is a route rather than a journey: it loads at the bell, waits for its complement and works through its stops. Fifty minutes between bell and drop is unremarkable and an hour is common on longer routes. A bus-riding student and a car-collected student living in the same tower have evenings that begin up to an hour apart, which changes what tutoring can achieve.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session realistically start here?
faqs.answer: Online, between about four o'clock and twenty past five depending on the school and the transport. A student collected by car from a creek-side school can be ready at four. A bus-riding student at an inland or western school is often not through the door until a quarter to five and ready at about five. Add an in-home tutor's own journey across the creek and the session starts at half past five or later, which is the hour where a Diploma student's attention starts to fall away.

faqs.question: Will someone actually come to the apartment, or is this remote only?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video throughout the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. We say so plainly because home tutor is the phrase parents search. In a commuting district the online structure is a particular advantage rather than a compromise: the household has already lost an hour of the evening to transport, and adding a tutor's journey across the Ras Al Khor crossings removes a second one.

faqs.question: Should I give you the scheduled bus time or the real one?
faqs.answer: The latest time your child is usually actually through the door. Bus routes run long, and a tutoring slot set to the best case will be missed whenever it does, which means it gets renegotiated twice and then quietly abandoned. A slot set to the realistic worst case is kept, and on a good day the student has twenty spare minutes, which is a far better failure mode. We would rather start the session ten minutes later and keep it all year.

faqs.question: My child comes off the bus at a quarter to five. Which subject should we put in that hour?
faqs.answer: A discussion-led one. Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay or internal assessment conversation, English analysis, Economics evaluation or Business Management case-study work all function perfectly well after a commute. What does not is timed practice and non-calculator mathematics, because both measure speed and a tired student practises being slow. Move those to a weekend morning, where a rested student with no journey can sit a whole paper properly, which is the better slot for that work anyway.

faqs.question: What should the scarce weekday hour actually be spent on?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis, correction and feedback, which cannot be done alone. Working through a marked script to find why marks were lost, having a method questioned, getting written feedback on a draft, being warned that an internal assessment question will not yield enough data. Practice, reading and drafting can be done without a tutor and should be. A tutor who spends the hour watching your child complete exercises has used the scarcest resource in a commuting week on the thing the student could have done on the bus.

faqs.question: How should practice be set for a student who commutes?
faqs.answer: In short daily pieces, marked before the next session. A commuting Diploma student's evening absorbs fifteen minutes and cannot absorb ninety, so a long weekly task guarantees it competes with school homework and loses. Short frequent practice also suits what actually moves grades: command-term discipline, writing working, keeping units. Ask any prospective tutor what they will set and how they will mark it before booking; a tutor with no answer is proposing to be the practice rather than to set it.

faqs.question: Is a weekend session better than a weekday one for a commuting family?
faqs.answer: For whole timed papers and for mathematics, clearly yes. A Saturday morning reaches a rested student with no journey at either end, and ninety minutes then is worth more than a tired hour at half past five. The sensible pattern for a household with a long bus route is a weekday hour for discussion-led work and a weekend morning for the demanding work. The drawback is that weekend slots are easier to cancel, so agree them as a routine rather than week by week.

faqs.question: Which schools do Creek Harbour families usually travel to?
faqs.answer: The nearest provision is across the creek in Al Jaddaf and north in Dubai Festival City, with established IB and British-curriculum schools inland at Nad Al Sheba and Meydan, and further west in Al Quoz and Al Barsha. The closer destinations leave an evening most intact, and the length of a bus route is a scheduling consideration no prospectus mentions but which shapes every weekday for years. KHDA publishes current curricula and inspection outcomes for every Dubai private school on its own site.

faqs.question: Does the growth of this district change the commute?
faqs.answer: Eventually. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, with six new schools having opened during 2025-26 and enrolment up 6%. New provision nearer new districts is what shortens routes like these. Until it arrives, the scheduling problem on this page is the one households here have to plan around.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the timetable for a commuting household?
faqs.answer: Completely, and it has to be recalculated rather than assumed. School timings change, which changes the bell, the bus route and the drop, and the whole chain on this page shifts. Sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot, which works precisely because online delivery means no journey to renegotiate at either end, and a fasting student is better served later than in the afternoon. Agree the shift in advance so the slot is held rather than released to another family.

faqs.question: Can sessions continue while we travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for families in this district it is one of the clearer advantages of online delivery. The lesson follows the student rather than the address, so a fortnight away need not cost a fortnight of a subject. The one thing to settle in advance is which time zone the session is pinned to, so a student in Europe or India is not sitting a Higher Level lesson at six in the morning. Tell us early enough that the slot can be held rather than released.

faqs.question: Why are school holidays more valuable here than elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Because the commute disappears. In term time an hour a day goes to transport, and in a holiday week that hour comes back along with the school homework load. Three to five sessions across a holiday week, with a rested student and nothing competing, address a foundation gap properly rather than squeezing it into a shortened evening. It is the most underused block of time available to a commuting household, and it costs no more than the same sessions in term.

faqs.question: Should we book sessions during internal assessment deadline weeks?
faqs.answer: No, and protecting those weeks is the more useful decision. Internal assessment deadlines cluster across subjects and sit near the Extended Essay deadline, so those evenings are already spoken for, and in a household where the usable evening is an hour long, adding a session guarantees something else is dropped. The valuable conversation happens months earlier: narrowing the question, understanding the criteria, agreeing what finished looks like while there is still room to do the work.

faqs.question: What if the five o'clock slot we need is already booked?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than holding a slot we cannot reliably keep. Five o'clock Gulf Standard Time is exactly what commuting districts need, so it fills early. The alternatives are a different evening, a weekend morning, a shorter session that fits what remains, or a tutor based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed as such. Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay supervision and Higher Level mathematics with Paper 3 experience are thin everywhere, and we flag that before you book.

faqs.question: What should I send so the slot survives the whole year?
faqs.answer: Four things about getting home and two about the work. The school; whether your child buses or is collected; the latest time they are usually through the door; and the fixed weekly commitments including CAS, sport and music. Then the subject and level with the latest grade, and the teacher's last comment quoted rather than paraphrased. A photograph of one marked paper is worth more than the grade, and with the transport detail we can propose a slot that is not simply the first gap in a diary.

Tell us the school, the transport, the real arrival time and the fixed commitments, along with the subject and the latest grade, and we will propose a tutor and run the trial on a normal school day.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival-ci.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects for families in and around Dubai Festival City. Each one is matched to a named syllabus and level rather than a general subject label, because a Maths AA HL student and a Maths AI SL student need different people, not the same person charging the same rate.

intro.heading: What an IB home tutor in Dubai Festival City really costs, line by line
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest thing on the market and work upwards, because that is the order a budget is actually built in. Published rates in Dubai begin around AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya, both for online sessions delivered by tutors who are often undergraduates. That tier is real and it has a legitimate use: drilling arithmetic fluency, keeping a Year 8 student on top of homework, rebuilding confidence after a bad term. What it does not reliably do is diagnose why an IB Diploma student is stuck on 4s in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, because diagnosing that requires someone who has marked the paper and knows which command term the student is misreading.

The next band up is where most Dubai Festival City Diploma families end up. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts qualified subject specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. TutorChase quotes AED 270. These are the figures for a person who teaches the syllabus for a living, holds the subject guide in their head, and can tell you in one session whether your child's problem is content, exam technique or time.

Then there is the in-home premium, and this is the number worth staring at. Bestimate records in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in this market run about AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Read those two package prices side by side. The in-home option costs roughly twice as much for half the number of contact points, and the difference is not teaching. It is a car, a driver's hour, and the risk that a Garhoud interchange queue eats the first fifteen minutes of a lesson you paid for.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a Dubai Festival City family the delivery is one-to-one live video, which is why the travel component disappears from the invoice entirely. That is not a cost-cutting dodge dressed up as a feature. It is the mechanism that lets a family living beside Festival City Mall hire a Chemistry HL specialist who knows the data booklet cold, rather than settling for the best generalist within driving distance of Al Badia.

The rest of this page is about where the money leaks. Some of it leaks into travel. Some leaks into sessions booked before anyone has diagnosed the problem, so the first four hours are spent working out what the first hour should have established. Some leaks into paying a specialist rate for work a parent could supervise, and some into paying a cheap rate for work that needed a specialist and then paying again, properly, in March. We will put numbers on each of those, cite them, and be explicit about which figures are the market's and which are ours.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival-ci.programmesIntro: Dubai Festival City sits beside one of Dubai's longer-established IB continuum schools, so families here often need support at Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma level inside the same household. The cost structure differs sharply by programme, and knowing which is which stops a parent paying Diploma rates for Middle Years work.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP has no external examinations. Assessment is continuous, built around transdisciplinary units of inquiry and an exhibition in the final year. Tutoring at this level is about literacy and number fluency, reading stamina, and the habit of explaining reasoning aloud, which is the single skill that pays off most when the same child reaches Middle Years criterion-referenced marking.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Festival City households that plan to stay through secondary school usually keep PYP support light and short: one session a week for a term, aimed at a specific gap. Paying a Diploma specialist rate for Year 4 reading comprehension is one of the clearest money leaks in this market, and the rate difference between tiers is roughly threefold.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks each subject against four criteria, A to D, on a 1 to 8 scale, then converts the total to a 1 to 7 grade using published boundaries. Most students lose marks not on content but on the command verbs inside criterion strands, and on investigations where the method is sound and the evaluation is thin.
programmes.countryNote: This is the band where Dubai Festival City parents most often overspend, because MYP reports look alarming without explaining themselves. A single diagnostic session that reads the criterion grid back to you often replaces a term of weekly booking. Where a Personal Project is involved, support is supervision and questioning, never drafting.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Higher Level papers carry more content and, in sciences, a third paper. The Internal Assessment in each subject is marked against lettered criteria by the teacher and moderated by the IB, which is why IA coaching is about process and feedback rather than product.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma support is where a specialist rate is genuinely justified for a Dubai Festival City family. The market band for an IB specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, and a two-year plan priced at one session a week is a real commitment. We would rather a family bought fewer, better-targeted hours in the two terms that matter.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP combines a career-related study with at least two Diploma courses, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and suits students who want a vocational spine with IB academic rigour attached to it.
programmes.countryNote: CP students near Dubai Festival City typically need help with their two DP courses and with the reflective project's research method. Because the cohort is small, local tutor supply for CP is thin, which is exactly the scenario where online matching stops being a convenience and starts being the only way to reach a specialist at all.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival-ci.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Dubai Festival City families ask about most, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks go missing. Rate pressure differs by subject: sciences and Higher Level mathematics sit at the top of the market band because the pool of people who can teach them properly is smaller.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes any student who has been leaning on a graphic display calculator for routine manipulation. Most HL marks are lost in the long structured questions of Paper 2 and in the Paper 3 extended investigation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving, with the calculator permitted throughout. Marks go missing in interpretation: students compute a regression correctly and then say nothing useful about what it means in context, which is where the marks actually sit.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across the revised course, assessed by two papers plus the scientific investigation. The data booklet is provided and under-used. Organic mechanisms and the energetics calculations are the two places a Dubai Festival City Chemistry HL student most often stalls.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Space, time and motion through to nuclear and quantum physics. Paper 1 mixes multiple choice with data analysis; Paper 2 rewards clean algebra and units. Uncertainty and error treatment in the scientific investigation is the most commonly thin section in the whole report.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. Biology punishes vague language more than any other science: a sentence that does not name the structure, the process and the consequence scores zero even when the student understands it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis of unseen non-literary texts, Paper 2 comparative essay, plus the individual oral and, at HL, the essay. Students lose marks by paraphrasing rather than analysing, and by leaving the global issue unnamed in the oral.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and real-world engagement. The internal assessment is a portfolio of commentaries on published articles, and the single most common failure is a diagram drawn correctly but never referred to in the analysis.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Introduction to business management, human resource management, finance and accounts, marketing and operations. Marks are lost in the HL extension questions where students describe a tool instead of applying it to the stimulus organisation in front of them.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and computational thinking, with an internally assessed solution. The write-up, not the code, is where marks are won; a working program with a thin design document scores badly.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Diploma Arabic B students near Dubai Festival City often need targeted work on productive writing rather than comprehension.

regions.note: The residential and golf-course side of Dubai Festival City and the closest address to Deira International School. In-home quotes here are at the lower end of the travel premium simply because the school and the villas are minutes apart, which makes the online saving smaller but the specialist choice just as wide.

regions.note: Apartment living beside the mall and the marina. Weekday evening access is slowed by retail traffic rather than commuter traffic, so a 5pm in-home slot is less reliable here than the postcode suggests. A video lesson starting at 5pm starts at 5pm.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Older established housing just across Dubai-Al Ain Road, feeding a mix of British and Indian curriculum schools. Families here often run two curricula in one household, which is an argument for a platform match rather than a single local tutor.

regions.note: Villa community between Festival City and Mirdif with limited walkable school provision, so school runs are long. Parents in Nad Al Hamar frequently report that the realistic in-home start time is 5.30pm or later, which compresses any session into homework hours.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: The largest neighbouring family district and home to an IB continuum school of its own. Mirdif is where Dubai Festival City families most often find a local tutor, and also where they discover that local supply covers Middle Years far better than Higher Level sciences.

regions.note: Lower-density villa areas further east, with American and British curriculum provision nearby. Travel from central Dubai adds real cost to an in-home rate here; the in-home premium is at its widest in this part of the eastern suburbs.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: A denser, younger community to the south with its own large British-curriculum school. Supply of IGCSE tutors is reasonable; Diploma Higher Level supply is not, which is the same pattern repeated across the eastern corridor.

regions.note: University district adjoining Academic City schools. Undergraduate tutors are plentiful here, which explains the AED 45 to 65 budget band that EdFlik publishes and why that band exists at all.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Festival City and Al Badia
schoolClusters.note: The immediate cluster. Deira International School runs the IB continuum through to Diploma alongside IGCSE at 16, and Universal American School offers the Diploma on an American spine. Dubai Festival City School runs the English National Curriculum. A household here can genuinely be sitting MYP criteria, IGCSE codes and DP papers at the same kitchen table.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif and the eastern suburbs
schoolClusters.note: The wider catchment most Dubai Festival City families also consider. Uptown International School runs the IB continuum in Mirdif, and GEMS Modern Academy at Nad Al Sheba is one of the emirate's longer-running Diploma centres. This cluster is where the local tutor market concentrates, and where its Higher Level gaps become visible.

schoolClusters.note: The southern edge of the same corridor, reached from Festival City in twenty to thirty-five minutes depending on the hour. Several large British-curriculum schools sit here, which matters because a tutor who teaches one school's scheme of work will often already know the next school's.

sections.heading: What IB tuition costs around Dubai Festival City, in AED
paragraphs: A qualified online IB subject tutor in Dubai is priced by the market at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and an IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those two bands come from published provider pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. Nobody ranking for this query publishes them, which is a strange thing for a cost-led search to turn up, and it is the first reason this page exists.

The table below sets out the full ladder, lowest first, with the source for each band. Read it as the market, not as a price list: IB Gram's own commercial terms are set after the free trial lesson and after the diagnostic conversation, because quoting a single hourly number for Primary Years literacy and Chemistry Higher Level would be dishonest in both directions. What the table does is tell you whether a quote you have already received sits inside the market or outside it.

One more thing the ladder reveals. The gap between the budget band and the specialist band is roughly fourfold, but the gap between a good specialist and a premium named tutor at AED 650 is smaller than that, and much harder to justify on results. The money a Dubai Festival City family can most reliably save is not at the top of this table. It is in buying the right number of hours in the right band, and in not paying twice because the first attempt was aimed at the wrong problem.

sections.heading: The in-home premium: what the extra AED actually buys
paragraphs: Take the two package prices side by side, because they are the clearest comparison in the whole market. About AED 799 a month buys eight online sessions. AED 1,599 to 1,799 buys four in-home sessions of two hours each. Same total contact time, roughly double the price. The arithmetic is not subtle, so the question is what the second figure is buying that the first is not.

Three things, honestly. A physical presence, which for some younger students genuinely changes behaviour. A phone that cannot be scrolled under the table. And a parent's own reassurance, which is a real good even if it is not an academic one. Against that, the in-home rate pays for a car, a petrol bill, a driver's unpaid hour and a scheduling fragility that is specific to this corner of Dubai: a tutor coming from Jumeirah to Al Badia at 5.30pm is at the mercy of Garhoud Bridge, and the lesson that starts fifteen minutes late is still a lesson you paid for in full.

The harder cost is invisible on the invoice. An in-home tutor must live within driving distance, so the pool you are choosing from is defined by geography rather than by subject expertise. For Mathematics at Middle Years level that is fine; the eastern suburbs have plenty of capable people. For Chemistry Higher Level, Physics Higher Level or Maths Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, the pool inside a twenty-minute radius of Dubai Festival City is small enough that families routinely compromise on specialism to preserve proximity. That is the trade the table below prices out.

sections.heading: Where the money actually leaks
paragraphs: The biggest single waste in this market is not an overpriced hour. It is a correctly priced hour pointed at the wrong thing. A student is failing Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 2, so the family books calculus support, and four sessions later the tutor reports that the calculus is fine and the student cannot manipulate algebraic fractions reliably under time pressure. Those four hours were not stolen. They were spent discovering something a diagnostic session should have found in sixty minutes.

The second leak is buying continuity nobody needs. Weekly tuition across two years in a subject the student is coping with is comfortable and expensive. At the specialist band, one weekly hour across a Diploma year is a substantial commitment, and Bestimate's own monthly estimate for an exam-year specialist runs AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Some subjects need that. Many need a diagnostic block, a focused run before internal assessment deadlines, and an intensive before the examinations, with nothing in between.

The third leak is paying cheap and then paying properly. A budget-band tutor at AED 45 to 65 an hour is excellent value for the work that band is for. Pointed at a Higher Level science, it produces a term of reassurance and no grade movement, and the specialist is then hired in the final two terms at four times the rate with less time to work in. The honest version of this advice costs us money: if your child needs the budget band, use the budget band, and do not let anyone sell you upwards.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from a Dubai Festival City desk
paragraphs: Cost planning only works against a calendar, and this is where almost every competing page goes quiet. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series exists, but it is offered to India only, so no student at Deira International School or Dubai Festival City School will ever sit it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Those are the windows a Dubai budget has to fit around.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is a sentence worth reading twice before you trust any date printed on a tutoring website, including this one. Always open the school's own timetable or the board's live PDF.

For the IB Diploma, UAE schools sit the May examinations. We publish no specific IB session or results date on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a tutoring page is worse than no date. Your child's IB coordinator holds the real one. What we can plan from are the internal deadlines, which are set by the school and are the ones that actually dictate when tuition money needs to be spent.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is a cost question as much as a compliance one, because an unpermitted tutor is a cheap tutor for a reason. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here; a number circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source and we will not repeat it. The application route is MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two further points a Dubai Festival City parent should know. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit as a training institute. IB Gram does not hold one and does not describe itself as KHDA approved, because that phrase means something specific and we are not it. Separately, in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE code of conduct carries a comparable restriction, so hiring your child's own teacher privately is not a route anyone should market to you.

Ask a prospective tutor directly whether they hold it, and expect a straight answer

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA or Extended Essay
paragraphs: In a market where one competing site sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, a Dubai Festival City parent is entitled to a clear line. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain the assessment criteria letter by letter, interrogate a research question until it is answerable, model a worked example on a different topic, read a draft and give feedback, and teach referencing. A tutor may not write, draft, edit to completion or supply any part of the work.

The reason is not squeamishness. Internal assessment is marked against lettered criteria by the school's teacher and moderated by the IB, and the student signs that the work is their own. Work that is not theirs is malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student, not on the tutor who took the money. There is no version of that transaction where the family comes out ahead.

This also changes how IA support should be priced and booked. The useful shape is short and front-loaded: one or two sessions at the question-setting stage, where a bad research question is cheap to fix, and one session on a complete first draft. Buying ten hours of IA support usually means buying nine hours of someone watching a student type. Ask any provider to put in writing what they will and will not do with assessed work before money changes hands, and keep the reply.

The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay and to Theory of Knowledge. A supervisor at the school signs off on progress, a tutor can help a student plan a reading list and test whether an argument holds together, and nobody outside the student should be generating sentences. Families who understand this early spend less on coursework support and get more from it, because the hours go into thinking rather than into transcription.
bullets: Allowed: content teaching, criteria explanation, feedback on the student's own draft, referencing practice
Not allowed: writing, completing, rewriting or supplying any portion of assessed work
Useful shape: question-setting early, one feedback pass on a full draft, nothing in between
Any provider selling a finished IA is selling your child a malpractice finding

sections.heading: Tuition cost in context: Dubai school fees and the KHDA fee freeze
paragraphs: Tutoring is a second education bill arriving on top of a first one, so it belongs next to the first one on the page. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum taking 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26 per cent, US 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. That last share is the one families in Al Badia and Mirdif live inside, and it is small enough to explain why local Diploma specialists are harder to find than IGCSE ones.

On 22 May 2026, KHDA confirmed there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. For a family doing arithmetic on a tutoring budget, that freeze is the one fixed point in the calculation: the school bill is known, so the tuition decision is about marginal spend rather than about absorbing two rises at once.

Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. More Diploma places means more Diploma students needing Higher Level support, and the supply of Higher Level specialists does not grow on the same schedule. That is the structural reason an online match beats a local search in this corridor, and it is getting more true rather than less.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the cost nobody budgets for
paragraphs: If your child may apply to a UAE university, Ministry of Education equivalency sits at the end of the IGCSE and A-Level route and it has subject requirements that affect decisions taken years earlier. For the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That detail matters because at least one page currently ranking for UAE tutoring queries tells parents that six IGCSE subjects are required. It is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, and a family that plans around the wrong number either over-enters subjects at real examination cost or under-enters and discovers the problem too late to fix cheaply.

For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, we publish no points threshold, because none has been read on an official Ministry source and an invented figure would be the single most damaging thing on this page. Verify on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform equivalency and cannot influence its outcome.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA required these arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Dubai Festival City family this is a line on the timetable that competes with Diploma revision, and it is almost never discussed on tutoring pages.

The rules are specific enough to be worth knowing. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Two practical consequences. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. And for these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is strictly prohibited, which constrains what any tutor can legitimately offer: support means working with the school's own approved material, not importing a parallel course.

sections.heading: Getting started from Dubai Festival City, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The honest sequence is short. You tell us the subject, the level and the paper that is going wrong. We arrange a free trial lesson with a tutor matched to that exact syllabus and level, delivered as live one-to-one video. After it, you get a plain written note of where the gap sits, by topic, and a recommended number of hours. If that number is lower than you expected, that is the system working rather than a soft sell.

Sometimes the right specialist is not available at the hour a Dubai Festival City family needs. Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Physics and Maths Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level are the three slots that fill first, and after-school hours on Gulf Standard Time are the busiest in the week. When that happens we say so, offer the nearest alternative slot, or tell you the wait. Competing pages in this market do not disclose a coverage limit anywhere, and several route UAE parents to an Indian phone number without mentioning where delivery actually happens.

Everything runs online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch in the UAE and does not claim one. We also will not describe any tutor as a current IB or Cambridge examiner unless that status can be evidenced, because examiner labelling is the cheapest unverifiable credential in this market and it is used constantly. Ask us for the evidence; ask everyone else for it too.

process.title: Tell us the paper, not just the subject
process.description: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 1 is a different problem from Paper 3, and Chemistry HL organic is a different problem from energetics. Naming the component means the first session starts on the gap rather than on reconnaissance, which is the cheapest hour you will ever save.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A matched tutor runs a live one-to-one video session at no cost. Its purpose is diagnosis, so expect questions and a piece of timed work rather than a sales pitch. If the match is wrong, say so afterwards and we change it before any money is involved.

process.title: Read the written gap summary
process.description: You receive a short note setting out where the marks are going, by topic and by component, and the number of hours we think that needs. It is written to be argued with. A summary that only recommends more hours is not a diagnosis, and you should treat it as a sales document.

process.title: Book the shape that fits, not the maximum
process.description: Weekly across a term, a short diagnostic block, or a pre-session intensive. Most Dubai Festival City families need one of the three rather than all of them, and the right answer is often fewer hours placed better inside the school's own deadline calendar.

process.title: Review at each report cycle
process.description: School reports and mock results are free diagnostic data, so use them. Hours that are no longer earning their keep get cut, and subjects that have quietly deteriorated get picked up. The plan should look different in the second term from the first, otherwise nobody is reading the evidence.

whyPoints.title: The AED figures are on the page, with sources
whyPoints.description: Three of six researched competitors publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars to families who transact in dirhams. Every band here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, dated October 2026, so you can check it rather than take it.

whyPoints.title: Specialism instead of driving distance
whyPoints.description: An in-home tutor must live near Al Badia or Nad Al Hamar, so geography picks your tutor. A live video lesson lets a Dubai Festival City student work with a Chemistry HL or Maths AA HL specialist who may live nowhere near the eastern suburbs, at the mid rather than the in-home band.

whyPoints.title: We will recommend fewer hours
whyPoints.description: Undiagnosed tuition is the biggest waste in this market and it is profitable, which is why nobody warns you about it. The diagnostic block exists to shrink the booking where shrinking is right, and the trial lesson means that diagnosis costs nothing.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain criteria, and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not write or complete an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay. One site in this market sells finished IAs; the risk of that transaction lands entirely on the student.

whyPoints.title: Regulation described, never borrowed
whyPoints.description: We explain what KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE and the Ministry of Education each do, and we claim approval from none of them because IB Gram holds none. KHDA-approved tutors is the most dangerous phrase in this market and you should distrust everyone who uses it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about coverage limits
whyPoints.description: After-school hours on Gulf Standard Time fill fastest, and Higher Level sciences fill fastest within those. When no specialist is free we say so and give you the wait, rather than substituting a generalist and letting you find out in week three.

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor in Dubai Festival City actually cost?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: a qualified online IB subject tutor in Dubai is priced at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and an IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 table giving the 200 to 450 band. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 500 an hour because travel is inside the figure. IB Gram's own terms are set after a free trial lesson and a diagnostic conversation, because a single hourly number for Primary Years reading and Chemistry Higher Level would mislead you in both directions.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa in Al Badia or our apartment on Festival Boulevard?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. For Al Badia, Festival Boulevard and Marsa Al Khaimah families, tuition is delivered as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. The practical effect is that you are not paying a travel component inside the hourly rate, your session starts when the link opens rather than when the Garhoud queue clears, and the tutor is chosen for knowing your child's syllabus rather than for living within driving distance of Dubai Festival City.

faqs.question: Is the in-home premium in the eastern suburbs worth paying?
faqs.answer: Compare the two packages this market actually offers. Around AED 799 a month buys eight online sessions; AED 1,599 to 1,799 buys four in-home sessions of two hours. That is roughly double the money for the same contact time. The extra buys a physical presence, which genuinely helps some younger students, plus a phone that cannot be scrolled. It also buys a car, a driver's hour and the risk of a late start. For a Higher Level science, the bigger cost is choosing from whoever will drive to Nad Al Hamar.

faqs.question: What is the single biggest way Dubai Festival City families waste tuition money?
faqs.answer: Buying correctly priced hours aimed at the wrong problem. A family books calculus support for a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL student and learns four sessions later that the calculus was never the issue, the algebraic manipulation was. Those hours were not overpriced, they were misdirected. A diagnostic block of two or three sessions, starting with the free trial lesson, finds the gap before the budget commits to a term. The second biggest waste is weekly continuity in a subject the student is already coping with.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and should I check?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure you see online as unverified. Ask any tutor directly and expect a straight answer.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find a specialist for near Dubai Festival City?
faqs.answer: Chemistry Higher Level, Physics Higher Level and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, in that order. International Baccalaureate students were 7 per cent of Dubai's private school enrolment in 2024-25, so the Diploma pool is a small slice of a large market, and the Higher Level science slice of that is smaller again. Within a twenty-minute radius of Al Badia the number of people who teach those papers for a living is low enough that families regularly trade specialism for proximity. Online matching removes that trade entirely.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge examinations actually happen for a student at a Dubai Festival City school?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so no UAE candidate sits it, and any page telling you otherwise is quoting a date from the wrong country. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone timetable is the centre's own risk. Check your school's timetable, not a tutoring site's, including this one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my child's Internal Assessment if we pay more?
faqs.answer: No, and no price changes that. A tutor may teach the content, explain each lettered criterion, press on a research question until it is answerable, model a worked example on an unrelated topic, and give feedback on a draft your child has written. A tutor may not write, draft, edit to completion or supply any part of it. The work is signed as the student's own and moderated by the IB, so the consequence of anything else lands on your child. One site in this market sells completed IAs at AED 3,750; that is a malpractice finding with a price tag.

faqs.question: How many sessions should we book first for an IB Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Two or three, aimed only at finding out what is wrong, with the first being the free trial lesson. You then get a written note of the gap by topic and component, and a recommended number of hours. For a subject the student is carrying rather than failing, that recommendation is often one weekly hour for a single term, then a review. Booking a two-year weekly slot on day one is comfortable and expensive: Bestimate puts an exam-year specialist at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above per month for one weekly hour.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for a student who says they learn better face to face?
faqs.answer: Often it works better, for an unglamorous reason: a shared screen beats a shared notebook. Both people see the same working at the same size, a timed paper can be annotated live, and the session can be reviewed afterwards. What a video lesson needs is a quiet room, a charged device and a parent who checks in occasionally. What it removes is travel, late starts and the geographic limit on who your tutor can be. Try the free trial lesson before deciding on principle either way.

faqs.question: How does the KHDA school fee freeze affect our tutoring budget this year?
faqs.answer: It gives the calculation one fixed point. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. Because the school bill is known rather than rising, a tutoring decision becomes a question of marginal spend rather than of absorbing two increases at once. It is also a reminder to price tuition against the whole education bill, not in isolation.

faqs.question: For a Dubai Festival City IGCSE student, how many subjects does MoE equivalency count?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one page currently ranking for UAE tutoring queries states six, which is wrong and expensive if you plan around it. Verify on moe.gov.ae; IB Gram does not perform equivalency and cannot influence it.

faqs.question: Can sessions be scheduled around Ramadan and the Dubai school day?
faqs.answer: Yes. Lessons run on Gulf Standard Time and the slot is yours, so during Ramadan many Dubai Festival City families move to a post-Iftar time and keep the same tutor. Outside Ramadan the usual constraint is the school run: a Nad Al Hamar or Al Khawaneej household rarely has a student at a desk before 4.15pm, and an online lesson at 4.15pm begins at 4.15pm rather than whenever a car arrives. After-school hours fill first, so book the slot before the term starts if you can.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for Chemistry HL at the hour we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we tell you the wait. Higher Level sciences and Maths Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level fill fastest, and the after-school window on Gulf Standard Time is the busiest part of the week, so this is a real constraint rather than a hypothetical one. You will be offered the nearest alternative slot or an honest timeline, not a quiet substitution with a generalist. No competitor researched in this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere on their pages, which is worth noticing.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram KHDA approved, and does it have an office in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No to both, and anyone claiming either should be questioned. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and does not occupy a UAE office, centre or branch. What we do is explain what KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE and the Ministry of Education each govern, so you can check a provider's claims against the regulator rather than against its own marketing.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival-ci.closingHeading: Start with the diagnosis, then spend the money
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival-ci.closingBody: If you have read this far, you have the market numbers in AED, the sources behind them, and a clear view of where tuition budgets in this part of Dubai quietly leak. The next step costs nothing: a free trial lesson with a tutor matched to your child's exact syllabus and level, delivered as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, followed by a written note of where the marks are going. Then you decide how many hours to buy, and whether to buy them from us at all. A provider that will not tell you when fewer hours are the right answer is not advising you.

intro.heading: Starting mid-term in a Harbour tower, and what the calendar allows
paragraphs: Dubai Harbour is a recently delivered district built around a cruise terminal and a set of marina berths, sitting between Emaar Beachfront and the approach to Palm Jumeirah. Its towers filled quickly and with families who arrived from several different school systems, which means a great many of the Diploma students living here started their programme somewhere else. That produces a particular pattern of enquiry: not "we are planning for two years" but "we are eleven weeks into a term and the report was worse than expected".

The useful answer to that enquiry is a calendar answer. The Diploma year has fixed points and they are not evenly spaced. Internal assessment deadlines sit well ahead of the external papers. Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay milestones are set by the school and cluster in the middle of the two years. Mock windows fall between. A tutor booked in November of DP1 can still change the shape of the whole programme; a tutor booked in February of DP2 is working inside a fixed set of remaining weeks, and the plan has to say what will not be covered.

UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, because none could be confirmed from the IB directly for this project, and a wrong date that a parent plans around is worse than no date at all. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the real calendar, and the first request to make of them is for the internal deadlines in writing: internal assessments, the Extended Essay stages, the TOK components and the mock window.

There is a second thing worth settling early, because it is specific to tutoring in this country and almost nobody explains it. Private tuition in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. If you are considering an independent tutor who will visit a Harbour address, that is a reasonable question to ask them. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

The sections that follow set out the Diploma calendar in planning form, explain who may legally provide private tuition here and how a parent can check, put tutoring cost in context against a Dubai school fee under the current fee position, compare online delivery with what an in-home visit to this district actually involves, describe the regulator map across the emirates, state our coverage limits honestly, and explain the academic-honesty boundary on Diploma coursework. Confirm every date and weighting with your school before you build a plan on it.
