dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-internet-ci.programmesIntro: Internet City families sit across all three school-age IB programmes, usually because older children moved into the Diploma while younger siblings stayed in the primary years at the same school. Each programme is assessed differently, and each one needs a different kind of help at a different point in the year.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Progress is reported through teacher judgement against learning outcomes and through the Exhibition in the final year. Support at this stage is about the two things that carry into MYP: reading fluency and number sense. A child who leaves the PYP able to read a question carefully and estimate whether an answer is sensible will cope with MYP criteria far better than one who has been drilled on content.
programmes.countryNote: Primary-age children in the Internet City and Media City blocks are mostly enrolled at schools in Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and The Greens, with the bus leaving before 07:00. Evening sessions for this age group work best at 16:30 or 17:00, kept to forty minutes, and stopped completely in the fortnight before a school holiday rather than pushed through.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP subjects are marked against four criteria, each scored from 0 to 8, which the school converts to a 1-7 grade using published boundaries. A student can know the content and still lose a grade because the response does not do what the criterion asks. The final year carries the Personal Project, assessed on its own criteria and running across most of the year. Tuition here is mostly about reading the criterion and writing to it.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Year 5 students in this corridor often sit alongside classmates preparing for IGCSE at neighbouring schools, which makes comparing grades confusing for parents. A Dubai MYP 7 and an IGCSE grade 9 are different measurements of different work, and a tutor should explain that before suggesting any change of course.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the creativity, activity, service requirement. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment weighted between a fifth and a quarter of the final grade, marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The written papers come at the end of DP2, which means almost everything a student can still bank in the final six months sits in the IA, the mock evidence and the past-paper work.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students living near Internet City travel to schools across Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim, and the school day usually ends between 14:40 and 15:20. The realistic start for a weekday session here is 16:45, which leaves time for two subjects on different evenings without eating into the weekend coursework block.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-internet-ci.subjectsIntro: The requests that arrive from this corridor cluster around the Higher Level sciences and both Mathematics routes, with English A and Economics close behind. Every subject below is taught at the level your child is actually entered for, against your child's own school deadlines.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry most of the marks. HL students sit an additional paper on extended response work. The common failure is method marks lost to unshown working on questions a student could do mentally.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-dependent work. Graphical display calculator skill is assessed rather than assumed, and students who treat the calculator as a last resort lose marks on questions designed around it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Under the current guide the course is organised into themes rather than topics, with the scientific investigation carrying a fifth of the grade. Uncertainty treatment and graph-gradient interpretation are where competent students lose the most.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most of the lost marks at HL. Students who can recite definitions but cannot explain why a reaction goes one way need mechanism work, not more flashcards.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The command term decides the mark. Outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each demand a different structure, and a correct biological fact written under the wrong command term scores nothing.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, the comparative essay and the individual oral. Students in international schools often read well and still write unfocused responses because the global issue is not anchored to specific extracts.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy drives the marks. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram earns credit that no amount of surrounding prose can replace, and the HL paper rewards quantitative handling.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application against a real organisation. The research project rewards narrow, answerable questions; broad strategy questions produce descriptive answers that cap the mark.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Both are process-assessed. Support means supervision of the student's own thinking, question framing and structure, with written feedback on drafts the student produced.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-internet-ci.modesIntro: Three delivery patterns cover almost every request that comes from this part of Dubai. The right one depends on how far away the next fixed deadline is, not on how much support a family thinks it wants.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across a term
modes.description: One or two sessions a week with the same tutor, following your child's school scheme of work. This is the pattern for a student who is coping but underperforming, and it is the only pattern that reliably changes a predicted grade, because a prediction is built from accumulated classroom evidence rather than from a single strong week.

modes.title: Eight-week intensive block before a mock or final series
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week built around a fixed date. The block opens with a past paper sat under timed conditions, produces a short list of recoverable topics, and spends the remaining weeks on those topics alone. Content the student has already secured is deliberately left untouched, which is what makes the block fit into eight weeks.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Dubai Internet City can realistically start this week
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Dubai Internet City, in practice, means one-to-one teaching for a Diploma or MYP student living in or near the Internet City free zone, delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram matches by subject and level, usually within two to four working days for mainstream Higher Level subjects, and the first lesson is a free trial so a family can judge the match before paying for a block.

The first session is not a sales call. It is a working hour: the tutor asks for the most recent school report, the most recent piece of marked work, and the dates of the next three deadlines. From that, the plan either becomes a term of weekly lessons or an eight-week block aimed at a specific paper. A family that arrives six weeks before mocks gets the second plan whether or not they asked for it, because that is what six weeks can deliver.

What cannot happen is a tutor arriving at an Internet City address. IB Gram does not provide in-person tuition anywhere in the UAE, and no page on this site should be read as offering it. That is a deliberate limit rather than a gap in coverage: the alternative is restricting a Chemistry HL student to tutors who can reach Al Sufouh Road by 17:00, which in this market means a much smaller and much less specialised pool.

The practical shape of a first week, then, is a trial lesson within a few days of enquiry, a short written plan naming the target topics and the deadline they are aimed at, and the first paid session in the same slot the following week.
bullets: Bring the most recent report and one piece of marked work to the trial
Name the next three deadlines, including the school's own IA draft dates
Expect a written plan, not a verbal promise, after the trial
Book the slot your child can actually make every week, not the earliest one

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the final papers
paragraphs: Every Diploma deadline that matters is set months before the exam it feeds. Schools build their internal calendars around that, and parents usually see only the school's version, which is why an IA draft date in October feels arbitrary. It is not. It exists because teacher marking, internal standardisation and the IB's upload window all have to happen before results can be produced, and those steps run on a fixed schedule.

The table below sets out the sequence rather than specific dates, because the only dates worth acting on are the ones your child's school and the awarding body publish for the current session. UAE candidates sit the May session for the Diploma; Cambridge candidates in the UAE enter for the June and November series, and the February/March series is offered in India only. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the November window in 2026 ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January.

Read the sequence from the bottom up and the planning becomes obvious. If results depend on an upload that depends on school marking that depends on a final draft, then the real deadline for a student is the school's draft date, and the real deadline for tuition is six to eight weeks before that. A family that starts tuition after the draft date has already passed is paying for feedback on work that can no longer change.

The second thing the sequence shows is where the quiet months are. The stretch between the start of DP2 and the winter break carries no external deadline at all, which makes it the cheapest and most useful time to fix a weak topic. Tuition bought in that window costs the same per hour as tuition bought in the panic weeks and does several times as much work.

sections.heading: What the next eight weeks have to achieve
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the shortest period in which a Diploma grade can be moved honestly, and it only works if the eight weeks are spent on the right third of the course. The opening session is a full past paper, sat in one sitting, marked against the published scheme with the student watching. That produces a mark breakdown by question rather than a vague sense that physics is hard.

The breakdown almost always shows three categories. There are topics the student has secured, which get no further attention. There are topics where the understanding exists but the marks leak through presentation, unshown working or a misread command term, and those are the cheapest marks on the paper. There is a residue of genuinely unlearned content, which is ranked by how many marks it carries and cut off at whatever can fit in the weeks available.

Weeks two to six attack the leaking marks first and the unlearned content second. Each session ends with a specific set of past-paper questions, and the following session begins with the student's attempt rather than with new teaching. The point of that order is evidence: a student who can produce the method under timed conditions has moved, and a student who cannot has not, whatever either of us felt about the lesson.

The last fortnight is spent entirely on paper behaviour. Question order, time per mark, when to abandon a part question, how to present working so method marks survive a wrong final answer. None of that is new content, and all of it is routinely worth several marks a paper to a student who has never been taught it explicitly.
bullets: Week one: full timed paper, marked openly, broken down by question
Weeks two to four: the leaking marks, because they are the cheapest
Weeks four to six: ranked unlearned content, capped at what fits
Weeks seven and eight: timing, presentation and question selection only

sections.heading: What tuition costs around Internet City, counted by the month
paragraphs: Hourly rates make tutoring sound cheaper than it is, because nobody buys one hour. The number that decides whether a family can sustain support to the end of DP2 is the monthly one. Market estimates published by Bestimate for weekly one-hour sessions in Dubai put a budget arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month, a mid-market qualified tutor at AED 600 to 1,200, and exam-year specialist support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above.

Packaged offers in this market follow the same pattern. Online monthly bundles advertised at around AED 799 for eight sessions work out near AED 100 an hour, which places them firmly in the budget tier and usually means a university-student tutor rather than a subject specialist. In-home monthly packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits price the travel as much as the teaching, and the published rates reflect that: Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted between AED 200 and 500.

Online specialist rates sit between the two. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270; Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above; BartyED advertises AED 650 for premium named tutors. Those are other providers' published figures, cited as the market, not as IB Gram's price list. Our own rate depends on subject, level and block length, and the free trial comes before any of it.

The honest planning number for a Diploma student in this corridor is one or two sessions a week for two terms, with a heavier block in the eight weeks before the final papers. Costed at the mid-market band, that is a sustained commitment rather than an incidental one, which is exactly why the eight-week method above exists.

sections.heading: Online lessons against an in-home visit on the Al Sufouh Road corridor
paragraphs: The case for a tutor in the room is real and worth stating. A younger child works better with an adult beside them, handwriting is easier to correct on paper, and some parents want to see the lesson happening. For a Year 4 reader, that can outweigh everything else. The question is whether it still outweighs everything else for a Higher Level Diploma student eight weeks from a paper.

On this stretch of New Dubai the arithmetic is unusually clear. A tutor travelling to Internet City in the late afternoon is crossing the same Al Sufouh Road and Sheikh Zayed Road load as every school bus in the area. That travel is paid for either in money, through the in-home premium visible in the published rates above, or in time, through a session that starts late and ends at a fixed time anyway. It also narrows the pool: the specialist who has taught the current Chemistry guide may live in Mirdif, and for an in-home arrangement that makes them unavailable.

Online removes the travel from both sides and widens the pool to anyone teaching that subject at that level. It also changes the material. Past papers, mark schemes and worked solutions sit on a shared screen where both people can annotate them, and the whole session can be saved as notes the student rereads the following week. What it demands in return is a workable set-up: a headset, a door that closes, and a parent who checks occasionally that the session is happening rather than being half-attended.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai, so this comparison is not a sales choice we are offering. It is the reasoning behind a limit we have already set, published so that a family can disagree with it and look elsewhere.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the UAE term structure
paragraphs: A tuition plan written in September that ignores the UAE academic calendar breaks twice before the final papers. Dubai private schools run three terms with a long winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break, and the Diploma's heaviest internal deadlines are stacked immediately after one of those breaks rather than before it. A block of lessons that lapses over a holiday and resumes cold has lost more than the fortnight it skipped.

Ramadan changes the day rather than the calendar. School hours shorten, afternoon energy drops sharply, and the useful study window moves to after Iftar. Families who plan for that keep making progress: sessions shift to later in the evening, run shorter, and drop to one a week instead of two. Families who try to hold a 17:00 slot through the month usually cancel half of it and lose the rhythm entirely. Eid holidays then arrive as a genuine break, and the week after is the right moment to sit a timed paper and see what survived.

The practical rule is to write the term's dates down first and fit the lessons around them. Mark the school's own IA and Extended Essay draft dates, the mock window, the breaks, and Ramadan. What remains is the real number of teaching weeks available, and it is almost always fewer than a parent assumed when they counted months. Eight weeks of lessons between now and a mock often means eleven calendar weeks on the actual timetable.

Travel matters here too. Many families in this corridor leave the country for part of the summer and part of the winter break. Online sessions can follow a student to another time zone, which is one of the few genuine logistical advantages of the format, provided the slot is renegotiated rather than simply missed.
bullets: Write the school's term dates and draft deadlines down before booking any block
Expect shorter, later, less frequent sessions through Ramadan
Sit a timed paper in the week after a long break, not before it
Renegotiate the slot for travel rather than cancelling the block

sections.heading: Where the line sits on an Internal Assessment three weeks from the deadline
paragraphs: The pressure point in every Diploma year is a draft that is not working with the school deadline close. It is also where the tutoring market in this region behaves worst: at least one site selling to UAE parents advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Buying one puts a student's entire diploma at risk, because the IB treats submitted work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on the seller.

The useful boundary is simple to state. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, question a research design until its weaknesses are visible, point at a paragraph and say that the analysis does not yet support the conclusion, and model how a different piece of work handled a similar problem. A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure, edit to completion or supply text for any part of the submission, and may not provide data the student did not collect.

In practice that produces a different kind of session. The student reads their own draft aloud while the tutor holds the criteria open by letter. Every piece of feedback is phrased as a question or as a statement about the criterion, and the student leaves with a list of changes to make alone before the next session. The written record of what changed between drafts is also the student's own protection if the authenticity of the work is ever questioned.

Schools are the right partner here, not a workaround. The subject teacher is the person who marks the IA and knows the internal timetable, and a tutor's feedback should be consistent with what that teacher has already said. Where the two conflict, the teacher's reading of the criteria is the one that counts.

sections.heading: KHDA, the school map and what the inspection band actually tells you
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Inspection reports are published on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and parents in this corridor read them closely because the schools their children attend sit across several bands. The band is a judgement about a whole school, not about the Diploma cohort, and a strong school can still have a thin year in one Higher Level subject.

The market around Internet City is unusually dense. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, American at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. For the 2026-27 intake, seven new private schools are opening, four UK curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places; six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by six per cent.

Fees are the other half of the context. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family budgeting tuition on top of fees, a flat fee year is the one year where adding two sessions a week does not compete with an increase already announced.

None of this makes IB Gram a KHDA-regulated provider, and no page here should be read as claiming otherwise. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit; an individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which u.ae states is granted free of charge for two years. We name the regulators because parents should know who to check with, not to borrow their authority.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the date
process.description: The enquiry that gets matched fastest names the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, the school, and the next fixed deadline. Internet City, Media City and Barsha Heights addresses all run on the same evening slot pattern, so the slot question is usually settled in one exchange.

process.title: Match to a specialist, not to a generalist
process.description: Matching is by subject and level. A Chemistry HL request goes to someone who teaches the current Chemistry guide, including the scientific investigation, rather than to a science graduate who can cover any of the three. Mainstream Higher Level subjects are usually matched within two to four working days.

process.title: Sit the free trial lesson
process.description: The trial is a working hour with the most recent marked work on screen. At the end of it you should know what the tutor thinks the problem is, which is a different thing from being told your child has potential. If the match is wrong, say so and we will match again.

process.title: Agree a written plan against the calendar
process.description: The plan names the target topics, the deadline they are aimed at, the session frequency and what the student does between sessions. For an eight-week block it also names the dates of the timed papers, because those are the checkpoints that show whether the marks are moving.

process.title: Review against evidence, not impressions
process.description: Every few weeks the student sits something timed and marked. The plan changes when the evidence changes: a secured topic drops out, a stubborn one gets more time. If the evidence is not moving after a fair run, the honest answer is a different tutor or a different approach, and we will say so.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is the plan
whyPoints.description: Support here is written backwards from the next fixed date rather than forwards from the start of the syllabus. That decides how many sessions a week make sense, which topics get attention and which are deliberately left alone, and it is the difference between eight useful weeks and eight busy ones.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, matched by level
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level request goes to someone who teaches that level, with its additional papers and heavier content. Online delivery is what makes that possible for an Internet City family: the pool is every tutor teaching the subject, not every tutor who can reach Al Sufouh Road by five.

whyPoints.title: Published market rates, not vague reassurance
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are other providers' published figures with the source named, because three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all. You can check every band quoted here before you speak to anybody, including us.

whyPoints.title: A stated limit on what we do
whyPoints.description: IB Gram teaches UAE students online and does not send tutors to UAE addresses. Saying that plainly costs us the families who only want someone in the room, and it means the ones who stay know exactly what they are buying.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty treated as a boundary
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student wrote. Nobody here drafts an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay, and we will say no to that request in writing, because the risk of saying yes lands on the candidate.

whyPoints.title: Regulators named, never borrowed
whyPoints.description: KHDA, the Ministry of Education and MoHRE are described on this page so that parents know which body does what and where to verify a tutor's permit. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them and does not imply one.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who comes to our apartment in Dubai Internet City?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach UAE students one-to-one over live video and do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Independent home tutors do work in this corridor, and published market rates for them run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. If you want someone physically in the room, that is the market to look at. If what you want is a specialist in a particular Higher Level subject at a workable evening time, online is the format that makes it possible.

faqs.question: How many weeks before a Diploma mock should we start tuition in Internet City?
faqs.answer: Eight teaching weeks is the shortest honest run, and because of term breaks and Ramadan that usually means ten or eleven calendar weeks. The first week is spent on a full timed paper so the plan is built from a mark breakdown rather than a guess. Weeks two to six cover the leaking marks and the highest-value unlearned content. The final fortnight is timing and presentation only. Starting with three weeks left is not pointless, but it limits the work to paper technique rather than content, so expect smaller movement.

faqs.question: Which exam series do Cambridge candidates at schools near Internet City actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two open to UAE candidates. The February and March series is offered in India only, so a timetable quoting it does not apply to your child. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your school's exams officer holds the zone.

faqs.question: When do November International GCSE results reach students in the UAE?
faqs.answer: For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the November series sits in late autumn and results follow in January. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. For the previous series, November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Summer results come much faster: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live official timetable on the Pearson qualifications site rather than relying on a date quoted anywhere else.

faqs.question: What does an online IB Diploma tutor cost per hour in Dubai at the moment?
faqs.answer: Published market figures for Dubai put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors advertises IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270; BartyED advertises AED 650 for premium named tutors. Budget online options start far lower, from AED 33 to 65 an hour, which in practice means a university-student tutor. Those are other providers' published rates quoted as market context, not IB Gram's price list.

faqs.question: Is the free trial lesson genuinely free, and what happens in it?
faqs.answer: The trial lesson carries no charge and no card requirement, and you are not committed to a block afterwards. It runs as a working hour: the tutor asks for the most recent school report and one piece of marked work, looks at what the marks actually say, and spends the time teaching rather than selling. At the end you should have a clear statement of what the tutor thinks is going wrong and what the first four sessions would target. If the match feels wrong, tell us and we will match a different tutor.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in Dubai Internet City help with my child's Internal Assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the content behind the task, explain what each assessment criterion asks for, challenge a research design, and give written feedback on a draft the student produced. A tutor cannot write, rewrite, restructure or edit any part of it to completion, and cannot supply data the student did not collect. Sites advertising completed Internal Assessments are selling something the IB treats as malpractice, and the penalty falls on your child rather than on the seller. We refuse that request in writing.

faqs.question: How should sessions change during Ramadan for a student in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and afternoon concentration drops, so the useful window moves to after Iftar. The arrangement that survives the month is a later start, a shorter session and one a week instead of two, agreed before Ramadan begins rather than improvised. Trying to hold a 17:00 slot through the month usually means cancelling half of it and losing the routine. Plan a timed paper for the week after Eid instead of the week before, so you find out what the month actually cost and can adjust the remaining block honestly.

faqs.question: My child goes to school in Al Barsha and gets home at 16:30. What slot works?
faqs.answer: A 16:45 start is realistic for a secondary student on that run, and 17:00 is safer if the bus comes through Hessa Street. Younger children do better at 16:30 with a forty-minute session, before the day catches up with them. Two subjects are best split across different evenings rather than stacked back to back, because the second hour of a double is reliably weaker. Weekend mornings suit Internal Assessment and Extended Essay work, which needs a longer uninterrupted block than a weekday evening offers.

faqs.question: Does a KHDA inspection band tell me whether my child needs a tutor?
faqs.answer: Only indirectly. KHDA publishes inspection judgements for Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and that is a verdict on a whole school across all phases. It says little about one Higher Level subject in one year group, which is the level at which tuition decisions are actually made. The more useful evidence is your child's own marked work, the gap between their current grade and their predicted grade, and whether the subject teacher thinks the problem is content, technique or confidence.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you read as unverified.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects do families around Internet City ask for most often?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, both Mathematics routes, and English A: Language and Literature account for most requests from this corridor, with Economics and Business Management close behind. The pattern follows the schools: the Al Sufouh and Al Barsha secondaries send a lot of students towards engineering, medicine and business degrees, and those routes make the Higher Level sciences and Analysis and Approaches unavoidable. Internal Assessment supervision across any subject is the other steady request, usually arriving three to five weeks before a school draft deadline.

faqs.question: Can online lessons continue when we travel out of the UAE over a school break?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the format's genuine advantages for families in this area, many of whom spend part of the winter and summer breaks abroad. The slot has to be renegotiated rather than simply missed, because a tutor on Gulf Standard Time and a student four hours west need a different hour. Agree the holiday pattern before the break starts: usually one session a week instead of two, with the regular slot resuming on a named date. Sessions that lapse without a resumption date tend not to resume.

faqs.question: What should I expect to see after six weeks of weekly sessions?
faqs.answer: Evidence rather than reassurance. By week six there should be at least two pieces of timed, marked work showing where the marks have moved, a shorter list of weak topics than the one you started with, and a student who can explain what they do differently now in the subject. If none of that exists, the honest conclusion is that the match or the method is wrong, and changing it is better than buying another six weeks of the same. We would rather say that than keep the block running.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-internet-ci.closingHeading: Start from the next date on your child's calendar
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-internet-ci.closingBody: Tell us the subject, the level and the deadline you are working to, and we will match a specialist and put a free trial lesson in a slot your child can actually make from Internet City, Media City or Barsha Heights. After the trial you get a written plan naming the target topics, the timed papers that will test them, and the date each one is aimed at. If a specialist in your subject is not free this week, we will tell you how long the wait is rather than offering a substitute and hoping.

intro.heading: The honest answer to is there anyone out here who knows this syllabus
paragraphs: Dubai Investments Park is a large mixed-use district in the south of the city, split between DIP 1 and DIP 2, with industrial plots, warehousing and commercial space alongside residential communities including Green Community and Ritaj. It sits off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Emirates Road, near Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Jebel Ali and Dubai South, and it has its own Metro station on the line out towards Expo City.

So when a parent here searches for an IB home tutor and the question underneath is whether anyone nearby actually knows the Diploma, the honest answer is: for general support, probably yes, and for a specific Higher Level subject at a specific hour, probably not. That is not a slight on the district. It is arithmetic. The residential population of DIP is smaller than its footprint suggests, and the subset of that population who are qualified Diploma subject teachers, free at five o'clock and holding the MoHRE private tuition work permit required of individuals offering private lessons, is very small indeed.

Narrow the request and it gets smaller. Higher Level Chemistry with real internal assessment experience. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level with Paper 3 practice. Physics with uncertainty and graph technique. Each of those is a genuinely scarce specialism anywhere in Dubai, and in a southern district with limited residential density it can be unavailable on the exact evening a family needs it.

This is the argument for online delivery, and it is a practical argument rather than a marketing one. IB Gram delivers one-to-one Diploma tuition into DIP homes as live online video sessions, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. What that buys a family in Dubai Investments Park is the whole specialist pool rather than the slice of it that can reach a villa in Green Community at half past five.

Two practical facts about the district shape the scheduling. School runs from here go to the DIP schools, to Jebel Ali, to Al Furjan or out towards Dubai South, which means a weekday session realistically starts between 5pm and 5.30pm, and later where the run is long. And several of the schools in the wider southern corridor are recent, so families here supplement more often at senior level than families in older districts do.

The rest of this page is built on that premise and tries to earn it. There is a table setting out why DIP is a structurally hard district for in-home specialist supply, one defining what specialist actually means subject by subject, one disclosing our own coverage and fallback position, and one showing what the Dubai market charges in AED with every figure attributed. Then the regulator, the honesty boundary and how to start.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-investment-.programmesIntro: IB provision in and around Dubai Investments Park runs across the continuum, with two IB schools inside the district itself. Each programme below is described by what it means for a family living out here.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Grades run 1 to 7 for 42 points, with up to three further points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Each subject also carries internally assessed work marked by the school and moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: Almost all DIP tutoring demand sits here, and the scarcity is concentrated in Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. A family in this district asking for Higher Level Physics at 5pm on a Tuesday is asking for the hardest thing in the Dubai market, which is precisely why the delivery model matters.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight and converted to a 1 to 7 grade. MYP 5 includes the Personal Project, developed independently with a process journal. Families find the criterion language hardest, because fluent work can still sit mid-band if it never addressed what the criterion asked.
programmes.countryNote: The two IB schools inside DIP run the continuum, so middle-years support here is mostly criterion translation rather than content teaching. It is also the cheapest point at which a family can intervene, and the one most often skipped because nothing external is yet at stake.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based with no external examinations, closing with the Exhibition in the final year. Reporting is against learner-profile attributes and approaches to learning rather than subject percentages, which reads very differently from the British and Indian curriculum reports many DIP families are used to.
programmes.countryNote: Support at this stage is reading fluency and number sense rather than examination technique. The families who benefit most are those moving from a British or Indian primary into an IB middle school, where the reporting language changes overnight and nobody explains it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma Programme courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, service learning, personal and professional skills and language development. Offered by a small number of UAE schools rather than being widely available, and suited to a student wanting IB subject rigour with an applied qualification.
programmes.countryNote: A DIP family on this route is usually travelling further for school than a Diploma family, which is a real consideration in a district this far south. The tutoring demand comes from the DP courses inside the programme, assessed exactly as in the full Diploma.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-investment-.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects DIP families ask for, described by what they assess and, where it matters, how scarce the specialism genuinely is in this market.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with Paper 3 at Higher Level worth 20 per cent and usually reached late. Most lost marks are notation and justification rather than method. The scarcest Diploma mathematics specialism in Dubai at peak hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use, with fluent graphical display calculator work assumed. The characteristic failure is a correct calculation presented without the sentence of interpretation that answers the question asked.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the most Higher Level weight, with the internal investigation at 20 per cent. Students learn products and are examined on electron movement, which is a technique problem rather than a content one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty treatment, graph gradients with units and explanations that apply a named principle rather than describe a phenomenon. Higher Level adds longer reasoning chains, and the characteristic failure is an answer correct for two steps that then stops.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the grade more than recall does. An answer stating everything known about a topic scores less than one answering only what was asked. Statistical treatment is the weak point in most Higher Level investigations.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, correct labelling and evaluation that reaches a judgement. The internal assessment is three commentaries on published articles with strict word limits, and students lose marks by choosing an article that does not illustrate the intended concept.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, a comparative essay on studied works and the Individual Oral linking a global issue to two texts. Weak responses summarise; strong ones analyse how meaning is constructed and sustain it across the whole answer.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application under time pressure and an internal assessment on a real organisation. Choosing a company the student cannot obtain usable evidence about is the commonest planning error and is discovered far too late to change.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking, the board's own pseudocode conventions and the internal assessment solution for an identified client. Higher Level adds abstract data structures. A genuinely narrow specialism, and one where availability should be checked early.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together worth up to three points on the Diploma matrix. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words with required reflection sessions, and TOK is assessed by exhibition and prescribed-title essay. Both reward a narrow, arguable question.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-investment-.modesIntro: Three delivery patterns cover almost every DIP family. All are live one-to-one video sessions; none involves a tutor travelling to a UAE address.

sections.heading: Why Dubai Investments Park is a hard district for in-home specialists
paragraphs: This is not a criticism of the district and it is not an argument that DIP families are badly served. It is a structural observation with four parts, and understanding it saves a family weeks of calling people who cannot help.

First, land use. DIP is substantially industrial, commercial and warehousing, with residential enclaves inside a large footprint. That means the number of households in the district is low relative to its area, so the number of residents who happen to be qualified Diploma teachers is low in absolute terms, however willing they are.

Second, distance. DIP sits in the southern corridor off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Emirates Road. A tutor living in Al Barsha or Jumeirah can reach several Dubai districts inside twenty minutes at five o'clock; DIP is not usually one of them. In-home tutors ration their evening slots by drive time, and distant districts lose that rationing.

Third, specificity. General tutoring supply is reasonable almost everywhere. Diploma Higher Level supply is not, because each subject at each level is a separate specialism. Fourth, timing: everyone wants the same early-evening hour, and a tutor who drives fits two or three sessions into an evening where a tutor who does not fits four or five. All four factors compound, and they compound hardest on exactly the requests DIP families most often make.

There is a fifth factor that is rarely mentioned and worth knowing. The apparent local supply in any district includes staff at the schools in it, and that supply is not always available to you: in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a comparable code of conduct. So proximity can look like availability while being neither available nor appropriate.

sections.heading: What specialist actually means, subject by subject
paragraphs: Parents use the word specialist and providers agree to it, and the two sides frequently mean different things. So here is a definition that can be tested: a specialist in a Diploma subject is someone who has taught that subject at that level, knows its internal assessment criteria by letter, and can read a marked script from it and name the failing component rather than recommending general revision.

By that definition the market is much thinner than it appears. A tutor who covers all three sciences at Standard Level is a useful generalist and is not a Higher Level Chemistry specialist. A mathematics tutor who has not taught Paper 3 cannot prepare a student for 20 per cent of a Higher Level mathematics grade. Neither is a criticism; it is a mismatch, and it is the family's job to detect it because nobody else will.

Three questions detect it quickly, and they take one phone call. Which level have you taught this subject at, and for how many cohorts? What does criterion D ask for in this subject's internal assessment? And if I send you two marked scripts, can you tell me which component is losing marks before the first session? A specialist answers all three without hesitating, and the third answer is the one that matters.

sections.heading: KHDA, the inspection bands and what a newer school's report means
paragraphs: Every school a DIP child attends is regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak.

In the southern corridor one extra consideration applies. Several schools around Dubai South and Expo City are recent, and a new school in an early inspection cycle is a different proposition from an established school in the same band. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four British curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 with enrolment rising 6 per cent. Read the inspection report rather than the headline band, because the report usually says where a young school is in its development.

The band is also a whole-school judgement, which means it tells you very little about the one thing that matters if your child sits Higher Level Chemistry: whether Higher Level Chemistry is being taught well this year. A moderate Diploma cohort, which is what most DIP-area schools have, can be affected immediately by a single mid-year staffing change, and that is nobody's fault and still needs covering.

For scale, the Dubai private sector in 2024-25 held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula, with 7 per cent of students on an IB programme. Useful background, and no substitute for the subject-level evidence: which paper the marks are falling on, how the internal assessment draft scores against the criteria, and whether the gap is content or technique.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: One operator researched for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. The price is worth naming because it tells you what the market looks like to a stressed DP2 student: the product exists, it is advertised, and it is findable in a minute. Buying one is an academic honesty breach that can cost the entire Diploma, and the consequence falls on the student.

IB Gram does not write, complete, edit to completion or supply coursework of any kind, and no tutor working through us is permitted to. What a tutor does instead is teach the assessment: explaining each criterion in the IB's own terms, pressing on a research question until it can generate usable data, reading the student's own draft and saying which criterion it fails and why, and teaching whatever skill the draft reveals is missing.

The practical test for a family is simple. After a session, could your child explain and defend every change to their own work, in their own words? If yes, that was teaching. If no, the line has been crossed, and the school's academic honesty policy is the document that will decide the outcome.

A second boundary concerns materials. We do not publish, reproduce or offer IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables as downloads, because that material is the boards' copyright and unreleased content carries a malpractice exposure. We cite the official source, link to it, and work from what your child's school legitimately provides.

sections.heading: The calendar a DIP household has to hold
paragraphs: Many families in this district have children on two different systems at once, because the southern corridor mixes IB and British-curriculum schools and siblings are often split between them. That makes the household calendar more complicated than a single school's, and it is worth drawing once rather than rediscovering each term.

On the IB side, UAE schools sit the May session. Everything decisive before it is set by the school rather than by the IB: internal assessment deadlines, Extended Essay reflection sessions, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition, the mock window. IB session and results dates are not independently verified in this project, because ibo.org blocks automated access, so take any specific date from your child's IB coordinator rather than from a tutoring page.

On the Cambridge and Pearson side the position is published and clearer. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with the February and March series offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate sits June with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Both publish provisional timetables ahead of a series and revise them, so the official live document is the one to plan from.

Two checkable reference points, useful because they are the kind of thing a parent can verify: Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

paragraphs: The sequence is short. Send the subject, the level, the school and the last two marked pieces of work, whether a paper or an internal assessment draft. A specialist reading those can usually name the failing component in one sentence, and the free trial lesson exists to produce that before any payment.

Then the part this page has been building towards. Because specialist supply is genuinely constrained for the narrowest requests, booking earlier than feels necessary is worth real money out here. If you know a block is coming after mocks, agreeing the pattern now costs nothing and secures the slot. If we cannot cover the request, you will be told with a date rather than offered a substitute.

What will not be claimed. No grade promise, because nobody can honestly make one. No suggestion that tutoring is required for Ministry of Education equivalency, university admission or school progression, because that would be a false claim about a regulatory process. No regulator or board approval: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office, centre or branch. No satisfaction statistics, because a figure without its sample, date and method is decoration.

One last fact worth carrying into any conversation with any provider in this market. Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; it is granted free of charge for two years, eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB tutor near Dubai Investments Park who knows the Diploma?
faqs.answer: For general support, probably. For a specific Higher Level subject at a specific early-evening hour, local supply is genuinely thin, and we would rather say that than pretend otherwise. DIP is largely industrial and commercial land with residential enclaves, so resident numbers are low relative to the district's size, and qualified Diploma subject teachers who are also free at 5pm and hold the MoHRE private tuition permit are few. Online delivery removes the constraint by removing the drive.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our home in Green Community or Ritaj?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one Diploma tuition into Dubai Investments Park homes as live online sessions on Gulf Standard Time, and we send no tutors to any UAE address; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. Other Dubai providers do offer them at roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, per Bestimate's 2026 rate table, though arranging one this far south at a peak hour is harder than the rates alone suggest.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a tutor is really a subject specialist?
faqs.answer: Three questions on one call. Which level have you taught this subject at, and for how many cohorts? What does a particular internal assessment criterion ask for in this subject? And if I send two marked scripts, can you name the component losing marks before the first session? A specialist answers all three without hesitation, and the third answer is the one that distinguishes teaching from general support. Hesitation on the second question is itself an answer.

faqs.question: Which schools do children in Dubai Investments Park attend?
faqs.answer: Several are inside the district itself, including two IB schools and a British-curriculum school, with the International School of Choueifat also in DIP. Beyond it, families travel to the wider southern corridor: long-established British schools in Jebel Ali, a British school in Al Furjan, an IB school in The Sustainable City and newer provision around Dubai South. All are regulated by KHDA. We name them as market context only; IB Gram has no relationship with any of them and none is a client.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot find a tutor for our subject?
faqs.answer: You are told, given the nearest workable alternative and given a realistic date for when the slot you wanted is likely to open. Higher Level Physics is the hardest to cover at peak hours, with Higher Level Chemistry and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches close behind, and the constraint is sharpest in the weeks before the May session. What will not happen is a generalist being presented as the specialist you asked for, which is the standard failure mode in this market.

faqs.question: Could our tutor be based outside the UAE?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and if so it is stated rather than concealed. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for a subject, the match may be a teacher working from outside the country on Gulf Standard Time. Several providers hide this behind a non-UAE contact number, which is a trust failure rather than a delivery problem. The test that matters is unchanged: has this person taught this subject at this level, and can they name the failing component from a marked script?

faqs.question: Why is Higher Level Physics so hard to arrange?
faqs.answer: Because it is a narrow specialism competing for the narrowest window. Every DP2 household in Dubai wants the same early-evening hour, physics teachers who can also teach uncertainty technique and extended reasoning are a small group, and a tutor who drives fits fewer sessions into an evening than one who does not. The practical response is to agree the slot pattern before mocks rather than after results, which costs nothing and secures the time.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a compromise for a family this far south?
faqs.answer: It is the opposite, which is the point of this page. In a dense district with schools inside it, online delivery is roughly equivalent to in-home. In Dubai Investments Park it is better, because it is the only way to reach the specialist your child actually needs rather than whoever is willing to drive out at five o'clock. The compromise is the in-home version, and the compromise is in the choice of teacher rather than in the format.

faqs.question: How early should we book before the May session?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, and earlier here than in a central district. If you anticipate a block after mocks, agree the pattern now: it costs nothing, it secures the slot, and it means the plan can start on the week the mock results arrive rather than three weeks later. Narrow Higher Level specialisms at early-evening hours are the first thing to disappear, and the families who get them are the ones who asked before they needed them.

faqs.question: Our children are at an IB school and a British school. Can one plan cover both?
faqs.answer: The scheduling can be shared and the subject matching cannot. Each child is matched to a specialist in their own system, because Diploma internal assessment criteria and IGCSE paper structures are different things. What a single provider can do is sequence the sessions so one evening is not overloaded, keep one point of contact for the household, and help you draw the combined calendar once, which in the southern corridor is genuinely complicated because the two systems have different deadline rhythms.

faqs.question: Does living in a mostly industrial district affect what schools are nearby?
faqs.answer: Less than you would expect. Despite the industrial and warehousing land use, Dubai Investments Park contains two IB schools and a British-curriculum school within the district, which is better provision than the land use suggests. The wider southern corridor adds long-established British schools in Jebel Ali and newer schools around Dubai South and Expo City. What the land use does affect is resident tutor supply, which is the problem this page addresses.

faqs.question: Should we be worried that our school is new?
faqs.answer: Not worried, but read the inspection report rather than the band. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four British curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 with enrolment rising 6 per cent. A new school in an early inspection cycle is a different proposition from an established school in the same band, and KHDA's report usually says where a young school is in its development.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around a long school run and after-school activities?
faqs.answer: That is most of what scheduling in this corridor involves. Discovery Gardens and Dubai South runs are long in both directions, so a realistic weekday start is 5pm to 6pm depending on the school, and weekend mornings carry work that needs a longer unbroken session, such as internal assessment coaching. Because nothing depends on a tutor's drive time, the slot can be set by your household's actual day rather than by what a visiting tutor can reach.

intro.heading: The question underneath the search
paragraphs: A parent in a Marina tower typing a search for a nearby IB tutor is rarely interested in geography for its own sake. The real question is whether anybody within reach actually teaches the course their child is taking: not the International Baccalaureate in general, but Chemistry at Higher Level, or Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Economics with an internal assessment due in eleven weeks. Proximity is a proxy that parents use because it is the only filter a search engine offers them. It is a poor one, and the honest thing to do is explain why rather than pretend to satisfy it.

Consider what the Diploma actually asks. A student carries six subjects across the groups, three of them at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and an internal assessment in almost every subject. Each of those internal assessments is marked against published criteria with letters and mark allocations that differ by subject. A tutor who is strong in one subject at Standard Level is not interchangeable with one who has supervised twenty Higher Level explorations in another. Any parent who has watched a well-meaning generalist try to help with a Physics investigation knows this already.

Now consider the pool. Dubai had 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25, offering seventeen curricula, and the International Baccalaureate accounted for seven per cent of enrolment against thirty-seven per cent for the UK curriculum. Seven per cent is a real number of students and a small number of specialist teachers, and they are not distributed evenly across the city. Narrow that further to people who teach a particular Higher Level subject, are available at six on a Tuesday, and are willing to drive into a Marina tower and find parking: you are not choosing from a market any more, you are taking what is left.

The Marina itself compounds the problem in a way its residents recognise immediately. It is overwhelmingly residential high-rise. The secondary campuses that Marina and JBR families actually use sit outside the neighbourhood, along Al Sufouh, in Al Barsha and out towards Emirates Hills, which means the school run already consumes the early afternoon. Add a visiting tutor's own journey into the same window and the earliest realistic session drifts past six o'clock, which is after the point at which a tired sixteen-year-old does useful analytical work.

So here is the position stated plainly. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. What we do instead is match on the subject and the level, and deliver the lesson one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. A Marina family gets the Chemistry Higher Level specialist rather than whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive. The rest of this page is the detail behind that claim: the arithmetic of local availability, the six questions that test whether a tutor really knows a syllabus, what an in-home arrangement involves in this neighbourhood, how to check a tutor may legally work here, and what happens when the honest answer is that nobody is free.

What follows is what each programme assesses and what it means for finding help in this part of Dubai, where provision is strong but option blocks are narrow.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry organised around six themes, with no external examinations and an exhibition at the end of the programme. Assessment is continuous and teacher-led, so a parent rarely sees a mark they can interpret. Support at this stage is about literacy and number fluency rather than about the programme itself, because the habits that matter later are reading volume and arithmetic confidence, neither of which the programme measures directly.
programmes.countryNote: Several campuses used by Marina and JBR households run the Primary Years Programme and then hand students to a Middle Years Programme or a British Year 7, so the transition point varies by school. Confirm which route your child's campus uses before worrying about programme-specific support; at this age almost nothing needs it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each with published strands and achievement levels from one to eight. The criteria are the key to the whole thing: a student who does not know which criterion a task is marked against cannot aim at it. In the final year a Personal Project is completed, supervised in school, and it is the first piece of extended independent work most students meet.
programmes.countryNote: In the Marina cluster the common pattern is an MYP student whose school reports criterion levels that parents find impossible to interpret against the British grades their friends receive. Translating a report into what the criteria actually reward is often the single most useful first conversation with a tutor.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Most subjects carry an internal assessment marked against published criteria, and the external papers vary in weighting by subject and level. The load is not one subject at a time: it is six concurrent courses with coursework deadlines that collide in the second year.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Marina families most often look outside the school. The reason is structural rather than a comment on teaching: option blocks in any single campus are finite, so a student's third Higher Level is frequently the one with the thinnest specialist cover in the building.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Fewer campuses offer it and fewer parents have heard of it, which means that when a student is on it, finding anybody who has taught the reflective project is genuinely difficult. Where the Diploma courses are shared, subject support works exactly as it does for a Diploma student.
programmes.countryNote: Rarely offered in the New Dubai cluster, but worth naming because families comparing schools sometimes encounter it and assume it is a lesser Diploma. It is a different qualification with a different purpose, and the subject-level support available for it is thinner across the whole emirate.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-marina.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma subjects Marina and JBR families most often ask about, with what each actually assesses and where marks go missing. Read the descriptions as a shortlist for the conversation with a tutor: a specialist should recognise every detail here without hesitation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with Higher Level carrying an additional paper that rewards sustained multi-step reasoning. The exploration is marked against published criteria including personal engagement and reflection, which students consistently underweight. Marks go missing on notation, on unjustified steps and on calculator work that is not communicated in the script.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving. Often assumed to be the easier route and in fact a different one: it demands confident interpretation of real data and clear written explanation of what a model means. Students who chose it to avoid algebra and then meet the statistics content find the Higher Level version unexpectedly demanding.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The subject Marina families ask about most at Higher Level. Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics carry the conceptual load, and the scientific investigation is marked against published criteria that reward a focused research question above an ambitious one. Marks are lost on uncertainty treatment and on conclusions that restate the data instead of evaluating it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward precision with units, prefixes and significant figures, where a correct method and a sloppy final line still lose the mark. The investigation needs a measurable variable and a realistic uncertainty analysis, and the commonest failure is a question that cannot be answered with the equipment available to a school laboratory.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content plus data analysis. Higher Level adds depth in physiology and genetics, and the papers reward precise use of command terms far more than students expect. The investigation often founders on a design that produces a trend without a controlled variable, which no amount of writing afterwards can repair.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, evaluation and the internal assessment portfolio of commentaries on published news articles. Higher Level adds quantitative content and a policy paper. The commentary is where marks are won and lost: a clear link between a specific article, a named concept and a diagram beats a general discussion of the topic every time.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary and literary texts, an individual oral built on a global issue, and comparative analysis under time pressure. The individual oral is the component students prepare least and the one where a weak global issue cannot be rescued by good delivery. Higher Level adds an essay that demands sustained argument rather than close reading alone.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source evaluation, essay argument and a historical investigation marked against published criteria. The investigation rewards a tightly bounded question and genuine engagement with the limitations of the sources used. Higher Level adds regional depth studies, where the volume of specific detail required catches students who have revised themes rather than cases.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, theories and a research project at Higher Level built on primary and secondary evidence. The common failure is a project built on a question the student cannot actually get data for, which becomes apparent far too late. The papers reward application to the named organisation rather than recitation of the tool.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, with an experimental study written up to published criteria. Students lose marks on the inferential statistics and on an analysis section that describes the result without interpreting it. Specialist cover for this subject at Higher Level is thin across the whole emirate, not only in the Marina.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Comparative study, process portfolio and exhibition. Included because it is the subject where families most often assume no tutoring is possible and where process-portfolio support against the published criteria frequently makes the largest difference. The work remains entirely the student's own; a tutor's role is criteria literacy and feedback.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, both marked against published criteria and both routinely left too late. Theory of Knowledge is not a subject a student can revise, so support means structured thinking practice and a hard internal deadline, delivered early enough to be useful rather than in the final fortnight.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-marina.regionsTitle: The Marina cluster, and what the local specialist pool looks like in each part of it
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-marina.regionsIntro: These are the communities around Dubai Marina whose families ask the same question for the same reason. The differences that matter are which campuses the household is attached to and how much of the afternoon the journey consumes.

regions.name: JBR
regions.note: Immediately adjacent and functionally part of the same catchment. Households here face the same constraint as the Marina: towers, no secondary campus inside the community, and a school run that uses the early afternoon before any tutor could arrive.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, with its own tower density and a mixture of school attachments. JLT families ask more often about Middle Years Programme criteria and less often about a third Higher Level, which is a genuine difference in the enquiry mix rather than a slogan.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: Reached by a single bridge, which makes any visiting arrangement hostage to one route. Families here were among the first to tell us that a fixed video slot was more reliable than an appointment that depended on a causeway at half past five.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Where several of the campuses Marina families use actually sit. Households in Al Sufouh have the shortest school run in the cluster, which pushes the earliest workable session earlier and makes a five o'clock start realistic rather than theoretical.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Lower-rise and closer to Al Khail Road, with a noticeable share of Diploma students whose third Higher Level is the subject in question. The requests from here are disproportionately for specific Higher Level sciences rather than for general support.

regions.name: The Springs and The Meadows
regions.note: Villa communities inland from the Marina, where families often have two or three children on different programmes. Scheduling consecutive slots for siblings is straightforward over video and close to impossible with a visiting tutor in one evening.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Attached to campuses out along the same corridor, with longer runs in both directions. Sessions here settle later in the evening, and the subjects requested skew towards Higher Level mathematics and the Extended Essay.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: A single access road and a long internal distance, which makes the travel calculation worse than the map suggests. Enquiries from the Palm come with more term-time travel than other communities, so a schedule that follows a laptop matters here.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Further inland with a different school mix again, and a higher share of Middle Years Programme and IGCSE enquiries than Diploma ones. Worth listing because Marina families comparing notes with friends here are often comparing different problems.

schoolClusters.city: Campuses Marina and JBR households most often attend
schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend these schools; they are named as context about the cluster a Marina family chooses within, not as any relationship. What matters for finding a tutor is that option blocks and Higher Level combinations change by cohort, so confirm what actually runs in your child's year with the school rather than with a prospectus.

schoolClusters.city: Campuses reached inland along Al Khail Road and Hessa Street
schoolClusters.note: The second ring a Marina household realistically commutes to. The relevance to tutoring is the clock: a longer and less predictable afternoon run pushes the earliest workable session later, which is worth establishing before a weekly slot is agreed rather than after two cancellations.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-marina.modesIntro: Three shapes of support that Marina families use, with what each is honestly for. All of it is one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we provide only in India, and this page compares the two rather than blurring them.

modes.title: A Higher Level subject specialist, weekly
modes.description: The commonest request from this cluster and the one the whole page is about. A tutor matched to the exact subject and level, following the school's sequence, working on the student's own problems and marking against the published criteria. The point is the match: a Chemistry Higher Level specialist rather than a science tutor who will read ahead.

modes.title: Two subjects, two tutors, one evening
modes.description: A pattern that works over video and collapses in person. Two specialists in consecutive slots on the same evening, each strong in their own subject, rather than one convenient person stretching across both. Households in The Springs and Emirates Hills use this most, usually for a Higher Level science and mathematics.

Each subject taught by someone who teaches it at that level
