modes.title: Coursework supervision blocks
modes.description: A short series of sessions tied to one internal assessment, the Extended Essay or the Theory of Knowledge exhibition, timed to the school's internal deadlines rather than to the examination. The work remains the student's own throughout; what a tutor adds is criteria literacy, a view on whether a research question is answerable, and a hard deadline that is not the school's.
bullets: Research question stress-tested before any data is collected

sections.heading: The arithmetic of a local search, done honestly
paragraphs: Work the numbers rather than the feeling. Dubai has 227 private schools and 387,441 private pupils across seventeen curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for seven per cent of enrolment. That seven per cent is spread across the emirate, and the teachers who serve it are concentrated at the campuses that run the programme. Narrow to a single Diploma subject at Higher Level and the set of people who teach it in Dubai is a few dozen rather than a market. Narrow again to those willing and able to reach a Marina tower on a weekday at five: you are now choosing from a handful.

A parent who hires the best available tutor from that handful has done something quite reasonable and quite different from hiring the best available specialist in that subject. The distinction is invisible until it matters, which is usually the term the internal assessment is due. At that point the question stops being whether the tutor is good with teenagers and becomes whether they can look at a research question and say, within a minute, that it will not generate data capable of supporting a conclusion. That is a specific, learned judgement and it does not correlate with proximity at all.

The table below is the shape of the problem by subject. It is not a precise census and we do not publish one, because any headcount we printed would be unverifiable and this market already has enough unverifiable numbers in it. What the table does instead is describe availability honestly in words: which subjects we can usually match quickly, which take longer, and which we sometimes cannot cover at the time a family wants. That disclosure is uncommon in this SERP and it is the thing a parent can actually use.

The practical conclusion is to invert the search. Instead of asking who is near the Marina and then asking what they teach, ask who teaches this subject at this level and then ask when they are free. The second order produces a better tutor almost every time, and the only thing it costs is the idea of someone sitting at the dining table.

sections.heading: Why a recommendation between Marina families so often disappoints
paragraphs: The most common route to a tutor in this neighbourhood is a message in a building group or a conversation at the school gate. A friend's son improved, the tutor is available, the rate is known, and the arrangement starts the following week. Perhaps a third of the time it works well. The rest of the time it underperforms, and the reason is almost never that the tutor was bad.

What transfers in a recommendation is reliability, manner and whether the tutor turns up. What does not transfer is the subject-and-level match, which is the thing that actually determines the outcome. A tutor who was excellent for a Standard Level Mathematics student revising for papers is being asked to do something else entirely for a Higher Level student with an exploration due. A tutor who steadied a Middle Years Programme student through criterion-based assessment is not therefore equipped for a Diploma internal assessment with a different criteria structure.

There is a second mismatch that recommendations hide: what the student needed. One child needed a weekly adult who would make them sit down and work, and the tutoring was effectively supervised study with some teaching in it. Another child works willingly for three hours a night and is losing marks because nobody has told them their research question is unanswerable. Both families describe the purchase as a tutor, and the two purchases have almost nothing in common.

The useful way to use a recommendation is as evidence of character and nothing else. Then ask the subject questions separately, and ask them as though no recommendation existed. If a tutor recommended for Economics cannot describe how the internal assessment commentaries are marked, the recommendation is still true and still irrelevant.
bullets: A recommendation evidences reliability, not subject-and-level fit
Standard Level revision help and Higher Level coursework support are different jobs
Middle Years criteria and Diploma internal assessment criteria are different structures
Ask what the other family actually bought: supervision, teaching or criteria coaching
Then test the subject knowledge yourself, as though no recommendation existed

sections.heading: Six questions that test whether a tutor really knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Parents are often reluctant to interrogate a tutor, partly out of courtesy and partly because they do not feel qualified to judge the answers. In fact you do not need to judge the content of the answer at all. You need only notice whether it arrives immediately and specifically, or arrives wrapped in generalities. A specialist answers these in one sentence each. A willing generalist takes a paragraph and tells you about their approach.

Ask what the internal assessment in this subject is marked against, by name. A specialist will name the criteria and roughly what each is worth. Ask what the commonest reason is that students lose marks in this subject at this level. A specialist has three answers ready and will choose one. Ask what the difference between Higher and Standard Level actually is in this subject, since it varies: more content in one, an extra paper in another, a different internal assessment weighting in a third.

Then ask three practical ones. What would you want to see before the first lesson? The right answer involves the student's own work, not a questionnaire. How will I know in six weeks whether this is working? The right answer involves a marked piece of work compared against a previous one, not a progress report. And what would make you tell me to stop paying? A tutor who cannot answer that last one has never thought about it, which tells you something.

Use the free trial for this. The whole purpose of a trial lesson is to watch a tutor teach your child rather than to hear a coordinator describe a methodology, and the questions above take four minutes at the end of it. The table sets out the six with what a good answer sounds like, in a form you can keep open on a phone during the call.

sections.heading: Option blocks, and why the third Higher Level is the one that needs help
paragraphs: There is a structural reason that Diploma families go looking outside the school, and it has nothing to do with the quality of teaching. A school builds option blocks to fit a timetable and a cohort. With a finite number of students and a finite number of teachers, the blocks constrain which combinations of six subjects are actually possible. A student who wants Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics at Higher Level may find two of them available together and the third sitting in a block that clashes.

What usually happens next is a compromise. The student takes the third Higher Level in a subject they wanted less, or takes the subject they wanted in a group where the school has one teacher covering two levels. In a large cohort that is manageable. In a smaller one, which includes several of the campuses this cluster uses, it means a Higher Level set of a handful of students taught alongside a Standard Level group, or taught by a teacher whose own specialism is the adjacent subject.

This is why the enquiries from The Greens, The Views and Emirates Hills skew so heavily towards one specific Higher Level subject rather than towards general support. The family is not dissatisfied with the school. They have identified, correctly, that one of their child's six courses has thinner cover than the others, and they want that one course supported properly. It is a precise purchase and it should be priced and matched as one.

The practical advice is to establish this early. In the spring of the first Diploma year, ask the school which Higher Level sets are small, which are taught alongside Standard Level groups, and which teacher holds each subject. None of that is secret and all of it is useful. A family who knows in April that the third Higher Level has thin cover can arrange support in September, which is a different and much better conversation than the one that starts in February with an internal assessment due.

sections.heading: What an in-home arrangement in this neighbourhood actually involves
paragraphs: This deserves to be set out on the facts, because a parent searching for a home tutor is entitled to know what the market offers before being told what we do instead. Published market figures put in-home one-to-one tutoring in this country at AED 180 to 350 an hour according to Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, with independent home tutors quoted from AED 200 to 500 inclusive of travel. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits circulate in this market. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200.

The difference between those bands is the travel premium, and in the Marina it buys something quite concrete: a journey into a high-rise community with visitor parking constraints, at the hour when Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road are at their worst, for one hour of teaching. A tutor pricing that journey honestly has to charge for it, and a tutor who does not charge for it will quietly prefer clients closer to home. Neither outcome favours a family in a tower on the water.

The second cost is invisible and larger. Restricting the search to people who will make that journey restricts it to people who live nearby, and the pool of Higher Level specialists who happen to live within a short drive of the Marina is small. The premium therefore buys a commute while simultaneously reducing the quality of the choice, which is the opposite of what the parent paying it intends.

There are cases where a person in the room is genuinely better, and they should be named. A younger child who will not engage with a screen. A student who needs an adult physically present to start work at all. A subject requiring shared physical equipment. A Diploma student at sixteen or seventeen working on an exploration, a commentary or a past paper is none of those: the materials are a document, a criteria sheet and a script, all of which work better on a shared screen that saves the annotation. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. The table compares the two models on the dimensions that change the result.

sections.heading: Checking that a private tutor may lawfully teach in the UAE
paragraphs: A parent hiring privately in Dubai should ask one question that almost nobody asks, and the answer is a matter of public record rather than opinion. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

Two consequences follow for a Marina household. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the ministry are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any specific amount you see quoted online is unverified and should be treated as such. And because the permit is free and takes a stated two working days through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system under the service titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, there is no good reason for a working tutor not to hold one. Asking is reasonable and a professional will not be offended.

There is a further restriction that matters specifically when a family is tempted by the most convenient option of all. Press reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the permit's code of conduct also barring service to students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as the authority's exact wording and verify it against the current policy document, but take the direction seriously: your child's own teacher, privately, is not a route to pursue.

The institutional side is worth stating too, because it is where this market makes its loosest claims. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs an educational services permit for a training institute from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. IB Gram occupies no premises in the UAE, holds no such permit, and claims no approval, accreditation or endorsement from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the ministry of human resources, the IB or any examination board. Any page that claims otherwise about itself is worth reading twice.

sections.heading: What the trial lesson should prove, and what it cannot
paragraphs: A free trial is only useful if you know what you are watching for, and most families watch for the wrong thing. The instinct is to see whether the tutor and the child get on. That matters, but it is also the easiest thing in the world for a pleasant adult to achieve in an hour and it predicts very little about the next six months.

What a trial can prove is subject depth. Give the tutor a piece of your child's own marked work in advance and watch what they do with it. A specialist will find the pattern in it within a few minutes, name it, and work on that rather than on a prepared introductory topic. They will refer to the criteria or the mark scheme without being asked. They will ask your child to justify an answer rather than confirming it. And they will say something your child has not heard before, which is the clearest single signal available.

What a trial cannot prove is whether your child will do the work between sessions, which is the largest variable in the whole arrangement and the one no tutor controls. It also cannot prove that the match is right for a component the lesson did not touch. A tutor who is excellent on past-paper technique may be untested on an internal assessment, so if the coursework is the reason you are hiring, make the trial about the coursework.

Our own position on trials is deliberate: a full lesson with the tutor your child would actually keep, before any payment, rather than a consultation with a coordinator. If the honest outcome of that lesson is that your child does not need weekly support, or needs it in a different subject, that is a legitimate result and we will say so.

sections.heading: The schools around the Marina, and reading a KHDA report properly
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are inspected by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and inspection outcomes are reported on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. For a Marina family the report is useful in a narrow and specific way that has little to do with the headline band.

The columns to read are attainment and progress, and they are not the same thing. Attainment describes how students perform against expectations. Progress describes how far they have moved. A subject with Good attainment and Acceptable progress is a subject where capable students are coasting, and that is precisely the pattern that produces a Diploma student who has always been fine at Chemistry and is suddenly not fine at Higher Level Chemistry. A family reading only the overall band will miss it entirely.

The context is also worth holding. Dubai's private sector added six schools during 2025-26 with enrolment rising six per cent, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven more private schools, four following the UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. The authority also confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family budgeting tuition alongside fees, that freeze is the relevant anchor.

One further thing a Marina parent should know about every Dubai private school regardless of its curriculum: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory, with the authority's requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes.

sections.heading: When the honest answer is that nobody is free
paragraphs: Every page in this market promises availability and none of them discusses its limits, which is how a parent ends up with a willing generalist in a Higher Level subject. We would rather publish the limit. There are subjects and time slots where we cannot match a specialist quickly, and in the Marina cluster the pinch points are predictable: Higher Level Psychology, Higher Level Business Management, Visual Arts process portfolio work, and any subject at five o'clock on a Tuesday or Wednesday, which are the two most requested hours in New Dubai.

When that happens there are three honest options and we will put all three to you. Wait, usually a week or two, for the specialist to have a slot. Take a different hour, often a weekend morning, which for extended coursework work is frequently better anyway. Or decide not to proceed, which costs you nothing because the trial has not happened and no payment has been taken. What we will not do is place a tutor who does not hold the subject at that level and hope the family does not notice until February.

There is a fourth situation worth naming. Sometimes the right answer is that tutoring is not the purchase. A student who is not doing the work set by a perfectly good school does not need a seventh hour of instruction; they need the six they already have to land. A student whose internal assessment research question is unanswerable needs one hour with a specialist to find that out, not twenty hours of weekly support. We say these things in the diagnostic conversation, before money moves.

The reason for publishing all of this is simple. A parent in a Marina tower searching for someone nearby who knows the syllabus is asking a sensible question and getting, from most of this market, an answer designed to close a sale. The arithmetic says proximity does not deliver what they want. The honest alternative is a specialist over live video, a trial before payment, and a plain statement when we cannot help.

process.title: Name the subject and the level first
process.description: Not the programme and not the year group. Chemistry at Higher Level with an investigation due in the spring is a brief. IB help for a Year 12 student is not. The subject and level determine which specialists exist, and everything about scheduling comes after that rather than before it.

process.title: Send a piece of your child's own marked work
process.description: A returned internal assessment draft with the teacher's comments, or a marked past paper. Ten minutes with real work tells a specialist more than a half-hour call, and it lets us say honestly whether the problem is a knowledge gap, a criteria gap or a work-rate problem that no tutor fixes.

process.title: Hear the availability before the pitch
process.description: We tell you whether a specialist is free in your preferred hour, how long the wait is if not, and whether this is a subject where our cover is genuinely thin. Marina families overwhelmingly want five or six in the evening, and those slots fill. You get the real answer before any payment.

process.title: Use the free trial to test subject depth
process.description: A full lesson with the tutor your child would keep, not a consultation with a coordinator. Watch whether the tutor works from your child's own script, refers to the criteria unprompted, and says something your child has not heard before. Ask the six questions at the end; they take four minutes.

process.title: Set a review that uses marked work
process.description: Every four to six weeks, a marked piece compared with an earlier one against the same criteria. If the comparison does not show movement, the approach changes or we tell you to stop paying. An opinion about progress is not a review, and a monthly report that contains no marked work is an opinion.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level, not on distance
whyPoints.description: The search a Marina parent runs is for someone nearby; the thing they actually need is someone who teaches that subject at that level. We invert the order deliberately, because the pool of Higher Level specialists living within a short drive of the Marina is small and choosing from it is not the same as choosing well.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed, including its limits
whyPoints.description: There are subjects and hours where we cannot match quickly, and we name them: Higher Level Psychology, Higher Level Business Management, Visual Arts portfolio work, and five o'clock on the two busiest evenings. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit, and it is the most useful thing a parent can be told.

whyPoints.title: The internal assessment line is explicit
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reviews the student's own draft and explains the criteria letter by letter. A tutor does not write, redraft or complete an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. The risk of a breach falls on the student, so the boundary is on the page rather than in a private message.

whyPoints.title: You can test the tutor yourself
whyPoints.description: Six questions are published above with what a real answer sounds like, so a parent who does not know the subject can still judge the specialist. We would rather hand over that checklist than ask anyone to take a claim about tutor quality on trust.

whyPoints.title: Figures are other providers', named and dated
whyPoints.description: Every AED rate on this page is a published market figure from a named source in 2026, quoted so you can check it. There is no IB Gram rate card here, no invented statistic, no self-reported rating and no grade promise, because an unsourced number is a liability rather than a selling point.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. The comparison between the two models is published above on the dimensions that change the result.

faqs.question: Is there an IB home tutor in Dubai Marina who teaches my child's Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: Probably not in the way the question imagines, and the honest answer is worth more than a reassuring one. IB programmes account for about seven per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, so the pool of specialists in any one Higher Level subject is small and concentrated at the campuses that run the programme. Narrow it to people who will drive into a Marina tower at five in the evening and you are choosing from a handful. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; we match on the subject and level and teach over live video, which is how a Marina family reaches the specialist rather than the nearest option.

faqs.question: Do you have a tutor who actually lives in Dubai Marina?
faqs.answer: Where a tutor lives is not something we match on, and we would not build the service around it even if we could. The variable that determines whether a Diploma student improves is whether the tutor teaches that subject at that level and has supervised that internal assessment before. Residence predicts none of that. What we do instead is match by subject and level, deliver the lesson one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and tell you plainly how long a match will take. Home visits are a service we provide only in India, not anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a tutor really knows the IB syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask six questions and listen for speed and specificity rather than judging the content. What is the internal assessment in this subject marked against, by name? Where do students most often lose marks at this level? What actually differs between Higher and Standard Level in this subject, since it varies by subject? What do you want to see before the first lesson? How will I know in six weeks whether this is working? And what would make you tell me to stop paying? A specialist answers each in a sentence. A generalist answers in a paragraph about their approach.

faqs.question: Why do tutor recommendations between Marina families so often disappoint?
faqs.answer: Because what transfers in a recommendation is reliability and manner, and what does not transfer is the subject-and-level match that actually decides the outcome. A tutor who was excellent for a Standard Level student revising papers is being asked to do a different job for a Higher Level student with an exploration due. There is a second hidden mismatch: one family bought supervised study with some teaching in it, another bought criteria coaching, and both describe the purchase as a tutor. Use the recommendation as evidence of character, then test the subject knowledge separately.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find a specialist for in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: In the Marina cluster the predictable pinch points are Higher Level Psychology, Higher Level Business Management and Visual Arts process portfolio work, where provision is thin across the whole emirate rather than only locally. Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision are also rarely offered as a tutoring product at all, which is why we match those to the subject specialist the essay sits in rather than to a generic supervisor. We publish this because no competitor page states a coverage limit, and knowing it in September is far better than discovering it in February.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a Higher Level specialist for a Marina student?
faqs.answer: For Standard Level mathematics or a widely taught subject, usually a few days. For Higher Level mathematics or a Higher Level science at a specific preferred hour, a week is realistic. For the thinner subjects it can take longer, and for Visual Arts portfolio work it is the longest request in this cluster. The constraint is almost always the hour rather than the subject: five and six in the evening are the two most requested slots in New Dubai and they fill first. A weekend morning often matches immediately and suits extended coursework work better anyway.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's school offers the Higher Level combination he wants?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly, in the spring of the first Diploma year, and ask three specific things: which Higher Level sets are small, which are taught alongside a Standard Level group, and which teacher holds each subject. None of that is confidential and all of it is useful. Option blocks are built around a timetable and a cohort, so some combinations are simply not possible, and the compromise usually lands on the third Higher Level. A family who knows this in April can arrange support in September, which is a much better conversation than the one that starts in February.

faqs.question: What permit should I ask a private tutor in Dubai to show me?
faqs.answer: The private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The federal service is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, and it lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so ignore any amount quoted online.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who teaches Cambridge IGCSE also teach IB Diploma properly?
faqs.answer: Some can and many cannot, and the difference is not general ability. The Diploma assesses through internal assessments marked against published criteria, alongside papers whose weightings vary by subject and level, and it adds Theory of Knowledge and an Extended Essay on top. A tutor who has only ever prepared students for terminal written papers has not done the criteria work, and criteria literacy is where most avoidable Diploma marks are lost. Ask directly how many internal assessments in this subject they have supervised. The answer is specific, easy to give and immediately informative.

faqs.question: What should a free trial lesson actually prove?
faqs.answer: Subject depth, not rapport. Send a piece of your child's own marked work in advance and watch what the tutor does with it: a specialist finds the pattern within minutes, names it, refers to the criteria without being asked, and makes your child justify an answer rather than confirming it. The clearest single signal is whether your child hears something new. What a trial cannot prove is whether the work gets done between sessions, which is the largest variable in the arrangement, and it cannot test a component the lesson never touched.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to know my child's specific school to be useful?
faqs.answer: Far less than parents assume. What matters is the syllabus, the level and the assessment criteria, all of which are set by the IB and are identical whichever campus your child attends. What a tutor does need to know is the school's internal deadlines, because an internal assessment draft due in November drives the work far more than the examination does, and the teacher's own written feedback, because contradicting it confuses the student. Both are supplied by you in ten minutes. Familiarity with a particular building adds very little beyond small talk.

faqs.question: Can one tutor support a third Higher Level subject the school covers thinly?
faqs.answer: That is the single most common purchase we see from this cluster, and it is a good one because it is precise. The school is not failing; option blocks are finite, so one of a student's six courses usually has thinner cover than the others. A weekly hour with a specialist in exactly that subject and level, working on the student's own problems and marking against the published criteria, is a bounded and sensible intervention. Establish it in September rather than in February, because the internal assessment timeline is what makes the difference between support and rescue.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who scored highly in the Diploma better than a trained teacher?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and the two are often confused. A student who did very well in a subject knows how they succeeded, which is useful but is one route through the material. A teacher who has marked many scripts knows the twenty ways students fail, which is what diagnosis requires. For criteria-marked internal assessments the teaching experience matters more, because the judgement needed is whether a research question will generate data capable of supporting a conclusion. Ask about marking experience rather than about personal results, and be sceptical of any claim of current examiner status that cannot be evidenced.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is available for my child's subject this term?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we put three options to you rather than filling the slot. Wait a week or two for the specialist to have an hour. Take a different time, often a weekend morning, which for extended coursework is frequently better. Or do not proceed, which costs nothing because the trial has not happened and no payment has been taken. What we will not do is place a tutor who does not hold the subject at that level and leave you to discover it when the internal assessment is due.

faqs.question: Does support for Arabic or Islamic Education work the same way?
faqs.answer: The subjects sit differently in a Dubai school, so the context matters. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes are prohibited. Teaching material for these subjects is constrained: using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is not permitted.

faqs.question: Our tower has slow internet in the evening. Does that make online lessons unworkable?
faqs.answer: It is the most common practical worry from this neighbourhood and in practice it is manageable, because a one-to-one lesson needs far less bandwidth than a household assumes; the heavy part is a shared document and a whiteboard rather than high-definition video. Two things help. Test the connection at the hour you actually want the lesson rather than at midday, because evening congestion in a tower is a different condition. And agree a fallback before you need one, usually audio with the shared screen kept running, so a weak ten minutes costs ten minutes rather than the session.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-marina.closingHeading: Name the subject, then judge the tutor yourself
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-marina.closingBody: The useful next step is not a form. Tell us the subject and the level, send one piece of your child's own marked work, and we will tell you whether a specialist is free in the hour you want, how long the wait is if not, and whether this is a subject where our cover is genuinely thin. Then take the free trial lesson with the tutor your child would keep and ask the six questions published above. If the honest outcome is that your child needs a different subject supported, or no weekly support at all, we will say so. Lessons are one to one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

intro.heading: What Media City parents are really asking when they search for a home tutor
paragraphs: Dubai Media City is a working district. It sits in Al Sufouh between Sheikh Zayed Road and the sea, next to Dubai Internet City and Dubai Knowledge Park, served by the Dubai Tram at Media City station and by the Dubai Internet City Metro station on the Red Line. Its daytime population is large and almost entirely adult. Its residential population is small, concentrated in apartment towers, and scattered across the surrounding communities: Al Sufouh, The Greens, The Views, Barsha Heights, Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers. There is no school inside the free zone.

That geography produces a specific kind of search. A family living in or next to Media City is not asking where the nearest tutoring centre is, because they can see the answer is Al Barsha or the Marina. They are asking whether anyone in that radius actually knows the International Baccalaureate well enough to be useful. It is a reasonable worry. The IB is the smallest of the four main curricula in Dubai by enrolment, behind the UK, Indian and American curricula, and a general-purpose tutor who is excellent with a Year 9 British maths student may have never seen a Diploma Paper 3 or a Mathematics Exploration.

The honest answer has two halves. First, yes, there are real IB specialists working with families around Media City, and some of them live within a few kilometres. Second, finding them by proximity is a poor strategy, because the pool of people advertising locally is selected for availability rather than subject depth. The better strategy is to test for syllabus knowledge directly, which takes about four minutes on a phone call if you know what to ask. Most of this page is about how to do that.

The delivery question follows from the same logic. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Media City families run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 4.30pm and 9pm on school nights. That is not a compromise forced on us by logistics. It is what lets a family in an Al Sufouh tower work with a Chemistry Higher Level specialist instead of the best generalist within a twenty-minute drive.

If you take one thing from this page, take the six questions in the table further down. They work on any provider, including this one. A tutor who can tell you how many papers their subject has, what each is worth at Higher Level, and where the Internal Assessment marks sit is a tutor who knows the course. A tutor who answers in general language about confidence and foundations has told you something too.

The IB is the smallest of Dubai's four main curricula by enrolment
Each Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment worth 20 to 25 per cent

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-media-city.programmesIntro: Children living around Media City attend schools running several different programmes, and the three IB programmes behave very differently from each other. Here is what support looks like inside each, plus the British route most of their classmates take.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject has an Internal Assessment worth between a fifth and a quarter of the grade, and the final mark comes out of 45. The hard part is rarely a single topic. It is six sets of internal deadlines landing in the same term as revision.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, with a second session in November used mainly for retakes. Around Media City, GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh, Dubai American Academy in Al Barsha and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills all run the Diploma, so a cluster of DP students lives in these towers. Specific IB session and results dates are not published here; confirm them with your school's IB coordinator.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each marked against four criteria out of eight, with no public examination in most subjects. Grades accumulate from tasks across the year, so a weak term is expensive. MYP 5 ends with the Personal Project. Tutoring is usually about criterion literacy rather than content: teaching a student to answer what criterion C asks for instead of writing more.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai IB schools run the MYP only to age 14 and then switch to IGCSE, so children in the Al Sufouh towers can be on quite different tracks despite sitting in the same building. Dwight School Dubai and Bloom World Academy in Al Barsha South carry the continuum further. Ask the school which version your child is on before buying support.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based, organised by transdisciplinary themes, ending in the Grade 5 Exhibition. Reports describe learning approaches rather than marks, which parents arriving from British or Indian systems find hard to read. Support at this stage is usually reading fluency, number sense and written expression, kept deliberately light so it does not compete with the inquiry.
programmes.countryNote: The primary provision around Media City is mixed: Regent International School in The Greens is British, while the nearest full IB continuum primaries sit in Al Barsha South and Emirates Hills. Families planning to stay in the IB to Diploma should keep inquiry habits; families likely to move into a British school at Year 7 usually want quiet number and spelling work alongside.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: The externally examined British route taken by most 14 to 16 year olds in this part of Dubai, with Cambridge syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0620 Chemistry, and Pearson codes such as 4MA1. UAE candidates sit June and November with Cambridge, and May/June and November with Pearson Edexcel. Preparation is paper-shaped: past papers, mark schemes and command terms.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai College in Al Sufouh and the American School of Dubai in Al Barsha sit either side of Media City on completely different routes, and plenty of Media City families have one child doing IGCSE and another doing MYP. A tutor strong on one is not automatically useful on the other, which is the most common mismatch in this corridor.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-media-city.subjectsIntro: The requests that come from the Media City and Al Sufouh towers cluster heavily in the sciences, mathematics and economics, with a steady stream of Internal Assessment work. These are the subjects and where the marks go missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Three papers at Higher Level, two at Standard, with Paper 3 at HL carrying extended problem-solving worth a fifth of the grade. Most lost marks sit in proof, calculus technique and the step from a correct method to a justified conclusion. The Exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the mathematics itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with a graphic display calculator used throughout. Students who choose it expecting an easier course are surprised by the HL statistics and the modelling write-ups. Tutoring usually targets calculator fluency, interpreting output in context, and the habit of answering the modelling question that was asked.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and data analysis, Paper 2 is extended response, and the data booklet is permitted. Marks go missing in uncertainty treatment, graph gradients with units and explanation questions where the physics is right and the reasoning is unstated. The Internal Assessment is a single scientific investigation marked out of 24.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across both levels, with HL adding depth in energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Organic chemistry is the most requested topic from this corridor. The usual failure is memorising reactions without the mechanism, which collapses on any unfamiliar substrate in Paper 2.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy content, assessed with precise command terms. Students who write everything they know about a topic score below students who answer exactly what was asked. Data-based questions are the fastest place to gain marks, and they are also the part most students never practise deliberately.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries a surprising share of the marks, and HL adds quantitative questions and a policy paper. The Internal Assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles, which students routinely lose marks on by summarising the article instead of applying a named concept to it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay, plus the Individual Oral and, at HL, the essay. Strong readers lose marks by narrating rather than analysing how meaning is constructed. The work is annotation discipline and a repeatable paragraph structure for unseen texts.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released case for Paper 1 and the HL extension. The Internal Assessment is a research project on a real organisation, which is often where students pick a company with no accessible data and lose weeks. Tutoring frequently starts by changing the organisation.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory plus a solution-development Internal Assessment with a working product and documentation. Students build something that functions and then lose marks on the design and testing records. Support is usually split between algorithmic thinking and the documentation that carries the marks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The TOK exhibition and essay, and a 4,000-word Extended Essay in a chosen subject. Both are coached rather than taught: question framing, scope, research method, referencing and reflection. Tutors give feedback on the student's own drafts and write none of it, which is a rule and not a preference.

regions.note: Villa communities feeding Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills, Dubai British School and Emirates International School Meadows. More established informal tutoring networks, and families often comparing a neighbour's recommendation against a subject specialist.

schoolClusters.note: The gates closest to Media City. GEMS Wellington International School runs both British and IB Diploma routes; Dubai College is British and selective. Proximity here is real, which is precisely why these are the schools whose students most often have a local generalist and still need a subject specialist.

This is the default for DP1 and for Middle Years students, and the pattern that produces the steadiest change, because the student sees the effect inside two or three weeks of marked work rather than at the end of term.

sections.heading: Is there anyone near Dubai Media City who actually knows the IB?
paragraphs: Yes, and the number is smaller than the advertising suggests. An IB home tutor in Dubai Media City, in the sense parents mean, is a subject specialist who has taught one or two Diploma or Middle Years subjects repeatedly and can describe the assessment structure from memory. There are such people living in Al Sufouh, the Marina and Al Barsha. There are many more people advertising tutoring in those areas who are competent teachers of school mathematics or science and have never taught an IB course.

The arithmetic explains the gap. Dubai has 227 private schools running 17 different curricula, and the IB holds the smallest share of the four main curricula by enrolment. Within the IB, the Diploma splits across six subject groups and two levels, so the number of people who have taught, specifically, Physics at Higher Level, is a small slice of a small slice. When a search returns dozens of local tutors, what it is returning is the people who advertise locally, not the people who have marked a Physics Internal Assessment.

This is why the useful move is not to search harder in a smaller radius. It is to test for syllabus knowledge, which is quick and decisive. Ask how many papers the subject has at the level your child takes, what each is worth, how long each lasts, what is permitted in the examination room, and how the Internal Assessment is marked. Someone who knows the course answers immediately and in specifics. Someone who does not answers in the language of confidence and foundations.

Having tested for that, the location of the tutor stops being interesting. A family in a Media City tower can work weekly with a specialist who lives in Sharjah or Abu Dhabi without anybody noticing the difference, because the lesson happens over live video in Gulf Standard Time. That is the whole argument. The scarce resource is subject depth; bandwidth is not scarce in Al Sufouh.

sections.heading: Six questions that tell you whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: These are the questions to ask on a first call, with any provider. They take four minutes. They are deliberately factual, because facts are checkable and enthusiasm is not. The table sets out each question, the kind of answer that should worry you, and the kind that shows real familiarity with the course.

The logic behind them is simple. A tutor who has taught a Diploma subject repeatedly has watched students sit the papers, has read the mark schemes, and has supervised Internal Assessments through moderation. That experience leaves traces in how they talk. They know that Physics Paper 1 has a multiple-choice part and a data-analysis part. They know the Mathematics Exploration criteria are about communication and personal engagement as much as mathematics. They know a Biology data question is where marks are cheapest.

A tutor who lacks that experience is not necessarily a bad teacher, and for a Middle Years student who needs algebra fluency the distinction may not matter much. For a DP2 student with an Internal Assessment due and Paper 3 technique to build, it matters completely. The point of asking is not to catch anyone out. It is to establish which of those two situations you are in before you pay for a term.

Use the same questions on us. The only answer we would add is the honest one about availability: if no suitable specialist is free in your slot, you should be told that, with the earliest realistic alternative, rather than matched to the nearest available adult.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it costs
paragraphs: Begin with what the cheapest option in this market looks like, because it frames everything above it. Budget online tutoring in Dubai is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. That tier is usually university students or recent graduates, and for homework supervision it can be adequate. It is rarely the tier that knows a Diploma paper structure.

Above it, qualified subject tutors working online are quoted between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB and IGCSE specialists run from AED 200 to AED 450 and higher, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's specialist band at AED 200 to AED 450 or more. Premium named or examiner-led tutoring reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650. All of those are other providers' published figures, not IB Gram prices.

In-home one-to-one visits sit between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's band at AED 180 to AED 350. The useful way to read that is to ask what the gap over the online rate is buying. Across Al Sufouh at five in the afternoon, it is buying about an hour of a tutor's driving and a slot that collapses when the tram corridor backs up. It is not buying better teaching, and it is not buying a deeper specialist, since the pool shrinks to whoever is willing to make the drive.

Monthly packages make the same point more plainly. Published rates in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. That is roughly double the money for half the number of contacts. For a subject where the thing you need is weekly continuity, the online package is the better buy before any argument about who is teaching.

sections.heading: Which subjects are genuinely hard to cover here, and what happens then
paragraphs: Mathematics and the sciences are the easy matches. The difficult ones are predictable: Higher Level Computer Science, Economics Internal Assessment supervision in the autumn crunch, Visual Arts, Theory of Knowledge coaching, Design Technology, and any language acquisition request outside French, Spanish and Arabic. These are the subjects where a local search returns nobody and families end up with a generalist by default.

Our position is to disclose coverage rather than imply it. If no suitable specialist is free in the slot you want, you are told so with the earliest realistic alternative. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a niche subject, the match may be a tutor based elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, and that is said before you book. Two providers ranking for Dubai searches route UAE parents to Indian phone numbers without disclosing it; the delivery works, but concealing it is a trust failure rather than an operational detail.

Timing changes how hard a match is. Requests in September are mostly easy. Requests in the final term before the examination session are the hardest, because every specialist in a popular subject already has a full evening. The practical consequence for a Media City family is that a DP1 student is cheap and easy to place, and a DP2 student in the spring is neither. Starting a term earlier than feels necessary is the single most useful scheduling decision available.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, and the line we will not cross
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment worth between a fifth and a quarter of the final grade, and every candidate writes a 4,000-word Extended Essay and completes Theory of Knowledge. Together that is a large share of the Diploma produced at home, over months, with no invigilator. It is also the part of the market where providers behave worst.

The boundary is not ambiguous. A tutor may teach research method, help narrow a research question to something finishable, explain the assessment criteria, teach referencing and data handling, and read the student's own draft and say precisely where it fails against a criterion. A tutor may not write any part of the work, may not redraft or restructure text on the student's behalf, and may not supply a model to be adapted. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. For the student, that is a malpractice finding waiting to happen.

There is a practical version of this that helps rather than scolds. The most common reason an Internal Assessment goes badly is not dishonesty. It is a research question that cannot be answered with the data the student can actually get, chosen in week one and discovered in week six. A tutor who spends the first session killing an unworkable question and replacing it with a narrower one has done more for the grade than any amount of later editing, and has done it entirely within the rules.

Ask any provider what their tutor does with a weak draft. The honest answer is that it comes back marked against the criteria with instructions to rewrite. Any answer in which the tutor improves the prose directly is an answer about the provider's risk appetite. The exposure in that transaction sits with your child.

sections.heading: Permits, and what a parent in Al Sufouh can actually verify
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page, listed as private tutor licensing, states a two-working-day completion time and no fee, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the words of the federal portal, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of fine amounts has been published, and figures circulating online could not be verified against a government source, so no amount appears on this page. If a provider quotes you one, ask where it came from.

A separate thing is often confused with this. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit as a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific permit for a specific kind of business. It is not something an individual tutor holds, and the phrase KHDA-approved tutor describes nothing that exists. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, and has no office in the UAE.

One more point worth knowing for families who move between emirates. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it against current ADEK guidance before relying on it. Either way, do not arrange tutoring with your child's own class teacher.

sections.heading: The examination calendar, counted backwards from a DP2 autumn
paragraphs: Families around Media City often start looking for help in the DP2 autumn, which is the most expensive moment to start and the least effective. The reason is the shape of the year. Internal Assessment deadlines set by the school land months before the examination session, so a DP2 student in the autumn is finishing coursework in six subjects while revision has not begun. Adding a tutor at that point means triaging, not teaching.

UAE IB schools sit the May session, with a second session in November used mainly for retakes. Specific IB session and results dates are not restated here: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and your school's IB coordinator is the authority. What can be stated with sources is the British board calendar, which matters because many students in this corridor sit IGCSE first.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and is not a UAE route. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states in its exams officers' guide that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date. sections.heading: Why online works for a tower in Al Sufouh specifically
paragraphs: The general argument for online tutoring is well worn. The specific argument for this corridor is better. Media City, Internet City and Knowledge Park form a continuous strip of offices between Sheikh Zayed Road and the sea, with residential towers threaded through them and no school inside any of the three. Every school-age child here travels out in the morning and back in the afternoon, and the roads around the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh school gates stall between 2.30pm and 3.30pm and again at the office exodus.

Drop a tutor into that pattern and the arithmetic is unflattering. A one-hour lesson at 5pm costs the tutor roughly two hours of their day, which is why in-home rates carry the premium they do. It also makes the slot fragile in a way that undermines the thing weekly tutoring depends on: the same hour, every week, for a term. A slot that is missed one week in four does not build the habit of marked work improving.

Removing the journey fixes both. The lesson starts on the minute, the rate reflects teaching rather than driving, and the tutor is selected from everyone teaching in Gulf Standard Time rather than from those willing to cross Al Sufouh in rush hour. For Higher Level sciences and mathematics, which is most of what this corridor asks for, that widening is the difference between a specialist and an approximation.

There are honest limits. A student who will not sit still without an adult physically present is harder to teach online, and a very young child usually is too. Both are real, and if that describes your child the right answer may not be us. What online delivery is not is a lesser version of a home visit for a motivated Diploma student working on Paper 2 technique with a screen-shared past paper and a shared document. For that student it is simply the better arrangement.

faqs.question: Can I find an IB specialist who lives close to Dubai Media City?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but proximity is a poor filter. Media City has no school inside it, and the IB is the smallest of Dubai's four main curricula by enrolment, so the number of adults nearby who have actually taught a Diploma subject at a given level is small. What a local search returns is the people who advertise locally. The faster route is to test for syllabus knowledge on the phone, then stop caring where the tutor lives, because lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: How do I tell a real IB tutor from a general subject tutor in four minutes?

How is the Internal Assessment marked and out of how many? Which topic do your students most often lose marks on, and why? What do you do with a weak draft? Someone who has taught the course answers immediately and in specifics. Someone who has not answers in the language of confidence and foundations, which tells you what you needed to know.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to apartments in Al Sufouh and the Media City towers?

faqs.question: What does the extra money for an in-home tutor actually buy?
faqs.answer: Mostly the car journey. Across Al Sufouh at five in the afternoon, a one-hour lesson costs the tutor about two hours, and that is what the premium reflects. It also narrows your choice to tutors willing to make the drive, which is the opposite of what you want when the scarce thing is Higher Level subject depth. Monthly packages make it plainer: published rates include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do children living around Media City attend?
faqs.answer: GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh and Dubai American Academy in Al Barsha both run the Diploma, and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Emirates International School Meadows sit in the villa belt behind Sheikh Zayed Road. Dwight School Dubai and Bloom World Academy in Al Barsha South run the continuum further down. Dubai College in Al Sufouh and the American School of Dubai are on different routes entirely. These are named as local context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Is a Higher Level science tutor different from a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Treat them as separate specifications. Higher Level adds content and, more importantly, adds the kind of extended reasoning that Paper 2 rewards and that Standard Level rarely requires. A tutor comfortable at Standard Level can leave a Higher Level student with correct physics and unstated reasoning, which marks badly. When matching, we treat the level as part of the subject request rather than a detail, and a tutor who cannot describe how the papers differ between levels is not a Higher Level match.

faqs.question: When is the worst time to start looking for a tutor in this corridor?
faqs.answer: The final term before the examination session. By then every specialist in a popular subject has a full evening, and the student has Internal Assessment deadlines, mocks and revision competing for the same weeks. Requests in September are easy to place and cheap in every sense. A DP1 student is straightforward; a DP2 student in the spring is neither. If you are reading this in the autumn of DP1, that is the moment where a weekly hour does the most work for the least money.

faqs.question: Where exactly does legitimate Internal Assessment help stop?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that is easy to state. A tutor may teach research method, narrow a research question, explain the assessment criteria, teach referencing and data handling, and read the student's own draft and say exactly where it fails against a criterion. A tutor may not write, redraft or restructure any part of it, and may not supply a model to adapt. The most valuable legitimate help usually arrives in week one, replacing an unanswerable research question with a narrower one that the student can actually finish.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma student around here usually need?
faqs.answer: One hour a week per subject, in one or two subjects, is the common pattern and the one that works. Six subjects of tutoring is a sign the problem is organisation rather than content, and is better addressed by fixing the week than by buying more lessons. Before the examination session, families often move to two or three sessions a week in a single subject for a short block. Sustained weekly contact in the subject that is actually failing beats thin coverage across everything.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with a Media City family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee, applied for through its app, website and e-services. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: Is any tutoring company in Dubai actually KHDA approved?
faqs.answer: A training institute with premises and staff can hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which involves initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a permit for a business with a physical centre. It is not something an individual tutor holds, and the phrase KHDA-approved tutor describes nothing that exists. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval or accreditation, and no UAE office.

faqs.question: My child is in an IGCSE year but will do the IB after. Which board calendar applies?
faqs.answer: Both, at different times. Cambridge runs June and November series in the UAE, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Once your child moves into the Diploma, UAE IB schools sit the May session with November as the retake route. Always work from the live official timetable rather than a date someone has restated.

faqs.question: How do weekly slots work through Ramadan for a Media City family?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. School days shorten during Ramadan and the useful study window moves to the evening, so weekly slots typically shift later rather than pausing. Because lessons are delivered over live video, there is no travel to reschedule around, which makes the move straightforward. Families who prefer to pause for the month and resume afterwards do that instead; what matters more is deciding in advance rather than letting four weeks disappear from a term that has Internal Assessment deadlines in it.

faqs.question: If the match is wrong after one paid lesson, what then?
faqs.answer: Say so after the first paid session and you are matched again. That matters more than any claim about tutor quality, because it is the only part you can test cheaply and quickly. The usual causes of a poor fit are pace and register rather than knowledge: a tutor pitched at a confident Higher Level student can lose one who is rebuilding from a weak Standard Level base. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a provider offering one is describing their marketing rather than their teaching.

faqs.question: Are lessons recorded, and is that useful or just a feature?
faqs.answer: They are recorded, and the use is narrow but real. Students rarely rewatch a whole hour. What they use is the ten minutes where a worked solution was built, replayed the night before a test, and the screen-shared annotation of a past-paper question. It also means a missed evening is recoverable rather than lost, which matters in a corridor where school trips, travel and sport regularly take out one week in four. Parents occasionally watch a few minutes to see how the teaching actually sounds.

intro.heading: Dubai Production City is a short drive from everything and close to nothing
paragraphs: Dubai Production City, still called IMPZ by almost everyone who lives there, sits west of Al Khail Road between Motor City and Dubai Investments Park. It is a compact grid of towers and low-rise clusters with a lake at the centre, and it has one quality that shapes every tutoring decision a family here makes: it is twelve minutes from a lot of places and thirty-five minutes from the schools that actually run the IB Diploma. There is no IB World School inside the community boundary. Children here commute out, in school buses that leave early and return late.

That geography is why a search for an IB home tutor in Dubai Production City behaves differently from the same search in Jumeirah. In Jumeirah, a parent is choosing between a dozen tutors who live within ten minutes. Here, the honest pool of IB Diploma specialists who will drive to IMPZ on a Tuesday at half past five is small, and it gets smaller the more specific the subject becomes. Economics SL is findable. Chemistry HL with Internal Assessment supervision, taught by somebody who has actually read the current assessment criteria, is a different question.

So this page is written as a comparison. We put Dubai Production City next to Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Dubai South, Emaar South, Jebel Ali and Green Community, because those are the communities a Production City family is realistically compared against when a tutor decides whether a journey is worth making. The useful finding is that the answer comes out the same in every one of them, and for the same reason: travel is the constraint, not talent. Removing the travel removes the constraint.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run in India only. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, which is why we can put a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL specialist in front of a Production City student on a weekday evening without anybody crossing Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road at six o'clock. We say that plainly rather than burying it, because a parent who books expecting a doorbell has been misled, and because the online case stands up on its own merits once you see the numbers side by side.

What follows is the detail: what the Dubai market charges per hour and per month, with the source for each band; how the travel premium is constructed and what it buys; how Production City compares with the six communities nearest to it; the IB assessment structure your child is being measured against; the exam calendar counted backwards from the May session; what KHDA and the MoHRE permit actually govern; and the academic-honesty line that separates a tutor from an essay mill. Figures were reviewed in October 2026.
