dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-production-.programmesIntro: Production City families sit across the full IB continuum, usually at different schools, because there is no single-campus continuum provider inside the community. A family with two children can easily have one at PYP in Motor City and one at DP in Al Barsha, on two different bus timetables.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around six transdisciplinary themes rather than separate subjects, assessed continuously against learner-profile attributes and approaches to learning. There is no external examination. Support at this stage is about building the number sense, reading stamina and written fluency that the Middle Years Programme will later assume, and it works best in short, frequent sessions rather than long ones.
programmes.countryNote: A Production City child in PYP is almost certainly bussed to Dubai Investments Park, Motor City or Al Barsha, which means a 7am pickup and a 4pm drop. Evening sessions have to start late or not at all, and that single scheduling fact is the most common reason local in-home arrangements collapse in the first month.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses eight subject groups against four criteria each, scored one to eight, converted to a 1-7 grade by published subject boundaries. Criterion labels are letters, not topics: in Mathematics, Criterion A is knowing and understanding, Criterion C is communicating. Most lost marks are communication marks rather than content marks, which is a fixable problem once a student sees what the descriptor asks for.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Year 11 is the pressure point for Production City families, because the jump into the Diploma is not mediated by an external exam the way IGCSE mediates it. Students arrive in DP1 having never sat a three-hour paper. We use the final MYP term to introduce timed conditions before the Diploma does it for them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The maximum is 45: 42 subject points plus three from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Each subject carries an internally assessed component, typically 20-25 per cent of the grade, completed during the course rather than in the exam hall.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Production City lose the most usable study time to the commute. A 35-minute bus each way in Dubai afternoon traffic is roughly five hours a week, and those are the hours families try to buy back. Online sessions starting at 6pm or 7:30pm Gulf Standard Time are the slots Production City households actually book.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and language development. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and suits a student with a defined vocational direction who still wants IB subject rigour in two or three areas.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision near Dubai Production City is thin, so a family considering it is usually weighing a longer commute to a specific campus. Where a student takes DP courses inside a CP framework, the subject teaching is identical, and we tutor those courses on exactly the same basis as a full Diploma student's.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-production-.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Production City and Jebel Ali families request most, with the component that most often decides the grade. The pattern across this cluster is science-heavy, which tracks the engineering and media employment base in and around the community.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry this course. HL adds Paper 3, a two-question problem-solving paper worth 20 per cent that rewards students who can read an unfamiliar structure and start anyway. Marks go missing in unjustified steps rather than wrong answers, because method marks need visible reasoning.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use dominate. The graphical calculator is assumed throughout, and a student who cannot run a chi-squared test or a regression on the device loses marks that have nothing to do with mathematics. HL adds a markedly harder statistics and probability strand.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The 2023 syllabus reorganised content into five themes with HL extensions. Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-analysis section; Paper 2 is extended response. Students lose marks on uncertainty treatment and on explain questions where they describe what happens without naming the physical principle.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity are now taught as two integrated strands. Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium produce most of the lost marks, usually because a student states a product without a mechanism or an arrow. The scientific investigation is a single piece of internally assessed work worth 20 per cent.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change are the organising themes. The volume of terminology is the real difficulty. Command terms matter more here than in any other science: outline, explain, distinguish and suggest each buy a different number of marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are the grade. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram with an explanation tied to it scores where a paragraph of prose does not. The internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries, each 800 words maximum, each on a different unit and a different article.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as Ansoff, SWOT and the business management toolkit are examined for application, not recall. Paper 1 works from a pre-released case study. The HL extension adds a 1,800-word research project built on primary or secondary data about a real organisation's issue.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessment is Paper 1 guided analysis of unseen non-literary texts, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral on a global issue, and at HL a 1,200-1,500 word essay. The individual oral is where confident students underperform, because it needs a defensible global issue, not a favourite text.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and computational thinking, plus HL options including resource management and control. The solution development internal assessment is a working product with documentation, and scope control decides the mark more often than coding ability does.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK is assessed by a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects with 950 words of commentary. Together with the Extended Essay it contributes up to three points. Students treat it as an afterthought and then discover it is the difference between 38 and 41.

sections.heading: What a home tutor in Dubai Production City really costs, once you count the road
paragraphs: A home tutor in Dubai Production City costs the published hourly rate plus a travel cost that nobody itemises. Market rates for in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai run roughly AED 180-350 per hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with individual home tutors quoting up to AED 500 for specialist levels, against roughly AED 150-300 for the same qualified subject tutor delivered online. That gap of AED 50-150 an hour is the travel premium, and it is the single largest line item in the decision.

The premium exists because a tutor driving to IMPZ cannot teach for the forty minutes they spend in the car, and they price that time into the lesson. From Al Barsha South, where several of the Diploma campuses sit, the drive to Production City is twenty minutes at ten in the morning and closer to forty between five and seven, which is exactly when a Diploma student is free. A tutor who teaches three Production City families in an evening spends more of the evening driving than teaching, and the rate reflects that arithmetic.

The second cost is invisible on an invoice. A tutor who can reach IMPZ in the window a Diploma student is awake is drawn from a geographic pool rather than a subject pool, so a family often ends up with a good general science teacher covering Chemistry HL instead of a Chemistry HL specialist. That trade is rarely made consciously. It is made by the map.

Published market figures below were read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table. They are the Dubai market, not IB Gram prices. Our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many hours the goal actually needs, which for most Diploma students is fewer than families expect and spread over longer.

sections.heading: Production City against the next community over, and why the answer does not change
paragraphs: Put Dubai Production City beside Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Dubai South, Emaar South, Jebel Ali and Green Community and a pattern appears immediately. The communities differ in density, in build type and in how long the school bus takes. They do not differ in the depth of the local IB Diploma tutor pool, because the pool is drawn from the same set of campuses and the same set of teachers, and those campuses are clustered in Al Barsha, Motor City and Dubai Investments Park regardless of which of these eight communities you live in.

That is the finding that matters. A family in Al Furjan sometimes assumes their shorter school run means a better local tutor market. It does not. It means a shorter school run. The Chemistry HL specialist who could teach your child is still a thirty-minute drive away in the evening, is still choosing between your 5:30pm and somebody else's, and is still pricing their car into the hour.

Discovery Gardens adds a wrinkle of its own: the clusters are dense, visitor parking is contested, and the last three minutes of a tutor's journey are often the slowest. Dubai South and Emaar South sit at the opposite extreme, with long distances between residential pockets and almost nothing in the way of established IB provision inside them. Both ends of that range point the same direction.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for a Production City household, line by line
paragraphs: The comparison that decides this is not quality against convenience. Both formats are one-to-one with a human teacher. The comparison is about which constraints each format imposes, and for a community with no IB campus inside it, those constraints fall very differently.

In-home tuition gives you physical presence, which genuinely helps a younger child who needs a hand kept on the page, and it gives a tutor the ability to see a desk, a phone and a distraction pattern. It costs you the travel premium, a smaller specialist pool, fragile scheduling and a cancellation whenever the Al Khail slip road backs up. For a Year 4 PYP child in Production City, that trade can still be worth making with a local tutor.

Online one-to-one gives you the specialist pool of the whole platform, a session that starts on time because nobody is driving, a shared digital whiteboard that produces a saved record of every worked solution, and the ability to run a session from a hotel room in half-term. It costs you physical presence and it asks a thirteen-year-old to manage their own attention for an hour, which some can and some cannot.

For Diploma students specifically, the balance is not close. A DP2 student needs somebody who knows that Paper 3 in Analysis and Approaches is twenty per cent and what the examiner wants in the first two lines of an answer. Subject precision beats proximity at that level, every time. IB Gram delivers UAE lessons online for exactly this reason, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

sections.heading: What a Diploma student is actually measured on, component by component
paragraphs: Families often buy tutoring against a report-card grade without knowing which components produce that grade. In the Diploma, every subject carries an internally assessed piece completed during the course, and in most subjects it is a fifth to a quarter of the final mark. It is also the only part of the grade a student can bank calmly, months before the exam hall, which makes it the highest-leverage thing to get right early.

The externally assessed papers vary more than parents expect. In the sciences, Paper 1 now splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, and the data section rewards a skill nobody teaches explicitly: reading a graph, deciding what the uncertainty is, and saying so in the language the mark scheme uses. In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, Paper 3 is a two-question extended problem-solving paper worth a fifth of the grade, and students who have never practised starting an unfamiliar structure lose that fifth before they begin.

Then there is the core. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three points on the 45-point scale. Three points is the difference between a conditional offer and a rejection at more universities than most families realise, and it is earned in writing done in DP1 and the first term of DP2, when nobody feels urgent.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session. That single fact restructures the whole of DP2, because the internal deadlines that actually govern a student's year sit months before it and are set by the school, not the IB. A family who starts planning in the spring term has already missed the two deadlines that mattered most.

Counting backwards is the useful exercise. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay are typically finished in the first half of DP2, while Internal Assessments across six subjects land in a cluster that schools stagger across the autumn and winter terms. Mocks usually sit in the winter term and are the first honest signal of where a student is. By the time May arrives, the internal component of the grade is already fixed and sitting on a server.

We do not publish specific IB session or results dates on these pages. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so every date in this project would be a date we could not verify, and a wrong date is a date a parent acts on. Confirm your child's exact windows with their IB coordinator or on ibo.org. What we can publish safely is the sequence and the lead times, which do not move.

For comparison, where a Production City student also sits Cambridge or Pearson qualifications, those calendars are published and verifiable. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: KHDA, the MoHRE permit, and how a Production City parent checks a tutor
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a rating on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Those reports are public, and they are the most useful free document a parent in this community can read before a school transfer.

Private tutoring is a separate regulatory question. Individuals offering private lessons in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE app, website or e-services.

u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody, including us. If a tutor tells you a specific figure, they are repeating something unverified.

What a parent can actually do: ask the tutor whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit and when it expires; ask which syllabus version and board they teach; ask for the mark scheme they marked your child's last paper against. IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved, IB authorised or Cambridge accredited, and does not hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence issued to training institutes with physical premises in Dubai. We have no premises in the UAE.

sections.heading: Where the academic-honesty line sits on an IA, Extended Essay or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the part of the market that should worry a Production City parent most, because the search results for Diploma coursework help include operators who sell finished work. One page in our own competitor research advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying that is an academic-malpractice finding against your child, and the consequence sits with the student, not the seller.

The line is clear once stated. A tutor may teach the subject content the assessment rests on, explain each assessment criterion and what the descriptors actually ask for, question a research question until it is answerable, discuss method and whether the data will support a conclusion, read a draft the student wrote and say where it falls short of a criterion, and teach referencing. Everything in that list is teaching.

A tutor may not write any part of the work, supply text to be pasted in, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, generate the data, choose the topic on the student's behalf, or edit a draft to completion. The distinction is authorship. Feedback that tells a student their Criterion C analysis does not interpret the uncertainty is legitimate; handing them two sentences of interpretation is not.

We also do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are copyright material and our tutors reference the official source and link to it. Where a school asks what external support a student received, we can provide a written record of the sessions and what was taught, which is a reasonable thing for a school to ask and a reasonable thing for us to be able to answer.

sections.heading: After the Diploma: MoE equivalency, Arabic, and what the ministry actually counts
paragraphs: A Diploma earned in Dubai often needs an equivalency certificate from the UAE Ministry of Education before it can be used for a UAE university place or certain employment routes. Most families meet this for the first time in DP2, under time pressure, which is the worst moment to discover a missing document.

For the British track the requirements are published and specific. Gulf Today reported in July 2026 that students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Critically, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule.

For the IB there is no equivalency points threshold we can responsibly publish. The source that sets out the British and American tracks states no IB figure, and we will not print a number read from a competitor page. Check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority directly, and ask your school's university counsellor, who handles this every year. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency for anybody.

Alongside all of this run the UAE's mandatory subjects. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and combined classes strictly prohibited. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. These are graded subjects on a Dubai report card and the reason many Production City families book Arabic support alongside Diploma subjects.

sections.heading: Starting, and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: The honest version of getting started has four steps and one caveat. You tell us the subject, the level, the school and what the last report said. We match a specialist in that exact subject and level. You take a free trial lesson, which is a real lesson and not a sales call, and you decide afterwards. If the match is wrong, you say so and we rematch once without charge.

The caveat is availability, and no competitor in our research discloses it. Some combinations are genuinely thin: Chemistry HL with Internal Assessment supervision in a specific evening slot, Computer Science HL, Arabic as a first language at Diploma level, Economics HL in the week before a mock. When that happens we say so and give you a date rather than putting a generalist in front of your child and hoping. Sometimes the honest answer is that the first available specialist slot is eleven days away.

Where a UAE-based tutor is not available for a niche subject, the specialist may be based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time. We tell you where your tutor is based before you book. Two of the competitor pages in our research route UAE parents to Indian phone numbers without disclosing delivery location at all; a parent should know, and should be able to ask.

On scheduling, Production City evenings are tight and we plan around that rather than against it. Buses return late, siblings have different pickup times, and during Ramadan families routinely move sessions to post-Iftar slots. All of those are normal requests. What is not normal, and what we will not do, is promise a tutor at your door in IMPZ. That is not a service IB Gram provides in the UAE, in this community or any other.

process.title: Tell us the subject, level and school
process.description: A short form or a WhatsApp message. The three things that make a match work are the exact subject, the exact level, and which school and board your child is on. A Production City family's answer to that third question is usually a campus in Al Barsha, Motor City or Dubai Investments Park, and it changes which tutor we propose.

process.title: We match one specialist, not a shortlist
process.description: You get one named tutor who teaches that subject at that level, with their background and where they are based. We do not send five profiles and ask you to choose, because choosing between strangers on paper is not a parent's job and it wastes a week you may not have before a mock.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then you decide
process.description: The trial is a genuine 60-minute teaching session on the topic your child is currently stuck on, not a consultation. Afterwards you get a short written note on what the tutor found. No card is held and nothing renews. If you do not want to continue, that is the end of it.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot around the bus
process.description: We set a repeating time that survives the school run, usually from 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time for Production City households. A fixed slot is what makes tutoring work over months. Ad hoc booking drifts, then stops, usually in the week the student most needed it.

process.title: Review against the school's own calendar
process.description: Every four to six weeks we look at whether the plan still matches what the school is assessing next. School assessment calendars move. If the Chemistry Internal Assessment deadline has shifted or a mock has been brought forward, the sessions change shape rather than continuing on a plan that no longer applies.

whyPoints.title: Subject match instead of postcode match
whyPoints.description: A Production City family searching locally is choosing from tutors who can reach IMPZ by six. Online, the pool is every specialist on the platform. For Analysis and Approaches HL or Chemistry HL, that difference is the whole quality of the teaching, and it is the clearest argument against the travel premium.

whyPoints.title: AED figures published with their source
whyPoints.description: Three of the six main competitor pages in our research publish no price at all, and two quote USD. We publish the Dubai market bands with the competitor or rate table each came from and the month they were read, so you can check them. We do not present market rates as our own price list.

whyPoints.title: Coursework handled the way the IB requires
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and TOK support is teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own drafts. We never write or complete assessed work. That is stated plainly because operators in this same search sell finished Internal Assessments, and the student carries the consequence.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed before you commit
whyPoints.description: If no specialist in your subject and slot is free, we give you the date rather than a substitute. If the tutor is based outside the UAE, we say so before booking. Neither disclosure appears on any competitor page in our research, and both are things a parent is entitled to know.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: We are not KHDA approved, ADEK approved, IB authorised or Cambridge accredited, and we hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit. We explain what each regulator does and link the official source. Phrases like KHDA-approved tutors are common in this market and, where untrue, are a real liability.

whyPoints.title: A written record that survives the year
whyPoints.description: Every session leaves notes and a saved whiteboard, so April revision can start from November's worked solutions rather than from memory. For a Diploma student across six subjects and six internal assessments, that record is the difference between revision and rediscovery.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who comes to our villa in Dubai Production City?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver every UAE lesson as one-to-one live video and do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only. Independent home tutors do operate in this area, and Dubai market rates for in-home one-to-one run roughly AED 180-350 an hour, rising to AED 500 for specialist levels. What you gain is physical presence. What you give up is the specialist pool, because the tutor has to be someone who can reach IMPZ in the evening, and for a Higher Level subject that constraint usually decides the teaching quality.

faqs.question: Is the tutor market in Al Furjan or Discovery Gardens any better than in Production City?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most useful thing on this page. Those communities have shorter or longer school runs, different housing density and different parking, but the IB Diploma tutor pool is drawn from the same campuses in Al Barsha, Motor City and Dubai Investments Park whichever of them you live in. A Chemistry HL teacher is a thirty-minute evening drive from Al Furjan and from Production City alike. Moving community changes your commute, not your access to a specialist. Removing the drive from the equation is the only change that actually widens the pool.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for IB Diploma tuition in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Dubai market rates for an IB Diploma specialist run roughly AED 200-450 an hour, from the Bestimate 2026 rate table and TutorChase's published AED 270. Qualified subject tutors sit lower at AED 150-300 online. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices. We start with a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many hours your actual goal needs, which is often fewer than a package assumes.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do Dubai Production City students usually attend?
faqs.answer: There is no IB World School inside the Production City boundary, so students commute. Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park is the nearest IB continuum campus. Beyond that, families use the Al Barsha ring, including Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and GEMS World Academy Dubai, while Fairgreen International School serves the southern corridor. Several nearby campuses are British curriculum with sixth-form routes, which is why IGCSE-to-Diploma transition questions are common here. We name these as context only and have no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: What time can an evening session realistically start for a Production City family?
faqs.answer: From about 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time for a secondary student, and later if there are siblings on different bus timetables. A Diploma student commuting to Al Barsha is typically on a bus that leaves early and returns between four and half past, and they need food and a break before anything useful happens. This is precisely why fixed online slots work here: the session starts at the booked minute because nobody is driving to it. Families who travel or who move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan keep the same tutor and shift the slot.

faqs.question: Does my child need a MoHRE permit check before we hire a private tutor?
faqs.answer: You should ask about it. Individuals offering private lessons in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. u.ae states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted as unverified. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold the permit and when it expires.

faqs.question: How many points are the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge worth together?
faqs.answer: Up to three, on the 45-point scale, awarded from a published matrix combining the two grades. Three points moves a student across most university offer thresholds, and it is earned by writing done in DP1 and the first term of DP2 rather than in the exam hall. The common Production City pattern is a strong science student who treats both as paperwork, finishes them late, and loses study time in the spring term writing what should have been finished in the autumn. Finishing the Extended Essay early is the cheapest grade improvement available in the Diploma.

faqs.question: Where exactly does legitimate Chemistry IA support stop for a Production City student?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the chemistry the investigation rests on, explain each assessment criterion and what the descriptors require, question the research question until it is answerable in the time available, discuss whether the method will produce usable data, and read a draft your daughter wrote and say where it falls short. A tutor cannot write any part of it, supply text, rewrite a paragraph to its final form, generate data or choose the topic. The test is authorship: every word and every number must be hers.

faqs.question: Why does online tuition cost less per hour than a home visit in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because roughly AED 50-150 of an in-home hour is the car, not the teaching. A tutor driving from Al Barsha South to Production City between five and seven spends thirty to forty minutes each way and cannot teach in that time, so they price it into the lesson. Comparing the published bands makes it visible: qualified subject tutors at AED 150-300 online against AED 180-350 in-home for the same tier. The premium buys physical presence in the room. Whether that is worth AED 100 an hour depends far more on the child's age than on the subject.

faqs.question: When do UAE IB students sit their exams, and when should we start tutoring?
faqs.answer: UAE IB schools sit the May session. We do not publish specific IB session or results dates because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a wrong date is one a parent acts on; confirm exact windows with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. On timing, the leverage sits in DP1 and the autumn of DP2, when internal assessments and the Extended Essay are live and still fixable. Starting in the spring term of DP2 means the internal quarter of each grade is already banked and only the written papers remain to work on.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge's February and March exam series apply to my child in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. The February and March series is offered to India only. UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June and November series, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Ask your school's exams officer which zone and which board your child is entered under, then read that specific timetable.

faqs.question: What is KHDA and does it regulate private tutors as well as schools?
faqs.answer: KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, is described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. It inspects private schools annually and publishes ratings from Outstanding to Very Weak. It does not license individual private tutors; that sits with MoHRE. KHDA does issue an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with physical premises in Dubai. IB Gram does not hold one and has no UAE premises, so any provider describing itself as KHDA-approved for one-to-one tutoring is worth a direct question about which permit they mean.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP Year 11 and moves into DP next year. What should we work on now?
faqs.answer: Timed writing and Criterion C communication. MYP assesses four criteria per subject on a one-to-eight scale, and the marks students most commonly leave behind are communication marks rather than content marks. Because MYP has no external examination, students arrive in DP1 having never sat a three-hour paper, and the first mock is a shock that reads as a content problem when it is a pacing problem. We use the final MYP term to introduce exam timing, structured answers and command-term reading before the Diploma applies that pressure for the first time.

faqs.question: What happens if you do not have a tutor free in my child's subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we give you a date. Thin combinations are real: Higher Level Chemistry with Internal Assessment supervision in a specific evening slot, Computer Science HL, Arabic as a first language at Diploma level. Rather than putting a generalist in front of your child, we say when the specialist is available, which is sometimes a week or more away. If the specialist is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we tell you that before you book. No competitor page in our research discloses either limit.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education compulsory if my child is on the IB Diploma in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes are strictly prohibited. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. These subjects are graded on a Dubai report card, which is why families in this community frequently book Arabic support alongside Diploma subjects.

faqs.question: Will five IGCSEs be enough for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency later?
faqs.answer: For the British track, Gulf Today reported in July 2026 that students must present five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor states six subjects are required, which does not match that published rule. For the IB Diploma no points threshold appears in our sourced material, so check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-production-.closingHeading: A Production City family's decision, reduced to one line
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-production-.closingBody: The choice here is not between a good local tutor and a distant stranger. It is between a tutor selected because they can reach IMPZ by six and a tutor selected because they teach your child's subject at your child's level. For a Primary Years child, presence in the room can still win. For a Diploma student working towards the May session with six internal assessments and an Extended Essay to land, subject precision wins and the comparison with Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens or Dubai South comes out the same. Book a free trial lesson, watch one hour of actual teaching, and decide from that rather than from a profile.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-oas.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects for families across Dubai Silicon Oasis and the neighbouring communities. Each is listed against a named subject and level, because the comparison that actually matters is not between neighbourhoods but between a specialist in your child's subject and whoever happens to be nearer.

intro.heading: Silicon Oasis against its neighbours, and why the answer does not change
paragraphs: Dubai Silicon Oasis sits on the eastern side of the Dubai-Al Ain corridor, with Academic City to the south, The Villa and Dubailand to the west, Nad Al Sheba and Ras Al Khor to the north, and Mirdif and Festival City beyond that. Families comparing these areas for schooling usually assume the tutoring market differs between them too. On school supply, commute and housing it genuinely does. On access to an IB Diploma specialist it does not, and understanding why saves a great deal of searching.

Start with what actually differs. Silicon Oasis has a large British-curriculum secondary school inside the community and several Indian-curriculum schools, which makes it unusually self-contained for daily logistics. Academic City is a university district with secondary provision attached. The Villa and Dubailand have grown their school provision quickly and are more car-dependent. Nad Al Sheba holds two long-established Diploma centres. Those are real differences and they matter when choosing a school.

Now what does not differ. The International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of private school enrolment in Dubai in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum and 26 per cent Indian. That ratio is roughly the same whichever of these communities you live in, because it is an emirate-level fact about the market rather than a neighbourhood one. The Diploma teaching pool is therefore small everywhere along this corridor, and smaller again once it is divided by subject and by level.

Then apply the two filters a visiting tutor has to pass. They must be willing to drive to your address inside the narrow window when a Diploma student is both home and still capable, and they must teach your child's exact subject at the exact level. For Business Management or Economics, that combination exists in several of these communities. For Chemistry at Higher Level, Physics at Higher Level or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, it mostly does not, in any of them.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Across Silicon Oasis, Academic City, The Villa, Nad Al Sheba and the rest of this corridor, lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. That is why the answer is the same in every neighbourhood on the comparison: once the driving radius stops being a filter, the only remaining questions are subject, level and hour, and those are answerable identically from Cedre Villas or from Nad Al Sheba.

The rest of this page does the comparison properly, with tables rather than impressions: how the communities differ on schools and commute, how deep local supply runs by subject, what the travel premium buys in a corridor this spread out, and what the Diploma actually requires at each stage. Use it to decide what to buy, not where to live.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-oas.programmesIntro: Which IB programme a child is in changes the comparison, because local supply is adequate for some stages and thin for others. These are the three and what each actually needs.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations and continuous teacher assessment. Support at this level is about reading stamina, number fluency and explaining reasoning out loud. The content demand is modest, so a strong primary teacher of any curriculum background is a legitimate match.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one stage where the neighbourhood comparison genuinely favours whoever is nearest. Across Silicon Oasis, Cedre Villas, Academic City and The Villa, local primary tutoring supply is adequate and proximity is a reasonable filter. Paying a Diploma specialist rate for Year 4 reading comprehension is the clearest waste available.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each on a 1 to 8 scale, with the totals converted to a 1 to 7 grade using published boundaries. Most bands are lost on one or two criteria rather than across a subject, and often on the strands covering investigation, evaluation or reflection.
programmes.countryNote: Local MYP supply along this corridor is thinner than parents expect, because most nearby tutors come from British and Indian curriculum backgrounds and criterion marking is unfamiliar to them. The test is simple: ask a prospective tutor to name the four criteria for the subject in question.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Higher Level carries additional content and, in the sciences, greater extended-response demand. Each subject has an internal assessment marked against lettered criteria and moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the neighbourhood comparison stops mattering. Nad Al Sheba holds long-established Diploma centres and Silicon Oasis does not, but neither fact changes whether a Chemistry HL specialist is free at 5pm on a Tuesday within driving distance of your villa. That is an emirate-wide scarcity, and online matching is the only thing that resolves it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-oas.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects families along this corridor ask about, with the part of each that a specialist knows and a capable generalist usually does not. The grid is the real comparison: tutor against tutor, rather than postcode against postcode.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, calculus and proof, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator and a Paper 3 extended problem-solving component at Higher Level. The non-calculator paper is where students who have leaned on a graphic display calculator for routine manipulation come unstuck.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led reasoning with the calculator permitted throughout. Marks go missing in interpretation rather than computation: a regression calculated correctly and then described without reference to the context in the question.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised around Structure and Reactivity, with a data booklet provided in the examination and systematically under-used. Organic mechanisms at Higher Level are the single most time-consuming part of the course to repair, because they require a way of seeing rather than a list.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes from space, time and motion through to nuclear and quantum physics. Uncertainty treatment in the scientific investigation and in the data-analysis section of Paper 1 is the most under-prepared skill in the subject by a wide margin.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. Biology penalises imprecise writing harder than any other science, because an answer that does not name structure, process and consequence scores nothing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and real-world engagement. The internal assessment is a portfolio of commentaries on published articles, and the commonest failure is a diagram drawn correctly and then never used in the analysis below it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Human resources, finance and accounts, marketing and operations. The Higher Level extension questions reward application to the stimulus organisation rather than description of a framework, which is where memorisers lose marks predictably.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and computational thinking, with an internally assessed solution. Marks sit in the documentation rather than the code, which consistently surprises strong programmers in a community full of them.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis of unseen non-literary texts, a comparative essay, the individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay. Students lose marks by paraphrasing rather than analysing and by leaving the global issue unnamed in the oral.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through the exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, with the essay externally marked. A tutor who treats Theory of Knowledge as general discussion rather than as an assessed component will not help in the weeks that count.

sections.heading: What actually differs between these communities
paragraphs: The honest comparison has three columns that matter and one that does not. School supply inside the community differs: Silicon Oasis has a large British-curriculum secondary school and several Indian-curriculum schools within its own boundary, which is genuinely unusual in Dubai. Car dependence differs: The Villa and Dubailand require more driving for routine errands than Silicon Oasis does. And commute to the Diploma centres differs, because Nad Al Sheba and Garhoud hold more of them than Silicon Oasis does.

The column that does not differ is the one families are usually searching on. Access to a Diploma subject specialist at a usable hour is an emirate-level constraint, not a neighbourhood one. Dubai had 227 private schools in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent of enrolment. Divide that cohort by six subject groups and two levels and the resulting pool is small wherever it is measured from.

This is counter-intuitive because the school position varies so visibly. A family in Nad Al Sheba lives beside a long-established Diploma centre and reasonably infers that Diploma tutors must be plentiful locally. The inference fails for a specific reason: teachers at a school are not an open tutoring pool. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a comparable code of conduct.

So the comparison below is written to be used for the decision it can actually inform, which is where to live and which school run to accept, rather than the one it cannot, which is where to find a Chemistry HL tutor. For that second question the answer is identical in all six rows, and it is the reason this page exists in the form it does.

sections.heading: The tutor pool arithmetic, which is identical everywhere
paragraphs: Take the three filters a visiting tutor has to satisfy at once and apply them honestly. First, subject: they must teach the subject your child needs. Second, level: Higher Level and Standard Level are different jobs in the sciences and in mathematics, and a tutor fluent in one is not automatically useful for the other. Third, geography: they must be willing and able to reach your address between roughly 4pm and 6pm, which is the only window in which a Diploma student is both home and still capable.

Each filter individually leaves a reasonable number of people. Applied together, they do not. For Primary Years and most Middle Years work the intersection is still populated, which is why a local tutor is a sensible choice at those levels. For Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Chemistry at Higher Level and Physics at Higher Level, the intersection in any single community along this corridor is close to empty, and the emptiness is structural rather than seasonal.

The table below reports the position by subject and level. It is deliberately unflattering in places, because the alternative is implying coverage that does not exist and letting a family discover it in week three. Several rows say that a local match is perfectly achievable, and those rows are as honest as the thin ones. The decision a parent should take from it is which filter to drop, and the answer is almost always geography.

One further point specific to this corridor. Because Silicon Oasis and Academic City hold so many Indian-curriculum schools and university campuses, the local tutoring market here is deeper than average at the budget end and no deeper at the Diploma end. That mismatch produces a particular failure: a family hires inexpensively, sees no grade movement over a term, and concludes that tutoring does not work, when what happened was that the band was wrong for the job.

sections.heading: What the E66 corridor does to a visiting tutor
paragraphs: This stretch of Dubai is organised around one main road and a handful of junctions, which makes it fast when it is clear and brittle when it is not. A tutor travelling from Mirdif or Garhoud to Silicon Oasis in the late afternoon is dependent on the Ras Al Khor and Nad Al Hamar junctions. A tutor coming from the western side crosses through Dubailand. Either way the journey is twenty-five to forty minutes in good conditions and materially longer in bad ones.

The consequence is not that in-home tutoring is impossible here. It is that the fifteen or twenty minutes lost to arrival come out of the lesson rather than out of the invoice, and that the loss repeats weekly. Across a term that is a meaningful fraction of what was paid for, and it lands on the earlier part of the session, which is the part a student is most able to use. Nobody quotes this and everybody experiences it.

There is a second-order effect on tutor choice. Because the corridor is long and the traffic unpredictable, tutors who do travel tend to cluster their appointments geographically and to prefer later slots that are easier to reach. That means the early window, which is the most valuable one for a Diploma student, is the hardest to buy from a visiting tutor along this road. Families end up with the hour the logistics permit rather than the hour the student needs.

Against that, a video lesson begins at the time it was booked, from Cedre Villas, from Arabian Gates, from The Villa or from Nad Al Sheba, with no difference between them. That is the whole of the operational argument, and it is why the neighbourhood comparison that opened this page ends in the same place for every row. The corridor shapes the school run and the shopping trip; it does not have to shape the tuition.

sections.heading: What the travel premium costs, in AED
paragraphs: The market prices this openly enough that a comparison is possible. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table and at AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, with travel inside the figure. A qualified online subject tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors advertising IB tuition from AED 200 an hour. Budget online runs AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. All read in October 2026.

The monthly packages make the comparison sharper. Around AED 799 a month buys eight online sessions in this market. AED 1,599 to 1,799 buys four in-home sessions of two hours. The contact time is the same and the price is roughly double, and the difference is not teaching. It is a car, a driver's unpaid hour, and the scheduling fragility described above. On a corridor this spread out, that premium buys less than it would in a dense neighbourhood.

None of these figures is an IB Gram rate. Our own terms follow a free trial lesson and a diagnostic conversation, because quoting one hourly number across Primary Years literacy and Chemistry Higher Level would mislead in both directions. What the table is for is checking a quote you already hold: if it sits above the published specialist band, ask what specifically justifies it and expect an answer about subject and level rather than about quality in general.

The honest caveat is that in-home tuition is not simply worse. A physical presence changes behaviour for some younger students, and a device that cannot be scrolled under the table is a real benefit. Those are worth paying for where they are the actual problem. Where the problem is that nobody has diagnosed which criterion or which paper is losing marks, paying a travel premium does not address it and the money would be better spent on a specialist who does.

sections.heading: Household with two curricula, which is common here
paragraphs: Silicon Oasis and Academic City hold an unusually mixed set of schools, so a household here frequently runs more than one curriculum. One child on the IB Diploma at a school in Nad Al Sheba or Garhoud, another on IGCSE at the British-curriculum school inside the community, perhaps a third on an Indian board. That is a logistical situation rather than an academic one, and it changes what the right tutoring arrangement looks like.

The instinct is to find one tutor who can cover both children, which looks efficient and usually is not. A tutor strong in IGCSE mathematics is not thereby equipped for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a tutor who knows MYP criterion marking is not automatically useful for a CBSE board examination. One person attempting both will serve one child well and the other adequately, and the adequate one is where the money is wasted.

Two separate matches at two different hours is almost always better and often cheaper, because the alternative involves paying a travel-inclusive rate for a session that half the household sits out. With online scheduling, splitting the booking is trivial: two tutors, two slots, one point of contact. On this corridor, where journeys between communities run twenty-five to forty minutes, the saving is larger than it would be in a dense area.

There is one real exception. Where two children are on the same board and within a year or two of each other, a shared small-group session can work well for content that both need, and it lowers the cost per student. The test is whether their weaknesses are the same, not whether their syllabuses are. Two students with different gaps in one session means the hour serves an average that fits neither of them.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, and what nobody here is approved by
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulate private education in those emirates, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Those powers are not identical. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, which is the rule underneath every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

Tutors are regulated separately and individually. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published anywhere official.

A provider that describes itself as KHDA approved is not paying itself a vague compliment; it is invoking a KHDA Educational Services Permit, issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, holds no IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, and claims neither. Ask every provider along this corridor the same question and compare what comes back.

sections.heading: The boundary on assessed work, which applies everywhere
paragraphs: A tutor may teach content, explain each lettered criterion, interrogate a research question until it is answerable, model a comparable example on a different topic, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short, and teach referencing properly. A tutor may not write, draft, complete, rewrite or supply any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or any other assessed work. That is the whole of the rule and there is no premium tier that changes it.

The reason is where the consequence lands. Internal assessment is marked against published criteria by the school's own teacher and moderated by the IB, and the student declares the work as their own. Work that is not theirs is malpractice, and the finding attaches to the student rather than to whoever was paid for it. One site competing for these queries sells completed internal assessments at AED 3,750, which is a malpractice outcome with a price tag attached.

Practically this changes how coursework support should be bought. The hours worth paying for sit at the start, where a weak research question is still cheap to correct, and at the point of a complete first draft, where feedback can still be acted on. The hours in between are usually someone watching a student type. A four-hour total across a Diploma internal assessment is a reasonable figure; a twenty-hour total is a sign that something other than teaching is being sold.

Ask any provider to put the boundary in writing before money moves, and keep the reply. This is not a formality. A provider willing to write down exactly what it will and will not do with assessed work has told you something about how it operates, and a provider that deflects the request has told you something more useful still. Apply it to us before you apply it to anybody else.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Silicon Oasis, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Send the subject, the level and the component that is going wrong, plus the hour your child is realistically at a desk. If there are two children on two curricula, say so, because the right answer is usually two matches rather than one. We then match tutors to those exact combinations and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost, and you get a written note afterwards setting out where the marks are going.

The limits are stated rather than buried. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. There is no UAE office, centre or branch, and we do not claim one. We hold no regulator or board approval. We publish no IB examination or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date that a parent plans around is worse than silence; your child's IB coordinator holds the real calendar.

We also disclose coverage. The after-school window on Gulf Standard Time is the busiest part of the week across the entire UAE, and within it Chemistry HL, Physics HL and Mathematics AA HL fill first. When your preferred combination is unavailable you get the nearest slot, a named wait, or an honest no. No researched competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere, and several route UAE parents to an Indian phone number without saying where delivery happens.

Finally, the comparison this page opened with. If you are choosing between Silicon Oasis, Academic City, The Villa and Nad Al Sheba, choose on schools, commute and housing, because those genuinely differ. Do not choose on tutoring access, because it does not. That is the single most useful thing a page about this corridor can tell you, and it is the reason the recommendation at the end is the same in every row of the table.

faqs.question: Is IB tutoring easier to find in Dubai Silicon Oasis than in Academic City or The Villa?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the useful finding. Those communities differ genuinely on school supply, car dependence and commute, but access to a Diploma subject specialist is an emirate-level constraint rather than a neighbourhood one. The International Baccalaureate was 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25, and dividing that cohort by subject group and level produces a small pool wherever it is measured from. Choose between these areas on schools and housing, not on tutoring access.

faqs.question: Do your tutors travel to Cedre Villas or Silicon Gardens?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons across Dubai Silicon Oasis are delivered as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. On this corridor that matters more than usual, because journeys between most points run twenty-five to forty minutes in the late afternoon and the delay comes out of the lesson rather than out of the fee, weekly, for a whole term.

faqs.question: Nad Al Sheba has long-established IB schools. Are there more IB tutors there?

Teachers at a school are not an open tutoring pool: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a comparable code of conduct. So living beside a Diploma centre improves school choice and does not change whether a Chemistry Higher Level specialist is free at 5pm on a Tuesday nearby.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects can we realistically hire locally along this corridor?

Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Chemistry at Higher Level and Physics at Higher Level mostly are not, in Silicon Oasis or in any of the neighbouring communities. For Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay process coaching the constraint is experience rather than geography, since few tutors anywhere have supervised one.

A tutor strong in IGCSE mathematics is not thereby equipped for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and one who knows MYP criterion marking is not automatically useful for a different board's examinations. faqs.question: Is the budget tutoring available near Academic City good value for Diploma work?
faqs.answer: For the right job, yes; for Diploma teaching, usually not. The concentration of university campuses is why Dubai's budget band exists at AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, and that band is genuinely effective for homework supervision, content recall and drilling mathematics that should already be automatic. Pointed at a Higher Level science it tends to produce a term of reassurance and no grade movement, after which the specialist is hired anyway with less time left.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Silicon Oasis family be matched to an IB tutor?
faqs.answer: For subjects with reasonable supply, usually within a few days, because the constraint is a mutually workable hour rather than finding a person. For Chemistry Higher Level, Physics Higher Level or Mathematics AA at Higher Level in the busiest after-school window, longer, and you will be given a named wait instead of a vague reassurance. If speed matters more than the exact hour, say so, because a weekend or earlier-afternoon slot often opens the match immediately.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working in Dubai Silicon Oasis need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published. Because it costs nothing, ask the question and expect a straight answer.

faqs.question: Our Silicon Oasis school deadline is close. Can a tutor draft part of the IA?
faqs.answer: No, and no deadline changes it. A tutor may teach the content, explain each lettered criterion, press on a research question until it is answerable, model a comparable example on a different topic, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach referencing. A tutor may not write, draft, complete or supply any part of it. The work is declared as the student's own and moderated by the IB, so the consequence falls on your child.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram KHDA approved, and is there an office near Silicon Oasis?
faqs.answer: No to both. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, requiring initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, no IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, and no UAE office, centre or branch. What we do is explain what each regulator governs so you can check any provider's claim against the authority rather than against its own marketing.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a student who prefers someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For Diploma work it often works better, because a shared screen beats a shared notebook. Both people see the same working at the same size, a past-paper question can be annotated live, and the published criteria can sit open beside the student's own draft. What it needs is a quiet room, a charged device and occasional parental attention. What it removes is travel, late arrivals and a radius limit on who is allowed to teach your child.

faqs.question: When is the best hour to book a Diploma session in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Between about 4pm and 6pm, after a half hour for food and decompression and before a student stops being able to reason. From Silicon Oasis to a school in Nad Al Sheba or Garhoud, arrival is typically mid to late afternoon depending on the route, so a 4.30pm or 5pm start is the realistic target. That window is also the busiest in the whole UAE, so book it before term starts rather than hunting for it in October.

The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and an unverified date that a parent plans around is the worst kind of error a tutoring page can make. UAE schools sit the May examinations, and your child's IB coordinator holds the actual windows and the internal deadlines, which are the dates that actually govern when tuition is worth buying.

faqs.question: What should we expect from the first month of IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three things, none of them a grade. Your child should be able to name which component is costing them marks. You should hold a written note saying the same thing, by topic and component. And one element of technique should visibly improve, because technique moves faster than content does. Grade movement takes longer than a month and nobody can promise it, so a provider that opens with a predicted grade has told you how it sells rather than how it teaches.

intro.heading: What an IB home tutor in Dubai South is really being asked to do
paragraphs: The phrase an IB home tutor in Dubai South is hired to solve is almost never "my child needs more hours". It is "my child is working hard and the marks are not moving". Those are different problems with different fixes. More hours on the same misunderstanding produces the same score with more fatigue. The fix is diagnostic: find out which command terms the student misreads, which papers they ration badly, which topics they have revised four times and still cannot start under timed conditions. That is a syllabus job, and it is the reason this page leads with syllabus content rather than with testimonials.

Dubai South sits at the southern end of the emirate, around Al Maktoum International and the Expo site, with Emaar South, Dubai Investments Park, Al Furjan, Jebel Ali and Green Community as its neighbours. It is a newer community than Jumeirah or Mirdif, which has a direct consequence for tutoring: the residential density that supports a deep local tutor market is still forming. A family in Dubai South who insists on a tutor physically present is choosing from whoever is willing to drive out along Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road at 5pm. That is a geography filter, not a quality filter, and in the IB it is an expensive one, because the IB is not one subject. It is a Chemistry HL paper with a 35% Paper 2, a Maths AA internal assessment marked on five criteria, and a Theory of Knowledge essay with six prescribed titles.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. For Dubai South the delivery is live one-to-one video, screen shared both ways, with the student's own past-paper script on screen and the mark scheme beside it. This is stated plainly because the alternative — implying a car will arrive — would be false. What the online model buys a Dubai South family is the tutor pool: instead of the handful of teachers within a tolerable drive, the match is made from specialists who teach that subject at that level every week.

The rest of this page is built around the syllabus, because that is what separates an IB specialist from a tutor who is good at maths. You will find the Diploma assessment structure with component weightings, the topics where UAE students most reliably lose marks, the internal assessment criteria named by letter with their mark allocations, what the academic-honesty rules permit a tutor to do with an IA draft, and what the Dubai market actually charges in AED per hour with the source of each band stated. There is also the part most tutoring pages leave out: what happens when no specialist for a niche Higher Level subject is free in the week you ask.

One framing note before the detail. KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, is the body responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. It inspects schools and publishes ratings. It does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership — any tutoring page that implies otherwise is misrepresenting the regulator. Individual tutors in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and that is the credential a parent can actually ask to see.
