dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-south.programmesIntro: Dubai South and its neighbouring communities feed a mix of IB continuum schools and British-curriculum schools that run the Diploma in the sixth form. The three programmes below are the ones families in this cluster ask about, and each carries a note on what it means specifically here.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme is transdisciplinary: there is no subject timetable in the conventional sense, and learning is organised around six units of inquiry a year. Assessment is continuous and descriptive rather than graded, which is why parents moving in from a CBSE or American system often cannot tell whether their child is behind. The concrete skills that matter later are number fluency, reading stamina and the ability to structure a written explanation. Tutoring at this stage is short, frequent and built on those three.
programmes.countryNote: PYP children in Dubai South also sit KHDA's mandatory subjects alongside the inquiry units. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are compulsory in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Families relocating into Emaar South or Al Furjan frequently discover this only at enrolment.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme marks each subject against four criteria, A to D, on a 0-8 scale, then converts the totals to a 1-7 grade. The criteria differ by subject group: in Sciences, criterion B is inquiring and designing and criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science. Students who are strong at content and weak at process lose most of their marks in B and D, not in A. The Personal Project in the final year is separately assessed and is where most of the time pressure lands.
programmes.countryNote: MYP in this part of Dubai is usually a feeder into the Diploma at the same school or at a British-curriculum sixth form nearby. The transition that catches students is MYP Mathematics to Diploma Mathematics: the MYP criterion-based marking rewards communication and reflection, while Diploma Paper 1 rewards accuracy under time with no calculator. Eight weeks of timed drill before Year 12 closes most of that gap.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment worth between 20% and 25% of the final grade, marked by the teacher and moderated externally. The externally assessed papers carry the rest. The arithmetic matters: a student who is good in class and poor in examinations is losing three quarters of the available marks in each subject, and no amount of classroom participation recovers them.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai South Diploma students sit the May session, which is the session UAE schools use. The internal deadlines that actually govern a Year 13 autumn are set by the school's IB coordinator, not by the IB, and they land months before the examinations. A Dubai South family planning tuition around examinations alone will miss the IA and Extended Essay deadlines entirely, which is why the planning conversation starts with the coordinator's calendar.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and is a genuine route for a student who wants Diploma-standard academics in two subjects alongside a vocational specialism. Tutoring demand on CP is almost entirely in the Diploma courses taken within it and in the reflective project's writing structure.
programmes.countryNote: CP is rare in the Dubai South cluster, so a family whose child is on it is often the only one in their circle. That isolation has a practical cost: parents have nobody to compare notes with about what the reflective project should look like. A specialist who has supervised the component elsewhere is the straightforward fix, and online delivery is the only way to reach one from Dubai South.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-south.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects most requested by families in Dubai South, Emaar South and Dubai Investments Park. Each description names what the subject actually assesses and where the marks leak, rather than restating the course title.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where most of the damage is done. Students who have learned the course through a graphical display calculator cannot sketch a derivative or manipulate a logarithm by hand. Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers and vectors. The exploration is marked on five criteria including personal engagement and reflection, which are process marks, not mathematics marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, with statistics, modelling and financial mathematics carrying the weight. The trap is the opposite of Analysis and Approaches: students assume the calculator does the thinking and then lose marks for not stating a hypothesis, not justifying a model choice, or not interpreting a correlation coefficient in context. Higher Level brings in graph theory and matrices.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is multiple choice with no mark for method, so a single unit slip costs the whole question. Paper 2 is extended response where graph-drawing and uncertainty treatment carry marks students rarely practise. Higher Level adds fields, induction and quantum phenomena. The internal assessment needs a measurable independent variable and a defensible uncertainty analysis; most weak scripts fail on the second.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and energetics produce the largest spread of marks. Mechanism questions require curly arrows drawn from the correct lone pair or bond, and examiners do not award a half-drawn mechanism. Higher Level adds entropy and spontaneity, equilibrium calculations and transition metal chemistry. The data booklet is permitted and most students have never learned where anything in it is.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume of recall is the problem, not the difficulty of any single idea. Marks are lost on command terms: outline, explain, distinguish and suggest demand different lengths and different structures, and writing an explain answer where outline was asked wastes time without gaining marks. Higher Level adds plant biology, genetics depth and physiology detail that reward structured note-making over rereading.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked. A correctly labelled diagram with axes, curves and a shifted equilibrium earns marks that prose cannot. Higher Level adds quantitative questions and a theory-of-the-firm style depth. The internal assessment is three commentaries on news articles, each 800 words, each applying one unit of the syllabus; students lose marks by summarising the article instead of applying the theory.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Higher Level sits a pre-released case study for Paper 2, which rewards months of structured preparation rather than last-minute revision. Tools such as Ansoff, force field analysis and investment appraisal must be applied to the specific firm, not described. The internal assessment at Higher Level is a 1,800-word research project based on primary research into a real organisation.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis of a non-literary passage under time, and the guided question is the single biggest source of lost marks because students ignore it and write a general appreciation. The individual oral is a ten-minute presentation plus five minutes of questions, linking a global issue to one literary and one non-literary text. Higher Level adds the 1,200-1,500 word essay.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode in the examination follows the IB's own notation, not Python, and students who have only coded in one language lose marks on syntax they never practised. Higher Level adds resource management, object-oriented programming and a case study. The internal assessment is a solution developed for a real client with a documented design, which means the client conversation has to actually happen.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by a 1,600-word essay on one of six prescribed titles and an exhibition of three objects with commentaries. The essay fails when students write about the topic rather than about the knowledge question in the title. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three bonus points, and students who treat them as optional regularly finish three points short of their offer.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay in one Diploma subject, marked on five criteria with the research question and the critical thinking criterion carrying the most weight. The commonest failure is a question too broad to answer in 4,000 words. A supervisor may discuss and give feedback on one complete draft; writing any part of the essay is malpractice under IB rules.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Taken by many non-Arab students in Dubai schools because Arabic is mandatory under KHDA rules, and frequently the subject that drags a Diploma point total down. Assessment is productive and receptive: a written task, listening and reading comprehension, and an individual oral based on a visual stimulus. The oral is the recoverable component, because it rewards drilled structures rather than broad vocabulary.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-south.regionsIntro: Dubai South online tuition reaches the surrounding communities on the same terms, with the same tutor pool and the same evening slots. These are the neighbourhoods families on this page most often come from.

regions.name: Dubai South
regions.note: The district around Al Maktoum International and the Expo site, taking in Residential District, The Pulse and Expo Golf Villas. Families here are typically a short drive from Dubai Investments Park and Emaar South schools, and a long one from the Jumeirah and Al Barsha school belt.

regions.name: Emaar South
regions.note: A villa and townhouse community inside Dubai South, built around the golf course. Household composition skews towards primary and lower-secondary children, which makes Middle Years Programme and IGCSE demand higher here than Diploma demand, and makes early-evening slots the busiest.

regions.name: Al Furjan
regions.note: Immediately north on the Sheikh Zayed side, with its own school provision and a metro link at Al Furjan station. Secondary students here often travel to schools in Discovery Gardens or Dubai Investments Park, with afternoon arrivals home between 15:45 and 16:30.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park
regions.note: The school cluster for this whole corner of Dubai, with British, IB continuum, Indian and SABIS provision in a tight radius. A Dubai South family's school run usually ends here, which sets the earliest realistic tuition slot at around 16:30 on a weekday.

regions.name: Jebel Ali
regions.note: The older residential and industrial zone to the west, with established British and Indian-curriculum schools. Students here are frequently IGCSE candidates in Years 10 and 11 who move into the Diploma or A Level afterwards, so transition tutoring is a recurring request.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens
regions.note: High-density apartment living with a younger, cost-conscious parent population and strong demand for shared-subject support. Evening slots after 18:00 dominate here because working parents prefer to be at home while a session runs.

regions.name: Green Community
regions.note: A low-rise community within Dubai Investments Park, close enough to the school cluster that students can be home by 15:45. That makes it one of the few neighbourhoods in this group where a 16:00 session is genuinely workable during term.

regions.name: Dubai Production City
regions.note: North-east of the cluster, mixing apartments and villas, with families who often drive children to schools in Motor City or Sports City. The longer school run pushes tuition towards 17:30 and later, and towards weekend mornings for double sessions.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Investments Park and Green Community
schoolClusters.note: The main school cluster serving Dubai South and Emaar South, and the one most students on this page attend. It carries IB continuum, British and SABIS provision within a few minutes of each other, which means a single community can contain Diploma, A Level and IGCSE candidates in the same street.
schools: The International School of Choueifat Dubai Investments Park

schoolClusters.city: Al Furjan, Jebel Ali and Discovery Gardens
schoolClusters.note: The northern arc of the cluster, dominated by British-curriculum schools that run IGCSE at 16 before splitting into A Level or the Diploma. Families here commonly need IGCSE support in Years 10 and 11 and then Diploma support two years later, from the same household.

schoolClusters.city: Dubailand and the southern corridor
schoolClusters.note: A short drive east, and the destination for Dubai South families who choose an IB continuum school over a nearer British one. The commute is the reason evening tuition in this group rarely starts before 17:00 during term time.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-south.modesIntro: Three ways families in Dubai South use one-to-one online tuition. All three are delivered over live video with a specialist; none involves a tutor travelling to a UAE address.

modes.title: Weekly subject tuition
modes.description: One or two sessions a week in a single subject, running across a term. This is the format that moves a grade, because it creates a cycle: diagnose in the session, practise between sessions, mark the practice at the start of the next one. Most Dubai South Diploma families start with one subject and add a second only once the first is stable.

modes.title: Internal assessment and Extended Essay supervision
modes.description: Structured support across the months an internal assessment or Extended Essay actually takes. The tutor works on the student's research question, method, data handling and argument structure, and gives feedback on the student's own writing. Nobody drafts, rewrites or produces content for the student, because under IB academic-honesty rules that is malpractice.

modes.title: Examination-window intensives
modes.description: Compressed blocks of sessions in the weeks before papers, built entirely around timed questions under examination conditions. Content teaching stops; the work is question selection, timing, mark-scheme language and the specific topics the student's own past scripts show as weak. Used by Dubai South families in the spring term and over the winter break.

modes.title: Transition support between programmes
modes.description: Short blocks for students moving between systems: Middle Years to Diploma, IGCSE to Diploma, or an incoming CBSE or American student joining a Dubai South IB school mid-year. The work is gap mapping — identifying what the new course assumes the student already knows and closing those specific gaps before term starts.

sections.heading: Diploma assessment structure: where the marks actually sit
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject splits its marks between externally assessed papers and one internally assessed component marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The internal assessment is worth between 20% and 25% depending on the subject and level. That single fact reorganises a tutoring plan, because the internal assessment is the only component a student can improve months in advance with certainty, while the papers depend on performance on one morning.

The table below sets out the pattern across the subjects most requested from Dubai South. Read it as a planning document rather than a reference: a Chemistry HL student with a strong internal assessment and a weak Paper 2 is losing marks in the component that carries 36% of the grade, and no amount of further laboratory polishing recovers that. Conversely a Maths AA student who has not started the exploration by the spring of Year 12 is gambling 20% of the subject on a rushed piece of work.

The weightings also explain why a specialist matters more in the IB than in most systems. A tutor who knows that Physics Paper 1 carries no method marks will spend sessions on precision and unit discipline. A tutor who does not will spend them on explanation, which is what Paper 2 rewards. Both are reasonable-sounding lessons; only one matches the paper the student is about to sit.

One further consequence for Dubai South families specifically. Because the internal assessment is marked by the school teacher and then moderated by the IB, the mark a student sees on a returned draft is provisional. Moderation can move an entire cohort's internal marks up or down if the school has marked generously or harshly against the published criteria. That is a reason to aim a clear band above the target rather than at it, and a reason to read the criteria directly rather than relying on a classroom comment.

sections.heading: The internal assessment criteria, named by letter
paragraphs: Almost no tutoring page in this market names a single internal assessment criterion, which is strange, because the criteria are published and they are how the mark is produced. A student who does not know that personal engagement is a separate criterion worth marks of its own will write a technically correct exploration and score in the middle band. A student who does know will spend two paragraphs establishing why they chose the question, and gain marks that have nothing to do with their mathematics.

The table gives the criteria and mark allocations for the components Dubai South students most often need help with. Use it to read a returned draft: if the teacher's comment is vague, the criteria tell you precisely which band the piece sits in and what the next band up requires. This is also the honest limit of what a tutor does here. The tutor explains the criterion, asks the questions that expose a weak section, and gives feedback on the student's own draft. The tutor does not write, redraft or supply content.

Two practical notes for families in this cluster. First, internal deadlines are set by the school's IB coordinator and are typically far earlier than students expect, often in the autumn of Year 13 for work examined the following May. Second, a draft that has been through one round of substantive feedback is the maximum the IB permits for the Extended Essay; further rounds are not allowed, so the single draft has to be used well.

sections.heading: Where Dubai South students lose marks, topic by topic
paragraphs: Losing marks is diagnosable. Across the Diploma subjects this cluster asks about most, the same specific failures recur, and they are failures of technique rather than of intelligence. In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches the single largest is non-calculator algebra: students who learned the course on a graphical display calculator cannot differentiate a quotient by hand or solve a logarithmic equation without one, and Paper 1 forbids the calculator entirely.

In Physics the recurring losses are units, uncertainties and graph work. Paper 1 awards nothing for method, so a correct calculation with a wrong power of ten scores zero. Paper 2 awards marks for drawing a line of best fit with a sensible gradient triangle, and for stating an uncertainty with the right number of significant figures, and most students have practised neither. In Chemistry the losses concentrate in organic mechanisms and in multi-step calculations where an early rounding error propagates through to a wrong final answer that was worth most of the question.

In the essay subjects the pattern changes. English A Paper 1 scripts lose marks because students write an appreciation of the passage instead of answering the guided question printed above it. Economics scripts lose marks because the diagram is unlabelled or the axes are wrong, and a diagram that cannot be read earns nothing. Biology scripts lose marks on command terms: an outline answer written as an essay burns ten minutes and gains no extra credit. Each of these is correctable in a handful of sessions once it has been named, which is the entire argument for diagnostic tutoring over additional general teaching.

Published monthly packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are the brackets a Dubai South family is choosing between.

sections.heading: Online against in-home tuition for a Dubai South household
paragraphs: The honest comparison is not cost against cost. It is what each format can actually deliver to an address in Dubai South. An in-home tutor is drawn from whoever will drive to Dubai South for a 17:00 session, which in practice means a radius around the southern corridor and the Investments Park cluster. An online specialist is drawn from everyone who teaches that subject at that level, wherever they are. For a Standard Level subject the two pools overlap enough that either works. For Chemistry Higher Level, Computer Science or Arabic B they do not.

Travel is the hidden cost. A tutor driving from Jumeirah to Dubai South at 16:30 is committing ninety minutes of unpaid time around a sixty-minute lesson, and that time is priced into the hourly rate — which is why Bestimate's in-home band starts at AED 180 while its online band starts far lower. It also constrains scheduling: a tutor who can fit two online sessions back to back in an evening can fit one in-home session, so the slots available to you are fewer and less flexible.

What in-home genuinely buys is physical presence with a younger child who will not sit still for a screen, and the ability for a parent to observe without being in the room. Those are real advantages and they matter most in primary years. For Diploma work the balance tips the other way: the material is a past-paper script and a mark scheme, both of which are more legible shared on screen than passed across a table. sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: This section exists because one page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. Buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller: a finding of malpractice can mean no grade awarded in that subject and, in serious cases, no Diploma. A parent paying for help needs to know where the line sits, and any provider unwilling to state it is the wrong provider.

What a tutor may do is substantial. A tutor may teach the subject content the assessment rests on. A tutor may discuss a proposed research question and push back on one that cannot be answered in the word limit. A tutor may explain each criterion and what distinguishes one band from the next. A tutor may read a complete draft the student has written and give feedback on it — for the Extended Essay, the IB permits one round of substantive feedback on one draft. A tutor may teach referencing conventions, data presentation and the structure of an argument.

What a tutor may not do is produce the work. Not writing a paragraph, not rewriting a section into better English, not supplying a dataset, not editing a draft to completion, not choosing the research question on the student's behalf. The practical test is simple: if a sentence in the submitted document was composed by anyone other than the student, the document is no longer the student's own work. IB Gram tutors teach, question and give feedback, and that boundary is explained to the student at the first session rather than discovered at the end.
bullets: Teaching content, explaining criteria and feedback on the student's draft are all permitted

sections.heading: KHDA, the regulator and what a Dubai South parent can verify
paragraphs: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it inspects private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Those ratings are published on KHDA's own site and are the single most useful public document about a school a Dubai South family is considering. KHDA also sets the mandatory-subject requirements: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in every Dubai private school regardless of the curriculum it is licensed to teach.

What KHDA does not do is accredit private tutors. There is no such thing as a KHDA-approved tutor, and a provider claiming the status is either confusing it with the Educational Services Permit issued to training institutes with physical premises, or inventing it. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval, licence or partnership, and does not operate a centre in the UAE. The credential that does exist for an individual tutor is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

Across the wider UAE the regulator changes with the emirate: ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The table below is the full map, which matters more than it sounds for a Dubai South family, because households in this corner of the emirate sometimes have a child at a school across the Abu Dhabi border and are then dealing with two regulators at once.

sections.heading: Tutor availability from Dubai South, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in this market implies infinite availability. None discloses a limit. The truth is that availability varies sharply by subject and level, and a parent planning a Year 13 autumn deserves to know which requests are matched within days and which take longer. Diploma Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English A are the deep end of the pool and a match is usually quick. Computer Science Higher Level, Arabic B, Theory of Knowledge and the less common Group 3 subjects are thinner, and a request in those can wait.

The honest version of what happens when no specialist is free: we say so. The alternative — putting a general science tutor in front of a Chemistry Higher Level student — is worse than waiting a week, because it costs the family money and the student confidence while teaching nothing they could not have read in the textbook. If the wait is unacceptable, we will say what we can do instead, which is usually a shorter block with a different specialist on the component that is most urgent.

The table sets out typical availability for the subjects this cluster requests. It is a coverage statement, not a promise about a particular week. One structural point behind it: because delivery is online rather than in-home, availability is not limited by who lives near Dubai South. That is the single largest practical benefit of the model, and it is why a Higher Level request from Emaar South is no harder to fill than the same request from Jumeirah.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE school calendar and when work actually gets done
paragraphs: A tutoring plan written without the UAE calendar in it fails in predictable places. The academic year runs from late August or early September to the start of July, with a long winter break in December, a spring break, and a shortened school day during Ramadan. For Diploma students the spring term is when examinations arrive, and it is also the term most likely to contain Ramadan, which changes both the school timetable and the hours in which a teenager can concentrate.

The practical adjustments are straightforward once they are planned rather than improvised. During Ramadan, sessions move later in the evening, after iftar, and shorten from ninety minutes to sixty. Content teaching gives way to timed question practice, which is less cognitively expensive per mark gained. Families who want to keep momentum without adding fatigue typically drop from two sessions a week to one, and use the winter and spring breaks for the intensive blocks instead.

The breaks are the underused resource in this cluster. A Dubai South student with a weak Paper 1 technique has more usable hours in the two weeks of the winter break than in the six weeks either side of it, because the school's own workload drops to nothing. Internal assessment drafting is the other work that fits a break well, since it needs long uninterrupted stretches rather than weekly slots. Planning the year this way — breaks for blocks, term for maintenance, Ramadan for timed practice — is the difference between a plan that survives contact with the calendar and one that quietly stops in March.

Timed practice costs less concentration per mark than new content

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what a Dubai South IB student should know now
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that recognises a school-leaving certificate for use in the UAE, and families usually meet it for the first time at the point of a university application, which is far too late to do anything about the requirements. It is worth knowing the shape of it in Year 11 rather than Year 13, particularly in a cluster like this one where households move between curricula more often than average.

For the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade no lower than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among those five. That last detail matters: one competitor page in this market tells UAE parents that six IGCSE subjects are required, which is wrong, and a family planning around it may pay for a subject they did not need.

For the American track, English proficiency is shown by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics by at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB there is no points threshold published in the source material available here, and this page will not invent one — a figure on 2,654 pages that nobody verified is 2,654 liabilities. Check the IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority directly. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and tutoring is not a requirement of the process.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Not just the subject. Chemistry Higher Level with a weak Paper 2 and a finished investigation is a different brief from Chemistry Higher Level with strong papers and no investigation started. Naming the component means the first session is diagnostic rather than introductory, and it is the single most useful thing a Dubai South parent can send in the first message.

process.title: Send a recent script if you have one
process.description: A marked mock paper or a returned internal assessment draft tells a specialist more in five minutes than a long conversation does. Where marks were lost is visible on the page. If there is no script, the first session produces one by setting a short timed section and marking it against the official scheme.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched specialist
process.description: One full session, no charge and no card required, with the tutor who would teach the term. The output is a written note naming what was covered, what the diagnosis is, and what the first four sessions would address. If the match is wrong, say so and we match again rather than asking you to persist with it.

process.title: Fix a weekly slot around the school run
process.description: Dubai South and Emaar South school runs usually end between 15:45 and 16:30, so the earliest workable weekday slot is around 16:30 and the busiest run from 17:00 to 19:30. Weekend mornings suit double sessions and internal assessment work. The slot is held for the term unless you move it.

process.title: Work the cycle: diagnose, practise, mark, repeat
process.description: Each session ends with set work; the next session starts by marking it. That cycle is what moves a grade, because it converts the tutor's diagnosis into the student's own practice and then checks whether the practice landed. Without it, sessions become weekly explanations that feel productive and change nothing.

process.title: Review against the coordinator's calendar each half term
process.description: Every half term, compare what has been covered against the school's internal deadlines for the internal assessment, Extended Essay and mock papers. Those dates, not the examination dates, govern the autumn of Year 13. The review is where a plan gets re-pointed before a deadline arrives rather than after.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level, not on location
whyPoints.description: A Dubai South family hiring locally is choosing from tutors willing to drive south in the evening. Matching online removes the geography filter entirely, so a Physics Higher Level request from Emaar South is filled from the same pool as one from Jumeirah. For Standard Level subjects this matters little; for Higher Level and niche subjects it is the whole difference.

whyPoints.title: Sessions built on scripts and mark schemes
whyPoints.description: The working material is the student's own marked paper with the official mark scheme beside it, both shared on screen. That is a more legible arrangement than passing paper across a table, and it keeps sessions anchored to how marks are awarded rather than to how the topic is explained in the textbook.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach content, explain criteria by letter and give feedback on the student's own draft. They do not write, rewrite or edit coursework to completion. The boundary is explained to the student in the first session, which protects the Diploma the family is paying to improve.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed, including when it is thin
whyPoints.description: If no Computer Science Higher Level specialist is free this week, we say so and give a date. The alternative is placing a general tutor in a specialist seat, which costs money and confidence while teaching nothing. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit; this one does.

whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the band stated. Three of the most visible competitors in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. A parent should be able to check a number, which is the only reason to publish one.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims, because there are none to make
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership, and operates no UAE office or centre. The regulators are named on this page to explain what they do, which is useful, rather than to borrow authority, which would be false.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor in Dubai South who comes to the villa?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. For Dubai South the delivery is live one-to-one video with a subject specialist, timed to Gulf Standard Time. Independent in-home tutors do operate in this part of Dubai, and Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-350 an hour with independent tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. The trade is straightforward: you gain physical presence and lose access to specialists who do not live within driving distance of the southern corridor.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do Dubai South families usually attend?
faqs.answer: Most students on this page attend schools in the Dubai Investments Park and Green Community cluster, where IB continuum, British and SABIS provision sit within a few minutes of each other, or travel to the Dubailand corridor for an IB continuum school. Al Furjan and Jebel Ali supply the British-curriculum schools that run IGCSE at 16 before splitting into A Level or the Diploma. KHDA publishes inspection ratings for every one of them on its own site, which is the document worth reading before a conversation with an admissions office. IB Gram has no affiliation with any school named here.

faqs.question: How much of an IB subject grade comes from the internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Between 20% and 25% depending on the subject and level. In Mathematics the exploration is 20%; in the sciences the investigation is 20%; in Economics the three commentaries total 20%. That proportion is the part of the grade a student controls with time rather than with performance on one morning, which is why a tutoring plan should name the component it is targeting. It also means a student who has not started the internal assessment by the spring of Year 12 is gambling a fifth of each subject on work done under deadline pressure.

faqs.question: What does Paper 1 in IB Physics punish that Paper 2 does not?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 is multiple choice and awards nothing for method, so a correct chain of reasoning with a wrong power of ten scores zero. Paper 2 is extended response and does award method, which means partial credit is available for a well-structured answer that ends in the wrong number. The practical consequence for tutoring is that Paper 1 preparation is unit discipline, estimation and speed, while Paper 2 preparation is structure, graph work and uncertainty statements. Treating them as the same revision task is a common and expensive mistake.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to help with my child's Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, within defined limits. A supervisor or tutor may discuss the research question, push back if it is too broad to answer in 4,000 words, explain the five assessment criteria and what separates one band from the next, and give feedback on one complete draft the student has written. The IB permits one round of substantive feedback on one draft. What is not permitted is writing, rewriting or editing any part of the essay to completion. If a sentence in the submitted document was composed by anyone other than the student, the essay is no longer the student's own work.

faqs.question: Are there KHDA-approved IB tutors in Dubai South?
faqs.answer: No, because KHDA does not accredit private tutors. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects schools and sets mandatory-subject requirements; it issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with physical premises, which is a different thing entirely. Any provider advertising KHDA-approved tutors is misdescribing the regulator. The credential that does exist for an individual is the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. That is the document a parent can reasonably ask a tutor to produce. IB Gram holds no KHDA approval or partnership.

faqs.question: My child is strong in class but drops marks in exams. What changes?
faqs.answer: The session content changes from explanation to timed production. A student who understands the material and underperforms on papers is usually losing marks to timing, command-term misreading, or presentation — writing an essay where outline was asked, skipping a diagram label, not stating an uncertainty. None of those is a knowledge gap and none of them improves with more teaching. The work is a diagnostic pass over the student's own marked scripts to name the specific losses, then repeated timed sections targeting them, marked against the official scheme with the wording compared line by line.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start on a Dubai South weekday?
faqs.answer: Around 16:30 for most families. School runs in this cluster usually end between 15:45 and 16:30, depending on whether the school is in Dubai Investments Park, Al Furjan or the Dubailand corridor. Green Community households sometimes manage 16:00 because the school is minutes away. The busiest slots run from 17:00 to 19:30, and the latest weekday start is 21:30 Gulf Standard Time. Weekend mornings suit double sessions and internal assessment work, which needs longer uninterrupted stretches than a weekday evening allows.

faqs.question: Which IB Maths route should a Dubai South student choose?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches if the destination is engineering, physics, mathematics or most economics degrees; Applications and Interpretation if it is business, social sciences, design or medicine in many systems. The deciding factor is the university prerequisite rather than which course looks easier, because some programmes specify Analysis and Approaches by name. Check the requirement for the actual courses on the shortlist before Year 12 subject choices close. The practical difference in the classroom is that Analysis and Approaches has a non-calculator Paper 1 and heavier algebra, while Applications and Interpretation is calculator-permitted throughout with statistics and modelling carrying the weight.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an IB Diploma student need?
faqs.answer: One a week in one subject is the usual starting point, and it is enough if the cycle is working: diagnose in the session, practise between sessions, mark the practice at the start of the next. Two a week makes sense in an examination term or when an internal assessment deadline and a mock paper collide. More than two in one subject is rarely productive, because the limit is how much independent practice a student can complete between sessions, not how much teaching they can absorb. Adding a second subject before the first is stable usually slows both.

faqs.question: Do I need a private tutor for my child to get MoE equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process that recognises a school-leaving certificate, and tutoring is not a requirement of it. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. The IB requirement is not published in any source this page can verify, so check it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority. IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees equivalency.

faqs.question: What should I send when I first ask about IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three things make the first session diagnostic rather than introductory: the subject and level, the component that is weak, and a recent marked script. A mock paper with the examiner's marks on it shows a specialist exactly where the losses are, and a returned internal assessment draft shows which criterion the band is sitting in. If no script exists, the first session creates one by setting a short timed section and marking it against the official scheme. The school's internal deadline calendar is the fourth useful item, particularly for a Year 13 autumn.

faqs.question: Does tutoring stop during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It usually changes shape rather than stopping. School days shorten, concentration in the afternoon drops, and sessions move later into the evening after iftar. Ninety-minute sessions typically become sixty, and content teaching gives way to timed question practice, which costs less concentration per mark gained. Families who want momentum without added fatigue often drop from two sessions a week to one for the month and move the intensive work into the spring break instead. Planning that shift in advance works considerably better than discovering it in the second week.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist in my child's subject is available?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we give a date rather than a substitute. Diploma Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English A are usually matched within a few days. Computer Science Higher Level, Arabic B and Theory of Knowledge are thinner and a request can wait a week or more. Putting a general science tutor in a Chemistry Higher Level seat costs a family money and a student confidence while teaching nothing new, so we do not do it. Where the wait is unworkable, we propose a shorter block with a different specialist on the single most urgent component.

faqs.question: Is Arabic compulsory for an IB student in a Dubai private school?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, under KHDA's requirements. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For an IB Diploma student, Arabic B is frequently the subject that drags a point total down, and the recoverable component is usually the individual oral, which rewards drilled structures rather than broad vocabulary.

faqs.question: How do online IB sessions actually run?
faqs.answer: Live video, one-to-one, with a shared screen in both directions. The working documents are the student's own marked script and the official mark scheme, open side by side, annotated as the session runs. Work is set at the end of each session and marked at the start of the next, and a short written note goes to the parent naming what was covered and what comes next. A tablet with a stylus helps in mathematics and the sciences but is not required; a phone camera pointed at a worked page does the same job less comfortably.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-south.closingHeading: Start with the syllabus, not with a search for somebody nearby
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-south.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB home tutor in Dubai South, the useful first question is not who lives close by. It is which component is losing marks and who teaches that component every week. Send us the subject, the level and a recent marked script, and the free trial lesson will come back with a written diagnosis rather than a sales conversation. Lessons are delivered live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, by a specialist matched to the paper your child is actually sitting. If the subject we are asked for is thin that week, we will say so and give you a date.

Each is matched to one course at one level, so a Sports City student taking Chemistry HL and Maths AI SL works with two specialists rather than one all-rounder stretched across both.

intro.heading: Start with the syllabus, not the schedule
paragraphs: Most tutoring enquiries from Dubai Sports City begin with logistics. The hour that would suit, the Hessa Street traffic at five, the sibling at Victory Heights Primary who finishes earlier. Those are real constraints, and they get solved. But they are not the reason a Diploma student is three marks short on every Paper 2 response, and solving them first tends to produce a pleasant weekly hour that changes nothing on the transcript.

The IB publishes, for every course, a subject guide that states what is assessed, how it is weighted, and the command terms examiners use. It publishes assessment criteria for the Internal Assessment with letters and mark ceilings attached. Almost no student has read either document. Almost every student who moves from a 4 to a 6 has, by then, read both. A tutor whose first session is a diagnostic against the actual syllabus outline is working from the same map the examiner uses.

That is the shape of IB Gram's work for families here. A first lesson takes the student's most recent school assessment, sorts the lost marks into categories — content not known, content known but not retrieved under time, command term misread, working not shown, units or significant figures dropped — and produces a short list of syllabus sections to rebuild. From that point the weekly hour has a target, and the student can tell you what it is.

Delivery is where expectation and reality part company in the UAE. Parents in Sports City search for a home tutor because that is the familiar phrase and because a villa in Victory Heights has a perfectly good dining table. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Sports City students run live online over video, one to one, with a shared whiteboard and the past paper on screen.

The practical effect is a different tutor pool. Matching by drive time means choosing from whoever is free within twenty minutes of Dubai Sports City on a Tuesday at six. Matching by subject means a Physics HL specialist who has taught Option B, or a Maths AA teacher who has supervised thirty explorations, regardless of which emirate or time zone they sit in. For a Diploma subject at Higher Level, that difference is the whole of the result.

Everything below is written to be used rather than skimmed: what each DP course actually assesses, where the marks go missing, what the market charges in AED, what the Internal Assessment criteria are called, and how to count a term backwards from the written papers. Read the rate table and the in-home comparison together, because the two answer the question the search is really asking: what does the convenience cost, and what does the money buy instead.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-sports-city.programmesIntro: Dubai Sports City and the communities around it feed schools running the IB continuum alongside British and American curricula. The three programmes below are the ones that generate tutoring requests from this part of Dubailand, with what each actually demands of a student.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internally assessed component and two or three written papers. The grade for each subject runs 1 to 7, and the diploma total of 45 includes up to three points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Higher Level courses add both extra syllabus content and an extra paper in most sciences.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Dubai sit the May session, which is the session Dubai schools timetable their mocks and internal deadlines around. Because KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the licensed curriculum, a Sports City DP student is carrying more timetabled subjects than the six on the IB transcript, and revision planning has to account for that.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of interdisciplinary study assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8 and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. There are no external papers in most schools until the optional eAssessment at the end of MYP 5. Criterion wording matters more than content recall: a strong answer that ignores the strand the criterion names scores in the middle band.
programmes.countryNote: In the Dubailand communities, MYP students most often need help with the gap between criterion-referenced marking at school and the content density of DP or IGCSE the following year. The usual request from Sports City families is a bridging block in MYP 5, focused on algebraic fluency and written scientific explanation.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led transdisciplinary learning with no external examination, assessed through the Exhibition in the final year. Support at this stage is almost entirely about reading fluency, number sense and written structure rather than examination technique, and sessions are shorter — thirty to forty-five minutes is usually the ceiling for useful concentration.
programmes.countryNote: Primary families around Victory Heights and Motor City typically ask for help after a school report flags reading comprehension or multiplication recall. The honest answer is often a short block of eight sessions rather than a year-long commitment, and that is what gets recommended when a diagnostic supports it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-sports-city.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses Sports City families ask for most, described by what the assessment actually rewards. The descriptions are deliberately specific: a parent should be able to tell from them whether the problem is content, technique or timing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation carry the grade. HL adds Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper where students are led through an unfamiliar investigation. Marks are lost on method lines never written down, on reasoning that jumps from statement to conclusion, and on calculator work presented without the supporting algebra.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving. The graphic display calculator is central, and the common failure is treating it as the answer rather than the tool: a regression printed with no interpretation, a hypothesis test run with no conclusion in context. Contextual sentences earn marks in this course that pure computation does not.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, thermal and nuclear physics, with the HL extension reaching further into induction and quantum phenomena. The reliable mark losses are vector direction, unit conversion before substitution, and explanation questions answered with a formula instead of a causal chain. Paper 1 penalises arithmetic slips that no working can rescue.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic chemistry, with HL adding depth in each. Organic mechanisms and equilibrium shifts produce the widest spread of marks. Students who can describe Le Chatelier in words often cannot apply it to a specific perturbation, and that gap is diagnosable in one session.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cell biology through to ecology and physiology, assessed heavily on data interpretation. The highest-yield work is reading graphs and tables precisely, quoting figures with units, and distinguishing correlation from mechanism. Long-answer questions reward structure: a claim, the evidence, and the biological explanation in that order.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with the Internal Assessment built from commentaries on published news articles. Diagrams are where marks are won and lost: axes unlabelled, shifts undrawn, or a correct diagram never referenced in the written evaluation. HL adds quantitative questions and a policy paper.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, marketing, operations and finance, with tool-based analysis running through every paper. Candidates lose marks by naming a tool without applying it to the stimulus, and by writing evaluation that lists advantages and disadvantages instead of reaching a judgement supported by the case material.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works, plus the Individual Oral and, at HL, the essay. The common weakness is feature-spotting: identifying a technique without saying what it does to a reader. Marks follow from linking device, effect and the writer's purpose in a single sentence.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive skills across five prescribed themes. For non-Arab students in Dubai schools this course sits alongside the KHDA mandatory Arabic requirement, and the two are often confused. Writing tasks are marked on register and text type as much as on vocabulary, so a correct letter in the wrong register loses more than a grammar slip.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition of three objects and the prescribed-title essay, contributing with the Extended Essay to three diploma points. Students treat it as unexaminable and then lose points that would have changed a university offer. Support here is structural: choosing a title that can actually be argued, and keeping the essay anchored to knowledge questions.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Dubai Sports City means in practice
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Dubai Sports City, as the search is actually used, means private one-to-one Diploma or Middle Years tuition arranged outside school for a student living in or around the Sports City master plan. IB Gram provides exactly that, delivered live online over video rather than by a visitor to a Dubai address. In-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and no page on this site promises otherwise.

The phrase survives because it describes a category rather than a delivery method. For twenty years, private tuition in Dubai meant someone arriving after work with a folder. That model still exists in Sports City, it has a real market rate, and the section below quotes what the market charges for it. What has changed is that the constraint it was built around — the tutor has to be nearby — has stopped being a constraint, while the price of travel has not.

The consequence matters more at Higher Level than anywhere else. A Sports City cohort may have four students taking Physics HL in a given year. The number of local tutors who have taught the HL extension, rather than general secondary science, is small. Online matching replaces the drive-time filter with a subject filter, and for a student who needs Option B or the astrophysics content, that is the only filter that predicts anything.

What a parent should expect from the arrangement is unglamorous: a fixed slot, a named specialist, a syllabus checklist that gets shorter, and a written note after each session saying what was covered and what was set. If an enquiry cannot be matched to a genuine specialist for that course and level, the honest answer is a wait or a referral, not a general tutor presented as one.

sections.heading: The Diploma assessment structure, component by component
paragraphs: Diploma grades are built from a small number of components with fixed weightings, and most students cannot name them. A student who knows that the Internal Assessment is a fifth of the Chemistry grade behaves differently from one who treats it as homework. The table below sets out the pattern across the courses most requested in Sports City; exact weightings are published in each subject guide on the IB's own site and should be checked there for the student's cohort.

Two structural facts do most of the work. First, the internally assessed component is marked at school against published criteria and then moderated, which means it is the one part of the grade a student controls in slow time rather than in two hours under invigilation. Second, Higher Level in the sciences and in Maths AA carries an additional paper, so an HL student is not doing the SL course with extra reading — the examination shape itself differs.

This is why a diagnostic session starts by asking which components a student has actually attempted under timed conditions. It is common to meet a Year 13 student in the Dubailand belt who has written four full Paper 2 essays and never once sat Paper 1 to time. The missing component is almost always the one bleeding marks, and it never appears in a school report as anything other than a grade.

The practical instruction that follows is to build the revision plan component by component rather than subject by subject. A student lists every paper and every internally assessed task across all six subjects, then marks which ones they have attempted to time and which they have only met in class. The unattempted column is the plan. Done in the first Diploma year, it takes an afternoon and removes most of the surprises that otherwise arrive with the mock results.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Lost marks fall into a short list of categories, and sorting a student's last marked paper into them takes one session. Content genuinely not known is the smallest category in most cases. The larger ones are retrieval under time pressure, command terms misread, working not written down, and answers that are correct but unsupported.

Command terms are the cheapest fix available. The IB defines them, and the definitions are enforced in marking. A question that says 'outline' wants a brief account and will not pay for three paragraphs. 'Explain' requires reasons or causes, so a correct description scores nothing. 'Evaluate' requires a judgement, and an answer that balances advantages against disadvantages and stops short of deciding has not completed the task. Students who learn the fifteen or so terms that recur in their courses pick up marks within weeks.

The second cheap fix is arithmetic and presentation discipline in the sciences and maths. Units dropped before substitution, significant figures rounded early, vectors treated as scalars, and method lines left in a calculator rather than on paper. Each of these is worth one or two marks per paper, and across six subjects that is a grade boundary.

The expensive problems are different in kind: a topic never properly taught, a gap carried forward from MYP or IGCSE, or a student who has stopped believing the subject is learnable. Those need sequencing rather than technique work, and they need to be identified early enough in the first Diploma year to be rebuilt rather than patched.

sections.heading: What IB tuition costs around Dubai Sports City, in AED
paragraphs: Begin with the monthly figure, because that is what a family actually budgets. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai rate table puts weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Converted to an hourly view, the published bands are wide. EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, both at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. Bestimate's in-home band runs AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoted between AED 200 and 500 once travel is priced in.

Those figures are the market, published by the providers named, and they are not IB Gram's price list. The point of printing them is that three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Sports City family transacts in. A parent should be able to see the bands before any conversation about fees.

The structural reading is simple: the in-home premium is a travel charge, not a teaching charge. Comparing the AED 150 to 300 qualified-online band with the AED 180 to 500 in-home band, the difference buys a car journey. At Higher Level, the same money spent on specialist selection rather than on proximity buys a tutor who has taught the component the student is failing.

sections.heading: Home visits in Sports City against live online lessons
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search deserves, and it is better made with numbers than with adjectives. A home visit in Sports City costs the published in-home band, takes a tutor out of circulation for the journey each way, and limits the pool to people who live or work within a reasonable drive on that specific evening. An online lesson costs the online band, starts on the minute, and draws from a pool defined by subject rather than geography.

Hessa Street and the Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed interchange decide the practical timing. A tutor crossing from Al Barsha or Jumeirah at six in the evening is budgeting forty minutes each way, and that time is in the fee whether it is itemised or not. Families in Remraam and Dubailand Residence see the effect more sharply still, because the second journey of the day lands on the student rather than the tutor.

There are genuine advantages to a person in the room, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. A young primary student is easier to keep on task in person. A practical skill demonstrated on real apparatus is not identical to one demonstrated on screen. For Diploma students working on past papers, the balance tips the other way: the shared screen is a better surface for annotating a mark scheme than a dining table, and the session recording can be rewatched before a mock.

IB Gram's position is stated plainly rather than hedged. No tutor is sent to a UAE address. Lessons for Sports City students are live, one-to-one and online, and the argument for that model is in the table below rather than in a promise nobody should make.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject has an internally assessed component, and every one of them is marked against named criteria with a published mark ceiling for each. Students routinely submit work that is strong on one criterion and empty on another, which is the single most avoidable loss in the Diploma. No competitor page in this market names a single criterion, which tells you how rarely it is explained to families.

The sciences use a small set of criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The mathematical exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The pattern is consistent: roughly half the available marks are for process and communication rather than for the result. A student who produces a competent experiment and writes two sentences of evaluation has left marks on the table that no amount of extra data would recover.

Process coaching, done properly, is criterion teaching. The tutor explains what each criterion rewards, the student self-marks their own draft against it, and the tutor gives feedback on what the student has written. The boundary is firm and it is an IB rule rather than a house style: a tutor may teach, question and review, and may not write, complete or produce any part of assessed work. An exploration drafted by somebody else is a malpractice finding against the student, not a shortcut.

Timing is the other half of it. Internal deadlines are set by the school, usually well before the examination window, and they are the dates a Sports City family should have on the fridge. A research question agreed in the first term leaves room for data collection to fail once and be redone. A research question agreed three weeks before submission does not.

sections.heading: Counting a term backwards from the written papers
paragraphs: Revision plans fail because they are counted forwards from today. Counted backwards from the papers, the same calendar gives different instructions. Dubai Diploma students sit the May session, and because IB session and results dates are not published in a form this page can verify, the only honest advice is to confirm every IB date with the school's Diploma coordinator and against ibo.org before acting on it.

For the Cambridge and Pearson qualifications that sit alongside the Diploma in many Sports City households, the dates are sourced and usable. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate plans around June and November and nothing else. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct zone timetable; it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after reading the wrong one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For the most recent completed cycles: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why a school should always work from the live official timetable rather than from a restated date.

The planning consequence is the part worth acting on. Entry deadlines sit months before papers, mock windows sit a term before, and internal coursework deadlines sit before that again. Working backwards, an exam-year student in Sports City should have finished Internal Assessment drafting before the mock window opens, because the fortnight those two collide in is the one that produces the panicked February enquiry.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects, and what a school report leaves out
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. A Sports City parent reading an inspection report is reading a KHDA document, and the six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak is a judgement about the school, not about a cohort or a subject.

The market context is worth stating because it explains why Diploma cohorts here are small. KHDA reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest by enrolment, Indian second, American third and the IB accounting for 7% of pupils. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

Alongside the licensed curriculum, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Using different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry permission is prohibited.

What that means for a tutoring plan is practical. A Diploma student in Sports City is timetabled for more than six subjects, so the hours available for revision are fewer than the IB transcript suggests. And a school report that gives a grade and a comment does not say which component produced the grade. That is the question a diagnostic answers, and it is the reason the first session is spent reading the student's marked paper rather than the report.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and what to ask before you book anyone
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. A separate point applies in Abu Dhabi, where ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school; the permit's code of conduct is reported to bar the same thing. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, and it should be verified against the current ADEK text before being relied on.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor, and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit, holds no regulator or examination-board accreditation, and claims none. It is an independent matching platform; the regulators named on this page are described because parents need to know who does what, not because any of them endorses this service.

The questions worth asking any provider in Sports City are short. Which course and which level has this tutor actually taught, and for how long? Does the tutor hold a MoHRE private tuition permit? Is the quoted rate per hour or per session, and does it include VAT? What happens after one lesson if the match is wrong? And, the one most providers dodge: what exactly will the tutor do with an Internal Assessment, and what will they refuse to do?

process.title: Tell us the course, the level and the last mark
process.description: A short enquiry naming the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, the school, and the most recent assessment result. The marked paper itself is more useful than the report. That is enough to decide whether a specialist is available for that exact course and level.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the proposed specialist
process.description: A full online session with the tutor who would teach the block, not a sales call with a coordinator. The tutor works through the student's own marked paper and sorts the lost marks by cause. Parents receive a written summary afterwards with the syllabus sections to rebuild.

process.title: Agree a plan with a target, not a term
process.description: Sessions are booked in short blocks against a named objective: Paper 1 timing, organic mechanisms, the exploration's research question. A block with a target can be judged. A standing weekly hour with no target tends to continue regardless of whether it is working.

process.title: Weekly work with marked homework
process.description: Each session ends with past-paper work set and marked against the published scheme before the next one. The syllabus checklist is updated, and the written note to parents says what was covered and what was set rather than reporting that the session went well.

process.title: Review after four sessions and change if needed
process.description: At the four-session mark the plan is reviewed against the target. If the marks have not moved, the usual answers are a different diagnosis, a different tutor, or a different number of sessions. Changing the match costs nothing and happens more often than most providers admit.

whyPoints.title: Matched by course and level
whyPoints.description: A request for Chemistry HL is matched to a Chemistry HL teacher, not to a science graduate. Where no specialist is free for that course and level, the answer is a stated wait or a referral elsewhere, because a general tutor presented as a specialist wastes a term that an exam student does not have.

Three of the best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all. A parent in Sports City should see the bands before the conversation, not after.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria, question method and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not write, complete or produce any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or coursework. Pages in this market sell completed assessments; that is a malpractice finding waiting to land on the student.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are live, one-to-one and online, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and home visiting is offered only in India. The format is on the page rather than discovered after a deposit.
