IB session dates are not published here because they could not be verified from the IB directly, and inventing one would be worse than omitting it.

whyPoints.title: Short blocks with a target
whyPoints.description: Work is sold in reviewable blocks tied to a named objective and reviewed after four sessions. The alternative — an open-ended weekly hour nobody evaluates — is how families end up paying for a year of pleasant conversation that the June or May results do not reflect.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor in Dubai Sports City who comes to the villa?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons for every UAE family are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Independent tutors in Sports City do visit homes, and published market rates for in-home one-to-one sessions run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is priced in, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The premium buys a car journey rather than better teaching, which is why the online model is the one offered here.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects do Sports City families most often ask for?
faqs.answer: Mathematics at both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, Chemistry, Physics and Biology at Higher Level, Economics, and English A Language and Literature. Requests concentrate in the second Diploma year, when Internal Assessment deadlines and mock examinations land in the same term. The subject pattern reflects university intentions: students aiming at engineering and medicine carry two or three Higher Level sciences, and those are the courses where a local tutor pool of general science teachers stops being sufficient.

faqs.question: How does a first online session with a Diploma student actually run?
faqs.answer: The student brings their most recent marked school assessment. The tutor works through it on a shared screen, sorting lost marks into categories: content not known, content known but not retrieved under time, command term misread, working not shown, units or significant figures dropped. By the end there is a short list of syllabus sections to rebuild and one piece of past-paper work set. Parents get a written summary. It is a diagnostic rather than a sales call, and it is free before any block is booked.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Maths Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and calculus route, with proof and manipulation carrying the grade and a non-calculator Paper 1. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led, with the graphic display calculator permitted throughout and marks attached to interpreting results in context. Neither is the easy one. Some degree courses in engineering, mathematics and physics expect the Analysis route, so the choice should be checked against the admissions pages of the specific universities a student is considering before it is made on comfort.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IB Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the assessment criteria, explain the mark ceiling attached to each, question the research design, discuss whether the data supports the conclusion, and give feedback on what the student has written. A tutor cannot write, complete or produce any part of it. That boundary is an IB academic-honesty rule, and work a student did not produce becomes a malpractice finding against the student. Pages in this market sell finished Internal Assessments; treating that as a service rather than a risk is how candidates lose a diploma.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Sports City Diploma student usually need?
faqs.answer: One per subject per week is the common starting point, which is why a student needing two subjects ends up with two tutors rather than one longer session. In the run-in to written papers that often rises to two or three sessions a week in a single subject, built entirely around timed papers and mark-scheme review. The number should follow a diagnosis rather than a package. Where one targeted block of eight sessions will do, booking a year is a waste of money.

faqs.question: Is a private tutor working in Dubai Sports City required to hold a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system under the service 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so quoted amounts should be treated as unverified.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge exam series do UAE students sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in those two series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate should never plan around it. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential; it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after working from the wrong version.

faqs.question: Does the IB Diploma work for admission to UAE universities?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education operates an equivalency process for secondary certificates, and it is the Ministry rather than any tutoring provider that decides an outcome. For the British track the published requirements are five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. No verified IB points threshold is published here, so an IB family should confirm the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 5 and moving to the Diploma. What is worth doing now?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fluency and written scientific explanation, in that order. MYP marks four criteria out of eight each and converts them to a 1-7 grade, so a student can hold a solid grade while leaving one criterion consistently weak. The Diploma then prices that weakness in content terms. A bridging block in the final MYP year, aimed at manipulation without a calculator and at structured explanation answers, removes most of the first-term shock reported by Dubailand families each September.

faqs.question: Should a Diploma student in Sports City keep tutoring running through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Diploma students it is usually the better arrangement. School days shorten during Ramadan and concentration in the late afternoon drops, so a session placed after Iftar generally produces more work than the same hour at four o'clock. Because lessons are online, moving a slot needs no journey to be rearranged on either side. Families in Sports City and Motor City often use the period for Internal Assessment process work rather than timed papers, which suits a shorter and more variable day.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for a Higher Level subject in Dubai Sports City?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a realistic wait, or referred elsewhere. The alternative practice in this market is to supply a general subject tutor and describe them as a specialist, which costs an exam-year student a term they cannot recover. Availability is tightest in Higher Level Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches during the second Diploma year, because that is when demand across every Dubai cohort peaks at once. Booking ahead of the mock window rather than after it is the practical fix.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education compulsory for an IB student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For revision planning this matters: a Diploma student is timetabled for more than the six IB subjects.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: By marks on timed papers, not by how the sessions feel. Set a measurable target at the start of a block — a Paper 1 score, a reduction in method marks lost, an Internal Assessment criterion self-marked accurately — and review it after four sessions. If the target has not moved, the diagnosis, the tutor or the session count is wrong, and all three are changeable. A provider who cannot tell you what the current block is trying to move is not measuring anything either.

faqs.question: Is a free trial lesson genuinely free in Sports City?
faqs.answer: The trial lesson is a full one-to-one online session with the tutor proposed for the block, with no card required and no obligation to continue. The condition worth stating is that it is one session per subject, and it is a teaching session rather than an assessment sold separately afterwards. If the match is wrong, the next step is a different tutor rather than a refund conversation, and changing a match early is normal rather than awkward.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-sports-city.closingHeading: Start with the marked paper, not the timetable
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubai-sports-city.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB home tutor in Dubai Sports City, the fastest useful step is to send the course, the level and your child's most recent marked assessment. That is enough to say honestly whether a specialist in that exact course and level is free, and what the first block should try to move. The trial lesson is a real teaching session with the tutor who would do the work, delivered live online in Gulf Standard Time, and it ends with a written list of syllabus sections to rebuild. If no specialist is available, you will be told that instead of being matched to a general tutor.

Each is listed by the courses they actually assess against, with the level stated, because a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL brief is not the same job as Mathematics Applications SL.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near Dubailand who actually knows this syllabus?
paragraphs: That is the real question behind the phrase. A parent in Dubailand types "IB home tutor" and gets back a list of people sorted by postcode, which is the wrong sort order for the problem. The Diploma Programme is not one subject with one difficulty setting. It is six subject groups, two levels, three core components, and a marking regime where the same topic is examined differently depending on whether the student sits Higher or Standard Level. A tutor who is twelve minutes away and teaches general secondary maths cannot read a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL paper and tell you which of the five assessment objectives your child is dropping marks against.

Dubailand makes this sharper than most Dubai districts. It is a very large development zone rather than a compact neighbourhood, stretching south-east along Al Ain Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and taking in Arabian Ranches, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, DAMAC Hills, Town Square, Mudon and Remraam. Two families both living in Dubailand can be twenty-five minutes apart. A tutor who agrees to a six o'clock slot in Arabian Ranches is not the same person who can make a six o'clock slot in Town Square, and the one who can do both is charging for the car.

The supply side matters too. Independent tutors concentrate where they already work and where public transport reaches, which in Dubai means the Marina and Jumeirah corridor, Al Barsha, Business Bay and Deira. The Dubailand belt is villa-led and car-dependent. The practical result is that the closer a parent insists the tutor must live, the narrower the subject pool gets, and the narrower that pool gets, the more likely the available person teaches the wrong level of the right subject.

There is also a legal layer most search results do not mention. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. A parent is entitled to ask whether the person sitting with their child holds it, and a neighbourhood-first search makes that question harder to answer, not easier.

So the honest answer to the search is this. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Dubailand villa; home visits are a service we run only in India. What we do is remove distance from the matching problem entirely, so the constraint becomes the subject and the level rather than the drive. The rest of this page sets out what the in-home market charges in this part of Dubai, how the two formats compare on cost and time, how to count backwards from the exam series, and where a tutor's role stops under IB academic-honesty rules.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubailand.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes run in Dubai schools and families in the Dubailand belt meet all of them, often across siblings. The notes below say what each one is actually assessed on and what that means for a student living this far from the city centre.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Progress is judged through transdisciplinary units of inquiry, a portfolio of work and the Year 6 Exhibition, which is a student-led project rather than a test. Tutoring at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining reasoning aloud, because the Middle Years Programme that follows asks for written justification immediately and children who were never asked to produce it struggle in Year 7.
programmes.countryNote: Several primary schools serving the Dubailand belt run PYP, and families here frequently move a child from a British Foundation Stage setting into a PYP class mid-phase because of villa handover dates. The gap that shows up is almost never arithmetic; it is the expectation that a seven-year-old can say why an answer is reasonable. Short weekly sessions close that faster than extra worksheets do.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks each subject against four criteria, A to D, each on a 0-8 scale, and the criteria descriptors are what the grade is built from rather than a percentage. Year 10 and 11 students sit eAssessment in some schools, and the Personal Project is required of every student in MYP 5. Marks are lost where students answer the question but not the criterion, which is a skill a tutor can teach directly by working through descriptor language against the student's own draft.
programmes.countryNote: Dubailand families often meet the MYP as the programme their child is in when a transfer happens, because the belt's school supply mixes British and IB settings within a few kilometres. A student arriving from a Year 9 IGCSE track into MYP 4 has the content but not the criterion habit. That is a term of work, not a year, provided somebody sits with the actual rubric rather than with a textbook.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The external papers differ between HL and SL in content, duration and weighting, so a tutoring plan built for the wrong level wastes hours on material the student will never be examined on.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools enter candidates for the May session, and the internal deadlines a Dubailand student actually works to are set by their own coordinator months earlier. The practical consequence is that the useful tutoring window for internal assessment work opens in the spring of the first Diploma year, long before anyone is thinking about papers, and the belt's families tend to arrive a term late because the school calendar does not advertise it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs at least two Diploma Programme courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a language development portfolio and personal and professional skills. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and suits students who want a vocational specialism without dropping academic subjects. Tutoring usually targets the DP courses inside it, since those carry the external examinations.
programmes.countryNote: Very few schools in the Dubailand belt run CP, so a family here that wants it is usually looking across the city rather than down the road. That is exactly the case where distance-based tutor search fails hardest: the course is rare, the cohort is small, and the person who has taught the reflective project to completion is unlikely to be a neighbour.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubailand.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma Programme courses Dubailand families ask about most, with the level and the specific place marks go missing. A tutoring request that names the course and the level gets matched in hours; one that says "IB maths" has to be unpicked first.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most UAE engineering and economics applicants need. HL adds proof, complex numbers and a far heavier calculus load, and Paper 3 is a non-calculator-free extended investigation. Marks go missing in method communication: students reach correct answers without showing the reasoning the markscheme pays for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led and calculator-active throughout. Students who moved here from a British GCSE track often underrate it, then lose marks on modelling questions that require interpreting a context in words rather than producing a number. The HL course carries substantially more statistical inference than the SL one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity dominate the mark distribution and both are taught early, so weaknesses compound for two years. HL adds further topics and a longer Paper 2. The recurring failure is unit and significant-figure discipline in the data-analysis questions, which costs marks on content the student genuinely understands.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics carry the difficulty. HL extends into further organic and spectroscopic analysis. Students lose marks by describing when the command term asks them to explain, and by writing equations that balance but omit state symbols the markscheme requires.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and vocabulary-dependent. The common pattern is a student who can recall the process but cannot answer a six-mark question in the structure the examiner needs. Statistical treatment of data in the internal assessment is where otherwise strong candidates drop a band.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks: axes labelled, curves shifted the right way, the new equilibrium identified. HL adds calculation papers. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles, and choosing an unusable article is the most common early mistake.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-driven, and the tools must be applied to the case rather than described. Students who learned to define terms for IGCSE keep defining them here and run out of time. The HL extension and the case study released ahead of the examination both reward structured practice far more than rereading notes.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two assessed orals and written papers on unseen texts. The Individual Oral requires a global issue linked to two works and students routinely pick an issue too broad to sustain for ten minutes. Close analysis of how a text produces meaning is the skill that lifts a grade, not plot knowledge.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a working solution with documentation, and the documentation is where marks are won. HL adds abstract data structures and a case study. Students who code well often under-score because they never recorded their design decisions against the criteria.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic regardless of licensed curriculum, so almost every IB student here carries it. Separate classes are required for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Tutoring targets the productive skills, which is where the assessment weight sits.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubailand.regionsIntro: Dubailand is a zone rather than a street, and the communities inside and beside it have genuinely different school runs, different traffic and different realistic session times. The notes below are operational rather than promotional.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: The established end of the belt, with on-community primary provision and a short run to Sheikh Zayed Road schools. Secondary students here often travel out of the belt, so a 4pm session is unrealistic and a 6.15pm start works.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Later handover and a younger cohort, so PYP and lower MYP dominate. The Al Qudra Road approach is the pinch point in the afternoon, which is why parents here tend to prefer sessions that do not involve anybody driving.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 3
regions.note: Newest of the three, with families still settling school places and a high rate of mid-year curriculum transfers. Transition support between British Year 9 and MYP 4 is the single most requested piece of work from this community.

regions.name: Motor City
regions.note: Apartment-heavy and closer in than the Ranches, with on-site school provision and a denser evening calendar of sport. Sessions here get squeezed between training slots, so a fixed 45-minute weekday format outperforms a flexible 90-minute one.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Academy timetables run the household. Students in football and cricket programmes train most weekday evenings, which pushes serious revision to mornings on the weekend. That is a workable pattern online and an expensive one for a tutor driving in.

regions.name: DAMAC Hills
regions.note: Villa community off Umm Suqeim Road extension with its own school and a long outbound commute for anybody attending a Jumeirah-corridor school. The arrival time home on a weekday is the constraint that decides when tutoring can start.

regions.name: Town Square
regions.note: At the far end of the belt on Al Qudra Road, and the community where distance-based tutor search breaks down most completely. The subject specialist a Diploma student needs is rarely willing to make the drive twice a week at any price.

regions.name: Mudon and Remraam
regions.note: Mixed villa and apartment stock with school provision inside or beside the community for primary years and longer journeys from Year 7. Families here ask more often than most about covering two children in one evening, which online scheduling handles cleanly.

schoolClusters.city: Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills and the Al Qudra corridor
schoolClusters.note: The older, villa-led half of the belt. School provision runs from on-community primaries to full through-schools a short drive north, and the mix of IB and British secondary means siblings in one household are often on different boards entirely.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Motor City, Sports City and the southern Dubailand communities
schoolClusters.note: Denser, newer and more apartment-led, with several schools inside the communities themselves. Evening sport is heavier here than anywhere else in the belt, and it is the practical reason tutoring slots move later in the week.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubailand.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every request that arrives from this part of Dubai. All of them run over live video; the difference is cadence and who else is in the room.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, term-time
modes.description: A fixed slot with the same subject specialist each week, pinned to the student's own school assessment calendar rather than to a generic scheme of work. This is the format that suits a student holding a grade but wanting the band above, and it is the only one that reliably builds the method-communication habit that IB markschemes reward.

modes.description: A short, dense block of sessions around the internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. The tutor works on research question viability, criterion interpretation, method and the student's own draft. The student writes every word; the tutor reads, questions and gives feedback, which is the only form this support may take under IB rules.

Sessions move faster and carry more between-session work. It is a sharpening format, not a rescue format: it works where content is broadly in place and marks are being lost to method.

sections.heading: Why the nearest tutor and the right tutor are rarely the same person in Dubailand
paragraphs: Set the two requirements side by side and the conflict is obvious. The first is geographic: somebody who can be in your villa by a particular hour, twice a week, for a school year. The second is technical: somebody who has taught your child's exact course at your child's exact level recently enough to know how the markscheme behaves. In a compact city those two sets overlap. In a development belt that runs for fifteen kilometres along Al Ain Road and Al Qudra Road, they mostly do not.

The arithmetic of a tutor's week explains why. A specialist teaching a single Diploma course has a finite number of usable weekday evening slots, because every family wants the same ones: after school, before homework collapses. If each visit costs forty minutes of driving at either end, the tutor can serve perhaps three families a week in a dispersed area against six in a dense one. The rate has to carry the car, and the subject range has to widen to fill the diary. That is how a parent searching for a Chemistry HL specialist ends up being offered a general science tutor who is available on Tuesdays.

Widen the search beyond driving distance and the constraint inverts. The question stops being who is free and near and becomes who has taught this course at this level, which is a question with a real answer. A family in Town Square and a family in Arabian Ranches can be matched to the same Physics HL teacher at different hours of the same evening, and neither of them is paying for fuel or waiting to see whether Al Qudra Road is moving.

None of this makes in-home tutoring a bad product. It makes it an expensive answer to a problem that has a cheaper one, and in the Dubailand belt specifically the premium buys travel rather than expertise. The table below sets out where the two formats genuinely differ, including the places where in-home wins.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring actually costs around Dubailand, and what the premium buys
paragraphs: Start with the number nobody publishes. Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this market quote no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The figures below are market rates gathered from published competitor pricing and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table, not an IB Gram price list. They are here so that a parent can tell whether a quote they have been given is normal.

The cheapest band, roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, is university students and generalists working online. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For primary numeracy or reading practice that band is often perfectly adequate. For a Diploma Programme internal assessment it is not, because the person at that rate has usually never read an IB markscheme, and a parent who buys twenty cheap hours instead of six specialist ones ends up paying more for less movement.

The middle band, AED 150 to 300, is where a qualified subject tutor working online sits. Above it, AED 200 to 450 and upward is the IB, IGCSE and A Level specialist band; TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 plus. The top of the market, AED 500 to 650, is named or examiner-led provision, with BartyED advertising AED 650. Monthly packages circulate too: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Read the in-home column as a travel premium rather than a quality premium. A tutor charging AED 350 for a visit in Town Square is charging for ninety minutes of driving attached to sixty minutes of teaching, and the teaching is not better for having been delivered in person. IB Gram's own answer to the pricing question is a free trial lesson and a consultation, because the sensible unit of comparison is whether this particular specialist moves this particular student, not an hourly figure quoted before anybody has met.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the examination series
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a session, a registration deadline or a results date. That is strange, because the calendar is the one thing a tutoring plan has to be built around. The first thing to get right is which series applies in the UAE. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series; the February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE page quoting it is giving parents a date they cannot act on. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. IB candidates in UAE schools sit the May session.

Work backwards from the examination and the useful dates stop being examination dates. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers because centres have to submit candidate data and order materials. Internal assessment deadlines are set by the school, not the board, and they are typically several months before the final submission window so that teachers can mark and the coordinator can moderate. That is why a Diploma student who starts thinking about the internal assessment when the examination timetable appears has already missed the window where tutoring helps most.

Backward-looking dates are worth citing because they are checkable. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are the real intervals: roughly ten weeks from paper to result in the summer, and closer to nine from the November series. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which can be revised, so the official timetable is the thing to check rather than any figure restated on a tutoring page.

One Cambridge detail catches families who have moved emirates or countries. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask the school's examinations officer which zone the centre sits in before building a revision plan around a timetable found online.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and what they do to a Dubailand week
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In 2024-25 the emirate had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula, with the British curriculum the largest by enrolment at 37 per cent, Indian next at 26 per cent and the International Baccalaureate a minority share. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the following academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Dubai's next intake also adds seven new private schools, four British and three IB, creating 16,846 new places.

The part that reshapes a timetable is the mandatory subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

Those subjects have their own language rules. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies for Arab students is delivered primarily in Arabic; and non-Arab students take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can reasonably ask about.

For a Dubailand student the practical effect is a longer taught week than the Diploma or IGCSE subject list suggests. Instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that no mandatory subject lesson should run shorter than 25 minutes. A revision plan that ignores those periods overestimates how much free evening time exists. It is also worth knowing that for these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, so Arabic support works within the school's own material.

sections.heading: Where a tutor's job stops: academic honesty on the IB core
paragraphs: This is the section that should decide which provider a Dubailand family uses, and almost nobody writes it. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments for a four-figure sum. That is not a competitive product; it is an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. A diploma can be withheld. So the boundary needs stating plainly rather than left to inference.

What a tutor may do is substantial. They may teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion actually asks for, test whether a research question is viable before the student commits a term to it, review a draft the student has written and say where it is losing marks, model an analysis on a different data set, and teach referencing and citation properly. They may ask hard questions about method. They may read a conclusion and point out that it does not follow from the results.

What a tutor must never do is produce the work. A tutor does not write the exploration, does not draft the Extended Essay, does not compose the Theory of Knowledge essay, does not supply a Personal Project and does not edit a student's text to the point where the voice is no longer theirs. Nor should any tutoring page offer to supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables as downloads: those are the board's copyright, and the right move is to cite the official source and link out to it.

There is a UAE-specific line worth knowing too. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. Reporting on this is press-sourced rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it against the current ADEK text before relying on it, but the direction of travel is clear: your child's own classroom teacher is not the right person to pay privately.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: This question has a definite answer in the UAE and most tutoring pages avoid it. Private tutoring is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and states a two-working-day completion time, with applications through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences follow. The first is that there is no excuse for not holding one: the permit costs nothing and takes two working days. The second is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and a figure circulating online could not be verified, so treat any page quoting a specific amount with caution.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. That requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. No tutoring platform in Dubai may honestly describe its tutors as KHDA-approved, and that phrase is not one we use. IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved, SPEA approved or accredited by the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no honest tutoring platform in this market should claim otherwise.

What a Dubailand parent can do with this is practical. Ask the question directly before the first paid session, ask which category of eligibility the tutor falls into, and ask whether the child attends the tutor's own school. Those three answers tell you more about a provider than any testimonial on a landing page.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what a Dubailand IB or IGCSE student has to show
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which the UAE Ministry of Education recognises a foreign secondary certificate, and it matters because it sits between a school leaving certificate and a UAE university place. Zero competitor pages in several of the query clusters researched for this project mention it at all, and one ranking page publishes the wrong subject count for the British track. For a family in Dubailand with one child on IGCSE and another on the Diploma, getting this right is more useful than any revision tip.

On the British track, the published requirements are specific. Students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. That five-subject rule is the number to work to; a competitor page claiming six is wrong, and planning a child's IGCSE option block around the wrong count has real consequences.

On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the International Baccalaureate there is a point worth being blunt about: no verified IB points threshold for UAE equivalency could be read on an official Ministry source for this project, so no figure is published here. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority directly.

Two cautions. Equivalency is not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or expedites, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. IB Gram describes the process and points to the official channel; the application itself belongs to the family and the Ministry. Nor is tutoring required for university admission or school progression, and any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: What happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Every tutoring platform in this market writes as though a tutor is always available for every course at every level. That is not true of any of them, and pretending otherwise just moves the disappointment to the week after the enquiry. So here is the honest version for a Dubailand family.

Common requests are matched quickly. Mathematics at both Diploma routes, Physics, Chemistry and Biology at HL and SL, Economics, Business Management, English A and the IGCSE sciences have deep coverage, and a trial lesson can usually be arranged within a few days of an enquiry. Where a family wants a specific slot that everybody else also wants, the limiting factor is the hour rather than the subject, and shifting a session fifteen minutes earlier or later often solves it immediately.

Narrower courses are different. A rarely-offered Group 2 language, Theory of Knowledge supervision at short notice, Computer Science HL with a specific programming paradigm, or Career-related Programme reflective project support may take longer, and sometimes the right answer is that we do not currently have the right person. In that case the useful thing is to say so and give a date, rather than to put a near-fit in front of a Diploma student in their final year.

There is one further disclosure that belongs on a UAE page. Tutoring here is delivered online by specialists who may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, and the network includes experienced IB and Cambridge teachers outside the Emirates. That is a feature of how a Town Square family gets a Chemistry HL specialist at all, but a parent is entitled to know it up front rather than discover it from a dialling code. Nobody is sent to a UAE address in any scenario; home visits are a service IB Gram operates only in India.

process.title: Tell us the course and the level
process.description: Not "IB maths" but "Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL, Year 12, struggling with calculus and Paper 3 technique". Name the school if you are willing to, because the internal assessment calendar differs between Dubailand schools and that changes the sequencing of the first month's work.

process.title: Say when the student is actually free
process.description: Work out the real arrival time home on a weekday, after the bus and after sport. A slot that looks fine on paper and is fifteen minutes too early fails every week. Academy families in Sports City and Motor City often find weekend mornings work far better than weekday evenings.

process.title: Meet the specialist in a free trial lesson
process.description: A full session, no charge, no card. The point is diagnostic: the tutor should finish it able to tell you which specific skill is costing marks. If the fit is wrong, say so and we match again rather than asking you to persist with somebody your child does not click with.

process.title: Agree a plan with dates in it
process.description: A short written plan naming the topics, the cadence and the checkpoints, anchored to the school's own assessment calendar rather than a generic scheme. A plan without dates is a wish. Internal assessment blocks get their own milestones because those deadlines are set by the school months ahead.

process.title: Review at six sessions, then at the series
process.description: Six sessions is enough to see movement in method even where the grade has not shifted yet. Review against the diagnostic, not against a feeling. Pause for school examination weeks and travel; nothing about the schedule has to run continuously to be effective.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus, not by map
whyPoints.description: The brief we match against is the course code and the level, so a family in Town Square and a family in Arabian Ranches get the same quality of specialist. In a belt this dispersed, that is the single biggest practical difference between online and in-home provision.

whyPoints.title: Prices stated as the market, not as spin
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the competitor or source that published it, with the band named. Three of the most visible pages in this market publish no price at all. A parent should be able to check whether a quote is normal before paying for a first hour.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line drawn in writing
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not produce internal assessments, Extended Essays or Theory of Knowledge essays. One page ranking in this market sells completed coursework; that is a malpractice risk carried by the student, not the seller.

whyPoints.title: The calendar built in from the start
whyPoints.description: Plans are sequenced against entry deadlines, school internal assessment dates and the series the student actually sits - June and November for Cambridge, May for IB candidates in UAE schools. The Cambridge February/March series is offered in India only and has no place in a UAE plan.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claimed that we do not hold
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or accredited by the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and does not operate a UAE office or centre. We explain what each regulator does and link to it. A platform claiming an approval it does not hold is telling you something about the rest of its page.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: Where a niche course has no specialist free, we say so and give a date rather than putting a near-fit in front of a final-year Diploma student. No competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is why parents keep discovering them in week three.

faqs.question: Can I actually get a home tutor who comes to my villa in Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service we run only in India; everything we deliver to UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Independent in-home tutors do work across the Dubailand belt, and the market quotes them at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. The honest comparison is that the premium over an online specialist buys driving rather than better teaching, and in a belt stretching from Arabian Ranches to Town Square it also narrows the subject pool to whoever is willing to make the journey twice a week.

faqs.question: Why is it so hard to find an IB specialist who lives near Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Because independent tutors cluster where demand is dense and journeys are short, which in Dubai means the Marina and Jumeirah corridor, Al Barsha, Business Bay and Deira. The Dubailand belt is villa-led, car-dependent and spread over fifteen kilometres. A tutor losing eighty minutes to driving per visit can serve roughly half as many families as one working in a dense area, so they widen their subject range to fill the diary. That is why a parent asking for Chemistry HL is so often offered general science instead, and why removing the drive from the equation widens the choice rather than narrowing it.

faqs.question: Which schools do Dubailand students usually attend?
faqs.answer: The belt mixes on-community provision with schools a short drive north. Families here name Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches, Ranches Primary School, GEMS Metropole in Motor City, Victory Heights Primary School, South View School, Fairgreen International School, GEMS FirstPoint School at The Villa and Bradenton Preparatory Academy, with secondary students often travelling out to Safa Community School, Kent College Dubai or GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail. Schools are named as catchment context only, with no affiliation implied. Current inspection ratings should be read on the KHDA website rather than taken from any tutoring page.

faqs.question: What time can a weekday session realistically start in the Dubailand belt?
faqs.answer: Work from the real arrival time home rather than the school bell. A secondary student travelling from a Jumeirah-corridor school to Arabian Ranches 2 or Town Square is often not home before half past four, and in Motor City and Sports City evening training frequently occupies five until seven. The slots that survive a full term are usually after six for secondary students, and weekend mornings for anybody on an academy timetable. Online sessions start minutes after the student walks in, which is the main scheduling advantage over a visit that depends on Al Qudra Road moving.

faqs.question: Does my child's IB tutor need a permit to teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published. Since the permit costs nothing and MoHRE states a two-working-day completion time, there is no reasonable explanation for not holding one.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for IB Diploma tutoring around Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: a qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named provision reaches AED 650. Budget online tutoring starts far lower, around AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik. For Diploma internal assessment work the budget band is usually false economy. IB Gram's answer is a free trial lesson first, because the right comparison is movement, not an hourly figure.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely as effective as somebody sitting at the kitchen table?
faqs.answer: For secondary students, in most cases yes, and for some it is better. Diploma work is screen-based anyway: papers, data sets, graphing software, annotated drafts. A shared screen with both people writing on the same document does things a paper exercise book cannot, and the session is recorded in notes rather than evaporating. The honest exception is younger children, roughly below Year 5, and students with significant attention difficulties, where physical presence does real work. For an MYP 5 or Diploma student in Dubailand, the limiting factor is the specialist's expertise, not the format.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both my children if they are on different programmes?
faqs.answer: Usually it is better that they do not. A child in MYP 3 and a sibling in Diploma Year 2 need different things, and the person who is excellent at criterion-based MYP feedback is not automatically the right Physics HL specialist. What works well in practice is two consecutive slots with two specialists on the same evening, which costs nothing extra in travel because there is none. Families in Mudon and Remraam ask for this arrangement more than anyone else in the belt, and online scheduling makes it ordinary rather than complicated.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child actually sit in the UAE?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge International qualifications, the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any UAE page quoting a March entry deadline is giving you a date you cannot use. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. IB Diploma candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. One further Cambridge detail matters: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and you must use the timetable for your zone, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Internal Assessment without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each criterion asks for, test whether a research question is viable before the student commits a term to it, read a draft the student has written and identify where marks are being lost, model an analysis on different data, and teach referencing properly. A tutor must never produce the work: not the exploration, not the Extended Essay, not the Theory of Knowledge essay. One page ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments. That is an IB malpractice trigger, and the penalty lands on the student.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks left before the Dubailand school sits its papers. Worth starting?
faqs.answer: Not too late to be useful, but the plan has to change. Eight weeks is a technique window, not a content window. A diagnostic paper comes first, then the work targets the two or three places marks are actually being lost, which at this stage is usually command-term reading, method communication and timing rather than missing knowledge. Expect two or three sessions a week and real work between them. What eight weeks will not do is rebuild two years of a Higher Level course, and any provider promising a specific grade from here is selling something they cannot deliver.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit around an IB timetable in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They are compulsory. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. The practical effect for a Dubailand family is a fuller taught week than the IB subject list implies, so a revision plan built only around the six Diploma subjects overestimates available evening time.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers and mark schemes for my child to work through?
faqs.answer: We do not reproduce or supply board material. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are the boards' copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. What a tutor does instead is point to the official source, show the student how to use what the school has legitimately provided, and build equivalent practice questions in the same style. If a provider is offering a download library of papers, that is a copyright problem they have not thought about and you would be inheriting it.

faqs.question: What if the tutor you match us with is not the right fit?
faqs.answer: Say so and we match again. The trial lesson exists precisely to surface this before money changes hands, and the useful signal is not whether the session was pleasant but whether the tutor could name the specific skill costing marks by the end of it. If a fit fails later in the term, the same applies. What we will not do is ask a final-year Diploma student to persist with a near-fit because the diary is full, and where no specialist is genuinely free for a narrow course we will say that and give a date instead.

faqs.question: Is tutoring needed for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: No, and any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. Equivalency has published requirements: on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which is wrong. No verified IB points threshold could be read on an official Ministry source for this project, so none is published here. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubailand.closingHeading: Start with the subject, not the postcode
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-dubailand.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB home tutor in Dubailand, the thing to fix first is the brief. Name the course, the level and the specific problem, then ask who has taught exactly that recently. Distance is the constraint that makes the question unanswerable in a belt this dispersed, and it is the one constraint online delivery removes entirely. Book a free trial lesson with a Diploma Programme specialist, judge it on whether the tutor can tell you which skill is costing marks, and decide from there. No card is required, nothing is sent to your address, and the only thing being tested is whether this particular teacher moves this particular student.

intro.heading: Emaar Beachfront, Dubai Marina, JBR: the same tutoring answer three times
paragraphs: Emaar Beachfront sits on a man-made peninsula reached by a single road link off King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street, wedged between Dubai Harbour on one side and the open water of Dubai Marina on the other. There is no school on the island. There is no tuition centre on the island. Every child living in one of its towers travels off the peninsula to study, which makes the phrase "home tutor" unusually literal here: the alternative to a tutor in the apartment is a second journey after a school journey that already ate an hour.

That geography is why parents here start by comparing neighbourhoods. A family in a Beachfront tower will ask whether they would get better tutoring coverage if they moved the search to Dubai Marina, or JBR, or across to Al Sufouh. It is a reasonable question and it has a disappointing answer. The three neighbourhoods draw on the same freelance pool, feed the same cluster of schools in Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Jumeirah, and sit inside the same evening traffic window. Changing the pin on the map changes almost nothing about who is available to teach Physics HL on a Tuesday.

What does change the answer is the delivery model. A tutor who drives to a Beachfront address is constrained by the causeway, by visitor parking in a tower with a shared basement, and by the fact that an hour of lesson time costs them two hours of their evening. That cost shows up in the rate and in the shortlist: the pool shrinks to people who already live within a short drive and who happen to teach the subject and level you need. For a widely taught subject at SL, that pool is adequate. For Chemistry HL, Maths AA HL, Economics HL or an Extended Essay in a niche discipline, it is thin, and the thinness is invisible until you have interviewed four people who cannot help.

IB Gram works the other way round. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, so the question becomes which IB specialist is the right teacher for your child rather than which IB specialist lives near the Marina. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Saying so plainly matters more than the keyword: a page that implies a tutor will ring your doorbell in Emaar Beachfront and then delivers a video call has misled a parent at the worst possible moment, eight weeks before an exam series.

The rest of this page does the comparison properly. It publishes what the Dubai market charges in AED, by provider model, with each figure attributed. It sets Emaar Beachfront beside Dubai Marina, JBR, Dubai Harbour and Palm Jumeirah on the things that actually differ: school commute, realistic earliest session start, which curricula the nearby schools run. It explains what a tutor may and may not touch on an Internal Assessment under IB academic-honesty rules. And it says what happens when no specialist is free, which no competitor page in this market discloses.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-emaar-beachfront.programmesIntro: Children in Emaar Beachfront towers are spread across three IB stages at once, because the towers attract families with a wide age spread rather than a single school cohort. Each stage needs a different kind of help, and conflating them is the commonest planning error we see from this part of New Dubai.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examination. Progress is judged through transdisciplinary units of inquiry, a portfolio, and the Year 6 Exhibition. Tutoring at this stage is about securing number sense, reading fluency and the habit of explaining a method out loud, because the MYP assumes all three. A PYP student who can get the right answer but cannot say why will stall in MYP Criterion C.
programmes.countryNote: Beachfront primary children typically travel to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah, which means a bus pickup before 07:00 and a return after 15:30. A 25-minute online session at 17:00 fits that day; a tutor arriving at 16:30 does not, because the child has not eaten.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks run on four criteria per subject, each scored 0-8, and the conversion to a 1-7 grade is published by the school rather than the IB. Most families only discover this in MYP 4. Tutoring here is largely criterion literacy: knowing that Criterion D asks for application in unfamiliar contexts, and that a technically correct answer with no reflection scores in the middle band.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving this cluster run MYP to Year 9 and then switch to IGCSE, so a Beachfront family may be planning for MYP 5 that never happens. Check the school's published pathway before booking a two-year MYP plan.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at HL, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades are 1-7 per subject with up to three bonus points from TOK and the EE. The Diploma is where the specialist shortage bites: a student taking Chemistry HL, Maths AA HL and Physics HL needs three different subject teachers, not one generalist.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. Internal deadlines for IA drafts, the EE and TOK land across the preceding autumn and spring, which is why a January start on a DP2 subject is late rather than early. Confirm every IB date with your school's Diploma coordinator.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and is often overlooked by families comparing the Diploma against A Levels. Tutoring focuses on the DP courses inside it, which are marked to full DP standards even though the overall award is different.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP provision in Dubai is narrow, families in this cluster who want it usually travel further than they would for the Diploma. That is one of the few cases where the neighbourhood you live in genuinely changes the schooling decision.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-emaar-beachfront.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and MYP subjects requested most often by families in Emaar Beachfront, Dubai Harbour and the surrounding Marina towers. The description says what the subject actually assesses and where the marks leak, because that is what determines how many sessions a student needs.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof. HL adds a third paper with no formula support beyond the booklet. Marks go missing in method communication: a correct final answer with no intermediate line scores a fraction of the available marks, and that habit is formed in MYP.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy problem solving. The graphic display calculator is assumed throughout. Students lose marks by failing to state the model, define variables, or comment on whether the result is reasonable in context.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal, waves, electricity, circular motion and fields. HL extends into quantum and nuclear content. The recurring failure is a half-drawn free-body diagram: the physics is sound, the forces are unlabelled, and the mark scheme never gets to see the reasoning.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. HL adds depth across every theme. Organic mechanisms are where DP1 students stall, usually because they memorise arrows rather than the reason an electron pair moves.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, molecular biology, genetics, ecology, physiology and the HL extensions. The marks are in the command terms: "outline" and "explain" carry different expectations, and answering the easier one is the most common self-inflicted loss across the whole subject.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed through diagram-led extended response and three commentaries drawn from published news. HL adds calculation-based policy questions. Weak diagram labelling costs more than weak theory.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with a research project at the centre. Students who treat the project as an essay rather than an evidence-led analysis of one real organisation lose the top band.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary and literary texts, the Individual Oral, Paper 1 guided analysis and Paper 2 comparative essay. The Individual Oral is where preparation pays most, because it is the one component a student can rehearse against a global issue they have chosen.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic regardless of the licensed curriculum, so Beachfront children sit Arabic alongside their IB courses. Tutoring streams split by prior exposure, because combining first-language and additional-language learners is not permitted in school classes.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects against a prescribed prompt, plus a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. TOK is graded A-E and feeds the bonus points. Students lose marks by describing knowledge rather than examining how a claim comes to be justified.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in one subject, supervised at school. Tutoring here is process coaching: research question scope, method, source criticism and structure. A tutor may read and comment; the writing must be the student's own.

subjects.name: Design Technology and Computer Science
subjects.description: Both carry heavy internal assessment weightings and both reward documentation discipline over flair. Students who build first and document later cannot reconstruct the design cycle evidence the criteria demand.

Each of these areas is within a few kilometres of Emaar Beachfront, each is often suggested as a better base for finding a tutor, and in each case the operative difference is commute rather than tutor supply.

regions.name: Emaar Beachfront
regions.note: A gated cluster of residential towers on a reclaimed peninsula with one road link. No school, no tuition centre, and basement parking that visitors cannot reach without a resident escort. Online sessions remove all three frictions at once.

regions.name: Dubai Harbour
regions.note: Immediately adjacent, built around the cruise terminal and marina berths. Shares the same access corridor and the same school-run pattern, so a Harbour family and a Beachfront family face an identical evening timetable.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Dense, older and far better served by road and tram, which does widen the pool of tutors willing to travel. It also puts a 17:00 session inside the worst of the Marina's own congestion, which cancels most of the advantage.

regions.name: JBR
regions.note: Walkable, with a long-established resident population and the most mature local tutoring market in the cluster. Families here still report the same specialist gap at HL, which is the clearest evidence that proximity is not the constraint.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: One trunk road and a monorail, with villa frontlines and apartment towers served by separate access points. Travel times inside the Palm are unpredictable enough that in-home tutors commonly quote a premium for it.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Where much of the cluster's schooling actually happens, including long-established British and IB provision. A tutor based here can reach Beachfront in good traffic, which is to say not between 15:30 and 19:00.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Towers and offices across Sheikh Zayed Road from the Marina, with the highest concentration of freelance tutors in the cluster. The road crossing at the wrong hour is the whole problem with relying on them.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Low-rise apartment communities with their own feeder school provision and a settled family population. Often held up as the easy-tutoring neighbourhood; in practice it has the same HL specialist thinness as the Beachfront towers.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: This is where most secondary-age children from Emaar Beachfront and Dubai Harbour study. The cluster runs both British provision to A Level and full IB continuum schools, which is why a single Beachfront tower can hold a Year 11 IGCSE student and a Year 11 MYP student with completely different assessment calendars.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Jumeirah Park
schoolClusters.note: The second commute direction from the Beachfront causeway, taken by families who prioritised a particular curriculum over distance. Journey times here are more predictable in the morning than in the afternoon, which is the opposite of what parents expect when they first move in.

schoolClusters.city: The Greens, The Meadows and Jumeirah Village
schoolClusters.note: The inland alternative, reached by Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Khail Road. Several of these schools run the IB Middle Years Programme into Year 9 and then move students onto IGCSE, so the pathway question matters more here than the commute.

sections.heading: What "IB home tutor in Emaar Beachfront" is really asking
paragraphs: The phrase means: find someone who can teach my child IB content at our address, this term, without adding another journey to an already long day. That is a logistics request dressed as a subject request, and it deserves a logistics answer. On Emaar Beachfront the logistics are unusual enough to change the recommendation. The peninsula is reached by one road link. There is no school inside it and no tuition centre inside it. Visitor access to tower basements needs a resident to clear it. An hour of teaching at a Beachfront address therefore costs the tutor roughly two and a quarter hours door to door, and that cost is priced in.

The second half of the question is subject supply, and here the island is no different from anywhere else in New Dubai. The pool of people who can teach IB Chemistry HL to a Diploma standard, in Dubai, who are free at the hour your child is actually able to concentrate, is small. Narrowing that pool further to people who will drive onto a peninsula is how families end up accepting a generalist for a specialist job. The generalist can keep a student afloat in SL content. They cannot reliably diagnose why a student is losing four marks a paper on equilibrium calculations.

IB Gram answers the question by separating the two halves. The logistics problem is solved by delivering lessons online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The supply problem is solved because removing travel removes the geographic filter: the tutor who teaches your child Chemistry HL is chosen for the subject and level, not for a postcode. We do not run home visits in the UAE, and the page would be dishonest if it implied otherwise. What follows is the evidence for why that trade is a good one, including the market rates that make the case better than any argument could.

paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure, because that is the number a family budgets against. A single weekly one-hour session with a qualified subject tutor, taken online, lands between roughly AED 600 and AED 1,200 a month on Bestimate's published Dubai estimates for mid-tier tutoring. A specialist exam-year arrangement runs AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and upwards on the same source. Budget provision, usually a university student, sits at AED 240 to AED 600. Package pricing seen in this market includes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those monthly bands resolve into hourly rates that vary mostly by format rather than by brilliance. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, both at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist cover. Bestimate's own range for IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists is AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED sits at the top of the visible market at AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits, with travel included, are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and at AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors.

The gap between the online and in-home columns is the travel premium, and it buys exactly one thing: a person in the room. It does not buy a better-qualified teacher, and on a peninsula with a single access road it does not reliably buy punctuality either. Three of the seven competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays tuition in. sections.heading: Emaar Beachfront, Dubai Harbour, Marina, JBR and the Palm, compared properly
paragraphs: Families moving into this part of New Dubai are told the neighbourhoods are interchangeable for schooling. They are not, but the differences are not the ones estate agents mention. What varies between these five addresses is the school commute, the earliest hour a child can realistically sit down and think, and how predictable the afternoon is. What does not vary is the depth of the local specialist pool, because all five draw on the same tutors and the same school cluster in Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Jumeirah.

Emaar Beachfront and Dubai Harbour are effectively one unit for this purpose. Both are new, both are tower-dense, both reach the mainland through the same corridor, and neither contains a school. Dubai Marina and JBR have the advantage of age: more residents, more established freelance tutors, more foot traffic. That advantage is spent on congestion, because the same density that attracts tutors also means a 17:00 arrival is a coin toss. Palm Jumeirah is the clearest case of distance mattering: a single trunk road, separate access for frontline villas and towers, and in-home tutors who commonly add a surcharge for it.

The conclusion holds across all five. If your child needs Economics HL and the three people in your area who teach IB Economics are already booked on Tuesdays, your postcode is irrelevant. Online delivery is what breaks that constraint, and it breaks it identically for a Beachfront tower, a Harbour apartment and a Palm villa. sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home visit, cost and hour by hour
paragraphs: Set the two formats side by side on the things a Beachfront parent can verify. An in-home visit means a tutor in the room, a fixed arrival time that depends on the causeway, a rate carrying travel, and a shortlist limited to people who live nearby and teach the subject. Online one-to-one means a tutor who may live anywhere, a rate with no travel component, a slot that can shift by half an hour at short notice, and a shortlist limited only by who teaches the subject at the level required.

The second format wins on the two measures that decide outcomes: who teaches, and whether the session happens at all. An in-home arrangement breaks when the tutor is delayed, when the family travels, when the child has a late school activity, or when the tutor moves apartment. An online arrangement survives all four. It also produces a written artefact by default, because the shared working page from each session stays available for the student to revise from, which an exercise book on the dining table does not.

Where the in-home format genuinely wins is with very young children who cannot yet hold attention on a screen, and with students who need physical apparatus handled for them. For PYP-age support, that is a real consideration and we say so. For MYP and Diploma work, which is diagram-heavy, past-paper led and almost entirely mediated through written working, the shared screen is not a compromise. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the honest framing is this: if a tutor in the room is non-negotiable for your child, the market rates above tell you what that costs locally.
