sections.heading: Why the specialist, not the distance, is the scarce thing
paragraphs: A Diploma student taking three Higher Levels needs three subject teachers. That sentence looks obvious and it is routinely ignored, because the in-home model pushes families towards one tutor who will take whatever is on offer. The result is a Chemistry HL student being taught by someone whose own strength is Biology, which works for the first term of DP1 and fails in the organic mechanisms and equilibrium content of DP2. The failure is not visible in session; it shows up as a plateau at 4 or 5 that nobody can explain.

Run the arithmetic on supply. Dubai had 227 private schools in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with IB programmes accounting for about 7% of private enrolment. That is a real but narrow IB population, spread across the whole emirate. The subset of adults who teach Chemistry HL to Diploma standard is correspondingly narrow. Now filter for people who will drive onto Emaar Beachfront at 17:30 on a Tuesday and you are choosing from a handful, if that. Filter instead only for subject and hour, and the shortlist is a shortlist again.

This is also why we publish a coverage position rather than implying unlimited availability. If no specialist is free for a niche subject at the hour you need, we say so and offer the nearest workable alternative: a different slot, a different HL subject taught first, or a short block with a specialist who has limited weekly availability. No competitor page researched in this market discloses a coverage limit at all. Several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas phone number instead, which is the same problem handled dishonestly.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: The Diploma puts a large share of every subject grade inside work the student produces at school under supervision. That makes coursework the single most sensitive area in IB tutoring, and the one where this market contains outright malpractice. One page researched for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. A student who submits one risks the loss of the entire Diploma, and the school is obliged to report it.

The boundary is clear and worth stating in plain terms. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria and what each band actually requires. A tutor may help narrow a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. A tutor may review a method, question whether the data supports the conclusion, and point out that a graph has no uncertainty bars. A tutor may read a draft the student has written and give feedback on structure, clarity and evidence. A tutor may teach the subject content the piece depends on.

A tutor may not write any part of the piece. A tutor may not edit it to completion, supply paragraphs for insertion, select and write up the data, or produce a worked version for the student to adapt. IB Gram tutors work on the first list and refuse the second, and they will tell a student directly when a request has crossed the line. Supervision of the EE and the IA belongs to the school; a tutor supports the student's own work alongside it and keeps the school's internal deadlines as the schedule.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Families moving into Emaar Beachfront from outside the UAE are often surprised that their child's IB timetable includes subjects the IB does not set. Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic language, Islamic Education and social and moral studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to teach. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond those subjects, but must follow the Ministry's general regulations. KHDA's own mandatory-subjects guidance set the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the implementation point, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The structural detail matters for tutoring. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies: combined classes for Arab and non-Arab students are prohibited, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. For non-Arab students, Islamic Education and the moral, social and cultural studies strand are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than 25 minutes.

Two practical consequences follow. First, a tutor supporting Arabic has to know which stream the child sits in, because the material is not interchangeable. Second, for these subjects the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, so support has to work with the school's own material rather than substituting a parallel syllabus. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach them, which is a credential question worth asking your school directly.

sections.heading: Getting started from a Beachfront address, including what can go wrong
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the year group, the subjects, the level, the school and the two or three hours in the week that are genuinely free. We come back with a specialist for each subject and a proposed slot in Gulf Standard Time. One free trial lesson per student follows, with no card required and no obligation after it. If the match is wrong, you say so and we change the tutor rather than asking you to persist with it.

What can go wrong is worth naming in advance. The commonest problem is a slot that looked free on paper and is not: a 16:30 start fails on this peninsula roughly as often as it succeeds, because the school bus is the variable. Move it to 17:00 or 17:30 and the same arrangement holds for a year. The second commonest problem is booking one tutor for three Higher Levels. It feels efficient and it caps the ceiling in at least two of the three subjects. The third is starting a DP2 subject in January and expecting to recover ground that was lost across DP1; it is possible, but the plan has to be past-paper led from the first session rather than a re-teach of the course.

And sometimes we cannot help immediately. A niche HL subject at a specific hour may have no specialist free that week. When that happens we say so and offer the realistic alternatives: a different slot with the right person, a different subject started first, or a short intensive block with someone whose weekly availability is limited. That is a less attractive answer than pretending otherwise, and it is the only one that does not waste a term.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who comes to our Emaar Beachfront apartment?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and we do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Independent home tutors in Dubai do visit Beachfront addresses, and market sources quote AED 180 to 500 an hour for in-home one-to-one with travel included. What you give up by choosing online is the person in the room. What you gain is a tutor chosen for Chemistry HL rather than for living near the Marina, and a session that is not at the mercy of one access road.

faqs.question: Would we find more IB tutors if we lived in Dubai Marina instead?
faqs.answer: Marginally more people willing to travel, and no more specialists. Marina and JBR have older, denser resident populations and a more established freelance market, so a Beachfront family moving there would see a longer list of names. The list would still thin to almost nothing for Chemistry HL, Maths AA HL or Economics HL at a workable hour, because the constraint is how few adults teach those courses in Dubai at all. That is why the recommendation on this page is the same for Beachfront, Harbour, Marina, JBR and the Palm.

faqs.question: What is a realistic session time for a child travelling to school in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Plan for 17:00 at the earliest on a weekday, and 17:30 if the bus is unreliable. Children from this peninsula leave before 07:00 and return after 15:30, and the hour immediately after that is for food and decompression rather than calculus. A session that starts too early gets cancelled or wasted, which is how families conclude tutoring does not work when the real problem was the clock. Weekend mornings are the most productive slots we schedule for this cluster, particularly for coursework blocks.

faqs.question: How much should I budget each month for one IB subject?
faqs.answer: For a qualified subject tutor online, once a week, Bestimate's Dubai estimates put the monthly spend at roughly AED 600 to 1,200. Specialist exam-year support runs AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Budget provision, usually a university student, sits at AED 240 to 600 a month. Package pricing in this market includes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices; our own number depends on subject count and session length and is fixed after the free trial.

faqs.question: My child takes three Higher Levels. Can one tutor cover all of them?
faqs.answer: One tutor can cover all three badly. Higher Level content in Chemistry, Physics and Maths AA diverges sharply from DP1 into DP2, and a teacher whose own depth is in one of them will keep a student afloat in the others without being able to diagnose where four marks a paper are going. Expect three names for three Higher Levels. It costs more per week and it is the difference between a plateau at 5 and movement at the top of the grade, which is the whole reason for hiring anyone.

faqs.question: Which schools do children from Emaar Beachfront and Dubai Harbour usually attend?
faqs.answer: Most travel to the Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim cluster, which includes long-established British provision to A Level and full IB continuum schools, or to Jumeirah and Al Safa. A smaller group goes inland to The Greens, The Meadows and Jumeirah Village. Neither peninsula has a school inside it. We name these schools to describe the area your child studies in; IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them, and no page should imply otherwise.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for diagram-heavy subjects like Physics?
faqs.answer: For MYP and Diploma work it works well, because the subject is already mediated through written working. A shared page lets the tutor watch a free-body diagram being drawn and intervene at the moment a force goes unlabelled, which is harder across a dining table than people assume. The page also persists, so revision happens from the student's own annotated examples. Where a screen is genuinely weaker is with very young children who cannot hold attention on it, and we say so rather than pretending the format suits everyone.

faqs.question: Is private tutoring in Dubai regulated, and should I check anything?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a MoHRE work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published. Ask any independent tutor about their permit; the official route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Chemistry Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the chemistry the investigation depends on, discuss whether the research question is answerable in the word limit, question the method, point out that a results table has no uncertainties, and give written feedback on a draft your child has written. A tutor cannot write it, process the data, or edit it to completion. One page in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright; submitting one puts the entire Diploma at risk and the school must report it. Our tutors will refuse that request explicitly.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit Cambridge IGCSE and IB exams?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered to India only, so do not plan around it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For the Diploma, UAE schools sit the May session. IB session and results dates in this project are not confirmed from the IB directly, so check every Diploma date with your school's coordinator or on ibo.org before acting on it. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones, and the zone timetable is the one that matters.

faqs.question: What do you do when nobody is available to teach the Higher Level we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you. A niche Higher Level subject at a specific hour sometimes has nobody available that week, and the honest options are a different slot with the right teacher, starting a different subject first, or a short intensive block with someone whose weekly availability is limited. No competitor page researched for this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE parents to an overseas phone number instead. Finding out in week one costs you nothing; finding out in week eight costs a term.

faqs.question: Do you teach the Arabic my child has to take alongside the IB?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one caveat that matters. Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires Arab and non-Arab streams to be taught separately because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Support therefore has to be matched to the stream your child actually sits in, and it has to work with the school's own material: for these mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited. Tell us which stream applies and we will match accordingly.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start if the mock results have already come back?
faqs.answer: Usually not, but the plan has to change shape. After mocks the work becomes diagnostic rather than instructional: the tutor reads the script, identifies which marks were lost to content gaps and which to technique, and sequences the remaining weeks backwards from the exam window. Two sessions a week across eight to ten weeks is the pattern that moves a grade at this stage. What does not work is re-teaching the course from the start. Bring the actual mock paper to the trial lesson rather than the reported grade.

faqs.question: Do school fees in Dubai tell me anything about what tutoring should cost?
faqs.answer: They give you context rather than a formula. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Against a frozen fee, a weekly specialist session at AED 200 to 450 an hour is a visible addition to the household education budget, and worth planning by term rather than by month. Dubai also added seven new private schools for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB.

faqs.question: How quickly can lessons start from a Beachfront address?
faqs.answer: For a widely taught subject at SL, usually within a few days of the first conversation, because the only variable is matching a free hour. For a Higher Level specialist at a popular evening slot it can take longer, and for a niche subject it occasionally cannot be done that week at all. We would rather give you a date we can hold than a promise we cannot. The free trial lesson is the first fixed point; the weekly slot is agreed immediately after it.

intro.heading: Nobody in Emaar South walks to school, and that changes everything about tutoring
paragraphs: Emaar South is a golf-course community inside Dubai South, built out as villas and townhouses across Golf Links, Urbana, Expo Golf Villas, Parkside and Greenview. It has parks, a clubhouse and a steadily growing resident population. What it does not have is a school inside it. Every child here travels out to one, usually to Dubai Investments Park, Al Furjan, Jebel Ali or further east along the Dubailand corridor, and that journey is the single most important fact in any tutoring plan written for this community.

The arithmetic is simple and it is routinely ignored. A school day ending at 15:00 plus a twenty-five to forty-five minute journey, plus the time it takes a teenager to get through the door, change and eat something, puts the earliest workable session at around 16:45 for most Emaar South households. A bus route with multiple stops puts it later. Two children at two different schools, which is common here, puts it later still and introduces a second arrival time to plan around.

That is why a plan copied from a family in Dubai Investments Park, who are home by 15:45 because the school is minutes away, does not survive contact with an Emaar South week. The same plan books a 16:00 session, the child arrives at 16:35, the session is cut short twice, and by half term attendance has slipped. The failure looks like motivation and is actually scheduling, which is a much easier thing to fix if it is named at the start.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and no tutor is dispatched to an Emaar South address. Students here are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time. For a community this far south that is also an operational advantage rather than a compromise: a visiting tutor would be absorbing the same journey the child just made, in the same traffic, and pricing it into the hour.

The rest of this page works from the journey outwards. Which schools Emaar South households actually use and what each journey costs in time. When a session fits and why the second-earliest slot beats the earliest. How a 48-hour homework cycle is built around a long school day. What the weekend genuinely buys for internal assessment work. What the in-home travel premium is, in published AED, and what it is paying for. And the IB-specific point underneath all of it: the Diploma's internal assessments need long uninterrupted stretches that a weekday evening in this community cannot supply.

One factual note so expectations are set correctly. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes annual school inspection ratings, which are worth reading before any admissions conversation about a school your child will travel to daily. KHDA does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership and operates no UAE centre. Individual tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-emaar-south.programmesIntro: Emaar South's age profile is younger than the Dubai average because the community is newer, so Middle Years demand here runs ahead of Diploma demand. All four stages below appear in requests from this community.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and organised around units of inquiry, with continuous descriptive assessment rather than grades. The three things that transfer into later success are number fluency, reading stamina and the ability to structure a written explanation. Sessions at this age should be short and frequent, which in this community means thirty to forty minutes rather than an hour.
programmes.countryNote: For an Emaar South primary child the journey is the binding constraint on tutoring, more than at any other stage. A seven year old off a forty-minute bus is not going to produce useful work at 16:45, which is why primary sessions here are better placed at 17:30 after a proper break, or moved to a weekend morning entirely.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, labelled A to D, each marked 0 to 8 and converted to a 1-7 grade. The criteria differ by subject group, so criterion B in Sciences asks something different from criterion B in Individuals and Societies. Students strong on content and weak on process sit in the middle bands across every subject at once.
programmes.countryNote: This is the heaviest demand in Emaar South because of the community's age profile. Sixty-minute sessions in the 16:45 to 18:00 band are the pattern that works here, and those slots fill first. The Personal Project in the final year needs longer stretches and almost always moves to a weekend morning in this community.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment worth 20% to 25%, and the school coordinator's internal deadlines for those land far earlier than the May papers that families plan around.
programmes.countryNote: An Emaar South Diploma student is managing a long daily journey alongside a workload designed on the assumption of shorter ones. The practical response is fewer, better-placed sessions rather than more: one well-timed weekday evening session plus a weekend morning beats three rushed weekday slots, and it survives a term.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Tutoring demand falls on the Diploma courses within it and on the reflective project's argument structure. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools.
programmes.countryNote: Rare in this part of Dubai, which means an Emaar South family whose child is on it has nobody nearby to compare notes with about whether a reflective project is on track. A specialist who has supervised the component elsewhere resolves that, and online delivery is the only practical route to one from this community.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-emaar-south.subjectsIntro: The IB subjects Emaar South families request, with a note on what each demands of a student who has already spent an hour and a half on a bus that day.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is non-calculator, which makes hand algebra the deciding skill and the one that benefits most from short daily practice rather than one long weekly session. Twenty minutes a day of manipulation beats ninety minutes on a Tuesday, and it fits a long school day better.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, with statistics, modelling and finance carrying the weight. The marks are lost on interpretation rather than calculation, which means written justification practice. That is work a tired student can still do well, which makes it a reasonable choice for a later evening slot.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 gives no method credit, so a prefix slip costs the whole question. Uncertainty and graph technique carry marks independently of the physics, and both are procedural enough to be practised late in an evening when conceptual work would not land.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Multi-step calculations punish early rounding, and organic mechanisms require every arrow to start in the right place. Mechanism drill is repetitive rather than demanding, which makes it one of the few chemistry tasks that holds up in a 19:30 session after a long day.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: High recall volume, so the gains come from structured note compression and command-term discipline rather than rereading. Note-building is good weekend work; command-term practice is short enough to fit a weekday slot even after a long journey.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked, and a correctly labelled diagram earns credit that prose cannot. The three 800-word commentaries that make up the internal assessment need uninterrupted stretches, which in this community means weekend mornings or a school break.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Higher Level sits a pre-released case study for Paper 2, which rewards months of structured preparation rather than late revision. Working through the case in short weekly instalments suits an Emaar South timetable better than attempting it in blocks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 prints a guided question above the passage and the markbands reward answering it directly. Unseen analysis practice needs a clear head, so it belongs in the earlier part of the week rather than at the end of a long Thursday.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on one of six prescribed titles plus an exhibition of three objects with commentaries. Together with the Extended Essay it carries up to three bonus points. The essay needs sustained thinking time, which is weekend work by default in this community.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent essay with critical thinking worth twelve of the available marks. It cannot be written in weekday fragments after a long journey. Families here who plan it into the winter break and weekend mornings finish it; families who plan it into term evenings generally do not.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Taken by many non-Arab students because Arabic is mandatory in Dubai private schools under KHDA rules. The individual oral is the most recoverable component and rewards drilled structures, which is precisely the kind of work that survives a tired evening slot.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The examination uses the IB's own pseudocode notation rather than a real language, and trace tables are reliable marks that almost nobody drills. Both are procedural, both suit short sessions, and the specialist pool for Higher Level is thin enough that early booking matters.

sections.heading: The Emaar South school run, costed in minutes
paragraphs: Start with the journeys, because every scheduling decision follows from them. Emaar South has no school inside the community, which means four destinations in practice: the Dubai Investments Park cluster to the north-east, Al Furjan and Jebel Ali to the north and west, and the Dubailand corridor to the east. Each has a different time cost and the difference between the shortest and the longest is around twenty minutes each way, which is forty minutes a day and most of a session a week.

The journeys are longer in the afternoon than in the morning. Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Emirates Road both carry end-of-working-day traffic through the window in which school buses are running, and the Jebel Ali industrial area adds its own congestion. A run that takes twenty-five minutes at 07:15 can take thirty-five at 15:15, which is exactly the variability that makes a fixed 16:00 session unworkable.

School buses are slower than private cars, sometimes considerably, because a route with six or seven stops spends time at each one. A child who is the last drop on a route from Dubailand can be home half an hour after a classmate who was first. That is worth establishing precisely rather than estimating, because it is the number that determines which slot to book and it is knowable: the school can supply the route timing.

The table sets out the journeys as they actually run. Use it to find your own household's arrival time rather than reading it as an average, because the spread within Emaar South is wide enough that two neighbours can need slots forty-five minutes apart. That precision is the entire point of this section, and it is the thing most tutoring arrangements never ask about before booking a time.

sections.heading: Why the second-earliest slot beats the earliest
paragraphs: Families book the earliest available slot because it feels like getting ahead of the evening, and in a community with a long school run it is usually the wrong choice. A student walking through the door at 16:30 and sitting down at 16:35 brings nothing to the session. They are hot, hungry and still mentally on the bus, and the first twenty minutes go on settling rather than on work. The session nominally lasts ninety minutes and delivers about sixty-five.

Pushed back an hour, the same session delivers close to its full length. The student has changed, eaten and had some decompression time, and arrives at the screen able to engage with a marked script rather than endure it. The change costs nothing, it does not extend the evening materially, and in this community it is the single highest-return scheduling decision available.

There is a second reason, which is attendance over a term. A session that is consistently uncomfortable gets missed. Not refused outright, just moved, then moved again, then quietly dropped around half term, and the explanation offered is usually that the child is not motivated. In Emaar South that pattern is often pure logistics, and it resolves when the slot moves an hour later rather than when anybody has a conversation about effort.

The practical rule we use with families here is that the session starts at least forty-five minutes after the front door opens, and never inside the first thirty. For a household with two children arriving at different times, that means two slots rather than one shared one, which is straightforward online and impossible with a visiting tutor who has one evening to spend. The last weekday start available is 21:30 Gulf Standard Time, which leaves plenty of room to place a session properly rather than early.

sections.heading: Building a 48-hour homework cycle round a long day
paragraphs: Tutoring only works when something happens between sessions, and that is where a long school run does the most damage. A student who loses ninety minutes a day to travel has ninety minutes a day less for independent practice than a classmate living next to the school. Across a week that is seven and a half hours, which is more than the difference any amount of extra tutoring could make up.

The response is not to demand more. It is to make the set work smaller, more frequent and self-marking. Twenty minutes on four or five days, with the student marking their own work against the official scheme before sending it, produces more usable practice than a single ninety-minute homework task that gets started at 21:00 on a Sunday. It also produces better diagnosis, because five short attempts reveal a pattern that one long attempt hides.

The forty-eight hour part matters. Work set at the end of a session and attempted within two days, while the session is still fresh, lands. Work attempted five days later has to be reconstructed first, and the reconstruction eats the practice time. For an Emaar South family that usually means setting work on a Tuesday evening session for Wednesday and Thursday, reviewed at the weekend morning slot, rather than setting it for the following Tuesday.

The bus itself is a resource worth naming, carefully. A forty-minute journey is not a place to attempt new mathematics, but it is a reasonable place to read a set of notes, work through flashcards or listen to a recorded explanation. Several families here use it that way deliberately. It is not a substitute for desk work and it is a genuine recovery of time that would otherwise be lost entirely, which in this community is worth having.

sections.heading: What the weekend actually buys in Emaar South
paragraphs: The Diploma contains work that cannot be done in weekday fragments. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words. A mathematics exploration is twelve to twenty pages. An Economics internal assessment is three 800-word commentaries. A full timed paper takes two hours plus review. None of these fits into an hour at 18:30 after a long journey, and attempting them that way produces starts without finishes.

Weekend mornings are where that work belongs, and in this community they are the most valuable hours in the week because the journey disappears. A two-hour slot on a Saturday morning, with the student rested, does work that four weekday evenings would not. The students who finish internal assessments comfortably in Emaar South are almost always the ones who have a standing weekend slot rather than more weekday ones.

The second advantage is reviewing within forty-eight hours. A full timed paper sat on Saturday morning and reviewed on Sunday is a different exercise from one sat on Saturday and reviewed the following Thursday, because the student still remembers what they were thinking when they wrote each answer. That memory is most of the diagnostic value, and it decays faster than anybody expects.

Breaks extend the same logic. The winter and spring breaks remove both the school workload and the journey at once, which in Emaar South is a larger gain than it is anywhere closer to a school cluster. Four to six sessions on consecutive days in a break does work that a term cannot accommodate, and families here who use them consistently arrive at the spring of Year 13 ahead rather than behind. sections.heading: Two children, two schools, one evening
paragraphs: Emaar South households frequently have children at two different schools, because the community's provision sits outside it and families choose differently for a primary child and a secondary one. That produces two arrival times, sometimes an hour apart, and it is the scheduling problem that defeats in-home arrangements entirely.

A visiting tutor can be in one house at one time. If the younger child arrives at 16:15 and the older at 17:05, a single visit serves one of them properly and the other badly. Two visits on different evenings means two travel premiums and two evenings committed. In practice families in this position either accept that one child gets the inconvenient slot or stop after a term, and the second outcome is more common.

Online, two consecutive one-to-one sessions in one evening is ordinary. The younger child takes 17:00 to 17:45, the older takes 18:00 to 19:30, each with their own tutor if the subjects require it, each with their own set work and written note. Nothing is shared and nothing is compromised, and the household commits one evening rather than two. For a family in this community that is the clearest practical difference between the two delivery models.

There is a related case worth naming: one child needing two subjects. A Diploma student weak in both Chemistry and Mathematics does not need two evenings; they need two slots that can sit anywhere in the week, including one at the weekend. The flexibility to place them independently of a tutor's driving route is what makes a two-subject plan sustainable in a community this far from the school belt.

sections.heading: The travel premium, in published AED
paragraphs: A visiting tutor coming to Emaar South is making the same journey the child made, in the same traffic, and that time is paid for whether or not it appears on the invoice as a separate line. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200.

The monthly packages published in this market make the difference starker than the hourly rates do: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four in-home sessions of two hours. That is four visits against eight sessions, at roughly double the monthly cost, and the gap is largely the driving rather than the teaching. For a community at the southern end of the emirate the premium is at the upper end of those bands, because the journey is longer.

There is a second cost that never appears in a rate card: scheduling. A tutor committing ninety minutes of travel around a sixty-minute lesson in Emaar South can fit one session that evening. That constrains which slot you are offered, makes a sibling pair difficult and a two-subject plan impractical, and means a cancellation is harder to rearrange because the tutor's whole evening was allocated to your address.

None of that makes in-home provision wrong. It buys physical presence, which matters for a young child who will not settle at a screen, and it lets a parent observe from the next room. Those are real advantages and they are worth paying for at primary age. For a Diploma student working through a marked script against a published markband, the material is two documents that read better shared on a monitor, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case. sections.heading: Ramadan and the breaks from an Emaar South address
paragraphs: During Ramadan the school day shortens, which shortens the journey window as well and changes the shape of the evening. Afternoon concentration drops and the usable window moves after iftar. For a community with a long commute this is, unusually, an improvement in one respect: the child is home earlier, so there is more of the afternoon available even though less of it is useful.

The practical adjustments are to move sessions later, shorten them from ninety minutes to sixty, and switch from new content to timed question practice or procedural drill, which costs less concentration per mark gained. Mechanism work in chemistry, non-calculator algebra and language structures all hold up well in a late session. Unseen textual analysis and new conceptual physics generally do not.

The breaks are where this community gains most relative to families living next to a school cluster. A fortnight of winter break removes both the workload and the journey, which in Emaar South returns around fifteen hours a week of a teenager's time. Four to six sessions placed on consecutive days, with full timed papers marked and reviewed inside forty-eight hours, does work that no arrangement of term evenings can match.

The planning action that follows is to count the real working weeks in January rather than April. Subtract the final fortnight before the May papers, which should be pacing only. Mark the weeks that fall in a break and the weeks that fall in Ramadan. What remains is the genuine term-time window, and in a long-commute household it is smaller than the raw count suggests, because each of those weeks holds fewer usable hours than it would closer to town.

sections.heading: Specialist matching, and why it matters more this far south
paragraphs: Everything above is logistics. The reason logistics matter here is that the alternative, hiring whoever will drive to Emaar South, applies a filter that has nothing to do with teaching. Start with everyone who can teach a given Diploma subject at a given level. Remove everyone unwilling to make a forty-minute drive to a community at the southern edge of the emirate for one evening session. Remove everyone whose free slot does not match your child's unusually late arrival. What remains is a very short list.

For a Standard Level subject that list may still contain somebody suitable. For Chemistry or Physics at Higher Level, for Computer Science, for Arabic B or Theory of Knowledge, it generally does not, and a family ends up with a general science or general maths tutor because that is who was available. The cost is not just the fee; it is a term during which the student's actual problem is never diagnosed.

Online delivery removes the travel filter and nothing else. It does not create specialists, and this page will not imply that availability is unlimited. Diploma Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English A usually match within a few days. Computer Science Higher Level, Arabic B and Theory of Knowledge are thinner and can take a week or more. Where no specialist is free we say so and give a date rather than making a substitution.

The honest summary for an Emaar South family is that the community's distance from the school belt costs you nothing in tutor quality once lessons are delivered over video, and costs you a good deal if they are not. What the distance does still cost is time, which is why the whole of this page is about placing sessions properly rather than about claiming the distance does not matter. It does matter. It just does not have to determine who teaches your child.

process.title: Tell us the arrival time, not the preferred time
process.description: What time does your child actually walk through the door, and is that by bus or by car? For an Emaar South household those two answers set the slot more reliably than any preference does. If there are two children at two schools, we need both arrival times, because the plan will need two slots.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Chemistry Higher Level with a weak Paper 2 is a different brief from Chemistry Higher Level with no investigation started. Naming the component means the first session diagnoses rather than introduces, which matters more in a household where every session has to count.

process.title: Send a recent marked script
process.description: A marked mock or a returned internal assessment draft tells a specialist in five minutes what a conversation approximates in an hour. Where marks were lost is visible on the page. Without a script, the first session produces one from a short timed section.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched specialist
process.description: One full session at no charge and no card, taught by the person who would take the term. It returns a written diagnosis and a proposed weekly shape, including which slot is realistic given the journey. If the match is wrong we rematch rather than asking you to persist.

process.title: Place one weekday slot and one weekend morning
process.description: The weekday session at least forty-five minutes after the door opens, for script review and technique. The weekend morning for timed papers, internal assessment work and anything needing uninterrupted hours. Two well-placed sessions outlast three badly placed ones in this community.

process.title: Book the breaks before the term starts
process.description: The winter and spring breaks remove the workload and the journey at once, which returns more usable hours to an Emaar South student than to almost anybody else in Dubai. Four to six consecutive-day sessions in each is the single best-value arrangement available from this community.

whyPoints.title: Slots set from your household's real arrival time
whyPoints.description: Emaar South has no school inside it, so arrival times here range across more than an hour depending on destination and whether a bus or a car is used. Booking from a standard slot list produces sessions that start before the student is home. We ask for the actual time and build from it.

whyPoints.title: The second-earliest slot, deliberately
whyPoints.description: A session starting within thirty minutes of a long journey loses its first twenty to settling, and an uncomfortable slot gets quietly dropped around half term. Moving it an hour later costs nothing and recovers most of the session, which in this community is the highest-return scheduling decision available.

whyPoints.title: Two children in one evening, each one-to-one
whyPoints.description: Households here commonly have children at two schools with arrival times an hour apart. Two consecutive one-to-one sessions in one evening is ordinary online and impossible for a visiting tutor. Each child keeps their own tutor, their own set work and their own written note.

whyPoints.title: Homework built for a student who loses time to travel
whyPoints.description: Twenty minutes on four days, self-marked against the official scheme, within forty-eight hours of the session, outperforms a single long task attempted late on a Sunday. It also diagnoses better, because five short attempts reveal a pattern that one long attempt conceals.

whyPoints.title: The travel premium named in published figures
whyPoints.description: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500 once travel is priced in, against AED 150-300 online for a qualified tutor. Published monthly packages are AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home ones. Those are market figures, not ours.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims and no UAE centre
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE or IB approval, accreditation or partnership and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Regulators appear on this page because reading a KHDA inspection rating is genuinely useful before choosing a school your child will travel to daily.

faqs.question: Are there schools inside Emaar South?
faqs.answer: Not inside the community itself, which is the fact that shapes every tutoring decision here. Families travel out, most commonly to the Dubai Investments Park cluster, to Al Furjan or Jebel Ali, or east along the Dubailand corridor. Journeys run twenty-five to forty-five minutes each way by car and longer by school bus, which is why the earliest workable weekday session for most households here is around 16:45 rather than the 16:00 that suits a family living next to the school cluster.

faqs.question: What time should an Emaar South session actually start?
faqs.answer: At least forty-five minutes after your child walks through the door, and never within the first thirty. A student who sits down five minutes after a forty-minute journey spends the first twenty settling, so a ninety-minute session delivers about sixty-five. Pushed back an hour the same session delivers almost its full length. For most households here that means somewhere between 17:00 and 18:00, and weekday sessions can be placed as late as 21:30 Gulf Standard Time if that works better.

faqs.question: Does the school bus make a real difference to the plan?
faqs.answer: A substantial one. A route with six or seven stops spends time at each, so a child who is the last drop can be home half an hour after a classmate who was first. That is the difference between a 17:00 slot working and not working. It is also knowable rather than guessable: the school can supply the route timing. Establishing it precisely before booking a slot is one of the few pieces of administration that reliably improves a tutoring arrangement in this community.

faqs.question: Can both my children have sessions on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Emaar South that is usually the right arrangement. Households here often have children at two different schools with arrival times an hour apart, so one slot cannot serve both. Online, two consecutive one-to-one sessions in one evening is ordinary: the younger child takes the earlier slot, the older takes the later one, each with their own tutor where the subjects require it, their own set work and their own written note. A visiting tutor can only be in one place at one time.

faqs.question: How should homework work for a child with a long commute?
faqs.answer: Smaller, more often, and self-marked. A student losing ninety minutes a day to travel has seven and a half hours less practice time a week than a classmate living by the school. Twenty minutes on four or five days, marked by the student against the official scheme before sending, produces more usable work than one ninety-minute task started late on a Sunday. It also diagnoses better, because five short attempts show a pattern that one long attempt hides.

faqs.question: Is the school bus a useful place to study?
faqs.answer: For some things. A forty-minute journey is not a place to attempt new mathematics or write under time, but it is a reasonable place to read a set of notes, work through flashcards or listen to a recorded explanation. Several families in this community use it deliberately that way. It is not a substitute for desk work, and treating it as one leads to disappointment, but it recovers time that would otherwise be lost entirely, which in Emaar South is worth having.

faqs.question: Why does internal assessment work have to go at the weekend?
faqs.answer: Because it needs uninterrupted hours and a weekday evening in this community cannot supply them. An Extended Essay is 4,000 words, a mathematics exploration is twelve to twenty pages, an Economics internal assessment is three 800-word commentaries. None fits into an hour at 18:30 after a long journey, and attempting them that way produces starts without finishes. Students in Emaar South who finish their internal assessments comfortably almost always have a standing weekend morning slot rather than extra weekday ones.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an Emaar South villa?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Students here are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time. It is worth saying that a visiting tutor would be absorbing the same journey your child just made, in the same traffic, and pricing it into the hour: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500 once travel is included. Independent in-home tutors do operate in Dubai if presence is your priority.

faqs.question: How much more does in-home tuition cost from this far south?
faqs.answer: The published bands put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced into the hour, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. For a community at the southern edge of the emirate the premium sits at the upper end, because the journey is longer. Published monthly packages make it clearest: AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home sessions. These are market figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do Emaar South families usually choose?
faqs.answer: Most travel to the Dubai Investments Park and Green Community cluster, where IB continuum provision sits alongside British and SABIS schools within a few minutes of each other, or east to the Dubailand corridor for a particular IB continuum school. Al Furjan and Jebel Ali supply the British-curriculum alternatives that run IGCSE at sixteen. KHDA publishes annual inspection ratings for all of them, which is the document worth reading before committing a child to a daily journey. IB Gram has no affiliation with any school named here.

faqs.question: Why do sessions get dropped around half term in this community?
faqs.answer: Usually because the slot was placed too early rather than because the student lost interest. A session that is consistently uncomfortable gets moved, then moved again, then quietly abandoned, and the explanation offered is motivation. In a household with a forty-minute school run the cause is often logistics, and it resolves when the slot moves an hour later rather than when anyone has a conversation about effort. That is worth checking before concluding that tutoring is not working.

faqs.question: What do the school breaks give an Emaar South student specifically?
faqs.answer: Both the workload and the journey disappear at the same time, which returns around fifteen hours a week of a teenager's time in this community, more than it would for a family living beside a school cluster. Four to six sessions placed on consecutive days in a break, with full timed papers marked and reviewed inside forty-eight hours while the student still remembers their reasoning, does work that no arrangement of term evenings can match. Booking those sessions before the term starts is the single best-value decision available here.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the evening in Emaar South?
faqs.answer: The school day shortens, which shortens the journey window too, so the child is home earlier even though less of the afternoon is useful. Sessions move after iftar and shorten from ninety minutes to sixty, with content teaching replaced by timed practice or procedural drill. Mechanism work in chemistry, non-calculator algebra and drilled language structures all hold up in a late session. Unseen textual analysis and new conceptual physics generally do not, so those move to the weekend or wait.

faqs.question: Can one child have two subjects without two evenings committed?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where the flexibility matters most. Because nobody is driving, two slots can sit anywhere in the week, including one on a weekend morning. A Diploma student weak in both Chemistry and Mathematics can take one subject on a Tuesday evening and the other on a Saturday morning, with different specialists if the subjects need them. With a visiting tutor both slots would have to fit a driving route, which in a community this far south usually means two separate evenings and two travel premiums.

faqs.question: Does living in Emaar South limit which IB tutors are available?
faqs.answer: Only if the tutor has to travel. Hiring whoever will drive to a community at the southern edge of the emirate applies a filter that has nothing to do with teaching: it selects for willingness to make a forty-minute journey. For a Standard Level subject the surviving pool may still contain somebody suitable. For Chemistry or Physics at Higher Level, Computer Science or Arabic B it usually does not. Online delivery removes that filter, though it does not create specialists, and thin subjects can still take a week or more to match.

faqs.question: What should I send in a first message about tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four things, and the first will not be obvious. Your child's actual arrival time and whether that is by bus or car, because in Emaar South that sets the slot. The subject and level. The component that is weak, since Chemistry Higher Level with a weak Paper 2 is a different brief from the same course with no investigation started. And a recent marked script if one exists. With those four the first session diagnoses instead of introducing, which matters in a household where every session has to count.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-emaar-south.closingHeading: Tell us when the bus gets in, and we will build round it
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-emaar-south.closingBody: Finding an IB home tutor in Emaar South is less about who is nearby than about when your child is actually available. Send the arrival time and whether it is by bus or car, the subject, the level, the weak component and a recent marked script. The free trial lesson returns a written diagnosis and a weekly shape that fits your journey rather than a standard slot list. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, as late as 21:30 if that works better. Home visits are an India-only service and are not offered in the UAE.

intro.heading: Work out the date first, because it decides what help can honestly do
paragraphs: A parent in Emirates Hills who starts looking for an IB tutor is rarely starting from zero. Something has happened: a mock paper has come back lower than expected, a subject teacher has used the word concern at a parents' evening, or an internal assessment deadline has arrived and nothing is written. The instinct is to ask how good the tutor is. The more useful first question is how many weeks are left, because the answer changes what any tutor can reasonably promise.

Eight weeks is the unit worth thinking in. In eight weeks of weekly one-to-one work, one subject can move: a named topic can be rebuilt, a paper technique can be trained, a set of command terms can be learned, an internal assessment can be planned and drafted. What eight weeks cannot do is lift six subjects at once, close two years of accumulated gaps, or replace content the student has never been taught. A tutor who agrees to the first and declines the second two is giving you accurate information, not being unambitious.

The IB calendar makes this harder to plan than the British one, for a reason worth stating plainly. The IB's examination and results dates are published by the IB, and the organisation's website blocks automated checking, so nothing on this page states an IB session or results date as fact. Dates for your child's session must come from your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org directly, and you should take them from one of those two sources before building a plan. Cambridge and Pearson, by contrast, publish their dates openly, and this page uses those as the worked example of how far ahead a deadline sits.

The other thing a calendar-led plan reveals is how many of the dates that matter are set by your child's school rather than by the IB. Internal deadlines for the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and each subject's internal assessment are the school's. Mock windows are the school's. Predicted grades, which drive university offers, are the school's. Study leave is the school's. For an Emirates Hills family those are the dates to write on a wall calendar, because they arrive earlier than the examination session and they bite harder.

A word on the phrase in the heading of this page. An IB home tutor is what parents search for and it is the right phrase to use, so it is used here. What IB Gram actually provides is one-to-one tuition delivered online over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. The published dirham figures for visiting tutors appear further down because the comparison is genuinely useful when you are working to a deadline, and against a deadline the online format wins on the two things that matter most: who is available, and whether a session can be moved.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-emirates-hills.programmesIntro: Which calendar you are on depends on where your child sits in the continuum. The notes below describe what the next eight weeks should be achieving at each stage, as Emirates Hills families meet them, with the dates that are verifiable kept separate from the ones that are not.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, with the final year adding the Personal Project. Assessment is internal and continuous rather than built around a single examination window, so the calendar is a sequence of school-set task deadlines rather than one terminal date.
programmes.countryNote: For an Emirates Hills family the Middle Years calendar question is almost always the Personal Project, which arrives in MYP 5 and is the item most often started late. The eight weeks that matter are the first eight, when the goal is set and the process journal begins. Work done then prevents the rescue job families contact us about in the final fortnight.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Standard or Higher Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component alongside written papers, and the internal components have school-set deadlines that fall well before the examination session.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma families here run two calendars at once. The school's internal deadline calendar, which is specific to your school and must be asked for, and the examination session itself, whose dates come from the Diploma coordinator or ibo.org. The internal calendar is the one that produces the crisis, because three subjects can set deadlines in the same fortnight.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken with a career-related study, a reflective project and a core of personal and professional skills. The Diploma courses within it carry the same assessment and the same session timing as a full Diploma candidate's.
programmes.countryNote: The calendar risk here is the reflective project, which sits outside the subject deadlines and therefore outside the reminders that come with them. Few Dubai schools run this route; if your child is on it, ask for the reflective project timeline in writing at the start of the year rather than waiting for it to be announced.

programmes.name: IGCSE, where the dates are published
programmes.description: Cambridge runs IGCSE and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a candidate sitting in Dubai is always working towards June or November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year.
programmes.countryNote: Use the Pearson International GCSE calendar as the model for how far ahead a deadline sits, because it is published and checkable for this region. Count the November 2026 series backwards: the final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results reached students in the January that followed, the way November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. Entries for a series that finishes in November are settled long before the autumn term is underway, which is why a family asking about tutoring in September is already late for some decisions and perfectly on time for others. The Cambridge equivalent works the same way on a June axis: entries close in the spring, months ahead of the first paper, and the exact day is printed on the centre's statement of entry rather than guessed at here. An entry deadline sitting months before the paper is normal, not unusual.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-emirates-hills.subjectsIntro: The list below is organised by what the next eight weeks can realistically do in each subject area, because the answer is different in a mathematics course than in a language or a humanity. Use it to decide where one block of tutoring belongs rather than spreading it across six subjects.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Eight weeks can train a non-calculator paper technique or rebuild one named topic such as integration or trigonometric identities. It cannot cover two years of algebra. The highest-value eight-week block here is timed Paper 1 sections followed by mark-scheme review, because the loss is usually technique rather than knowledge.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Eight weeks can secure the statistics and modelling topics that carry the heaviest marks, and can get the exploration from a topic to a draft. Students here lose marks on interpretation rather than calculation: a correct number with no sentence saying what it means for the context scores poorly.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Eight weeks fits one theme rebuilt properly plus a data-paper block, or an internal assessment taken from data to finished analysis. It does not fit the whole course. Fields is the theme most often named in requests from this part of Dubai, and it responds well to a short, concentrated block.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Eight weeks is enough for organic mechanisms, which need per-attempt correction rather than reading, or for energetics and equilibrium argument. The internal assessment needs its own block. Mechanism work in an eight-week window before a mock is one of the clearest returns available in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Eight weeks works well here because the losses are usually command terms and specificity rather than content: answers that describe when the question says explain, or that name a process without naming the structure. Training answer shape against mark schemes moves marks faster than rereading notes.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Eight weeks can train diagram discipline and evaluation, which is where most of the marks sit. Students lose marks by drawing a correct diagram and not referring to it in the prose, and by writing evaluation that lists both sides without reaching a judgement. Both are quick to fix with a specialist.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Eight weeks is enough to prepare the individual oral properly or to train unseen commentary under time. It is not enough to read the texts for the first time. The reliable loss is analysis replaced by description: saying that a technique appears rather than showing how it creates an effect.

subjects.name: Languages: Arabic, French, Spanish, Hindi
subjects.description: Eight weeks shifts speaking confidence and the structure of written tasks more than it shifts vocabulary range. The highest-value work is the individual oral and the written task format, both of which have a shape that can be taught. Vocabulary needs longer and is mostly the student's own work.

subjects.name: The internal assessments
subjects.description: Each subject has one, each carries a meaningful share of the grade, and each has a deadline set by your school rather than by the IB. Eight weeks is a comfortable window for planning, data or research, and drafting with feedback. Four weeks is a rescue. One week is not a tutoring problem.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay with supervision from a school supervisor. Eight weeks can take a student from a confirmed research question to a complete first draft if the reading is underway. It cannot produce the research. Tutoring here is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay and the exhibition both have school-set deadlines and both are assessed against published criteria. Eight weeks is sufficient for either with room to spare, and the common failure is the opposite of lateness: students write confidently and never address the prescribed title directly, which is where the marks go.

sections.heading: What a given number of weeks can honestly achieve
paragraphs: The most useful conversation a parent can have before hiring anyone is about arithmetic rather than ambition. Count the weeks between today and the date that matters, subtract the weeks the family is travelling, subtract the fortnight either side of any other deadline in the same subject, and work with what is left. The number that survives is small, and it is the number a plan should be built on.

With twelve or more weeks, there is room to diagnose, rebuild a topic, train a paper technique and then consolidate. With eight, one of those has to be dropped and the diagnosis has to be fast, which is why marked work sent before the first session matters so much. With four weeks, the only honest objective is technique: command terms, timing, answer shape and the mechanics of presenting work, because content built in four weeks does not survive examination pressure. With two weeks, a tutor's job is to stop the student doing the wrong thing.

Where families go wrong is not in starting late. It is in asking for too much from the weeks they have. A request to lift six subjects in eight weeks produces thin work across all of them, and the grade moves in none. A request to lift one subject by one grade band in eight weeks is achievable often enough to be worth doing, and the subject to pick is the one closest to a boundary rather than the one furthest behind. That is counter-intuitive and it is almost always correct.

The table sets the realistic objective against the weeks available. Use it to decide what to ask for rather than as a promise, and remember that nothing here is a guarantee about a grade; no tutor can offer one and any provider doing so should be treated with real scepticism. What a good tutor can commit to is the plan, the diagnosis and the feedback cycle, which is the part that is actually within anyone's control.

sections.heading: Who sets which date, and where to check each one
paragraphs: An IB Diploma family is managing at least five separate calendars, and only one of them belongs to the IB. Mixing them up is the most common planning error we see, because it leads parents to assume a date is fixed when it is their school's choice, or to assume it is flexible when it is not.

Be direct about the IB dates. The IB publishes its examination and results dates, but ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. That means this page does not state one. Get your child's session dates from the school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org directly, write them down with the date you checked, and recheck in the examination year. Any page that hands you an IB date without naming where it came from is handing you something it has not verified.

Cambridge and Pearson do publish checkable dates, and they are worth using as the model for how early a deadline sits. Cambridge runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; the February and March series belongs to India and a Dubai candidate cannot sit it. Take Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE series and count backwards from the end: the final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, results followed in January, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson's June route runs on the same logic one term earlier, with June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026. For Cambridge June, entries close in the spring, well ahead of the first paper, and the precise date comes from the school's examinations officer on the statement of entry. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after reading the wrong one.

One Cambridge detail deserves its own sentence, because the consequence is irreversible. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. If your child is sitting Cambridge papers, confirm the zone with the examinations officer rather than downloading a timetable from a search result.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor or an online specialist, judged against a deadline
paragraphs: When the calendar is tight, the comparison between a visiting tutor and online one-to-one stops being about preference and becomes a question of logistics. Three things decide it: who is actually available, what happens when a session has to move, and whether the arrangement survives a family's travel. All three go the same way, and it is worth setting out why rather than asserting it.

Availability first. Emirates Hills is a gated villa community set around a golf course, reached through community roads with their own speed limits and gate queues. A visiting tutor's working radius is therefore smaller than the map suggests, and the pool narrows to those who can complete the journey and still teach a useful hour. For a Higher Level subject in a specific component, that pool can be one or two people, and in a deadline week the odds of one of them being free at your time are poor. Online, the constraint disappears and the match is made on the subject.

Then rescheduling. In the eight weeks before a mock, sessions move. A match runs over, a school event appears, a child is unwell, a parent's flight shifts. Moving an online session is a message. Moving a visiting session means re-planning somebody's afternoon and, in the published market, often means paying for it anyway. Over an eight-week block the difference between losing one session and losing three is the difference between finishing the plan and abandoning it.

The money is the third piece, and the figures are published. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and home tutors more broadly at AED 200 to 500, with travel inside the rate; monthly packages of four two-hour visiting sessions are quoted at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Against that, EdFlik publishes online tuition from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52, Unitors IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase AED 270, and Bestimate puts specialist IB and IGCSE work at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those figures were read in October 2026 and belong to those providers. What the travel premium buys, measured honestly, is the journey; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and the online format is why a subject specialist is available in a deadline week at all.
