sections.heading: What to do with mock results, in the order that matters
paragraphs: A Diploma mock produces six results at once, and the instinct is to act on the lowest. That is usually the wrong call. With a limited number of weeks and a limited budget, the subject to work on is the one closest to a boundary, because moving a subject from the top of one band to the bottom of the next costs fewer marks than moving a subject that is two bands adrift.

So the first job after a mock is triage, and it needs the marked scripts rather than the grades. For each subject, find out how far the total sat below the next boundary, which component the lost marks came from, and whether the losses were content, technique or timing. Three subjects will usually have a clear answer, two will be fine, and one will need a conversation with the teacher. That exercise takes an evening and it is the highest-value hour of the whole term, whether or not you hire anybody.

The second job is to separate the three kinds of loss, because they need different responses and only one of them needs a tutor urgently. Timing losses show up as unanswered questions at the end of a paper and are fixed by timed practice the student can do alone. Technique losses show up as correct content written under the wrong command term, and respond fast to a short specialist block. Content losses show up as blank or wrong across a whole topic, and are the slowest to fix, which is why they need the most weeks.

The third job is to decide what not to do. A mock is also permission to stop something. If a subject is secure, stop revising it weekly and check it monthly. If an internal assessment is complete, stop thinking about it. If an activity is genuinely unsustainable alongside the final term, the household can decide that now rather than in April. Families who come out of a mock having chosen two things to focus on and two things to drop do better over the following eight weeks than families who resolve to work harder at everything.

sections.heading: Two calendars that are not the IB's: the Dubai school year and the mandatory subjects
paragraphs: Something no competitor page in this market mentions: your child's revision calendar is competing with subjects that sit outside the IB programme entirely. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The rules are specific enough to plan around. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language is used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson lasts at least twenty-five minutes.

Two further details matter. Schools must ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. And for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which is why tutoring in these subjects follows the school's own material rather than an outside scheme. If your child has an Arabic assessment in the fortnight you had earmarked for Diploma past papers, the Diploma work moves.

The second non-IB calendar is the household one. Ramadan shortens the school day and shifts when useful work happens, which commonly means a post-Iftar session or a late morning rather than a cancelled one. The two-month Dubai summer sits between the two Diploma years and is the single largest uninterrupted block available for a bridging or catch-up plan. And Emirates Hills families travel, which is manageable online and not manageable with a visiting arrangement. Write the travel dates on the same calendar as the deadlines before you count available weeks, because a plan that ignores three weeks abroad is not a plan.

sections.heading: Retakes, the November session and the cost of deciding late
paragraphs: Results day produces a decision, and the window for it is short. A student who has narrowly missed a university condition has three broad options: accept the offer that is available, ask for a re-mark or enquiry upon results through the school, or enter for a later session and reapply. Each has a deadline, and only the first one is obvious.

The enquiry upon results route runs through the school, not the family, and it has a deadline set by the board rather than by the school. That means the conversation has to happen in the first days after results rather than in the second week. Ask the coordinator what the deadline is, what the enquiry costs, and what evidence makes it worth attempting, because a re-mark is worth requesting when a total sat a mark or two below a boundary and rarely worth it otherwise.

A retake decision is harder because it rearranges a year. The IB runs a November session as well as a May one, and the practical questions are whether your child's school enters candidates for it, whether the subject can be re-sat without redoing internally assessed components, and what the university will accept. All three answers come from the school and the university rather than from a tutoring page, and all three should be established before any tutoring is booked. Confirm every session date with your Diploma coordinator or ibo.org.

What tutoring can do in this situation is well defined. A diagnostic session on the returned scripts, once available, to establish exactly where the marks went. A focused block on the components that lost them, with timed practice. And an honest assessment of whether the gap is closeable in the weeks before the next session. Deciding in July costs less than deciding in September, which is the only reason this section sits on a calendar-led page.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the paperwork calendar nobody mentions until Year 13
paragraphs: A separate calendar appears at the end of the Diploma for families staying in the UAE, and it catches people out because nobody warns them in Year 12. Secondary certificates generally need equivalency from the Ministry of Education before they can be used for university admission in the UAE, and the requirements differ by curriculum track.

The British-track requirements are published and specific. A student must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That five-subject rule is worth noting carefully, because at least one ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published requirement says.

The American track has its own thresholds. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB specifically, no points threshold is published in the source we have read, so this page states none. Confirm the IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority, and do not accept a figure from a page that does not say where it came from.

Two boundaries on this. Equivalency is a process run by the Ministry of Education, not something IB Gram performs, guarantees or expedites, and nothing about tutoring is required for it. We describe it, cite the authority and point you to the official channel. The reason it belongs on a calendar-led page is simply that the paperwork takes time and the deadline is a university's, so the right moment to start reading about it is Year 12 rather than the week the offers arrive.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and what the next eight weeks should look like
paragraphs: Two rules before the practical steps. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, with no fee stated and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published.

The second rule concerns assessed work, and it bites hardest in a deadline week. A tutor may teach the criteria, discuss a research question, explain a method and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor must never write an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay, supply data or rewrite a paragraph into final form. The pressure to cross that line rises as a deadline closes, which is exactly why the boundary should be agreed in writing at the start rather than negotiated at the end. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not approved, accredited or licensed by the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education.

Starting takes one message. Send the subject and level, the school and year group, the date you are working towards and who set it, the component where the marks are going, and two windows that work in an Emirates Hills week. Attach the marked mock or the last two assessments. A tutor who reads those before the trial arrives with a plan for eight weeks rather than an introduction to the subject.

Then the free trial lesson, which runs in full online with no payment and no card details. Ask the tutor to state, out loud, what week eight should look like and what the student has to do between sessions to get there. Write it down. Review against that at week four. If the plan is on track, continue; if nothing has moved, change the approach or the tutor rather than extending out of politeness. And if no specialist in the right component is free in your window, we will tell you and offer an alternative time rather than putting a generalist into the brief, because in a deadline term a mismatched hour is worse than no hour.

process.title: Write the date down and name who set it
process.description: Internal assessment deadline, mock window, predicted grades cut-off or examination session, and whether it comes from the school, the board or the IB. Verify the IB dates with your Diploma coordinator or ibo.org and note when you checked. A plan built on an unverified date is a plan built on nothing.

process.title: Count the weeks that actually exist
process.description: Subtract travel, subtract the fortnight around any other deadline in the same subject, subtract the week of the mock itself. The number left is what the plan has to work with, and it is usually smaller than the calendar suggests. Decide what to ask for after you have that number, not before.

process.title: Triage from the marked scripts
process.description: For each subject, find how far the total sat below the next boundary, which component lost the marks, and whether the losses were content, technique or timing. Work on the subject nearest a boundary rather than the one furthest behind. This evening's work is the highest-value hour in the term.

process.title: Brief the tutor on the deadline, not the subject
process.description: Send the subject and level, the date, the component, the school and two windows. Attach the marked work. A tutor briefed this way plans eight weeks backwards from the date; a tutor told only the subject starts at the beginning of the syllabus and uses three of your weeks getting oriented.

process.title: Agree what week eight looks like
process.description: In the free trial, ask the tutor to state the objective for the end of the block and what the student must do between sessions. Write both down. A block with a written goal can be reviewed honestly at the halfway point, which is the only moment when changing course is still cheap.

process.title: Review at week four, not week eight
process.description: Check the error log and the timed work against the goal agreed in week one. On track, continue. Nothing moved, change the approach or the tutor. Waiting until the block ends to find out it did not work wastes the one resource a calendar-led plan cannot replace, which is weeks.

whyPoints.title: Dates with a source attached
whyPoints.description: Every date on this page names who sets it and where to check it, and no IB session or results date is stated as fact because ibo.org blocks automated verification. Cambridge and Pearson dates are quoted from their own published pages with the series named. A date without a source is not information.

whyPoints.title: Planned backwards from your deadline
whyPoints.description: Blocks are built from the date you are working towards, with a written objective for the final week and a review at the halfway point. That is a different product from an open weekly booking, and in a term with a fixed deadline it is the only shape that reliably finishes.

whyPoints.title: Matched on component, not on proximity
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run over live video, the tutor is chosen for having taught the component where your child is losing marks. From a gated villa community that is the whole difference: the pool of specialists who could physically arrive before six is very small, and in a deadline week it is smaller still.

whyPoints.title: Sessions that move without costing a week
whyPoints.description: In the eight weeks before a mock, sessions get displaced by matches, school events and travel. Moving an online session is a message. Over a block, the difference between losing one session and losing three decides whether the plan finishes, which is why format matters more under a deadline than at any other time.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line agreed in advance
whyPoints.description: Teaching, feedback and process coaching on the student's own work. Never writing an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay, supplying data or rewriting to final form. The pressure to cross that line rises as a deadline closes, so the boundary is written down at the start.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, and a plan instead
whyPoints.description: No tutor can promise a grade and any provider offering one should be treated with real scepticism. What we commit to is the diagnosis, the written objective, the feedback cycle and an honest review at week four, which are the parts anybody can actually control.

faqs.question: My child's IB exams are a few months away. Is it too late to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, but it changes what to ask for. With twelve or more weeks there is room to diagnose, rebuild a topic and then train paper technique. With eight, pick one subject and one named weakness. With four, work on technique only: command terms, timing and answer shape, because content built in four weeks rarely survives examination pressure. With two, the job is to stop the specific habits losing marks. Starting late is not the problem; asking for six subjects to move in eight weeks is.

faqs.question: Where do I get the actual dates for my child's IB examination session?
faqs.answer: From your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org directly, and nowhere else. The IB publishes its session and results dates, but its site blocks automated checking, so this page deliberately states none. Ask the coordinator in writing, record the date you asked, and recheck in the examination year. Any page that gives you an IB examination or results date without naming its source is passing on something unverified, and secondary sources on these dates do not always agree with each other.

faqs.question: Which deadlines matter more than the exam session itself?
faqs.answer: The ones your school sets, because they come first and they are specific to your school. Subject internal assessment deadlines are set department by department, so three can land in the same fortnight. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge timelines come from the Diploma coordinator. The mock window and the predicted grades cut-off are the school's, and predicted grades drive university offers. Ask the subject teachers directly for their internal dates rather than relying on a whole-school calendar.

faqs.question: After a mock, should we work on the worst subject or a different one?
faqs.answer: Usually a different one. With limited weeks and a limited budget, the subject to work on is the one closest to a boundary, because moving a total from the top of one band to the bottom of the next costs fewer marks than closing a two-band gap. Get the marked scripts, find how far each total sat below the next boundary, and identify whether the losses were content, technique or timing. Timing is fixable alone, technique responds fast to a specialist, content needs the most weeks.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to houses in Emirates Hills, or are lessons online?
faqs.answer: IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video; we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. The market does offer visiting tutors, at published rates of AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by home tutors generally, with travel inside the figure. Against a deadline the online format wins on the two things that decide an eight-week block: which specialist is actually available, and whether a displaced session can be moved rather than lost.

faqs.question: How far ahead of an exam does an entry deadline usually fall?
faqs.answer: Months, and the published Pearson calendar shows it most clearly for this region. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students the following January, as November 2025 results did on 22 January 2026; the June route is the same shape one term earlier, with June 2026 results to centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit June and November only, since the February and March series is offered to India, and Cambridge June entries close in the spring, months before the first paper. Treat an entry deadline sitting two to three months ahead of the exam as normal, read the timetable for your centre's Cambridge zone, and confirm your own dates with the school's examinations officer.

faqs.question: Our school sits Cambridge papers: what is the zone timetable trap?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. The consequence is irreversible, so confirm the zone with your school's examinations officer rather than downloading a timetable from a search result. It takes one email and it removes a risk nobody can fix afterwards.

faqs.question: How many weeks does an internal assessment actually need?
faqs.answer: Eight is comfortable, four is a rescue, one is not a tutoring problem. The schedule should run backwards from the school's deadline: viability or research question first, then data collection or extended reading, then drafting with written feedback, leaving the final fortnight for review rather than writing. The commonest failure is a research question that cannot produce a usable result, discovered weeks in. One session spent testing that before any work begins saves the whole exercise.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor do on an Extended Essay as the deadline closes?
faqs.answer: Teach the assessment criteria, discuss whether the research question is answerable, explain how to structure an argument, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. What a tutor must never do is write it, supply the research, or rewrite a paragraph into its final form. The pressure to cross that line rises as the date approaches, which is why the boundary belongs in writing at the start. The essay must be the student's own work, and the consequences of anything else fall on the student.

faqs.question: Can sessions continue when we travel out of Dubai during term?
faqs.answer: Yes, which is one of the practical reasons online suits this community. Lessons run over live video, so a session continues from wherever there is a reliable connection, and the schedule can shift by a few hours to fit a different time zone. A visiting arrangement simply stops for the duration. If your family travels for three weeks in an eight-week block, write those weeks on the calendar before you count available sessions, because a plan that ignores them is not a plan.

faqs.question: Does an eight-week block survive Ramadan, and how should it shift?
faqs.answer: By moving, not by pausing. The school day shortens, so sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar slot or to a late morning, and the content should move with the slot. Heavy work such as derivations, timed papers and extended writing goes in the morning when energy is highest; lighter work such as marked-script review, error tagging and recall practice goes in the later slot. Families who plan the shift in advance keep the block on track; families who cancel for the month lose four of their eight weeks.

faqs.question: Does study leave change what tutoring should look like?
faqs.answer: Completely, and for the better. Study leave shortens or ends the school day and opens the mornings, which is the only period in two years when the best hours are available. That is the window for full papers under timed conditions followed immediately by mark-scheme review while the attempt is fresh, something no term-time evening slot can accommodate. Two or three shorter morning sessions a week return more than one long evening session, and the triage can span subjects rather than sticking to one.

faqs.question: If results are disappointing, what are the real options and their deadlines?
faqs.answer: Three, and the window is short. Accept an available offer. Ask the school to submit an enquiry upon results, which runs through the school on a board-set deadline and is worth attempting mainly when a total sat a mark or two below a boundary. Or enter for a later session and reapply, which depends on whether your school enters candidates for it and whether internally assessed components carry over. Ask the coordinator all three questions in the first days after results, not the second week.

faqs.question: What does UAE Ministry of Education equivalency require from a British-track student?
faqs.answer: Published requirements are one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, plus five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five. One ranking competitor page states six IGCSE subjects are required, which is not what the published rule says. For the IB specifically, no points threshold is published in the source read, so confirm it on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Does my child need tutoring to get equivalency or a university place?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process with published requirements, and nothing about private tutoring is part of it. IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency or attestation, and any suggestion that tutoring is required for a regulatory process is a false-urgency claim rather than information. We describe the process, cite the authority and point you to the official channel. The reason it appears on a calendar-led page is only that the paperwork takes time and university deadlines do not move.

faqs.question: What should the first eight weeks with a new tutor actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written objective agreed in week one, a feedback cycle that runs every week, and a review at week four honest enough to change course. The objective names one subject and one component. The cycle means the student attempts timed work alone, it gets marked, and the session starts from the marked attempt. The week-four review checks the error log against the objective. If nothing has moved by then, change the approach or the tutor; no tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does should be treated with real scepticism.

We will match a specialist and agree a written objective for week eight before anything is paid for, and the first lesson is free. Lessons run one to one over live video.

intro.heading: The Diploma is six subjects and a core, and the core is where points leak
paragraphs: A Diploma candidate earns up to 42 points from six subjects and up to three more from the core: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, with Creativity, Activity, Service required but not graded. Those three points are a small fraction of the total and a large fraction of the stress, because they come from two long independent pieces of work with school-set deadlines that nobody chases until they are close.

This page is built around that structure rather than around a single weak subject. It sets out the six groups and what the internally assessed component looks like in each, then treats Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay as real work with their own failure modes, because in this catchment they are the components most often left until they cannot be done properly.

Green Community is a specific kind of place for this conversation. It sits inside Dubai Investments Park, low-rise and walkable, with schools close enough that a family's whole school run can be a short drive or a walk. That changes expectations: parents here are used to things being nearby. The one thing that is not nearby is a Diploma subject specialist, because IB provision in this part of Dubai is concentrated in a handful of schools and the tutoring market has grown up around UK and Indian curricula instead.

KHDA, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment. Seven per cent is a substantial absolute number thinly spread, and this catchment is not where it concentrates.

There is a second reason to treat the core as the organising idea on a page like this. Subject difficulty announces itself: a grade falls, a teacher comments, a parent acts. The core does not announce itself at all. A student can be eighteen months into the Diploma with a thoughtful but unnarrowed Extended Essay question and no Theory of Knowledge example worth the name, and nothing on a report card will say so. By the time it becomes visible, the research weeks have gone to the mocks and the internal assessments.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a Green Community family the trade is clear. You give up a person in the room and you gain the whole pool of specialists in your child's actual subject, rather than the subset willing to drive into Dubai Investments Park on a weekday evening.

What follows: the six groups with their internal components, the core treated properly, the Higher and Standard Level decision, the AED market bands read from the monthly end, the academic-honesty boundary, and how to start. Read it with your child's subject list and one marked assessment to hand.

programmes.name: The six subject groups
programmes.description: Candidates take one subject from each of studies in language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences and mathematics, plus either an arts subject or a second from another group. Three subjects are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7 from external papers plus an internally assessed component moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: Green Community students reach the Diploma mainly through the IB continuum schools in Dubai Investments Park and The Sustainable City, or by transferring from a UK-curriculum school at 16. The transfer route produces most of our requests, because IGCSE success predicts content comfort and nothing about internally assessed work.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Together these contribute up to three points. Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition. The Extended Essay is an independent research piece in a subject of the student's choice, with a 4,000-word limit and a supervisor. Creativity, Activity, Service is required for the Diploma to be awarded but carries no grade.
programmes.countryNote: Both are where points go missing in this catchment, and almost never because the work is too hard. The Extended Essay fails on a research question too broad to answer in 4,000 words. Theory of Knowledge fails on essays that make large claims about knowledge with no worked example to test them against.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four lettered criteria out of eight, with the Personal Project in MYP 5. No external papers for most students, which means the record of these years is a sequence of criterion judgements rather than test results.
programmes.countryNote: For Green Community families the MYP question is usually whether the criterion profile predicts Diploma success. A student scoring well on inquiry and reflection criteria is better placed for the Diploma's internal components than their final grade alone suggests, and the reverse is also true.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and organised around transdisciplinary themes, finishing with the Year 6 Exhibition. Assessment is formative and portfolio-based, with no external test, so number fluency and reading stamina can lag without anything flagging it until the MYP's written demands arrive.
programmes.countryNote: The continuum schools serving this community run PYP through to the Diploma, so a child here may spend fourteen years inside IB assessment language. Tutoring at this stage is nearly always arithmetic fluency, handwriting speed and reading comprehension rather than anything programme-specific.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-green-community.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma subjects Green Community families ask about, described by their internally assessed component, because that is the part of the grade a tutor can most legitimately help improve.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral links a global issue to two studied texts and is internally assessed. Paper 1 is unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, and HL adds the written essay. Marks follow analysis of technique and effect; accurate retelling earns very little.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: Similar component structure with literary texts throughout. Candidates lose marks by writing about what happens rather than how the writing produces its effect, which is the same habit that limits Paper 1.

subjects.name: French B and Spanish B
subjects.description: Productive and receptive skills across prescribed themes with an individual oral. The oral is internally assessed, and students who prepare content without preparing spontaneous interaction lose marks in the unprepared section.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Relevant beyond the Diploma because KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. A language B grade sits alongside that mandatory provision rather than replacing it, and the streams are distinct.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal portfolio is a set of commentaries on published news articles. Article choice decides the ceiling before writing begins, because an article with no usable economics cannot support diagram-led analysis.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A research project on a real organisation, marked on the question, the tools applied and the evaluation reached. Thorough description of a company scores below selective use of data that leads to a judgement.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation is internally assessed and includes evaluation of sources. Students who narrate the topic rather than interrogating the evidence lose the criterion that carries most of the marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The scientific investigation plus heavy command-term sensitivity on the papers. "Outline", "explain" and "discuss" demand different depths, and answering all three at one depth caps the paper independently of knowledge.

subjects.name: Mathematics: both courses
subjects.description: The exploration is internally assessed against criteria including reflection, which students routinely write as a conclusion rather than as critical evaluation. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are matched to different specialists.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Portfolio and exhibition components in which documentation of thinking carries marks alongside the finished work. Under-documenting is the usual failure, because the development the criteria want to see was never recorded.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-green-community.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Diploma request from this community, and they are chosen by which component is under pressure.

modes.title: One subject, one specialist, weekly
modes.description: A fixed slot with one tutor in one subject at one level, running through the term and following the school's scheme of work rather than a parallel syllabus. The default arrangement, and the one that suits a named subject difficulty.

modes.description: Process coaching alongside the school supervisor, not instead of them. The work is narrowing the research question until it can be answered in 4,000 words, designing a method, evaluating sources and understanding what the assessment criteria reward.

modes.description: Short blocks on the essay and the exhibition, both of which fail for the same reason: abstraction with no worked example. The work is anchoring every knowledge claim to something specific the student can actually interrogate.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay, and why 4,000 words is the real constraint
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is an independent research piece with a 4,000-word limit, and that limit is the design brief nobody reads as one. A question that would need a book cannot be answered in 4,000 words, so what gets submitted is a survey: broad, competent, and short of the marks that go to investigation. It is the commonest reason a capable Green Community student scores below their subject work on the core.

Narrowing is therefore the first and largest job, and it is one a tutor can do without touching a word of the writing. The method is mechanical rather than inspired. Take the question. Ask what evidence would answer it. Ask whether the student can actually obtain that evidence in the time available. If either answer is no, narrow and repeat. A question about education policy becomes a question about one measure, in one setting, assessed one way.

The second job is the internal calendar, which is set by the school rather than by the IB and sits earlier than families expect because the supervisor and the school both need time before submission. A student who has not chosen a subject by the end of the first Diploma year is compressing the research phase into the same term as the mocks and the internal assessments.

The third job is the boundary, and it is firm. A tutor may discuss the question, teach the subject content, explain the assessment criteria, evaluate sources with the student, check referencing conventions and read a draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not supply the question, write any part of the essay, or edit it to a finished state. Services in this market sell completed coursework, one advertising finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; submitting bought work risks the Diploma itself.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge: the component that rewards one good example
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition, and students in this catchment lose marks in the same way almost every year: by writing abstractly. Large claims about how knowledge works, attached to nothing in particular, with no example the reader can test the claim against. The result reads thoughtful and scores poorly.

The remedy is specific. Every knowledge question needs an example concrete enough that the student can interrogate it, and good examples are usually small. A particular disputed measurement in a science the student studies. A specific historical account and the sources behind it. One piece of mathematics the student has actually used. The claim then has something to be tested against, which is what the assessment is looking for.

The second recurring failure is answering the title the student wishes had been set. Prescribed titles are precise, and a strong essay about a neighbouring question scores badly. The useful first session on any Theory of Knowledge essay is spent entirely on the title: what each clause actually demands, what would count as addressing it, and what an answer would have to contain.

For the exhibition, the objects matter less than what they let the student argue. A visually interesting object with nothing to say about the prompt is a worse choice than a mundane one that does. Students choose objects first and reasons second; reversing that order is a single session's work and it changes the mark.
bullets: Anchor every knowledge claim to one small, testable example
Spend the first session on the prescribed title, not on the content
Answer the title set, not the neighbouring question
Choose exhibition objects for what they let you argue
The tutor questions and marks; the student writes every word

sections.heading: Higher or Standard Level: a decision made twice
paragraphs: Every Diploma candidate takes three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and the choice is made before the student has experienced either. It is then frequently revisited a term or two in, when the Higher Level load becomes real, and that second decision is where families need good information rather than reassurance.

The difference is not merely volume. Higher Level adds content, and in the sciences and mathematics it adds a paper built around sustained problem-solving across linked parts, which punishes students who abandon a question when one part does not resolve. It also raises the expected depth of the internally assessed component. A student who is comfortable with the content but not with sustained unfamiliarity may be better at Standard Level with a higher grade.

The destination has to be read before the decision is confirmed. Some degree programmes specify particular subjects at Higher Level, and some specify Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation. The only reliable method is to read the entry requirements for two or three target programmes directly, including any UAE universities on the list, and to do that before the drop deadline rather than after it.

Where a change is being considered, the evidence should be a marked assessment rather than a feeling about workload. A student losing Higher Level marks to technique - unwritten method, command-term depth, abandoned linked questions - is not necessarily in the wrong level. A student who cannot access the Higher Level questions at all is a different case, and an hour of marking makes the distinction clear.

sections.heading: What Diploma tutoring costs, read from the monthly figure down
paragraphs: Households budget monthly, so start there. Dubai rate guidance published for 2026 estimates a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Packages visible in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Set those two packages beside each other and the structure of this market becomes clear. Roughly double the monthly cost buys half the number of contacts, and the difference is the tutor's travel. For a Green Community family that travel is a real cost to somebody, and it is being paid for in money and in a later start time.

The hourly bands behind the monthly figures, published October 2026 and attributed: Tutopiya from about AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level; Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 online; Dubai rate guidance putting in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independent tutors to AED 500; specialists at AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase around AED 270; and BartyED at AED 650.

None of these are IB Gram prices and this page carries no rate card, because the fee depends on subject and level and is quoted after the free trial lesson. The point of publishing the bands is that a quote becomes checkable. Three of the pages ranking for this search publish no price at all, and its own FAQ on one of them asks what tutoring costs and declines to answer.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one from a walkable community, and where it does not fit
paragraphs: Green Community is built for short journeys, and most things a family needs are close. Diploma subject specialists are the exception, because the IB cohort in this part of Dubai is small and the local tutoring market grew up around other curricula. The consequence is that the convenience argument for an in-home tutor, which holds for most services here, does not hold for this one: the specialist usually is not local to begin with.

IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and we state that near the top of the page rather than leaving it to be discovered after a booking, because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote.

What online delivery gives a household here is the full specialist pool and an earlier start. A 4.30pm session catches a student who can still think; a 6pm session, after a tutor has crossed the city, often does not. Diploma work is largely document work - a marked script, a draft essay, an exploration - and a shared screen where both people annotate the same page suits it better than one paper copy between two chairs.

The limitations deserve naming. A student who will not begin work without an adult physically present does better in person. Younger children lose attention faster on screen. A weak connection shortens the hour whatever the clock says. And a shared study space - more common in the apartment blocks here than in the villas - undermines the lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room. If one of those applies, hire locally and ask about the MoHRE private tuition work permit first.

sections.heading: Academic honesty across the core and the internal components
paragraphs: This is the most consequential section on the page. The IB treats submitting work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the outcome can be the loss of the Diploma rather than a mark penalty. With the core in particular - two long documents produced largely outside class - the temptation and the exposure are both at their highest.

The legitimate space is wide and worth knowing precisely, because families who do not know it are vulnerable to services that trade on the confusion. A tutor may teach subject content, explain each assessment criterion and what it caps, help narrow a research question, discuss method and source evaluation, explain referencing conventions, mark a draft against the descriptors and explain the marking. That covers nearly everything a Diploma student genuinely needs.

What a tutor may not do is write, rewrite or complete any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or exhibition commentary, supply a research question wholesale, produce data, or edit a document to a finished state. The test after every session is simple: was every sentence in that document typed by your child? There are services selling completed Internal Assessments in this market at AED 3,750, and that transaction buys an investigation the student cannot defend.

Three further claims to discount. We do not describe tutors as IB examiners, because current examiner status is not evidenceable for individuals and is routinely used to imply access to marking or boundaries that nobody has. We do not host or distribute IB papers, mark schemes, boundary tables or subject guides, which are copyright material; we link the official sources. And IB Gram is not KHDA approved - a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with physical premises, which we neither hold nor occupy.
bullets: Every sentence submitted must have been typed by the student
Criteria explanation, source evaluation and draft marking are all legitimate
Supplying a research question or writing a paragraph is not
No examiner claims, no distributed papers, no regulator approval claimed
A service selling finished coursework is selling a malpractice finding

sections.heading: Permits and what to ask a tutor you hire directly
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and families hiring an individual directly should know what to ask. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The UAE government states that the permit is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligibility is deliberately broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, publishes no fee, lists a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

The consequence of skipping it is stated plainly by the government: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so we quote no amount and you should be sceptical of pages that do. In Abu Dhabi there is an additional layer, with ADEK's professional-ethics rules reported as barring private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

So the two questions to put to any independent tutor before the first lesson are whether they hold the MoHRE permit, and whether they have taught that specific subject at that specific level to IB criteria. Both are fair, both are answerable in a sentence, and a tutor who hesitates on either has told you something useful. And never arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher.

sections.heading: Starting, including what happens when nobody suitable is free
paragraphs: Send the subject and level, the school, and whichever document is the live pressure: a marked assessment, a draft internal component, or an Extended Essay question that is not yet narrow enough. The document is the useful part. Twenty minutes describing the term tells us less than two minutes with a marked script.

Matching runs on subject and level rather than availability. Standard Level subjects and both mathematics courses usually match within a day. Higher Level sciences, Arabic B and less common language B courses take two or three days, because the pool is narrow and we will not put a near-miss in front of a Higher Level draft. We tell you which case applies at the enquiry rather than after you have waited.

Core support is matched differently again. Extended Essay work is matched to the essay's subject, not to a general essay tutor, because the criteria and the expected method are subject-specific. Theory of Knowledge is its own specialism, and a good subject teacher is not automatically good at it.

The trial lesson is free, taught by the matched specialist rather than a salesperson, and built on the document you sent. It ends in a written note of what the document showed and what the first month should target, and that note is yours whether or not you continue. When nobody suitable has a slot at the hour you want, we say so and offer a different weekday, a short block, or an honest recommendation to look locally with the two questions above in hand.

whyPoints.title: The core is treated as real work
whyPoints.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry up to three points and cause most of the stress, and they fail for known reasons: a question too broad for 4,000 words, and abstraction with no worked example. Both are fixable early and expensive late.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not a local shortlist
whyPoints.description: Green Community is convenient for most things and not for Diploma specialists, because IB provision here is concentrated in a few schools. Online delivery hands you the whole pool rather than the subset willing to drive into Dubai Investments Park.

whyPoints.title: Extended Essay support matched to the subject
whyPoints.description: The criteria and the expected method are subject-specific, so an essay in history needs a historian rather than a general essay tutor. That distinction is why some Extended Essay support achieves nothing.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or guide that published it in October 2026. Three pages ranking for this search publish no price, and one has an FAQ that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it.

whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria, evaluate sources with the student, teach content and mark drafts. They never write, rewrite or complete assessed work. A service offering more is offering your child a malpractice finding at a price.

faqs.question: Can we get a tutor to come to our house in Green Community?
faqs.answer: Local agencies do serve this community, and Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 per hour with independent tutors advertising up to AED 500, travel included in the figure. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The particular problem here is that Diploma specialists are not local to begin with, because IB provision in Dubai Investments Park is concentrated in a few schools, so an in-home booking usually means a generalist rather than a nearer specialist.

faqs.question: How much do Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay actually matter?
faqs.answer: Together they contribute up to three points on top of the 42 available from six subjects, so arithmetically they are a small share. In practice they matter more than that, for two reasons. They are the components most likely to be left until they cannot be done properly, which turns a manageable three points into a term of pressure during the mocks. And a student who has not learned to narrow a research question or anchor an argument in evidence carries that gap into every subject's internal component.

faqs.question: Is 4,000 words a target or a ceiling for the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Four thousand words is the upper limit rather than a target, and treating it as a target is what produces padded essays. The more useful way to read the limit is as a design constraint: if the research question could not be answered within it, the question is wrong and should be narrowed before any writing starts. A narrow, well-evidenced essay comfortably inside the limit outscores a broad survey that reaches it. Your school will also publish its own internal deadlines, which bind earlier than the word count does.

faqs.question: My child's TOK essay reads well but scores badly. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always abstraction. Theory of Knowledge rewards knowledge claims that are tested against something specific, and essays that make large statements about how knowledge works with no example attached read thoughtfully and score poorly. The second common cause is answering a neighbouring question rather than the prescribed title that was actually set. The fix for both is a session spent entirely on the title and on finding one small, concrete example the student can genuinely interrogate, before any further writing happens.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects do Green Community families ask about most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, split between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, with Higher Level Analysis and Approaches the single commonest request. Chemistry and Biology follow, usually tied to a scientific investigation deadline. English A Language and Literature arrives when Paper 1 marks stay flat despite strong classwork. Economics and Business Management come up around the internal portfolio or project rather than the papers. Arabic B appears steadily, because Arabic is required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum.

faqs.question: Should my child move a subject from Higher to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Decide it on a marked assessment rather than on how the workload feels. Higher Level adds content and, in the sciences and mathematics, a paper of sustained linked problems that punishes abandoning a question partway. A student losing marks to technique - unwritten method, command-term depth, questions left after part one - is not necessarily in the wrong level. One who cannot access the questions at all is a different case. Read the entry requirements of two or three target degree programmes before confirming, and ask the school when the deadline falls.

faqs.question: How should a Green Community tutor work alongside the school's EE supervisor?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should offer to. The supervisor is appointed by the school and is part of the assessment process, with required meetings and a reflection record. A tutor works alongside that relationship: narrowing the question, teaching the subject content, discussing method and source evaluation, explaining the criteria and marking a draft against the descriptors. A tutor who proposes to replace the supervisor, or to write any part of the essay, is proposing something that puts the student's Diploma at risk rather than helping it.

faqs.question: Are the AED figures on this page IB Gram's prices?
faqs.answer: No. They are market rates read from published competitor pages and Dubai rate guides in October 2026, included so that any quote you receive can be judged against something real. Entry-level online tuition is advertised from around AED 33-65 per hour, qualified online subject tutors from AED 150-200, in-home visits at AED 180-500 including travel, specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and one premium provider at AED 650. IB Gram's own fee depends on subject and level and is quoted after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: How does the Individual Oral work for a Diploma English student?
faqs.answer: It is an internally assessed oral in which the student links a global issue to two studied texts, one in translation where the course requires it, and it is recorded and moderated. Students prepare content thoroughly and then lose marks in the unprepared discussion, because they have rehearsed a presentation rather than built an argument they can extend. Useful preparation is therefore practising being questioned on the chosen extracts rather than polishing the opening, and that is straightforward to do over video.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring effective for a Diploma student in Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: For Diploma work, generally yes, because so much of it is document work: a marked script, a draft investigation, an Extended Essay outline. A shared screen where tutor and student annotate the same page suits that better than a single paper copy across a table. The scheduling gain matters too, since a 4.30pm start catches a student who can still think while a 6pm start after a cross-city drive often does not. It works less well for a student who needs an adult present to begin work at all.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level specialist is available at our preferred hour?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we offer the real options rather than filling the slot. Those are a different weekday with the right specialist, a shorter block until a regular slot opens, or an honest recommendation to look locally with two questions in hand: does the tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and have they taught that subject at that level to IB criteria. No competitor in this market publishes what happens when it cannot help, which is precisely why it is written here rather than left to a delayed reply.

faqs.question: Do you cover Arabic for the Dubai mandatory subject requirement as well as Arabic B?
faqs.answer: We cover Arabic streams, and the first step is identifying which one applies. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and mandates separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA also requires schools to ensure teachers of these subjects hold appropriate KHDA approval. Tell us the stream and the school's scheme of work.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma student start working on the core?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay subject should be chosen in the second half of the first Diploma year and the question narrowed before the long summer break, because the research phase otherwise collides with the mocks and the internal assessments. Theory of Knowledge benefits from starting with the prescribed titles as soon as they are available, since the first useful session is spent on the title rather than on content. Both have school-set internal deadlines that land earlier than families expect, and the coordinator holds the calendar.

faqs.question: Will sessions still work during Ramadan for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: They move rather than stop, and the shape changes. School hours shorten, households reorganise their evening around iftar, and a weekday 5pm slot usually becomes early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. For Diploma students the component under pressure decides what to protect: internal assessment work can take fewer, longer sessions, while anything quantitative needs frequency over length. Because nobody is travelling to your address, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation of someone's commute.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-green-community.closingHeading: Start with the component under pressure
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-green-community.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB home tutor in Green Community, the fastest useful step is to name the component rather than the subject. A marked script, a draft internal assessment, or an Extended Essay question that is still too broad to answer in 4,000 words: send whichever one is actually causing the trouble, along with the subject, the level and the school. A specialist in that subject reads it and teaches a free one-to-one trial lesson online at a Gulf Standard Time hour that fits the short school run here, finishing with a written diagnosis that is yours whether or not you continue.

intro.heading: Four neighbourhoods, four different front doors, one answer
paragraphs: Hor Al Anz is one of the denser residential districts in Deira: mid-rise apartment blocks on tight streets, limited visitor parking, and Abu Hail metro station within walking distance for much of it. Families here compare their position constantly against Al Mamzar on the coast, Al Qusais inland and Deira proper to the west, and the comparison is worth running properly - the practical conditions genuinely differ. For the IB question specifically, they turn out not to matter, and that is worth explaining rather than asserting.

The differences are real at the front door. A visiting tutor coming to a Hor Al Anz apartment block faces narrow streets and parking that is frequently unavailable rather than merely slow. In Al Mamzar the streets are wider and the parking easier, but the journey in from the rest of the city is longer. In Al Qusais the roads are better and the school cluster is on the doorstep. Deira proper is the most congested of the four. Four genuinely different arrival problems.

None of them changes who teaches the International Baccalaureate. IB programmes account for about 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, in a sector of 227 private schools and 387,441 students teaching seventeen different curricula. That 7 per cent concentrates in Emirates Hills, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim and the New Dubai belt, with the nearest provision to Hor Al Anz sitting in Al Garhoud, Dubai Festival City and east in Mirdif. Tutors cluster where their market is, and their market is not Deira.

So the arithmetic is the same from every one of these four addresses. The number of people in this city who have taught Higher Level Chemistry, or Analysis and Approaches Paper 3, or who can supervise an Extended Essay properly, is small. The number of those who are also free at the hour your child can concentrate and willing to cross the city and find parking on a Hor Al Anz street at 5pm is smaller again. Choosing on the second condition means accepting a worse answer on the first.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Hor Al Anz or anywhere else in the UAE; a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. This page makes that case on the specifics - what a visit actually costs in teaching minutes from a dense Deira address, how the four neighbourhoods compare, and where the local market genuinely is the better option, because for Arabic and for CBSE support in this district it often is.

The order below follows the question. First, what a home visit costs in teaching minutes from a dense Deira address, with the four districts set against each other on arrival time rather than on atmosphere. Second, why the IB answer resolves identically from all four, explained through the three filters that actually govern availability. Then what the phrase 'IB tutor' has to contain before it means anything, the rate read per teaching minute rather than per hour, the slot that survives a term from a metro-adjacent address, and the internal assessment boundary that protects the candidate rather than the provider.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.programmesIntro: An IB family in Hor Al Anz may be in any of three programmes, and the comparison with neighbouring districts plays out differently in each. These are the stages and what they require here.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with transdisciplinary themes rather than subject syllabuses and no external examination. Support here is rarely subject tutoring - the useful work is literacy, numeracy fluency and the research and presentation habits the programme assumes, and a generalist primary teacher is a better match than a specialist.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one stage where the neighbourhood comparison does change the answer. Primary support does not require IB-specific expertise, and the local tutoring market across Hor Al Anz, Abu Hail and Al Qusais is deep and well priced for exactly that. A nearby tutor is often the better option, and we would say so.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria each scored zero to eight, converted to a one-to-seven grade. What is scarce here is not subject knowledge but criteria literacy - the ability to read a descriptor and teach the skill it names. That competence is thinly spread in Deira because the programme is thinly represented.
programmes.countryNote: The Personal Project in MYP 5 is the component where a Hor Al Anz family is most likely to be working without local peers who have done it before. Twenty-four marks across planning, applying skills and reflecting, with the process journal as the evidence base for all three - and no neighbour to tell you that the journal is the whole thing.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups at Higher or Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Sat in the May session UAE schools use, with a November session also available. This is where the supply gap between this district and the New Dubai belt is widest, and where online matching changes the answer most.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student in Hor Al Anz is commuting, because no IB school sits in the district. The nearest provision is Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City, roughly fifteen to thirty minutes depending on the hour, with further provision east in Mirdif. That commute is the reason afternoon appointments in this neighbourhood are so often rescheduled.

programmes.name: The core components, separately
programmes.description: The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS are not simply extra subjects. Supervising an Extended Essay well is a different skill from teaching the subject it sits in, and Theory of Knowledge asks for a form of argument that appears nowhere else in the programme. Both are scarcer than any individual subject.
programmes.countryNote: The school supervisor is and should remain the primary route for the Extended Essay. What an outside tutor can usefully add is interrogating whether a research question is answerable within the word limit and the resources available, and giving feedback on a draft the student has written - not producing text.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Hor Al Anz families ask about, with the component that decides the grade and an honest note on coverage.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, which is where understanding is really tested. Higher Level Paper 3 carries 20 per cent and is the component students have practised least. Standard Level coverage is reasonable; Higher Level is thinner.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with calculator access throughout. The Higher Level statistics content is demanding and is among the hardest requirements in the set to match a specialist for, from any district.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume and the data-based questions decide the grade. The most frequently requested Diploma science in this catchment, driven by health-science ambitions, and reasonably well covered.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole-based calculations drain marks across every paper, and organic is taught last and revised least. Higher Level organic specialists are scarce city-wide rather than only on this side of it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circuits are the reliable mark drains, and the data-analysis section of Paper 1 rewards uncertainty work that is rarely taught as a system. Higher Level coverage is thin.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Both popular in a district where many parents work in trade and logistics around Deira and Al Hamriya. Command terms and diagram accuracy decide more marks than content does, and coverage is good.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper on unseen non-literary texts are where marks move. Wide reading alone does not help; shaping an argument to the question asked does.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Taken by many students in this catchment whose home language is not English. The individual oral and the writing task reward timed practice rather than vocabulary work, and coverage is good.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Demand for the first-language pathway is above the city average in this district, and local supply for it is genuinely deep. This is the clearest case where a nearby tutor beats an online match.

subjects.name: Psychology and Global Politics
subjects.description: Both reward command-term discipline and the use of specific studies or cases rather than general argument. Coverage is moderate and thinner for the Higher Level extensions.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Scarcer than any subject, because supervision is a distinct skill. Support is on question viability, criteria understanding and feedback on the student's own draft, never on producing the work.

subjects.name: Approaches to Learning across the Diploma
subjects.description: Workload planning, backwards planning from internal deadlines, revising against weightings rather than evenly. One person can cover this across six subjects, and it is frequently the right purchase for a student who is drowning rather than failing.

sections.heading: What a home visit costs in teaching minutes from a dense Deira address
paragraphs: It is worth taking the home-tutor question seriously rather than deflecting it, because the market offers the service and the search is sensible. In-home one-to-one tutoring in Dubai is advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's in-home band at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoted at AED 200 to 500. Advertised monthly packages run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. The travel is inside the price in every case.

In Hor Al Anz, though, the cost is not only in the rate - it is in teaching minutes. The district is dense mid-rise on tight streets with visitor parking that is frequently unavailable rather than merely slow. A tutor who arrives at the right time and then spends twelve minutes finding a space has turned a sixty-minute lesson into forty-eight, and the first five of those are spent settling rather than teaching. Repeat weekly and the loss is a session a month.

That is a different problem from the one a villa community has, and it is why the comparison with neighbouring districts is worth making precisely. Al Mamzar has easier parking and a longer inbound journey. Al Qusais has both better roads and easier parking. Deira proper has the worst congestion. Each produces a similar net loss by a different route, which is the point: the arrival problem varies in form and barely in size.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Hor Al Anz, in Dubai, or anywhere in the UAE; a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. So this is not a service we are selling against - it is why the delivery model is what it is. The table sets the four districts out honestly, including the one genuine advantage of a visit, which is that for a younger student a person in the room is worth paying for.

sections.heading: Why the IB answer is identical from all four addresses
paragraphs: The reason has nothing to do with online tuition being inherently better and everything to do with how scarce supply behaves under constraints. Think of three filters applied in order. First: people who have taught this programme, in this subject, at this level. Second: of those, the ones who can diagnose where a particular student is losing marks rather than simply teach the content again. Third: of those, the ones free at a usable hour and willing to drive to a specific street and park there.

The first filter cuts hard, because IB programmes are about 7 per cent of Dubai's enrolment and that share concentrates away from Deira. The second cuts harder, because teaching a subject and diagnosing a failure pattern are different competencies. The third cuts again, and crucially it cuts in a way uncorrelated with teaching quality - willingness to circle a Hor Al Anz street at 5pm tells you nothing about how well someone explains an energy cycle or an Extended Essay research question.

Applying the third filter therefore means accepting a worse result on the first two, and that trade is the same whether the street is in Hor Al Anz, Al Mamzar, Abu Hail or Al Qusais. It is also why the comparison between those four, while genuinely interesting on parking and commute, resolves identically on the question the search was actually about. Removing the logistics filter does not improve the tutor; it stops geography choosing on your behalf.

There is one honest exception, and it runs the other way. For Arabic as a first language and for primary-stage support, local supply in this district is deep and well priced, because that is where local demand sits. In those cases the nearby option is frequently the better one, and the comparison between districts matters again because proximity to a particular school community genuinely helps. Supply is uneven in both directions, and which direction depends on the subject.

sections.heading: What an 'IB tutor' has to mean before the word is useful
paragraphs: 'IB tutor' is not a specification, and treating it as one is how families in this district end up paying for a term that produces nothing. Three pieces of information turn it into a specification: the programme, the subject, and the level. A tutor for Middle Years sciences, a tutor for Standard Level Biology and a tutor for Higher Level Chemistry are three different people, and only the second two are even in the same programme.

Level matters more than families expect. Higher Level courses add depth woven through the content rather than a block at the end, so a tutor who has taught Standard Level thoroughly may be genuinely unable to handle the Higher Level extension - and will discover that in week three rather than admitting it in week one. Asking for the level in the booking is not pedantry; it is the difference between a match and an approximation.

The core components need naming separately again. An Extended Essay supervisor, a Theory of Knowledge tutor and a subject tutor are distinct roles. Supervising an essay is about question viability, scope, methodology and criteria rather than about content, and Theory of Knowledge asks for a kind of argument that appears nowhere else in the programme. A subject specialist who agrees to cover Theory of Knowledge as a favour is usually doing neither job well.

The test a parent can run, without subject expertise, is three questions in a free trial. What is each paper worth, and what does the internal assessment contribute? Name the internal assessment criteria for this subject and the marks for each. And here is a marked script - what does the pattern of lost marks indicate, and what would the first three sessions therefore do? Ten minutes of that sorts the market more reliably than any credential list.

sections.heading: The rate, read per teaching minute rather than per hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates hide the thing that matters in a dense district, which is how much of the hour is teaching. Published figures first. Online, the budget band starts at roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour with Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik, which generally means a university student. A qualified subject tutor online is published from around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB work is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at around AED 270, and examiner-led sessions at around AED 650 with BartyED.

In-home one-to-one sits at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price. Now apply the Hor Al Anz arrival problem. A sixty-minute visit that loses ten to fifteen minutes to street parking and settling delivers forty-five to fifty teaching minutes, which moves the effective rate up by a fifth or more. That is before any session is cancelled outright, and in this district the appointments most often cancelled are the ones depending on somebody else's drive and somebody else's parking space.

The monthly comparison makes it clearer. Advertised packages in this market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. Eight contacts against four, at half the price, and with no minutes lost at the door. For building fluency in a subject, contact frequency matters more than session length, which makes that comparison unflattering in a way the hourly figures conceal.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page, because a figure quoted without knowing the programme, the subject, the level and the frequency is a number rather than information. The trial lesson and the consultation are free, and the figures above are other providers' published rates. For budgeting context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.
