sections.heading: The slot that survives a term, and why Abu Hail station matters
paragraphs: There is one logistical feature of this catchment that genuinely changes the answer, and it is the Green Line. A student who travels to school by metro from a station near their school and walks home from Abu Hail arrives predictably, usually by around 3.30pm, with little week-to-week variance. That makes a 4.30pm session viable in a way it is not for a student travelling by car across the creek or from Mirdif in afternoon traffic.

For students who do travel by car the picture is different. A journey back from Al Garhoud or Dubai Festival City takes fifteen to thirty minutes depending on the day, and the variance rather than the average is the problem. A 5pm booking against a twenty-minute swing becomes a 5.20pm start often enough that the slot becomes unreliable across a term, and an unreliable slot is worse than a later one because the student stops planning around it.

The post-dinner slot at 7.30pm or 8pm is the most robust option in this district and the one that also fits working parents. Many parents in this catchment work in Deira and finish after 6pm, and being present for a session - or at least in the next room - matters more for a Middle Years student than for a Diploma one. The trade is alertness, which is why it suits Years 10 to 13 better than Years 7 and 8.

The weekend block is the piece most families here leave out. In apartment living with siblings and limited quiet space, a longer Saturday or Sunday morning session is frequently the only time a student can sit a full timed paper and review it in the same sitting. Without that there is no diagnosis, only an impression, and the whole value of a block depends on being able to compare a paper at the end against one at the start.

sections.heading: Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the line that protects the student
paragraphs: Internal assessments carry a fifth of the grade in most Diploma subjects, and with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay they are where the honesty question is sharpest - long independent pieces, produced under deadlines, by seventeen-year-olds with five other subjects making demands. The boundary is clear and worth fixing in mind before any pressure arrives.

A tutor may teach content, explain what each criterion rewards, interrogate a research question, model a technique on different material, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not produce the work. The research, the data, the argument and the words have to be the student's own, and the school authenticates that. If the authentication is untrue, the sanction falls on the candidate rather than on whoever helped or was paid, which is the asymmetry that matters.

One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price. The seller keeps the fee, the candidate carries the entire risk, and no part of that transaction improves the student's position if it is detected. Recognising it for what it is matters more than any rule, because the rule is enforced in one direction only. The same applies to offers described as editing or polishing when they go beyond clarity.

Materials follow the same principle. We reference IB subject guides, past papers and mark schemes, cite them and point to the official source rather than reproducing them, because they are the board's copyright and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. We also publish no IB session or results dates on these pages, because ibo.org blocks automated access and nothing in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself - the May session is the one UAE schools sit, and exact dates come from the school's Diploma coordinator.

sections.heading: The permit, and the claim nobody should make
paragraphs: There is one thing about any tutor that a parent in Hor Al Anz can verify with a single question, and almost nobody asks it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system, and it lists no fees alongside a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published anywhere official, so any figure quoted to you as the penalty - including those circulating in parent groups - should be treated as unverified.

Anyone telling you private tutoring in Dubai is unregulated, or that a permit is optional, is wrong, and that is a useful signal about everything else they say. The opposite error is equally telling: a tutoring service claiming regulator endorsement is describing something specific. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises - initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. A platform without premises does not hold one and should not imply it.

There is a related point about who teaches. Abu Dhabi's ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct barring the same arrangement. Those are press-reported positions and should be verified against the current policy document, but the principle travels across the UAE: engaging your child's own classroom teacher privately is the arrangement most likely to put that teacher in breach, however convenient it looks from an apartment block five minutes from the school.

Paying your child's own classroom teacher privately risks breaching a code of conduct

sections.heading: Five regulators, and why two of them matter in Deira
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. For a family in Hor Al Anz the rest of the regulator map is not background: the Sharjah boundary is a short drive, and some households in this district have children at schools under a different authority from their neighbours.

In Abu Dhabi, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. In Sharjah, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education; in Ras Al Khaimah, the Department of Knowledge does the same. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies are the complete map, and ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched in this market.

The Sharjah distinction is substantive rather than administrative. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum and fee approval, not merely inspection outcomes, sits with the emirate regulator. A family here with one child at a Dubai school and another across the boundary is dealing with two approval frameworks and two sets of published reports.

Within Dubai, the mandatory UAE subjects apply regardless of the licensed curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated against a forty-minute lesson unit; separate classes are required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; and additional or different content in those subjects needs prior permission from the Ministry of Education, which constrains what any tutor may legitimately offer in them.

process.title: Name the programme, subject and level
process.description: Middle Years or Diploma, the subject, and Higher or Standard. Those three together are a specification; any two of them is a guess, and a request without the level comes back with a question rather than a tutor.

process.title: Ask about coverage before anything else
process.description: We will tell you whether that combination is well covered, thin, or unavailable at your preferred hour, and roughly how long a match takes. Ask every provider the same question - the answers, and the willingness to answer, are both informative.

process.title: Send a marked script
process.description: A marked paper distinguishes content gaps from unwritten method, misread command terms and running out of time. A predicted grade distinguishes none of them, and the four need different first sessions.

process.title: Use the free trial to run the three tests
process.description: Paper weightings, internal assessment criteria by name and marks, and interpretation of the marked script. Ten minutes of that tells you more than a credential list, and nothing has to be unwound if the answers are vague.

process.title: Choose the slot by arrival reliability
process.description: A Green Line walk home from Abu Hail makes 4.30pm viable. A car journey from Al Garhoud varies by twenty minutes and breaks a 5pm slot. We will usually recommend the slot that depends on nothing.

process.title: Book a weekend block for diagnosis
process.description: In apartment living with siblings, a longer weekend morning session is often the only time a full timed paper can be sat and reviewed in one sitting - and without that there is no measurement, only an impression.

whyPoints.title: The comparison answered, not dodged
whyPoints.description: We set out what genuinely differs between Hor Al Anz, Al Mamzar, Abu Hail and Al Qusais - parking, journeys, metro access - and then explain why the IB answer is the same from all four.

whyPoints.title: No minutes lost at the door
whyPoints.description: A sixty-minute visit to a dense Deira address delivers forty-five to fifty teaching minutes after street parking and settling. Online sessions start on time, which changes the effective rate by a fifth before anything is cancelled.

whyPoints.title: Specified by programme, subject and level
whyPoints.description: Higher Level adds depth woven through the content, so a Standard Level tutor may not scale up. The booking records the level because that is where approximate matches fail in week three.

whyPoints.title: Core components treated as distinct roles
whyPoints.description: Extended Essay supervision and Theory of Knowledge are not add-ons to a subject tutor's job. We say which we can cover and point to the school supervisor as the primary route for the essay.

whyPoints.title: Honest about where local wins
whyPoints.description: For Arabic as a first language and for primary-stage support, local supply in this district is deep and well priced. We name those cases rather than arguing against every nearby alternative.

whyPoints.title: Two siblings, one evening, no second visit
whyPoints.description: Multi-child households are the norm here and apartment living makes a second visitor disruptive. Back-to-back online sessions with different specialists cost nobody any travel.

faqs.question: Does a family in Al Qusais have an easier time finding an IB tutor than we do in Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: On parking and roads, yes - Al Qusais is the easiest of these four districts for a driver, and a visiting tutor loses five to ten minutes there against ten to fifteen on a Hor Al Anz street. On the actual question, no. IB programmes are about 7 per cent of Dubai's enrolment and concentrate away from Deira entirely, so the number of Higher Level specialists within reach is the same small number from either address. The parking advantage does not create tutors.

faqs.question: Will you send a tutor to our building in Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Hor Al Anz, in Dubai, or anywhere else in the UAE - a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In-home tutoring does exist in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and in a dense district the visit also costs ten to fifteen teaching minutes at the door.

faqs.question: How much of a paid hour does a visiting tutor actually teach on these streets?
faqs.answer: Forty-five to fifty minutes is realistic in Hor Al Anz, once street parking and settling are counted, and sometimes less in Deira proper. Al Qusais is better at around fifty-five. That moves the effective rate up by a fifth or more against the published figure of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, before any session is cancelled outright. Cancellations in this district fall disproportionately on appointments that depend on somebody else's drive and somebody else's parking space.

faqs.question: Which schools near Hor Al Anz actually run IB programmes?
faqs.answer: None in the district itself. The nearest provision is in Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City, roughly fifteen to thirty minutes away depending on the hour, with further IB continuum provision east in Mirdif. Everything else is a longer run towards Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim, which is where most of the city's IB schools and IB-experienced teachers sit. Check programme authorisation on KHDA's own site rather than on reputation, because it changes between intakes.

faqs.question: Is there any case where the local option beats an online specialist for us?
faqs.answer: Two, and we would rather name them than argue against every alternative. Arabic as a first language: demand for that pathway is above the city average in this district and local supply is genuinely deep. And primary-stage support, where IB-specific expertise is not what is needed - the Primary Years Programme has no subject syllabus, and literacy, numeracy fluency and research habits are what actually help. In both cases a nearby tutor is often the better choice.

faqs.question: What exactly should I say when asking for an IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Three things: the programme, the subject and the level. Middle Years sciences, Standard Level Biology and Higher Level Chemistry are three different people, and only two of them are even in the same programme. Level matters more than families expect, because Higher Level adds depth woven through the content rather than a block at the end - so a tutor who has taught Standard Level thoroughly may be unable to handle the extension, and will discover that in week three.

faqs.question: Can one tutor support a Diploma student across all six subjects?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody can. The Diploma is six subjects from different groups at two levels plus three core components, each with its own assessment structure - the sciences investigation criteria, two separate mathematics courses, the English individual oral, a form of argument unique to Theory of Knowledge. What one person can usefully cover is the layer underneath: workload planning, criteria literacy, backwards planning from internal deadlines, revising against weightings. For a student who is drowning rather than failing, that is often the right purchase.

faqs.question: Does the metro make any real difference to tutoring here?
faqs.answer: It makes the single biggest practical difference in this catchment. A student who travels to school by metro and walks home from Abu Hail arrives predictably, usually by around 3.30pm, with little week-to-week variance, which makes a 4.30pm session genuinely viable. A student travelling by car from Al Garhoud faces a twenty-minute swing, which turns a 5pm booking into an unreliable one across a term. Reliability matters more than the hour itself, because an unreliable slot stops being planned around.

faqs.question: How do we fit two children's sessions into an apartment on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Back to back, online, which is the arrangement most multi-child households in this district end up with. Two sessions at 6.30pm and 7.45pm with different specialists if the subjects differ, no second visitor to admit or park, and no travel for anybody. The practical requirement is a quiet corner and headphones rather than two separate rooms. In-home visits for two children mean the travel component is paid twice and two arrival problems instead of one.

faqs.question: Why is Extended Essay help so hard to find at any price?
faqs.answer: Because supervising an essay is a different skill from teaching the subject it sits in, and far fewer people have it. The work is about question viability, scope, methodology and the assessment criteria rather than about content. The school supervisor is the primary route and should remain so. What an outside tutor adds is interrogating whether the research question can actually be answered within the word limit and the resources available, and commenting on a draft the student has written - never producing text.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at an internal assessment the week before a school deadline?
faqs.answer: Only to a limited and legitimate extent, and we say so rather than taking a larger booking. Most internal assessment marks are decided at the design and planning stage - whether the question is answerable, whether the data supports analysis, whether reflection was written as the work developed. A week out, what remains is checking the student's own work for clarity against the published criteria. Anything beyond that crosses into producing assessed work, and the risk of that falls entirely on the candidate.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor is allowed to teach privately here?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule, so treat quoted penalty figures as unverified.

faqs.question: Our neighbour's child is at a Sharjah school. Does that change anything for them?
faqs.answer: It changes the framework around them. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than KHDA, and SPEA approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum and fee approval, not only inspection, sits with the emirate. Practically, border traffic makes an afternoon appointment unrealistic from here, which means an evening online session is effectively the only workable arrangement rather than merely the better one.

faqs.question: Suppose the Higher Level specialist we need is fully booked - what do you tell us?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting someone approximate. Some combinations are genuinely thin - Higher Level physics or chemistry at short notice, Applications and Interpretation Higher Level statistics, a Group 2 language other than English or Arabic, or Extended Essay supervision. When that happens you get three straight answers: how long a match realistically takes, whether a closely related specialist can cover part of the need, and whether the school's own department is the better route for now.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.closingHeading: Run the comparison, then set it aside
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.closingBody: The comparison between Hor Al Anz, Al Mamzar, Abu Hail and Al Qusais is worth running. The streets differ, the parking differs, the metro access differs, and a visiting tutor loses a different number of minutes at each door. Then set it aside, because none of it changes how few people in this city teach Higher Level Diploma subjects or supervise an Extended Essay properly. Tell us the programme, the subject and the level, send a marked script, and ask us the coverage question before you pay anything. We do not visit homes in the UAE, and we would rather explain the arithmetic than pretend the question was not asked.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-international-cit.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IB Diploma and Middle Years Programme subjects for students living in International City and the surrounding districts, with the deepest coverage in mathematics, the sciences, economics and English.

intro.heading: The monthly number, before anything else
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages in this market describe quality and avoid money. Three of the six leading pages publish no price at all, and two quote United States dollars, which is not a currency anyone in International City transacts in. So this page starts with the figure a family actually budgets against, which is monthly rather than hourly, and it names the source of every number.

Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget tutoring at AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-range at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are the brackets. Everything else on this page is about what sits inside them.

Working back to an hourly rate, the market divides cleanly. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one with travel included runs AED 180 to 500.

International City matters to this arithmetic in a specific way. There is no international school inside the district - children travel out to Al Warqa, Al Qusais, Mirdif, Silicon Oasis or Academic City - and an in-home tutor would therefore be crossing the city at the same time of day the family already does. That travel is paid for twice: once in the hourly premium of roughly AED 50 to 150, and once in the dead time around the session that no invoice shows.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and we say so here because the phrase in this page's title is what parents search rather than a promise to drive to Al Warsan. What we do instead is one-to-one tuition over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the subject and the level. For a family in International City that removes the travel line from the bill entirely.

The rest of this page is about value rather than price. What a month at each budget genuinely buys. The four places tutoring money is most often wasted, which between them account for most of the complaints families have about tutoring in this emirate. And tutoring set against the other education costs a household here carries, including the fee position KHDA confirmed in May 2026.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-international-cit.programmesIntro: What a programme costs to support differs more than families expect, because the work is different at each stage rather than merely harder.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations and no marks on the report, which makes it the stage where tutoring is most often bought on anxiety rather than on evidence. The two things worth paying for are number fluency to automatic recall and structured writing. Both are cheap now and expensive later, and neither needs a specialist rate.
programmes.countryNote: For an International City family the sensible PYP purchase is short and specific: a term of weekly sessions on one skill at the lower end of the market, not an open arrangement. At AED 45 to 150 an hour this is genuinely affordable, and it is the one stage where the budget band contains perfectly adequate help.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Graded 1 to 8 against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. Tutoring is most efficient when it targets the single weak criterion rather than the subject, and the criterion breakdown from the school is what makes that possible. Mid-band rates are appropriate here; specialist rates usually are not.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP is where a modest monthly budget goes furthest, because a term aimed at one named criterion often moves a grade. Families in International City who ask the school for the four criterion marks before buying anything routinely spend less and get more, because they stop paying for general support across three subjects.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored out of 45. Each subject carries an internally marked, externally moderated assessment. This is where specialist rates become genuinely necessary, particularly at Higher Level, and where the budget band stops containing usable help.
programmes.countryNote: The honest arithmetic for a Diploma family here: one Higher Level subject at one session a week, at mid to specialist rates, is roughly AED 600 to 2,000 a month depending on the tutor. Two subjects doubles it. Which is why the diagnostic matters, because most students need one subject supported properly rather than three supported thinly.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: TOK, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together carry up to three Diploma points. Support for both is naturally finite - four to eight sessions timed to the school's deadlines - which makes it one of the few tutoring purchases with a defined end and a predictable total cost.
programmes.countryNote: Core support is the best-value block most Diploma families in this cluster buy, because three points matter at the margin of a university offer and the work is bounded. The thing to refuse is anybody offering to write it. One operator in these search results sells completed assessments outright, and the consequence of that falls on the candidate.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-international-cit.subjectsIntro: Where the money goes differs by subject, because some problems take six sessions and others take two years. These are the requests we see from this district.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, calculus and proof. Most lost marks are method rather than understanding - working omitted, rounding applied early - which means a well-targeted six to eight sessions often moves a grade. One of the better returns in the subject list.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use. The failure is interpretive: a correct regression line with nothing said about what the gradient means. Teachable as a writing habit, which again makes it responsive to a short block rather than a long arrangement.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics, equilibrium and acid-base work. Mole calculations underpin all of it, and a student weak there loses marks across the whole paper. Six to eight sessions of stoichiometry drilling is the highest-value chemistry purchase available.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty handling and graph linearisation account for a large share of recoverable marks and are rarely taught as lessons. Content gaps at Higher Level take months rather than weeks, which is the distinction a diagnosis should establish before you commit a budget.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty, with command terms deciding the grade. 'Outline' and 'explain' carry different allocations and students answer both as 'describe'. A fortnight of deliberate practice here is worth more than a term of re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams must be titled, labelled and referenced in the prose to score; HL adds a calculation-heavy paper. The internal assessment is three 800-word commentaries, and the marks sit in evaluation rather than theory, which is coachable in a short block.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Applied toolkit work on stimulus material, with higher bands requiring a justified judgement rather than a balanced list. HL candidates sit an additional paper on pre-released stimulus material issued ahead of the session.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen non-literary analysis, a comparative essay, the Individual Oral and, at HL, an essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. The Individual Oral is where a few sessions change an outcome, usually by narrowing a global issue that was pitched far too broadly.

subjects.name: Mathematics bridging from MYP 5
subjects.description: Indices, surds, algebraic fractions, function notation and basic differentiation, all assumed automatic from the first Diploma week. Six to eight summer sessions at mid-band rates, and the cheapest genuinely useful purchase in the whole programme.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The DP1 exhibition and the 1,600-word DP2 essay. Bounded work with a defined end, which makes the total cost predictable. Support is questioning on the student's own objects and drafts, never supplied argument.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Most failures are early and structural: a research question too broad for the word count, or no stated method. Four to six sessions at the question-setting stage prevents far more expensive remedial work later in the second Diploma year.

subjects.name: Internal assessment coaching across the sciences
subjects.description: Research design, variable control, uncertainty propagation and the evaluation section, all on the student's own data. Worth roughly a fifth of each science grade, and a finite block rather than an open commitment.

sections.heading: What each monthly budget actually buys
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutoring is sold and monthly totals are how it is paid for, so the useful table is the second one. The brackets below come from Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions and from packages providers in this market publish, all read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram rate; ours is quoted after the free trial against the work the diagnosis identifies.

The thing worth noticing is not the price but the ceiling on each band. At the lowest band you are generally buying a university student or a general secondary tutor, which is entirely adequate for Primary Years number work and for Middle Years content support, and is rarely adequate for a Diploma Higher Level subject. Paying specialist rates for a generalist is the most common expensive mistake in this market; paying budget rates for Higher Level physics is the second.

The second thing worth noticing is that the step from one session a week to two does not double the benefit, although it does double the bill. A second session is worth buying in two situations: a genuinely missing topic that needs rebuilding over months, or the final weeks before a session when timed practice is the whole activity. Outside those, a single well-targeted session plus homework the student actually does outperforms two sessions of passive attendance.

The third is that the cheapest effective purchase in the entire programme is often the smallest: six to eight bridging sessions between the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma, bought in a summer when nothing is urgent. Families in this district who buy that spend less across the two Diploma years than families who react to a first-term report.

sections.heading: The four places tutoring money gets wasted
paragraphs: Across enquiries from this part of Dubai, the same four patterns account for most of the money families regret spending. None of them is fraud. All of them are avoidable with one question asked before the first session, and together they probably waste more than the entire difference between the budget and specialist bands.

The first is buying three subjects when the problem is one. A student with a disappointing science report usually has one of the three sciences carrying the problem, and one timed paper in each identifies which. The second is paying a specialist rate for a generalist, which happens most often in the fortnight after mock results, when demand peaks and the specialists are fully committed.

The third is a rota of tutors rather than one. Each new tutor restarts the diagnosis, which means a family pays two or three sessions of exploratory work several times over. The fourth is sessions with no homework between them: a weekly hour in which the tutor explains and the student watches is roughly a third as useful as one followed by work the student does alone, and it costs exactly the same.

The table below sets each pattern against what it costs and what to do instead. The common thread is that all four are diagnosis failures rather than teaching failures, which is why we run a free trial lesson and send a written note afterwards rather than quoting a package first.

sections.heading: Tutoring set against the other education costs here
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely the only education line in a household budget, and it helps to see it beside the others. The most useful anchor is the fee position: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family planning tutoring, that is one cost that is not moving.

Dubai's private school sector is also expanding, which matters for families in this district who travel for school. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 with enrolment up 6%. More places nearer home would change the travel arithmetic on this page considerably.

Against that, the tutoring numbers look small per month and substantial over two years. One Diploma subject at one session a week for the two Diploma years, at the mid band, is a four-figure annual commitment; at the specialist band it is more. That is the figure worth comparing against a school move, a different subject choice, or simply doing nothing and letting the school's own support run its course.

The honest point is that tutoring is not always the right purchase. A student who is not doing the work set by the school will not be rescued by more teaching, and a student whose difficulty is organisational rather than academic needs a different intervention. The diagnostic session exists partly to establish which of those situations you are in, and we would rather say so than take the booking.

sections.heading: What the travel premium costs a family in this district specifically
paragraphs: In-home rates in Dubai carry a travel premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour. That is not a markup for its own sake - a tutor crossing the city at five in the afternoon spends well over an hour unpaid to deliver sixty paid minutes, and the rate has to reflect it. The question is what that money buys for a household in the clusters around Dragon Mart.

It buys presence in the room, which some students genuinely need and most do not. It does not buy subject depth. And from International City it buys a longer journey than from almost anywhere else in this part of Dubai, because the district sits off the main school corridors: the schools its children attend are in Al Warqa, Al Qusais, Mirdif, Silicon Oasis and Academic City, and a tutor coming to the home is travelling against the same traffic the family already fights twice a day.

There is a second, quieter cost. An in-home session consumes household time either side of the lesson - the arrival, the settling, the leaving - and in a flat with other children that is real. An online session starts when the laptop opens. Over a Diploma year at two sessions a week, the difference in household time is measured in days rather than hours.

The budgetary consequence is simple. The same monthly figure buys more sessions online, or the same number of sessions with a better-matched tutor, or a specialist in a subject where no local specialist exists. For a family in this district that last option is the one that actually changes an outcome, because the pool of Diploma Higher Level tutors living within reach of Al Warsan is close to empty.

sections.heading: Where the money is genuinely well spent
paragraphs: Having been sceptical about four kinds of spending, it is worth naming the purchases that reliably repay themselves. The first is the bridging block between the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma: six to eight sessions in a summer on indices, surds, algebraic fractions, function notation and timed essay structure. Nothing is urgent, rates are at their most negotiable, and the effect runs across two years of Diploma teaching.

The second is method work in mathematics and the sciences. Working shown, rounding controlled, command terms answered as asked, units checked, long questions attempted rather than abandoned. Most lost marks at both Middle Years and Diploma level are habits rather than gaps, and habits change in weeks. A six-session block aimed at a student's three recurring errors is the best value in the entire market.

The third is core support in the Diploma: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together carry up to three points, the work is bounded, and three points matter at the margin of a university offer. The fourth is a single diagnostic engagement in a subject where you genuinely cannot tell whether there is a problem - one timed paper, marked properly, with a written note.

What those four have in common is a defined end. Open-ended weekly arrangements across several subjects are where tutoring budgets disappear without anybody being able to say what changed. Bounded purchases with a stated aim are where the money does something, and they are easier to evaluate afterwards, which is the point.

sections.heading: What a parent should ask before paying anything
paragraphs: Five questions eliminate most of the bad outcomes in this market, and any provider worth hiring answers all five without hesitation. They are deliberately about money and accountability rather than about teaching philosophy, because the teaching is not usually where things go wrong.

First: does the individual teaching my child hold a current MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it? Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated - the permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted at you.

Second: is the quoted figure per hour or per session, and does it include VAT? Third: which subject and level have you taught, and for how many cohorts? Fourth: what is the replacement policy if the match fails, and who decides it has failed? Fifth: exactly what will you do with an internal assessment, and what will you refuse to do?

On that last point we are explicit because the search results this page sits in include an operator selling completed assessments at a published price. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Anything else is malpractice, and the finding falls on the candidate. We also state what we are not: no UAE office or centre, no KHDA Educational Services Permit, no approval or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, no guaranteed grades and no star ratings we cannot evidence.

sections.heading: Coverage, and the limit we publish rather than hide
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses what it cannot staff, and several conceal non-local delivery behind a phone number. We publish the limit instead, because the alternative is a family paying specialist rates for a generalist and finding out in week three - which is one of the four wasted-money patterns above.

The pattern is consistent. Mathematics in both courses, the sciences at Standard Level, Economics, Business Management and English are generally available within days. Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level take longer, particularly in the fortnight either side of mock examinations when demand across the emirate concentrates. Less commonly taught Group 2 languages take two weeks or more. Further Mathematics, Music and Film we often cannot staff at all.

When we cannot cover something properly there are three honest responses and we use all three: give a realistic wait, offer adjacent-subject support with the boundary stated plainly, or decline. The one thing we will not do is put a Standard Level tutor in front of a Higher Level candidate and let a pleasant trial lesson carry the arrangement, because that is exactly how a budget gets wasted.

On delivery, to be unambiguous: every IB Gram lesson for a family in International City is one-to-one and online, on Gulf Standard Time. No tutor travels to an address in this district or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer in India only, and the reason this page targets the phrase is that it is what parents type, not that it describes what we do.

sections.heading: The Diploma calendar, and why timing is a cost question
paragraphs: Timing affects price indirectly but substantially, because availability is what actually varies through the year. UAE schools sit the May examination session, and demand for Diploma tutoring in Dubai peaks twice: once after mock results and once in the final weeks. In those windows the specialists are committed, and a family booking then pays the same rate for a less suitable tutor.

The crowded point in the Diploma is the January and February window of the second year, when internal assessments across four or five subjects, the Extended Essay final submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the school's mock examinations all land within a few weeks. Booking core support during the first year rather than reacting in that window is both cheaper in total and more likely to get the right person.

We publish no specific IB session or results dates on this site. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a wrong date on a page a family plans around is worse than no date, so confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the dates are sourced: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November.

Ramadan is the other scheduling fact with a budget consequence in this district. School days shorten, late-afternoon concentration is poor, and a session booked at four during the month is often money spent on an hour nobody benefits from. Weekend mornings and post-Iftar slots work. Because no tutor is travelling, moving the pattern costs nothing but needs deciding before the month starts.

process.description: Short written reviews every few weeks against the school's own marking. If the match has failed we reassign rather than defend it, and we do not rotate tutors as a matter of course, because each new tutor re-bills the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor in International City?
faqs.answer: You can get one-to-one IB tutoring for a child living in International City, and with IB Gram it is delivered live online rather than by a tutor coming to your flat. Home visits are a service we offer in India only. The Dubai market does include tutors who travel, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with published monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. From this district that premium buys a long journey rather than a better tutor.

faqs.question: What does IB tutoring actually cost per month for a family here?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget tutoring at AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-range at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are market figures from the sources named, read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices - ours is quoted after the free trial lesson against the work the diagnosis identifies.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest tutoring band ever worth using?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right work. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from 33 to 52, and that band contains perfectly adequate help for Primary Years number and writing work and for Middle Years content support. Where it falls short is Diploma Higher Level teaching and internal assessment coaching. Paying budget rates for Higher Level physics is as wasteful as paying specialist rates for a generalist.

faqs.question: Is a second weekly session worth double the monthly cost?
faqs.answer: One, in most situations. A second session doubles the bill and does not double the benefit, because the limiting factor is usually the work the student does between sessions rather than the teaching time. Two sessions a week earn their cost in two cases: a genuinely missing topic that needs rebuilding over months, and the final weeks before an examination session when timed practice is the whole activity. Outside those, one well-targeted session plus homework outperforms two passive hours.

faqs.question: Why do families here end up paying for three tutors?
faqs.answer: Because a disappointing report names a subject area rather than a subject, and nobody runs the diagnosis. A student with weak science results usually has one of the three sciences carrying the problem, and one timed paper in each identifies which within a single session. The same applies across a Diploma profile. It is the single most expensive avoidable mistake in this market, and it is why we mark papers before quoting rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: What is the travel premium on an in-home tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour, comparing the in-home band of AED 180 to 500 with the online qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300. It is not a markup for its own sake: a tutor crossing the city at five in the afternoon spends well over an unpaid hour to deliver sixty paid minutes. What it buys is presence in the room. It does not buy subject depth, and from International City it buys the longest journey in this part of Dubai.

faqs.question: Which schools do children from the clusters around Dragon Mart attend?
faqs.answer: No international school sits inside International City, so children travel out. The nearest substantial provision is in Al Warqa and Al Qusais, including Universal American School on IB programmes, GEMS Our Own English High School, The Millennium School Dubai and Apple International School. Diploma students more often travel to GEMS Wellington Academy in Silicon Oasis or further to Uptown International School in Mirdif. Those schools are named as local context; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: What time can a session start on a weekday from International City?
faqs.answer: Around six, honestly. Children here travel out to Al Warqa, Al Qusais, Silicon Oasis, Academic City or Mirdif, and in several clusters the school bus rather than a family car sets the return time. Weekend mornings are the better slot for anything demanding - a full timed paper cannot be sat properly at seven in the evening - so one weekday session plus a weekend morning usually works better here than two weekday evenings.

faqs.question: Is there a cheaper way to get Extended Essay or internal assessment help?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a shape rather than a discount. Core and internal assessment support is naturally finite: four to eight sessions timed to the school's deadlines, with the session count agreed before the block starts, so the total is known at the outset. That makes it the most controllable purchase in the programme for a household watching a monthly figure. What to refuse is anybody offering to write it, whatever the price, because the malpractice consequence falls on your child.

faqs.question: Are school fees going up in Dubai this year?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a household planning tutoring alongside fees, that is one line that is not moving. Dubai's 2026-27 intake also adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time of year to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: The rate does not change, but what you can buy with it does. Demand in Dubai peaks twice - after mock results and in the final weeks before the May session - and in those windows the specialists are fully committed, so a family booking then pays the same money for a less suitable tutor. Booking in the first term secures the right person at the same price. The genuinely cheapest useful purchase is the summer bridging block between the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma.

faqs.question: Does the price include VAT, and is it per hour or per session?
faqs.answer: Ask every provider this explicitly, including us, because the two framings are not comparable and some quotes mix them. We publish our own figure after the free trial lesson, against the specific subject, level and session length, and we state plainly whether VAT is included. What we will not do is state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition generally, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation we are not in a position to give on a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Is tutoring always the right thing to spend the money on?
faqs.answer: No, and the diagnostic session exists partly to establish that. A student who is not completing the work the school already sets will not be rescued by more teaching, and a difficulty that is organisational rather than academic needs a different intervention entirely - often a conversation with the school rather than a purchase. We would rather say that after the trial lesson than take a booking, because a tutoring arrangement that cannot work is worse value than no arrangement at all.

faqs.question: Must a tutor working privately in Dubai hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so no tutor can legitimately price it into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted at you as unverified. Ask the person teaching your child whether they hold a current permit and ask to see it.

faqs.question: What happens to our money if the tutor is the wrong fit?
faqs.answer: The free trial lesson exists so that decision is made before anything is paid. If a mismatch surfaces later we reassign rather than defend the original match, because a tutor the student has stopped talking to is teaching nothing at full price. What we will not do is rotate tutors as a matter of routine: each new tutor restarts the diagnosis, which means paying two or three sessions of exploratory work over again every time.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jbr.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects at the levels JBR students are sitting this year. Each profile names the subject, the level and the papers that tutor works on most, so you can read the match before you book the trial lesson rather than after it.

intro.heading: The JBR school run is the real constraint, not the subject
paragraphs: Jumeirah Beach Residence is a strip of roughly forty towers between the beach and King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street, with Bluewaters Island across a short bridge and the Dubai Tram running the length of it. What JBR does not have is a private secondary school inside it. Every Diploma student living in these towers commutes out of the community in the morning and back into it in the afternoon, which is why a parent typing "IB home tutor in JBR" is almost never asking a question about teaching quality. They are asking a question about time.

Work the timings through and the shape of the problem appears. Secondary school days in Dubai mostly finish between 14:30 and 15:15. A school bus from Al Barsha South into JBR in afternoon traffic takes between thirty-five and fifty-five minutes once it has dropped the rest of its route. A car coming north on Sheikh Zayed Road from Umm Suqeim after 15:30 is unpredictable in a way that no tutoring schedule survives. The practical consequence is that a JBR student is rarely at a desk, fed and settled, before 16:00, and in exam term is often not settled before 16:30.

That single fact does more damage to in-home tutoring in this neighbourhood than price does. A tutor driving to a JBR tower has to arrive after the student, find visitor parking in a basement designed for residents, clear a security desk, and share a lift bank at the busiest hour of the building's day. Thirty minutes of billable time can disappear before anyone opens a textbook, and the tutor has to be out again in time to reach their next booking, which is why in-home sessions in this area tend to be sold in two-hour blocks the student is too tired to use well.

IB Gram answers the same search differently. Tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. There is no home-visit option here: home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. What that buys a JBR family is the thing the commute took away. The session starts at the minute it was booked, because nobody has to arrive. A sixty-minute slot at 16:15 is sixty minutes of teaching. And the tutor is chosen because they teach Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, not because they happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of the Walk.

This page is written around the school run on purpose. It sets out which school clusters JBR children travel to, what time each cluster releases them, when a weekly session can honestly start, how online compares with an in-home visit on cost and on lost time, what the Dubai market charges, and how the Diploma year looks counted backwards from the May examination session. Where a figure appears, its source is named. Where something cannot be verified, the page says so instead of guessing.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jbr.programmesIntro: JBR households are mixed: Diploma students in Years 12 and 13, Middle Years students at the same schools, and a steady flow of families arriving mid-cycle from British or American systems. These are the three programmes that come up most on this stretch of coast, with what each one does to a weekday evening.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessments in every subject run on school deadlines that cluster in the same two months, which is what turns a manageable DP1 into a difficult DP2. Tutoring here is usually one or two subjects deep rather than broad: the Higher Level that is dragging the predicted total down.
programmes.countryNote: For a JBR family the Diploma's problem is scheduling, not content. Two Higher Level subjects needing weekly support means two fixed slots a week after a commute that already eats ninety minutes. Online slots at 16:30 and 18:00 on different evenings work; two in-home visits in one week rarely survive a month of Dubai traffic.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 0-8, with no public examination unless the school enters students for eAssessment. Parents often misread an MYP report because a criterion score is not a percentage. The useful tutoring work in MYP 4 and 5 is criterion literacy plus the algebra and scientific writing that the Diploma will assume from day one.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in JBR finish school earlier than their Diploma siblings and get home with more of the afternoon left, so a 16:00 slot is genuinely available to them. Families with one child in each programme usually stack the MYP session first and the DP session after dinner.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, with reading, number fluency and written expression carried underneath. Support at this stage is short and frequent: thirty to forty-five minutes, twice a week, on one specific thing such as number bonds, fraction sense or sentence structure, not a general hour of catch-up.
programmes.countryNote: Several JBR towers have nurseries at ground level, but primary-age children still travel to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah. Short online sessions suit them because a tired seven-year-old will give a focused thirty minutes at 16:00 and nothing useful at 18:00.

programmes.name: Diploma core: EE, TOK and the IAs
programmes.description: The Extended Essay runs to a 4,000-word limit and the Theory of Knowledge essay to 1,600 words, both assessed against published criteria rather than against a syllabus. These components fail on process far more often than on knowledge: a research question that cannot be answered in the word count, or a reflection written the night before the deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Process coaching is where this work belongs, and it belongs in writing. A tutor reads what the student has written, points at the criterion the paragraph is missing, and hands it back. IB Gram tutors do not write, draft or complete any part of an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or internal assessment.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jbr.subjectsIntro: Requests from this neighbourhood skew towards the Higher Levels that gate university applications and towards the subjects where a school's teaching group is large. These are the subjects JBR families ask about most, with what the assessment actually rewards and where marks tend to go missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where most of the damage happens: students who can get an answer from a graphing screen cannot always reach it by hand. Proof, complex numbers and the algebra of integration are the HL pressure points. The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, with six of those marks for the mathematics itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, with statistics, modelling and interpretation carrying the weight. Marks are lost in the words rather than the working: a correct regression with no comment on what the gradient means in context scores poorly. HL adds matrices, graph theory and a far heavier statistical load than most students expect from the easier-sounding route.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The syllabus rewards precision about definitions and about what a graph gradient physically represents. Circular motion, fields and the HL-only sections on induction and quantum phenomena are the reliable trouble spots. Data-analysis questions need uncertainty handled properly, and that skill transfers straight into the internal assessment, which is worth 20 per cent of the grade.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics separate a 5 from a 7, because both demand that a student explains rather than recalls. Multi-step calculations lose marks on units and significant figures rather than on method. The internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to generate real data in a school laboratory within the time the school allows.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms do the work here. "Outline", "explain" and "discuss" ask for different amounts of writing, and students who answer every question at the same length leave marks everywhere. HL depth on nucleic acids, metabolism and plant biology is examinable detail, not background, and the statistical treatment in the internal assessment is marked as carefully as the biology.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the fastest available gain: an axis mislabelled, a shift drawn in the wrong direction, an equilibrium not marked. Paper 2 requires data response written with evaluation attached, and HL Paper 3 is quantitative in a way the textbook chapters do not advertise. The portfolio of commentaries is assessed on published criteria and is the student's own work.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure, and most students lose marks by summarising a text instead of analysing how it works. The Individual Oral requires a global issue linked to two specified extracts, and the HL essay runs to 1,200-1,500 words. Preparation is about building a repeatable analytical move, not about reading more.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as Ansoff, SWOT and break-even analysis are easy to name and hard to apply to an unfamiliar case study, which is exactly what the papers ask for. Higher Level adds the pre-released case study with its own research demands. Quantitative questions on ratios and cash flow are frequently the difference between a 4 and a 6.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode under examination conditions is a distinct skill from writing code in an editor, and the paper tests tracing and dry-running as much as design. HL abstract data structures, recursion and the case study carry heavy marks. The solution component is assessed on documented process, so the development record matters as much as the finished program.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Marked on a 1,600-word essay from a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. Students who write about knowledge in general score badly; the criteria reward precise argument about a specific claim with real examples. One hour a fortnight from October is usually enough if it starts early rather than in the last fortnight.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jbr.regionsTitle: JBR and the communities around it

regions.name: Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: Around forty towers on a single beachfront strip, served by two Dubai Tram stops and the Walk. No private school inside the community, so every school-age child commutes out and back, which fixes the earliest session start at about 16:00.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Immediately inland across the tram line, with the same traffic pattern and a slightly earlier arrival home for families whose buses come down Al Khail Street rather than Sheikh Zayed Road. Marina and JBR households frequently share a bus route.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: Connected to JBR by a single bridge, which is the whole scheduling story: one incident on that bridge changes an afternoon. Online sessions are unaffected by it, which is why Bluewaters families book the same evening slots as JBR.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The nearest cluster of senior schools, fifteen to twenty-five minutes from JBR outside peak. Children from here get home earliest, so a 16:00 start is genuinely available rather than theoretical.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, on the Red Line between DMCC and Sobha Realty. Apartment living and shared study space mean background noise matters: headphones and a fixed corner make more difference to an online lesson here than bandwidth does.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Low-rise and closer to Al Barsha, with shorter bus routes and a 15:45 arrival home for many families. A 16:15 session works here on a school night without anyone being rushed.

regions.name: The Springs, The Meadows and The Lakes
regions.note: Villa communities inland on the far side of Sheikh Zayed Road. Longer bus routes with multiple drops push the realistic start to 16:30, and Friday mornings are the slot these families use for longer revision blocks.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Larger plots, longer driveways and a school run that often runs through Al Khail Street. Families here commonly run two children in different programmes, which makes two separate online slots easier to manage than one shared visit.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim - the short commute
schoolClusters.note: The closest senior schools to JBR and the ones whose buses reach the towers first. Students from this cluster are typically home by 15:30 to 15:45, which makes them the only JBR group for whom a 16:00 weekday session is comfortable rather than tight.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Dubai Science Park - the long bus
schoolClusters.note: A large share of JBR Diploma students travel to this cluster, and the return journey with multiple drops is the reason 16:30 and 17:00 slots exist. Families here benefit most from a session that starts the moment the student logs in.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills, Jumeirah Park and the villa belt
schoolClusters.note: Inland communities whose routes cross Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Khail Street twice a day. Arrival home is the least predictable of the three clusters, so these families most often choose a later fixed slot plus a weekend morning block in exam term.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in JBR is really asking
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in JBR, in the sense the phrase is normally meant, is a private tutor who drives to a tower in Jumeirah Beach Residence and teaches at the kitchen table. That service exists in Dubai and the market rate for it runs from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour depending on level and on whether travel is priced separately, according to the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table and the published from-rates of UAE agencies reviewed in October 2026. IB Gram does not sell it. Tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

Saying that plainly at the top of the page is more useful than burying it, because the two services solve different halves of the problem. An in-home visit solves supervision: an adult is physically present and a younger child cannot wander off. Online one-to-one solves specialism and time: the tutor is chosen for teaching Chemistry HL rather than for living nearby, and no part of the hour is spent on the drive, the visitor pass or the lift. For a Diploma student with a Higher Level problem and ninety minutes of commute already gone, the second trade is usually the better one.

The rest of this page treats the question seriously in both directions. It gives the honest numbers for what an in-home tutor costs in this area, the honest numbers for what the online market charges, and a side-by-side comparison of the two on the things that actually change a JBR evening. Then it gets specific about the school run, because the single most common reason tutoring stops in this neighbourhood is not price or quality. It is that the slot was set at a time the student was still on a bus.

sections.heading: The JBR school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: Dubai secondary school days mostly end between 14:30 and 15:15. What happens next depends entirely on which cluster the school sits in, and the spread is wide enough to make a single recommended session time useless. A student at a school in Al Sufouh can be home in JBR in fifteen to twenty-five minutes. A student on a bus route out of Al Barsha South, with four or five drops before the towers, can take fifty-five. The same child, same school, can be home at 15:35 one day and 16:20 the next, depending on Sheikh Zayed Road.

That variability is the argument for a later fixed start rather than an earlier optimistic one. A session booked for 15:45 is a session that will be fifteen minutes short most weeks and missed entirely some weeks, and after a month of that the family quietly stops. A session booked for 16:30 happens. It is worth asking your school's transport office for the actual drop time for your tower rather than the published arrival window, because the two often differ by twenty minutes once the route is loaded.

sections.heading: Why there is no IB school inside JBR, and what that changes
paragraphs: JBR was built as a residential and retail strip rather than as a master-planned family community with a school plot in the middle of it. There are nurseries at tower level, but no private secondary school stands inside the community, so the schooling map for a JBR teenager is drawn entirely outside it. That is unusual in Dubai, where villa communities such as The Springs or Jumeirah Park typically have a school within a few minutes of the gate, and it is the structural reason the tutoring question here is a logistics question.

It also means a JBR tower holds students from an unusually wide spread of schools and curricula. One lift bank can carry a Diploma student heading to Al Sufouh, a British Year 11 student going to Al Barsha and an American-curriculum student travelling to Jumeirah, which is why neighbour recommendations travel badly in this community. The tutor who was excellent for the child three floors up may teach a different programme at a different level for a different board.

For tutoring, the practical consequence is that matching has to be done on the specific syllabus and level rather than on proximity or reputation. Dubai had 227 private schools serving 387,441 students across seventeen different curricula in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate schools accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment according to the Dubai Media Office. In a neighbourhood with no school of its own, that diversity lands in the same building, and the only reliable filter is the syllabus code and level the student is actually sitting.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home tutor in JBR
paragraphs: The comparison most pages in this market avoid is the one a parent most needs, so here it is on the terms that matter in a tower block. The honest summary: an in-home visit costs more per useful minute in JBR than it does in a villa community, because the building adds friction a villa does not. Basement parking designed for residents, a visitor pass at the desk, and a shared lift at the hour everyone comes home all sit between the tutor arriving and the lesson starting.

The tutor pool is the second difference, and it is larger than most families expect. A tutor willing to drive to JBR for a single sixty-minute booking is drawn from whoever is both free and close, and that pool thins fast at the top of the Diploma. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, Chemistry HL and Economics HL specialists are not evenly distributed across Dubai neighbourhoods. Online, distance stops being a filter and the only question left is whether the tutor teaches the level your child is sitting.

None of this makes an in-home tutor a poor choice for every family. A primary-age child who needs an adult in the room, or a household with unreliable connectivity, is better served in person, and IB Gram will say so rather than sell around it. What this page will not do is promise a tutor at a JBR address. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai, and the comparison below is offered so the decision is made on evidence rather than on a phrase in a search box.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in this market, and what the rate buys
paragraphs: Three of the six ranking pages in this search publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The bands below are the market, not an IB Gram price list, and they come from published UAE agency from-rates and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, reviewed in October 2026. For what IB Gram itself charges, the trial lesson and the consultation are the route; the rate depends on the subject, the level and the number of sessions, so a single published figure would be misleading.

Read the bands alongside the school-fee context, because tutoring is a marginal cost on top of a large fixed one. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second phase of Dubai's economic incentives package. A family whose fees have held flat is usually making the tutoring decision against a known budget rather than a moving one, which is why the cost-per-grade question gets asked more sharply here than elsewhere.

The thing worth paying attention to is what sits inside the rate. A low hourly figure that excludes marking means a student does timed papers that nobody reads carefully, which is the most expensive saving available in DP2. A higher figure that includes marked scripts, written follow-up and contact with the school's deadline calendar is usually cheaper per grade point. Ask what happens between sessions before comparing two numbers that look different.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May examination session, and the useful way to plan tutoring is backwards from it rather than forwards from today. Working backwards reveals the two pinch points that catch JBR families out every year. The first is the window when internal assessments across several subjects reach final submission within a few weeks of each other, which arrives in DP2 term two. The second is the mock examination period, which is early enough that a student who starts revising afterwards has lost the diagnostic the mocks were for.

One caution on dates, stated here because other pages in this market get it wrong. The International Baccalaureate blocks automated retrieval of its calendar, so no specific IB session or results date is published on this page. Confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before planning around it. Cambridge and Pearson dates are a different matter and are published by the boards, with one correction worth stating plainly: in the UAE a Cambridge candidate sits the June series or the November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so any February timetable a parent finds online is for somewhere else. Cambridge June entries close in the spring, a term or more ahead of the first paper, and the exact day belongs on the statement of entry the centre issues. Pearson's published figures show the same gap without any guessing: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The shape below is therefore a rhythm rather than a calendar. It shows what the school is typically doing, what a JBR family should have in place by then, and roughly how many hours a week that implies. The point of publishing it is that no competitor page in this search names a session, a deadline or a results stage at all, and a parent choosing in October needs to know which of these windows they are already inside.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the boundary that gets students into real trouble, and it is worth stating precisely because at least one page ranking for these searches sells finished internal assessments outright. Under IB academic-honesty rules the work submitted must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion is asking for, ask the questions that expose a weak research question, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of that work.

In practice the line is easier to hold than it sounds, because the honest version is also the more useful one. If a tutor tells a student that criterion C is thin, the student has to go back into their own reasoning and fix it, and the thinking that produces is exactly what the examiner is marking. If a tutor supplies the paragraph instead, the student learns nothing, the writing does not sound like them, and a supervisor who knows the student's voice will notice.

The consequences are not theoretical. A finding of malpractice can cost a candidate the diploma, and it attaches to the student, not to whoever sold them the text. IB Gram tutors work on the student's own draft and nothing else, and will say no to a request to do otherwise. Separately, no tutor on this platform supplies IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those are the boards' copyright and are referenced and linked rather than reproduced.
