sections.heading: Ramadan, Gulf Standard Time and the weeks the schedule changes
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the UAE academic calendar breaks twice a year. During Ramadan, school days shorten and the whole rhythm of a JBR evening moves: a student who was settled at 16:30 in February may be better taught after Iftar in March, and a family fasting through the afternoon will get very little from a 17:00 session. Sessions move to post-Iftar slots for the month and move back afterwards, which is straightforward to arrange online and genuinely difficult to arrange with a tutor driving across Dubai at that hour.

Gulf Standard Time is the second scheduling fact, and it cuts both ways. A tutor based in the UAE shares the student's clock. A tutor in another time zone may be the right specialist for a niche Higher Level subject, and in that case the slot has to be chosen so neither party is teaching or learning at a stupid hour. IB Gram states the tutor's working hours in local time before the trial lesson rather than after the first missed session.

Travel is the third. JBR households travel more than most, between school holidays, summer out of the UAE and family commitments abroad. An online slot follows the student, which means a Diploma student in the submission cluster does not lose three weeks of momentum to a trip. Where a time difference makes the usual slot impossible, the sensible move is a shorter session at a different hour rather than a cancelled block, and that is agreed before the travel rather than during it.

sections.heading: If no specialist is free: the honest version
paragraphs: Availability transparency is missing from every competitor page examined in this cluster, so it belongs here. Some subject and level combinations are genuinely thin. Higher Level Computer Science, Higher Level Economics in the weeks before the session, Arabic as a first language and the less common second languages all run short of specialists at peak. When that happens, there are only three honest answers, and a page that implies otherwise is setting a family up for a bad match.

The first answer is a wait with a date attached: the right tutor has a slot in two weeks and it is worth waiting for. The second is a different format: a shorter session twice a week with a tutor who has fragments of availability rather than one long block that does not exist. The third is a redirect: the student does not need the subject specialist they asked for, they need the Mathematics underneath it, and that is a wider pool. Deciding which of the three applies is what the consultation is for.

What should not happen is a match made on availability alone, which is how a family ends up paying specialist rates for general help. If IB Gram cannot cover a combination to the standard the level needs, the right answer is to say so. A trial lesson exists so the match is tested before any commitment is made, and it takes no card details to book; if the fit is wrong, the honest outcome is a different tutor or no tutor rather than a term of sessions nobody believes in.

process.title: Tell us the school, the subjects and the bus
process.description: The useful first message names the school, the programme year, the two or three subjects causing trouble, and roughly what time your child is actually home in JBR. That last detail decides the slot, and getting it right at the start prevents the most common cause of tutoring quietly stopping in this neighbourhood.

process.title: We match on syllabus and level
process.description: Matching is done against the exact course and level your child is sitting, not against a general subject label. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL and Applications and Interpretation SL are different jobs. Where more than one tutor fits, the tie-breaker is the time slot that works for your commute.

process.title: Trial lesson first, no card required
process.description: The first session is a trial so the match is tested on real work rather than on a profile. It takes no card details to book. Your child brings the current topic or a returned paper, and you get a short written note afterwards on what the tutor found and what they would do over the first month.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot and keep it
process.description: Once the trial works, the slot is set for the same evening each week and held through the year, including exam term. A fixed appointment survives a Dubai term. A session rebooked weekly around other commitments tends to have disappeared by the time mock results arrive.

process.title: Review against the school's own calendar
process.description: Progress is reviewed against the deadlines your child's school actually set, not a generic plan: the internal assessment dates, the mock window, the predicted grade point. If a subject stabilises, the hours move to the one that has not, and if nothing is moving, that gets said rather than billed.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the commute, not to a driving route
whyPoints.description: Every slot on this page is built around when a JBR student is genuinely at a desk, which is later than most schedules assume. Starting at 16:30 with a settled student beats starting at 15:45 with one still on Sheikh Zayed Road, and the difference compounds across a term.

whyPoints.title: Matched on level, not on distance
whyPoints.description: A tutor is chosen for teaching the exact course and level your child sits. Removing distance from the filter is what makes Higher Level specialists available to a tower in JBR, where an in-home search is limited to whoever will drive over for a single booking.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to a published rate card or survey and dated October 2026, and no IB examination date is stated because the board blocks automated verification. Numbers without a source are the norm in this market and they are not useful to a parent.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty treated as a boundary
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, review and give feedback on work the student wrote. No internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is drafted, rewritten or completed for a candidate, and no board material is handed over as a download. That boundary protects the student's diploma.

whyPoints.title: Independent, with no school affiliation
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. Schools are named on this page as the places JBR students commute to, and nothing more is implied: there is no affiliation with, endorsement from or contract with any named school, group, regulator or examination board.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Where a subject and level combination is thin, you are told so with a date for availability rather than matched with whoever is free. A trial lesson tests the match before any commitment, and a wrong fit ends in a different tutor rather than a term of sessions.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who comes to my JBR tower?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video; home visits are a service offered only in India. Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do sell in-home visits, at market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel usually priced in. In a JBR tower that format loses time to basement parking, the security desk and the lift at the hour everyone arrives home. Online, the hour you book is the hour your child is taught, and the tutor is selected for teaching the level your child sits.

faqs.question: What time should a JBR session start on a school night?
faqs.answer: Between 16:00 and 17:00 for most families, depending on which cluster the school sits in. Children travelling from Al Sufouh are often home by 15:40 and can start at 16:00. Buses from Al Barsha South with several drops can arrive at 16:10, which makes 17:00 the realistic start. Ask your school's transport office for the actual drop time at your tower rather than the published route window, then book twenty minutes after it. A slot set at the optimistic time runs short most weeks and is abandoned by November.

faqs.question: Are there any IB schools inside JBR itself?
faqs.answer: No private secondary school sits inside Jumeirah Beach Residence. There are nurseries at tower level, but every school-age child in these towers commutes out of the community and back, most commonly to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Jumeirah or the villa communities inland. That is why neighbour recommendations travel poorly here: one lift bank can carry students from three different curricula at three different stages. Matching a tutor to the specific course and level a child is sitting matters more in JBR than in a community built around a single school.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma student in JBR usually need?
faqs.answer: One hour a week per struggling subject is the normal starting point, rising to two in the subject under most pressure during the internal assessment submission cluster and the final revision term. Families who start with four hours a week in October rarely sustain it past December, and the sessions that get dropped are not chosen carefully. Starting with one well-placed hour in the subject dragging the predicted total down, then adding only when the first subject stabilises, holds up far better across a Dubai school year.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow my child's own school deadlines?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the practical difference between useful support and generic tutoring. Internal assessment dates, the mock window and the school's own submission calendar vary between Dubai schools by several weeks, so a plan built on a generic timeline will be wrong for most students. Share the deadline sheet your school issued and the tutoring rhythm is built against it: criterion work before a submission, timed papers before mocks, and recall work rather than new content in the final weeks before the written session.

faqs.question: During Ramadan, does the JBR session time change?
faqs.answer: Yes. School days shorten during Ramadan and a fasting student gets very little from a late-afternoon session, so slots move to post-Iftar for the month and move back afterwards. This is simple to arrange when the lesson is online and genuinely difficult when a tutor has to drive across Dubai at that hour. Agreeing the Ramadan slot a fortnight in advance rather than in the first week avoids the gap that otherwise swallows two or three sessions at a point in the year when coursework deadlines are still moving.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring actually effective for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For Diploma-age students, yes, and the reason is specific rather than general. Most of what a DP tutor does is work on a shared document or a marked script: annotating a proof, rebuilding a graph, showing where a command term was answered at the wrong depth. A screen shows that work more clearly than a notebook between two people at a table. The format is weaker for very young children who need an adult physically present, and IB Gram will say so rather than sell an unsuitable fit.

faqs.question: What does IB Gram charge for an hour of IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: The rate depends on the subject, the level and how many sessions you book, so a single published figure would mislead more than it helps; the trial lesson and the consultation are where you get a real number. For context, the Dubai market in October 2026 runs at roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget online tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for qualified subject tutors online, and AED 200 to AED 450 or more for IB and IGCSE specialists, per published agency rate cards and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table.

faqs.question: Is a MoHRE permit required before a tutor teaches a JBR student?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a private tutor work permit from MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. People tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. MoHRE's own service page is the route to verify a permit.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the internal assessment itself?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the content behind it, explain what each criterion is asking for, challenge a research question that cannot be answered within the limits, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, draft, rewrite or complete any part of it. That line comes from IB academic-honesty rules, and crossing it risks the candidate's diploma rather than the tutor's business. Any service offering a finished internal assessment is selling the student a malpractice finding with the text attached.

faqs.question: Which schools do JBR students most often commute to?
faqs.answer: Three clusters cover most of this neighbourhood. Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim hold the closest senior schools and the shortest bus routes. Al Barsha and Dubai Science Park take a large share of JBR Diploma students on longer routes with multiple drops. The inland villa belt around Emirates Hills, Jumeirah Park and the Meadows accounts for the rest. Schools are named on this page only as context for the commute; IB Gram has no affiliation with or endorsement from any of them.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no tutor free for my child's subject in JBR?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date. Some combinations are genuinely thin, particularly Higher Level Computer Science, Arabic as a first language and the less common second languages close to the examination session. The three honest options are a short wait for the right tutor, a different format such as two shorter sessions instead of one long block, or a redirect to the underlying skill that is actually the problem. What should not happen is a match made on availability alone at specialist rates.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my child's subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single tutor covering Mathematics and Physics at the same level removes a slot from a crowded week. Pairings that work are usually within one discipline: the two Mathematics routes, Physics with Mathematics, Chemistry with Biology at Standard Level. Pairings across unrelated Higher Levels usually mean one subject gets a specialist and the other gets a generalist, which is the trade that produces a disappointing term. Two tutors on different evenings is normally the better answer.

faqs.question: How quickly can a JBR family start after the first enquiry?
faqs.answer: Most common subject and level combinations can be matched and trialled within a few days, because the constraint is the slot rather than the search. Niche Higher Levels and less common languages take longer, and in the weeks before the written session everything takes longer because the specialists with the right availability are already booked. If timing matters, the single most useful thing in a first message is the window your child is genuinely free in Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: What do you need from us to make the first session useful?
faqs.answer: Three things, none of them long. The school and the exact course title with level, so the match is made against the right syllabus. A recent piece of marked work, which tells a tutor more in two minutes than a description does in twenty. And the school's deadline sheet for internal assessments and mocks. With those, the trial lesson starts on real material instead of on introductions, and the written note you get afterwards is about your child rather than about tutoring in general.

intro.heading: What a Jebel Ali parent is really asking when they search for an IB home tutor
paragraphs: The phrase "IB home tutor in Jebel Ali" is almost always typed by a parent who has just read a report card. Something is wrong in one subject, or in two, and the school's comment was polite enough to be useless. The parent does not actually want a stranger in the living room. They want the problem named and fixed, and "home tutor" is simply the phrase that has always meant private help.

So this page answers the subject question rather than the logistics question. An IB Diploma grade is built out of named components with published weightings. Paper 1, Paper 2 and Paper 3 carry fixed percentages. The Internal Assessment is marked against lettered criteria, each with its own mark ceiling. A student losing marks is losing them somewhere specific, and that place can be found in an hour of looking at their last two assessments against the mark scheme.

IB Gram delivers that work as live one-to-one online tuition to Jebel Ali addresses. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. The reason is not cost. It is that a Jebel Ali family needs a Chemistry HL specialist or a Maths Analysis and Approaches specialist, and the pool of people who both teach that subject properly and are willing to drive to Jebel Ali Village at 5pm on a Tuesday is small enough to be a lottery.

Jebel Ali sits at the industrial end of Dubai. The port and the free zone dominate it, and the residential communities that feed its schools spread outward into Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Green Community and Dubai South. That geography matters for one reason only: a family here has a longer drive to most of the city's tutoring centres than a family in Jumeirah does, which makes the travel premium a real number rather than a theoretical one.

Dubai's private schools are inspected by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment. That 7% is a minority inside the emirate but a large absolute number, and it is concentrated in a handful of IB continuum schools.

What follows is the syllabus detail, the mark-scheme detail and the market pricing that the pages currently ranking for this search leave out. Read the assessment tables with your child's last report next to you, and start with the component that lost the most marks rather than the subject that caused the most arguments at home.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jebel-ali.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and a Jebel Ali student may be in any part of it. The Diploma Programme is where most tutoring requests land, because it is where external examinations and fixed component weightings arrive at once. The programme below that matters for a different reason: the habits it does or does not build.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject is graded 1-7 and the core adds up to three bonus points, for a maximum of 45. Grades come from externally marked papers plus an Internal Assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. HL subjects carry extra content and, in the sciences and maths, an extra paper.
programmes.countryNote: Jebel Ali and Dubai South students mostly reach the DP through one of the IB continuum schools in the Dubai Investments Park and Sustainable City belt, or by moving across from an IGCSE school at 16. The second route is the one that produces most of our requests, because an IGCSE A* in Mathematics does not predict an HL Analysis and Approaches 7.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria, each lettered A to D and each worth up to eight marks. There are no external papers for most students; the final grade is a judgement against descriptors. MYP 5 ends with the Personal Project, a long independent piece with its own criteria, and some schools enter students for optional eAssessments.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP is where Jebel Ali families most often ask whether anything is actually wrong, because criterion grades out of eight do not map onto the percentages they grew up with. A criterion C score of 5 means a specific thing in the descriptors. Reading the school's own criterion report with a tutor is usually more useful than a term of general maths practice.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than subject periods, and finishing with the Year 6 Exhibition. Assessment is formative and portfolio-based. There is no external test, which makes gaps in number fluency and reading stamina easy to miss until a child meets the MYP's written assessment demands.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Green Community and Dubai Investments Park run the full PYP-to-DP continuum, so a child may spend fourteen years inside IB assessment language. Tutoring at this stage is almost always arithmetic fluency, handwriting speed and reading comprehension rather than anything IB-specific.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, language development and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by far fewer UAE schools than the Diploma, and it changes which parts of a student's workload are externally examined.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is rare across Dubai and rarer still in the Jebel Ali catchment, but it is worth knowing it exists before assuming a sixth-form offer is the full Diploma. If your child is on the CP, the DP courses inside it are examined exactly as DP courses are, and that is where tutoring applies.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jebel-ali.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Jebel Ali families ask about most, with what each one actually assesses and the place marks go missing. The descriptions are deliberately specific: a tutor who cannot name the component is not going to move the grade.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency under time pressure, calculus and proof. HL adds Paper 3, a long problem-solving paper that rewards students who can carry an unfamiliar structure through several parts. Marks are lost in method lines that were never written down, so the examiner cannot award the working.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and graphical technology. The calculator is central rather than incidental, and marks go missing when students quote a regression result without stating the model or the variable. HL adds a third paper built around extended modelling tasks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Built around themes from motion and matter through to fields and nuclear physics, with HL extensions inside each. The scientific investigation is the internally assessed component. Uncertainty treatment and graph gradients with units are where otherwise strong candidates shed marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity, with organic chemistry and energetics as the usual pinch points. Paper 1 mixes multiple choice with data-based questions; Paper 2 is extended response. Mechanism arrows drawn from the wrong atom cost marks that content knowledge cannot recover.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and continuity. Command terms drive the mark: "outline" and "explain" are not interchangeable, and students who answer every six-mark question as a list cap themselves well below a 7.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis; Paper 2 is comparative essay on studied works; the Individual Oral links a global issue to two texts. HL adds the written essay. The common failure is paraphrase where analysis of technique and effect was wanted.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed through papers that demand accurate, labelled diagrams. The Internal Assessment is a portfolio of commentaries on published news articles, and weak article choice limits the mark before any writing happens.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as the Ansoff matrix and break-even analysis applied to real organisations, with a research project as the Internal Assessment. Marks go to candidates who evaluate rather than describe, and who use the data supplied in the case study.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and programming in a chosen language, plus a solution-development project. Students who can code but cannot explain algorithm complexity in words lose the written-paper marks.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Productive and receptive skills across prescribed themes. Relevant in Dubai because KHDA requires Arabic in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and a DP language B grade sits alongside that requirement rather than replacing it.

sections.heading: The Diploma is a sum of named components, and so is the problem
paragraphs: An IB Diploma grade is not a general impression. Each subject grade comes from a fixed set of components with published weightings, and each component is marked against published criteria. If your child's Chemistry grade fell from a 6 to a 4, the fall happened inside one or two of those components. Finding out which one takes one session and the last two assessment papers.

This is the single biggest difference between a subject specialist and a general tutor. A general tutor will reteach the topic the student says they found hard. A specialist asks to see the marked script, counts where the marks went, and often finds the topic was understood but the answer was structured in a way the mark scheme could not reward. Those are different problems with different fixes, and only one of them is solved by more content.

The Internal Assessment is the clearest case. It is marked against lettered criteria, each carrying its own maximum. A student can write a technically correct investigation and still cap themselves because one criterion was never addressed at all. A tutor who knows the criteria reads the draft and says, in plain words, that criterion is worth marks and your draft does not engage with it. No amount of enthusiasm substitutes for that.

For Jebel Ali families the practical point is that this diagnostic work does not need anyone in the room. It needs a marked script on a shared screen and someone who knows the scheme. That is exactly what a live online session does well.

sections.heading: Subject by subject: the mark-scheme traps that recur in this catchment
paragraphs: Across the students we see from Jebel Ali, Al Furjan and Dubai Investments Park, the same small set of errors appears again and again, and almost none of them are knowledge errors. They are habits formed in a classroom where the teacher reads generously and the mark scheme does not.

In Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, the recurring loss is unwritten working. A student arrives at the right value on the calculator and writes only the answer. The mark scheme awards method marks for the line that was skipped. Over a full paper this is routinely the difference between a 5 and a 6, and it is fixable in three sessions because it is a discipline rather than a concept.

In the sciences, uncertainty and units carry a surprising share of the marks. A gradient quoted without units, an uncertainty propagated by guesswork, a graph with a line of best fit drawn through the origin because it looked tidier. In Chemistry, organic mechanisms drawn with the arrow starting at the wrong place cost the whole mark even when the product is right. In Physics, the word "explain" means a causal chain, and a correct formula with no chain earns part marks at best.

In the essay subjects, the trap is paraphrase. English A Paper 1 asks for analysis of how a text produces its effect. A student who retells the extract accurately and then adds an adjective has described, not analysed. Economics loses marks to unlabelled axes. Business Management loses them to students who never return to the case-study data they were given.

sections.heading: Past-paper work that changes a grade, and past-paper work that does not
paragraphs: Most students in this catchment have already done past papers. Many have done a great many of them, and their grade has not moved. The reason is almost always that the papers were done untimed, self-marked, and then filed. That is practice in the sense that playing a piece badly is practice.

Past-paper work that changes a grade has three features. It is timed, with the clock enforced to the real duration. It is marked by someone against the official mark scheme, not by the student against their own memory of what they meant. And the marking produces a short written list of the specific habits that cost marks, which the next session attacks directly rather than moving on to a fresh paper.

The second and third features are where a tutor is doing something the student cannot do alone. Self-marking systematically over-rewards, because the student knows what they intended to write. An examiner-literate reader marks what is on the page. When a student sees two marks withheld for a missing unit, three times, the habit changes. That is the mechanism, and it is unglamorous.

A practical note on sources: IB, Cambridge and Pearson papers are copyright material. We reference and link the official sources and work from the school's own licensed copies. We do not host, supply or distribute question papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, and any site offering you unreleased material should be treated with real suspicion rather than curiosity.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs around Jebel Ali, and who charges what
paragraphs: Most pages ranking for this search publish no price at all. Two of the better-known ones quote US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays a tutor in. So here are the AED bands, attributed, as of October 2026, with the clear statement that these are market rates and not an IB Gram price list.

At the bottom of the market, EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 per hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33-52, both for online lessons usually delivered by university students or early-career tutors. In the middle, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 per hour for a qualified subject tutor online. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-350 and specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors at AED 200-450 and above. At the premium end, BartyED publishes AED 650.

Read those bands as a ladder of what you are buying rather than a ladder of quality. At the lowest band you are usually hiring a capable undergraduate who can get a Year 9 through a worksheet. They are not reading an HL Chemistry draft against criterion D. The AED 650 figure usually attaches to a named individual with examiner or senior-teacher credentials and a waiting list.

The in-home band is the interesting one for Jebel Ali. The AED 180-350 range includes the tutor's travel, and the travel from most of Dubai to Jebel Ali Village at 5pm is not twenty minutes. That premium buys you presence in the room. It does not buy you a wider choice of specialist, and for a single HL subject the specialist is the thing that matters.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one versus an in-home tutor, priced honestly for a Jebel Ali address
paragraphs: The honest comparison is not online against in-home in the abstract. It is online against in-home from a Jebel Ali address specifically, because that is where the travel variable bites. A tutor living in Mirdif who takes a Jebel Ali Village booking is committing to a round trip that can approach two hours in term-time evening traffic. That cost appears in the rate, in the limited number of slots offered, and in the cancellation rate.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all. We say that plainly rather than burying it, because two competitors in this market route UAE parents to an Indian phone number without mentioning that delivery is remote. Our in-home service exists only in India. For the UAE, lessons are live, one-to-one and over video, with screen sharing so the tutor and student work on the same script at the same time.

What the online format gives a Jebel Ali family is selection. Instead of choosing among the subject tutors who will drive to Dubai Investments Park, you choose among all the specialists in that subject. For a common need such as IGCSE Mathematics, the difference is modest. For Physics HL, Economics HL or Arabic B, it is the difference between a specialist and a near-miss.

The format has real limitations and it is worth naming them. A student who will not sit at a desk without an adult present does better with a person in the room. Very young children lose focus faster on a screen. And a weak home internet connection turns a 60-minute lesson into 45. Those are the cases where in-home genuinely wins, and if your child is one of them you should hire locally rather than take our word for it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may do with an IA, an Extended Essay or a TOK essay
paragraphs: This matters more than anything else on this page, because getting it wrong ends a student's Diploma. The IB treats work submitted as the student's own when it is not as malpractice, and the consequence can be the loss of the qualification rather than a mark penalty. Parents who do not know the line are vulnerable to services that cross it.

There are sites in this market that sell completed Internal Assessments. One of them advertises them at AED 3,750. What is being sold is not tutoring. It is a document that, if submitted, exposes the student to an investigation they cannot win, because the IB's own authenticity checks exist precisely for this. No tutoring relationship is worth that risk, and no price makes it worth it.

The legitimate boundary is clear and it is generous. A tutor may explain what each lettered criterion asks for. A tutor may read the student's own draft and say which criteria it does not yet address. A tutor may teach the subject content the investigation needs, help narrow a research question from unanswerable to answerable, explain referencing conventions, and discuss method design. A tutor may mark a draft against the descriptors and explain the marking.

A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph into their own prose, supply a research question wholesale, produce the data, or edit the piece to a finished state. The test we use is simple: at the end of the session, every sentence in the document must have been typed by the student. If a tutor ever offers you more than that, decline, and tell the school.

sections.heading: KHDA, the school report and what an inspection band actually tells you
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band for each school on a six-point scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Parents in this catchment read those bands closely, and they are useful, but they are not a statement about your child.

An inspection band is a judgement about a school as a whole: teaching quality, student outcomes across the age range, leadership, inclusion. A Very Good school can have one department running thin in a particular HL subject, and a Good school can have an outstanding Physics teacher. When a family in Al Furjan asks whether their child's subject difficulty is the school's fault, the inspection band almost never answers the question. The marked scripts do.

Two other KHDA facts are worth knowing here. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA also requires schools to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects.

One thing IB Gram is not: KHDA approved. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with physical premises in Dubai, and we do not hold one and do not operate premises in the UAE. Any tutoring service describing itself as KHDA-approved tutors should be asked to show the permit number.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a surprising number of pages in this market either ignore the point or imply it does not apply. It does. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The UAE government states that the permit is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligibility is broad. The government lists teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, publishes no fee, lists a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

The consequence of skipping it is real: the government states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so we do not quote a figure, and you should be sceptical of pages that do. In Abu Dhabi there is an additional layer, with ADEK's professional-ethics rules reported as barring private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

The practical point for a Jebel Ali parent hiring an individual directly: ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit, and ask before the first lesson rather than after. A tutor who has one will say so without hesitation, because it costs nothing to hold. And never ask your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately for a fee; the permit's code of conduct and ADEK's ethics rules both point the other way.

sections.heading: Getting started, including what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: The process is short and the first step produces something useful whether or not you continue. Send the subject, the level, the school and - this is the part that matters - a photograph of the most recent marked assessment. A marked script tells us more in two minutes than a twenty-minute phone call about how the term has gone.

We then match a tutor by subject and level, not by availability. If the request is IGCSE Mathematics we will usually have several options within a day. If it is Physics HL with a scientific investigation due in three weeks, or Arabic B at Higher Level, the pool is narrower and the honest answer may be two or three days. We would rather tell you that than put a general science tutor in front of an HL Physics draft.

Occasionally the honest answer is that no suitable specialist has a slot at the time you need. When that happens we say so and offer the alternatives: a different weekday slot with the right specialist, a shorter block until a regular slot opens, or nothing at all with a suggestion of what to look for locally. Nobody in this market publishes what happens when they cannot help, which is why it is worth saying.

The trial lesson is free and is a real diagnostic lesson rather than a sales call: the tutor works through the marked script with the student and writes up what they found. After that you decide. There is no package to commit to before the trial and no card required to book it.

process.title: Send the subject, level and a marked script
process.description: One message with the subject, HL or SL, the school and a photograph of the last marked assessment. The script is the useful part: it shows where marks were actually lost rather than where the student felt uncertain.

process.title: We match on subject and level
process.description: A specialist in that exact subject and level, not the nearest available generalist. Common subjects are usually matched within a day; narrow HL subjects and Arabic B can take two or three. We tell you which case you are in.

process.title: A free diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: A real lesson, online and one-to-one, working through the marked script. The tutor writes up what they found and what the first month should target. No card details and no package commitment to book it.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: The same tutor at the same time each week, set after the school run rather than squeezed into it. Sessions move for mocks, examinations and Ramadan timings, which in practice means most families shift at least once a year.

process.title: Written notes you can check
process.description: After each session a short note of what was covered and what the student is to do before the next one. It is there so you can see progress against the original diagnosis rather than relying on your child's summary of the hour.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: A tutor is chosen because they teach that subject at that level and know its mark scheme. Geography is irrelevant to an online lesson, which removes the single biggest constraint on specialist choice for families out at Jebel Ali and Dubai South.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, with sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are attributed to the competitors and rate guides that published them, with the month we read them. No page in this market cites a source for a single AED figure, which makes an unsourced number easy to print and impossible to check.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain criteria and mark drafts. They do not write, rewrite or complete an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay. Services selling finished coursework in this market expose the student to a malpractice finding they cannot recover from.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we do not do
whyPoints.description: There are no IB Gram home visits in the UAE, no UAE office, and no claim of KHDA, ADEK, MoE, IB or Cambridge approval, because we hold none. Every delivery claim on this page is one we can meet.

whyPoints.title: Regulatory facts, cited to the authority
whyPoints.description: The permit position, the equivalency rules and the regulator map come from u.ae, MoHRE and KHDA's own documents, and we link out rather than restating figures that can change. Where a figure is unverified, such as IB session dates, we say so instead of publishing it.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for a UAE school week
whyPoints.description: Slots run on Gulf Standard Time, around a Monday-to-Friday school week, and shift for Ramadan and examination periods. A tutor on a mismatched timezone turns a 5pm lesson into a 9pm one by February.

faqs.question: Can I actually get a home tutor who comes to our villa in Jebel Ali?
faqs.answer: Local agencies do send tutors to Jebel Ali addresses, and market rates for that service run roughly AED 180-500 per hour depending on subject and level, with the tutor's travel included in the figure. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For Jebel Ali families we teach live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time. The trade is straightforward: you give up a person in the room and you gain the whole pool of subject specialists rather than the subset willing to drive out to Jebel Ali at 5pm.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects do Jebel Ali families ask for most often?
faqs.answer: Mathematics is first by a wide margin, split between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and the single most common request is HL Analysis and Approaches in the second Diploma year. Chemistry and Physics follow, usually at Higher Level and usually tied to a scientific investigation deadline. English A Language and Literature arrives when Paper 1 marks stay flat despite strong classwork. Economics and Business Management come up around the Internal Assessment rather than the papers. Arabic B appears steadily because Arabic is required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's problem is content or examination technique?
faqs.answer: Look at a marked script rather than a report card. If marks are lost on questions the student could explain to you verbally, the problem is technique: unwritten method lines, command terms answered at the wrong depth, or structure the mark scheme cannot reward. If marks are lost on questions they cannot explain at all, it is content. The two need different work, and the common mistake is to buy content teaching for a technique problem, which is why some students do many past papers and never move. A diagnostic session with the script answers it in under an hour.

faqs.question: What does an Internal Assessment tutor do that my child's teacher does not?
faqs.answer: Nothing the teacher could not do with unlimited time, which they do not have. A tutor reads one student's draft against the lettered criteria for that subject and names, criterion by criterion, what the draft does not yet address. That is slow work and it is specific to the document in front of them. The tutor does not write, rewrite or complete any part of it; every sentence submitted must be the student's own. Anything beyond explanation, teaching and marking against descriptors is an academic-honesty matter that can cost the student the Diploma.

faqs.question: Are the AED rates on this page what IB Gram charges?
faqs.answer: No. They are market rates read from published competitor pages and Dubai rate guides in October 2026, quoted so you can judge any price you are offered against something. Budget online tuition is advertised from around AED 33-65 per hour, qualified online subject tutors from AED 150-200, in-home visits at AED 180-500 including travel, specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and one premium provider at AED 650. IB Gram's own fee depends on subject and level and is quoted after the free trial lesson, so you see the tutor before you see the number.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a licence to teach my child privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE. The UAE government states the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published. Ask any independent tutor whether they hold it before the first lesson.

faqs.question: My child is in the second Diploma year. Is it too late for tutoring to matter?
faqs.answer: It is late for content building and not late for mark recovery. In the final two terms the gains come from examination technique and from the Internal Assessment, because both are still movable and both carry fixed weight. A timed-paper cycle with real marking against the official scheme typically exposes two or three repeated habits, and habits can change in weeks. What will not happen in that window is covering a year of missed HL content. An honest tutor will tell you which of the two you are dealing with after reading one marked paper.

faqs.question: How does an online lesson handle a Physics or Chemistry practical?
faqs.answer: It handles the assessed part, which is the thinking rather than the glassware. The internally assessed scientific investigation is marked on research question, method design, data treatment, uncertainty handling and the quality of the analysis, and all of that is screen work. A tutor reads the student's data, checks the uncertainty propagation, looks at whether the graph supports the claim being made, and tests the conclusion against the evidence. The hands-on procedure happens in the school laboratory under the teacher's supervision, as the IB requires, and no tutor substitutes for that.

faqs.question: Which schools near Jebel Ali actually run the full IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The catchment mixes curricula rather than concentrating on one. Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park runs an IB continuum, and Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City is also an IB school, while Sunmarke School in Al Furjan offers the Diploma alongside a UK-curriculum route. The Winchester School Jebel Ali, Dove Green Private School and South View School are UK curriculum, Delhi Private School Dubai is Indian curriculum and The International School of Choueifat Dubai runs SABIS. Check each school's current authorisation on its own site, since programme offerings change year to year.

faqs.question: Should the same specialist take both Maths and Physics for a Jebel Ali student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is usually a worse idea than it looks. Maths and Physics overlap enough that one specialist can genuinely hold both, and Economics with Business Management is a reasonable pair. Chemistry and Biology are taught by different specialists in most schools for a reason, and the gap between HL Chemistry mechanism work and HL Biology command-term discipline is wide. Our default is one subject per tutor, because the point of the match is component-level knowledge of a specific mark scheme, and that narrows as the level rises.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers and mark schemes for us to work from?
faqs.answer: We do not host, supply or distribute them. IB, Cambridge and Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are copyright material, and reproducing them is an infringement, while circulating unreleased material is a malpractice exposure for the student. What we do is reference the official sources, link them, and work from the copies your child's school is licensed to provide. Any service offering you a library of papers, or material that has not yet been released, is worth declining on those grounds alone.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do most Jebel Ali Diploma students start with?
faqs.answer: One session a week in one subject is the normal starting point, and it is usually right. Two subjects at once doubles the homework load on a student who is already carrying six subjects plus the core, and the first month is diagnostic anyway. Families who start with three subjects most often reduce by half term. The exception is the final run into the examination session, where a short intensive block of two or three sessions a week in a single subject does real work because it is built entirely on timed papers and marking.

faqs.question: Will the lesson time still work during Ramadan and examination weeks?
faqs.answer: It has to move, and we plan for that rather than reacting to it. School hours shorten during Ramadan, families shift their evening around iftar, and a 5pm slot usually becomes either an early afternoon one or a post-iftar one. Examination weeks need the same flexibility in the other direction, with sessions clustered before papers and paused afterwards. Because tutors are not travelling to an address, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation of someone's commute, which is one of the quieter advantages of the online format.

faqs.question: What qualifications do the tutors teaching Diploma subjects hold?
faqs.answer: A subject degree in what they teach and classroom or tutoring experience with that specific programme and level, which is the part that matters. Knowing Chemistry is not the same as knowing how the IB marks a Chemistry investigation, and the second is what we select for. We do not describe tutors as IB examiners or Cambridge examiners, because we cannot evidence current examiner status for individuals and examiner status is routinely used in this market to imply access to marking or boundaries that nobody has. Ask any agency to evidence the claim.

faqs.question: Do IB grades need Ministry of Education equivalency for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: School-leaving certificates generally need equivalency from the Ministry of Education before a UAE university application, and the requirements differ by curriculum. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. No IB points threshold is published in the source we read, so we do not state one. Verify the current IB requirement on moe.gov.ae before relying on any figure.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jebel-ali.closingHeading: Start with the marked script, not the brochure
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jebel-ali.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB home tutor in Jebel Ali, the fastest useful step is not a phone call about packages. Send the subject, the level, the school and a photograph of your child's most recent marked assessment. A specialist in that subject reads it, names where the marks actually went, and works through it with your child in a free one-to-one trial lesson online. You get a written diagnosis at the end of that hour whether or not you continue. From there, a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, the same tutor each week, and a short written note after every session so you can check progress against what the script said at the start.

intro.heading: What the travel premium on an IB home tutor in JLT actually buys
paragraphs: Start with the line nobody itemises. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, which matches Unitors' published rates of AED 150 upward for IGCSE and AED 200 upward for IB. The same calibre of tutor coming to a JLT apartment is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's Dubai rate table and at AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors. The gap between those two bands is the travel premium, and it is worth asking what it purchases, because the answer is not more teaching.

It purchases three things. The tutor's driving time, which on the run between Al Barsha or Business Bay and JLT at 17:00 is rarely under thirty-five minutes each way. The cost of their being unable to teach anyone else in that window, which is why visiting tutors cluster their bookings geographically rather than by subject. And the risk premium on a session that cannot start because Sheikh Zayed Road has stopped, which lands on the family as a late start or a rescheduled hour. None of those three improves a Diploma grade.

Jumeirah Lakes Towers adds its own friction. It is a grid of lettered clusters around four artificial lakes, with podium parking, visitor registration at most towers and lifts that serve thirty-plus floors. A tutor arriving at 17:05 for a 17:00 start may genuinely have been in the building for ten minutes. Families who have tried a visiting arrangement in JLT usually describe the same two problems: the first ten minutes of the hour evaporate, and the arrangement collapses the week the tutor's own schedule changes.

The useful way to budget IB support is not per hour at all. It is per Diploma. Two years from the start of Year 12 to results day is the real unit, because that is the period over which the decision plays out, and it is where the difference between formats compounds. One weekly hour of mid-market online tutoring across two Diploma years is a four-figure commitment. The same hours with travel inside the rate is a materially larger one, for the same contact time and a smaller shortlist of candidates.

IB Gram delivers to JLT as one-to-one online tuition over live video. We do not run home visits in Dubai; that is an India-only service, and this page says so rather than letting the URL imply otherwise. What a JLT family gets instead is the whole specialist pool rather than the drivable fraction of it, a session that starts at 17:00 because nobody is in traffic, and a rate with no travel line inside it. Context helps too: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, so the tutoring line is the one that still moves in a household budget.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jlt.programmesIntro: Most JLT enquiries concern the Diploma, but the programme a child is in decides what support is even possible. The Diploma has fixed external exams and internal assessment deadlines; the Middle Years Programme has criteria and no external papers in most subjects. Costing support without that distinction is how families buy the wrong thing.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Scored out of 45, with 42 subject points and up to three from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, which means a Diploma budget has two distinct peaks: the coursework months and the final revision run. Those peaks are months apart and should not be funded as one continuous expense.
programmes.countryNote: JLT students sit the Diploma at schools in Al Barsha, Al Sufouh, Barsha South and across the Marina. The commute means a weekday session before 16:30 is usually unrealistic, and Year 13 students juggling Extended Essay deadlines often prefer a single 90-minute slot to two shorter ones. UAE schools sit the May session, which sets the whole Year 13 calendar.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of 8. There is no external paper in most subjects, so a grade is built from tasks across the year rather than from one sitting. For a budget this matters enormously: money spent in May has almost nothing left to influence, while the same money in October sits in front of every remaining assessed task. The Personal Project in MYP 5 is externally moderated and needs process coaching rather than content teaching.
programmes.countryNote: JLT families with a child in MYP 4 or 5 are often deciding between a Diploma and an A Level route for 16-plus. That decision changes what MYP support is for. Preparing for Analysis and Approaches is an algebra and proof problem; preparing for A Level Mathematics is a different emphasis again, and the school's own guidance should come first.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, with units of inquiry rather than discrete subject syllabuses and no external examination. Support at this stage is inexpensive relative to the Diploma and disproportionately useful, because number fluency and written structure carry into every later criterion. Shorter sessions work better than long ones, and a 45-minute slot twice a week usually outperforms a single ninety-minute block for a child under eleven.
programmes.countryNote: Primary-age children in JLT mostly attend schools in Al Barsha and the Marina and are home earlier than secondary siblings, which makes a 16:00 start realistic. Households running two children in one evening find consecutive online slots far cheaper than a visiting tutor whose waiting time between siblings is inside the billed hour.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, a language-development portfolio and service learning. Offered by a small number of UAE schools. For a student with two strong subjects and three weak ones it can be a better fit than the full Diploma, and the tutoring spend concentrates on those two Diploma courses plus the portfolio, which rewards steady work rather than a late push.
programmes.countryNote: Few schools in the JLT and Marina catchment run the Career-related Programme, so a family considering it is usually looking at a change of school as well. Confirm with the school's IB coordinator which pathways actually run in Year 12 before funding two years of preparation for a route that is not on offer nearby.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jlt.subjectsIntro: Not all Diploma subjects cost the same to support, because they fail in different ways. The grid below names what each subject actually assesses and where the hours go, which is the information a JLT family needs before deciding how many subjects to fund at once.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency is the gate. At Higher Level the paper burden includes an extended-response paper and a technology-permitted paper, and marks go on proof structure and on method marks never claimed. Students who arrived from the MYP without secure manipulation spend their first term catching up, which is the most expensive term to be behind in.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with heavier calculator use. Marks are lost on interpretation rather than computation: a correct regression with no comment on validity scores poorly. Support here is cheaper per grade point than Analysis and Approaches because the techniques are discrete and teachable in blocks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the recurring pressure points, and the internal assessment requires a genuinely independent investigation. Higher Level adds substantial content on top of the shared core, so an HL Chemistry plan is usually the longest single commitment in a Diploma budget.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks are lost on unit handling, uncertainty treatment and the gap between knowing a formula and selecting it. The investigation rewards careful error analysis, which is teachable in two or three sessions and is where a mid-range mark usually becomes a strong one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy with precise command-term expectations: 'outline', 'explain' and 'evaluate' each demand a different answer shape. Students who revise content without revising command terms plateau, and that is a cheap plateau to break.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the marks. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on real news articles, which is a process and deadline problem as much as a content one, and it responds well to fortnightly rather than weekly support.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole subject. Students who learn the tools but never practise applying them to an unseen organisation sit several marks below their knowledge. Support is best timed around the school's mock case study rather than spread across the year.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis under time, plus the individual oral and the HL essay. Marks move on structure and on the quality of the line of inquiry rather than on vocabulary, which means a small number of well-directed sessions can shift a grade.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source evaluation for Paper 1 and essay argument for Papers 2 and 3. Higher Level adds a regional depth study, which doubles content. The historical investigation is 2,200 words and wants a researchable question, which is the single most useful thing a tutor can fix early.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay together feed the three bonus points with the Extended Essay. Support is coaching on argument and on the choice of real-world objects, never writing. Few families budget for it and many then pay for rushed help in the final weeks.

Useful when the rest of the Diploma is sound and one subject is dragging the total. It is also the format to start with if you have never used a tutor, because it produces evidence before it produces a commitment.

sections.heading: Itemising the travel line on a JLT home-tutoring rate
paragraphs: This page exists because 'home tutor in JLT' is what parents type, so here is the honest answer to it. The in-home market in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate's 2026 rate table and at AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors. Online delivery from a qualified subject tutor is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing AED 150 upward for IGCSE and AED 200 upward for IB. Monthly packages tell the same story more plainly: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Work the second pair through. Eight online sessions a month is roughly AED 100 an hour. Four two-hour in-home visits is eight contact hours for AED 1,599 to 1,799, or roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour. Identical contact time, double the rate. The table below splits that difference into what it is actually paying for, and only the first row is teaching.

None of these are IB Gram's prices. They are market rates published by the providers named, quoted here because a JLT parent weighing a visiting tutor against an online one deserves the arithmetic rather than a slogan. Our own model opens with a free trial lesson, with no card details required, and a consultation that sets the plan before any figure is agreed. One further point about the market figures: they are hourly, and hourly is the unit that flatters the cheapest tier, because a budget tutor at AED 60 who needs three sessions to close what a specialist closes in one is the more expensive choice by the end of the term.

sections.heading: The two-year Diploma budget, counted from Year 12 to results
paragraphs: Hourly rates are a poor unit for a decision that runs twenty-two months. The table below puts the Diploma in context against the household's other education costs, using figures that are either published market rates or published regulator facts. The anchor is useful: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are therefore the one line not moving; tutoring is the line that is.

The arithmetic parents find most surprising is the continuous weekly booking. Thirty-two teaching weeks a year, two years, one hour a week, at a mid-market AED 220, is roughly AED 14,000 for a single subject. Two subjects on the same basis approaches AED 28,000. The same money spent as two funded peaks, one around coursework deadlines and one before the final session, typically buys the outcomes that mattered at well under half the total.

Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a single weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist exam-year support. Those ranges are a reasonable planning basis. What they do not include, and what families forget, is examination entry if a student ever sits as a private candidate, and the cost of a second subject added in Year 13 when a grade slips.

sections.heading: What a JLT tower makes hard about a visiting arrangement
paragraphs: Jumeirah Lakes Towers is a planned grid of lettered clusters arranged around four artificial lakes, and it behaves like three separate neighbourhoods depending on which side of the lakes you live. Access is the first friction. Most towers register visitors at a desk, parking is at podium level and often permit-controlled, and the lift bank on a thirty-plus floor tower at 17:00 is shared with everyone else coming home. A tutor who left Al Barsha at 16:20 can be in the building at 16:58 and still be unpacking a laptop on your dining table at 17:08.

The second friction is that the arrangement is fragile. A visiting tutor's week is a route, not a timetable. When one booking in the cluster ends, the economics of the drive change and your slot moves. Families in the towers describe the same pattern: a good first term, a renegotiated time in January, and a replacement tutor by March who does not know the subject as well.

The third is the quiet one. Hiring someone who will drive to JLT restricts you to people who will drive to JLT. For Standard Level Mathematics that is a large enough group. For Higher Level Chemistry with a deadline on an independent investigation, or Higher Level History with a regional depth study, it is not, and the compromise shows up in the teaching rather than on the invoice. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and the reason is this one: the format quietly costs the family the specialist.

Visiting schedules are routes; when a neighbouring booking ends, your slot moves
The drivable shortlist is adequate for common subjects and thin for Higher Level ones

sections.heading: Which Diploma subjects soak up the hours, and why
paragraphs: A Diploma budget is not six equal sixths. Higher Level sciences carry the most content above the shared core, which is why Higher Level Chemistry and Higher Level Physics plans tend to be the longest in any family's two years. Higher Level History adds a regional depth study on top of the prescribed subject and the world history topics, so its hours go on breadth of content and on essay argument rather than on technique.

The mathematics pair behaves differently. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is a fluency problem first: a student who cannot manipulate algebraic expressions quickly will be slow on every paper regardless of how well they understand the ideas. That is drillable, which makes it expensive in session count but predictable in result. Applications and Interpretation is a set of discrete techniques, cheaper to support because each one can be closed in a session or two.

The subjects families under-fund are Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which together feed up to three points on the matrix. Three points is the difference between several university offers. Neither needs weekly teaching; both need a handful of coaching conversations at the right moments, which is the cheapest high-value support in the Diploma and the most commonly skipped. The practical planning rule that follows is to rank the six subjects by how far the school's predicted grade sits below the grade the university offer needs, fund the largest gap first, and leave the subject where your child is already comfortable entirely alone. Families who fund all six evenly spend the most and move the total least, because four of those six were never the problem.
bullets: Higher Level sciences carry the most additional content and the longest plans
Analysis and Approaches needs fluency drilling; Applications and Interpretation needs discrete techniques
Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay feed up to three matrix points

sections.heading: The examination calendar, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Dates are where this market is weakest, and where a JLT family can plan properly with ten minutes of reading. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

In the UAE the choice is not when the series happens but which of the two you aim at, because Cambridge runs a June series and a November series here and the February and March series is offered to India only. June is the main event and November is the resit route, and the gap between them is what gives a JLT family a second attempt without losing a year. Cambridge June entries close in the spring, months before the first paper, and the exact day is printed on the centre's statement of entry rather than guessed at; November entries then close over the summer, after June results have shown whether one subject is worth repeating. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations work on the same two-chance rhythm, available in May and June and again in November: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Read either calendar backwards from the paper and the entry deadline always lands months earlier, which is the point worth planning around.

IB dates are deliberately absent from this page. UAE schools sit the May session, and that is the session a Year 13 calendar is built around, but no IB session or results date here has been confirmed against ibo.org, which blocks automated checking. Confirm every IB date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly, and treat any page that publishes one without a source with caution. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning from.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, emirate by emirate
paragraphs: JLT families move within the UAE more often than they expect, and the regulator changes with the emirate. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The powers are not identical. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sit with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. At federal level, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, which is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

For a tutoring plan the practical consequences are two. First, the inspection framework and its published bands differ by emirate, so a report from a Dubai school and one from a Sharjah school are not read the same way. Second, a family relocating mid-Diploma should ask the receiving school which regulator it answers to and which assessment calendar it follows, because the session the school enters students for is what the plan must be built around.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and what a JLT family must show
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that turns a school certificate into something a UAE university or employer can accept, and it is where the published competitor information in this market is actually wrong rather than merely thin. For the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

Two details matter and are frequently misreported. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. And one page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying.

For the IB there is no figure on this page, and that is deliberate. The source that sets out the British and American requirements states no IB points threshold, so no IB equivalency number should be published without reading it on a Ministry of Education page or the emirate attestation authority's own site. Equivalency is also not something IB Gram performs, arranges or guarantees: we describe it, cite the authority, and point you to the official channel. Nor is tutoring required for it, whatever a page implying urgency might suggest.
