sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: The Diploma's internal components are where this question becomes urgent, and one page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a four-figure price. Buying one is a malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. The boundary is not subtle. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria, explain what the command terms demand, interrogate a research question, point at a weak paragraph, and give written feedback on work the student has already produced.

A tutor may not draft, rewrite to completion, or hand over text that then appears in a submission. The practical test for a parent is the draft trail. If each version is visibly your child's own writing getting better, with the tutor's feedback showing as changes your child made, the arrangement is sound. If a draft arrives in a voice your child does not use in conversation, a moderator will notice what you noticed.

The same restraint applies to materials. Official IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are referenced and linked from the board's own site, never reproduced or supplied as downloads. A provider that sends you a folder of scanned mark schemes has told you how it treats rules in general, which is worth knowing before Year 13. Ask any provider two direct questions before the first paid session: what would you do if my child sent you a finished draft and asked you to fix it, and what would you refuse to do. The answers separate a teacher from a service, and they are cheaper to collect in September than in April.

sections.heading: Starting from a JLT address, and what we will decline
paragraphs: The sequence is short and the trial comes before any money. Tell us the school, the year group, the subjects and levels, and what the last school report actually said. We propose a tutor and a weekday slot set after the commute home rather than during it, you take one free trial lesson with no card details required, and only then is anything agreed. Matching usually takes two to four working days for common Diploma subjects.

Availability is disclosed rather than assumed, because concealing it is how families end up with a weak match they cannot easily exit. Mathematics, the three sciences, English, Economics and Business Management are normally covered in UAE evening hours. A niche Higher Level option, a less common language, or a specific Theory of Knowledge requirement may not be, and if we do not have the right person this term we will say so and you should look elsewhere.

Three things we will decline. Producing any part of an assessed component. Claiming a regulator or board relationship we do not hold, including anything that reads as KHDA endorsement, because a training-institute permit is a specific thing issued to operations with premises and IB Gram does not operate one. And promising a particular grade, which no honest provider can sell. What we will quote is a plan, a session count and a review point at which you decide whether to continue. The last of those matters most in a two-year budget, because a plan with no review point renews itself by habit, and habit is the single most expensive feature of any tutoring arrangement in this city.

process.title: Send the report, not just the subject list
process.description: The last school report, with predicted grades and internal assessment marks if it carries them, tells us where the hours should go. Without it the first session is diagnosis you have already paid your school to produce, and in a two-year budget that is a line worth removing.

process.title: Pick the slot after the commute, not during it
process.description: We work back from the school finish and the route home to JLT. A student still on Sheikh Zayed Road at 16:30 should not have a 16:30 session. For most JLT towers 17:00 is dependable and 17:30 is safe when the route comes through Barsha South.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One full session at no cost, with no card details required, so your child meets the tutor before any commitment. If the fit is wrong, say so and we propose someone else. A trial that ends in an honest refusal has done exactly its job.

process.title: Decide between a continuous slot and two funded peaks
process.description: We will usually recommend the peaks: a block around coursework deadlines and a block before the final revision run, with the quiet months unfunded. A continuous weekly slot is available if the gap is genuinely structural, and we will tell you which case we think yours is.

process.title: Review at the next marked task
process.description: At the end of a block we look at the next real piece of school assessment. If it moved, we close or pause the plan. If it did not, we change the method or the tutor rather than adding hours to an approach that is not working, and we say which we are doing and why.

whyPoints.title: The travel line is shown, not buried
whyPoints.description: Market rates for in-home and online delivery are published side by side on this page with their sources, so the premium is visible. Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all and two quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai household transacts in.

whyPoints.title: A whole-Diploma budget, not an hourly rate
whyPoints.description: Two years is the unit the decision plays out over, so the figures here are set out monthly and in total, anchored against KHDA's confirmation of no private-school fee increase for 2026-27. An hourly rate flatters the cheapest tier and hides the arrangement's real size.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and limits stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram runs no home visits in the UAE and holds no UAE office or centre. A page with 'home tutor' in the URL owes the reader that sentence early rather than in a footnote.

whyPoints.title: Board dates from the boards
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson milestones here come from the boards' own published pages and are cited as such. No IB session or results date appears, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unsourced date on a planning page is worse than no date.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary on coursework
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria, question research questions and give feedback on the student's own drafts. Nobody drafts an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. In a market where a ranking page sells finished coursework, that line needs writing down.

whyPoints.title: Coverage disclosed before you commit
whyPoints.description: If a Higher Level option has no specialist free this term, we say so at the matching stage rather than placing a general tutor and hoping. A declined enquiry costs us the booking and saves you a term of a plan that was never going to work.

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in JLT charge once travel sits inside the rate?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts in-home one-to-one tutoring at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors quote AED 200 to 500. The same calibre of tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing from AED 150 for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB. The difference is driving time, the tutor's unsellable travel window, tower access and the risk of a late start. Package rates make it starker: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions is about AED 100 an hour against roughly AED 200 to 225 for in-home visits.

faqs.question: What does two years of Diploma support cost from Year 12 to results?
faqs.answer: Taken as a continuous weekly hour at a mid-market AED 220, thirty-two teaching weeks a year across two years is roughly AED 14,000 for one subject, and about AED 28,000 for two. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 upward for specialist exam-year work. Most families get what mattered for well under half the continuous figure by funding two peaks instead: the coursework window, then the final revision run.

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach our JLT apartment without a visitor pass every week?
faqs.answer: Most JLT towers register visitors at a desk, with podium parking that is often permit-controlled, so a weekly visiting arrangement usually means a weekly registration and a lift share at the busiest hour of the day. Families describe losing five to ten minutes of a billed hour to it. That is one of the reasons IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai: lessons run one-to-one over live video, so a 17:00 session starts at 17:00 whatever the lobby and Sheikh Zayed Road are doing.

faqs.question: Which is dearer to support properly, Higher Level Chemistry or Higher Level History?
faqs.answer: Chemistry, usually, and for a structural reason. Higher Level Chemistry carries substantial additional content above the shared core, and its internal assessment requires a genuinely independent investigation, so the plan runs long in both content and process. Higher Level History adds a regional depth study to the prescribed subject and world history topics, so its hours concentrate on breadth and essay argument. History responds faster to technique work on source evaluation; Chemistry needs sustained content coverage, which is more sessions over more months.

faqs.question: How far before the examination does the entry deadline actually fall?
faqs.answer: Further than most families expect, and in the UAE you are counting back from June or November, never from a February paper, because Cambridge offers the February and March series to India only. Cambridge June entries close in the spring, months ahead of the first paper, with the exact day printed on the statement of entry; November entries close over the summer, which is what makes November a workable resit route once June results are in. Pearson gives the clearest published illustration: its November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct timetable version for your zone is essential, since it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper.

faqs.question: Does the KHDA fee freeze change what tutoring should cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not directly, but it changes which line in your budget is variable. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are therefore fixed for the year while tutoring is not, which makes the tutoring line the one worth scrutinising. It is also the line most easily reduced by scoping work to blocks with an end date rather than a standing monthly commitment.

faqs.question: Who regulates the school if we move from Dubai to Sharjah mid-Diploma?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate and, unlike KHDA, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the Ministry of Education. Ask the receiving school which assessment session it enters students for, because that is what a support plan has to be rebuilt around.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education require for British-curriculum equivalency?
faqs.answer: Students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. One page ranking for these searches states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Equivalency is not something IB Gram performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: If our child sits Arabic at IGCSE, does it reduce the five we still need?
faqs.answer: No. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count, which means a student needs five other accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3 in addition to them. That detail changes subject-choice planning in Year 9 and Year 10, because a family counting Arabic towards the five would believe they had met the rule when they had not. Verify the current wording with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation authority before relying on it for a university application.

faqs.question: How much of the Diploma grade sits in internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Enough that the coursework months are one of the two places a budget should concentrate. Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component, and alongside them sit the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, which together feed up to three points on the matrix. The exact weighting differs by subject and level, so ask your child's teacher for the subject's own breakdown rather than taking a general figure from a tutoring page. The practical consequence is that support in the coursework window buys more than the same money in the quiet term before it.

faqs.question: Where exactly does Extended Essay help stop being allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may interrogate the research question, explain the assessment criteria, discuss method and sources, point at a paragraph that does not do its job, and give written feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor may not draft the essay, rewrite it to completion, or supply text that appears in the submission. The test a parent can apply is the draft trail: each version should visibly be your child's own writing improving. A provider offering a finished Extended Essay is selling a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Is one 90-minute session a week better value than two 60-minute ones?
faqs.answer: For Year 13 coursework work, usually yes, because an Extended Essay or internal assessment conversation needs runway and two short sessions spend their openings twice. For fluency work such as Analysis and Approaches algebra, two shorter sessions are better, since the gains come from frequency rather than from length. For a Year 12 student new to the Diploma, start with one 60-minute slot and change it once you can see which kind of work the sessions are actually doing.

faqs.question: What should we do if nobody is free for our Higher Level option this term?
faqs.answer: Hear it plainly and plan around it. We disclose coverage at the matching stage rather than placing a general tutor against a specialist requirement, so if a niche Higher Level option or a less common language has no specialist available in UAE evening hours this term, we say so and you should approach someone else. In the meantime the school's own subject teacher remains the best route, and a short block on a different subject that is also slipping may be a better use of the same money.

faqs.question: Do lessons continue when we travel out of Dubai over the summer?
faqs.answer: They can, and the summer is often the cheapest useful window in the whole Diploma. With no school timetable competing, July and August suit transition work: algebraic fluency before Analysis and Approaches, command-term practice before a science Higher Level, or a research question settled before the Extended Essay term begins. Online delivery follows you as long as the time difference leaves a workable slot for both sides. Families who prefer to pause keep the slot and resume in September rather than rejoining a queue.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest month of the Diploma to start paying for help?
faqs.answer: September of Year 12, counterintuitively, because every assessed task in the two years is still ahead of it and a short block then prevents the structural gaps that cost most to close later. The dearest month is April of Year 13, when the specialists with strong records are fully booked, availability rather than the published band sets your price, and there is almost nothing left in the calendar for the work to influence. If you can only fund one block, fund the first one.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jlt.closingHeading: Budget the Diploma, not the hour, and keep the travel line out of it
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jlt.closingBody: Searching for an IB home tutor in JLT is reasonable; paying AED 180 to 500 an hour so that someone can cross Sheikh Zayed Road at 17:00 is harder to justify. The teaching is the part worth buying, and it transfers to a screen without loss. Set the budget across both Diploma years, fund the coursework window and the revision run rather than every quiet month in between, and start with a free trial lesson that costs nothing and needs no card details. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, timed to arrive after the commute home rather than in the middle of it.
